וְכֵן הַחֵלֶק מִכְּבוֹדוֹ הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַחָכְמָה, דְּ״כָבוֹד חֲכָמִים יִנְחָלוּ״ (מִשְׁלֵי ג:לה) וּ״בִי מְלָכִים יִמְלֹכוּ״ (שָׁם ח:טו)
and likewise the impartation of His glory is through Chochmah, for "the wise shall inherit honor" (Mishlei 3:35) and "by Me kings reign" (ibid. 8:15);
וְהַמַּעֲמַקִּים שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ וָלֵב הַנִּסְתָּרִים, הֵם לְעוֹלָם דְּבוּקִים בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַפְרִידָם כְּלָל עַל יְדֵי שׁוּם חֵטְא גַּם כֵּן
and the hidden depths within the brain and heart are perpetually cleaved unto the Blessed Name, impossible to be severed by any sin whatsoever;
דְּ״מַחֲשָׁבָה רָעָה — אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְצָרְפָהּ לְמַעֲשֶׂה״ (קִדּוּשִׁין מ׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
for "an evil thought the Holy One, blessed be He, does not combine with deed" (Kiddushin 40a),
דְּאֵין חֵטְא מַגַּעַת לַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ וָלֵב, רַק כָּל הַחֲטָאִים הֵם בְּמַעֲשִׂים שֶׁבְּפֹעַל
seeing that sin cannot reach the inner thought within brain and heart, all sins being confined to concrete physical actions.
וּבַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דְּמַעֲנִישִׁים עַל מַחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב (קִדּוּשִׁין שָׁם)
And regarding idolatry, where Heaven punishes for thoughts within the heart (Kiddushin 40a),
הַיְינוּ מִשּׁוּם דְּכָל מַחְשְׁבוֹת הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת אֶפְשָׁר לְהַחְזִירָן לִמְקוֹרָן עַל יְדֵי הִתְבּוֹנְנוּת דְּ״הַכֹּל בָּרָא לִכְבוֹדוֹ״ (אָבוֹת ו:יא)
that is because all other imaginative thoughts can be restored to their divine source through the contemplation that "everything He created for His glory" (Avos 6:11),
וְגַם כָּל הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֶפְשָׁר לִקַּח מֵהֶם לִכְבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
and from all worldly imaginations one can extract lessons for His glory;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן עַל זֶה, דְּהוּא מַחֲשָׁבָה הַנִּמְשֶׁכֶת מֵאֵל זָר שֶׁבְּגוּפוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם בֶּחָלָל הַשְּׂמָאלִי שֶׁבַּלֵּב (שַׁבָּת ק״ה עַמּוּד ב׳)
unlike idolatrous thought, which is drawn from the "strange god" within man's body residing in the left ventricle of the heart (Shabbos 105b),
שֶׁהוּא מַמָּשׁ הֵיפֶךְ כְּבוֹדוֹ
being the exact antithesis of His glory;
וְזוֹ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה אֵין לָהּ שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת וְהִתְדַּבְּקוּת עִם מַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב שֶׁל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
and this foreign thought has no connection or bond with the inner depths of the heart of the souls of Israel,
רַק הִיא נִטְפֶּלֶת אֶל כֹּחוֹת הַמִּתְפַּשְּׁטוֹת מִן הַלֵּב אֶל הָאֵבָרִים שֶׁהֵם כֹּחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה
but merely attaches to the powers that extend from the heart unto the limbs, which are the faculties of action.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם מַחֲשָׁבָה זוֹ תִּיקּוּנָהּ קַל מְאֹד בַּחֲרָטָה בְּעָלְמָא
And nevertheless, even this thought's rectification is swift and simple through sincere remorse alone;
וְהָעוֹלָה שֶׁבָּאָה עַל הִרְהוּר הַלֵּב (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ז:ג), בָּאָה לְדוֹרוֹן בְּעָלְמָא
and the Olah offering, which atones for sinful thoughts of the heart (Vayikra Rabbah 7:3), is brought merely as a gift of appeasement;
וַאֲפִילּוּ פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים חֲרָטָה
and even the sinners of Israel are filled with remorse (Eruvin 19a);
וּמִיָּד שֶׁמִּתְחָרֵט בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ, מַחֲשָׁבָה מוֹצִיאָה מִידֵי מַחֲשָׁבָה הַקּוֹדֶמֶת
and immediately when he repents in his mind, this holy thought expels the preceding thought,
כִּי זוֹ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁל הַחֲרָטָה הִיא הַיּוֹצֵאת בֶּאֱמֶת מִמַּעֲמַקֵּי לִבּוֹ, וְנִתְבַּטֵּל מִמֵּילָא מַחֲשָׁבָה הַדִּמְיוֹנִית הַקּוֹדֶמֶת
for this thought of regret issues genuinely from the depths of his heart, and the prior illusory thought is automatically nullified.
וְעַל כֵּן שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת דְּהַשֵּׁם הֵם נִגְלִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן
Therefore the first two letters of the Name (Yud-Hei) are manifest in this world as well;
אַף עַל גַּב דְּמִצַּד עוֹלָם הַזֶּה: ״זֶה שְּׁמִי לְעֹלָם״ (שְׁמוֹת ג:טו) כְּתִיב — לְהַעְלִים
even though from the vantage of this world "this is My Name forever (l'olam)" (Shemos 3:15) is written defectively to mean "to conceal (l'alem)",
דְּ״לֹא כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּכְתָּב נִקְרָא״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (פְּסָחִים נ׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
for "not as the Name is written is It pronounced," as written [in Pesachim 50a];
דְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה הַמּוֹרֶה עַל יִחוּד כָּל כֹּחוֹת הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת עִם הַנִּגְלוֹת יַחַד כּוּלָּם בִּלְתִּי לַה׳ לְבַדּוֹ, דָּבָר זֶה הוּא נֶעְלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
for the Tetragrammaton, which signifies the absolute unity of all hidden and revealed powers unto Hashem alone, remains concealed in this world;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא גָּלוּי בִּכְתָב מְפוֹרָשׁ דְּהָאֱמֶת הוּא כֵּן, דְּ״אַתֶּם הַדְּבֵקִים וְגוֹמֵר״ הוּא דֶּרֶךְ אֱמוּנָה וְהֶעְלֵם
although in the written text of the Torah it is explicitly revealed that the truth is so, for "you that did cleave, etc." is experienced in this world by way of faith and concealment;
דְּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה: ״[כִּי אָדָם] אֵין צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר [יַעֲשֶׂה טּוֹב וְלֹא יֶחֱטָא]״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כ)
for in this world: "there is not a righteous man upon earth that does good and sins not" (Koheles 7:20);
״בָּאָרֶץ״ דַּיְיקָא, מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַמַּחְשִׁיךְ וּמַעֲלִים הָאֱמֶת
"upon earth" specifically, from the perspective of this earthly world that darkens and obscures the truth;
אֲבָל לֶעָתִיד יִתְבָּרֵר דְּ״עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים״ גַּם בְּפֹעַל גָּמוּר
but in the Future it will be clarified that "Your people are all righteous" even in actual deed,
דְּגַם ״כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ״ (יְשַׁעְיָה כ״ו:י״ב) וְהַכֹּל הָיָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, אָז יִהְיֶה נִקְרָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּכְתָּב
for "all our works You have wrought for us" (Yeshayah 26:12) and everything was ultimately for the sake of Heaven, and then the Name will be pronounced as It is written;
אֲבָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵינוֹ נִקְרָא בַּפֶּה לִהְיוֹת מְבוֹרָר כֵּן
but in this world It is not pronounced verbally so as to be openly manifest.
רַק הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת הֵם מְבוֹרָרוֹת לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי בַּנִּסְתָּרוֹת אֵין שַׁיָּיךְ בֵּירוּר לָעַיִן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דְּאֵין יַד עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שׁוֹלֶטֶת שָׁם
Rather, the hidden depths are clarified unto the Blessed Name alone, for in the hidden realms empirical human verification has no bearing, the power of this world possessing no dominion there;
דְּאֵין אָדָם יוֹדֵעַ מַה בְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ, וּכְלַפֵּי שְׁמַיָּא גַּלְיָא מַעֲמַקֵּי הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת דְּאֵין שָׁם רַע בֶּאֱמֶת כְּלָל
for no man knows what is in the heart of his fellow, while before Heaven the hidden depths are revealed, showing that no true evil resides there at all,
וְהַנִּגְלוֹת מְחוּבָּרוֹת עִם הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת דֶּרֶךְ הֶעְלֵם מִיהַת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and the revealed deeds remain bound with the hidden realms in concealment in this world.
וְכָל רְצוֹן עֲמָלֵק הוּא לְהַפְרִיד הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת מֵהַנִּגְלוֹת לְגַמְרֵי
And the entire drive of Amalek is to sever the hidden realms from the revealed realms completely,
שֶׁרְצוֹנוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עוֹלָם נִפְרָד מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
desiring to render this world an autonomous domain disconnected from the Blessed Name,
שֶׁזֶּה חֵשֶׁק כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת שֶׁאֵין חֶפְצָם בְּעוֹל תּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת וְעוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם
which is the desire of all the nations who reject the yoke of Torah, mitzvos, and the Kingdom of Heaven;
וַעֲמָלֵק הוּא רֵאשִׁית כֹּחַ זֶה דִּפְרִיקַת עוֹל וְלֵילֵךְ בִּשְׁרִירוּת לִבּוֹ בְּכָל מִינֵי הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת
and Amalek is the primal source of this power of casting off the yoke to walk in the stubbornness of one's heart in every unrestrained expansion;
וְזֶהוּ פֵּירוּד שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת אַחֲרוֹנוֹת, שֶׁהוּא כֹּחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, מִן הַשֵּׁם לְגַמְרֵי:
and this is the mystical severance of the final two letters (Vav-Hei)—the faculties of action in this world—from the Holy Name entirely.
The theme: The severance of the Aleph from the Throne
Kaf-Samech without Aleph

and the perpetual war against Amalek. The word Kisei (כסא) derives from Kes (כס), its spherical shape reflecting the letters Chaf and Samech, while the letter Aleph represents the Master of the Universe
Alupho shel Olam
concealed within it. The universe resembles an achsadra
open on the north side, Bava Batra 25b
, shaped like a square Beis
kanfei ha-aretz

, while the heavens are curved like a Chaf. Amalek seeks to sever the Aleph from the Kes, claiming that the natural realm is devoid of the transcendent Master. Hence "Hashem has a war with Amalek from generation to generation"
Shemos 17:16
. Hashem is termed an "Ish Milchamah"
Man of War
because this war is fought within the human heart
Ish signifying the power of overcoming the yetzer, Avodah Zarah 19a
. Human effort in this battle is concentrated in memory
"Remember... do not forget", Devarim 25:17–19
, because the fantasies of Amalek flourish only through forgetfulness, which is dispelled by the awe-inspiring thread of Techeiles in the Tzitzis that mirrors the Throne of Glory.
וּפֵירוּד אוֹת אָלֶ״ף מִן הַכִּסֵּא, שֶׁהוּא הַמָּקוֹם לִשְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ דֶּרֶךְ קְבִיעוּת כְּמוֹ כִּסֵּא מַלְכוּת מוֹשַׁב הַמֶּלֶךְ
And likewise Amalek causes the severance of the letter Aleph from the Throne (Kisei, leaving only Kes), the Throne being the permanent resting place of His Shechinah like a royal throne;
וְעִיקַּר שֵׁם ״כִּסֵּא״ הוּנַח לְכִסֵּא מְלָכִים כִּמְדוּמֶּה בִּלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ, וְעִיקַּר הַמִּלָּה ״כֵּס״
and the title Kisei was primarily coined for royal thrones in the Holy Tongue, the core root of the word being Kes;
כִּי כֵן דְּמוּת הַכִּסֵּא עָגוֹל וְדוֹמֶה לְסָמֶ״ךְ וּלְכַ״ף
for the structural form of the throne is circular, resembling the letters Samech and Chaf;
וְרוֹב מִלּוֹת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ הֵם מוֹרוֹת בִּתְמוּנָתָן עַל הַדָּבָר שֶׁהֵם מוֹרִים עָלָיו
and most words of the Holy Tongue indicate through the geometric form of their letters the very realities to which they refer,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַב הַאי גָּאוֹן וְרַב נַטְרוֹנַאי גָּאוֹן עַל ״וָוֵי הָעַמּוּדִים״ (שְׁמוֹת כ״ז:י׳) מוּבָא בְּמַהֲרַ״ם אַלְשַׁקַר סִימָן ק׳
as Rav Hai Gaon and Rav Natronai Gaon explained regarding the hooks (vavei) of the pillars (Shemos 27:10) cited in Responsa Maharam Alashkar (§100);
וְכָךְ הָיוּ עוֹשִׂים תְּמוּנַת הַכִּסֵּא: פְּעָמִים פָּתוּחַ מִצַּד צָפוֹן, פְּעָמִים סָתוּם
and so they fashioned the form of the throne: sometimes open from the north, and sometimes enclosed.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּידוּעַ מַה שֶּׁכָּתְבוּ חַכְמֵי הָאֱמֶת בְּעִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ל״א עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה כִּלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם״
And this is as the masters of Kabbalah wrote regarding the Talmudic dictum: "The Torah speaks in the language of human beings" (Berachos 31b),
שֶׁגַּם זֶה רַק כִּלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם, דְּבֶאֱמֶת דִּבְּרוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם בִּלְשׁוֹן תּוֹרָה
which itself is formulated in the language of human comprehension, for in primordial truth humans speak with the vocabulary of the Torah;

וְכָל הַשֵּׁמוֹת וְהַלְּשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה עַל צַד הַהַשְׁאָלָה כְּ״יַד ה׳״ וְ״עֵינֵי ה׳״ וְכַדּוֹמֶה, הוּא לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר עַל הַקְּדוּשָׁה וְהָיָה קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם וּבוֹ נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם

and all anthropomorphic terms in the Torah like "the hand of Hashem" and "the eyes of Hashem" are expressions of the Holy Tongue established in supernal holiness prior to Creation, through which the cosmos was brought into being;
וְכֵן שֵׁם ״כִּסֵּא״ עִיקָּרוֹ עַל כִּסֵּא כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ, וְ״הַשָּׁמַיִם כִּסְאִי״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ס״ו:א׳)
and likewise the title Kisei applies fundamentally to the Throne of His Glory, and "the heavens are My throne" (Yeshayah 66:1);
וְהֵם אֲחוּזִים וּפְגוּשִׁים בָּאָרֶץ כְּפִי דִּבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בַּהַסְּפִינָה דְּנָשְׁקֵי שְׁמַיָּא וְאַרְעָא אַהֲדָדֵי (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ע״ד עַמּוּד א׳)
and the heavens touch the earth as the Sages related regarding the sailors who saw where heaven and earth kiss each other (Bava Batra 74a),
וְכֵן אִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ: כּוֹנֵן קוּרְקְסֵי וְכוּלֵיהּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה ט״ו:כ״ב)
and so is it taught in the Midrash: He fastened clasps linking heaven and earth, see there (Shemos Rabbah 15:22);
וְהַיְינוּ בְּצַד צָפוֹן הַפָּתוּחַ
which is at the northern side which is open,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא כ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳): ״עוֹלָם לְאַכְסַדְרָה דּוֹמֶה״
as written (Bava Batra 25b): "the world is like an achsadra [a porch open on the north]",
וְהוּא דּוֹמֶה לְבֵי״ת דִּמְרוּבָּע כְּפִי דִּבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
and the earth is square like the letter Beis according to our Sages,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״בְּכַנְפוֹת הָאָרֶץ״ (אִיּוֹב ל״ח:י״ג), וְ״כָּנָף״ הַיְינוּ מְרוּבָּע כִּכְנַף דְּצִיצִית, וְעַל כֵּן דּוֹמֶה לְבֵי״ת
as it is written: "the corners (kanfos) of the earth" (Iyov 38:13), and a corner denotes a square edge like the corner of Tzitzis, wherefore it resembles a Beis.
וְהַשָּׁמַיִם עֲגוּלִים דּוֹמִים לְכַ״ף מִצַּד חִיבּוּרָם לָאָרֶץ דְּהַצָּפוֹן פָּתוּחַ, וּמִצַּד עַצְמָם הֵם סְתוּמִים מִכָּל צַד
And the heavens are curved like the letter Chaf at their junction with the earth where the north is open, while in themselves they are sealed on all sides like a Samech;
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא ״כִּסֵּא״ — ״כֵּס״ עַל שֵׁם תְּמוּנָתוֹ
wherefore the Throne is termed Kes
(כס)
after its visual form,
וְאָלֶ״ף עַל שֵׁם אַלּוּפוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם דְּגָנִיז בְּגַוֵּיהּ, עַל כֵּן אֵין נִרְגֶּשֶׁת בַּמִּבְטָא
and the letter Aleph represents the Master of the Universe (Alupho shel Olam) concealed within it, which is silent in phonetic pronunciation;
וַעֲמָלֵק שֶׁרוֹצֶה לְהַפְרִיד הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת מֵהַנִּגְלוֹת וְלוֹמַר דְּאֵין שָׁם הֶעְלֵם בַּנִּגְלֶה כְּלָל, הֲרֵי מַפְרִיד הַכִּסֵּא גַּם כֵּן, ״כֵּס״ מִן הָאָלֶ״ף
and Amalek, seeking to sever the hidden from the revealed and asserting that no transcendent Master is concealed within nature, severs the Aleph from the Kes;
וְעַל כֵּן: ״מִלְחָמָה לַה׳ בַּעֲמָלֵק מִדֹּר דֹּר״ (שְׁמוֹת י״ז:ט״ז)
therefore: "Hashem will have war with Amalek from generation to generation" (Shemos 17:16).
דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִקְרָא ״אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה״ (שְׁמוֹת ט״ו:ג׳)
For the Blessed Name is termed "a Man of War" (Shemos 15:3);
כִּי תֹּאַר מִלְחָמָה שַׁיָּיךְ רַק גַּבֵּי אִישׁ, דִּכְלַפֵּי מַעְלָה אֵיךְ שַׁיָּיךְ מִלְחָמָה כְּלָל, הֲלֹא בְּיָדוֹ הַכֹּל
for the description of "war" applies strictly to an earthly man, as how could warfare apply Above when everything is in His hand?
רַק הַמִּלְחָמָה הוּא בְּלֵב הָאָדָם, שֶׁהַכֹּחַ דְּחֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמַּעַל שֶׁבְּקִרְבּוֹ נִלְחָם עִם כֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר רָע
Rather, the battle is waged within the human heart, where the divine spark within him fights against the evil inclination,
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מָסַר הַבְּחִירָה לָאָדָם, אֶלָּא שֶׁ״אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ [אֵין יָכוֹל לוֹ]״ (קִדּוּשִׁין ל׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
the Blessed Name having granted free choice to man, yet "were not the Holy One assisting him, he could not overcome it" (Kiddushin 30b);
וְהַסִּיּוּעַ דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַמִּלְחָמָה דַּה׳ בַּעֲמָלֵק בְּהִתְלַבְּשׁוּתוֹ בְּלֵב הָאָדָם
and this divine aid is the war of Hashem against Amalek enclothed within the heart of man.
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא ״אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה״, דְּשֵׁם ״אִישׁ״ נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם כֹּחַ הִתְגַּבְּרוּתוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״כִּי כְאִישׁ גְּבוּרָתוֹ״ (שׁוֹפְטִים ח:כא)
And therefore He is called "a Man of War," for the title Ish denotes the power of conquest, as it is written: "for as the man is, so is his strength" (Shoftim 8:21),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (י״ט עַמּוּד א׳) עַל פָּסוּק ״אַשְׁרֵי הָאִישׁ״ (תְּהִלִּים א:א): שֶׁמִּתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִצְרוֹ כְּשֶׁהוּא אִישׁ
and as written in Avodah Zarah (19a) on the verse "Happy is the man" (Tehillim 1:1): one who overcomes his yetzer while he is an Ish [in full vigor].
וְהַהִתְגַּבְּרוּת הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי עֵזֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְסַיַּיעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא זוֹ הוּא רַק בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁבַּלֵּב
And this triumph is achieved solely through the help of the Blessed Name, this heavenly aid operating within the root of the heart;
דְּאַחַר שֶׁיָּצָא לְפוֹעַל מַה שֶּׁהָיָה כְּבָר הוּא, וְצָרִיךְ לִתְשׁוּבָה דְּגַם כֵּן עִיקָּרָהּ בַּלֵּב כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״וּלְבָבוֹ יָבִין וְשָׁב״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ו:י)
for once sin has materialized into deed it has already occurred, requiring repentance which likewise resides primarily in the heart: "his heart shall understand, and he shall return" (Yeshayah 6:10);
וְכֵן שׁוֹרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק הוּא בַּלֵּב, שֶׁהוּא הָרֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם דְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כֹּחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה דְּרָע
and so too the root of Amalek attacks the heart, being the first of the nations in spreading the active powers of evil.
וְכָל כֹּחַ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם בָּזֶה הוּא רַק בִּזְכִירָה: ״זָכוֹר... אַל תִּשְׁכָּח״ (דְּבָרִים כ״ה:י״ז–י״ט)
And the entire human effort in this war is concentrated in remembrance: "Remember... do not forget" (Devarim 25:17–19);
כִּי כָּל הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת הַגּוֹבְרוֹת בְּלֵב בְּנֵי אָדָם הֵם רַק מִצַּד הַשִּׁכְחָה בָּאֱמֶת שֶׁבּוֹ דָּבוּק נֶפֶשׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי
for all the false imaginations that dominate human hearts arise solely from forgetting the divine truth to which the Jewish soul is cleaved;
דְּעַל זֶה הוּא מִצְוַת צִיצִית: ״וּרְאִיתֶם אֹתוֹ וּזְכַרְתֶּם [אֶת כָּל מִצְוֺת ה׳]... וְלֹא תָתוּרוּ אַחֲרֵי לְבַבְכֶם [וְאַחֲרֵי עֵינֵיכֶם]״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר ט״ו:ל״ט)
toward which serves the mitzvah of Tzitzis: "that you may look upon it, and remember all the commandments of Hashem... and that you seek not after your own heart and your own eyes" (Bamidbar 15:39);
הוּא סְגֻלָּה שֶׁלֹּא לָתוּר אַחֲרֵי דִּמְיוֹנוֹת עַל יְדֵי הַזְּכִירָה בְּמִצְוֹת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁבָּא עַל יְדֵי צִיצִית הַמְּעוֹרֶרֶת יִרְאָה בְּלֵב הָאָדָם
being a divine remedy not to wander after illusions through remembering the commandments, awakened by Tzitzis which stirs holy awe in the heart,
כִּידוּעַ בַּזֹּוהַר בְּסוֹד הַצִּיצִית וְהַתְּכֵלֶת
as known in the Zohar regarding the mystery of Tzitzis and the blue thread (Techeiles),
שֶׁבְּכָל מִצְוָה יֵשׁ עִנְיָן מְיוּחָד, וְזוֹ הַמִּצְוָה מְעוֹרֶרֶת יִרְאָה הַמְּבִיאָה לִידֵי זְכִירָה
for each commandment possesses a specific quality, and this mitzvah arouses awe which leads to active remembrance;
דְּהַשִּׁכְחָה בָּא רַק מִפְּנֵי ״עַצְלָה תַּפִּיל תַּרְדֵּמָה״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ט:ט״ו), וְעַל יְדֵי יִרְאָה וּפַחַד ה׳ הוּא מִתְעוֹרֵר מִשְּׁנָתוֹ
for forgetfulness arises only because "slothfulness casts into a deep sleep" (Mishlei 19:15), while through awe and fear of Hashem one is awakened from his slumber;
וְעַל כֵּן: תְּכֵלֶת דּוֹמָה לַיָּם, וְיָם דּוֹמֶה לָרָקִיעַ, עַד לְכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד (מְנָחוֹת מ״ג עַמּוּד ב׳) שֶׁשָּׁם גִּלּוּי שְׁכִינָה הַמֵּבִיא מוֹרָא גָּדוֹל
wherefore: Techeiles resembles the sea, the sea resembles the firmament, reaching unto the Throne of Glory (Menachos 43b), where the revelation of the Shechinah inspires great awe.
וּבַעֲמָלֵק נֶאֱמַר: ״וְלֹא יָרֵא אֱלֹהִים״ (דְּבָרִים כ״ה:י״ח)
And concerning Amalek it is written: "and he feared not God" (Devarim 25:18);
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכ״ג עַמּוּד ב׳) דְּעַל כֵּן נוֹפֵל בְּיַד זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: ״אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים אֲנִי יָרֵא״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מ״ב:י״ח)

and the Sages of blessed memory stated (Bava Batra 123b) that therefore Amalek falls specifically into the hand of the seed of Yosef, concerning whom it is written: "for I fear God" (Bereishis 42:18);
וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּ״וְלֹא יָרֵא אֱלֹהִים״ אַיִּשְׂרָאֵל קָאֵי, הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי עֲמָלֵק ״אֲשֶׁר קָרְךָ״ שֶׁהִכְנִיס לְתוֹכָם דִּמְיוֹנוֹת וְכֹחוֹת הַמַּשְׁכִּיחִים
and even though the phrase "and he feared not God" refers contextually to Israel, that occurred because Amalek "happened upon you," injecting into them fantasies and forces of forgetfulness,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשׂוּ עָיֵף וְיָגֵעַ וְלֹא יָרֵא אֱלֹהִים, שֶׁבָּאוּ לְדִמְיוֹנוֹת
whereby they became faint and weary and devoid of divine awe, succumbing to illusions.

וְהָעֵצָה: ״זָכוֹר אֵת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה [לְךָ עֲמָלֵק] וְגוֹמֵר״ (דְּבָרִים כ״ה:י״ז), שֶׁיִּזְכּוֹר וְיִתְבּוֹנֵן שֶׁהַשִּׁיקּוּעַ שֶׁלּוֹ בְּדִמְיוֹנוֹת הוּא נִמְשָׁךְ מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ עֲדַיִין בָּעוֹלָם

And the divine counsel is: "Remember what Amalek did unto you, etc." (Devarim 25:17), that one should remember and reflect that his personal immersion in fantasies is drawn from the root of Amalek still active in the world;
עַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּעַצְמוֹ הוּא מִתְעוֹרֵר לָצֵאת מֵהַדִּמְיוֹן
through this very contemplation he is stirred to break out of the illusion;
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם אַחַר שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּקַּע אֵין יוֹצֵא בְּקַל וְצָרִיךְ מִלְחָמָה
yet once submerged he does not emerge easily and must wage spiritual warfare;
״וְהָיָה בְּהָנִיחַ [ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְךָ מִכָּל אֹיְבֶיךָ מִסָּבִיב] וְגוֹמֵר״ (שָׁם:י״ט), שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ לְנִיחָא וּמְנוּחַת הַלֵּב שֶׁלֹּא יְבַלְבְּלֶנּוּ עוֹד דִּמְיוֹנוֹת הַמַּשְׁכִּיחִים

"Therefore it shall be, when Hashem your God has given you rest from all your enemies round about, etc." (ibid. 25:19), when one attains tranquility and inner peace where distracting fantasies no longer confuse him,
אָז יִתְאַמֵּץ ״תִּמְחֶה אֶת זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק מִתַּחַת הַשָּׁמָיִם״ (שָׁם)
then he shall exert himself to "blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven" (ibid.),
רָצָה לוֹמַר מִכָּל חַדְרֵי מוֹחוֹ וְלִבּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁכַּח עוֹד:
meaning from all the chambers of his brain and heart, so that he shall never forget again.

5.h: The theme: The two historical battles against Amalek and King Saul's tragic error in sparing Agag. The first war was fought prior to the Giving of the Torah through Yehoshua from the seed of Yosef, because Amalek ("first among the nations") arose to confront the emerging head of Israel when Israel's virtue had been established solely through the natural moral restraint (derech eretz) of Yosef in Egypt. The second war was commanded to King Saul from the seed of Binyamin—representing the restraint dictated by the Torah's laws—at the inception of the Israelite monarchy. Saul was commanded to utterly annihilate Amalek, yet he spared Agag and the choice animals. Saul perceived that Haman's root (alluded to in the question ha-min ha-etz, Chullin 139b) reflects the illusion of the withdrawal of divine providence, which perversely enables human free choice; he mistakenly thought this hidden root could be salvaged as an aveirah lishmah and consecrated to Hashem. While ordinary nations possess sparks that can be converted to holiness, Amalek's outward manifestation is irredeemably evil and no converts are accepted from them (Mechilta). The tradition that Haman's descendants taught Torah in Bnei Brak (Sanhedrin 97a) occurred only through an unmanifested seminal drop absorbed into an Israelite woman, for Amalek's intrinsic nature can never be transformed into good.

p: וּבִשְׁתֵּי פְּעָמִים הָיָה הַמִּלְחָמָה בְּפֹעַל, שֶׁעַל זֶה דָּרְשׁוּ: ״מִדֹּר דֹּר״ (שְׁמוֹת י״ז:ט״ז)
And twice the war against Amalek was waged in actual physical battle, concerning which they expounded: "from generation to generation" (Shemos 17:16; Tanchuma, Ki Seitzei 11):
בְּדוֹר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עַל יְדֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף, שֶׁאָז הָיְתָה הַתְחָלַת צְמִיחַת קֶרֶן יִשְׂרָאֵל
in the generation of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, through Yehoshua from the seed of Yosef, for then was the beginning of the sprouting of the pride of Israel;
וְהוּא, לִהְיוֹת ״רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ד:כ׳), לְעוֹלָם מִתְעוֹרֵר נֶגֶד הָרֵאשִׁית דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
and Amalek, being "the first of the nations" (Bamidbar 24:20), perpetually arouses himself against the first and foremost of Israel;
וְאָז הָיָה קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה עֲדַיִין, שֶׁלֹּא נִתְבָּרְרָה מַעֲלַת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲדַיִין אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי יוֹסֵף
and that war occurred prior to the Giving of the Torah, when the supreme stature of Knesset Israel had not yet been clarified except through Yosef;
כִּי הוּא הָיָה מֶלֶךְ בְּמִצְרַיִם קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ שֶׁקָּדְמָה לַתּוֹרָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ט:ג)
for Yosef was king in Egypt prior to the Giving of the Torah by way of ethical discipline (derech eretz) which preceded the Torah (Vayikra Rabbah 9:3);
דְּכָל הָאוּמּוֹת אֵינָם בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ גַּם כֵּן, דְּהַהַגְדָּרָה בַּתַּאֲווֹת הוּא מִצַּד מִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ גַּם כֵּן
for all the nations lack true derech eretz, seeing that moral boundary-setting in desires likewise stems from the attribute of derech eretz;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה לִמְשׁוֹל עֲלֵיהֶם
and through this virtue Yosef merited to rule over them;
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁהוּא גָּדַר עַצְמוֹ מִן הָעֲרָיוֹת, עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִגְדְּרוּ גַּם כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל שָׁם
and because he fenced himself against sexual immorality, through this all Israel were likewise shielded from immorality there,
כִּי הוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ לִקְדֻשַּׁת הַבְּרִית דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּידוּעַ
for he is the root of the holiness of the Covenant for the Children of Israel, as is known.
וּלְפִי שֶׁהָיָה קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, הָיָה בְּכֹחַ עֲמָלֵק לָבוֹא וּלְהִתְעוֹרֵר נֶגְדָּם
And because it was prior to the Giving of the Torah, it was within the capacity of Amalek to come and attack them;
כִּי הַגּוֹיִם אוֹמְרִים שֶׁהֵם בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ וְיִשּׁוּב הָעוֹלָם
for the gentiles claim that they conduct themselves with derech eretz and civilize the world,
אַךְ הַדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ שֶׁלָּהֶם הוּא מִצַּד הַהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְלֹא מִצַּד יִרְאַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
yet their worldly conduct stems from immersion in the material pleasures of this world and not out of fear of the Blessed Name;
וְעַל כֵּן נָפַל בְּיַד זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף
wherefore Amalek fell into the hand of the seed of Yosef (Bava Batra 123b).
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בִּימֵי שָׁאוּל שֶׁהוּא תְּחִלַּת מַלְכוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל, לֹא נִתְעוֹרֵר עוֹד עֲמָלֵק, דְּאַחַר מַתַּן תּוֹרָה יָדַע שֶׁאֵין לוֹ כֹּחַ

And afterward in the days of Saul, which was the beginning of the monarchy of Israel, Amalek did not initiate an assault on his own, for after the Giving of the Torah he knew that he lacked the power;
אֶלָּא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹרֵר אֶת שָׁאוּל שֶׁבָּא לִהְיוֹת הָרֵאשִׁית דְּמַמְלְכוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל, לִמְחוֹת אֶת הָרֵאשִׁית דְּגוֹיִם
but rather the Blessed Name aroused Saul, who came to be the first of the kingdom of Israel, to blot out the first of the nations;
וְהוּא מִזַּרְעָא דְּבִנְיָמִין שֶׁהוּא הַהַגְדָּרָה שֶׁעַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה
and Saul was from the seed of Binyamin, who embodies the restraint defined by the Torah;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ ״בְּהָנִיחַ [ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְךָ מִכָּל אֹיְבֶיךָ מִסָּבִיב] וְגוֹמֵר״ (דְּבָרִים כ״ה:י״ט)
which is the fulfillment of: "when Hashem your God has given you rest from all your enemies round about, etc." (Devarim 25:19),
דְּהַתּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין לַיֵּצֶר שֶׁעַל יָדָהּ יָכוֹל לָנוּחַ מִכָּל אוֹיְבָיו
for the Torah is the spice against the yetzer (Kiddushin 30b), through which one can attain rest from all his spiritual adversaries,
רָצָה לוֹמַר מִכָּל מִינֵי הִתְגַּבְּרוּת יֵצֶר רָע שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ כָּל כָּךְ לְמִלְחָמָה וְנִיצּוּחַ בִּכְבִישָׁה
meaning from all manners of attacks of the yetzer hara, where one does not require intense warfare and suppression through coercive battle,
רַק בִּמְשִׁיכָה לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ, דְּמִמֵּילָא מִתְבַּטֵּל וְנִימּוֹחַ וּמִתְפּוֹצֵץ
but merely by dragging it into the study hall, whereby it is automatically nullified, dissolved, and shattered.
עַל כֵּן נִצְטַוָּה לִמְחוֹתוֹ וּלְהַחֲרִימוֹ לְגַמְרֵי
Therefore Saul was commanded to blot Amalek out and utterly destroy him (I Shmuel 15:3);
וְלֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדוֹ, שֶׁהִשְׁאִיר לַאֲגָג דִּנְפַק מִינֵּיהּ הָמָן בְּאוֹתָהּ לַיְלָה
yet he did not succeed, for he spared Agag, from whom Haman issued on that very night (Megillah 15a),
הַיְינוּ הָרֵאשִׁית דְּרֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם
namely the very pinnacle of the "first of the nations";
כִּי גַּם הָרֵאשִׁית עַצְמוֹ הוּא קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ רֹאשׁ וְסוֹף
for that primary root is itself an entire spiritual structure possessing a head and an end;
וְהָרֹאשׁ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק הוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ נִמְשֶׁכֶת הַשִּׁכְחָה
and the head of Amalek is the primal source from which all spiritual forgetfulness is drawn;
כִּי הָעוֹקֵר עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה צָרִיךְ לְשָׁרֵשׁ אַחֲרֶיהָ
for one who uproots idolatry must root it out completely (Avodah Zarah 45b),
וְהוּא חָמַל עַל הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ, הַיְינוּ חָשַׁב דְּאֵין בָּזֶה
yet Saul had compassion upon that root, believing that there was some constructive utility within it.

כִּי שׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָמָן, שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּחֻלִּין (קל״ט עַמּוּד ב׳) דְּרָמוּז בַּתּוֹרָה בִּקְרָא: ״הֲמִן הָעֵץ [אֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִיךָ לְבִלְתִּי אֲכָל מִמֶּנּוּ אָכָלְתָּ]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג:יא)

For this root is the essence of Haman, regarding whom the Sages stated in Chullin (139b) that he is alluded to in the Torah in the verse: "Is it from the tree (ha-min ha-etz) whereof I commanded you that you should not eat, that you have eaten?" (Bereishis 3:11);
וּמִלַּת ״הֲמִן״ הוּא לְשׁוֹן שְׁאֵלָה, וּבָזֶה נִיתַּן פֶּתַח לִטְעוֹת שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צָרִיךְ לִשְׁאוֹל
and the word ha-min is an expression of inquiry, and through this phrasing an opening was provided to mistakenly think that the Blessed Name needs to ask questions;
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה כֵּן, שֶׁהָרוֹצֶה לִטְעוֹת יָבוֹא וְיִטְעֶה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ח:ה)
and the Blessed Name willed it so, that whoever wishes to err may come and err (Bereishis Rabbah 8:5);
וּמִזֶּה נִמְשָׁךְ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָמָן שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ טָעוּת, לַחְשׁוֹב שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ סִלֵּק יְדִיעָתוֹ מִתַּחְתּוֹנִים
and from this derived the root of Haman, which is the false notion that the Blessed Name removed His foreknowledge and providence from the lower worlds;
וּמִזֶּה הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ וְהַתְחָלָה לְהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בְּדִמְיוֹנוֹת וְהַפְרָדָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and from this originates the inception of immersion in illusions and separation from the Blessed Name.
וּמִבְּנֵי בָּנָיו שֶׁל הָמָן לָמְדוּ תוֹרָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
Yet "descendants of Haman taught Torah in Bnei Brak" (Sanhedrin 97a);
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת לְעִנְיַן מִצְוֹת הַתּוֹרָה צָרִיךְ הָאֱמוּנָה בִּבְחִירָה שֶׁהִיא בְּיַד הָאָדָם, שֶׁהִיא הֵיפֶךְ הַיְּדִיעָה
for in truth, regarding the performance of the commandments, one requires the operational belief in free choice resting in human hands, which functions as the inverse of absolute foreknowledge;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזֶּהוּ קוֹדֶם מַעֲשֶׂה וְשָׁם הוּא אַחַר מַעֲשֶׂה, וּבָזֶה וַדַּאי כְּלַפֵּי שְׁמַיָּא גַּלְיָא
even though free choice applies prior to the deed while foreknowledge encompasses the reality after the deed, wherein all is certainly revealed before Heaven;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, כֵּיוָן דְּיֵשׁ בְּמִקְצָת עִנְיַן סִילּוּק יְדִיעָה תּוֹעֶלֶת לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּלְקִיּוּם הַמִּצְוֹת
nevertheless, since in a certain respect the subjective concealment of foreknowledge serves the study of Torah and the fulfillment of mitzvos,
חָשַׁב שָׁאוּל דְּזֶהוּ הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁאֵין לְאַבְּדוֹ, וְעַל זֶה הוּא שֶׁחָמַל
Saul thought that this was a constructive root that should not be eradicated, and concerning this point he had compassion;
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה הֵם בָּנָיו שֶׁלָּמְדוּ תוֹרָה
and from this hidden aspect emerged Haman's descendants who taught Torah!
וְעַל כֵּן הִנִּיחַ גַּם כֵּן הַצֹּאן וּבָקָר לְהַקְרִיב לַה׳
And therefore Saul likewise spared the choice sheep and cattle to sacrifice unto Hashem (I Shmuel 15:15);
כִּידוּעַ לְעוֹלָם בְּכָל דָּבָר ״נָעוּץ סוֹפוֹ בִּתְחִלָּתוֹ״ (סֵפֶר יְצִירָה א:ז)
for as is universally known, in every matter "its end is wedged in its beginning" (Sefer Yetzirah 1:7);
וְקִנְיָנֵי הָאָדָם שֶׁהֵם הַנִּטְפָּלִים לָאָדָם וּמִכְּלַל הַסּוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה, הֵם נְעוּצִים בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה וּבְעֹומֶק רֵאשִׁית
and the material possessions of a person, which are secondary attachments to man and part of the final outcome of action, are rooted in the initial thought and the depth of the beginning;
וּמִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא חָשַׁב שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּעֹומֶק רֵאשִׁית שֶׁלּוֹ אֵיזֶה דָּבָר טוֹב שֶׁרָאוּי לַחְמוֹל עָלָיו
and because Saul assumed that in the depth of Amalek's beginning there existed some positive element worthy of being spared,
גָּרַם לוֹ לִטְעוֹת גַּם בְּעֹומֶק אַחֲרִית, שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּקִנְיָנָיו גַּם כֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ טוֹב לִהְיוֹת רְאוּיִם לְהַקְרָבָה לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

this led him to err regarding the outer edge of Amalek's property as well, imagining that in his livestock there likewise existed a good root worthy of being offered in the service of the Blessed Name.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָמַר בְּפֵירוּשׁ לְהַחֲרִים הַכֹּל, חָשַׁב הוּא זֶה עַל דְּבַר ״עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ״ לִקְלוֹט הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ טוֹב מִמֶּנּוּ
And even though the Blessed Name explicitly commanded to destroy everything utterly, Saul viewed this through the perspective of an aveirah lishmah, seeking to harvest the spark of good from him;
דְּנִיצּוּחַ כָּל אוּמָּה הוּא עַל יְדֵי קְלִיטַת הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַטּוֹב מִמֶּנּוּ לַקְּדוּשָׁה
for the true conquest of any gentile nation is accomplished by gathering its holy spark into holiness,
כְּמוֹ בְּמִצְרַיִם עַל יְדֵי בִּתְיָה בַּת פַּרְעֹה, שׁוּב כָּל הַנִּשְׁאָר מֵהָאוּמָּה הוֹלְכִים לַאֲבַדּוֹן
as occurred in Egypt through Bisyah the daughter of Pharaoh (Megillah 13a), after which the remainder of the nation fell into ruin;
וּבַעֲמָלֵק שֶׁנִּצְטַוָּה לְהַחֲרִים הַכֹּל, וְהוּא חָשַׁב דְּגַם בּוֹ יֵשׁ אֵיזֶה שׁוֹרֶשׁ טוֹב לִקְלוֹט לַקְּדוּשָׁה
yet with Amalek, where Saul was commanded to destroy all, he reasoned that within him too there lay a good spark to be absorbed into holiness.
אַף דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צִוָּה לְהַחֲרִים הַכֹּל, הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לְצִירְעָא: ״לֹא מִדּוּבְשָׁךְ [וְלֹא מֵעוּקְצָךְ]״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה כ:א)

And even though the Blessed Name commanded to annihilate all, Saul thought this command was merely along the lines of what is said to the wasp: "Neither your honey nor your sting" (Bamidbar Rabbah 20:1);
לְפִי שֶׁיָּדַע שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר נְקִיִּים כָּל כָּךְ שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לִקְלוֹט הַטּוֹב לְבַד בְּלִי שׁוּם עֵירוּב רָע
assuming that Hashem commanded this only because the Israelites of that generation were not sufficiently pure to extract the good alone without absorbing evil;
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא וְהָעָם חָמְלוּ עַל אוֹתוֹ מְעַט הַטּוֹב שֶׁדִּמּוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם
wherefore he and the people had compassion upon that perceived fragment of good;
וְדִמּוּ שֶׁיַּכְנִיסוּ עַצְמָם לְכָךְ אַף דִּמְעוֹרָב בְּרָע גַּם כֵּן
and they presumed to enter into this extraction even though it was entangled with evil,
וְהִתְחַכְּמוּ לְהַקְרִיב מֵהַצֹּאן לַה׳, וְ״שׁוֹמֵר מִצְוָה לֹא יֵדַע דָּבָר רָע״ (קֹהֶלֶת ח:ה)
seeking to outsmart the command by offering from the sheep unto Hashem, trusting that "whoever keeps the commandment shall know no evil thing" (Koheles 8:5);
עַד שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ שְׁמוּאֵל: ״הִנֵּה שְׁמֹעַ [מִזֶּבַח טוֹב] וְגוֹמֵר, [כִּי חַטַּאת קֶסֶם מֶרִי] וְאָוֶן וּתְרָפִים הַפְצַר״ (שְׁמוּאֵל א ט״ו:כ״ב–כ״ג)
until Shmuel rebuked him: "Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice... and stubbornness (hafzar) is as iniquity and idolatry" (I Shmuel 15:22–23);
פֵּירוּשׁ ״הַפְצַר״ הוּא עַקְשָׁנוּת לְהִתְחַכֵּם יוֹתֵר נֶגֶד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
the meaning of hafzar being the stubborn audacity to rationalize and outsmart the command of the Blessed Name.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם רָאוּ יָפֶה דְּמִבְּנֵי בָּנָיו שֶׁל הָמָן וְכוּלֵיהּ, הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה אֵיזֶה דָּבָר טוֹב גָּנוּז בַּגּוֹיִם
And although they foresaw accurately that descendants of Haman would teach Torah, proving that a hidden good spark was concealed there;
כְּבָר כָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר דְּנִרְאֶה לִי דְּהָיָה עַל יְדֵי אֶחָד מִזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאוֹנֶס
I have already written elsewhere that it appears to me that this occurred through one of Haman's descendants who violated an Israelite woman under duress,
דִּקְרוּי בְּנָהּ וְקָרוּי גַּם כֵּן בְּנוֹ בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב, וְהוּא בֶּן אִישׁ מִצְרִי (וַיִּקְרָא כ״ד:י׳)
so that the child is called her son, yet also designated his son in scriptural idiom, as with the son of the Egyptian man (Vayikra 24:10);
אֲבָל בְּלָאו הָכִי אֵין מְקַבְּלִין גֵּר מֵעֲמָלֵק, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמְּכִילְתָּא (בְּשַׁלַּח פָּרָשָׁה ב׳)
for otherwise, no converts are accepted from Amalek, as written in the Mechilta (Beshalach, parashah 2);
כִּי אֵין בָּהֶם שׁוּם צַד לַחְלוּחִית שֶׁל קְדוּשָׁה אַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר יָצָא לְפֹעַל לִהְיוֹת עָלָיו שֵׁם עֲמָלֵק
for they possess no moisture of holiness once they have emerged into actuality bearing the name of Amalek.
כִּי אִילּוּ הָיָה מָקוֹם לְהָפְכוֹ לְטוֹב, לֹא הָיָה רָע כְּלָל
For had there been any possibility of transforming him into good, he would not have been absolute evil at all;
שֶׁהֲרֵי כָּל שָׁרְשׁוֹ הוּא רַק הָרָע שֶׁבַּכֹּחַ וּבַנִּסְתָּרוֹת לְהַמְשִׁיךְ לְפֹעַל
seeing that his entire essence is the primordial evil within potentiality and hidden thought seeking to manifest in deed;
וְאֵצֶל הָאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם ״מַחֲשָׁבָה רָעָה — מְצָרְפָהּ לְמַעֲשֶׂה״ (קִדּוּשִׁין מ׳ עַמּוּד א׳), דְּגַם זֶה רַע גָּמוּר כִּי שָׁרְשָׁם כֵּן
and among the nations of the world "an evil thought is combined with deed" (Kiddushin 40a), for even their thought is consummate evil, such being their root;
וַעֲמָלֵק כָּל הָרָע שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה, דְּבוֹ הוּא עִיקַּר הַפְּשִׁיטוּת טְלָפַיִם דְּעֵשָׂו
and with Amalek his primary evil resides in thought, embodying the very core of Esav's deceptive display of split hooves;
וְאִם הָיָה מָקוֹם לְהִתְהַפֵּךְ לְטוֹב, הַיְינוּ דְּאֵין שָׁרְשׁוֹ כֵּן, כִּי הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ לֹא יִתְהַפֵּךְ, אִם כֵּן אֵינוֹ רַע כְּלָל

and had there been any potential for his root to be inverted to good, it would mean his root was not intrinsically evil, for an essential root cannot be inverted, so he would not be absolute evil at all;
וְרַק בְּכָל אוּמָּה שֶׁשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע שֶׁלָּהּ הוּא בַּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת בְּפֹעַל, זֶה אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְהַפֵּךְ וּבְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יִתְכַּנֶּה
and only in other nations whose evil root resides in the outward expansion of concrete deed is it possible to convert and be called by the name of Israel (Yeshayah 44:5),
לְהִתְדַּבֵּק בְּעֹומֶק רֵאשִׁית שֶׁלּוֹ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבָּהֶם הוּא הָרֵאשִׁית דְּגֵרִים, וְלֹא בַּעֲמָלֵק שֶׁהוּא הָרֵאשִׁית דְּגוֹיִם
cleaving in his hidden primal beginning unto Israel who are the source of righteous converts, which cannot occur with Amalek who is the first of the nations.
אַךְ עֲמָלֵק עַצְמוֹ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְהִתְהַפֵּךְ כְּלָל, דְּ״הֲיַהֲפֹךְ כּוּשִׁי עוֹרוֹ״ (יִרְמְיָה י״ג:כ״ג), כִּי הָעַצְמִיּוּת אֵין מִתְהַפֵּךְ רַק הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת
Yet Amalek himself can never be transformed, for "can the Ethiopian change his skin?" (Yirmiyah 13:23), seeing that intrinsic essence cannot be altered, but only external expansion;
אֲבָל מַה שֶּׁנִּקְלַט מִמֶּנּוּ הוּא הַטִּיפָּה זַרְעִיּוֹת שֶׁהִיא נִמְשֶׁכֶת מֵעֹומֶק רֵאשִׁית הַנֶּעְלָם מֵהָאָדָם עַצְמוֹ
but what was extracted from him was the seminal drop drawn from the transcendent depth of the beginning concealed from the man himself;
וְכַנּוֹדָע דִּבְבָנִים מִתְגַּלֶּה מַעֲמַקֵּי לֵב הָאָבוֹת מַה שֶּׁהָיָה נֶעְלָם מֵהֶם עַצְמָם
and as is known, within children are revealed the inner depths of the fathers' hearts that were hidden from the fathers themselves;

וּכְשֶׁאוֹתָהּ טִיפָּה נִקְלְטָה מִיָּד בָּרֶחֶם הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהּ שׁוּם הִתְגַּלּוּת בְּפֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל לְזֶרַע עֲמָלֵק, עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיּוּקְלַט לַקְּדוּשָׁה

and when that drop was immediately absorbed within the Israelite womb, possessing no manifest realization in this world as Amalekite seed, in this manner alone was it possible to be integrated into holiness.
כִּי בְּוַדַּאי יֵשׁ אֵיזֶה נִיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשִׁים בַּעֲמָלֵק גַּם כֵּן, דְּלוּלֵי כֵן מִנַּיִן הָיָה לוֹ חַיּוּת וְקִיּוּם כְּלָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
For certainly there exist some holy sparks within Amalek as well, for otherwise whence would he derive vitality and existence in this world?
אֲבָל הִיא בִּלְתִּי נִגְלֵית לוֹ עַצְמוֹ וְלֹא לְשׁוּם בְּרִיָּה בָּעוֹלָם, כִּי כָּל מַה שֶּׁבָּא לִידֵי גִּלּוּי מִמֶּנּוּ הוּא רַע גָּמוּר
Yet that spark is completely unrevealed to Amalek himself and to any creature in the world, for whatever comes into manifestation from him is absolute evil;
וְהַנִּיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ הַמְחַיֵּהוּ הוּא רַק הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ מַה שֶּׁרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מְצִיאוּת דָּבָר כָּזֶה בָּעוֹלָם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא עַצְמוֹ צִוָּה עָלָיו לְמוֹחֲתוֹ:
and the holy spark that animates him is solely the primordial root wherein the Blessed Name willed that such a dark entity exist in the world, even though He Himself commanded to blot it out!

5.h: The theme: The secret things of Hashem (kavshei d'Rachmana), Saul's spiritual injury, and the intoxication of Purim (ad d'lo yada). Sparing Agag was King Saul's tragic error: he sought to investigate the transcendent divine secret of Amalek's hidden spark, misapplying the principle "it is the glory of kings to search out a matter" (Mishlei 25:2). While kings possess the Holy Spirit (ruach ha-kodesh) through Malchus (Chochmah Tata'ah), the ultimate spark of Amalek is beyond human comprehension. Saul ate excessive honey ("It is not good to eat much honey", Mishlei 25:27), suffering the fate of Ben Zoma who "gazed and was harmed" (Chagigah 14b), stricken with an evil spirit of melancholy and losing his throne. Nevertheless, through this deep perception his descendants Mordechai and Esther triumphed over Haman, mastering the domain of silence and concealment (pelech ha-shesika). On Purim, when wine enters and the secret emerges (nichnas yayin yatza sod, Eruvin 65a), the suspension of conscious intellect (ad d'lo yada) reveals that even when intoxicated and acting for personal enjoyment (kulam modim d'ba'inan lachem, Pesachim 68b), a Jew's inner heart remains cleaved unto Hashem.

p: וְדָבָר זֶה ״כִּבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא״ (בְּרָכוֹת י׳ עַמּוּד א׳) וּמֵ״הַנִּסְתָּרֹת [לַה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ]״ (דְּבָרִים כ״ט:כ״ח), וְאֵין בּוֹ שׁוּם דֶּרֶךְ גִּלּוּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל

And this matter belongs to the "secrets of the Merciful One" (Berachos 10a) and "the secret things that belong unto Hashem our God" (Devarim 29:28), possessing no manner of manifestation in this world whatsoever;
וְזֶה הָיָה טָעוּת שָׁאוּל, דְּחָשַׁב ״כְּבֹד מְלָכִים חֲקֹר דָּבָר״ (מִשְׁלֵי כ״ה:ב׳)
and this was the error of Saul, who thought: "the glory of kings is to search out a matter" (Mishlei 25:2);
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כ״א עַמּוּד ב׳) עַל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: ״בִּנְבִיאִים לֹא קָם, אֲבָל בִּמְלָכִים קָם״
wherefore the Sages stated (Rosh Hashanah 21b) regarding King Shlomo: "among prophets there arose not, but among kings there arose";
הַיְינוּ מִצַּד מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת כְּבוֹד שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים, שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
meaning from the aspect of the attribute of Malchus, which is the manifestation of the glory of His Shechinah below, attained through the Holy Spirit;
וְהוּא נְבִיאַת הַחֲכָמִים דְּעָדִיפֵי מִנְּבִיאִים, שֶׁהֵם רוֹאִים רַק הַדָּבָר שֶׁמַּרְאִים לָהֶם
which is the prophecy of the Sages who are superior to prophets (Bava Batra 12a), seeing that prophets perceive only that which is shown to them;
אֲבָל בַּעֲלֵי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ מַשִּׂיגִים הַדָּבָר בְּהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת וַחֲקִירַת שִׂכְלָם כַּנּוֹדָע, וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת, חָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה
whereas masters of the Holy Spirit grasp matters through the contemplation of their intellect, operating through Malchus, the lower wisdom (Chochmah Tata'ah);
וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה רַבָּן שֶׁל כָּל בַּעֲלֵי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִיזַ״ל בְּשַׁעַר רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ)
and David HaMelech, peace be upon him, was the master of all possessors of the Holy Spirit (as the Arizal wrote in Sha'ar Ruach HaKodesh),
שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הַתְחָלַת הַמַּלְכוּת הַקַּיֶּמֶת לָעַד
from whom begins the eternal monarchy.
וְשָׁאוּל שֶׁהִשִּׂיג גַּם כֵּן ״כְּבוֹד מְלָכִים״, עָלָה לְמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵיגָתוֹ
And Saul, who likewise attained this "glory of kings," ascended beyond his appropriate spiritual level,
שֶׁחָשַׁב לַחְקוֹר וְלַעֲמוֹד בְּסוֹד ה׳, דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא נִיתַּן לְדַעַת אָדָם לַחְקוֹר וְלַעֲמוֹד עָלָיו כְּלָל
presuming to delve into the hidden counsel of Hashem, which was never granted to human intellect to fathom;
וְחָשַׁב דִּלִמְלָכִים נִיתַּן רְשׁוּת לַחְקוֹר גַּם עַל זֶה
assuming that unto kings permission was granted to investigate even this deepest mystery;

וּדְשְׁמוּאֵל שֶׁהָיָה רַק נָבִיא בְּהַשָּׂגַת נְבוּאָה, לֹא הִשִּׂיג דֶּרֶךְ קְלִיטָה נִיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ מֵעֲמָלֵק, כִּי לֹא יָדַע שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אֵיזֶה גִּלּוּי לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ נִיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ זֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and that Shmuel, whose perception was prophetic vision, did not perceive the path of extracting the holy spark from Amalek because he did not know of any earthly revelation for it;
אֲבָל הוּא חָשַׁב לְהַשִּׂיגוֹ וְשֶׁיּוּכַל לְקָלְטוֹ, מַה שֶּׁנֶּעְלַם מִשְּׁמוּאֵל בִּנְבוּאָתוֹ
whereas Saul imagined that he could grasp and extract what was hidden from Shmuel in his prophecy.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״אָכֹל דְּבַשׁ הַרְבּוֹת לֹא טוֹב״ (מִשְׁלֵי כ״ה:כ״ז)
And concerning this it is said: "It is not good to eat much honey" (Mishlei 25:27);
וְקָרָה לוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁקָּרָה לְבֶן זוֹמָא דְּהֵצִיץ וְנִפְגַּע (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב חֲגִיגָה י״ד עַמּוּד ב׳)
and there befell him that which befell Ben Zoma who "gazed and was harmed" (Chagigah 14b),
בְּרוּחַ רָעָה שֶׁהָיְתָה מְבַעַתּוֹ (שְׁמוּאֵל א ט״ז:י״ד)
being afflicted with an evil spirit that terrified him (I Shmuel 16:14);
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה נִיטְּלָה מַלְכוּתוֹ
and in this manner his kingdom was taken from him;
כִּי עִיקַּר מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת הוּא: ״לְבִלְתִּי רוּם לְבָבוֹ מֵאֶחָיו״ (דְּבָרִים י״ז:כ׳), שֶׁלֹּא יַחְפּוֹץ לַעֲלוֹת יוֹתֵר מִמַּדְרֵיגָתוֹ
for the foundation of the royal attribute is "that his heart be not lifted up above his brethren" (Devarim 17:20), not striving to ascend beyond his designated rung;
וּכְמִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, דְּבִמְקוֹם גְּדוּלָּתוֹ שָׁם עַנְוְתָנוּתוֹ (מְגִלָּה ל״א עַמּוּד א׳)
mirroring the attribute of the divine Sovereignty: wherever you find His greatness, there you find His humility (Megillah 31a).
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם זָכָה וְיָצָא מִמֶּנּוּ מָרְדֳּכַי וְאֶסְתֵּר שֶׁנִּצְּחוּ לְהָמָן
And nevertheless Saul merited that Mordechai and Esther descended from him, who triumphed over Haman;
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ שֶׁחָשַׁב שֶׁהִשִּׂיג הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּנִיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ הַמְחַיֶּה לַעֲמָלֵק לֹא הָיָה דִּמְיוֹן כּוֹזֵב
for in truth, even his perception of the holy spark animating Amalek was not an empty illusion;
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַשָּׂגָתוֹ זוֹ הָיָה רַק בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה דֶּרֶךְ הַשָּׂגָה לְבַד, וְלֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לַהֲבִיאוֹ לְהִתְגַּלּוּת בְּפֹעַל בְּמַעֲשֶׂה כְּלָל שֶׁזֶּה דָּבָר שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר
except that this perception belonged solely to the realm of thought, and it was impossible to bring it into concrete manifestation in action, which is unattainable;

אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד הַהַשָּׂגָה שֶׁלּוֹ בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחַיּוּת שֶׁל הָמָן, עַל יְדֵי זֶה נָתְנָה אֶסְתֵּר אֶת מָרְדֳּכַי עַל בֵּית הָמָן (אֶסְתֵּר ח:ב), שֶׁבָּהֶם הָיָה גָּנוּז הַשָּׂגַת שׁוֹרֶשׁ חַיּוּתוֹ
yet by virtue of Saul's perception of the root vitality of Haman, Esther set Mordechai over the house of Haman (Esther 8:2), wherein was concealed the mastery over Haman's vitality.
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי אֲחִיזַת פֶּלֶךְ הַשְּׁתִיקָה שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הַהֶעְלֵם
And this was accomplished through seizing the craft of silence (pelech ha-shesikah, Bereishis Rabbah 71:5), which is the power of concealment;
עַל יְדֵי זֶה יָכְלוּ לְהַשִּׂיג הַנֶּעְלָם מֵעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דְּרַק מִצַּד הַגִּלּוּי דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא נֶעְלָם
through which they were enabled to grasp that which is hidden from this world, being concealed only on the revealed earthly plane;
וּבְפוּרִים ״חַיָּיב לִבְסוֹמֵי״, דְּמִשֶּׁנִּכְנַס יַיִן יָצָא סוֹד (עֵרוּבִין ס״ה עַמּוּד א׳), שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ כֹּחַ הַהַעֲלָמָה
and on Purim one is obligated to become intoxicated, for "when wine enters, the secret comes out" (Eruvin 65a), which is the inverse of concealment;
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא ״עַד דְּלֹא יָדַע בֵּין וְכוּלֵיהּ״ (מְגִלָּה ז׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
wherefore the obligation is "until he cannot distinguish between 'Cursed be Haman' and 'Blessed be Mordechai'" (Megillah 7b);
וְיָדוּעַ מִטַּעַם הָאֲרִיזַ״ל שֶׁהוּא לְאוֹתוֹ הַנִּיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם
and it is known from the Arizal (Sha'ar HaKavvanos) that this refers to elevating that very holy spark, see there;
וְהַיְינוּ דְּעַל יְדֵי הַשִּׁכְרוּת מִתְגַּלֶּה הַנֶּעְלָם, אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא בְּלֹא דַּעַת וּבְשִׁכְרוּת
meaning that through drunkenness the concealed spark is revealed, though without conscious intellect and in intoxication;
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן רוּחַ רָעָה דְּשָׁאוּל שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן הֲסָרַת דַּעַת
and this is the esoteric mystery of the evil spirit of Saul, which was likewise a suspension of conscious intellect;
לְפִי שֶׁחָשַׁב לְגַלּוֹת הַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁלּוֹ, וְדָבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק בְּלֹא דַּעַת
because he sought to reveal his concealed spark, an attainment impossible in this world except through the suspension of conscious mind.
וְזֶהוּ בֵּירוּר הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן עִיקָּרָן רַק בְּהֶעְלֵם
And this is the clarification of the imaginations of the Children of Israel, which fundamentally exist in concealment;
וְאֵצֶל הַשִּׁכּוֹר, כָּל מַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּדִמְיוֹנוֹ יוֹצֵא בְּגִילּוּי
and in the drunkard, whatever lies within his subconscious imagination emerges into manifestation;
וְעַל כֵּן אִיתָא בְּעֵירוּבִין (ס״ה עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דְּאָדָם נִיכָּר בְּכוֹסוֹ״
wherefore it is taught in Eruvin (65b): "A person is recognized by his cup";
וּבְפוּרִים הַכֹּל מוֹדִים דְּ״בָּעֵינַן נַמֵּי לָכֶם״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (פְּסָחִים ס״ח עַמּוּד ב׳)
and on Purim all concede that we require bodily rejoicing: "for you" (lachem), as written in Pesachim (68b);
וְכָל מַה שֶּׁחוֹשֵׁב לְגַרְמֵיהּ הוּא גַּם כֵּן לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
so that whatever a Jew desires for personal pleasure is likewise consecrated for the sake of Heaven;
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם כָּל הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁהֵם רַק מַה שֶּׁהַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שְׁקוּעָה בְּמַה שֶּׁהוּא לְגַרְמֵיהּ, אָז הוּא הַהַכָּרָה בְּכוֹסוֹ דְּהַכֹּל לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
wherefore even all imaginations—which consist of thoughts absorbed in personal gratification—reveal through his cup on Purim that everything is truly for the sake of Heaven;
וַאֲפִילּוּ אִם הוּא ״עַד דְּלֹא יָדַע וְכוּלֵיהּ״, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָז הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת מַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב
and even when he reaches "until he cannot distinguish," nevertheless then the innermost depths of the heart are revealed:
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ אוֹמֵר עַל יָמִין שֶׁהוּא שְׂמֹאל, מִכָּל מָקוֹם נְקֻדַּת הַלֵּב דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ:
that even if he calls the right left, the essential point of his heart remains cleaved unto the Blessed Name!

6.h: The theme: The four mitzvos of Purim corresponding to the four letters of the Tetragrammaton and Haman’s metaphysical prosecution against the five soul-levels of Israel. The four physical mitzvos of Purim (reading the Megillah, sending food portions, gifts to the poor, and festive feasting) parallel the four letters of Havayah, through which the eternal war against Amalek is won across every generation. The essence of redemption is the spiritual rectification of the very defect that brought the affliction ("and out of your wounds I will heal you", Yirmiyah 30:17); the removal of Ahasuerus's signet ring brought Israel to complete repentance (teshuvah me-ahavah). Haman—the master of the evil tongue—aimed his prosecution directly at the King of kings: "there is one people dispersed and scattered, their laws are diverse, neither keep they the king's laws" (Esther 3:8). He argued that Israel had corrupted all five soul-levels (Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, Yechidah) corresponding to the four worlds of ABY"A and the crown of the Yud. He claimed that "asleep from the mitzvos" severed their Chayah and Yechidah; "scattered" severed their unified heart (Neshamah / Beriah); "their laws are diverse" severed their character traits (Ruach / Yetzirah); and "neither keep they the king's laws" corrupted concrete deeds (Nefesh / Asiyah). Presuming their holy moisture was entirely exhausted, Haman offered ten thousand talents of silver to substitute for Hashem's eternal promise never to destroy them.

p: אַרְבַּע מִצְוֹת יֵשׁ בְּפוּרִים: מִקְרָא מְגִלָּה, וּמִשְׁלוֹחַ מָנוֹת, וּמַתָּנוֹת לָאֶבְיוֹנִים, וּמִשְׁתֶּה וְשִׂמְחָה
There are four mitzvos on Purim: reading the Megillah, sending food portions, gifts to the poor, and festive feasting and rejoicing;
וְנִרְאֶה לִי שֶׁהֵם נֶגֶד אַרְבַּע אוֹתִיּוֹת שֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה בָּרוּךְ הוּא
and it appears to me that they correspond to the four letters of the Name Havayah, blessed be He,
דְּ״מִלְחָמָה לַה׳ בַּעֲמָלֵק מִדֹּר דֹּר״ (שְׁמוֹת י״ז:ט״ז)
regarding which it is said: "Hashem will have war with Amalek from generation to generation" (Shemos 17:16);
וְהַנִּצּוּחַ הוּא עַל יְדֵי אַרְבַּע מִצְוֹת מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת אֵלּוּ
and the victory is achieved through these four practical commandments;
דְּכָל מִצְוֹת שֶׁעוֹשִׂין לְזֵכֶר הַנֵּס, הוּא מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם כֹּחַ וְחַיּוּת שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה בִּשְׁעַת מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהָיָה הַיְשׁוּעָה בְּפֹעַל
for all commandments instituted to commemorate a miracle embody the spiritual power and divine vitality that were revealed at the very time the historical salvation occurred in practice;
וְעַל יְדֵי אוֹתָם מִצְוֹת מִתְגַּלֵּית אוֹתָהּ יְשׁוּעָה בְּפֹעַל בְּכָל דּוֹר
and through those commandments that selfsame salvation is revealed in actual deed in every single generation.
וְעִיקַּר הַיְשׁוּעָה הוּא כְּשֶׁנּוֹשָׁעִים בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם חִסָּרוֹן שֶׁמֵּחֲמָתוֹ בָּאָה הַצָּרָה
And the primary salvation is when they are redeemed through the very spiritual deficiency on account of which the affliction originally arose;
דְּזֶהוּ כָּל יְשׁוּעַת יִשְׂרָאֵל: יְשׁוּעַת הַנֶּפֶשׁ, וְלֹא יְשׁוּעַת הַגּוּפוֹת בִּלְבַד
for this is the essence of all salvation of Israel: the salvation of the soul, and not merely the rescue of the physical bodies;
וְכָל הַצָּרָה בָּא עַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁמִּזֶּה יִצְמַח הַיְשׁוּעָה
and the entire distress came about precisely so that from it the ultimate redemption would sprout;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״[כִּי אַעֲלֶה אֲרֻכָה לָךְ] וּמִמַּכּוֹתַיִךְ אֶרְפָּאֵךְ [נְאֻם ה׳]״ (יִרְמְיָה ל:יז)
as it is said: "For I will restore health unto you, and I will heal you out of your wounds, says Hashem" (Yirmiyah 30:17),
רָצָה לוֹמַר מֵהַמַּכּוֹת עַצְמָם וְעַל יָדָם הוּא הָרְפוּאָה
meaning from the very blows themselves, and through their agency, comes the cure;
וְכֵן ״מִשָּׁם יְקַבֶּצְךָ [ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ] וּמִשָּׁם יִקָּחֶךָ״ (דְּבָרִים ל:ד), הַיְינוּ מִשָּׁם דַּיְיקָא יִצְמַח הַקִּיבּוּץ וְשֶׁיִּקָּחֶךָ
and likewise "from there will Hashem your God gather you, and from there will He fetch you" (Devarim 30:4), meaning that precisely from there will sprout the ingathering and the taking;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּמְגִלָּה (י״ד עַמּוּד א׳): ״גְּדוֹלָה הֲסָרַת טַבַּעַת וְכוּלֵיהּ שֶׁהֶחֱזִירָתָן לְמוּטָב״
and as written in Megillah (14a): "Greater was the removal of Ahasuerus's signet ring than forty-eight prophets and seven prophetesses, for it returned them to the good path";
וְלָקְחוּ לְמָשָׁל זֶה בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ״ז עַמּוּד ב׳): ״מַעֲמִיד לָהֶם מֶלֶךְ קָשֶׁה כְּהָמָן״
and they cited this as a paradigm in Perek Chelek (Sanhedrin 97b): "Hashem sets up a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman";
דִּבִימֵי הָמָן שָׁבוּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵימָה וְקִבְּלוּ עַל עַצְמָם וְעַל זַרְעָם כָּל הַתּוֹרָה מֵאַהֲבָה
for in the days of Haman they returned in complete repentance and accepted upon themselves and their seed the entire Torah out of pure love (Shabbos 88a);
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַיְשׁוּעָה שֶׁהָיָה עַל יְדֵי גְּזֵירָה זוֹ: שֶׁזָּכוּ לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מֵאַהֲבָה וְשָׁבוּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵימָה, וּמִמֵּילָא נִתְבַּטְּלָה הַגְּזֵירָה

and this was the essential salvation produced through that decree: that they merited to accept words of Torah out of love and returned in complete repentance, whereby the decree was automatically annulled;
כִּי אֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר לְאַבְּדָם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם עוֹד, דַּאֲפִילּוּ צִפֳּרָא מִבַּלְעֲדֵי שְׁמַיָּא וְכוּלֵיהּ
for how would it be possible to destroy them, God forbid, any further, seeing that even a bird does not perish without the decree of Heaven (Yerushalmi Shevi'is 9:1)!
וְהַגְּזֵירָה הָיְתָה מֵה׳ בְּמִשְׁפָּט תְּחִלָּה
And the decree was originally issued from Hashem in strict justice;

וְאַף עַל פִּי כְּבָר הִבְטִיחַ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: ״וְאַף גַּם זֹאת בִּהְיוֹתָם [בְּאֶרֶץ אֹיְבֵיהֶם] לֹא [מְאַסְתִּים וְלֹא גְעַלְתִּים] לְכַלֹּתָם [לְהָפֵר בְּרִיתִי אִתָּם]״ (וַיִּקְרָא כ״ו:מ״ד), וְכֵן בְּכַמָּה מִקְרָאוֹת

even though the Blessed Name had already promised: "And yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly, to break My covenant with them" (Vayikra 26:44), and so in numerous biblical verses;
אֲבָל כְּבָר אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִלָּה י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳): ״לֵיכָּא דְּיָדַע לִישָׁנָא בִישָׁא כְּהָמָן״
yet the Sages of blessed memory already stated (Megillah 13b): "There was none who knew how to formulate malicious slander like Haman";
וְאִיתָא בְּמִדְרַשׁ אֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ג׳ (ז׳): דְּכָל ״מֶלֶךְ״ סְתָם [בַּמְּגִלָּה] — בְּמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הַלֵּל מְדַבֵּר

and it is taught in the Midrash Esther Rabbah (3:7) that wherever the Megillah mentions an unqualified "king," the text speaks homiletically of the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He;
אִם כֵּן כָּל דְּבָרָיו ״וְלַמֶּלֶךְ אֵין שֹׁוֶה [לְהַנִּיחָם]״ (אֶסְתֵּר ג:ח), ״אֶשְׁקוֹל עַל גִּנְזֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ״ (שָׁם:ט׳) הוּא כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה

if so, all of Haman's words—"therefore it is not for the king's profit to suffer them," "I will pay ten thousand talents of silver into the king's treasuries"—were directed upward against the Almighty.
וּתְחִלָּה קִטְרֵג עֲלֵיהֶם מֵחֲטָאֵיהֶם, כִּי כְּבָר קִלְקְלוּ לְגַמְרֵי כָּל קוֹמַת הָאָדָם שֶׁחָלוּק לְדָלֶ״ת שֶׁהֵם הֵ״א
And initially he prosecuted against them on account of their sins, asserting that they had already ruined entirely the whole stature of Man, which is divided into four that are five:
כִּידוּעַ חֲלוּקַת נֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם לְה׳ מַדְרֵיגוֹת: נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה, חַיָּה, יְחִידָה
as is known, the division of the human soul into five rungs: Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, and Yechidah (Bereishis Rabbah 14:9);
וְהֵם נֶגֶד אַרְבָּעָה עוֹלָמוֹת: אֲצִילוּת, בְּרִיאָה, יְצִירָה, עֲשִׂיָּה
corresponding to the four worlds of Atzilus, Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah;
וּבְסוֹד אַרְבַּע אוֹתִיּוֹת הַשֵּׁם וְקוּצּוֹ שֶׁל יוּ״ד
and in the mystical secret of the four letters of the Name (Havayah) and the tip of the letter Yud.
וְאָמַר: ״יֶשְׁנוֹ עַם אֶחָד״ (אֶסְתֵּר ג:ח) — ״שֶׁיְּשֵׁנִים מִן הַמִּצְוֹת״ (מְגִלָּה י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳)
And Haman said: "There is (yeshno) a certain people" (Esther 3:8)—which the Gemara expounds (Megillah 13b): "they are asleep (yashnu) from the commandments";
זֶהוּ נְפִילַת הַמּוֹחִין דִּבְעֵת הַשֵּׁינָה
this representing the falling of consciousness (nefilas ha-mochin) that occurs during sleep;
שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ טְהוֹרָה, וְהֵם חֶלְקֵי חַיָּה יְחִידָה דְּבָהֶם אֵין מְצִיאוּת שׁוּם פְּגָם
for although the soul within the brain is pure, and these upper faculties of Chayah and Yechidah admit no reality of blemish;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם טָעַן דִּכְבָר נִסְתַּלְּקוּ מֵהֶם לְגַמְרֵי וְאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת עוֹד עִמָּהֶם
nevertheless Haman claimed that these higher lights had completely departed from them and had no remaining connection with them.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר ״עַם אֶחָד״, לְרַמֵּז עַל חֵלֶק ״יְחִידָה״ הָרָמוּז בְּקוּצּוֹ שֶׁל יוּ״ד
And this is why he said "one (echad) people," alluding to the soul-level of Yechidah hinted in the thorn of the letter Yud,
דְּשָׁם אֵין שׁוּם חִילּוּק וּפֵירוּד כְּלָל בֵּין כְּלַל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
wherein there is no distinction or separation whatsoever among all the collective souls of Israel;
וְגַם שָׁם הוּא הַשֵּׁינָה וְהִסְתַּלְּקוּת אוֹתוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ
and even there, he argued, slumber and the withdrawal of that transcendent root had taken place.
״מְפֻזָּר וּמְפֹרָד״ (אֶסְתֵּר ג:ח) — הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵינָם בְּאַחְדוּת וְיֵשׁ בֵּינֵיהֶם פֵּירוּד לְבָבוֹת
"Dispersed and scattered" (Esther 3:8)—meaning that they are not in unity and there exists among them discord of hearts;
וְדָבָר זֶה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין הַלֵּב בִּשְׁלֵימוּת לִהְיוֹת דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא רָאוּי לְלִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
and this occurs because the heart is not in complete devotion cleaved unto the Blessed Name as is fitting for the heart of Israel,
דְּאָז הָיָה כָּל הַלְּבָבוֹת מְיוּחָדוֹת יַחַד וְלֹא הָיוּ פֵּירוּד כְּלָל
for then all hearts would be unified as one without any division whatsoever;
וּמִצַּד זֶה מַגִּיעַ הַפְּגָם לַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁהוּא מִכּוּרְסְיָין דְּעוֹלַם הַבְּרִיאָה
and from this deficiency a blemish reaches the Neshamah which derives from the Throne in the world of Beriah,
דְּשָׁם רוּבּוֹ טוֹב וּמְצִיאוּת מִיעוּט הָרָע הוּא רַק מִפְּנֵי שֶׁכְּבָר הִתְחִיל עָלְמָא דְּפֵירוּדָא שֶׁיֵּשׁ נִבְרָא נִפְרָד מֵהַבּוֹרֵא וְאֵין דָּבוּק לְגַמְרֵי

where the majority is good and the existence of a minority of evil arises only because the realm of separation (alma d'peruda) has begun, wherein a created being exists distinct from the Creator and is not completely cleaved.
״וְדָתֵיהֶם שֹׁנוֹת [מִכָּל עָם]״ (אֶסְתֵּר ג:ח) — הַיְינוּ נִימּוּסֵי עַצְמָם, שֶׁחָשַׁב שֶׁאֵינָם בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ שֶׁקָּדְמָה לַתּוֹרָה
"And their laws are diverse from every people" (Esther 3:8)—referring to their social conduct, Haman arguing that they lacked the ethical discipline (derech eretz) that preceded the Torah;
דְּהַיְינוּ הַנְּקִיּוּת בַּמִּדּוֹת שֶׁבָּהֶם נִתְחַכְּמוּ כָּל בַּעֲלֵי הַנִּימּוּסִים וְהַפִּילוֹסוֹפִים מֵהָאוּמּוֹת גַּם כֵּן לִהְיוֹת בַּעֲלֵי מִדּוֹת טוֹבוֹת
namely the refinement of moral character traits (middos), in which the ethicists and philosophers of the nations likewise exercised intellect to cultivate good traits,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ שְׁלֵימוּת כְּלַל גּוּף הָאָדָם וְכֹחוֹת הַגּוּפָנִים
which constitutes the ethical perfection of the human body and bodily faculties;
דִּידוּעַ דְּכָל הַמִּדּוֹת כְּלוּלִים בַּמִּדּוֹת הַיְּדוּעוֹת הָרְמוּזוֹת בְּשֵׁם [ז׳] דַּהֲוָיָ״ה
as is known, all character traits are included within the seven attributes alluded to in the Name Havayah,
שֶׁהוּא צוּרַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הַחֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת צוּרַת הָאָדָם
which corresponds to the form of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, engraved upon the Throne of Glory, representing the perfection of the form of Man.
וּבֶאֱמֶת: ״אַתֶּם קְרוּיִם ׳אָדָם׳ וְכוּלֵיהּ״ (יְבָמוֹת ס״א עַמּוּד א׳)
And in truth: "You are called 'Man' (Adam), and the nations are not called 'Man'" (Yevamos 61a);
שֶׁהָאוּמּוֹת אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת לִשְׁלֵימוּת הַמִּדּוֹת
for the nations possess no intrinsic connection to true perfection of character traits;
רַק שֶׁמִּצַּד צוּרָה הַגּוּפָנִית שֶׁלָּהֶם שֶׁהִיא גַּם כֵּן כִּדְמוּת אָדָם, הֲרֵי הֵם כְּקוֹף הָרוֹצֶה לְהִתְדַּמּוֹת לְאָדָם
but merely from the aspect of their bodily form which likewise resembles the human figure, they are like an ape that seeks to mimic a human being,
וַחֲפֵיצִים לְהִשְׁתַּלֵּם גַּם כֵּן בַּמִּדּוֹת, שֶׁבָּזֶה הוּא יִתְרוֹן הָאָדָם מִן הַבְּהֵמָה
aspiring to perfect themselves in character traits, in which lies the superiority of man over beast;
וְזֶהוּ נֶגֶד הָרוּחַ, כִּי נֶפֶשׁ יֵשׁ גַּם לַבְּהֵמָה שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה כֹּחַ הַמַּעֲשִׂים בְּפֹעַל
and this corresponds to the Ruach [the emotional faculty in Yetzirah], for a Nefesh belongs even to the beast whence derives the power of physical action,
אֲבָל רוּחַ וְרָצוֹן לַעֲשׂוֹת כָּךְ אוֹ כָךְ וְלִבְחוֹר בַּטּוֹב — זֶהוּ רַק בָּאָדָם
but a spirit (Ruach) and will to act in this manner or that and to choose the good exists only in man;
וְהֵם חוֹשְׁבִים שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְהִשְׁתַּלֵּם בָּזֶה
and the nations imagine that they can achieve consummate perfection in this;
וּבֶאֱמֶת כָּל הַמִּדּוֹת נוֹבְעוֹת מֵהַלֵּב, וְאֶצְלָם ״לֵב אָיִן״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ז:ט״ז) וְהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ חָסֵר
yet in truth all character traits flow from the heart, and within them "there is no heart" (Mishlei 17:16), the divine root being absent;
אֲבָל הָמָן חָשַׁב דִּלְאוּמּוֹת יֵשׁ שְׁלֵימוּת הַמִּדּוֹת מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
but Haman claimed that the nations possess ethical perfection while the Children of Israel do not!
״וְאֶת דָּתֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ אֵינָם עֹשִׂים״ (אֶסְתֵּר ג:ח) — הַיְינוּ מִצְוֹת הַתּוֹרָה בְּפֹעַל, שֶׁבָּזֶה נִפְגָּם הַנֶּפֶשׁ
"Neither keep they the king's laws" (Esther 3:8)—referring to the practical commandments of the Torah in deed, whereby the Nefesh [in Asiyah] is blemished;
בְּאֹפֶן שֶׁקִּטְרֵג שֶׁכְּבָר פָּגְמוּ וְקִלְקְלוּ כָּל קוֹמַת הַנֶּפֶשׁ
in such a manner that he prosecuted, alleging they had already blemished and ruined the entire structure of the soul,
עַד שֶׁאֵין לְמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים שֹׁוֶה וְשׁוּם הֲנָאָה לְהַנִּיחָם
so that it was no longer profitable or pleasing for the King of kings of kings to suffer them to remain.

וְעַל כֵּן ״אִם עַל הַמֶּלֶךְ טוֹב [יִכָּתֵב לְאַבְּדָם] וְגוֹמֵר״ (אֶסְתֵּר ג:ט) — רָצָה לוֹמַר: דְּיָדַע דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּבָר הִבְטִיחַ שֶׁלֹּא לְכַלּוֹתָם, עַל זֶה אָמַר שֶׁיִּשְׁקוֹל כֶּסֶף מְחִירָם

And therefore "If it please the king, let it be written that they be destroyed, etc." (Esther 3:9)—meaning: he knew that Hashem had promised never to destroy them utterly, and on this account he proposed to weigh ten thousand talents of silver to substitute for their worth;
כִּי מַה שֶּׁקִּטְרֵג לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים ״לְהַשְׁמִיד וְגוֹמֵר״, הַיְינוּ לֹא הַגּוּפוֹת לְבַד
for his accusation before the King of kings to destroy them referred not to the physical bodies alone;
כִּי אִם הָיָה חוֹשֵׁב שֶׁיֵּשׁ אֵיזֶה קְדוּשָׁה וְדָבָר טוֹב בְּנַפְשָׁם, וַדַּאי לֹא יִהְיֶה הַמִּשְׁפָּט לְכַלּוֹת הַגּוּפִים גַּם כֵּן
for had he thought that there remained any holiness or goodness in their souls, the divine judgment would certainly not have decreed the annihilation of their bodies either;
רַק שֶׁטָּעַן דְּאֵין בָּהֶם עוֹד שׁוּם נִיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשִׁים וְשֶׁיַּגִּיעַ הַמִּשְׁפָּט שֶׁיִּכְלוּ לְגַמְרֵי
but he claimed that there remained within them no holy sparks whatever, and that divine justice warranted their total obliteration;
וְהַהַבְטָחָה שֶׁלֹּא לְכַלּוֹתָם הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בָּהֶם לְעוֹלָם אֵיזֶה נִיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ שֶׁזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּכְלֶה מֵהֶם כְּלָל
whereas the divine promise never to destroy them presupposed that there would always endure within them an indestructible holy spark that could never be extinguished;
וְהוּא כְּפִי מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ הַמְזוֹהֶמֶת דִּמָּה שֶׁכְּבָר כָּלָה כָּל לַחְלוּחִית קְדוּשָׁה מֵהֶם
while Haman, in his defiled mind, imagined that all moisture of holiness had already vanished from them,
וְהַהַבְטָחָה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא הַבְטָחָה בְּעָלְמָא
and that the covenantal oath was merely an arbitrary promise;
וְאִם כֵּן הוּא דָּבָר שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לְהַחֲלִיפוֹ בְּדָבָר אַחֵר וְיִתְקַיֵּים הַהַבְטָחָה עַל אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר:
and if so, it was something that could be exchanged for another currency, fulfilling the promise upon that substitute!

6.h: The theme: Unconditional divine love versus earned reward and the clarification of Purim (ad d'lo yada). Haman knew the world cannot exist without righteous servants upon whom it stands ("on one pillar the world stands and Tzaddik is its name", Chagigah 12b). He envisioned that the nations would replace Israel, a delusion stemming from Esav’s hypocrisy and Amalek’s arrogance ("Whom would the king delight to honor more than myself?", Esther 6:6). Haman imagined that Hashem's choice of Israel is based on earned human exertion (b'chol me'odecha / money), offering ten thousand talents of silver to outbid them. The Midrash refutes this: "If a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned" (Shir HaShirim 8:7)—Hashem’s love for Israel is essential and unconditional (ahavah she-einah teluyah b'davar). Israel's root is unconditionally cleaved to Hashem; even when they sin, it is merely the external "yeast in the dough." When faced with death, they surrendered their souls and returned to Hashem with all their heart and might, restoring their spiritual stature: "The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honor" (Esther 8:16). "Light" (Orah) is the wisdom of the brain, commemorated through reading the Megillah. "Gladness" (Simchah) is the joy of the heart, commemorated through feasting and drinking. Haman accused them of feasting for selfish pleasure; Purim proved that an Israelite’s physical delight is innately consecrated for Heaven. Hence one is obligated to drink until he cannot distinguish between "Cursed be Haman" and "Blessed be Mordechai" (ad d'lo yada), revealing that even when conscious intention is suspended, a Jew's essence remains bound to Hashem.

p: וְהָעִנְיָן: דְּהוּא יָדַע דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָעוֹלָם בְּלֹא יִשְׂרָאֵל, הַיְינוּ צַדִּיקִים עוֹבְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דַּעֲלֵיהֶם הָעוֹלָם עוֹמֵד
And the explanation is: Haman knew that the universe cannot exist without Israel, meaning righteous servants of the Blessed Name upon whom the world stands,
וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב (חֲגִיגָה י״ב עַמּוּד ב׳): ״עַל עַמּוּד אֶחָד הָעוֹלָם עוֹמֵד, וְצַדִּיק שְׁמוֹ״
as written (Chagigah 12b): "Upon a single pillar the world stands, and Tzaddik is its name";
אֶלָּא שֶׁכְּבָר אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (תַּנְחוּמָא וַיֵּרָא ה׳): גָּלוּי לְפָנָיו דַּעֲתִידִין אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לְתַרְגֵּם הַתּוֹרָה וְלוֹמַר ״אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל״ וְכוּלֵיהּ
but the Sages already noted (Tanchuma, Vayeira 5) that it was revealed before Him that the nations of the world would translate the Torah and claim, "We are Israel";
וְעֵשָׂו בְּיִחוּד יֵשׁ לוֹ כֹּחַ זֶה דִּפְשִׁיטוּת טְלָפַיִם
and Esav in particular possesses this deceptive trait of displaying split hooves (Bereishis Rabbah 65:1);
וּמִמֶּנּוּ עֲמָלֵק עוֹד יוֹתֵר, שֶׁהוּא ״רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ד:כ׳)
and from him derives Amalek all the more so, being "the first of the nations" (Bamidbar 24:20);
וּמִמֶּנּוּ הָמָן שֶׁהוּא כָּל הַתַּמְצִית דַּעֲמָלֵק, שֶׁלֹּא קָם מִתְנַגֵּד לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְגַמְרֵי כָּמוֹהוּ
and from him emerged Haman who was the very extraction of Amalek, than whom no absolute adversary to Israel ever arose;
וּבוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחַ דִּמְיוֹן זֶה, בִּהְיוֹתוֹ ״זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:יד) נֶגֶד ״[כִּי] יַעֲקֹב בָּחַר לוֹ יָהּ״ (תְּהִלִּים קל״ה:ד׳)
and within him was the root of this delusion, standing as the direct antithesis to "For Hashem has chosen Jacob unto Himself" (Tehillim 135:4);
הוּא חוֹשֵׁב עַל עַצְמוֹ שֶׁבּוֹ בָּחַר ה׳
Haman imagining that he was the one whom Hashem chose,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר: ״לְמִי יַחְפֹּץ הַמֶּלֶךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת יְקָר [יוֹתֵר מִמֶּנִּי]״ (אֶסְתֵּר ו:ו), וְהַמֶּלֶךְ סְתָם הוּא מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים
as he said in his heart: "To whom would the king delight to do honor more than to myself?" (Esther 6:6), the "king" referring homiletically to the King of kings;
וְחָשַׁב דְּהוּא הַיּוֹתֵר נִבְחָר אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִכָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
assuming that he was more chosen by the Blessed Name than the entire world!
רַק שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת הוּא מָלֵא זוּהֲמָא וְטוּמְאָה וְכָל מַחְשְׁבוֹתָיו לְגַרְמֵיהּ, וְשֶׁבְּחִירַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא רַק לַעֲשׂוֹת יְקָר וּגְדוּלָּה
Except that in truth he was filled with defilement and self-centered pleasure (l'garmei), imagining that divine election is merely a means to achieve personal honor and aggrandizement;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל: כָּל מַה שֶּׁמּוֹסִיף לָהֶם גְּדוּלָּה — מַקְטִינִין עַצְמָן, כִּמְשַׁאזַ״ל (חֻלִּין פ״ט עַמּוּד א׳)
unlike the Children of Israel: the more greatness Hashem gives them, the more they humble themselves, as the Sages stated (Chullin 89a);
וְכָל חֶפְצָם בִּבְחִירַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּהֶם, הַיְינוּ לְקָרְבָם לַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
and their entire desire in being chosen is to draw near to His sacred service;
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַבְּחִירָה בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁכָּל שֶׁהוּא גָּדוֹל יוֹתֵר וּמַשִּׂיג יוֹתֵר — הוּא מַכִּיר יוֹתֵר שְׁפַל עֶרְכּוֹ וּמַקְטִין עַצְמוֹ יוֹתֵר
and this is the true hallmark of divine election in Israel: the greater and more perceptive one is, the more he recognizes his lowliness and humbles himself,
כִּי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁכָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם, וְרַק מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חֲנָנוֹ הַכֹּל בְּחֶסֶד חִנָּם
knowing that all his human striving is nothing, and that the Blessed Name bestowed everything upon him out of unearned grace;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם רֹאשׁ אוּמָּתֵנוּ: ״קָטֹנְתִּי מִכֹּל הַחֲסָדִים [וּמִכָּל הָאֱמֶת]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״ב:י״א)
as Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, the head of our nation, said: "I am not worthy of the least of all the mercies, and of all the truth" (Bereishis 32:11);
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר ״וָאֶתְחַנַּן״ (דְּבָרִים ג:כג), שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ מַתְּנַת חִנָּם (רַשִׁ״י שָׁם)
and Moshe Rabbeinu said: "And I besought (va'eschanan) Hashem" (Devarim 3:23), asking for an unearned gift (Rashi ibid.).
אֲבָל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם חוֹשְׁבִים שֶׁמִּשְׁתַּדְּלִים, וּמַה שֶּׁהוּא מַשִּׂיג אֵיזֶה דָּבָר וּשְׁלֵימוּת הוּא מִצַּד הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ, וְאֵין קֵץ לַגְּמוּל הַמַּגִּיעַ לוֹ עַל זֶה
But the nations of the world imagine that their attainments derive from their own exertion, and that boundless reward is deservedly due them;
וְחוֹשְׁבִים שֶׁבְּחִירַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא מִצַּד הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת, וְשֶׁגַּם הֵם יְכוֹלִים לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל וְאָז הֵם ״יִשְׂרָאֵל״
assuming that divine election is earned through exertion, and that by striving they too can claim to be "Israel";
וְזֶהוּ הַכֶּסֶף שֶׁאָמַר לִשְׁקוֹל, דְּהַיְינוּ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת דִּ״בְכָל מְאֹדֶךָ״ (דְּבָרִים ו:ה)
and this was the silver Haman offered to weigh out, representing striving with "all your might" (b'chol me'odecha / money).

אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ עַל זֶה בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ח:ד): ״׳אִם יִתֵּן אִישׁ אֶת כָּל הוֹן בֵּיתוֹ בָּאַהֲבָה׳ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ח:ז) — בָּאַהֲבָה שֶׁאוֹהֵב הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, ׳בּוֹז יָבוּזוּ לוֹ׳ (שָׁם)״

But in truth, they expounded upon this in the Midrash (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 8:4): "'If a man would give all the substance of his house for love' (Shir HaShirim 8:7)—for the love wherewith the Holy One loves Israel—'he would utterly be contemned'";
הַיְינוּ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאוֹהֲבִים אֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל מְאֹדָם, אֵינוֹ בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁיֹּאהֲבֵם כְּלָל, רַק שֶׁהֵם בְּעֶצֶם יֵשׁ לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת וְדִיבּוּק לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
meaning that when Israel love the Blessed Name with all their might, it is not in order that He love them in return, but because they possess an essential connection and cleaving unto Him;
וְהֵם אוֹהֲבִים אוֹתוֹ בְּלֹא סִבָּה וְתוֹעֶלֶת עַצְמָם, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹהֲבָם גַּם כְּשֶׁאֵין שֹׁוֶה וַהֲנָאָה מַגִּיעַ לוֹ כְּלָל
loving Him without external cause or selfish motive, and likewise He loves them even when no profit or pleasure reaches Him;
אֲבָל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם הוּא בִּשְׁבִיל הָאַהֲבָה שֶׁיֹּאהֲבֵם
whereas the nations strive solely so that He love them;
וְדָבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם, וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (ד׳ עַמּוּד א׳) שֶׁבְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם נִקְרָא אֲפִילּוּ רָשָׁע עַל זֶה וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָא צַדִּיק גָּמוּר

and such conditional striving amounts to nothing, as written in Rosh Hashanah (4a) that an idolater who acts on condition of reward is considered wicked, while an Israelite is termed a complete tzaddik;
לְפִי שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ מִתְכַּוֵּין עַל מְנָת לְקַבֵּל פְּרָס, אֵין זֶה עִיקַּר כַּוָּונָתוֹ רַק טָפֵל
because even if an Israelite intends to receive a reward, that is not his primary intent but merely secondary,
וְגַם אִם לֹא יִתְּנוּ לוֹ שׁוּם פְּרָס יֵהָנֶה מִזֶּה עַצְמוֹ שֶׁעָשָׂה רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and even if no reward be given, he delights in the sheer fact that he performed the will of the Blessed Name;
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקְּדוּשָׁה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאֵין נִיתֶּקֶת מֵהֶם לְעוֹלָם, עַד שֶׁעַל כֵּן אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְכַלּוֹתָם
and this is the root holiness of Israel that can never be severed, wherefore it is impossible to destroy them.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיִּזְדַּמֵּן שֶׁיְּשֵׁנִים מֵהַמִּצְוֹת וְחוֹטְאִים גַּם כֵּן, הַיְינוּ הַכֹּל רַק מִצַּד הַהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְלֹא מִצַּד שָׁרְשָׁם
And even when they are asleep from the commandments and stumble in sin, that occurs solely from immersion in this physical world and not from their essential root.
וְהַבֵּירוּר הוּא: דִּבְהָצֵר לָהֶם הֵם חוֹזְרִים לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרוֹאִים שֶׁהוּא מֵצֵר לָהֶם
And the proof of this is: when distress strikes them, they return unto the Blessed Name even though seeing that He is the One afflicting them;
וְעַל כֵּן בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם: ״וְהָיָה כִי יִרְעַב וְהִתְקַצַּף וְקִלֵּל [בְּמַלְכּוֹ וּבֵאלֹהָיו] וְגוֹמֵר״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ח:כא)
wherefore among the nations it is written: "and it shall come to pass, that when they shall be hungry, they shall fret themselves, and curse by their king and by their God" (Yeshayah 8:21);
אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁאֵין כַּוָּונָתָם לְקַבֵּל פְּרָס רַק אוֹהֲבִים בְּעֶצֶם לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, אֶלָּא שֶׁהַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה מַשְׁכִּיחָם
whereas Israel love the Blessed Name in their very essence, the "yeast in the dough" merely causing temporary forgetfulness;
וּבְהֵיצֵר, וּבִפְרָט כְּשֶׁהָיוּ מוּכָנִים לֵיהָרֵג דְּהוּתַּשׁ כֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר, שָׁבוּ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל לְבָבָם וּבְכָל נַפְשָׁם וּבְכָל מְאֹדָם
and when distress arrived, especially when facing death, the power of the yetzer was shattered and they returned unto the Blessed Name with all their heart, soul, and might.
וְאָז: ״לַיְּהוּדִים הָיְתָה אוֹרָה וְשִׂמְחָה וְשָׂשֹׂן וִיקָר״ (אֶסְתֵּר ח:טז), דְּשָׁבוּ לָהֶם כָּל הַמַּדְרֵיגוֹת
And then: "The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honor" (Esther 8:16), all spiritual levels returning unto them (Megillah 16b):
״אוֹרָה״ — זוֹ תּוֹרָה וְחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ, וְנֶגְדָּהּ עוֹשִׂין לַדּוֹרוֹת מִצְוַת מִקְרָא מְגִלָּה דִּקְרוּיָה ״סֵפֶר״ כַּאֲמִתָּהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִין לְאוֹרָה

"Light" (Orah)—this is Torah and the wisdom of the brain, opposite which we perform through all generations the reading of the Megillah which is termed a Sefer like the truth of the Torah, meriting light through it;

״וְשִׂמְחָה״ — הוּא בַּלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״[נָתַתָּה] שִׂמְחָה בְלִבִּי״ (תְּהִלִּים ד:ח), ״וּבְשִׂמְחָתוֹ [לֹא יִתְעָרַב זָר]״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ד:י׳), וְנֶאֱמַר: ״לֵב שָׂמֵחַ [יֵיטִב גֵּהָה]״ (שָׁם י״ז:כ״ב), ״וּלְיִשְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה״ (תְּהִלִּים צ״ז:י״א), וְזָכוּ לְיִשְׁרַת לֵב וְשִׂמְחָה

and "Gladness" (Simchah)—this is in the heart, as written: "You have put gladness in my heart" (Tehillim 4:8), "and a stranger does not intermeddle with its joy" (Mishlei 14:10), "a merry heart is a good medicine" (ibid. 17:22), and "and gladness for the upright in heart" (Tehillim 97:11), meriting uprightness of heart and joy;
וְעַל זֶה הוּא מִצְוַת שִׂמְחָה וּמִשְׁתֶּה
and toward this points the mitzvah of festive joy and feasting.
וְהָמָן הָיָה מְקַטְרֵג עַל זֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (אֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה ז:יב) שֶׁאָמַר: ״אוֹכְלִין וְשׁוֹתִין וְאוֹמְרִים ׳עֹנֶג שַׁבָּת׳, ׳עֹנֶג יוֹם טוֹב׳״
And Haman had prosecuted against this, as written in the Midrash (Esther Rabbah 7:12) that he complained: "They eat and drink and say: 'this is the delight of Shabbos, the delight of Yom Tov'!";

הַיְינוּ דְּאֵצֶל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לַעֲשׂוֹת דָּבָר שֶׁל הֲנָאַת עַצְמָם לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, כֵּיוָן דְּהֵם כָּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ כַּוָּונָתָם הוּא רַק הֲנָאַת עַצְמָם, וְ״כָל טִיבוּ דְּעָבְדִין — לְגַרְמַיְיהוּ״ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא י׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)

meaning that among the nations it is impossible to perform an act of bodily pleasure for the sake of Heaven, since their root intent is purely self-serving: "all the kindness that they do is for themselves" (Bava Batra 10b);
וַאֲפִילּוּ מַה שֶּׁעוֹשִׂין לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם הוּא לְקַבֵּל פְּרָס וּלְהַנָּאָתָן
and even what they ostensibly perform for Heaven is to receive reward for their own benefit;
