אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם גּוּף הַמַּעֲשֶׂה אֵינוֹ הֲנָאָה חוֹשְׁבִים דְּזֶה נִקְרָא לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, אֲבָל כְּשֶׁגּוּף הַמַּעֲשֶׂה גַּם כֵּן הֲנָאָתָן, מַה לְּשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם יֵשׁ בָּזֶה
only that when the bodily action itself involves no physical pleasure they consider it "for Heaven," but when the act itself is pleasurable, what aspect of Heaven could exist in it?
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שׁוֹרֶשׁ כַּוָּונָתָם לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא לַהֲנָאָתָן כְּלָל, וַאֲפִילּוּ מְכַוֵּין הֲנָאָה וְקַבָּלַת פְּרָס אֵין זֶה הָעִיקָּר אֶצְלוֹ
But in truth, within the Children of Israel the root intent is for the sake of Heaven without self-interest, and even when one consciously anticipates reward that is not the essential core;
וְאִם כֵּן אֲפִילּוּ גּוּף הַמַּעֲשֶׂה גַּם כֵּן הֲנָאָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַהֲנָאָה טְפֵלָה אֶצְלָם וְעִיקַּר הַכַּוָּונָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם לֹא נִתְבַּטְּלָה עַל יְדֵי זֶה
and if so, even when the bodily action itself is pleasurable, the physical pleasure is secondary and the core dedication to Heaven is not annulled;
דַּאֲפִילּוּ שֶׁיִּתְבַּטֵּל אַחַר כָּךְ הַהֲנָאָה, הוּא חוֹשֵׁק לָזֶה עַצְמוֹ שֶׁל עֲשִׂיָּה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם לְבַד
for even were the bodily pleasure subsequently removed, he yearns for the fulfillment of the divine will alone;
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַהֶבְדֵּל בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר בְּפוּרִים
and this was the fundamental distinction between Israel and the nations that was clarified on Purim.
וְעַל כֵּן עִיקָּרָם נִקְרָא ״יְמֵי מִשְׁתֶּה וְשִׂמְחָה״ (אֶסְתֵּר ט:כב), וְ״חַיָּיב לִבְסוֹמֵי עַד דְּלֹא יָדַע וְכוּלֵיהּ״ (מְגִלָּה ז׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
And therefore these days are termed "days of feasting and gladness" (Esther 9:22), and "one is obligated to become intoxicated until he cannot distinguish" (Megillah 7b);
דְּאָז וַדַּאי אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם כַּוָּונָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, אֶלָּא דִּסְתָמָן לִשְׁמָן קָיְימֵי אֵצֶל זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֵין צָרִיךְ כְּלָל לְכַוָּונָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
for then he certainly lacks conscious intent for Heaven, yet among the seed of Israel their actions are intrinsically consecrated (staman lishmah qaymei), requiring no conscious intention;
כִּי הֵם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם שֶׁשָּׁרְשָׁם תָּקוּעַ בָּזֶה, וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּלֹא כַּוָּונָתָם:
for all their deeds are directed toward Heaven, their soul-root being firmly planted in this holiness, even without their conscious thought!

6.h: The theme: The esoteric correspondence of "gladness" (Sasson) to circumcision and Mishloach Manot, and "honor" (Yakar) to Tefillin and Matanot LaEvyonim. The Talmud expounds "and gladness—this is circumcision" (Megillah 16b), which represents the perfection of moral traits terminating in Yesod through guarding the covenant of sexual purity (geder ervah). The generation of the Flood breached this boundary and was eradicated; for Israel, circumcision was granted to Avraham Avinu prior to the Torah as the primary foundation of the nation, an inborn trait whereby even uncircumcised Israelites are legally called circumcised (Nedarim 31a). The generational continuation of this inner trait is channeled through Mishloach Manot: while gentiles appear benevolent on the surface, their love is rooted in self-interest (l'garmei); Israel performs mutual love purely for the sake of Heaven. "And honor—these are Tefillin" (Megillah 16b), representing the perfection of concrete deed, binding head and hand to Hashem's commandments. Flawless action is exceedingly precious and rare in this world ("there is not a righteous man upon earth that does good and sins not", Koheles 7:20); yet Hashem testifies that Israel are "all righteous" because their deeds are directed for Heaven. This is continued through Matanot LaEvyonim (charity, termed simply mitzvah), which is fulfilled on Purim by giving to everyone who stretches out a hand, elevating all four mitzvos to complete the Divine Name Havayah, banish the illusions of the yetzer, and conquer Amalek.

p: וְ״שָׂשֹׂן״ (אֶסְתֵּר ח:טז) — זוֹ מִילָה (מְגִלָּה ט״ז עַמּוּד ב׳), הַיְינוּ שְׁלֵימוּת הַמִּדּוֹת שֶׁשָּׁרְשָׁם וְסִיּוּמָם בִּיסוֹד
And "and gladness" (Esther 8:16)—this is circumcision (Megillah 16b), meaning the perfection of character traits whose root and culmination reside in Yesod;
דְּזֶהוּ עִיקַּר שְׁלֵימוּתָן בִּשְׁמִירַת גֶּדֶר עֶרְוָה
for this is their primary perfection: in guarding the fence against sexual immorality;
דְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל שֶׁפָּרְצוּ בוֹ, יָצְאוּ מִכְּלַל מִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ הַקּוֹדֶמֶת לַתּוֹרָה וְנֶאֶבְדוּ מִן הָאָרֶץ
for the generation of the Flood, who breached this boundary, departed from the scope of ethical discipline (derech eretz) that preceded the Torah, and were obliterated from the earth;
וְעַל כֵּן זֶהוּ הָאוֹת לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְלֹא נִקְרָא הָעָרְלָה אֶלָּא עַל שֵׁם אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
wherefore this is the covenantal sign for the Children of Israel, and the foreskin is designated solely upon the name of the nations of the world (Nedarim 31b),
דְּלָהֶם אֵין שְׁלֵימוּת בָּזֶה כְּלָל דְּאֵין קְרוּיִן ״אָדָם״ (יְבָמוֹת ס״א עַמּוּד א׳)
who possess no perfection in this realm at all, not being termed "Adam" (Yevamos 61a);
וְנִיתַּן לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הַמִּצְוָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁל בִּנְיַן אוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית
and circumcision was given unto Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, prior to the Giving of the Torah as the first commandment forming the Israelite nation,
שֶׁהוּא כְּמוֹ הַדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ שֶׁקָּדַם לַתּוֹרָה
which is like the natural moral discipline that preceded the Torah.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּתוֹלָדָה
And this quality is ingrained within the Children of Israel by birth;
שֶׁהֲרֵי אֲפִילּוּ עַרְלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרְאוּ מוּלִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (נְדָרִים ל״א עַמּוּד א׳)
for behold, even uncircumcised Israelites are termed "circumcised," as written in Nedarim (31a);
שֶׁכְּבָר נוֹלְדוּ מִזֶּרַע אַבְרָהָם, יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב הַנִּימּוֹלִים, וְהֵם שָׁרְשָׁם כָּךְ, וְאָז נִתְבָּרַר זֶה
having already been born of the circumcised seed of Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov, such being their essential root, and then [in the days of Mordechai] this was clarified;
וְהַמְשָׁכַת גִּלּוּי אוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָׁה לַדּוֹרוֹת הוּא עַל יְדֵי מִשְׁלוֹחַ מָנוֹת אִישׁ לְרֵעֵהוּ
and the generational channeling of that holiness across time is accomplished through sending food portions one to another (Mishloach Manot);
דְּדָבָר זֶה הוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הַמִּדּוֹת שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן, דְּגֶדֶר עֶרְוָה וּקְדֻשַּׁת הַבְּרִית אֵין בָּהֶם כְּלָל

for interpersonal benevolence is the apparent perfection of character traits that seems to exist among the nations of the world, seeing that the fence of chastity and the sanctity of the covenant do not exist within them at all.
כִּי כְּלַל שְׁתֵּי הַמִּדּוֹת הֵם חֲלוּקוֹת לִשְׁתַּיִם נֶגֶד שְׁתֵּי הַקְּצוֹת, חֶסֶד וּגְבוּרָה
For the general emotional attributes divide into two, corresponding to the two opposite poles of Chesed [kindness] and Gevurah [severity],
שֶׁמִּפְּסֹולְתָּם נִמְשָׁךְ שְׁתֵּי הַיְּצָרִים דְּקִנְאָה וְתַאֲוָה, וְהֵם שְׁתֵּי הֲפָכִים
from whose dross are drawn the two inclinations of envy and lust, which are opposites:
דְּמִי שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל תַּאֲוָה הוּא טוֹב לַבְּרִיּוֹת
for one who is inclined toward desire is sociable and benevolent toward creatures;
וְזֶהוּ אֵצֶל הָאוּמּוֹת, יֵשׁ לְמַרְאִית עַיִן מִי שֶׁעֵינוֹ טוֹבָה לַבְּרִיּוֹת וְיֵשׁ לוֹ אַהֲבָה לָהֶם
and this is found among the nations, where to outward appearances there are individuals who possess a generous eye and affection toward people;
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן מִצְוַת מִשְׁלוֹחַ מָנוֹת, לוֹמַר דְּגַם זֶה הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת רַק בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד
and this is the purpose of the mitzvah of Mishloach Manot: to demonstrate that true altruistic benevolence exists in truth only within Israel alone;
דְּהָאַהֲבָה וְעַיִן טוֹבָה שֶׁלָּהֶם לְרֵיעֵיהֶם הוּא גַּם כֵּן רַק לְאֵיזֶה כַּוָּונָה לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמָם, כְּאַהֲבַת נָשִׁים
for among the nations, affection and goodwill toward companions are motivated by personal gratification, like the physical love of women;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁעוֹשִׂין גַּם זֹאת רַק לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
unlike Israel, who perform even social kindness purely for the sake of Heaven,
וּמִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צִוָּה עַל זֶה אוֹ שֶׁחֲכָמֵינוּ צִוּוּ עַל זֶה, וְהַכֹּל רַק לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּלְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם:
because the Blessed Name commanded it or our Sages commanded it, all solely to fulfill the will of the Blessed Name for the sake of Heaven.
וְ״יָקָר״ (אֶסְתֵּר ח:טז) — זוֹ תְּפִלִּין (מְגִלָּה ט״ז עַמּוּד ב׳), הַיְינוּ שְׁלֵימוּת הַמַּעֲשִׂים
And "and honor (yakar)" (Esther 8:16)—these are Tefillin (Megillah 16b), meaning the perfection of concrete physical actions;
מַה שֶּׁנּוֹשְׂאִין עֲלֵיהֶם עוֹל מִצְוֹת, זֶהוּ מִצְוַת תְּפִלִּין
that which they accept upon themselves the yoke of the commandments, this being embodied in the mitzvah of Tefillin,
שֶׁמְּקַשְּׁרִין הָרֹאשׁ שֶׁהוּא רֹאשׁ הַגּוּף, וְהַיָּד שֶׁהוּא כְּלִי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וְהַפְּעֻלָּה
binding the head which is the crown of the body, and the arm which is the instrument of concrete action,
יִהְיֶה קָשׁוּר וּמְשׁוּעְבָּד לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּלְעוֹל הַמִּצְוֹת הָאֲמוּרִים בְּפָרָשִׁיּוֹתֵיהֶן
that it be bound and subjugated unto the Blessed Name and the yoke of the commandments written in their scriptural passages;
שֶׁעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״וּקְשַׁרְתָּם [לְאוֹת עַל יָדֶךָ וְהָיוּ לְטֹטָפֹת בֵּין עֵינֶיךָ]״ (דְּבָרִים ו:ח)
concerning which it is said: "And you shall bind them for a sign upon your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes" (Devarim 6:8),
רָצָה לוֹמַר עוֹל הַמִּצְוֹת יִהְיוּ קְשׁוּרִים לְאוֹת וּלְזִכָּרוֹן שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁכָּחֵם
meaning that the yoke of the commandments shall be bound as a sign and remembrance that you never forget them.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא ״יָקָר״ — דָּבָר יָקָר, כִּי הַשְּׁלֵימוּת בְּמַעֲשִׂים הוּא דָּבָר יָקָר מְאֹד בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And this attainment is yakar—a precious, rare thing (davar yakar), for perfection in action is exceedingly precious and scarce in this world;
דְּ״[כִּי אָדָם] אֵין צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה [טּוֹב וְלֹא יֶחֱטָא]״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כ)
for "there is not a righteous man upon earth that does good, and sins not" (Koheles 7:20);
אֶלָּא דִּלַיְּהוּדִים הָיְתָה זֶה דְּ״עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ס:כא), שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָעִיד עֲלֵיהֶם שֶׁכָּל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
except that for the Jews this unfolded: that "Your people are all righteous" (Yeshayah 60:21), the Blessed Name testifying upon them that all their actions are for the sake of Heaven;
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן עֵדוּת הַתְּפִלִּין, דְּ״שֵׁם ה׳ נִקְרָא עָלֶיךָ וְיָרְאוּ מִמֶּךָּ״ (דְּבָרִים כ״ח:י׳; בְּרָכוֹת ו׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
and this is likewise the testimony of Tefillin, that "the Name of Hashem is called upon you, and they shall be afraid of you" (Devarim 28:10; Berachos 6a);
דְּהָאוּמּוֹת עַצְמָן יוֹדְעִים שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם שׁוּם שְׁלֵימוּת בְּמַעֲשִׂים כְּלָל וְאֵין מִתְפָּאֲרִים אֶלָּא בִּשְׁלֵימוּת בַּמִּדּוֹת
for the nations themselves know that they possess no true perfection in actions whatsoever, boasting only of ethical character traits;
וּתְפִלִּין דְּמָארֵי עָלְמָא כְּתִיב בְּהוּ: ״[וּ]מִי כְּעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹי אֶחָד [בָּאָרֶץ]״ (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א י״ז:כ״א), דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵעִיד עַל כֵּן

while in the Tefillin of the Master of the Universe it is written: "And who is like Your people Israel, a nation one in the earth" (I Divrei HaYamim 17:21; Berachos 6a), the Blessed Name Himself testifying thus;
וְזֶה הָיָה הַבֵּירוּר אָז מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהֵעִיד עֲלֵיהֶם כֵּן:
and this was the revelation then on the part of the Blessed Name, Who testified concerning them in this manner.
וְהַהַמְשָׁכָה לַדּוֹרוֹת בְּפֹעַל הוּא בְּמִצְוַת מַתָּנוֹת לָאֶבְיוֹנִים
And the generational continuation of this in actual practice is channeled through the mitzvah of gifts to the poor (Matanot LaEvyonim);
כִּידוּעַ דִּצְדָקָה נִקְרָא סְתָם ״מִצְוָה״ בְּכָל מָקוֹם בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ל״ד:ח׳)
as is known, charity is termed the unqualified "mitzvah" everywhere in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 34:8);
וְכָל צְדָקָה וָחֶסֶד שֶׁאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם עוֹשִׂין הוּא לְגַרְמֵיהּ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (י׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) דְּהוּא ״חַטָּאת״ לָהֶם
and all charity and kindness that the nations of the world perform is for their own self-interest, and as written in Bava Batra (10b) it is accounted a "sin" unto them (Mishlei 14:34);
וְהִיא לְבַדָּהּ מִצְוָה שֶׁיֶּשְׁנָהּ גַּם אֵצֶל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, וְאֶצְלָם הוּא חַטָּאת וְאֵצֶל יִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא מִצְוָה
and charity is the unique commandment practiced likewise among the nations, yet with them it is a sin while with Israel it is a holy mitzvah;
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא ״מִצְוָה״ סְתָם, וְהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְכָל הַמִּצְוֹת מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת
wherefore it is termed "mitzvah" unconditionally, standing as the root of all practical commandments.
וְצָרִיךְ לָזֶה סַיַּיעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֻכָּה (מ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דְּלָא כָּל הָרוֹצֶה לִקְפּוֹץ קוֹפֵץ... ׳מַה יָּקָר חַסְדְּךָ [אֱלֹהִים]׳ (תְּהִלִּים ל״ו:ח׳)״

And for true charity one requires divine assistance, as written in Sukkah (49b): "Not everyone who wishes to jump forward [to perform charity] can jump... 'How precious (yakar) is Your lovingkindness, O God' (Tehillim 36:8)";
שֶׁזֶּה דָּבָר יָקָר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁלֹּא כָּל מַה שֶּׁאָדָם חוֹשֵׁב שֶׁהוּא מִצְוָה הִיא מִצְוָה, רַק צָרִיךְ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָעִיד עָלָיו שֶׁהוּא מִצְוָה
for it is a precious, rare thing in this world, seeing that not everything a person presumes to be a mitzvah is genuinely a mitzvah, requiring the Blessed Name to testify that it was pure;
וּבְפוּרִים, דְּ״כָל הַפּוֹשֵׁט יָד — נוֹתְנִים לוֹ״ (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא ע״ח עַמּוּד ב׳; יְרוּשַׁלְמִי מְגִלָּה פֶּרֶק א׳ הֲלָכָה ד׳), הֲרֵי הַכֹּל מִצְוָה
while on Purim, where the rule is: "Whoever stretches out a hand, we give to him" (Bava Metzia 78b; Yerushalmi Megillah 1:4), behold every gift is a certified mitzvah;
וְאֵינוֹ דָּבָר יָקָר אָז כְּלָל, כֵּיוָן דְּכָךְ הַמִּצְוָה בְּפֵירוּשׁ לִיתֵּן לְכָל הַפּוֹשֵׁט יָד וְהַכֹּל נֶחְשָׁב לְמִצְוָה
and it is not an elusive, rare thing at all on that day, since the halachic commandment explicitly dictates giving to whoever stretches forth a hand, all gifts being reckoned a mitzvah;
עַל כֵּן עַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִים לְ״יָקָר״ זֶה שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שְׁלֵימוּת הַמִּצְוֹת:
therefore through this we merit that very "honor" (yakar) achieved through the perfection of the commandments.
וּבָזֶה נִשְׁתַּלֵּם שֵׁם הַהֲוָיָ״ה בְּקוֹמַת הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַדְּבֵקִים בְּשֵׁם הַהֲוָיָ״ה
And through this the Name Havayah is perfected within the stature of the souls of Israel who cleave unto the Name Havayah;
וְנַעֲשֵׂית הַמִּלְחָמָה בַּעֲמָלֵק וּמְחִיָּתוֹ בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר בְּפוּרִים עַל יְדֵי הַמִּצְוֹת שֶׁבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂים בּוֹ
and the war against Amalek and his eradication is accomplished in every generation on Purim through the commandments that the Children of Israel perform on it;
וּפוֹעֲלִים לְהוֹצִיא דִּמְיוֹנוֹת מֵהַלֵּב וּמוֹחַ עַל יְדֵי הָאוֹרָה, דִּ״מְעַט מֵהָאוֹר דּוֹחֶה הַרְבֵּה מִן הַחֹשֶׁךְ״, שֶׁהוּא הַדִּמְיוֹן וְהַשִּׂמְחָה
working to purge illusions from the heart and mind through "Light," for "a little light expels much darkness," darkness being the false imagination, and through "Gladness";
דְּהַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת בָּא מֵעַצְלוּת וְשֵׁינָה וְתַרְדֵּימַת מַחְשְׁבוֹת הָאֲמִתִּיּוֹת
for fantasies arise from indolence, slumber, and the dormancy of truthful thoughts;
וְהַהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת וְהַשִּׂמְחָה מוֹלֶדֶת זְרִיזוּת וְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת
while contemplation and holy joy generate alacrity and spiritual awakening;
וְ״שָׂשׂוֹן״ וְ״יָקָר״ הֵם הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת הַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת הַנִּכְנָסוֹת אַחַר כָּךְ וְנִמְשָׁכוֹת מֵהָאוֹרָה וְהַשִּׂמְחָה
and "Gladness" (Sasson) and "Honor" (Yakar) are the holy thoughts that subsequently enter, drawn from Light and Joy;
וּלְהַמְשִׁיךְ גַּם כֵּן בְּכָל כֹּחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה וְהַמַּעֲשִׂים עַצְמָן קְדוּשָׁה וְכַוָּונָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם בְּכָל דָּבָר:
and to channel into all faculties of action and concrete deeds themselves holiness and pure intention for the sake of Heaven in all things.

7.h: The theme: The Four Parshiyot as the four letters of the Tetragrammaton and the mystery of Parashat Shekalim. The Four Special Portions read in Adar (Shekalim, Zachor, Parah, Hachodesh) correspond to the four letters of Havayah. The two portions read prior to Purim (Shekalim and Zachor) parallel the first two letters (Yud-Hei), through which the World to Come and this world were created (Menachos 29b). The letter Yud embodies thought (machshavah) and the World to Come, which arose in thought and remains concealed; every Jew possesses a portion in the World to Come because in the deepest recesses of the heart Hashem is the "rock of their heart" (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2). All divine punishments are the natural byproduct of the sin itself ("the reward of a transgression is a transgression", Avos 4:2; Bava Batra 16a). Faith in the World to Come is a cardinal foundation of Judaism: he who believes in it is the "Israelite saved by Hashem," enabling one to remember the day of death not with despair (like the nations who say "let us eat and drink for tomorrow we die", Yeshayah 22:13), but as an incentive to return to Hashem. In Ki Tisa, the census counts each individual separately, exposing the individual to the scrutiny of the prosecuting Satan, who gains dominion when souls are itemized rather than joined in an aggregate community (agudah achat). To nullify this vulnerability, the Torah gives the half-shekel (machatzis ha-shekel), representing the letter Yud (ten gerahs) and the shofar's simple, unified sound that silences and confuses the Satan.

p: אַרְבַּע פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת נִרְאֶה לִי שֶׁהֵם נֶגֶד אַרְבַּע אוֹתִיּוֹת שֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה בָּרוּךְ הוּא
The Four Portions (Arba Parshiyot) appear to me to correspond to the four letters of the Name Havayah, blessed be He;
שְׁתַּיִם לִפְנֵי פוּרִים, שֶׁעֲדַיִין אֵין הַשֵּׁם שָׁלֵם קוֹדֶם מְחִיַּיִת עֲמָלֵק, הוּא נֶגֶד שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת
the two portions read prior to Purim [Shekalim and Zachor], when the Name is not yet complete prior to the blotting out of Amalek, correspond to the first two letters (Yud-Hei),
שֶׁבָּהֶם נִבְרְאוּ ב׳ עוֹלָמוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּמְנָחוֹת (כ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
through which two worlds were created [the World to Come with Yud and this world with Hei], as written in Menachos (29b);
וְהַיּוּ״ד עַל שֵׁם הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַשִׁ״י עַל פָּסוּק ״אָז יָשִׁיר [מֹשֶׁה]״ (שְׁמוֹת ט״ו:א׳)
and the letter Yud signifies thought (machshavah), as Rashi wrote on the verse "Then sang (yashir, with a future yud) Moshe" (Shemos 15:1),
וּדְבָרָיו נֶאֶמְנוּ עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַסּוֹד כִּידוּעַ
and his words are faithful according to the mystical tradition as is known;
וְהוּא עוֹלָם הַבָּא דְּעָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה וְאֵינוֹ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת
and this is the World to Come, which arose in primordial thought and is not openly manifest;
וְ״כָל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
and "all Israel have a portion in the World to Come" (Sanhedrin 90a),
הַיְינוּ דְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לְבָבָם הַנֶּעְלָם שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת כְּלָל אֲפִילּוּ לָאָדָם עַצְמוֹ
meaning that the hidden depths of their heart, which are not revealed even to the person himself,
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתָם, חֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמַּעַל
being the root of their soul, an actual divine portion from Above,
שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה:ב) דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
regarding which they stated (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2) that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel;
דָּבָר זֶה הוּא סוֹד הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד לִיבָּא כִּידוּעַ
this reality is the esoteric secret of the World to Come which corresponds to the heart as is known;
וְהוּא הַחֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲפִילּוּ לַחוֹטְאִים
and this is the portion in the World to Come possessed by every Jew, even sinners;
שֶׁכָּל הַחֲטָאִים הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַחֹמֶר וְהַהִתְגַּלּוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְלֹא מִצַּד עֹומֶק הַנְּשָׁמָה הַטְּהוֹרָה הַנֶּעְלֶמֶת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
for all sins derive solely from the material vessel and earthly manifestation, and not from the depth of the pure soul which remains concealed in this world,
וּמִתְגַּלֵּית לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה ״[וְהָיָה] אוֹר הַלְּבָנָה כְּאוֹר הַחַמָּה״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ל:כו)
and will be unveiled in the Future when "the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun" (Yeshayah 30:26);
דְּהַיְינוּ אוֹר כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל יִהְיֶה מֵאִיר וּמַבְהִיק כְּשֶׁמֶשׁ וּמָגֵן ה׳ כִּבְיָכוֹל
meaning the light of Knesset Israel will shine and radiate like the sun and the shield of Hashem (Tehillim 84:12), as it were,
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ע״ה עַמּוּד ב׳): ״עֲתִידִים יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיִּקָּרְאוּ בִּשְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא״
as they stated (Bava Batra 75b): "In the Future Israel will be called by the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He";
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּתְכַּלְּלוּ בִּמְקוֹרָן, שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק אֵלּוּ עוֹבְרִין (פְּסָחִים נ׳ עַמּוּד א׳): דְּיִהְיֶה נִקְרָא כְּמוֹת שֶׁהוּא נִכְתָּב
meaning that they will be integrated into their Source, concerning which they said at the end of Perek Ellu Ovrin (Pesachim 50a): that the Divine Name will then be pronounced as It is written;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה פְּנִימִיּוּת הָאוֹר בְּלֹא לְבוּשׁ הַמַּעֲלִים וּמְכַסֶּה
meaning that the inwardness of the light will be revealed without any garment that conceals and veils,
שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ הֶעְלֵם וְלֹא נִגְלָה דְּבֵיקוּתָם בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים לְגַמְרֵי
from which concealment stems the condition of Knesset Israel in this world, where their cleaving unto the Living God is hidden and not fully manifest,
עַד לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְחַדֵּשׁ עוֹלָמוֹ, דְּהַיְינוּ אוֹתוֹ עוֹלָם בְּעַצְמוֹ, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם יִהְיֶה מְחוּדָּשׁ לְגַמְרֵי
until the Future when the Holy One renews His universe, which is the selfsame universe, yet completely renewed.
וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דַּי מַה שֶּׁיּוֹדְעִין שֶׁיֵּשׁ עוֹלָם הַבָּא, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק
And in this world it is sufficient that they know that the World to Come exists, whereby they possess a portion within it;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק חֵלֶק: דְּמִי שֶׁכּוֹפֵר בָּזֶה, אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק
and as written in the opening of Perek Chelek (Sanhedrin 90a): one who denies the resurrection of the dead from the Torah has no portion in it;
וְכָל הָעוֹנָשִׁין דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵינָם בָּאִים כְּמוֹ עוֹנְשֵׁי מֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם שֶׁהוּא דֶּרֶךְ קְנָס מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעָבַר מִצְוָתוֹ
and all punishments of the Blessed Name do not operate like the penalties of a human king, which are arbitrary fines for having violated a decree;
רַק כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּאָבוֹת (ד:ב): ״שְׂכַר עֲבֵרָה — עֲבֵרָה״, וְ״[חַטָּאִים] תְּרַדֵּף רָעָה״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ג:כ״א)
but as written in Avos (4:2): "the consequence of a transgression is a transgression," and "evil pursues sinners" (Mishlei 13:21);
דְּהָעֲבֵירָה וְהָרָעָה עַצְמָהּ הִיא הָעֹונֶשׁ הָרוֹדְפוֹ
for the transgression and the evil itself is the very punishment that pursues him;
כִּי מִמֵּילָא הֲרֵי נִמְשָׁךְ אַחַר הָרָע, וְהָרָע דַּעֲבֵירָה הוּא עַצְמוֹ הָרָע דְּעֹונֶשׁ
for he is drawn after the evil, and the evil of the sin is identical to the evil of the punishment;
כִּי כָּל סִטְרָא דְּרָע הַכֹּל אֶחָד, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ט״ז עַמּוּד א׳): ״הוּא שָׂטָן, הוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע, הוּא מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת״
for the entire domain of evil is one, as written (Bava Batra 16a): "He is the Satan, he is the yetzer hara, he is the Angel of Death";
וְהַכְּפִירָה בְּאֵיזֶה דָּבָר הוּא שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְדָבָר זֶה
and denying a spiritual reality means that one has no connection with that reality;
דְּעַל כֵּן בָּא חֲבַקּוּק וְהֶעֱמִידָן עַל אַחַת: ״[וְצַדִּיק] בֶּאֱמוּנָתוֹ יִחְיֶה״ (חֲבַקּוּק ב:ד; מַכּוֹת כ״ד עַמּוּד א׳)
wherefore Chabakuk came and based the entire Torah upon a single principle: "the righteous shall live by his faith" (Chabakuk 2:4; Makkos 24a);
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי אֱמוּנַת הַנֶּפֶשׁ בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת וְדִיבּוּק לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַאֲמִין אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת בְּנַפְשׁוֹ
for through the soul's faith in the Blessed Name it possesses an intrinsic bond with Him, whereas one who lacks faith has no connection in his soul;
וְהָאֱמוּנָה בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא הוּא הַחֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל
and faith in the World to Come is the very vessel that secures the portion in the World to Come for every Jew.
וְזֶהוּ מֵעִיקָּרֵי הַיַּהֲדוּת: לְהַאֲמִין שֶׁיֵּשׁ עוֹלָם אַחֵר הַנִּצְחִי, וְאֵין הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה תַּכְלִית הָאָדָם
And this is among the primary principles of Judaism: to believe that there exists another, eternal world, and that this world is not the ultimate purpose of man;
וְכָךְ קִבַּלְתִּי וְשָׁמַעְתִּי בְּפֵירוּשׁ בְּלָשׁוֹן זֶה: שֶׁהָאָדָם הַיּוֹדֵעַ וּמַאֲמִין שֶׁיֵּשׁ עוֹד עוֹלָם אַחֵר, הוּא יִשְׂרָאֵל הַנּוֹשָׁע בַּה׳
and thus I received and heard explicitly in this exact phrasing: that a person who knows and believes that there exists another world is an "Israelite saved by Hashem" (Yeshayah 45:17);
וְהֵם דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים, כִּי בָּזֶה נָקֵל לָאָדָם לְהַשְׁלִיךְ כָּל חֶמְדּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and these are the words of the Living God, for through this realization it is easy for man to cast away all the worldly cravings of this life;
וְהוּא זִכְרוֹן יוֹם הַמִּיתָה שֶׁהוּא הַמַּדְרֵיגָה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה לְנִיצּוּחַ הַיֵּצֶר רָע (בְּרָכוֹת ה׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
and this is remembering the day of death, which is the final stratagem for conquering the yetzer hara (Berachos 5a),
לְהַזְכִּיר לְנַפְשׁוֹ כִּי לֹא יָרְדָה לְהִשְׁתַּקֵּעַ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְהוּא רַק כִּפְרוֹזְדּוֹר וּמוּכֶנֶת לָצֵאת מִמֶּנּוּ לִטְרַקְלִין (אָבוֹת ד:טז)
reminding one's soul that it did not descend to sink into this world, this world being merely an antechamber (prozdor) prepared to lead into the banquet hall (traklin, Avos 4:16);
וְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת לָזֶה לָשׁוּב עַל יְדֵי זֶה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, בָּא מִצַּד הַחֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל
and the awakening to return unto the Blessed Name through this derives from the portion in the World to Come inherent within all Israel.
כִּי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזּוֹכְרִין יוֹם הַמִּיתָה, אַדְּרַבָּא עַל יְדֵי זֶה אוֹמְרִים: ״אָכוֹל וְשָׁתוֹ כִּי מָחָר נָמוּת״ (יְשַׁעְיָה כ״ב:י״ג)
For the nations of the world, even when they remember the day of death, on the contrary say through it: "Let us eat and drink; for tomorrow we shall die" (Yeshayah 22:13);
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק בַּמֶּה מַדְלִיקִין (שַׁבָּת ל״א עַמּוּד ב׳): דְּאֵין חֲרֵידִין וַעֲצֵבִין מִפְּנֵי הַמִּיתָה
and as written in Shabbat (31b): they do not tremble or grieve over mortality;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כ״א:כ״ב) מֵאוֹתוֹ גּוֹי שֶׁעָשָׂה סְעוּדָה דְּאָמַר: ״אָנוּ, אִם אֵין לָנוּ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְכוּלֵיהּ״
and as related in the Midrash (Bamidbar Rabbah 21:22) regarding that gentile who made a feast, saying: "If we do not enjoy in this world, what have we?";

דְּאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא כְּלָל, אִם כֵּן אַדְּרַבָּא עַל יְדֵי זִכְרוֹן יוֹם הַמִּיתָה מוֹסִיפִין לְמַלֹּאות כָּל תַּאֲוָתָם וּשְׁרִירוּת לִבָּם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דְּ״אִם לֹא עַכְשָׁיו — אֵימָתָי״ (אָבוֹת א:יד)
for having no portion in the World to Come, remembering death merely drives them to indulge all physical lusts, saying "if not now, when?";
וְאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם הִתְעוֹרְרוּת עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְבַקֵּשׁ הָאֱמֶת הַקִּיּוּם לָעַד, כִּי הוּא דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת עִמּוֹ
possessing no spiritual awakening through death to seek eternal truth, having no connection with it.
אֲבָל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁמִּטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה, כּוּלּוֹ זֶרַע אֱמֶת, דְּ״תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב״ (מִיכָה ז:כ)
But the seed of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, whose bed is complete (Pesachim 56a), are entirely a seed of truth: "You will show truth to Jacob" (Michah 7:20);
וְיֵשׁ בְּכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל נְקֻדָּה זוֹ דִּ״שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ב:י״ט)
and there exists within every single Jew this point of "the lip of truth shall be established forever" (Mishlei 12:19);
[וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּוהַר תִּשָּׂא קפ״ח עַמּוּד א׳] דְּעַל נְקֻדָּה זוֹ נֶאֱמַר: ״הַשֹּׁמֵר אֱמֶת לְעוֹלָם״ (תְּהִלִּים קמ״ו:ו׳)
[and as written in Zohar, Ki Tisa 188a] that concerning this inner point it is said: "Who keeps truth forever" (Tehillim 146:6);
שֶׁהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים ״שׁוֹמֵר עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַד״ (בִּרְכַּת הַמַּחֲזִיר שְׁכִינָתוֹ)
which parallels the liturgical blessing "Who guards His people Israel forever";
דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִבְטִיחַ: ״לֹא מְאַסְתִּים [וְלֹא גְעַלְתִּים] וְגוֹמֵר״ (וַיִּקְרָא כ״ו:מ״ד), ״[כִּי] הֶהָרִים יָמוּשׁוּ... וּבְרִית שְׁלוֹמִי לֹא תָמוּט״ (יְשַׁעְיָה נ״ד:י׳)

for the Blessed Name promised: "I will not reject them, neither will I abhor them, etc." (Vayikra 26:44), and "the mountains may depart... but My covenant of peace shall not be removed" (Yeshayah 54:10);
וּדְהַגַּם שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּ ״נִהְיֶה כַגּוֹיִם וְגוֹמֵר״ (יְחֶזְקֵאל כ:לב), ״הָעֹלָה עַל רוּחֲכֶם הָיוֹ לֹא תִהְיֶה... [כִּי בְּיָד חֲזָקָה] וּבְחֵמָה שְׁפוּכָה אֶמְלוֹךְ עֲלֵיכֶם״ (שָׁם:ל״ב–ל״ג)

and even should they declare "we will be as the heathen, etc." (Yechezkel 20:32), "that which comes into your mind shall not be at all... and with fury poured out will I be King over you" (ibid. 20:32–33);
וְאֵין מַנִּיחַ כְּלָל לִנְקֻדַּת עֶצֶם הַיַּהֲדוּת לְהִתְעָרֵב בְּגוֹיֵי הָאֲרָצוֹת וְשֶׁיַּגִּיעַ הַקִּלְקוּל לַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּלָל
never permitting the essential core of Judaism to be assimilated among the gentiles or allowing blemish to touch the ultimate soul-root.
עַל כֵּן יֵשׁ בְּכָל אֶחָד מִזֶּרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל כֹּחַ זֶה לְהִתְעוֹרֵר עַל יְדֵי זִכְרוֹן יוֹם הַמִּיתָה וְשֶׁיֵּשׁ עוֹד עוֹלָם אַחֵר
Therefore there exists within every descendant of Israel the capacity to be awakened through the memory of the day of death and the knowledge that another world exists,
לָשׁוּב אֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת עַל יְדֵי זֶה, מֵאַחַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ נְקֻדָּה וְחֵלֶק הַשַּׁיָּיךְ לְאוֹתוֹ עוֹלָם הַקַּיָּים לָעַד
returning unto the Blessed Name in truth through this, since he possesses an indelible point belonging to that eternal world;
וְאוֹתָהּ נְקֻדָּה נִמְשֶׁכֶת מֵאוֹת הַיּוּ״ד דְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה בָּרוּךְ הוּא
and that inner point is drawn from the letter Yud of the Name Havayah, blessed be He,
שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הוּא עֹומֶק רֵאשִׁית שֶׁל כָּל הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת וּרְצוֹנוֹת שֶׁבְּנֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, עַד שֶׁלֹּא בָּאוּ לְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ
whence derives the primordial depth of all thoughts and desires in the Jewish soul, prior to their expanding into revealed consciousness.
וְעַל כֵּן: ״כִּי תִשָּׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ [בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לִפְקֻדֵיהֶם] וְגוֹמֵר״ (שְׁמוֹת ל:יב)
And therefore: "When you take the sum of the children of Israel according to their number, etc." (Shemos 30:12);
דְּהַמִּנְיָן הוּא שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד בִּפְרָט מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל נִמְנֶה וְנֶחְשָׁב וְלֹא הַכְּנֵסִיָּה בִּכְלָל
for a census counts each Jew individually as a distinct entity, and not merely as an aggregate community;
וּכְשֶׁהֵם בִּכְלַל אֲגֻדָּה אַחַת, אֲפִילּוּ חֶלְבְּנָה מִצְטָרֵף עִם הַלְּבוֹנָה וְנוֹתֵן רֵיחַ טוֹב (כְּרֵיתוֹת ו׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
and when they are unified as one collective, even the pungent galbanum (chelbenah, representing sinners) joins with the frankincense to produce a sweet fragrance (Kerisos 6b);
וַאֲפִילּוּ ״חֲבוּר עֲצַבִּים אֶפְרָיִם הַנַּח לוֹ״ (הוֹשֵׁעַ ד:יז; בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ל״ח:ו׳), דְּמַה שֶּׁחָסֵר זֶה — הִשְׁלִים זֶה
and even "Ephraim is joined to idols; let him alone" (Hoshea 4:17; Bereishis Rabbah 38:6), for what one lacks, his fellow completes;
וְעַל כֵּן עִיקַּר טַעֲנַת הַמְקַטְרְגִים וּמְקוֹם שְׁלִיטָתָם הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר מִתְפָּרֵט כָּל אֶחָד בִּפְרָט וְלֹא יַחַד בִּכְלָל
wherefore the primary claim of the accusers and their domain of prosecution arises when each individual is scrutinized alone and not shielded within the collective.
וְעַל כֵּן בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, דְּכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם ״עוֹבְרִין [לְפָנָיו] כִּבְנֵי מָרוֹן״ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה ט״ז עַמּוּד א׳), אֶחָד אֶחָד
And therefore on Rosh Hashanah, when all who enter the world "pass before Him like sheep" (Rosh Hashanah 16a), one by one;
אָז הוּא זְמַן הַדִּין דְּ״יָבֹאוּ בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים לְהִתְיַצֵּב [עַל ה׳]״ (אִיּוֹב א:ו)
then is the severe time of judgment when "the sons of God came to present themselves before Hashem" (Iyov 1:6);
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ד׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): דְּלָא לִיצַלֵּי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בְּיָחִיד
wherefore the Sages stated (Avodah Zarah 4b) that an individual should not pray the Mussaf of Rosh Hashanah in isolation without a congregation;
וְכֵן אִיתָא בַּזֹּוהַר (חֵלֶק ב׳ מ״ד עַמּוּד ב׳) עַל פָּסוּק ״בְּתוֹךְ עַמִּי אָנֹכִי יֹשָׁבֶת״ (מְלָכִים ב ד:יג)
and so it is taught in the Zohar (II, 44b) on the verse "I dwell among my own people" (II Melachim 4:13):
דִּבְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בָּעֵי לְאַכְלָלָא נַפְשֵׁיהּ בִּכְלָלָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
that on Rosh Hashanah one must integrate his individual soul into the collective body of Israel;
וְ״הַיּוֹצֵר יַחַד לִבָּם״ (תְּהִלִּים ל״ג:ט״ו), כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (י״ח עַמּוּד א׳): דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל ״גּוֹי אֶחָד״ יְכוֹלִים לְהִתְאַחֵד בִּנְקֻדַּת הַלֵּב שֶׁהוּא מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ אֶחָד
and "He fashions their hearts together" (Tehillim 33:15; Rosh Hashanah 18a): Israel, being a unique nation, can unite at the inner point of the heart which stems from a single source.
וְזֶהוּ קוֹל שׁוֹפָר, שֶׁהוּא קוֹל פָּשׁוּט הַיּוֹצֵא מֵעֹומֶק הַלֵּב שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ חִיתּוּךְ אוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁהוּא חִילּוּק הַפְּרָטִים
And this is the blast of the Shofar: a simple, unarticulated sound issuing from the depths of the heart, containing no division of verbal letters which divide into details;
דִּכְשֶׁבָּא לְדִבּוּר אָז הוּא מִתְפָּרֵט לְאוֹתִיּוֹת, שֶׁכָּל אוֹת פְּרָט בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
for when sound becomes speech, it breaks into distinct letters, each letter standing as a separated detail;
וְכֵן הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם אוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה
and so the souls of Israel correspond to the letters of the Torah;
וְקוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הָיָה קוֹל הַשּׁוֹפָר הֶחָזָק מְאֹד, שֶׁהוּא קוֹל פָּשׁוּט הַכְּלָלִי שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ נִמְשְׁכוּ אַחַר כָּךְ הַפְּרָטִים הַמִּתְפָּרְטִים
and prior to the Giving of the Torah there sounded the exceeding loud blast of the Shofar (Shemos 19:19), which was the primal, universal simple sound whence later issued the specific letters;
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל מִתְכַּלְּלִים עַצְמָם יַחַד וּלְהִכָּלֵל בִּמְקוֹרָם שֶׁהוּא אֶחָד
and through the simple shofar blast Israel integrate themselves together to be unified in their primordial Source which is One;
וְאָז אֵין עוֹד מָקוֹם לְשׁוּם קִטְרוּג, וְהַשָּׂטָן מִתְעַרְבֵּב:
and then no place remains for prosecution, and the Satan is confounded and silenced (Rosh Hashanah 16b).

7.h: The theme: The distinction between the judgment of Rosh Hashanah and the individual elevation of Ki Tisa, and the mystery of the half-shekel (machatzis ha-shekel) as the fiery coin. On Rosh Hashanah, all creatures pass before Hashem like a flock of sheep (kivnei maron, Rosh Hashanah 16a), a universal remembrance (Yom HaZikaron) of the initial creation where Hashem sustains the whole collective. In contrast, the census of Ki Tisa ("when you elevate the head of the children of Israel", Shemos 30:12) itemizes every individual separately before the King's entourage, stripping away the protection of the community and exposing each soul to the scrutiny of the prosecuting Satan. To avert plague, Hashem commanded a ransom (kofer nefesh): the half-shekel of ten gerahs, representing the letter Yud, the Ten Sefirot, and the indestructible bone of luz (Bereishis Rabbah 28:3) which survives fire and decay to rebuild the body. The full shekel is twenty gerahs (representing Keser, the letters Kaf and Yud-Yud of the divine union); Israel offers their ten gerahs (machatzis ha-shekel) to Hashem. While strict prophecy dictates "the soul that sins shall die" (Yechezkel 18:4; Yerushalmi Makkos 2:6), Hashem redeems the souls of His servants ("Hashem redeems the soul of His servants, and none of them that trust in Him shall be desolate", Tehillim 34:23). Moshe struggled to comprehend how a soul could be redeemed from the mortality of the Serpent until Hashem showed him a coin of fire taken from beneath the Throne of Glory. Money encompasses all physical cravings (khol me'odecha / khol mamonecha, Berachos 54a); when a person surrenders his money to Hashem, he elevates the fleeting life of this world (chayei sha'ah) into eternal life (chayei olam).

p: וְכָל מִצְוֹת הַתּוֹרָה הֵם עֵצוֹת מִגְּדוֹל הָעֵצָה יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ
And all commandments of the Torah are divine counsels from the Great in Counsel, blessed be His Name (Yirmiyah 32:19),
לַנֶּפֶשׁ הַדְּבֵקָה בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁלֹּא תְאֻנֶּה אֵלֶיהָ רָעָה הַמַּפְרִידָה מִדְּבֵיקוּת זֶה
unto the soul that cleaves to the Blessed Name, that no evil befall it to sever it from this cleaving (Tehillim 91:10);
וּבְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הוּא פְּקִידָה, דְּמִי לֹא נִפְקַד כְּהַיּוֹם הַזֶּה (פִּיּוּט זִכְרוֹנוֹת)
and on Rosh Hashanah there occurs a general remembrance, for who is not remembered on this day?
אֲבָל לֹא דֶּרֶךְ נְשִׂיאוּת רֹאשׁ, שֶׁהוּא רַק יוֹם הַזִּכָּרוֹן מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָז ״הֲרַת עוֹלָם״ (שָׁם) וְנִבְרְאוּ
yet not by way of elevating each head individually, it being merely the Day of Remembrance because on that day the universe was conceived and created;
בְּאוֹתוֹ יוֹם תָּמִיד מִתְעוֹרֵר מֵחִידּוּשׁ וְהַזִּכָּרוֹן כִּבְיָכוֹל לְפָנָיו
on that day the cosmic renewal and the remembrance constantly awaken before Him, as it were;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא הַמִּשְׁפָּט עַל הַמְשָׁכַת הַשֶּׁפַע, שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי תְּחִלַּת הַבְּרִיאָה דְּ״אַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם״ (נְחֶמְיָה ט:ו)
and through this is executed the judgment regarding the channeling of sustenance, operating through the primal creation where "You preserve them all" (Nechemyah 9:6);
וּמִשְּׁעַת יְצִירָה נִגְזַר טִפָּה זוֹ מַה תְּהֵא עָלֶיהָ (נִדָּה ט״ז עַמּוּד ב׳)
and from the very moment of conception it is decreed concerning that seminal drop what shall become of it (Niddah 16b);
וּבְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מִתְעוֹרֵר שְׁעַת יְצִירָה דְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ בְּכָל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לִיצִירָה דְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁנָה
and on Rosh Hashanah the primordial moment of conception of the entire universe is awakened anew for the creative life of that coming year.
אֲבָל הַעֲבָרַת הַצֹּאן עַל יְדֵי מוֹנֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, זֶהוּ נְשִׂיאוּת רֹאשׁ לְכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בִּפְרָט
But the counting of sheep through an active human counter in this world constitutes the elevating of the head for each individual Jew in particular,
שֶׁהוּא נִמְנֶה בְּפַמַלְיָא שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ וְאֵינוֹ מִתְכַּלֵּל כְּלָל
being numbered within the royal entourage of the King, unshielded by the collective;
כִּי הוּא פְּרָט שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ לַכְּלָל, דְּכָל פְּרָט נִמְנֶה וּמְסוּיָּם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
for he stands as an individual detached from the community, each single person being counted and specified on his own;
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה צָרִיךְ כֹּפֶר נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה נֶגֶף וּשְׁלִיטָה לַמְקַטְרֵג
and in this exposed state one requires a soul-ransom (kofer nefesh) so that there be no plague or dominion for the prosecuting Satan,
דְּ״[כִּי אָדָם] אֵין צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ [אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה טּוֹב וְלֹא יֶחֱטָא]״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כ)
for "there is not a righteous man upon earth that does good and sins not" (Koheles 7:20).
וּמַחֲצִית הַשֶּׁקֶל הוּא הַיּוּ״ד דְּהוּא עֶשֶׂר גֵּרָה, וְרוֹמֵז לְעֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת
And the half-shekel is the letter Yud, which equals ten gerahs (Shemos 30:13), alluding to the Ten Sefirot,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק ב׳ קפ״ז עַמּוּד ב׳) רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תִּשָּׂא, עַיֵּין שָׁם
as written in the Raya Mehemna [Zohar II, 187b], at the beginning of Parashat Ki Tisa, see there;
דְּעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״הֶעָשִׁיר לֹא יַרְבֶּה״ (שְׁמוֹת ל:טו) — עַמּוּדָא דְּאֶמְצָעִיתָא
concerning which it is said: "The rich shall not give more" (Shemos 30:15)—this is the Central Pillar (Amuda d'Emtza'ita);
כִּדִתְנַן בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה (א:ד): ״עֶשֶׂר וְלֹא אַחַד עָשָׂר״, ״וְהַדַּל [לֹא יַמְעִיט] וְכוּלֵיהּ״, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם
as we learned in Sefer Yetzirah (1:4): "Ten and not eleven," and "the poor shall not give less, etc.," see there;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּתְעוֹרֵר לְבָבוֹ, דַּאֲפִילּוּ נִשְׁקַע לְמָקוֹם שֶׁנִּשְׁקַע, מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ נְקֻדַּת אֱמֶת בִּלְבָבוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁקְעָה כְּלָל וְלֹא יִשְׁלוֹט בָּהּ שׁוּם רָע

meaning that his heart should awaken to the realization that even if he has sunk into whatever low place he has sunk, there remains an unblemished point of truth in his heart that never sank and over which no evil can ever hold dominion;
וְהוּא הַלּוּז שֶׁבַּשִּׁדְרָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כ״ח:ג׳)
and this is the bone of luz in the spine, concerning which the Sages of blessed memory stated (Bereishis Rabbah 28:3)
שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִרְקָב וְלֹא נִשְׂרָף וְלֹא מִתְפּוֹצֵץ בְּכָל מִינֵי תַּחְבּוּלוֹת, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ בִּנְיַן הַגּוּף לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא
that it does not rot, nor is it consumed by fire, nor does it shatter under any blows, and from it the physical body will be rebuilt in the Future;
וְיָדוּעַ דְּמִסְפַּר עֶשֶׂר הוּא קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה, וְכֵן נְקֻדָּה זוֹ הַדּוֹמָה לְיוּ״ד הוּא קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה
and it is known that the number ten constitutes a complete spiritual structure (komah sheleimah), and likewise this inner point resembling the letter Yud is a complete stature,
עַד שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ קִלְקֵל כָּל הַקּוֹמָה, יוּכַל לְהִתְחַדֵּשׁ מִמֶּנָּה כָּל הַקּוֹמָה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת
so that even if a person has corrupted his entire visible stature, his complete stature can be renewed anew from this pristine point.
וְהַשֶּׁקֶל הוּא עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה, כַּ״ף רוֹמֵז לְכֶתֶר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ הַקְדָּמַת הַזֹּוהַר (ב׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
And the full biblical shekel is twenty gerahs, the letter Chaf (numerical value 20) alluding to Keser [Crown] as written at the start of the Introduction to the Zohar (2a);
וְהוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵהָרֹאשׁ וְהַקּוֹמָה, וְהוּא הַתְּפִלִּין שֶׁבָּרֹאשׁ שֶׁהֵם כְּמוֹ כֶּתֶר עַל הָרֹאשׁ
and it transcends the head and the mortal stature, embodying the Tefillin worn upon the head which rest like a crown above the head;
וְהוּא הַהִתְקַשְּׁרוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְכָל קוֹמַת הָאָדָם וְעֹומֶק רֵאשִׁית כָּל מַחְשְׁבוֹתָיו שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
representing the bond of attachment that the entire stature of man and the deepest inception of his mental thoughts possess with the Blessed Name,
בְּקַבָּלַת עוֹל מַה שֶּׁאָמַר הַכָּתוּב בַּפָּרָשִׁיּוֹת שֶׁבַּתְּפִלִּין וְהַהַכָּרָה דַּה׳ אֶחָד
through accepting the yoke of what Scripture proclaims in the passages of the Tefillin and recognizing that Hashem is One;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשָׂה הַיִּחוּד דְּקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ
and through this is accomplished the supernal union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah;
דְּאָז יֵשׁ יוּ״ד דִּילֵיהּ וְיוּ״ד דִּילַהּ שֶׁהֵם כַּ״ף
for then there is the Yud of the Holy One and the Yud of the Shechinah, which together form twenty (Chaf);
וּמַחֲצִית הַשֶּׁקֶל הוּא הַיּוּ״ד דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד, וְנוֹתְנִים זֶה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and the half-shekel is the Yud of Knesset Israel alone, which they offer unto the Blessed Name;
וְהוּא הַכֹּפֶר נֶפֶשׁ
and this is the soul-ransom:
כִּי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַמְקַטְרֵג טוֹעֵן כְּמִשְׁפַּט הַנְּבוּאָה: ״הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַחֹטֵאת הִיא תָמוּת״ (יְחֶזְקֵאל י״ח:ד׳), כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דְּמַכּוֹת (פֶּרֶק ב׳ הֲלָכָה ו׳)
for even though the prosecutor argues according to the strict justice of prophecy: "The soul that sins, it shall die" (Yechezkel 18:4), as written in the Yerushalmi [Makkos 2:6],
וְ״תְמוּתַת רָשָׁע רָעָה וְשֹׂנְאֵי צַדִּיק יֶאְשָׁמוּ״ (תְּהִלִּים ל״ד:כ״ב)
and "Evil shall slay the wicked; and they that hate the righteous shall be held guilty" (Tehillim 34:22);
יֵשׁ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ פִּדְיוֹן עַל זֶה לַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּ״פֹּדֶה ה׳ נֶפֶשׁ עֲבָדָיו וְלֹא יֶאְשְׁמוּ [כָּל הַחֹסִים בּוֹ]״ (שָׁם:כ״ג)

the Blessed Name possesses a transcendental redemption for the souls of Israel, for "Hashem redeems the soul of His servants, and none of them that take refuge in Him shall be held guilty" (ibid. 34:23).
וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה נִתְקַשָּׁה מֹשֶׁה, דִּבְמִשְׁפַּט הַנְּבוּאָה לֹא יָכוֹל לְהַשִּׂיג זֶה
And regarding this matter Moshe struggled, for within the judicial framework of prophecy he could not grasp this,
וְ״אָח לֹא פָדֹה יִפְדֶּה אִישׁ, לֹא [יִתֵּן לֵאלֹהִים כָּפְרוֹ]״ (תְּהִלִּים מ״ט:ח׳), וְאֵין פִּדְיוֹן לְיוֹם הַמִּיתָה
for "no man can by any means redeem his brother, nor give to God a ransom for him" (Tehillim 49:8), there being no earthly ransom against mortality;
דְּהַמִּיתָה הוּא מִצַּד עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע שֶׁבַּתּוֹלָדָה
for death entered through the instigation of the Serpent which is the hereditary root of evil at birth (Shabbos 55b);
וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִרְאֶה זֶה כְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ רָע, וּמַה פִּדְיוֹן יֵשׁ עַל זֶה
and in this world this appears as an absolute evil root, so what ransom could redeem it?
אַךְ ה׳ דַּיְיקָא פּוֹדֶה, מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יֵשׁ פִּדְיוֹן לַעֲבָדָיו דַּוְוקָא, הֵם כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל: ״כִּי לִי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבָדִים, עֲבָדַי [הֵם]״ (וַיִּקְרָא כ״ה:נ״ה)

Yet Hashem specifically redeems: from the side of the Blessed Name there is a sovereign ransom exclusively for His servants, who are all Israel: "For unto Me the children of Israel are servants; they are My servants" (Vayikra 25:55).
וְהֶרְאָה לוֹ מַטְבֵּעַ שֶׁל אֵשׁ (תַּנְחוּמָא כִּי תִשָּׂא ז׳)
And He showed Moshe a coin of fire (Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 7);
הַיְינוּ דְּעִיקַּר חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא נִכְלָל בְּתַאֲוַת מָמוֹן שֶׁהוּא תַּאֲוָה הַכּוֹלֶלֶת
meaning that the general cravings of this world are all concentrated within the desire for money, which is an all-inclusive lust,
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג כָּל מִינֵי פְּרָטֵי הַתַּאֲווֹת
for through money one can purchase and attain every specific physical pleasure;
שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְכָל אֶחָד בִּפְרָט תַּאֲוָה לְדָבָר מְיוּחָד, וְתַאֲוַת מָמוֹן הוּא כּוֹלֵל כָּל אֶחָד, שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מִתְאַוֶּוה לָזֶה כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּשִּׂיג עַל יְדֵי זֶה תַּאֲוָתוֹ הַפְּרָטִית
for while each individual possesses a distinct passion for a specific thing, the lust for money encompasses everyone, each craving it to realize his personal desire;
וְזֶהוּ הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁנָּתַן הָאֱלֹהִים לִבְנֵי אָדָם לַעֲנוֹת בּוֹ, דְּאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (קֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה א:יד): ״זֶהוּ שִׁפּוּטָהּ שֶׁל מָמוֹן״
and this is the travail that God gave to the sons of men to be exercised therewith (Koheles 1:13), which the Midrash interprets (Koheles Rabbah 1:14): "this refers to business and dealing in money";
וּבָזֶה הוּא כְּלַל הַהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and herein lies the entirety of human immersion in this physical world.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״בְּכָל מְאֹדֶךָ״ (דְּבָרִים ו:ה), דְּאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּ״הָרוֹאֶה״ (בְּרָכוֹת ס״א עַמּוּד ב׳): ״בְּכָל מָמוֹנְךָ״
And regarding this it is said: "with all your might (me'odecha)" (Devarim 6:5), which the Sages expounded in HaRo'eh (Berachos 54a): "with all your money";
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַ״מְּאֹד״ שֶׁל הָאָדָם, וְזֶה תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת הָאַהֲבָה שֶׁהָאָדָם מוֹסֵר גַּם הַ״מְּאֹד״ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for this represents man's very excess and might (me'od), and this is the consummate height of love: that man surrenders even his material might unto the Blessed Name;
וְדָבָר זֶה נֶאֱמַר בְּפָרָשַׁת ״וְאָהַבְתָּ״ לַיָּחִיד, לֹא בְּפָרָשַׁת ״וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ״ לָרַבִּים
and this dedication is stated in the singular passage of Ve'ahavta (addressed to the individual), and omitted from the plural passage of Vehaya Im Shamoa (addressed to the community);
שֶׁהַיָּחִיד בִּפְרָט רוֹצֶה לִהְיוֹת מְדוּגָּל בְּאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, צָרִיךְ הִתְחַזְּקוּת וְהִתְאַמְּצוּת יְתֵירָה נֶגֶד הַמַּשְׂטִינִים וְיֵצֶר הַמֵּסִית
for when an individual seeks to stand out distinguished in the love of Hashem, he requires exceptional fortitude against prosecuting accusers and the inciting yetzer;
וְעַל כֵּן צָרִיךְ הוּא לְהִתְגַּבֵּר בְּכָל מְאוֹדוֹ לִמְסוֹר גַּם הַ״מְּאֹד״ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
wherefore he must prevail with all his strength to surrender even his wealth unto the Blessed Name.
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת שָׁם): דְּיֵשׁ לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁמָּמוֹנוֹ חָבִיב עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ, עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר ״בְּכָל מְאֹדֶךָ״
And our Rabbis stated (ibid.): "There is a person whose money is dearer to him than his body, therefore it is said: 'with all your might'";
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזֶּה לִכְאוֹרָה מִדָּה רָעָה וְזָרָה, עִם כָּל זֶה מָצִינוּ בְּפֶרֶק גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה (חֻלִּין צ״א עַמּוּד א׳) דְּהוּא מִדָּתָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים דְּמָמוֹנָם חָבִיב מִגּוּפָם

and although this appears superficially to be an alien and flawed trait, nevertheless we find in Chullin (91a) that it is the praiseworthy attribute of the righteous that their money is dearer to them than their bodies;
וְלָמְדוּ מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ מִדַּת הָאֱמֶת הַקַּיָּים לָעַד, שֶׁלֹּא חָשַׁק לְשׁוּם דָּבָר שֶׁלְּפִי שָׁעָה
and they derived this from Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, who is the root of eternal truth, who never lusted after anything of transient worth;
וּמָה קִיּוּם לָעַד יֵשׁ בְּמָמוֹן, דְּהוּא וַדַּאי דָּבָר שֶׁלְּפִי שָׁעָה לְבַד
and what eternal permanence could exist in money, which is certainly a fleeting material thing?
אֲבָל יָדוּעַ דְּ״יָפָה שָׁעָה אַחַת בִּתְשׁוּבָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִכָּל חַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא״ (אָבוֹת ד:יז)
But it is known that "better is one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world than all the life of the World to Come" (Avos 4:17);
וְיֵשׁ מִצַּד זֶה מַעֲלָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה, אֲבָל בּוֹ הוּא מְקוֹם הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וְהַבְּחִירָה
and in this respect there is a unique virtue in this world: although it is temporary, here alone is the arena of spiritual exertion and free choice;
וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא נִקְרָא: ״שָׁנִים אֲשֶׁר תֹּאמַר אֵין לִי בָהֶם חֵפֶץ״ (קֹהֶלֶת י״ב:א׳), כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק שׁוֹאֵל (שַׁבָּת קנ״א עַמּוּד ב׳)
whereas the World to Come is called "years wherein you shall say: I have no pleasure in them" (Koheles 12:1; Shabbos 151b),
דְּעִיקַּר הָאָדָם הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי הוּא הַחֵשֶׁק וְחֵפֶץ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for the essential glory of an Israelite is the passionate longing and desire he possesses for the service of the Blessed Name;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כ:ז) עַל פָּסוּק ״וְאֶל אִישֵׁךְ תְּשׁוּקָתֵךְ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג:טז): אֵין תְּשׁוּקָתָךְ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶלָּא לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
as written in the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 20:7) on the verse "and your desire shall be to your husband": the true desire of Israel is to none other than the Holy One, blessed be He;
וְהִתְגַּבְּרוּת הַחֵשֶׁק הוּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ רִיחוּק לִפְעָמִים
and the intensification of holy desire is generated specifically through temporary distance and concealment,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (נִדָּה ל״א עַמּוּד ב׳) בְּטַעַם הַנִּדָּה: כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּהֵא חֲבִיבָה [עַל בַּעְלָהּ]
as the Sages stated (Niddah 31b) regarding the reason for ritual separation: so that she be beloved to her husband;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״[וְרָאִיתִי אָנִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ] יִתְרוֹן [לַחָכְמָה מִן הַסִּכְלוּת כִּ]יתְרוֹן הָאוֹר מִן הַחֹשֶׁךְ״ (קֹהֶלֶת ב:יג)
and as it is written: "wisdom excels folly, as light excels darkness" (Koheles 2:13), illuminating out of the dark;
וְעַל כֵּן בְּרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם: בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא (שַׁבָּת ע״ז עַמּוּד ב׳)
wherefore in the creation of the cosmos: first came darkness and then light (Shabbos 77b);
וְעַל כֵּן עִיקַּר הַחֵשֶׁק וְהַחֵפֶץ הוּא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא וַחֲשׁוֹכָא
wherefore the ultimate longing and will operate within this world, the world of falsehood and obscurity.
אֲבָל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִשְׁלִיךְ אֱמֶת אַרְצָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ח:ה), וְיוּכַל לִדָּבֵק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן בַּתּוֹרָה דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ ״אֱמֶת״ (מִשְׁלֵי כ״ג:כ״ג)
Yet the Blessed Name cast truth unto the earth (Bereishis Rabbah 8:5), enabling man to cleave within this world to the Torah whereof "truth" is written (Mishlei 23:23);
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יָפָה מִכָּל חַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַבָּא
and through this engagement an hour in this world excels all the life of the World to Come,
כִּי הוּא מְהַפֵּךְ הַחַיֵּי שָׁעָה דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם:
for he transforms the fleeting life of this world (chayei sha'ah) into eternal life (chayei olam)!

7.h: The theme: Yaakov Avinu, the eternity of garments, and the fiery coin of the half-shekel. Yaakov Avinu cleaved so completely to truth that he inverted the world of falsehood into the World of Truth, wherefore he never died (Ta'anis 5b) and enjoyed a life devoid of sorrow and the yetzer hara (Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah, ch. 5). While physical possessions seem completely severed from eternal life, the resurrection of the dead reveals that the righteous will rise in their garments (omdim b'levusheihem, Kesubos 111b). Material wealth forms the garment of the body, just as the body garments the soul; because most commandments involve monetary resources, wealth consecrated to mitzvos acquires eternal endurance. Money (kesef) stems from desire (khasaf) and nature (teva, the coin matbea), possessing the numerical value of Elokim (86, strict judgment). The righteous invert this judgment into mercy and the Name Havayah. This is the coin of fire that Hashem showed Moshe: elevating inert matter (the lowest element, earth) into fire (the highest element), fulfilling "all that Hashem made is for His praise." In the World to Come, the inner soul of all righteous is equal—depicted as a circle (machol la-tzaddikim, Ta'anis 31a) without hierarchical rank; the only differentiation between souls lies in the beauty of their garments, which are woven from their personal exertion and sacrifices in this world.

p: וְזֶהוּ כָּל עִנְיַן מַדְרֵיגַת ״אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב״ (מִיכָה ז:כ), שֶׁדָּבַק בֶּאֱמֶת לְגַמְרֵי עַד שֶׁנִּתְהַפֵּךְ אֶצְלוֹ גַּם עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא לְעוֹלַם הָאֱמֶת
And this is the profound quality of "truth to Jacob" (Michah 7:20), who cleaved to truth so completely that for him the world of falsehood was inverted into the World of Truth;
דְּעַל כֵּן לֹא מֵת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַעֲנִית (ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
wherefore he did not die, as written in Ta'anis (5b);
וְזָכָה לְחַיִּים שֶׁלֹּא בְּצַעַר וְיֵצֶר הָרָע, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (פֶּרֶק ה׳) בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא
meriting in this world a life without sorrow and without the yetzer hara, as written in Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah (ch. 5), experiencing a foretaste of the World to Come.
וּמָמוֹן הֵם כְּלַל קִנְיָנֵי הָאָדָם דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם כְּפִי הַנִּרְאֶה שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא וְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם
And monetary possessions encompass all human acquisitions in this world, which to outward appearances seem to possess no connection to the World to Come and eternal life;
דְּהַגּוּף, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגַּם כֵּן כָּלָה בַּקֶּבֶר, מִכָּל מָקוֹם חוֹזֵר וְנִבְנֶה לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא
for the physical body, although decomposed in the grave, will nonetheless be rebuilt at the Resurrection of the Dead;
אֲבָל הָרְכוּשׁ אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת גַּם לְגוּף הָאָדָם
whereas material wealth seems to have no permanent affinity even to the physical body.
אֲבָל רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ (כְּתוּבּוֹת קי״א עַמּוּד ב׳): שֶׁעוֹמְדִין בִּלְבוּשֵׁיהֶם
But our Rabbis of blessed memory stated (Kesubos 111b): that the righteous will rise in their garments;
וּבְוַדַּאי אוֹתָם לְבוּשִׁים שֶׁיִּתְחַדְּשׁוּ יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן אַחַר הָרְקָבוֹן, יִהְיוּ קַיָּימִים לְעוֹלָם כְּמוֹ הַגּוּפִים
and certainly those garments that will be renewed ex nihilo following decomposition will endure forever just like the resurrected bodies;

וַעֲדִיפֵי מִלְּבוּשִׁים דִּבְמִדְבָּר, דְּאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (הוּבָא בְּרַשִׁ״י דְּבָרִים ח:ד) שֶׁהָיוּ גְּדֵילִים עִמָּהֶם, וְנֶאֱמַר: ״שִׂמְלָתְךָ לֹא בָלְתָה [מֵעָלֶיךָ] וְגוֹמֵר״ (דְּבָרִים ח:ד)

surpassing even the garments worn in the wilderness, regarding which the Sages stated (cited in Rashi, Devarim 8:4) that they grew along with them, as it is said: "Your clothing did not wear out upon you, etc." (Devarim 8:4);
וַהֲרֵי יֵשׁ הַשְׁאָרָה קְצָת מֵהָרְכוּשׁ גַּם כֵּן לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד, שֶׁהוּא נַעֲשָׂה לְבוּשׁ לַגּוּף
and behold, there is a lasting eternal remnant preserved from physical wealth as well, being transformed into a garment for the body!
וְהַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַתּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹתֶיהָ, דְּיֵשׁ הַרְבֵּה מִצְוֹת וְכִמְעַט רוּבָּם תְּלוּיִם בְּמָמוֹן וּרְכוּשׁ הָאָדָם
And this occurs through the Torah and its commandments, for there are numerous commandments—indeed the majority—that depend upon man's money and wealth;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִמְשָׁךְ גַּם בָּהֶם חַיֵּי עוֹלָם וְנִצְחִיּוּת
and through this holy utilization, eternal life and imperishability are drawn into material wealth as well;
וְהַגּוּף לְבוּשׁ הַנֶּפֶשׁ, וְהָרְכוּשׁ לְבוּשׁ הַגּוּף
the body serving as the garment of the soul, and wealth serving as the garment of the body.
וְהַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁכְּבָר נִזְדַּכֵּךְ גּוּפָם, חֲבִיבוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם לַלְּבוּשׁ שֶׁהוּא הַמָּמוֹן
And for the righteous whose bodies are already refined, their special care is directed toward this outer garment which is money;
דְּכָל מַה שֶּׁהוּא גַּס יוֹתֵר וּלְבוּשׁ חִיצוֹנִי יוֹתֵר, צָרִיךְ בּוֹ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת יוֹתֵר
for the coarser and more external a garment is, the greater the exertion required to elevate it;
וְעַל כֵּן זֶה חָבִיב וְיָפֶה לָהֶם יוֹתֵר שֶׁשָּׁם הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת יוֹתֵר, כִּי שָׁם הַחֵשֶׁק יוֹתֵר
and therefore it is more precious to them because greater spiritual exertion and longing are invested there.
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא ״כֶּסֶף״ לְשׁוֹן חֶמְדָּה וְתַאֲוָה (כִּסּוּפִין)
And therefore silver is called kesef, denoting longing, yearning, and desire (nikhsaf);
וְ״כַסְפָּא טַבְעָא״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק הַזָּהָב (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא מ״ד עַמּוּד א׳), לְשׁוֹן ״טֶבַע״
and the Talmud calls silver currency kaspa tav'a (Bava Metzia 44a), derived from the root teva [nature],
שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִצַּד טֶבַע הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עִיקַּר מַטְבֵּעַ הַיּוֹצֵאת בּוֹ
for according to the nature of this world, silver is the primary circulating coin;
וְהַנְהָגַת הַטֶּבַע הוּא הַנְהָגַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁמִּצַּד הַהֶעְלֵם
and the governance of nature (ha-teva) is the order of this world operating in concealment;
וְכִידוּעַ שֶׁהוּא בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא אֱלֹהִי״ם (86), שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת הַדִּין
and as is known, ha-teva
(הטבע)
has the numerical value of Elokim
(אלהים = 86),
which is the Attribute of Judgment;
וְהַצַּדִּיקִים מְהַפְּכִים אוֹתוֹ לְמִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים וְשֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה, שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַפְּנִימִיּוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַבָּא גַּם בָּזֶה
and the righteous invert this natural concealment into the Attribute of Mercy and the Name Havayah, revealing the inner light of the World to Come even within monetary affairs.
וְזֶהוּ הַמַּטְבֵּעַ שֶׁל אֵשׁ שֶׁהֶרְאָה לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁיֵּשׁ מַטְבֵּעַ דְּאֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן
And this is the coin of fire that the Holy One showed Moshe Rabbeinu: that there exists an ethereal coin of fire as well;
כִּי בְּכָל מַדְרֵיגוֹת הַיּוֹתֵר תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה יֵשׁ דּוּגְמָתָם בַּמָּרוֹם, דְּ״כֹּל פָּעַל ה׳ לַמַּעֲנֵהוּ״ (מִשְׁלֵי ט״ז:ד׳), לְקִילּוּסוֹ
for within all the lowest physical rungs of this world there exists a counterpart Above, for "Hashem has made everything for His purpose" (Mishlei 16:4), for His praise;
וְיוּכְלוּ לְהוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל (יִרְמְיָה ט״ו:י״ט), וְשֶׁיִּתְהַפֵּךְ הַדּוֹמֵם שֶׁהוּא יְסוֹד הָאַחֲרוֹן לְאֵשׁ שֶׁהוּא יְסוֹד הָעֶלְיוֹן
and man is empowered to "extract the precious from the vile" (Yirmiyah 15:19), transforming the inert mineral [the lowest element, earth] into celestial fire [the supreme element];
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִקְרָא ״אֵשׁ אֹכְלָה״ (דְּבָרִים ד:כד)
and the Blessed Name is termed "a consuming fire" (Devarim 4:24);
וְאָמַר לוֹ: ״זֶה יִתְּנוּ״ (שְׁמוֹת ל:יג)
and He commanded him: "This they shall give" (Shemos 30:13):
כִּי כְּשֶׁהָאָדָם מְדוּגָּל בִּפְרָט, צָרִיךְ לְעוֹרֵר נְקֻדַּת הָאֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב הַחֲקוּקָה בּוֹ, עַד שֶׁיִּמְסוֹר גַּם כָּל מְאוֹדוֹ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיְּזַכֵּךְ גַּם הַלְּבוּשׁ

for when an individual stands counted on his own, he must awaken the inner point of Yaakov's truth engraved within him, to the point of surrendering all his material wealth unto the Blessed Name to purify even the outermost garment.
וּבָזֶה הוּא הַתְנַשְּׂאוּת שֶׁל כָּל נֶפֶשׁ בִּפְרָט לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא
And herein lies the individual elevation of each soul in the Future:
דְּמִצַּד פְּנִימִיּוּתָן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה מָחוֹל לַצַּדִּיקִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סוֹף מַסֶּכֶת תַּעֲנִית (ל״א עַמּוּד א׳), שֶׁהֵם בְּעִיגּוּל
for from the perspective of their inward essence, the Holy One makes a dance for the righteous, as written at the end of Ta'anis (31a), seated in a circle;
וְאֵין חִילּוּק מַדְרֵיגוֹת, רַק הַחִילּוּק הוּא מִצַּד הַלְּבוּשִׁים שֶׁאֵין כָּל אֶחָד לָבוּשׁ בְּשָׁוֶה
and in a circle there is no hierarchy of rungs, the only differentiation between souls lying in their spiritual garments, wherein not everyone is attired alike;

כִּי פְּנִימִיּוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ, שֶׁהוּא הַנְּשָׁמָה הַטְּהוֹרָה שֶׁנָּתַן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בּוֹ שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, אֵין שָׁם חִילּוּק מַדְרֵיגוֹת, דְּכָךְ נָתַן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לָזֶה כְּמוֹ לָזֶה:
for the inwardness of the soul, which is the pure Neshamah imparted by the Blessed Name, possesses no distinction of rank, for Hashem endowed this soul equally as that soul.

7.h: The theme: Spiritual garments, the heart's dependence on money, and the equality of the half-shekel. All spiritual gradations arise strictly from human effort (hishtadlus) in this world, which refines the outer garments of the soul where free choice resides. Because the final deed is rooted in the initial thought (sof ma'aseh b'machshavah techilah), purifying the external garments clarifies the innermost depths. The Jerusalem Talmud notes: "the heart hangs upon the purse" (liba b'chisa talya, Yerushalmi Terumos 8:4)—even great Amoraim experienced a loss of composure in Torah study when suffering financial loss, because human vitality depends on nourishment purchased through money. Man was created last on the sixth day, like an honored guest entering a banquet hall prepared with all necessities (Sanhedrin 38a); the banquet corresponds to the primal darkness (chashocha d'reisha) which becomes light (nehura) when illuminated by the "lamp of Hashem, the soul of man." The spiritual order of devotion begins with "with all your heart" (inner devotion), extends to "with all your soul" (the animal soul governing the limbs of action), and culminates in "with all your might" (money, the outermost garment). The half-shekel sanctifies this inert material wealth, anchoring the end of deed into the pure root of truth where no prosecution can exist; hence "the rich shall not give more and the poor shall not give less," for at this foundational point of truth all Israel are completely equal.

p: וְהַמַּדְרֵיגוֹת הֵם רַק מִצַּד הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And spiritual gradations exist solely on account of human exertion in this world;
וְכָל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַלְּבוּשִׁים לַפְּנִימִיּוּת שֶׁבּוֹ הַבְּחִירָה
and all exertion in this world operates through the garments that clothe the inward soul, within which free choice is situated;
וְעַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת מַעֲמַקֵּי הַפְּנִימִיּוּת הוּא הִזְדַּכְּכוּת חִיצוֹנֵי הַחִיצוֹנִיּוּת
and through awakening the inner depths, the outermost garments are refined;
דְּ״סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה — בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה״ (פִּיּוּט לְכָה דוֹדִי)
for "the end of action is rooted in the initial thought";
וְ״לִבָּא בְּכִיסָא תַּלְיָא״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי (סוֹף פֶּרֶק ח׳ דִּתְרוּמוֹת הֲלָכָה ד׳)
and "the heart is suspended upon the purse," as written in the Yerushalmi [Terumos 8:4],
דְּלֹא הָיָה לוֹ יִשּׁוּב הַדַּעַת לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
where the Sage lacked composure for words of Torah following a financial loss;
וְאַף דְּהָיָה לוֹ לֵב רָחָב בַּתּוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדָה, וּבְוַדַּאי כָּל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה לֹא הָיָה אֶצְלוֹ כְּלוּם נֶגֶד כְּלַל הַתּוֹרָה
and although he possessed an expansive heart in Torah and divine service, and certainly all affairs of this world were as nothing to him compared to the Torah;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה לוֹ הֶרְגֵּשׁ בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב עַל יְדֵי הֶפְסֵד מָמוֹן
nevertheless, he experienced a disturbance in the depths of his heart through the loss of money.
כִּי כְּמוֹ שֶׁיָּצַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָאָדָם שֶׁיִּצְטָרֵךְ לְמָזוֹן לְהַחֲיוֹת נַפְשׁוֹ
For just as the Blessed Name formed man requiring food to sustain his soul,
וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ הָרוּחָנִית תְּלוּיָה בַּמָּזוֹן הַגַּשְׁמִי, וְ״אֵלָיו הוּא נֹשֵׂא אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ״ (דְּבָרִים כ״ד:ט״ו)
the spiritual soul depending upon physical nourishment, and "unto it he sets his soul" (Devarim 24:15);
כָּךְ יָצַר כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ לְצֹרֶךְ הָאָדָם, וְשֶׁיִּהְיוּ קִנְיָנָיו וּרְכוּשׁוֹ שֶׁמֵּהֶם יִקַּח מְזוֹנוֹ וּפַרְנָסָתוֹ, וְנִמְצָא חַיּוּתוֹ תָּלוּי בָּהֶם
so too He created the entire universe for the sake of man, that his possessions and wealth should provide his sustenance, his life depending upon them;
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא נִבְרָא אָחוֹר לְמַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית
wherefore man was created last in the work of Creation,
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין ל״ח עַמּוּד א׳): כְּאָדָם הַמֵּכִין כָּל צָרְכֵי סְעוּדָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַזְמִין אוֹרְחִים
the Sages stating (Sanhedrin 38a): like a host who prepares all banquet necessities and only then invites the guests;
וְכָל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ הֵם צָרְכֵי הַסְּעוּדָה, וְהֵם הַחֲשׁוֹכָא דִּבְרֵישָׁא
and the whole physical world constitutes the provisions of this banquet, representing the primal darkness (chashocha d'reisha);
כִּי מֵהֶם נִמְשָׁךְ כָּל הַחַשְׁכוּת וְהַהַאֲפָלָה לְלֵב הָאָדָם כְּשֶׁיִּשְׁתַּקַּע בָּהֶם
for from them arises all darkness and obscurity within the human heart when one sinks into them;
אֲבָל ״הֲדַר נְהוֹרָא״ עַל יְדֵי נֵר ה׳ נִשְׁמַת אָדָם הַמְּאִירָה לוֹ, נִסְתַּלֵּק הַחֹשֶׁךְ וְנַעֲשָׂה כּוּלּוֹ אוֹר
but afterward comes light (hadar nehura): through the "lamp of Hashem, the soul of man" (Mishlei 20:27) that illuminates him, the darkness is dispelled and all becomes light;
וְהַכֹּל לְצֹרֶךְ סְעוּדָתוֹ, סַעְדָּא דְּלִבָּא, וְהַלֵּב תָּלוּי בּוֹ
and everything serves the needs of his banquet, the support of the heart (sa'ada d'liba), the heart depending upon it;
וְכִידוּעַ עַל פָּסוּק ״נַפְשָׁם בָּהֶם תִּתְעַטָּף״ (תְּהִלִּים ק״ז:ה׳): שֶׁחֶלְקֵי הַנֶּפֶשׁ מְעוּטָּף בִּמְזוֹן הָאָדָם וְכֵן בְּכָל רְכוּשׁוֹ וְקִנְיָנָיו
and as is known on the verse "their soul fainted (tis'ataf, was enclothed) in them" (Tehillim 107:5): sparks of the soul are enclothed within human food and in all his wealth.
וְסֵדֶר הָעֲבוֹדָה ״בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ״ — הוּא בִּפְנִימִיּוּת
And the order of divine service begins "with all your heart"—in the inward depths;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ ״בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ״ — הוּא לְבוּשׁ הַלֵּב
and subsequently "with all your soul"—which is the outward garment of the heart;
וְשָׁם הַחֲטָאִים, דְּ״[כִּי אָדָם] אֵין צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״נֶפֶשׁ כִּי תֶחֱטָא״ (וַיִּקְרָא ד:ב)
and there sins occur, for "there is not a righteous man upon earth," as it is written: "If a soul (nefesh) shall sin" (Vayikra 4:2);
שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי נֶפֶשׁ הַבַּהֲמִית, דְּגַם כֵּן יֵשׁ לָהּ נֶפֶשׁ אַף שֶׁאֵין לָהּ פְּנִימִיּוּת שֶׁהוּא הַיִּרְאַת שָׁמַיִם שֶׁבַּלֵּב
which takes place through the animal soul, which likewise possesses a nefesh though lacking the inwardness of the fear of Heaven in the heart,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיוֹמָא ע״ב עַמּוּד ב׳ עַל פָּסוּק ״וְלֵב אָיִן״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ז:ט״ז), רַק כֹּחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה דְּמַזְקָא וְנָשְׁכָא וּבָעֲטָה
as written in Yoma (72b) on the verse "seeing he has no heart": possessing merely the active powers of goring, biting, and kicking;
זֶהוּ כֹּחַ הַנֶּפֶשׁ, וְצָרִיךְ לִמְסוֹר כָּל כֹּחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
this being the force of the Nefesh, requiring one to surrender all active bodily faculties unto the Blessed Name.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ, לִהְיוֹת מְנוּשָּׂא בִּפְרָטִיּוּתוֹ גַּם כֵּן, צָרִיךְ עוֹד ״בְּכָל מְאֹדֶךָ״
And afterward, to be elevated in one's individual standing, one requires further devotion "with all your might";
שֶׁהוּא הָרְכוּשׁ, לְבוּשׁ הַנֶּפֶשׁ, לְזַכֵּךְ גַּם זֶה לִמְסוֹר לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
which is wealth, the garment of the Nefesh, to refine it and surrender it unto the Blessed Name;
וְעַל כֵּן כֹּפֶר הַנֶּפֶשׁ הוּא הָרְכוּשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (פְּסָחִים קי״ח עַמּוּד א׳): ״עָשִׁיר בְּשׁוֹרוֹ, עָנִי בְּשֵׂיוֹ״
wherefore the soul-ransom is paid through property, as written (Pesachim 118a): "the rich man with his ox, the poor man with his sheep";
כִּי גַּם זֶה חֵלֶק מֵהַנֶּפֶשׁ הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט לִלְבוּשִׁים חִיצוֹנִים, דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה הֵם לְבוּשִׁים לָהּ, וּמִקְצָת נֶפֶשׁ כְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ
for this too is an extension of the soul spreading into outer garments, and a part of the soul is equivalent to the whole soul;
וְזֶהוּ כְּשֶׁנּוֹתֵן לַמְקַטְרֵג, אֲבָל הַבָּא לִהְיוֹת מְנוּשָּׂא צָרִיךְ לִיתֵּן כֹּפֶר נַפְשׁוֹ לַה׳ שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל עוֹד מְקַטְרֵג לִשְׁלוֹט עָלָיו
and this occurs when one yields to the accuser, whereas one who comes to be elevated must offer his soul-ransom unto Hashem, that the prosecutor may have no dominion over him.
וְהוּא הַמַּטְבֵּעַ שֶׁל אֵשׁ, שֶׁיַּכְנִיס קְדוּשָׁה גַּם בְּכָל הַחָמְרִיּוּת עַד שֶׁיִּקָּרֵא שֵׁם ״קֹדֶשׁ״ גַּם עַל הַשֶּׁקֶל וּמַטְבֵּעַ הַדּוֹמֶמֶת
And this is the coin of fire: instilling holiness into all materiality until the title "Holy" is designated even upon the shekel and the inanimate coin;
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָאֱמֶת שֶׁבְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה, שֶׁבּוֹ נָעוּץ סוֹף הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
operating through awakening the root of truth in the initial thought, wherein the culmination of action is embedded;
וְעַל אוֹתָהּ נְקֻדָּה אֵין שׁוּם מְקוֹם קִטְרוּג
and against that inner point of truth no prosecution can ever stand;
וְעַל כֵּן: ״הֶעָשִׁיר לֹא יַרְבֶּה וְהַדַּל לֹא יַמְעִיט״ (שְׁמוֹת ל:טו), כִּי בִּנְקֻדָּה זוֹ הַכֹּל שָׁוִים:
therefore: "The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less" (Shemos 30:15), for at this foundational point all are completely equal.

7.h: The theme: The half-shekel (machatzis ha-shekel) as the human vessel of deficiency yearning for completion. The surrender of man's material might (me'od) stems from the innermost point of the soul: the letter Yud, which equals ten gerahs, representing Chochmah drawn from Keser (the full shekel of twenty gerahs / Ayin). Human perception is inherently incomplete and filled with deficiencies; man attains spiritual perception precisely because a deficient creature yearns for wholeness. Hence the dimensions of the holy Ark were all halves (Shemos 25:10), for Torah departs from high places and seeks the humble and deficient (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2; Ta'anis 7a: "If they were ugly they would have learned more"). The Torah was given to mortals wrestling with the yetzer hara rather than angels (Shabbos 89a), because Torah is attained through recognizing that alone man is merely "half a body" (pelag gufa), finding completion only through cleaving to his Creator. The ten gerahs correspond to Sefer Yetzirah's dictum "ten and not eleven"—the Central Pillar (Amuda d'Emtza'ita) and the truth of Yaakov (nachalah bli metzarim). One must contract his intellect ("the rich shall not increase", Shemos 30:15) so as not to grasp beyond his spiritual capacity: "in that which is too wondrous for you, do not inquire" (Chagigah 13a).

p: וְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת מְסִירָה זוֹ דִּ״מְאֹד״ הַבָּא מִצַּד הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַנְּקֻדָּה שֶׁבַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ
And the awakening of this surrender of one's material might (me'od), which arises through stirring the primal point at the soul's root;
דָּבָר זֶה שָׁוֶה בְּכָל מַחֲצִית הַשֶּׁקֶל שֶׁהוּא יוּ״ד שֶׁהִיא נְקֻדָּה
this reality is equal across all Israel through the half-shekel which is the letter Yud, being a point,
וְהִיא הַחָכְמָה כִּידוּעַ, הַנִּמְשֶׁכֶת מֵהַכֶּתֶר שֶׁהוּא הַכַּ״ף שֶׁקֶל הַשָּׁלֵם
and Yud is Chochmah as is known, drawn from Keser which is the letter Chaf (twenty gerahs), the complete shekel,
וְהוּא הָ״אַיִן״ דְּשָׁם אֵין הַשָּׂגָה
and Keser is the realm of Ayin [Nothingness] where conscious human perception cannot reach;
כִּי כָּל הַשָּׂגַת אָדָם אֵין בּוֹ שְׁלֵימוּת, דְּכוּלּוֹ מָלֵא חֶסְרוֹנוֹת
for all human perception lacks intrinsic perfection, being entirely filled with deficiencies,
וְכָל הַשָּׂגָתוֹ הוּא רַק מִצַּד זֶה שֶׁתְּשׁוּקָתוֹ לְמִילּוּי חֶסְרוֹנוֹתָיו, דְּבַעַל חִסָּרוֹן מִשְׁתּוֹקֵק לְהַשְׁלָמָה
and a person's entire perception arises solely because he yearns to fill his deficiencies, for one who is deficient longs for completion;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ קַמָּאֵי בְּטַעַם מִדּוֹת הָאָרוֹן הַכֹּל חֲצָאִים
and as the early commentators wrote regarding the reason why the measurements of the Ark were all broken halves (two and a half cubits, a cubit and a half; Shemos 25:10),
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַכְּלִי קִיבּוּל לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
teaching that a broken, humble vessel is the true receptacle for words of Torah;
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה א:ב) דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מַנִּיחִים מָקוֹם גָּבוֹהַּ וְהוֹלְכִים לְמָקוֹם נָמוּךְ
and along the lines of what they expounded (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2): words of Torah abandon a high place and flow to a low place;
וּבְתַעֲנִית (ז׳ רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דְּאִי הָווּ סָנוּ הָווּ גְּמִירֵי טְפֵי״
and in Ta'anis (7a): "If they were ugly they would have learned even more";
וְהַכַּוָּונָה עַל כֵּיעוּר נַפְשׁוֹ מִצַּד הַחֶסְרוֹנוֹת שֶׁבְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ
the inner intent referring to the perceived ugliness of one's soul from the deficiencies inherent in his worldly nature,
דְּעַל כֵּן נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לִבְנֵי אָדָם וְלֹא לְמַלְאָכִים
wherefore the Torah was given to human beings and not to ministering angels,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא (שַׁבָּת פ״ט עַמּוּד א׳) דְּאָמַר לָהֶם: ״כְּלוּם יֵצֶר רָע יֵשׁ בֵּינֵיכֶם״
as written in Shabbat (89a) where Moshe answered the angels: "Does an evil inclination exist among you?!";
וְעַל כֵּן ״לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא״ (דְּבָרִים ל:יב)
and therefore "it is not in heaven" (Devarim 30:12);
דְּעִיקַּר הַשָּׂגַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא רַק מִצַּד מַה שֶּׁמַּכִּיר חֶסְרוֹנוֹ
for the primary attainment of words of Torah occurs solely through recognizing one's deficiency,
וְשֶׁצָּרִיךְ הַשְׁלָמָה עַל יְדֵי הַדְּבֵיקוּת בְּקוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא הַמַּשְׁלִימוֹ
and realizing that he requires completion through cleaving unto his Creator Who alone completes him,
וּ״כְשֶׁאֲנִי לְעַצְמִי — מָה אֲנִי״ (אָבוֹת א:יד), וְהוּא כְּמוֹ פְּלַג גּוּף
and "when I am for myself, what am I?" (Avos 1:14), standing like merely half a body;
וְעַל כֵּן הַחָכְמָה שֶׁהוּא תְּחִלַּת הַשָּׂגָה יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן רְמוּזָה בְּמַחֲצִית הַשֶּׁקֶל, וְאֵין שְׁלֵימוּת אֶלָּא אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
wherefore Chochmah, being the inception of conscious perception ex nihilo from Ayin, is alluded to in the half-shekel, for perfection resides with the Blessed Name alone;
וְהָאָדָם נוֹתֵן מַחֲצִית הַשֶּׁקֶל הַיְינוּ כְּלַל קוֹמָתוֹ שֶׁהוּא יוּ״ד גֵּרָה
and man gives the half-shekel, which embodies his entire stature of ten gerahs;
״עֶשֶׂר וְלֹא אַחַד עָשָׂר״ (סֵפֶר יְצִירָה א:ד) מִצַּד עַמּוּדָא דְּאֶמְצָעִיתָא
"ten and not eleven" (Sefer Yetzirah 1:4) from the aspect of the Central Pillar,
הוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ ״אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב״ (מִיכָה ז:כ), נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים
which is the root of "truth to Jacob" (Michah 7:20), a boundless heritage (nachalah bli metzarim, Shabbos 118b),
וְיוּכַל לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט יוֹתֵר מִכְּפִי מַדְרֵגַת קוֹמָתוֹ
and because this boundless truth could expand beyond the proper measure of his stature;
וְעַל זֶה צָרִיךְ צִמְצוּם: ״[הֶעָשִׁיר] לֹא יַרְבֶּה״ (שְׁמוֹת ל:טו), שֶׁלֹּא יַחְשׁוֹק לְהַשָּׂגָה יוֹתֵר מִמַּדְרֵיגָתוֹ
toward this one requires holy contraction (tzimtzum): "the rich shall not give more" (Shemos 30:15), that he not lust for perception beyond his spiritual capacity;
וּ״בַמֻּפְלָא מִמְּךָ אַל תִּדְרוֹשׁ [וּבַמְכֻסֶּה מִמְּךָ אַל תַּחְקֹר]״ (חֲגִיגָה י״ג עַמּוּד א׳)
and "in that which is too wondrous for you, do not inquire, and in that which is hidden from you, do not search" (Chagigah 13a);
״מִמְּךָ״ דַּיְיקָא, כְּפִי מַדְרֵיגָתְךָ, לְכָל אֶחָד יֵשׁ מַה שֶּׁמֻּפְלָא מִמֶּנּוּ, אַךְ דִּלְגַבֵּי אַחֵר אֵין זֶה מֻפְלָא עֲדַיִין:

"from you" (mimcha) specifically: according to your own spiritual level, for every individual has that which is wondrous beyond him, though relative to another greater soul it may not be wondrous yet.

7.h: The theme: "Ten and not eleven, ten and not nine": Balancing Da'as and Keser, and the atonement of the half-shekel. The Arizal explains that "ten and not eleven" means one must never count Keser and Da'as together: Da'as is the active perception attained through the Holy Spirit (ruach ha-kodesh, Rashi on Shemos 31:3), while Keser is the transcendent surrounding light (or makif) grasped only through the realization that "the ultimate knowledge is that we do not know" (tachlis ha-yedi'ah she-lo neda). To breach this boundary and try to comprehend Keser with mortal intellect is dangerous ("If you have found honey, eat only as much as is sufficient for you", Mishlei 25:16). "The rich in perception shall not give more" (lo yarbeh—ten and not eleven); and "the poor in perception shall not give less" (lo yam'it—ten and not nine, meaning one must not neglect Da'as and fail to achieve what is within his grasp). Every Jew possesses an intrinsic capacity to perceive the absolute truth that "Hashem our God, Hashem is One and there is none else." Giving the physical half-shekel stirs this primal point of truth through surrendering wealth, wiping away (kinu'ach / kapparah) the defilement of sins, revealing that in their essence all sins are like the preordained years of Creation.

p: וְזֶהוּ ״וְלֹא אַחַד עָשָׂר״, דְּפֵירֵשׁ הָאֲרִיזַ״ל: שֶׁלֹּא לַחְשׁוֹב כֶּתֶר וָדַעַת יַחַד
And this is the meaning of "and not eleven," which the Arizal explained: that one must not count Keser [Crown] and Da'as [Knowledge] together (as two distinct Sefirot in the ten);
וּבֶאֱמֶת זֶה מַשְׁלִים הָיָה בַּחִיצוֹנִיּוּת וְזֶה בַּפְּנִימִיּוּת
and in truth, one completes the ten in externality and the other in internality;
הַיְינוּ ״דַּעַת״ הוּא הַהַשָּׂגָה שֶׁאָדָם מַשִּׂיג מִצַּד רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁבּוֹ
meaning: Da'as is the conscious perception that man attains through the Holy Spirit within him,
כִּדְפֵירֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י פָּרָשַׁת תִּשָּׂא (שְׁמוֹת ל״א:ג׳): ״דַּעַת — זֶה רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ״
as Rashi explained in Parashat Ki Tisa (Shemos 31:3): "'and in knowledge'—this is the Holy Spirit";
וְ״כֶתֶר״ הוּא מַה שֶּׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם וְעוֹמֵד בְּסוֹד מַקִּיף
and Keser is that which transcends human perception, standing in the mystical secret of the surrounding light (or makif);
וְגַם בָּזֶה יֵשׁ הַשָּׂגָה דְּ״תַכְלִית הַיְּדִיעָה — שֶׁלֹּא נֵדַע״
and within Keser too there is perception, through the realization that "the ultimate end of knowledge is to know that we do not know" (Chovot HaLevavot);
דְּזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית וּקְצֵה מַדְרֵגַת בַּהַשָּׂגָה: לְהַשִּׂיג שֶׁיֵּשׁ עוֹד דַּרְגָּה וְהַשָּׂגָה שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג
for this is the absolute pinnacle and frontier of perception: to grasp that there exists an infinite dimension and light which is impossible to comprehend;
