וְעַל כֵּן מִצַּד הַהַשָּׂגָה הַקּוֹמָה הוּא יוּ״ד בְּצֵירוּף הַדַּעַת שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחַ הַהַשָּׂגָה
wherefore from the aspect of conscious perception the spiritual stature is ten through the inclusion of Da'as, which is the root of perception;
וּמִצַּד הֶעְדֵּר הַהַשָּׂגָה וְתַכְלִית הַיְּדִיעָה הַקּוֹמָה הוּא בְּצֵירוּף הַכֶּתֶר, שֶׁהוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּשֶׁלֹּא נֵדַע וְתַכְלִית הַיְּדִיעָה
while from the aspect of the transcendence of perception and ultimate unknowing, the stature is ten through the inclusion of Keser, which is the root of unknowing and ultimate wisdom.
אֲבָל לָבוֹא לְגֶדֶר הַדַּעַת וְהַיְדִיעָה הַגְּמוּרָה גַּם אוֹתָהּ מַדְרֵגָה דְּלֹא נֵדַע וְשֶׁהוּא בַּמֻּפְלָא מִמֶּנּוּ, זֶה דָּבָר שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר
But to attempt to bring into the domain of conscious Da'as and intellectual comprehension that sublime rung of unknowing which is wondrous beyond us, this is impossible,
וְ״דְּבַשׁ מָצָאתָ — אֱכֹל דַּיֶּךָּ פֶּן [תִּשְׂבָּעֶנּוּ וַהֲקֵאתוֹ]״ (מִשְׁלֵי כ״ה:ט״ז)
and "Have you found honey? Eat so much as is sufficient for you, lest you be filled therewith, and vomit it" (Mishlei 25:16);
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״הֶעָשִׁיר״ — בְּהַשָּׂגָה בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת — ״לֹא יַרְבֶּה״ (שְׁמוֹת ל:טו)
and concerning this it is said: "The rich"—rich in expansive intellectual perception—"shall not increase" (Shemos 30:15);
״וְהַדַּל״ — בְּהַשָּׂגָה, דָּא צַדִּיק הַמִּשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּמַעֲשִׂים בְּפֹעַל וְלֹא בִּפְנִימִיּוּת כָּל כָּךְ — ״לֹא יַמְעִיט״
and "the poor"—poor in perception, namely the righteous person who exerts himself in concrete deeds and not in inward contemplation—"shall not diminish",
מִקּוֹמַת הַשָּׂגַת הַחָכְמָה בִּפְנִימִיּוּת, דְּיוּ״ד וְלֹא תֵּשַׁע
from the full stature of attaining Chochmah in internality, which is "ten and not nine";
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יַשִּׂיג הַכֶּתֶר וְהַדַּעַת גַּם שְׁנֵיהֶם
meaning: that he not forfeit both Keser and Da'as together,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ שׁוּם יְדִיעָה וְהַשָּׂגָה גַּם בַּמַּה שֶּׁאֶפְשָׁר לֵידַע
that is, that he should not remain devoid of all knowledge and perception even in that which is accessible to know,
לֹא מִצַּד הַמֻּפְלָא שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לֵידַע
not out of humility before the wondrous which cannot be known;
דְּכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא הִשִּׂיג עֲדַיִין מַה שֶּׁאֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְהַשִּׂיג כְּפִי מַדְרֵיגַת הַשָּׂגָתוֹ, לֹא הִגִּיעַ עֲדַיִין לְמַדְרֵיגַת הַיְּדִיעָה שֶׁלֹּא נֵדַע
for as long as he has not attained what is possible for him to attain according to his capacity, he has not yet arrived at the true level of knowing that we do not know,
שֶׁהוּא רַק כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לַמֻּפְלָא אַחַר שֶׁהִשִּׂיג וְיָדַע כָּל מַה שֶּׁאֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לֵידַע מִצַּד הַדַּעַת שֶׁבּוֹ
which is reached only when one touches the wondrous after having grasped all that is possible to know through the Da'as within him;
וְצָרִיךְ שֶׁגַּם הַדַּל לֹא יַמְעִיט מֵהִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַשָּׂגַת פְּנִימִיּוּת הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבּוֹ כְּפִי הַשָּׂגָתוֹ
and it is necessary that even the poor in intellect not diminish from awakening the inward Chochmah within him according to his capacity.
דְּכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַשָּׂגָה מַה שֶּׁיּוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג מִצַּד שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ שֶׁהִיא חֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמַּעַל
For every single Jew possesses an intrinsic root of perception that he can attain through his soul-root which is an actual divine portion from Above,
שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגַת הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ דַּה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ ה׳ אֶחָד וְאֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ
which is the perception of ultimate truth: that Hashem is our God, Hashem is One, and there is none else beside Him;
וּבִנְתִינַת הַשְּׁקָלִים בְּפֹעַל הָיָה הִתְעוֹרְרוּת נְקֻדַּת הַשָּׂגַת הָאֱמֶת שֶׁבְּכֹחַ הַנֶּפֶשׁ
and in the concrete giving of the shekels there occurred the awakening of this point of truth within the soul;
כִּי כָּךְ הֵם כֹּחַ כָּל הַמִּצְוֹת שֶׁהֵם נוֹתְנִים קְדוּשָׁה בַּנֶּפֶשׁ עַל מַה שֶּׁהוּא רְמִיזַת הַמִּצְוָה
for such is the power of all commandments: they impart holiness to the soul corresponding to that which is hinted within the mitzvah;
וּמִצַּד מַה שֶּׁמַּתְחִיל לִמְסוֹר קְצָת מִמְּאוֹדוֹ וּרְכוּשׁוֹ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and by beginning to surrender a portion of his wealth and possessions unto the Blessed Name,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְעוֹרֵר הַנְּקֻדָּה דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּרְדִיפַת הַשָּׂגַת הָאֱמֶת
through this is awakened the inner point of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, in pursuing the attainment of truth,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא הַכֹּחַ דִּמְסִירַת הַ״מְּאֹד״ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
through which is granted the strength to surrender one's material might unto the Blessed Name;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא הַכֹּפֶר, פֵּירוּשׁ ״קִינּוּחַ״ כִּדְפֵירֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״ב:כ״א) עַל כַּפָּרָה, לַנֶּפֶשׁ מִלִּכְלוּכֵי חֲטָאָיו

and through this is accomplished the ransom (kofer), meaning "wiping clean" (kinu'ach) as Rashi explained in several places (Bereishis 32:21) regarding atonement (kapparah), cleansing the soul from the soil of its sins;
כִּי כְּשֶׁמִּתְגַּלֶּה נְקֻדַּת הָאֱמֶת, אֵין שָׁם חֵטְא כְּלָל
for when the point of truth is revealed, no sin exists there at all,
כְּמוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא דְּיִתְגַּלֶּה דַּ״חֲטָאֵיכֶם... כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְּרֵאשִׁית״ (שַׁבָּת פ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳):
as in the World to Come, when it will be revealed that "your sins... are like these cosmic years that have been ordered and advancing since the six days of Creation" (Shabbos 89b).

7.h: The theme: The longing of the heart, the wisdom of the nations, Haman's ten thousand talents of silver, and the triumph of the Omer offering. The inner point of truth awakens through the yearning of the heart for Hashem ("it is revealed and known before You that our will is to perform Your will", Berachos 17a), where the "yeast in the dough" has no power. All spiritual attainment is called a "find" (metzi'ah), for "if you toiled and found—believe" (Megillah 6b); Hashem grants wisdom to the wise (Daniel 2:21) because wisdom itself is defined by the passionate desire to seek it ("I love them that love me, and those that seek me early shall find me", Mishlei 8:17). The ancient philosophers understood this, calling themselves "lovers of wisdom" (philosophers in Greek), a concept stolen from Israel. On the first of Adar, announcement is made concerning the shekels to precede our shekels to Haman's shekels (Megillah 13b). Haman, recognized as a sinister sage ("wise to do evil", Yirmiyah 4:22), knew that the universe was created for Israel; he offered ten thousand talents of silver to outbid Israel, assuming he could replace them as Hashem's chosen. Yet Haman's silver was overthrown by the handful of barley from the Omer offering (komotz se'orim, Megillah 16a; Vayikra 23:10). The Omer is the "jealousy offering" of the Woman of Valor, proving her unshakeable fidelity against the harlot (Zohar II, 148b). It is the "dinner of herbs where love is" (Mishlei 15:17) which excels the "stalled ox" of the wicked (Balaam's seven altars and Haman's silver). Although Israel may be poor in deeds ("I am brought low, and Hashem saves me", Tehillim 116:6), Hashem beholds their inward love and accepts the modest Omer of barley. By reading Parashat Shekalim, our lips pay the calves of our offerings (u-neshalmah farim sefaseinu, Hoshea 14:3), shutting the mouth of the prosecuting Satan.

p: וְעִיקַּר הִתְעוֹרְרוּת נְקֻדָּה זוֹ הוּא בְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַחֵשֶׁק וְהַתְּשׁוּקָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב פְּנִימִיּוּת כָּל אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
And the primary awakening of this point occurs through stirring the longing and yearning within the inward heart of every Jew toward the Blessed Name,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל מִצַּד שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיַּהֲדוּת שֶׁבּוֹ מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which exists within every single Jew from the root of Judaism inherited from Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק הָיָה קוֹרֵא (בְּרָכוֹת י״ז עַמּוּד א׳): ״גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנְךָ וְכוּלֵיהּ״
as written in Berachos (17a): "It is revealed and known before You that our will is to perform Your will, etc.";
הַיְינוּ עֹומֶק פְּנִימִיּוּת הָרָצוֹן, דְּשָׁם אֵין יַד הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה שׁוֹלֶטֶת
meaning the transcendent depth of inward will, where the hand of the "yeast in the dough" [the yetzer hara] has no dominion;
דְּהוּא יוֹשֵׁב רַק עַל מִפְתְּחֵי הַלֵּב וּבַחִיצוֹנִיּוּת הָרָצוֹן שֶׁבְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט לְכֹחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה
for the yetzer sits merely at the portals of the heart and in the external will of revealed consciousness extending into active limbs,
שָׁם הוּא יוֹשֵׁב וּמֵסִית וּמְפַתֶּה, לֹא בִּפְנִימִיּוּת
there it perches, incites, and seduces, but never in the inward depth;
וְהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתְחָלַת חֵשֶׁק הָרָצוֹן לְשׁוּם דָּבָר, וְהָעִיקָּר הוּא הַחֵשֶׁק
and that inward depth is the primal source of the will's desire for anything, and the essence of all devotion is this longing;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּמְגִלָּה ו׳ עַמּוּד ב׳: ״׳יָגַעְתִּי וְלֹא מָצָאתִי׳ — אַל תַּאֲמִין״
as written in Megillah (6b): "'I toiled and did not find'—do not believe";
כִּי כָּל הַשָּׂגָה וּמַדְרֵגָה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי הַיְגִיעָה, שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי הַחֵשֶׁק וְהַהִשְׁתּוֹקְקוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם לְדָבָר זֶה, וְלֹא יָנוּחַ וְלֹא יִשְׁקוֹט עַד שֶׁיִּמְצָא
for every spiritual perception and rung is attained solely through toil, which is fueled by the longing and passion a person possesses for this goal, resting neither day nor night until he finds it;
וְגוּף הַהַשָּׂגָה נִקְרָא ״מְצִיאָה״, דִּבְאֶמֶת ״ה׳ יִתֵּן חָכְמָה״ (מִשְׁלֵי ב:ו)
and the perception itself is called a "find" (metzi'ah), for in truth "Hashem gives wisdom" (Mishlei 2:6);
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאָדָם לְהַשִּׂיג שׁוּם דָּבָר בְּכֹחוֹ וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ כְּלָל
and it is impossible for man to attain anything through his independent human strength and striving at all;
אֶלָּא דְּהוּא ״יָהֵב חָכְמְתָא לְחַכִּימִין״ (דָּנִיֵּאל ב:כא), וְאֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת חַכִּימִין מִקּוֹדֶם
but rather He "gives wisdom unto the wise" (Daniel 2:21)—and how could one be wise beforehand?
אֲבָל זֶהוּ כָּל חָכְמַת הָאָדָם: מַה שֶּׁחוֹשֵׁק לִשְׁקוֹד וּלְיַיגֵּעַ לְהַשִּׂיג הַחָכְמָה
Rather, this is the entire wisdom of man: his passionate longing to diligently toil to attain wisdom;
וְהַחָכְמָה קוֹרְאָה בְּרֹאשׁ הוֹמִיּוֹת: ״אֲנִי אֹהֲבַי אֵהָב וּמְשַׁחֲרַי יִמְצָאֻנְנִי״ (מִשְׁלֵי ח:יז)
and Wisdom cries out at the bustling crossroads: "I love them that love me, and those that seek me early shall find me" (Mishlei 8:17).
וְאַף חַכְמֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הַקַּדְמוֹנִים הִשִּׂיגוּ דָּבָר זֶה, שֶׁקָּרְאוּ לְחַכְמֵיהֶם ״פִּילוֹסוֹפִים״
And even the ancient sages of the nations grasped this truth, calling their wise men "philosophers";
דְּפֵירוּשׁ הַמִּלָּה בִּלְשׁוֹן יְוָנִי ״אוֹהֲבֵי חָכְמָה״, לֹא ״חֲכָמִים״, דְּזֶה כָּל חָכְמָתָם שֶׁהֵם אוֹהֲבֵי חָכְמָה
the meaning of the word in Greek being "lovers of wisdom" and not "wise men," for their entire wisdom consisted in being lovers of wisdom;
וּבִלְתִּי סָפֵק גָּנְבוּ דָּבָר זֶה מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
and without doubt they plundered this concept from the Children of Israel.
וּבְאֶחָד בַּאֲדָר מַשְׁמִיעִין עַל הַשְּׁקָלִים (שְׁקָלִים פֶּרֶק א׳ מִשְׁנָה א׳), לְהַקְדִּים שְׁקָלֵינוּ לִשְׁקָלָיו שֶׁל הָמָן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מְגִלָּה י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳)
And on the first of Adar proclamation is made regarding the shekels (Shekalim 1:1), to precede our shekels to the shekels of Haman, as written in Megillah (13b);
כִּי נְתִינַת הַשְּׁקָלִים הִיא מְסִירַת עִיקַּר כִּיסּוּפָיו וַחֲשָׁקָיו לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for the giving of the shekels represents surrendering one's ultimate yearnings and desires unto the Blessed Name;
דְּהַיְינוּ לְהַשָּׂגַת אֲמִיתָּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַחָכְמָה הָאֲמִיתִּית
namely toward the attainment of His divine truth, this being the essence of true Chochmah,
שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן ״הַכָּרָה״ בַּאֲרַמִּית, לְהַכִּיר אֲמִיתָּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
which in Aramaic translates as "recognition" (hakara), recognizing His divine truth;
דְּזֶה כָּל הַשָּׂגַת חָכְמָה שֶׁנָּתַן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לַתַּחְתּוֹנִים, שֶׁבְּחָכְמָתָם יוּכְלוּ לְהַשִּׂיג שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹרֵא, דְּכֹל פָּעַל לְקִילּוּסוֹ
for this is the entire purpose of wisdom given to earthly mortals: that through their wisdom they recognize there is a Creator, and that all was made for His praise.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (אֵיכָה רַבָּתִי פָּרָשָׁה ב:יג): ״יֵשׁ חָכְמָה בַּגּוֹיִם — תַּאֲמֵן״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״[הֲלוֹא בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא נְאֻם ה׳] וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי חֲכָמִים מֵאֱדוֹם״ (עֹבַדְיָה א:ח)

And the Sages stated (Eichah Rabbah 2:13): "If a man tells you: There is wisdom among the nations—believe him," as written: "Shall I not in that day, says Hashem, even destroy the wise men out of Edom?" (Ovadyah 1:8);
הַיְינוּ גַּוָּון שֶׁל חָכְמָה שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן הַשָּׂגַת אֱמֶת בְּצַד מַה
meaning a shade of wisdom which is likewise an attainment of truth in a certain dimension;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּמְגִלָּה (ט״ז עַמּוּד א׳): ״הָאוֹמֵר דְּבַר חָכְמָה בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם — נִקְרָא חָכָם״
and as written in Megillah (16a): "Whoever utters a word of wisdom among the nations is called a sage,"
מֵחֲכָמָיו דְּהָמָן שֶׁהִשִּׂיגוּ הָאֱמֶת שֶׁיִּפּוֹל לִפְנֵי זֶרַע הַיְּהוּדִים
derived from the wise men of Haman who recognized the truth that he would fall before the seed of the Jews (Esther 6:13);
דְּזֶה כָּל חָכְמַת אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם: שֶׁיַּשִּׂיגוּ מַעֲלַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא יוּכְלוּ לָהֶם
for this is the ultimate wisdom of the nations: to recognize the supreme elevation of the Children of Israel and that they cannot prevail against them;
דִּלְהַשִּׂיג חָכְמַת הָאֱמֶת שֶׁהִיא חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה, דְּהַיְינוּ לְהַשִּׂיג אֲמִיתָּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם זֶה, דְּ״לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי״ (תְּהִלִּים קמ״ז:כ׳)
for to attain the wisdom of absolute Truth which is the wisdom of the Torah—comprehending His divine reality—is impossible for them, for "He has not dealt so with any nation" (Tehillim 147:20);
״וְהָאוֹמֵר ׳יֵשׁ תּוֹרָה בַּגּוֹיִם׳ — אַל תַּאֲמֵן״ (אֵיכָה רַבָּתִי שָׁם)
and "If a man tells you: 'There is Torah among the nations'—do not believe him" (Eichah Rabbah ibid.);
וְהַשָּׂגַת אֲמִיתָּתוֹ — זֶהוּ תּוֹרָה
and attaining His divine truth—this is Torah;
אֲבָל הַשָּׂגַת מַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל, זֶה הִשִּׂיג גַּם בִּלְעָם הָרָשָׁע שֶׁהָיָה מֵחַכְמֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, דְּזֶה נִקְרָא ״חָכְמָה״
but grasping the elevation of Israel was attained even by Balaam the Wicked who was a sage of the nations, this being termed "wisdom";
וְכָל מֶמְשָׁלָה שֶׁהוּא כָּבוֹד שֶׁחָלַק לְבָשָׂר וָדָם, הוּא מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה
and all earthly dominion, which is honor imparted unto flesh and blood, derives from wisdom,
כִּי ״כָּבוֹד חֲכָמִים יִנְחָלוּ״ (מִשְׁלֵי ג:לה), וְנֶאֱמַר: ״בִּי מְלָכִים יִמְלֹכוּ״ (שָׁם ח:טו)
for "the wise shall inherit honor" (Mishlei 3:35), and "By Me kings reign" (ibid. 8:15);
וְעַל כֵּן יֵשׁ מֶמְשָׁלָה בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְשָׁעָה גַּם בָּהֶם חֲכָמִים, עַד לֶעָתִיד דְּ״וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר״ וְאָבַד מֶמְשַׁלְתָּם

wherefore there exists temporary dominion among the nations in this world because sages temporarily exist among them, until the Future when "I will destroy the wise men out of Edom" and their dominion shall perish.
וַהֲסָרַת טַבַּעַת לְהָמָן, דְּאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (אֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה ג:ז) ״מֶלֶךְ״ סְתָם בַּמְּגִלָּה — בְּמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים מְדַבֵּר
And the removal of the signet ring to Haman, regarding which the Sages stated (Esther Rabbah 3:7) that an unqualified "king" in the Megillah refers to the King of kings;
הַיְינוּ דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נָתַן לוֹ מֶמְשָׁלָה, וַדַּאי הָיָה בוֹ חָכְמָה, הַיְינוּ לְרָעָה
meaning that when the Blessed Name granted him dominion, there certainly resided wisdom within him, albeit for evil;
דְּגַם זֶה נִקְרָא ״חָכְמָה״ בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב: ״חֲכָמִים הֵמָּה לְהָרַע״ (יִרְמְיָה ד:כב), וּבְיוֹנָדָב: ״[וִיהוֹנָדָב הָיָה] אִישׁ חָכָם מְאֹד״ (שְׁמוּאֵל ב י״ג:ג׳) לְרִשְׁעָה
for this too is termed "wisdom" in Scripture: "they are wise to do evil" (Yirmiyah 4:22), and of Yonadav: "he was a very wise man" (II Shmuel 13:3) in villainy;
וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (מְגִלָּה י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳): ״לֵיכָּא דְּיָדַע לִישָׁנָא בִישָׁא כְּהָמָן״
and this is what they meant: "there was none who knew how to formulate malicious slander like Haman";
דְּחָכְמָה נִקְרָא רַק הַכָּרַת הָאֱמֶת, וְהוּא יָדַע לְקַטְרֵג דְּבָרִים שֶׁהָיָה קִטְרוּג בֶּאֱמֶת כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה
for wisdom means the perception of truth, and he knew how to formulate accusations that were genuine spiritual indictments Above,
עַד שֶׁפָּעַל שֶׁנֶּחְתַּם הַגְּזֵירָה מִלְּמַעְלָה רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן
to the point that he caused the decree to be sealed Above, God protect us;
וְזֶהוּ כָּל ״חָכָם לְהָרַע״, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ז׳ עַמּוּד א׳) בְּבִלְעָם: דְּיָדַע לְכַוֵּון שָׁעָה שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא כּוֹעֵס
and this is the nature of one who is "wise to do evil," as they related (Berachos 7a) of Balaam: that he knew how to target the precise moment when the Holy One is angry.
וּמִצַּד הַחָכְמָה הָיָה וַדַּאי מַכִּיר זֶה דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָעוֹלָם בְּלֹא יִשְׂרָאֵל
And from this perspective of wisdom Haman certainly recognized that the world cannot exist without Israel;
וְעַל כֵּן הִתְחַכֵּם בְּרִשְׁעוּתוֹ לוֹמַר: ״עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים כִּכַּר כֶּסֶף אֶשְׁקוֹל עַל יְדֵי עֹשֵׂי הַמְּלָאכָה לְהָבִיא אֶל גִּנְזֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ״ (אֶסְתֵּר ג:ט)

wherefore he schemed in his villainy to say: "I will weigh ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of those that have charge of the business, to bring it into the king's treasuries" (Esther 3:9);
הַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים
meaning homiletically the King of kings of kings:
שֶׁאָמַר: כָּל הַיְּקָרוּת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לִמְסוֹר כָּל הַכִּיסּוּפִין וַחֲשָׁקוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, הִנֵּה גַּם הוּא יָכוֹל זֶה וְלִהְיוֹת הוּא תְּמוּרָתָם
asserting: all the preciousness of Israel lies in surrendering their yearnings and might unto the Blessed Name, behold I too can surrender this wealth and stand as their substitute!
וְהוּא הָיָה הַמַּתְחִיל לַחְשׁוֹב שֶׁהוּא יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה י״ד:י׳): דַּעֲתִידִים אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לוֹמַר ״אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל״
And Haman was the pioneer who first presumed that he was Israel, as the Sages stated (Bamidbar Rabbah 14:10): the nations are destined to claim "We are Israel";
וּמִמֶּנּוּ הָיָה הַתְחָלַת זֶה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״לְמִי יַחְפֹּץ הַמֶּלֶךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת יְקָר [יוֹתֵר מִמֶּנִּי]״ (אֶסְתֵּר ו:ו)
and from Haman was the inception of this, as written: "To whom would the king delight to do honor more than to myself?" (Esther 6:6);
דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים, שֶׁהִכִּיר בְּחָכְמָתוֹ דְּהַצְלָחָתוֹ הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁרָצָה לְרוֹמְמוֹ
meaning the King of kings, Haman recognizing in his dark wisdom that his meteoric rise derived from the Blessed Name Who willed to exalt him,
וְשֶׁהִסְכִּים עַל יָדוֹ בְּאִיבּוּד יִשְׂרָאֵל חַס וְחָלִילָה
and that Hashem had ostensibly consented through him to the destruction of Israel, God forbid;
וּמֵאַחַר דְּיָדַע דְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִילָם
and since he knew that the whole world was created solely for Israel (Bereishis Rabbah 1:4),
עַל כֵּן חָשַׁב דְּוַדַּאי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּחַר בּוֹ תְּמוּרָתָם
therefore he concluded that the Blessed Name had chosen him in their stead!
עַד שֶׁרָאָה דְּ״נַהֲפוֹךְ הוּא״ (אֶסְתֵּר ט:א), וְאָתֵי מְלֹא קוּמְצָא שַׂעֲרֵי דִּידַן וְדָחֵי עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים כִּכַּר כֶּסֶף דִּילֵיהּ (מְגִלָּה ט״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
Until he saw that "it was turned to the contrary" (Esther 9:1), and our handful of barley from the Omer came and pushed aside his ten thousand talents of silver (Megillah 16a);
דְּמִנְחַת הָעוֹמֶר נִקְרָא ״מִנְחַת קְנָאֹת״ כְּמִנְחַת סוֹטָה, כִּידוּעַ בַּזֹּוהַר (חֵלֶק ב׳ קמ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳)
for the meal-offering of the Omer is termed a "meal-offering of jealousies" like the offering of the Sotah (Bamidbar 5:15), as known in the Zohar (II, 148b);
דְּהוּא הַבְּדִיקָה דְּ״אֵשֶׁת חַיִל״ לְהַבְדִּילָהּ מֵ״אֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים״ הַמִּתְדַּמֵּית בְּרָזָא דְּאֵשֶׁת חַיִל
which is the celestial test verifying the fidelity of the "Woman of Valor" [Israel] to distinguish her from the "Woman of Harlotry" [the nations] who mimics her mystery;
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ: ״טוֹב אֲרֻחַת יָרָק [וְאַהֲבָה שָׁם] מִשּׁוֹר אָבוּס [וְשִׂנְאָה בוֹ]״ (מִשְׁלֵי ט״ו:י״ז)
and this follows the verse: "Better is a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith" (Mishlei 15:17),
שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אַקָּרְבָּנוֹת דְּבִלְעָם וְשִׁבְעַת הַמִּזְבְּחוֹת (בְּמִדְבָּר כ״ג:א׳)
which the Sages expounded regarding the sacrifices of Balaam and his seven altars (Bamidbar 23:1; Bamidbar Rabbah 20:18);
שֶׁגַּם הוּא חָשַׁב לִבְנוֹת מִזְבֵּחַ נֶגֶד כָּל הַצַּדִּיקִים וַאֲבוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁבָּנוּ, כְּהָמָן בִּשְׁקָלָיו
for Balaam likewise sought to erect altars countering all the altars built by the Patriarchs, just as Haman did with his shekels;
וְלוֹמַר כִּי יֵשׁ בּוֹ כֹּחַ לְהַקְרִיב וְלַעֲבוֹד נֶגֶד כּוּלָּם וְעוֹד יוֹתֵר
boasting that he possessed the power to sacrifice and worship equal to them all and more;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת צַו (א׳) דְּאִיתָא: דְּהֵם יַקְרִיבוּ ״אַלְפֵי אֵילִים... רִבְבוֹת נַחֲלֵי שָׁמֶן״ (מִיכָה ו:ז)
as written in Tanchuma (Tzav 1): that the nations claim they will offer "thousands of rams, and ten thousands of rivers of oil" (Michah 6:7).
אַךְ הַהֶבְדֵּל: דְּהֵם הִקְרִיבוּ לְרֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ, לִהְיוֹת נַחַת רוּחַ לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ
Yet the difference is: Israel sacrifices for a sweet savour, to bring delight unto Him, blessed be He;
וְהוּא הִקְרִיב כְּדֵי לְהַטִּיל שִׂנְאָה בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם עַל יְדֵי זֶה, וְהָיָה רַק לְהָרַע
while Balaam sacrificed in order to cast hatred between Israel and their Father in Heaven, acting solely for evil;
וְכָךְ שִׁקְלֵי הָמָן הָיָה רַק כְּדֵי שֶׁיּוּכַל עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְאַבֵּד חַס וְחָלִילָה בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
and so the shekels of Haman were offered solely to destroy the Children of Israel, God forbid!
וְעַל בֵּירוּר זֶה בָּא הָעוֹמֶר מִמָּחֳרַת הַפֶּסַח דִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם
And for this clarification comes the Omer offering on the morrow of Pesach following the Exodus;
דְּטָעַן גַּם כֵּן שַׂר מִצְרַיִם: ״הַלָּלוּ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְהַלָּלוּ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה״ (מִדְרַשׁ תְּהִלִּים ט״ו)
for the guardian angel of Egypt likewise prosecuted at the Sea: "These are idolaters and these are idolaters!" (Midrash Tehillim 15);
וְהוּצְרַךְ בֵּירוּר עַל זֶה, דְּאַף שֶׁלְּמַרְאִית עַיִן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שָׁוִים, בִּפְנִימִיּוּת אֵין שָׁוִים כְּלָל
and a divine clarification was required: that even though to outward appearances in this world they seemed equal, in their inward souls they were not equal at all;
וְדָבָר זֶה אֵין נִגְלֶה לַבְּרִיּוֹת, רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵעִיד עֲלֵיהֶם
and this truth is not visible to mortal creatures, the Blessed Name alone testifying upon them;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהֵעִיד עֲלֵיהֶם בְּמִצְרַיִם שֶׁהָיָה ״עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ״, שְׁטוּפֵי זִמָּה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״כְּמַעֲשֵׂה אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם אֲשֶׁר [יְשַׁבְתֶּם בָּהּ לֹא תַעֲשׂוּ]״ (וַיִּקְרָא י״ח:ג׳)
just as He testified upon them in Egypt which was the "nakedness of the land," flooded with depravity: "after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein you dwelt, shall you not do" (Vayikra 18:3);
וּשְׁמוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵעִיד עֲלֵיהֶם שֶׁהֵם בְּנֵי אֲבוֹתָם וְשֶׁכּוּלָּם גָּדְרוּ עַצְמָם מִן הָעֲרָיוֹת
and His Name testified that they were the holy children of their fathers and that all had fenced themselves against immorality (Vayikra Rabbah 32:5).
וְכֵן מִנְחַת הָעוֹמֶר הוּא הָ״אֲרֻחַת יָרָק״ שֶׁצִּוָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהָבִיא לְפָנָיו, וּמֵעִיד שֶׁ״אַהֲבָה שָׁם״
And so the meal-offering of the Omer is the "dinner of herbs" which the Blessed Name commanded to bring before Him, testifying that "love is there";
וְעַל כֵּן אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁ״דַּלּוֹתִי״ — וַאֲנִי דַּלָּה מִן הַמִּצְוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק עַרְבֵי פְסָחִים (פְּסָחִים קי״ח עַמּוּד ב׳): ״לִי נָאֶה לְהוֹשִׁיעַ״
and therefore even though "I was brought low (daloti)"—I am impoverished in mitzvos, as written in Pesachim (118b): "yet unto me it is fitting to save";
שֶׁעַל כֵּן אוֹכְלִין בְּפֶסַח ״לֶחֶם עֹנִי״ (דְּבָרִים ט״ז:ג׳), הַכֹּל לְזִכְרוֹן דַּלּוּתָם מֵהַמִּצְוֹת
wherefore we eat on Pesach the "bread of poverty" (lechem oni), all to remember our poverty in mitzvos;
וְכֵן הוּא מִנְחַת הָעוֹמֶר שֶׁל שְׂעוֹרִים, הַכֹּל רוֹמֵז לַעֲנִיּוּת וְדַלּוּת
and likewise the Omer offering is brought from animal food, coarse barley, all alluding to poverty and deficiency;
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָאָה פְּנִימִיּוּת אַהֲבַת מַעֲמַקֵּי לִבָּם וּדְבֵיקוּתָם בְּשָׁרְשֵׁי הַלֵּב בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
yet the Blessed Name beheld the inward love of their heart's depths and their cleaving unto Him;
עַל כֵּן אַף שֶׁהֵם דַּלֵּי מַעַשׂ, ״טוֹב אֲרֻחַת יָרָק וְגוֹמֵר״
therefore, though poor in deeds, "better is a dinner of herbs where love is!"
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם בִּימֵי הָמָן שֶׁקִּטְרֵג עֲלֵיהֶם דִּ״יְשֵׁנִים מֵהַמִּצְוֹת״ וְשֶׁהוּא יִשְׁקוֹל וְכוּלֵיהּ
And therefore likewise in the days of Haman who prosecuted that they were "asleep from the commandments" and offered to weigh out silver;
אָתֵי קוּמְצָא עוֹמֶר דִּידְהוּ וְדָחֵי
our handful of barley of the Omer came and pushed it aside (Megillah 16a);
וְזֶהוּ בְּנִיסָן, שֶׁאָז זְמַן הַנֵּס וִישׁוּעוֹת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁאֵין כְּדָאִים לְמַרְאִית עַיִן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and this occurred in Nissan, which is the season of miracles and divine salvation even when Israel seem undeserving to outward appearances;
אֲבָל בְּאֶחָד בַּאֲדָר מַשְׁמִיעִים עַל הַשְּׁקָלִים
but on the first of Adar proclamation is made regarding the shekels,
לְהַרְאוֹת דִּבְאֶמֶת אָנוּ טוֹבִים בְּפֹעַל לִמְסוֹר כָּל כִּיסּוּפֵינוּ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
to demonstrate that in truth we are good in actual deed, surrendering all our desires and wealth unto the Blessed Name;
וּמַקְדִּימִין שְׁקָלֵינוּ לִסְתּוֹם פֶּה קִטְרוּג הַמְקַטְרֵג גַּם כֵּן
and we precede our shekels to silence the mouth of the prosecuting accuser as well.
וְעַכְשָׁיו שֶׁאֵין לָנוּ שְׁקָלִים בְּפֹעַל, ״נְשַׁלְּמָה פָרִים שְׂפָתֵינוּ״ (הוֹשֵׁעַ י״ד:ג׳) בִּקְרִיאַת הַפָּרָשָׁה בַּצִּבּוּר
And now that we lack physical shekels in practice, "we render the calves of our lips" (Hoshea 14:3) through reading the portion of Shekalim in the congregation;
שֶׁהֲרֵי אָנוּ מוּכָנִים בְּכָל לֵב וּמִשְׁתּוֹקְקִים וּמִתְגַּעְגְּעִים לְקַיֵּים בְּפֹעַל וְלִיתֵּן שְׁקָלִים לְמִקְדַּשׁ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for behold we are prepared with all our heart, yearning and longing to fulfill it in actual deed and give shekels unto the Sanctuary of the Blessed Name,
הוּא יִתְבָּרַךְ יְזַכֵּנוּ לָזֶה בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ
may He, blessed be He, grant us to merit this speedily in our days;
וְכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל מוּכָן לָזֶה בְּכָל נִדְבַת לִבּוֹ לְהוֹסִיף כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה גַּם כֵּן אִם יִרְצוּ לְקַבֵּל מִמֶּנּוּ:
and every single Jew is ready for this with the generous devotion of his heart to add manifold amounts as well, were Heaven to accept it from him!

7.h: The theme: The letter Yud, the letter Hei, and the sequence of Shekalim and Zachor in vanquishing Amalek. The half-shekel represents the letter Yud—the point of Chochmah recognizing divine truth with all one's might, an inheritance from Yaakov Avinu. Through this illumination one merits to eradicate Amalek in Parashat Zachor through verbal remembrance, prompting Hashem to progressively blot out Amalek until the final redemption. This represents Binah in the heart, the source of repentance (u'levavo yavin v'shav) which uproots evil. The creation of the physical world began with the letter Beis because darkness precedes light (bereisha chashocha, Shabbos 77b); the Torah, however, begins with the letter Aleph (Anochi), placing light before the prohibition of darkness (Lo yihyeh lecha). Out of divine compassion, Anochi precedes Lo yihyeh lecha to grant everyone an entrance into Torah study even before being completely cleansed of evil. So too, Shekalim (Anochi / Yud) precedes Zachor (Lo yihyeh lecha / Hei): even when the light is merely a concealed point, "a little light expels much darkness," enabling man to blot out Amalek—the first among the nations who injects weariness into divine service and robs man of the fear of God. By verbalizing the remembrance of Amalek through the mouth ("the voice is the voice of Jacob", Bereishis 27:22), the light expands from the mind into the revealed chambers of the heart.

p: וּבָזֶה הוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הַיּוּ״ד, הַיְינוּ נְקֻדַּת הַחָכְמָה דְּהַכָּרַת אֲמִיתָּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל מְאוֹדוֹ, הַנְּטוּעָה בְּלֵב כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹרָשָׁה מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם

And in this lies the perfection of the letter Yud, which is the point of Chochmah recognizing His divine truth with all one's might, planted within the heart of all Israel as an inheritance from Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִים אַחַר כָּךְ לִמְחִיַּיִת עֲמָלֵק בְּפָרָשַׁת זָכוֹר בִּזְכִירָה בַּפֶּה ״אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה״
and through this one merits subsequently the eradication of Amalek in Parashat Zachor through verbal remembrance of "what he did" (Devarim 25:17);
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מוֹחֶה מִלְּמַעְלָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה, בְּכָל שָׁנָה מְעַט מְעַט עַד עֵת קֵץ שֶׁיִּמָּחֶה לְגַמְרֵי

for through this the Holy One, blessed be He, blots him out from Above, as the Sages of blessed memory expounded, little by little each year until the time of the end when he will be obliterated entirely (Tanchuma, Ki Seitzei 11);
וְזֶהוּ שְׁלֵימוּת הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, דְּמִמֶּנָּה הַתְּשׁוּבָה דְּ״לְבָבוֹ יָבִין וְשָׁב [וְרָפָא לוֹ]״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ו:י), שֶׁהוּא מְחִיַּיִת שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע מִן הַלֵּב

and this is the perfection of Binah within the heart, whence derives the repentance of "his heart shall understand, and he shall return, and be healed" (Yeshayah 6:10), which is the eradication of the root of evil from the heart.
וּבְרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם הוּא בְּבֵי״ת, מִשּׁוּם דִּבְרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם הוּא בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שַׁבָּת ע״ז עַמּוּד ב׳)
And the creation of the physical world began with the letter Beis (Bereishis 1:1), because in the creation of the cosmos first came darkness and then light, as written in Shabbos (77b);

אֲבָל הַתּוֹרָה מַתְחִיל בְּאָלֶ״ף שֶׁהוּא לְהֵיפֶךְ: תְּחִלָּה ״אָנֹכִי״ (שְׁמוֹת כ:ב) שֶׁהוּא הָאוֹר, וְאַחַר כָּךְ ״לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ״ (שָׁם:ג׳) שֶׁהוּא הֲסָרַת הַחֹשֶׁךְ, וְסֵדֶר הַתּוֹרָה כָּךְ הוּא

but the Torah begins with the letter Aleph (at the Decalogue) which is the reverse: first "I am (Anochi) Hashem your God" (Shemos 20:2) which is the light, and only afterward "You shall have no other gods" (ibid. 20:3) which is the removal of darkness, and such is the divine order of the Torah;
וְקִבַּלְתִּי דְּדָבָר זֶה רַחֲמֵי שָׁמַיִם עַל בְּרִיּוֹתָיו שֶׁהִקְדִּים ״אָנֹכִי״ לְ״לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ״
and I have received as a tradition that this represents the mercy of Heaven upon His creatures, having placed Anochi prior to Lo yihyeh lecha;
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה אֶפְשָׁר לְכָל אֶחָד לִיכָּנֵס לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, אַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ נָקִי מֵרָע לְגַמְרֵי, דְּכָל מִינֵי פְּסֹולֶת וְרָע כְּלוּלִים בְּ״לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ״

for through this it is possible for every individual to enter into words of Torah even when not completely cleansed of evil, seeing that all manners of dross and corruption are included within the negative prohibition of Lo yihyeh lecha;
וְאִילּוּ קָדַם ״לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ״, מַאן סָפוּן מַאן רָקִיעַ לִהְיוֹת נָקִי לְגַמְרֵי שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג דְּ״אָנֹכִי וְגוֹמֵר״
and had Lo yihyeh lecha preceded, who would be so hidden and exalted as to be entirely pure so as to be capable of attaining the illumination of Anochi?
וְגַם יֵשׁ לוֹמַר, עַכְשָׁיו שֶׁהִקְדִּים ״אָנֹכִי״, הַשָּׂגָה זוֹ עַצְמוֹ מֵאִיר לוֹ שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַגִּיעַ לְ״לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ״ גַּם כֵּן
And one can also say: now that He placed Anochi first, this very spiritual perception itself shines for man so that he can subsequently reach the purification of Lo yihyeh lecha as well;
וְלוּלֵי זֶה לֹא הָיָה כֹּחַ אָדָם לְהִתְגַּבֵּר נֶגֶד כֹּחוֹת הַזָּרִים וַאֲחֵרִים הַגּוֹבְרִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and were it not so, man would lack the strength to prevail against the alien, foreign forces that dominate within this physical world.
וְגַם לִמְחִיַּיִת עֲמָלֵק שֶׁהוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּ״לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ״ בַּעֲקִירַת הָרָע מִן הַלֵּב, קָדְמוּ הַשְּׁקָלִים שֶׁהוּא הָאוֹר דְּ״אָנֹכִי״
And likewise prior to the eradication of Amalek—which embodies the root of Lo yihyeh lecha in uprooting evil from the heart—preceded Shekalim, which embodies the light of Anochi,
בְּהַשָּׂגָה דַּה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ מַנְהִיגֶךָ וְשֶׁמּוֹסֵר עַצְמוֹ הַכֹּל לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
in the perception that Hashem is your God and Leader, and that one surrenders his entire being unto the Blessed Name;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעֲדַיִין הוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם וּכְנְקֻדָּה בְּעָלְמָא דּוּגְמַת יוּ״ד שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ עֲדַיִין
and even though this light is as yet in concealment and merely like a simple point after the pattern of the letter Yud, not having openly expanded into his conscious heart,
דְּכָל זְמַן שֶׁהַלֵּב אֵינוֹ נָקִי מִפְּסֹולֶת אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָאוֹר לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ
for as long as the heart is not purged of dross the light cannot expand into revealed consciousness;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם אוֹתוֹ מְעַט מֵהָאוֹר גַּם כֵּן דּוֹחֶה הַרְבֵּה מֵהַחֹשֶׁךְ, וְיוּכַל לָבוֹא לִמְחִיַּיִת עֲמָלֵק שֶׁהוּא ״רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ד:כ׳)
nevertheless, that small measure of light likewise expels much darkness, enabling one to arrive at the eradication of Amalek who is "the first of the nations" (Bamidbar 24:20);
דְּהַיְינוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת שֶׁל כָּל מִינֵי הִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בָּרָע שֶׁהוּא נַחֲלַת גּוֹיִם וְאֵינוֹ חֵלֶק יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָל
meaning the primary source of all manners of immersion in evil, which is the heritage of the nations and not the portion of Israel at all.
דְּעֶצֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם כְּצֹאן הַנִּמְשָׁכִים אַחַר הָרוֹעֶה, וְאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם הִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת בְּשׁוּם דָּבָר, רַק נִמְשָׁכִים אַחַר רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמַּנְהִיגָם

For the essential root of Israel is like a flock of sheep following after their Shepherd, possessing no immersion in any mundane entity, but drawn purely after the will of the Blessed Name Who guides them;

אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּצַּד הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה הוּא מַכְנִיס לַלֵּב פִּיּוּיִם וְהַסָּתַת שֶׁל מִינֵי רָע דְּנַחֲלַת גּוֹיִם עַל יְדֵי הָעֵירוּב טוֹב וָרָע שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה עַל יְדֵי הַחֵטְא, וְהוּא הַגּוֹרֵם מִמֵּילָא גַּם כֵּן לְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיּוֹת

except that through the "yeast in the dough" [the yetzer hara] seductions and incitements of the evil heritage of the nations enter the heart through the mixture of good and evil wrought by sin, which automatically causes the subjugation to the kingdoms of the world;
וּתְחִלַּת הַסָּתָתוֹ הוּא בְּכֹחַ הָרֵאשִׁית דְּגוֹיִם, כֹּחַ עֲמָלֵק שֶׁהוּא שֶׁקָּפַץ עֲלֵיהֶם בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה מִיָּד אַחַר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם

and the inception of its incitement operates through the power of the first of the nations, the force of Amalek who sprang upon them first immediately following the Exodus from Egypt (Shemos 17:8; Tanchuma, Ki Seitzei 9);
כִּי הוּא הָרֵאשִׁית וְהַתְחָלַת הַסָּתַת הָרָע דְּגוֹיִם, וְהַכְנָסָתוֹ בַּלֵּב הוּא לְהַכְנִיס עֲיֵיפוּת וִיגֵיעוּת בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for he is the primary head of the evil incitement of the nations, his method of infiltration being to inject weariness and exhaustion into the divine service of the Blessed Name;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה גַּם כֵּן מֵסִיר יִרְאַת אֱלֹהִים, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״וְאַתָּה עָיֵף [וְיָגֵעַ וְלֹא יָרֵא אֱלֹהִים]״ (דְּבָרִים כ״ה:י״ח), שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי מַה ״שֶּׁקָּרְךָ״

and through this he likewise removes the fear of God, as it is written: "and you were faint and weary, and feared not God" (Devarim 25:18), which occurred through that which he "happened upon you" (asher karcha);

שֶׁהֲרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכ״ג עַמּוּד ב׳): דַּעֲמָלֵק נוֹפֵל בְּיַד זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ ״[אֶת] הָאֱלֹהִים אֲנִי יָרֵא״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מ״ב:י״ח) וּבַעֲמָלֵק נֶאֱמַר ״וְלֹא יָרֵא אֱלֹהִים״

for behold, the Sages of blessed memory stated (Bava Batra 123b): Amalek falls into the hand of the seed of Yosef concerning whom it is said "for I fear God" (Bereishis 42:18), while of Amalek it is written "and he feared not God";
וַהֲרֵי הַךְ מִקְרָא קָאֵי עַל ״וְאַתָּה״, וּלִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹמֵר זֶה
yet behold, that verse refers to "and you," addressing this description unto the Children of Israel!
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּעַל יְדֵי עֲמָלֵק הוּא שֶׁבָּא לָהֶם זֶה
And perforce, it was through the corrupting influence of Amalek that this weariness and loss of awe befell them.
וְזֶהוּ עַל דֶּרֶךְ: ״תְּחִלַּת נְפִילָה — נִיסָה״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סוֹטָה מ״ד עַמּוּד ב׳)
And this follows the maxim: "The beginning of a military rout is flight," as written in Sotah (44b);
שֶׁנָּס מִן הַמַּעֲרָכָה וּמִתְיָאֵשׁ מִמִּלְחָמָה, מִמֵּילָא אַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁכְּנֶגְדּוֹ רוֹדֵף אַחֲרָיו וּמַפִּילוֹ
for when a soldier flees from the battle-line and despairs of fighting, automatically his adversary pursues and strikes him down;
כָּךְ עֲצַת הַיֵּצֶר בַּתְּחִלָּה: לְהַכְבִּיד עָלָיו הָעֲבוֹדָה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, עַד שֶׁיִּרְאֶה עַצְמוֹ עָיֵף מִמֶּנּוּ וְשֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִכֹּחוֹ
such is the tactic of the yetzer at the inception: to make divine service feel oppressively burdensome to man, until he views himself as exhausted from it and imagines it to be beyond his strength,
וּכְעִנְיַן ״רָאמוֹת לֶאֱוִיל חָכְמוֹת״ (מִשְׁלֵי כ״ד:ז׳), וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה ״בַּשַּׁעַר לֹא יִפְתַּח פִּיהוּ״ (שָׁם)
after the manner of "Wisdom is too high for a fool" (Mishlei 24:7), whereby "he opens not his mouth in the gate";
וּמְעַט מְעַט מַכְנִיס בְּתוֹכוֹ כָּל רָע, כִּי כְּשֶׁיּוֹצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ דְּבַר שֶׁל תּוֹרָה, נִכְנָס כְּנֶגְדּוֹ דְּבַר שֶׁל לֵיצָנוּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה א:ב)

and little by little the yetzer injects all manner of evil into him, for when a word of Torah departs from him, in its place enters a word of scoffing (leitzanus), as written in Shir HaShirim Rabbah (1:2);
וְהֵם דִּבְרֵי עֲמָלֵק, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כ״ז:ו׳) עַל פָּסוּק ״לֵץ תַּכֶּה״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ט:כ״ה) — זֶה עֲמָלֵק
and these are the words of Amalek, as the Sages expounded (Shemos Rabbah 27:6) on the verse "Smite a scorner" (Mishlei 19:25)—this is Amalek;
דְּזֶה שׁוֹרֶשׁ גּוֹיִם: לִהְיוֹת כָּל דֶּרֶךְ הָאֱמֶת אֶצְלוֹ לְלֵיצָנוּת
for this is the foundational root of the gentiles: that the entire path of sacred truth is reduced in their eyes to scoffing and mockery.
וְעַל כֵּן, מִיָּד שֶׁנִּכְנַס בּוֹ אוֹר קִימְעָא זֶה דֶּרֶךְ הֶעְלֵם לְהַשִּׂיג שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹרֵא עוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא
Therefore, immediately when this slight ray of light enters him in concealment, grasping that there is a Creator of this world and the World to Come,
שֶׁאֵלָיו הוּא מוֹסֵר נַפְשׁוֹ וּלְבָבוֹ וְכָל מְאוֹדוֹ, יוּכַל לִזְכּוֹר מְחִיַּיִת עֲמָלֵק בַּפֶּה
unto Whom he surrenders his soul, his heart, and all his might, he is empowered to remember the eradication of Amalek with his mouth;
דְּכָל כֹּחַ יַעֲקֹב נֶגֶד עֵשָׂו הוּא בַּפֶּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב [וְהַיָּדַיִם יְדֵי עֵשָׂו]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:כ״ב)
for the entire power of Yaakov against Esav resides in the mouth, as it is written: "The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau" (Bereishis 27:22; Bereishis Rabbah 65:20);
דַּעֲקִימַת שְׂפָתָיו הָוֵי מַעֲשֶׂה לַעֲקוֹר הָרָע מִן הַלֵּב
where moving the lips is legally reckoned a concrete action to uproot evil from the heart (Sanhedrin 65b);
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל פָּסוּק ״שִׂפְתֵי צַדִּיק יֵדְעוּן רָצוֹן״ (מִשְׁלֵי י:לב): שֶׁהַדִּבּוּר בַּפֶּה פּוֹעֵל לְהַכְנִיס רָצוֹן לַלֵּב
and as I heard on the verse "The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable" (Mishlei 10:32): vocalized speech in the mouth operates to instill holy will into the heart;
וְ״צַדִּיק״ דַּיְיקָא, שֶׁהוּא שִׂטְנוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק וְעֵשָׂו, וְאָז הָאוֹר מִתְרַחֵב בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ וְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת:

and "tzaddik" specifically, who is the cosmic adversary of Amalek and Esav (Bava Batra 123b), and then the light broadens into the revealed consciousness of the heart and expands throughout the being.

7.h: The theme: The letter Vav, Parashat Parah, and the incomprehensible statute of purifying the defilement of death (chukas ha-Torah / tumas meis). After rectifying Amalek through the letter Hei, one advances to the letter Vav—the letter of truth (os emes, Zohar III, 2a) symbolizing the stature of Yaakov Avinu, the Tree of Life who never died (Ta'anis 5b). This corresponds to Parashat Parah, which purifies corpse-defilement (tumas meis). King Shlomo declared of the Red Heifer: "I said: I will get wisdom; but it was far from me" (Koheles 7:23; Bamidbar Rabbah 19:3), because the ultimate purification of death cannot be understood until death is swallowed up forever (Yeshayah 25:8). Death is an absolute decree (chok) beyond human questioning, as Hashem told Rabbi Akiva: "Be silent, for thus it arose in Primordial Thought" (Menachos 29b). To Moshe alone was the secret of the Red Heifer revealed (Tanchuma, Chukas 8), because he ascended on High above mortal perception. Moshe's own passing was an absolute statute (chok), wherefore "no man knows his grave" (Devarim 34:6). Death stems from the Serpent's instigation (ityo shel nachash), against which Hashem declared: "And now, lest he put forth his hand... and live forever" (Bereishis 3:22), temporarily locking the doors of absolute physical immortality in this world. When a person contracts corpse-uncleanness (tumas meis, the father of fathers of impurity), the external trace of the Serpent is drawn upon him; Moshe questioned how such a person could be purified, seeing that normal repentance cannot atone for the Serpent's instigation, until Hashem revealed the statute of the Red Heifer—a divine decree mirroring the incomprehensible laws of nature.

p: וְזֶהוּ הַהֵ״א רִאשׁוֹנָה דְּהַשֵּׁם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הוּא מוֹסִיף בְּתִיקּוּן לְתַקֵּן גַּם הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בְּכָל זֶרַע אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן דְּמֵחֲמָתוֹ נִגְזַר הַמִּיתָה

And this is the first letter Hei of the Divine Name (Havayah); and afterward one advances in spiritual rectification to rectify even the root of the Serpent's instigation (ityo shel nachash) present within all descendants of Adam HaRishon, on account of which mortality was decreed (Shabbos 55b);
וְזֶהוּ פָּרָשַׁת פָּרָה הַבָּאָה לְטַהֵר טֻמְאַת מֵת
and this is Parashat Parah, which comes to purify the defilement of a corpse (tumat meis, Bamidbar 19);
וְדָבָר זֶה ״חֻקָּה״, וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר עַל זֶה: ״אָמַרְתִּי אֶחְכָּמָה וְהִיא רְחוֹקָה [מִמֶּנִּי]״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כג)

and this matter is an absolute statute (chukkah), concerning which King Shlomo, peace be upon him, proclaimed: "I said: I will get wisdom; but it was far from me" (Koheles 7:23; Bamidbar Rabbah 19:3);
הַיְינוּ הַשָּׂגַת דָּבָר זֶה לַאֲמִיתּוֹ, מְצִיאוּת הַטָּהֳרָה לְטֻמְאַת מֵת, שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג אֶלָּא לֶעָתִיד כְּשֶׁ״בֻּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח״ (יְשַׁעְיָה כ״ה:ח׳)

meaning the comprehension of this reality in its ultimate truth, the true mechanics of purification from corpse-uncleanness, which is impossible to comprehend except in the Future when "He will swallow up death forever" (Yeshayah 25:8);
דְּאָז יָבִינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְצִיאוּת טָהֳרָה לְטֻמְאַת מֵת, אֲבָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא רָחוֹק מֵהַשָּׂגָה
for then they will understand the reality of purification from corpse-defilement, whereas in this world it is far beyond human comprehension.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ קָבַע לָהֶם טָהֳרָה דֶּרֶךְ חֻקָּה, אַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּשָּׂג בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
Yet nevertheless the Blessed Name established for them purification by way of a statute, even though it cannot be intellectually grasped in this world;
וְזֶהוּ אוֹת הַוָּי״ו שֶׁהוּא אוֹת אֱמֶת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּוהַר רֵישׁ וַיִּקְרָא (ב׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
and this corresponds to the letter Vav, which is the letter of truth, as written in the Zohar at the beginning of Vayikra (2a);
הָרוֹמֶזֶת לִכְלַל הַקּוֹמָה דְּ״אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב״ (מִיכָה ז:כ), שֶׁהוּא עֵץ הַחַיִּים, דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא מֵת (תַּעֲנִית ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
alluding to the complete stature of "truth to Jacob" (Michah 7:20), which is the Tree of Life, for Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, never died (Ta'anis 5b);
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָנְטוּ חָנְטַיָּא וְסָפְדוּ סָפְדַיָּא וְקָבְרוּ קָבְרַיָּא, הַכֹּל כְּפִי הַמּוּשָּׂג בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וּבֶאֱמֶת לֹא מֵת

and even though the embalmers embalmed him, the eulogizers eulogized him, and the undertakers buried him, all this occurred according to the outward perception of this world, whereas in absolute truth he did not die;
וְדָבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ מוּשָּׂג כְּלָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה רַק דֶּרֶךְ חֻקָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁגּוּף עִנְיַן הַמִּיתָה הִיא גַּם כֵּן חֻקָּה דְּאִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְהַרְהֵר, רַק דְּכָךְ גָּזַר

and this reality cannot be comprehended in this world except by way of a statute, just as the phenomenon of death itself is likewise a divine statute concerning which one has no permission to question, but must submit that thus He decreed.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מְנָחוֹת כ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳) בְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: ״שְׁתוֹק, כָּךְ עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה [לְפָנַי]״
And as written in Menachos (29b) regarding Rabbi Akiva: Hashem commanded Moshe, "Be silent, for thus it arose in Thought before Me!";
וְלֹא תֵּירֵץ לוֹ כְּלוּם עַל שְׁאֵלָתוֹ הַחֲזָקָה ״זוֹ תּוֹרָה וְזוֹ שְׂכָרָהּ״, רַק אָמַר לוֹ שֶׁיִּשְׁתּוֹק
offering no philosophical explanation for his piercing question, "Is this Torah and this its reward?", telling him merely to be silent;
כִּי סוֹד דָּבָר זֶה אֵין לוֹ הִתְגַּלּוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת בְּדִבּוּר
because the secret of this matter has no manifestation in this world that could be articulated in mortal speech;
וְרַק כְּשֶׁיִּשְׁתּוֹק וְיִדְבּוֹק עַצְמוֹ לְעוֹלַם הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגַת עֹומֶק מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, יַרְגִּישׁ דְּכָךְ עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה
and only when one becomes silent and cleaves unto the World of Thought (Keser / Chochmah), perceiving the depth of His divine intention, will he sense that thus it arose in Thought;
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה יָכוֹל לְהַשִּׂיג זֶה
and Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, was capable of grasping this,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב גַּם כֵּן (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא פָּרָשַׁת חֻקַּת ח׳): ״לְךָ אֲנִי מְגַלֶּה טַעֲמֵי פָרָה״, כִּי הוּא עָלָה לַמָּרוֹם
as written in Midrash Tanchuma (Chukas 8): Hashem said, "Unto you alone I reveal the rationale of the Red Heifer," because Moshe ascended on High;
הַיְינוּ הַשָּׂגָה הַמְרוֹמֶמֶת מֵהַשָּׂגַת בְּנֵי אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
meaning a perception elevated far above the intellect of ordinary humans in this world.
וּמִיתָתוֹ הָיְתָה חֻקָּה גְּמוּרָה שֶׁגַּם לוֹ לֹא נִגְלָה הַטַּעַם
And Moshe's own death was an absolute statute whose inner reason was not revealed even to him;
דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּתְפָּרֵשׁ חֶטְאוֹ, הֲרֵי אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁעוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה
for even though his sin at the Waters of Merivah was explicitly specified, behold nothing stands in the way of repentance!
וְאַף עַל פִּי דְּהַכֹּל בְּמִשְׁפָּט לְמַאן דְּאָמַר (שַׁבָּת נ״ה עַמּוּד א׳) ״אֵין מִיתָה בְּלֹא חֵטְא״ וְאַף מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן וְכוּלֵיהּ
And although all is governed with justice according to the authority who holds (Shabbos 55a) that "there is no death without sin," and that even Moshe and Aharon died on account of a sin;

וּמִשּׁוּם ״דְּלֹא הֶאֱמַנְתֶּם [בִּי לְהַקְדִּישֵׁנִי]״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ:יב) נֶחְשַׁב לְגַבֵּי דִּידְהוּ כְּחִלּוּל הַשֵּׁם, דְּתָלוּי כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא אָדָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סוֹף יוֹמָא (פ״ו עַמּוּד א׳): ״כְּגוֹן אֲנָא וְכוּלֵיהּ״

and on account of "because you believed not in Me to sanctify Me" (Bamidbar 20:12), which relative to their exalted stature was accounted like a desecration of the Name (chilul Hashem), as stated at the end of Yoma (86a): "for instance someone like myself, etc.";
וּבְחִלּוּל הַשֵּׁם אֵין כֹּחַ בִּתְשׁוּבָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וְיִסּוּרִים לְכַפֵּר לְגַמְרֵי אֶלָּא בְּצֵירוּף הַמִּיתָה (יוֹמָא שָׁם)
and for a desecration of the Name, repentance, Yom Kippur, and tribulations have no power to atone completely without the addition of death (Yoma 86a);
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ עַל זֶה: ״נוֹרָא עֲלִילָה עַל בְּנֵי אָדָם״ (תְּהִלִּים ס״ו:ה׳; תַּנְחוּמָא וָאֵרָא ט׳), שֶׁנֶּחְשָׁב לַעֲלִילָה מַה שֶּׁיִּהְיֶה זֶה בְּגֶדֶר חִלּוּל הַשֵּׁם

nevertheless the Midrash expounds upon this: "He is terrible in His doing (alilah, pretext) toward the children of men" (Tehillim 66:5; Tanchuma, Va'era 9), meaning it was deemed a mere pretext that this strike should be categorized as a desecration of the Name;
וְזֶהוּ טַעַם: ״וְלֹא יָדַע אִישׁ אֶת קְבֻרָתוֹ״ (דְּבָרִים ל״ד:ו׳), הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה מוּשָּׂג לְשׁוּם אָדָם עִנְיַן מִיתָתוֹ וּקְבוּרָתוֹ כְּלָל
and this is the esoteric reason why "no man knows his grave" (Devarim 34:6), meaning that the inner reality of his death and burial was not comprehensible to any human being at all.
אֲבָל דָּבָר זֶה הוּא מֵעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ
Rather, this mortality was the consequence of the Serpent's instigation;
דְּנֶאֱמַר: ״וְעַתָּה פֶּן יִשְׁלַח יָדוֹ [וְלָקַח גַּם מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים וְאָכַל וָחַי לְעֹלָם]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג:כב)
for it is said: "And now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever" (Bereishis 3:22);
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כ״א:ו׳): אֵין ״וְעַתָּה״ אֶלָּא תְּשׁוּבָה
and the Sages of blessed memory stated (Bereishis Rabbah 21:6): "'And now' denotes nothing other than repentance";
הַיְינוּ דִּלְשׁוֹן ״וְעַתָּה״ הַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא עַתָּה כָּךְ מַה שֶּׁלֹּא הָיָה כֵּן מִקּוֹדֶם, וְזֶהוּ תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמִּתְחָרֵט עַתָּה עַל הַקּוֹדֵם
meaning that "and now" signifies that he is presently in a state that he was not in previously, which is repentance, regretting now his former sin;
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא רָצָה שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה תְּשׁוּבָה עַל חֵטְא זֶה וְשֶׁיִּשְׁלַח יָדוֹ וְגוֹמֵר שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם
and the Blessed Name did not wish that he repent for this specific sin and put forth his hand to eat and merit eternal physical life;
וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָעֲלִילָה שֶׁבָּא עַל בְּנֵי אָדָם, שֶׁסָּגַר מֵהֶם דַּלְתֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה הַגְּמוּרָה וְשֶׁיּוּכַל לִזְכּוֹת לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם מִיָּד בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and this is the root of the pretext that befell mankind: that Hashem closed before them the gates of absolute repentance that would grant physical eternal life immediately in this world;
וְכֵן בְּכָל צֶאֱצָאָיו בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה דְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ הַתָּקוּעַ בְּכָל אֶחָד מוֹרָשָׁה מֵאָב הָרִאשׁוֹן, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְתַקֵּן וְלָשׁוּב לְגַמְרֵי

and likewise throughout all his descendants, in this root of the Serpent's instigation embedded within each person as an inheritance from the first father, it is impossible to rectify and repent completely so as to escape physical death.
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן טֻמְאַת מֵת שֶׁהוּא אֲבִי אֲבוֹת הַטּוּמְאָה
And this is the concept of corpse-defilement, which is the "father of the fathers of impurity" (avi avos ha-tumah);
וּמְטַמֵּא לְפִי שֶׁהַמִּיתָה בָּאָה מִצַּד טוּמְאָה רִאשׁוֹנָה דְּנָחָשׁ הַקַּדְמוֹנִי, אֲבִי אֲבוֹת הַטּוּמְאָה
defiling so severely because death issues from the primordial impurity of the Ancient Serpent, the true father of the fathers of impurity;
וְהַמֵּת עַצְמוֹ אֵין לוֹ טָהֳרָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עַד עֵת קֵץ לִתְחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים
and the dead corpse itself has no purification in this world until the time of the end at the Resurrection of the Dead;
רַק עַל הַטְּמֵא מֵת שָׁאַל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: ״בַּמֶּה יִהְיֶה טָהֳרָתוֹ?״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
Moshe Rabbeinu asked only concerning the person who contracted uncleanness from a corpse: "Through what shall be his purification?", as the Sages stated (Bamidbar Rabbah 19:4);
וּכְפְשׁוּטוֹ הַשְּׁאֵלָה: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁזֶּה דָּבָר שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יִגְּעוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם בַּמֵּת כְּדֵי לְקָבְרוֹ
and in its plain sense the question was: because it is impossible for human beings not to touch a corpse in order to bury it,
וְכִי יִשָּׁאֲרוּ בְּטֻמְאָתָם לְעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא יוּכְלוּ לִיטָּהֵר כְּלָל, אֵין זֶה ״דַּרְכֵי נֹעַם״ (מִשְׁלֵי ג:יז)
and should they remain in their uncleanness forever, unable to be purified at all? That would contradict "her ways are ways of pleasantness" (Mishlei 3:17)!
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ הָאֱמֶת, שֶׁכָּל טוּמְאָה הוּא מִצַּד חִסָּרוֹן בַּנֶּפֶשׁ, וּבְשׁוּבוֹ מִדְּרָכָיו וְחָיָה — מִמֵּילָא דְּיִטְהַר גַּם כֵּן
And according to the mystical truth: all impurity stems from a deficiency in the soul, so that when one turns from his sins and lives, automatically he is purified;
וְעִנְיַן טֻמְאַת מֵת הוּא שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ גַּם עָלָיו זוּהֲמַת עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ שֶׁבַּמֵּת, שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַטּוּמְאָה שֶׁבּוֹ
and the essence of corpse-defilement is that there is drawn upon the living person the defilement of the Serpent's instigation residing in the dead body, which is the uncleanness within it;
וַהֲרֵי כָּל הַחֲטָאִים יֵשׁ לָהֶם תַּקָּנָה בִּתְשׁוּבָה, אֲבָל זֶה שֶׁמַּמְשִׁיךְ עָלָיו טֻמְאַת עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ שֶׁהוּא טוּמְאָה שֶׁאֵין עָלֶיהָ תְּשׁוּבָה

and behold, all human sins find remedy through repentance, yet this person draws upon himself the defilement of the Serpent's instigation, which is an uncleanness upon which repentance does not operate;
הוּקְשָׁה לוֹ: דְּאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁעוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה, כֹּל שֶׁאֵין הַחֵטְא מוּשְׁרָשׁ בְּעֶצֶם הַחַיּוּת שֶׁזֶּהוּ עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ
Moshe struggled: for nothing stands in the way of repentance, so long as the sin is not rooted in the very core of his personal life (which is the Serpent's instigation);
וַהֲרֵי טוּמְאָה זוֹ אֵינוֹ מִצַּד עֶצֶם חַיּוּתוֹ, רַק מִצַּד הַנְּגִיעָה אוֹ הָאֲהָלָה שֶׁל אַחֵר שֶׁהִמְשִׁיךְ עָלָיו
and this defilement does not stem from his own essential life, but merely from touching or overshadowing (ohel) the corpse of another who conveyed it upon him;
וַהֲרֵי זֶה כִּכְלַל טוּמְאוֹת דִּשְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה וְשִׁעְבּוּד גָּלֻיּוֹת שֶׁהֵם רַק כַּהוֹצֵי הַסּוֹבְבִים לְאָסָא
and behold this is like all other impurities caused by the "yeast in the dough" and exile, which are merely like thorns encircling the myrtle;
וְאִם כֵּן וַדַּאי יֵשׁ לוֹ טָהֳרָה, וּבַמֶּה יִהְיֶה טָהֳרָתוֹ כֵּיוָן דְּהוּא הַמְשָׁכַת טֻמְאַת עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ שֶׁאֵין כֹּחַ בִּתְשׁוּבָה לְכַפְּרוֹ
and if so he certainly must have a purification, yet through what could he be purified, seeing that it is an extension of the Serpent's instigation which normal repentance cannot atone?
עַד שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְפָרָשַׁת פָּרָה, נִתְגַּלָּה לוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָזֶה טָהֳרָה שֶׁאֵין מוּשֶּׂגֶת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה רַק דֶּרֶךְ חֻקָּה
Until he reached Parashat Parah, when it was revealed to him that there exists a purification that cannot be grasped in this world except by way of a divine statute;
כְּמוֹ חֻקֵּי הַטֶּבַע שֶׁחָקַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית, חֻקִּים דְּבָרִים שֶׁנִּלְאוּ כָּל חוֹקְרֵי טֶבַע לָתֵת טַעַם לָזֶה בְּשֵׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי

like the laws of nature that the Blessed Name engraved in the work of Creation, mysterious laws concerning which all natural philosophers have wearied to provide an explanation through human intellect,
כָּךְ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא דְּפוּס מַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית, יֵשׁ בָּהּ חֻקִּים שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָקַק כָּךְ:
so too the Torah, which is the cosmic blueprint of the work of Creation, contains statutes that the Blessed Name sovereignly decreed thus.

7.h: The theme: "Let the mother come and cleanse the excrement of her son" (Bamidbar Rabbah 19:8) and the sin of the Golden Calf. At Mount Sinai, Israel attained complete liberation from the Angel of Death and the yetzer hara, returning to the pristine stature of Adam HaRishon prior to the sin; through the sin of the Golden Calf, the Serpent's instigation returned to its place. The calf arose because they removed the face of the Ox from the left of the celestial Chariot (Shemos Rabbah 43:8). Torah originates from the side of Gevurah—the mystery of contraction (tzimtzum) restricting conduct into "do this" and "do not do that". Yet this physical contraction in action is the vessel for boundless spiritual expansion (merchav) in the mind, reflecting the heritage of Yaakov without boundaries ("Out of the straits I called upon Hashem; He answered me with divine expansiveness", Tehillim 118:5). The mixed multitude and Israel erred by isolating Gevurah from the Central Pillar (Kav HaEmtza'i), assuming Hashem desired pure, rigid tzimtzum, and demanding: "Arise, make us gods" (Shemos 32:1). Idolaters worship "other gods" knowing they are separate from Hashem; Israel, however, cleaved to truth, but mistakenly believed that in this world created through strict justice (Middas HaDin), spiritual transmission requires a rigid human teacher. Assuming Moshe who ascended on High would never return, and perceiving that Aharon represented the service of sacrifice (Avodah) rather than Torah, they sought to anchor the divine presence through sacrificial service alone.

p: וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה י״ט:ח׳): ״תָּבוֹא אֵם וּתְקַנַּח צוֹאַת בְּנָהּ״
And this is what they expounded (Bamidbar Rabbah 19:8): "Let the mother [the Red Heifer] come and cleanse the filth of her son [the Golden Calf]";
כִּי בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה הָיָה חֵירוּת מִמַּלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת וְיֵצֶר רָע (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה מ״א:ז׳; עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה׳ עַמּוּד א׳) כְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַחֵטְא
for at the Giving of the Torah there was absolute freedom from the Angel of Death and the yetzer hara, like Adam HaRishon prior to the sin;
וְעַל יְדֵי חֵטְא עֵגֶל חָזַר עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ לִמְקוֹמוֹ
and through the sin of the Golden Calf, the Serpent's instigation returned to its place;
וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁשָּׁמְטוּ אֶחָד מִטֶּטְרָמוֹלִין, פְּנֵי שׁוֹר מֵהַשְּׂמֹאל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה מ״ג:ח׳)
and this corresponds to their wrenching away one of the four faces of the celestial Chariot: the face of the Ox from the left side, as written in Shemos Rabbah (43:8);
דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק ב׳ פ״א עַמּוּד א׳), שֶׁהוּא סוֹד הַצִּמְצוּם, לִהְיוֹת מְצוּמְצָם בִּדְרָכָיו ״אֶת זֶה תַּעֲשֶׂה וְזֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה״
for the Torah derives from the side of Gevurah (Zohar II, 81a), which is the mystery of tzimtzum [contraction], to be rigorously bounded in one's ways: "this you shall do, and this you shall not do";
וְאָמְנָם צִמְצוּם זֶה שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא הַרְחָבָה גְּמוּרָה, דַּהֲרֵי זֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב בְּלִי מְצָרִים
yet this contraction of the Torah is nothing other than consummate expansiveness, for behold this is the root of the heritage of Yaakov without boundaries (Shabbos 118b);
וְעַל יְדֵי צִמְצוּם זֶה שֶׁלְּפִי שָׁעָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אָחֵיד בְּעֵץ חַיִּים, וְזוֹכֶה לְהַשְׁפָּעוֹת דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה דַּ״אֲרֻכָּה מֵאֶרֶץ מִדָּהּ [וּרְחָבָה מִנִּי יָם]״ (אִיּוֹב י״א:ט׳)

and through this temporary contraction in this world one grasps the Tree of Life, meriting the divine overflow of words of Torah that are "longer than the earth in measure, and broader than the sea" (Iyov 11:9);
דְּהַצִּמְצוּם הוּא רַק בִּפְעֻלּוֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים הַגּוּפָנִים
for the contraction applies strictly to physical actions and bodily deeds,
אֲבָל בַּהַשָּׂגָה שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה בַּהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת שֶׁבְּמוֹחוֹ וְלִבּוֹ, בָּזֶה יוּכַל לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט בְּלִי מְצָרִים
but in spiritual perception, which is the essence of the Torah's wisdom in the contemplation of brain and heart, one can expand without any boundary;
וּ״מִן הַמֵּצַר קָרָאתִי יָּהּ, [עָנָנִי בַמֶּרְחָב יָהּ]״ (תְּהִלִּים קי״ח:ה׳)
and "Out of the straits I called upon Hashem; Hashem answered me with expansiveness" (Tehillim 118:5):
הַקְּרִיאָה הוּא הַתְחָלַת הַכְּנִיסָה לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, דְּצָרִיךְ לָזֶה צִמְצוּם וּמֵיצַר
the initial call is the entrance into words of Torah, which requires contraction and the straits,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹנֵהוּ וְעוֹזֵר לוֹ, אָז הוּא בַּמֶּרְחָב
and subsequently, when the Blessed Name answers and assists him, he enters into the boundless expanse.
וְהֵם טָעוּ וְחָשְׁבוּ דִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בְּצִמְצוּם גָּמוּר, וְהִפְרִידוּ מִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה מִקַּו הָאֶמְצָעִי
And at the Golden Calf they erred, assuming that the will of the Blessed Name was absolute contraction, severing the attribute of Gevurah from the Central Pillar;
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ: ״קוּם עֲשֵׂה [לָנוּ אֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר יֵלְכוּ לְפָנֵינוּ] וְגוֹמֵר״ (שְׁמוֹת ל״ב:א׳)
and therefore they said: "Up, make us gods, which shall go before us, etc." (Shemos 32:1);
דְּגַם עַל זֶה נִקְרָא ״אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים״, שֶׁהֵם נִמְשָׁכִים מִצַּד הַפְּסֹולֶת שֶׁלְּעוּמַּת מִדַּת הַדִּין דִּקְדֻשָּׁה
for this idol is termed "other gods," which derive from the dross opposite holy Middas HaDin,
שֶׁרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה צִמְצוּם וְהֶעְלֵם בָּעוֹלָם כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מָקוֹם לִבְחִירָה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם, שֶׁיָּבוֹא מֵהַחֲשׁוֹכָא לִנְהוֹרָא
wherein the Blessed Name willed that contraction and concealment exist in the cosmos to provide space for free choice and human striving, so that man emerge from darkness into light;
וְעַל יְדֵי הַהֶעְלֵם מִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ מְקוֹם מְצִיאוּת לְמַה שֶּׁהֵיפֶךְ הַקְּדוּשָׁה דְּרוֹצֶה לְהִתְדַּמּוֹת כְּקוֹף לִבְנֵי אָדָם
and through this concealment there arises space for the unholy domain that seeks to mimic the human being like an ape,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ כָּל עִנְיַן הַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁהוּא גַּוָּון שֶׁל שֶׁקֶר הַמַּרְאֶה עַצְמוֹ דּוֹמֶה לֶאֱמֶת
which is the nature of concealment: a shade of falsehood presenting itself as a semblance of truth.
וְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת עוֹבְדִים לְאוֹתָם אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים, שֶׁיּוֹדְעִים שֶׁהֵם אֲחֵרִים שֶׁזּוּלַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם בְּחֵרוּם כִּי זֶה חֶלְקָם אֲשֶׁר חָלַק ה׳ וְגוֹמֵר

And the idolaters worship those other gods knowing they are external entities apart from the Blessed Name, choosing them because this is their portion which Hashem allotted to the nations (Devarim 4:19),
שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת בֶּאֱמֶת כְּלָל
possessing no affinity with absolute truth whatsoever;
אֲבָל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַדְּבוּקִים בֶּאֱמֶת, חָלִילָה לָהֶם לִטְעוֹת בְּשֶׁקֶר וְלִרְצוֹת לְהַפְרִיד עַצְמָם מֵאֱמֶת
but the Children of Israel who are cleaved unto truth, God forbid that they should intentionally choose falsehood or desire to sever themselves from truth;
רַק שֶׁטָּעוּ וְחָשְׁבוּ שֶׁזֶּה הוּא דֶּרֶךְ הָאֱמֶת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין, צָרִיךְ צִמְצוּם
rather, they erred by believing that this was the proper path of truth in this world: having been created through strict judgment, it required total contraction;
וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה הַהַנְהָגָה עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְלֹא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ
wherefore the governance in the wilderness was mediated through Moshe Rabbeinu and not the Blessed Name directly,
כַּלֶּעָתִיד דְּ״[כִּי] הֹלֵךְ לִפְנֵיכֶם ה׳ וּמְאַסִּפְכֶם [אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל]״ (יְשַׁעְיָה נ״ב:י״ב)
unlike the Future when "Hashem will go before you, and the God of Israel will be your rearward" (Yeshayah 52:12),
וְ״לֹא יְלַמְּדוּ עוֹד [אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ... כִּי כוּלָּם יֵדְעוּ אוֹתִי]״ (יִרְמְיָה ל״א:ל״ג)
and "they shall teach no more every man his neighbor... for they shall all know Me" (Yirmiyah 31:33);
כִּי יִהְיֶה שְׁפִיכוּת רוּחוֹ עַל כָּל בָּשָׂר דֶּרֶךְ שְׁפִיכָה, שֶׁהוּא הַשְׁפָּעָה בְּהַרְחָבָה וְלֹא מְצוּמְצֶמֶת בִּנְפָשׁוֹת מְיוּחָדוֹת
for there will be an outpouring of His Spirit upon all flesh (Yoel 3:1) by way of broad effusion, and not contracted into isolated elite individuals;
אֲבָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַכֹּל מְצוּמְצָם בְּעוֹלָם וְשָׁנָה וְנֶפֶשׁ
whereas in this world everything is contracted across Space (Olam), Time (Shanah), and Soul (Nefesh).
וּלְפִי שֶׁחָשְׁבוּ דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁעָלָה לַמָּרוֹם נִשְׁאַר שָׁם וְלֹא יֵרֵד עוֹד, וְנִשְׁאֲרוּ בְּלֹא רַב וּמַנְהִיג
And because they assumed that Moshe Rabbeinu who had ascended on High remained there and would not descend again (Shabbos 89a), they felt left without a master and guide;
וְהֵם הִרְגִּישׁוּ דְּעַדַיִין לֹא הִגִּיעוּ לְמַדְרֵיגַת ״כּוּלָּם יֵדְעוּ וְגוֹמֵר״, וְעַדַיִין צְרִיכִים לְרַב וּמוֹרֶה
and they felt that they had not yet attained the level of "they shall all know Me," still requiring a teacher and master;
וְאֵיךְ יַעַזְבֵם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּךְ אַחֲרֵי שֶׁכְּבָר הִתְחִיל לְהָאִיר עֵינֵיהֶם בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה
and how could the Blessed Name abandon them thus, after having already begun to enlighten their eyes at the Giving of the Torah?
וְהִשִּׂיגוּ דְּאַהֲרֹן הוּא כֹּחַ הָעֲבוֹדָה וְלֹא כֹּחַ הַתּוֹרָה דְּהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And they perceived that Aharon represented the power of the sacrificial service (Avodah) and not the power of Torah which was the unique rung of Moshe Rabbeinu;
וְדִמּוּ כִּי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּעֲבוֹדָה לְבַד:
and they mistakenly imagined that the will of the Blessed Name in this world was to be anchored in the sacrificial service alone.

7.h: The theme: The Three Pillars, the error of isolating sacrificial service (Avodah), and the idolatry of the Calf versus Pe'or. The three pillars—Torah, Avodah, and acts of kindness (Gemilus Chasadim, Avos 1:2)—correspond to the Central Pillar and the two polar extremes (Chesed and Gevurah). Torah is the Central Pillar (Kav HaEmtza'i): whoever holds fast to the Torah holds fast to all. Gemilus Chasadim derives from Avraham; if isolated, it produces dross like Yishmael (illicit lust). Avodah derives from Yitzchak, the binding on the altar, representing absolute contraction (tzimtzum); if isolated, it veers into the dross of idolatry. Israel sought to isolate Avodah when Moshe delayed, demanding of Aharon: "Up, make us gods" (Shemos 32:1), believing that through ritual worship alone they could manufacture a guiding intermediary. They chose the Calf—the small face of the celestial Ox (appe zutrei d'shor), corresponding to the attribute of Yosef HaTzaddik—just as the Cherub is the small face of Man (appe zutrei d'adam), the humble likeness of Yaakov Avinu. However, by severing the Ox from the Central Pillar, they slid to the left into idolatry. The Red Heifer comes to cleanse this filth (tzo'ah), as idolatry is termed excrement. True mockery of holy wisdom (leitzanus) is the root of Amalek and culminates in the idolatry of Ba'al Pe'or—the ultimate obscenity of defecating before the idol (Sanhedrin 64a). Moshe Rabbeinu, the embodiment of Torah which is the absolute antithesis of mockery, was buried directly opposite Beit Pe'or (Devarim 34:6) to neutralize its cynicism.

p: וְיָדוּעַ דִּשְׁלֹשָׁה עַמּוּדִים: ״תּוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדָה וּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים״ (אָבוֹת א:ב), הֵם שְׁנֵי קְצוֹת וְקַו הָאֶמְצָעִי שֶׁהֵם יְסוֹדֵי הָעוֹלָם

And it is known that the three pillars—"Torah, divine service (Avodah), and acts of kindness (Gemilus Chasadim)" (Avos 1:2)—are the two polar extremes and the Central Pillar that constitute the foundations of the world;
וְתוֹרָה הוּא קַו הָאֶמְצָעִי, דְּמַאן דְּאָחֵיד בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא — אָחֵיד בְּכוּלָּא (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק ג׳ ע״ג עַמּוּד ב׳)
and Torah is the Central Pillar, for whoever grasps the Torah grasps everything (Zohar III, 73b);
וּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים מִסִּטְרָא דְּאַבְרָהָם
and acts of kindness derive from the side of Avraham [Chesed];
וַעֲבוֹדָה מִסִּטְרָא דְּיִצְחָק, שֶׁהִקְרִיב עַצְמוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, וּבָזֶה הוּא עִיקַּר כֹּחַ הַצִּמְצוּם
and divine sacrificial service derives from the side of Yitzchak [Gevurah], who offered himself upon the altar, wherein lies the primary force of contraction (tzimtzum).
וּמִי שֶׁהוּא בִּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים לְבַד, יוּכַל לָצֵאת מִמֶּנּוּ פְּסֹולֶת עֲדַיִין כְּיִשְׁמָעֵאל מֵאַבְרָהָם, שֶׁהוּא יִצְרָא דַּעֲרָיוֹת וְתַאֲוָה
And one who is anchored in acts of kindness alone, from him dross can still issue forth like Yishmael from Avraham, which is the inclination toward illicit relations and lust;
וּמִי שֶׁבַּעֲבוֹדָה לְבַד, יוּכַל לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט הַפְּסֹולֶת, יִצְרָא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
and one who is anchored in sacrificial service alone, from him dross can expand into the inclination toward idolatry [as Esav from Yitzchak];
אֲבָל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּאָחֵיד בְּקַו הָאֶמְצָעִי, מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה שֶׁאֵין עוֹד פְּסֹולֶת כְּלָל
but the seed of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, who grasps the Central Pillar, his bed is complete (Pesachim 56a), having no dross whatsoever.
וְהֵם רָצוּ לְהַפְרִיד הָעֲבוֹדָה לְבַד, וְגָרַם דְּאָמְרוּ לְאַהֲרֹן: ״קוּם עֲשֵׂה [לָנוּ אֱלֹהִים] וְגוֹמֵר״ (שְׁמוֹת ל״ב:א׳)
And at the Golden Calf they sought to isolate sacrificial service on its own, which caused them to demand of Aharon: "Up, make us gods, etc." (Shemos 32:1);
שֶׁהַמִּתְאַמֵּץ בַּעֲבוֹדָה לְבַד יוּכַל לִטְעוֹת דְּכָל הָעֲבוֹדָה בְּיָדוֹ, אַף עֲשִׂיַּית אֱלֹהִים וְדַחֲלָן
for one who concentrates on ritual service alone can err in thinking that all service is in his hands, even the manufacturing of an intermediary deity;
שֶׁחָשְׁבוּ: מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עֲזָבָם כָּךְ בְּלֹא מוֹרֶה הַמֵּאִיר עֵינֵיהֶם, עַל כָּרְחֲךָ שֶׁהַכֹּל מָסוּר בְּיָדָם
for they presumed: since the Blessed Name seemingly left them without a guide to enlighten their eyes (Moshe having delayed), perforce everything was committed into their hands,
עַל יְדֵי עֲבוֹדָתָם יוּכְלוּ לְהַמְצִיא לָהֶם דָּבָר הַמֵּאִיר עֵינֵיהֶם וּמַדְרִיכָם גַּם כֵּן
that through their own ritual service they could invent a medium that would enlighten their eyes and guide them as well.
וְזֶהוּ ״עֵגֶל״, שֶׁהוּא אַפֵּי זוּטְרֵי דְּשׁוֹר
And this is the Calf, which is the small face of the celestial Ox (appe zutrei d'shor);
דִּכְמוֹ דִּכְרוּב, שֶׁהוּא פְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁבַּמֶּרְכָּבָה (חֲגִיגָה י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳), הוּא ״כְּרַבְיָא״ — אַפֵּי זוּטְרֵי
just as the Cherub, which is the face of Man in the celestial Chariot (Chagigah 13b), means "like a child" (k'ravya)—a small youthful face,
שֶׁהוּא דְּמוּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁנִּקְרָא בְּפָרָשַׁת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא ״דַּרְדַּקֵּי״ (שַׁבָּת פ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
which is the likeness of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, who is called in the discourse of Rabbi Akiva "children" (dardakei, Shabbos 89b),
דְּנִקְרָא ״יַעֲקֹב קָטָן״ (עָמוֹס ז:ב)
being designated "little Jacob" (Amos 7:2);
וְכִידוּעַ סוֹדוֹ שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד נְחֹשֶׁת, מִדַּת הָעֲנָוָה לְהַקְטִין אֶת עַצְמוֹ
and as its mystical secret is known, it corresponds to copper (nechoshes), the attribute of humility to lower and diminish oneself;
וְהוּא מְקוֹם גְּדוּלָּתוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, דְּשָׁם אַתָּה מוֹצֵא עַנְוְתָנוּתוֹ: לִהְיוֹת ״אֶת דַּכָּא וּשְׁפַל רוּחַ״ (יְשַׁעְיָה נ״ז:ט״ו)
and this is the locus of the greatness of the Blessed Name, where you find His humility (Megillah 31a): dwelling "with him that is of a contrite and humble spirit" (Yeshayah 57:15);
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם ״דַּל״, ״עָנִי״ וְכוּלֵיהּ, בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר, וְעַל כֵּן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עִמָּהֶם
and in every place where Scripture speaks of the "poor" and "destitute," it refers to Israel, wherefore the Blessed Name is with them;
וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת קַו אֶמְצָעִי, שֶׁאֵין מוֹצֵא לְנַפְשׁוֹ שׁוּם שְׁלֵימוּת
and this is the quality of the Central Pillar, which finds within itself no self-righteous perfection,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִי שֶׁנּוֹטֶה לְצַד אֶחָד, יוּכַל לִטְעוֹת שֶׁהוּא שָׁלֵם בְּאוֹתָהּ מִדָּה
unlike one who leans to an extreme side, who can delude himself into thinking he is consummate in that attribute.
וְהֵם הָיוּ שָׁרְשָׁם בֶּאֱמֶת מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁזֶּהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל: לְהַכִּיר חֶסְרוֹנָם וְשֶׁהֵם צְרִיכִים לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהַשְׁלִימָם
And in their inward root they derived truly from Yaakov Avinu, which is the soul-root of Knesset Israel: to recognize their deficiency and that they need the Blessed Name to complete them;
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם כְּשֶׁטָּעוּ לְהַחְשִׁיב תַּבְנִית שׁוֹר שֶׁבַּמֶּרְכָּבָה לְעִיקָּר דַּרְגַּת דְּיוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, אִיהוּ אַפֵּי זוּטְרֵי — תַּבְנִית עֵגֶל
wherefore even when they erred by considering the form of the Ox in the Chariot as the primary level of Yosef the Righteous (Devarim 33:17), they fashioned its small face—the form of a calf;
וְגַם בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ הָיוּ דְּמוּת כְּרוּבִים, שֶׁאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לִגְלְגוּ עַל זֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יוֹמָא נ״ד עַמּוּד ב׳)
and in the Holy of Holies too there were the forms of Cherubim, which the nations mocked as written (Yoma 54b);
וְאַף הֵם טָעוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת דּוּגְמָתָן
and Israel likewise erred in fashioning a physical counterpart to them;
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכֹּחַ הַטָּעוּת לְהַחֲלִיף בִּפְנֵי הַשּׁוֹר, נִמְשְׁכוּ לְצַד הַשְּׂמֹאל עַד שֶׁטָּעוּ לִקְרוֹתוֹ גַּם כֵּן אֱלֹהִים וְדַחֲלָן
except that through the error of substituting the face of the Ox, they were drawn to the left side (Gevurah / judgment) until they erred into calling it an idol and god.
וְזֶה כָּל עִנְיַן הַסָּתַת נָחָשׁ בְּעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע: הוּא לִנְטוֹת מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים שֶׁהוּא הַקַּו הָאֶמְצָעִי לַקְּצוֹת
And this is the entire essence of the Serpent's seduction regarding the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil: to deflect man from the Tree of Life (the Central Pillar) unto the polarized extremes;
דְּשָׁם יֵשׁ מְצִיאוּת לִפְסֹולֶת וִידִיעַת טוֹב וָרָע, וְאָז מִשָּׁם נָקֵל לוֹ לְהַטּוֹתוֹ לְצַד הָרָע לְגַמְרֵי
for at the extremes there is room for dross and the knowledge of good and evil, whence it is easy for the yetzer to tilt man entirely toward evil;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי [אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם]... אָכֵן כְּאָדָם תְּמוּתוּן״ (תְּהִלִּים פ״ב:ו׳–ז׳)
and concerning this it is said: "I said: You are godlike beings... nevertheless you shall die like Adam" (Tehillim 82:6–7).
וְהַפָּרָה הִיא הַמְקַנַּחַת צוֹאָה זוֹ, דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה נִקְרָא ״צוֹאָה״: ״צֵא תֹּאמַר לוֹ״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ל:כב; שַׁבָּת פ״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
And the Red Heifer cleanses this excrement, for idolatry is termed "excrement" (tzo'ah): "'Get you hence' (tzei), you shall say unto it" (Yeshayah 30:22; Shabbos 82a);
וְעַל כֵּן אוֹתוֹ שֶׁעָבַר עֲבֵירַת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה נִידּוֹן בְּצוֹאָה רוֹתַחַת (גִּיטִּין נ״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
wherefore one who transgresses in idolatry is punished in boiling excrement (Gittin 57a);
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִלְעִיג עַל דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים (עֵרוּבִין כ״א עַמּוּד ב׳)
and our Rabbis explained: because he mocked the words of the Sages (Eruvin 21b);
וְהַיְינוּ דִּבְזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
meaning that within the seed of Israel an intrinsic desire for idolatry cannot exist,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב דְּלֹא עָבְדוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֶלָּא לְהַתִּיר עֲרָיוֹת (סַנְהֶדְרִין ס״ג עַמּוּד ב׳)
as written that they served idols only to permit illicit sexual relations in public (Sanhedrin 63b);
וּמִי שֶׁאֵין כַּוָּונָתוֹ לְכָךְ, בָּא לוֹ מַחֲשָׁבָה זוֹ עַל יְדֵי הַלְעָגָה וְלֵיצָנוּת מִדִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים
and one whose motive is not lust arrives at foreign thoughts solely through mocking and scoffing at the words of the Sages;
דְּזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק, הָרֵאשִׁית דְּגוֹיִם שֶׁנִּקְרָא ״לֵץ״
for this is the root of Amalek, the first of the nations, who is called a "scorner" (leitz),
דְּמִמֶּנּוּ נִמְשָׁכִים אַחַר כָּךְ בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כָּל מִינֵי עֲבוֹדוֹת זָרוֹת שֶׁל כָּל עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
whence expand subsequently all manners of idolatries of all the pagan nations;
כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַהַלְעָגָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ נַעֲשָׂה כָּל גּוּפוֹ צוֹאָה, בִּהְיוֹת מוֹחוֹ בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא גָּמוּר שֶׁהוּא מָקוֹם לִיצִיאַת פְּסֹולֶת הַמַּאֲכָל
for through cynicism in the brain the entire body is rendered as excrement, the brain becoming a privy where food dross is excreted.
וְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה הֵם מְזוֹן הַנֶּפֶשׁ, וְהוּא לֶחֶם שֶׁמַּלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אוֹכְלִים
And words of Torah are the true nourishment of the soul, the bread that ministering angels eat (Yoma 75b),
מָזוֹן הַנִּבְלָע בִּרְמַ״ח אֵיבָרִים שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ פְּסֹולֶת
food absorbed directly into the 248 limbs without any waste;
אֲבָל חָכְמָה חִיצוֹנִית הַמְּצוּיָה גַּם בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
but external wisdom found among the nations of the world,
וְיֵשׁ מַה שֶּׁהוּא נִקְרָא ״חָכְמָה״ בֶּאֱמֶת שֶׁנִּקְרָא גַּם בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב חָכְמָה
and there is that which is genuinely termed "wisdom" even in the language of Scripture,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם קוֹלְטִים הַפְּסֹולֶת מִמֶּנּוּ כִּי בָּזֶה שָׁרְשָׁם, וּפְסֹולְתּוֹ הִיא הַלֵּיצָנוּת מֵחָכְמָה הָאֲמִיתִּית
yet they absorb the dross from it, such being their root, and its dross is mockery of true sacred wisdom;
וְכָל מִינֵי עֲבוֹדוֹת זָרוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ מַתְעִים הַהֲמוֹן, וַדַּאי הָיוּ מַרְאִים לָהֶם בְּחָכְמָתָם הַמְזוֹהֶמֶת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ מַמָּשׁ
and in all pagan idolatries that misled the masses, they demonstrated through their corrupted intellect that it supposedly held substance,
אֲבָל הַכֹּל נִמְשָׁךְ מִצַּד הַלֵּיצָנוּת מֵהָאֱמֶת, עַל יְדֵי זֶה מַמְצִיאִים שֶׁקֶר הַמִּתְדַּמֶּה לֶאֱמֶת
yet all of it derived from cynicism toward the truth, forging a falsehood that mimics the truth.
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן עִנְיַן עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דִּפְעוֹר
And this is likewise the nature of the idolatry of Ba'al Pe'or (Bamidbar 25:3);
דִּלְעֻומַּת זֶה נִקְבַּר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת עַל שְׁמוֹ
directly opposite which Moshe Rabbeinu was buried, he being the root of the Torah called by his name (Malachi 3:22),
שֶׁהוּא מַמָּשׁ הֵיפֶךְ הַלֵּיצָנוּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״נִכְנַס דְּבַר שֶׁל תּוֹרָה — יָצָא כְּנֶגְדּוֹ דְּבַר שֶׁל לֵיצָנוּת״ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א:ב)
which is the exact antithesis of mockery, as written: "when a word of Torah enters, a word of scoffing departs" (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2);
וּמִמֵּילָא נִתְבַּטֵּל עִנְיַן הַפְּעוֹר, שֶׁהוּא קְצֵה הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל לֵיצָנוּת
and automatically the power of Pe'or is nullified, which represents the extreme nadir of cynicism:
דַּעֲמָלֵק הוּא הָרֵאשִׁית דְּגוֹיִם, וּפְעוֹר הוּא הָאַחֲרִית דְּגוֹיִם
for Amalek is the beginning of the nations, while Pe'or is the end of the nations,
דְּ״אִם לַלֵּצִים הוּא יָלִיץ״ (מִשְׁלֵי ג:לד), וּכְלוּם יֵשׁ לֵיצָנוּת גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה הָעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דִּפְעוֹר
for "if it concerns the scorners, He scorns them" (Mishlei 3:34), and is there any mockery greater than the worship of Pe'or [defecating before the idol]?
וְלֵיצָנוּתָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דְּשַׁרְיָא הוּא בְּעִנְיָנִים אֵלּוּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם בַּגְּמָרָא דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ס״ד עַמּוּד א׳):
and mockery of idolatry which is permitted (Megillah 25b) applies specifically to such matters, see there in the Gemara in Sanhedrin (64a).

7.h: The theme: The purification of the Calf through the mother Heifer (imah) and the reduction to primordial dust (afar). At the beginning of the Exodus, Amalek confronted Israel; at the end of the forty years in the wilderness, the idolatry of Pe'or confronted them, completely subduing the full stature of pagan idolatry. The error of the Golden Calf, however, was not pagan idolatry, nor did Israel mock the Sages; they believed deeply in Moshe, but exaggerated his spiritual detachment, assuming he had permanently remained an angel on High. Excessive praise brings degradation ("he who praises his fellow excessively, it turns to slander", Bava Batra 164b), and from this slight mistake arose the tragedy of the Calf. Sweetening any spiritual defect occurs at its root, termed the "mother" (imah): "let the mother [the Red Heifer] come and cleanse the filth of her son [the Calf]".
