In maternal lineage, the mother represents the manifest root in this world, wherefore incantations and sorcery invoke the mother's name (Shabbos 66b; Zohar I, 84a). Animals lack spiritual paternal lineage because the animal soul (nefesh ha-bahamis) is confined to the temporary life of this world; hence its root relates entirely to the mother. Burning the Heifer to ash nullifies the animal soul's capacity for evil, returning it to a simple, uncompounded element (yesod pashut), the letter Vav, mirroring Avraham's nullification: "and I am dust and ashes" (Bereishis 18:27). The Resurrection cannot occur until the body decomposes into simple dust one hour prior (Shabbos 152b), from which it returns to the supernal simple source (ratzo v'shov), rebuilding an eternal vessel.

p: וּתְחִלַּת יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם פָּגַע בָּהֶם עֲמָלֵק, וּבְסוֹף דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר פָּגַע בָּהֶם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דִּפְעוֹר
And at the beginning of the Exodus from Egypt Amalek assaulted them, and at the end of the generation of the wilderness the idolatry of Pe'or assaulted them;
וְאָז הִשְׁלִימוּ לְהַכְנִיעַ כָּל הַקּוֹמָה דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁל עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
and then they completed the subjugation of the entire structure of the idolatry of the nations.
וְטָעוּת הָעֵגֶל לֹא הָיָה לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת חַס וְחָלִילָה
And the error of the Golden Calf had no connection to pagan idolatry, God forbid;
וְהֵם לֹא הִלְעִיגוּ עַל דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים חַס וְחָלִילָה, אַדְּרַבָּא הֶאֱמִינוּ מְאֹד בְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
nor did they mock the words of the Sages, God forbid, but on the contrary believed deeply in Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him;
רַק דְּאָמְרוּ: ״[כִּי זֶה מֹשֶׁה הָאִישׁ...] לֹא יָדַעְנוּ מֶה הָיָה לוֹ״ (שְׁמוֹת ל״ב:א׳)
except that they said: "as for this Moses, the man... we know not what is become of him" (Shemos 32:1),
שֶׁחָשְׁבוּ שֶׁהוּא עָמֹק עָמֹק לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲמוֹד עַל מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ וְלֵידַע מַה הָיָה לוֹ כְּלָל
assuming that he was profound and exalted beyond human perception, so that it was impossible to fathom his level or know what had become of him,
כִּי הוּא כְּאֶחָד מִצְּבָא הַמָּרוֹם בַּמָּרוֹם
for he was like one of the supernal host on High;
וְעַל כֵּן חָשְׁבוּ דְּנִשְׁאַר בַּמָּרוֹם וְאֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת עִם בְּנֵי אָדָם, וְזֶה אַדְּרַבָּא תּוֹסֶפֶת הַגְדָּלָה בִּכְבוֹדוֹ
wherefore they believed he had remained on High, having no further contact with mortals, which on the contrary was an excessive glorification of his honor!
וְגַם זֶה אֵין רָאוּי, וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק גֵּט פָּשׁוּט (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קס״ד עַמּוּד ב׳): ״אַל יְסַפֵּר [אָדָם בְּטוֹבָתוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ טוֹבָתוֹ בָּא לִידֵי רָעָתוֹ]״

Yet this too is inappropriate, along the lines of what they stated in Perek Get Pashut (Bava Batra 164b): "A person should never relate the praise of his fellow, for out of his praise he comes to his detriment";
דְּגַם זֶה נֶחְשָׁב לָשׁוֹן הָרָע, וְזֶה מֵבִיא לְהַשְׁפָּלַת עַצְמוֹ
for excessive praise is reckoned slander, leading to self-abasement;
וּכְדַרְכּוֹ שֶׁל יֵצֶר הָרָע: הַיּוֹם אוֹמֵר לוֹ עֲשֵׂה כָּךְ וְכוּלֵיהּ (שַׁבָּת ק״ה עַמּוּד ב׳)
and such is the strategy of the yetzer hara: today it tells him, "Do this," and tomorrow, "Do that" (Shabbos 105b);
כִּי כָּל טָעוּת קַל יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת לְאַט לְאַט ״מֵחַבְלֵי הַשָּׁוְא כַּעֲבוֹת הָעֲגָלָה״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ה:יח)
for any slight error can gradually expand from "cords of vanity" into "thick cart-ropes" (Yeshayah 5:18).
וְקִינּוּחַ זֶה עַל יְדֵי הַפָּרָה הַמּוֹלִידָה הָעֵגֶל
And the cleansing of this blemish is accomplished through the Cow that gives birth to the Calf;
שֶׁהַמְתָּקַת כָּל דָּבָר הוּא בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ, וְהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ נִקְרָא ״אִמֵּיהּ״ בְּכָל דּוּכְתֵּי
for the sweetening of every defect occurs at its root, and the root is called "its mother" (imeih) in all places:
כְּמוֹ בַּחֲגִיגָה (ט״ו עַמּוּד ב׳): ״כָּל עֲמַר דַּהֲוָה נָקֵי אַגַּב אִמֵּיהּ וְכוּלֵיהּ״ וְלֹא אֲבוּהּ
as in Chagigah (15b): "any wool that was clean through its mother, etc.," and it did not say its father;
כִּי הָאֵם הִיא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנִּגְלֶה, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הָאָב הוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם
for the mother is the manifest biological root, whereas the father is hidden;
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק בַּמֶּה אִשָּׁה (שַׁבָּת ס״ו עַמּוּד ב׳): ״כָּל מִנְיָינֵי — בִּשְׁמֵיהּ דְּאִמֵּיהּ״
wherefore they stated in Shabbat (66b): "all incantations are recited with the mother's name";
וּבַזֹּוהַר (שְׁמוֹת י״ז רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב׳) דִּמְכַשְּׁפִים מַזְכִּירִים שֵׁם אִמּוֹ
and in the Zohar (II, 17b) that sorcerers invoke the mother's name;
וְאִם אִיתָא הַטַּעַם: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ חֲשָׁדָא
and if the reason given is because there is no doubt of maternal parentage;
וְנִרְאֶה הַכַּוָּונָה גַּם כֵּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: כִּי כָּל כֹּחָם הוּא בַּנִּגְלֶה וְלֹא בִּפְנִימִיּוּת הַדָּבָר וּבְהֶעְלֵם כְּלָל
it also reflects this truth: their entire demonic power operates in the external, revealed realm and not in the hidden interior,
דְּכָל כֹּחָם רַק מִצַּד הִתְגַּלּוּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְהָאֵם הִיא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנִּגְלֶה
all their strength existing on the manifest plane of this world, and the mother is the revealed root;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הָאָב הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם דּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין מְבוֹרָר וְאִית בֵּיהּ חֲשָׁדָא
whereas the father is the concealed root which in this world is not visibly certified and admits doubt,
וּבָזֶה אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת וְכֹחַ שְׁלִיטָה עַד שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and in that hidden dimension the forces of sorcery possess no affinity or dominion;
וְעַיֵּין בַּזֹּוהַר לֶךְ לְךָ (פ״ד סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳) דְּאִיהוּ אָמַר בִּשְׁמָהּ דְּאִמֵּיהּ לְקַבֵּל מִלָּה עִילָּאָה וְכוּלֵיהּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם
and see Zohar (I, 84a) that he invoked his mother's name to receive the supernal word, see there;
רָצָה לוֹמַר גַּם כֵּן הַכַּוָּונָה: מִצַּד הַקִּיבּוּל דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַנִּגְלֶה צָרִיךְ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנִּגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
meaning likewise: from the perspective of receiving influx into the revealed world, one requires the revealed earthly root.
וּבִבְהֵמָה לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ יִחוּס אָב כְּלָל, דְּעַל כֵּן אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְזֶרַע הָאָב
And in an animal paternal lineage does not exist at all, wherefore the halachah generally does not suspect the seed of the father (Chullin 79a);
וְגַם לְמַאן דְּאָמַר חוֹשְׁשִׁין, מִכָּל מָקוֹם יִחוּס אָבוֹת לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ בְּהוּ
and even according to the authority who holds we do suspect the father's seed, genealogical lineage does not apply to them;
כִּי נֶפֶשׁ בַּהֲמִית הוּא רַק חַיֵּי שָׁעָה דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְאֵין לָהּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ נֶעְלָם כְּלָל, עַל כֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחָהּ מִתְיַיחֵס אֶל הָאֵם
for the animal soul is merely the temporary life of this world and possesses no concealed divine root, wherefore its root is attributed to the mother.
וְעַל כֵּן שׂוֹרְפִין הַפָּרָה לְאֵפֶר, שֶׁהוּא בִּיטּוּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַכֹּחַ זֶה דְּנֶפֶשׁ הַבַּהֲמִית לְרוֹעַ הַנָּטוּעַ בְּלִבְּבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
And therefore the Red Heifer is burned to ashes, which is the nullification of this root of the animal soul's capacity for evil planted within the hearts of Israel,
עַד שֶׁשָּׁב לְאֵפֶר שֶׁהוּא יְסוֹד פָּשׁוּט
until it returns to ash, which is a simple, uncompounded element;
דְּזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית הַבִּיטּוּל בַּמְּצִיאוּת כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר אַבְרָהָם: ״וְאָנֹכִי עָפָר וָאֵפֶר״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ח:כ״ז)
for this is the ultimate nullification of existence (bittul ba-metzi'us) before the Almighty, in the manner Avraham said: "and I am but dust and ashes" (Bereishis 18:27);
כִּי מִצַּד הַרְכָּבַת הָאַרְבָּעָה יְסוֹדוֹת הֵם כָּל מִינֵי בְּחִירָה וּנְטִיּוֹת לַצְּדָדִין
for from the composite mixture of the four elements arise all vacillations of choice and lateral inclinations;
אֲבָל בִּיסוֹד פָּשׁוּט הוּא הַפְּשִׁיטוּת בְּלִי שׁוּם נְטִיָּה
but within a simple, unmixed element reigns pure simplicity without divergence.
וְזֶהוּ אוֹת הַוָּי״ו שֶׁהוּא קַו פָּשׁוּט בְּלִי נְטִיָּה לַצְּדָדִין כִּשְׁאָר אוֹתִיּוֹת
And this is the letter Vav, which is a straight line without lateral deviation unlike other letters;
וְעַל יְדֵי הַפְּשִׁיטוּת יוּכַל לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט עַד אֵין קֵץ, וְלִהְיוֹת דָּבוּק בִּמְקוֹרוֹ
and through this simplicity it can extend endlessly and cleave unto its Source,
שֶׁבָּזֶה חוֹזֵר לְתַכְלִית הַפְּשִׁיטוּת הַגָּמוּר בְּלִי שׁוּם הַרְכָּבָה כְּלָל
returning to absolute primal simplicity devoid of any compound mixture.
וּתְחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים אִי אֶפְשָׁר עַד שֶׁתָּשׁוּב הֶעָפָר אֶל הָאָרֶץ כְּשֶׁהָיָה
And the Resurrection of the Dead cannot occur until the dust returns to the earth as it was (Koheles 12:7),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: דְּהַהִיא שָׁעָה אַחַת קוֹדֶם תְּחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים (שַׁבָּת קנ״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
as the Sages stated: that decomposition occurs during the single hour prior to the Resurrection (Shabbos 152b);
וְאָז כְּשֶׁיָּשׁוּב לִיסוֹד פָּשׁוּט דְּעָפָר גָּמוּר, אָז יוּכַל מִשָּׁם דַּיְיקָא לְהִכָּלֵל בַּמָּקוֹר הָעֶלְיוֹן שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן יְסוֹד פָּשׁוּט
and then, when it returns to the simple element of pure dust, specifically from there can it be integrated into the Supernal Source which is likewise a simple essence;
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ הַבְּרָקִים: ״רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב״ (יְחֶזְקֵאל א:יד), דִּלְמָקוֹם שֶׁהוֹלְכִים שָׁם שָׁבִים
after the manner of lightning: "running and returning" (Yechezkel 1:14), returning to the very place whence they went forth,
דְּחוֹזֵר וְנַעֲשָׂה הַסּוֹף רֹאשׁ, שֶׁזֶּה סוֹד ״נָעוּץ סוֹפָן בִּתְחִלָּתָן״ (סֵפֶר יְצִירָה א:ז) שֶׁבִּכְלַל הַבְּרִיאָה
where the end turns back into the beginning, which is the mystery of "their end is wedged in their beginning" (Sefer Yetzirah 1:7) throughout Creation;
וְיָשׁוּב לְהִתְבַּנּוֹת בִּנְיָן הַקַּיָּים לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד שֶׁלֹּא יִכְלֶה עוֹד כְּלָל
and the body will be rebuilt into an everlasting edifice that will never perish again.
וְעַל כֵּן אֵפֶר זֶה דְּפָרָה הוּא הַמְטַהֵר טְמֵאִים דְּטֻמְאַת מֵת
Therefore this ash of the Red Heifer purifies those defiled by corpse-uncleanness;
שֶׁזִּכָּרוֹן זֶה בַּלֵּב — הַיְינוּ שֶׁיַּעֲמוֹק בְּהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת לְבַטֵּל כָּל כֹּחוֹת הָרָע בִּמְקוֹרָן עַד שֶׁיָּשׁוּבוּ עָפָר וָאֵפֶר
for holding this remembrance in the heart—deeply contemplating to nullify all evil forces at their source until they return to dust and ashes—
הוּא קִינּוּחַ צוֹאַת הָעֵגֶל וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ טִנּוּפֶת זוֹ שֶׁבַּלֵּב
is the true cleansing of the filth of the Calf and the root of this pollution in the heart,
שֶׁלֹּא תִּתְבָּעֵר מִן הַלֵּב לְגַמְרֵי עַד עֵת קֵץ שֶׁיְּבוֹעַר הַיֵּצֶר רָע מִן הָעוֹלָם וּבֻלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח:
which will not be completely eradicated from the human heart until the time of the end when the yetzer hara is expunged and death is swallowed up forever.

7.h: The theme: The slow erasure through pekidah ("on the day when I visit, I will visit", Shemos 32:34) and Parashat Parah before Pesach. So long as man has not attained the ultimate level of the end of days, the sin of the Calf is visited slowly through pekidah ("and in the day when I visit, I will visit their sin upon them", Shemos 32:34). Unlike Amalek, whose evil expands outward into the revealed heart and is blotted out through verbal remembrance (zechirah / confession in the mouth), the Serpent's instigation is embedded within the concealed depths of the heart (ha-ne'elam she-ba-lev). It is purified through pekidah—concealed mental contemplation and the internal heartache (agmas nefesh) and bitterness over sin. Burning the Heifer to ash purifies contact with the dead, which signifies contact with the primordial "father of fathers of impurity"—the Serpent's instigation. Now that we lack the physical ash of the Heifer, "we render the calves of our lips" (u-neshalmah farim sefaseinu, Hoshea 14:3) by reading Parashat Parah before Pesach, instilling this purification into the heart little by little, to merit on Pesach the resurrection of the dead (alluded to in the Haftarah of the Dry Bones on Shabbat Chol HaMoed Pesach, Yechezkel 37).

p: וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ עֲדַיִין, נֶאֱמַר: ״וּבְיוֹם פָּקְדִי וּפָקַדְתִּי [עֲלֵיהֶם חַטָּאתָם]״ (שְׁמוֹת ל״ב:ל״ד)
And as long as humanity has not yet attained this final level, it is said: "Nevertheless in the day when I visit, I will visit their sin upon them" (Shemos 32:34);
שֶׁהוּא נִמְחֶה בִּפְקִידָה לְאַט לְאַט
the sin being erased through visitation (pekidah) little by little (Sanhedrin 102a),
וְלֹא כִּמְחִיַּיִת עֲמָלֵק שֶׁהוּא בִּזְכִירָה דְּהוּא בַּפֶּה
and not like the eradication of Amalek which is accomplished through active remembrance (zechirah) in the mouth;
הַיְינוּ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת בְּפֹעַל נִגְלֶה, הוּא עֲקִירַת הָרָע הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט בְּפֹעַל בַּלֵּב בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁעִקָּרָהּ וִוידּוּי דְּבָרִים בַּפֶּה
meaning that in revealed concrete action, it is the uprooting of the evil that actively spreads within the revealed heart through repentance, whose essence is verbal confession in the mouth;
כִּי הַפֶּה גּוֹמֵר, לִהְיוֹתוֹ שְׁלִיחַ הַלֵּב וּכְמוֹתוֹ
for the mouth completes the thought, being the emissary of the heart and like unto it [the mouth and heart corresponding to the two letters Hei of the Name Havayah as is known];
כִּי עֲמָלֵק הוּא ״רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ד:כ׳), וְאֶצְלָם הוּא גַּם בְּשָׁרְשָׁם וְכָל מַעֲמַקָּן הַנֶּעְלָם
for Amalek is the "first of the nations," and within them evil permeates their very root and all their hidden depths;
וְאֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא רַק מִצַּד הִתְגַּלּוּת הַלֵּב וְלֹא בַּנֶּעְלָם שֶׁבּוֹ
whereas within the Children of Israel, Amalekite evil touches merely the revealed surface of the heart and not its concealed core.
אֲבָל עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ נִמְשָׁךְ הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּרֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם וְהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה
But the instigation of the Serpent (ityo shel nachash), whence is drawn the root of the first of the nations, being the root of this root,
יֶשְׁנוֹ גַּם בַּנֶּעְלָם שֶׁבַּלֵּב, וְהוּא נִמְחֶה עַל יְדֵי פְּקִידָה שֶׁהוּא בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה הַנֶּעְלֶמֶת
is present even within the concealed depths of the heart, and it is erased through pekidah [visitation], which operates within concealed thought;
וּמְחִיָּתוֹ הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַיִּסּוּרִין וְעָגְמַת נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בַּלֵּב עַל הַחֵטְא
and its cleansing is achieved through the inner tribulations and mental anguish (agmas nefesh) one suffers in his heart over sin;
וְזֶהוּ: ״וּפָקַדְתִּי עֲלֵיהֶם חַטָּאתָם״ (שְׁמוֹת ל״ב:ל״ד), שֶׁיַּכְנִיס זֶה בִּלְבָבָם לְהִתְמַרְמֵר מְאֹד עַל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנְּטוּיָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב לָזֶה
and this is: "I will visit their sin upon them," that Hashem instills this deep grief into their hearts to become exceedingly embittered over the heart's subtle inclination toward evil;
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי שְׂרֵיפַת הַפָּרָה לְאֵפֶר
and this internal purification is wrought through the burning of the Red Heifer to ash;
וּבָזֶה הוּא הַטָּהֳרָה מִנְּגִיעָה בַּמֵּת, רָצָה לוֹמַר הַנְּגִיעָה בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ אֲבִי אֲבוֹת הַטּוּמְאָה דְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ
and in this lies purification from contact with the dead, meaning contact with the root of the father of fathers of impurity—the Serpent's instigation.
וְעַכְשָׁיו שֶׁאֵין לָנוּ אֵפֶר פָּרָה וַעֲשִׂיַּית הַמִּצְוָה בְּפֹעַל, ״נְשַׁלְּמָה פָרִים שְׂפָתֵינוּ״ (הוֹשֵׁעַ י״ד:ג׳) בִּקְרִיאַת הַפָּרָשָׁה

And now that we lack the ashes of the Heifer and the performance of the commandment in concrete practice, "we render the calves of our lips" (Hoshea 14:3) through the public reading of the portion of Parah;
שֶׁפּוֹעֵל לְהַכְנִיס דָּבָר זֶה בַּלֵּב מְעַט מְעַט
which operates to instill this spiritual purification into the heart little by little;
וְהוּא לִפְנֵי הַפֶּסַח, כְּדֵי לִזְכּוֹת עַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּפֶסַח לִתְחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אָז בְּפֶסַח
and it is scheduled prior to Pesach, in order to merit through it on Pesach the Resurrection of the Dead which will unfold on Pesach;
דְּעַל כֵּן מַפְטִירִין בְּשַׁבַּת חוֹל הַמּוֹעֵד פֶּסַח ״הָעֲצָמוֹת הַיְבֵשׁוֹת״ (יְחֶזְקֵאל ל״ז):
wherefore on the intermediate Sabbath of Pesach we read as the Haftarah the vision of the Dry Bones (Yechezkel 37).

7.h: The theme: The Resurrection of the Dead on the Sabbath of Pesach, the Four Portions, and the eternal monarchy of David versus the temporal reign of Yosef. The Resurrection of the Dead will occur on the Sabbath falling within Pesach, mirroring the Giving of the Torah which occurred on Shabbat according to all opinions (Shabbat 86b), when the reviving dew of resurrection descended (Shabbat 88b) and Israel merited temporary liberation from the Angel of Death. The Four Portions prepare for this: the two before Purim (Shekalim and Zachor) prepare for freedom from the yetzer hara through the destruction of Amalek; the two after Purim (Parah and HaChodesh) prepare for freedom from the Angel of Death. Parashat Parah corresponds to potentiality (the letter Vav), while Parashat HaChodesh corresponds to actualization (the final letter Hei), bringing forth the renewal of the month of Aviv. This alludes to David, King of Israel, who lives and endures (chai v'kayam), representing the perfection of eternal life attained through longing and prayer ("He asked life of You, You gave it to him", Tehillim 21:5). On the first of Nissan—the New Year for Jewish kings—the eternal sovereignty of the House of David begins to manifest. Although interrupted during exile, this cessation is merely an illusion of this world; in the ultimate redemption, all temporal losses will be seen as mere dreams ("we were like dreamers", Tehillim 126:1). In contrast, the sovereignty of Yosef was revealed only through dreams, because his reign was strictly temporary within this finite world.

p: וְנִרְאֶה לִי דְּיִהְיֶה תְּחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים בְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הַפֶּסַח
And it appears to me that the Resurrection of the Dead will occur on the Sabbath within the festival of Pesach;
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַתַּן תּוֹרָה דְּהָיָה בְּשַׁבָּת לְכוּלֵי עָלְמָא (שַׁבָּת פ״ו עַמּוּד ב׳)
and this follows the pattern of the Giving of the Torah which occurred on Shabbat according to all authorities (Shabbat 86b);
דְּיָרַד אָז גַּם כֵּן טַל שֶׁל תְּחִיָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא (שָׁם פ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳)
when there descended likewise the reviving dew of resurrection, as written in Perek Rabbi Akiva (ibid. 88b);
וְזָכוּ לְשָׁעָה לִהְיוֹת חֵירוּת מִמַּלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה מ״א:ז׳; עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
and they merited temporarily to be liberated from the Angel of Death;
וְשַׁבָּת שֶׁהוּא מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא (בְּרָכוֹת נ״ז עַמּוּד ב׳) הוּא הַזְּמַן לָזֶה
and the Sabbath, which is a foretaste of the World to Come (Berachos 57b), is the designated season for this;
וּבְפֶסַח שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא הַתְחָלַת הַחֵירוּת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, בּוֹ יִהְיֶה גַּם כֵּן הַגְּמָר דְּחֵירוּת מִמַּלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת וְיֵצֶר הָרָע
and in Pesach, wherein lies the inception of the freedom of the Children of Israel, in it will likewise unfold the ultimate completion of freedom from the Angel of Death and the evil inclination;
וְכָל אַרְבַּע פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת הֵם הֲכָנָה לָזֶה
and all Four Portions (Arba Parshiyot) are a spiritual preparation for this:
שְׁתַּיִם דְּקוֹדֶם פּוּרִים [שְׁקָלִים וְזָכוֹר] הֵם הֲכָנָה לִמְחִיַּיִת עֲמָלֵק, שֶׁהוּא הַחֵירוּת דְּיֵצֶר הָרָע
the two prior to Purim [Shekalim and Zachor] are a preparation for the eradication of Amalek, which is the liberation from the yetzer hara;
וּשְׁתַּיִם דְּאַחַר פּוּרִים [פָּרָה וְהַחֹדֶשׁ] הֲכָנָה לְחֵירוּת מִמַּלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת
and the two after Purim [Parah and HaChodesh] are a preparation for liberation from the Angel of Death.
וּפָרָשַׁת פָּרָה הוּא בְּכֹחַ, שֶׁזֶּהוּ אוֹת הַוָּי״ו שֶׁהֵם כֹּחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה שֶׁבַּכֹּחַ
And Parashat Parah represents potentiality (b'cho'ach), which is the letter Vav, embodying the active faculties within potential;
וּפָרָשַׁת הַחֹדֶשׁ הוּא הַהַמְשָׁכָה מִן הַכֹּחַ לַפּוֹעַל בְּהִתְחַדְּשׁוּת חֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב
and Parashat HaChodesh represents the actualization from potential into concrete realization in the renewal of the month of Aviv (Nissan);
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הֵ״א אַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁבַּשֵּׁם, שֶׁהוּא גְּמַר הַשְׁלָמַת כָּל הַהִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְגַלּוֹת בָּעוֹלָם
which is the final letter Hei of the Divine Name Havayah, being the final completion of the entire revelation that the Blessed Name willed to reveal in the world;
וְרוֹמֶזֶת לְדָוִד מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל הַחַי וְקַיָּים (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כ״ה עַמּוּד א׳)
and it alludes to David, King of Israel, who lives and endures (chai v'kayam, Rosh Hashanah 25a);
שֶׁהוּא הַשְּׁלֵימוּת דְּחַיֵּי עוֹלָם שֶׁרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם וְחֶשְׁקָם לָזֶה
who embodies the perfection of eternal life that the Blessed Name willed to exist in the lower realms through human exertion and longing for it;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״חַיִּים שָׁאַל מִמְּךָ — נָתַתָּה לּוֹ״ (תְּהִלִּים כ״א:ה׳), עַל יְדֵי הַשְּׁאֵלָה דַּוְוקָא
as it is written: "He asked life of You, You gave it to him" (Tehillim 21:5)—specifically through the asking!
הַיְינוּ הַחֵשֶׁק לָזֶה וְהַתְּפִלָּה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁזֶּהוּ רָזָא דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: ״וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה״ (שָׁם ק״ט:ד׳)
Meaning the intense longing for this and prayer unto the Blessed Name, which is the mystery of David HaMelech, peace be upon him: "but I am all prayer" (Tehillim 109:4).
וּבְאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לַמְּלָכִים מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה ב׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
And on the first of Nissan is the New Year for the kings of Israel (Rosh Hashanah 2a);
שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא הַתְחָלַת הִתְגַּלּוּת כֹּחַ הַמְּלוּכָה לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהִיא חֵלֶק מִמַּלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא מַלְכוּת כָּל עוֹלָמִים
wherein begins the revelation of the royal power of the Children of Israel, which is an impartation of His divine Kingdom which is an everlasting kingdom (Tehillim 145:13);
וְהַיְינוּ דָּבָר הַקַּיָּים דְּלָא יְסוּף וְלָא יֶעְדֵּי לְעוֹלָם (דָּנִיֵּאל ז:יד)
meaning an enduring reality that shall neither end nor pass away forever (Daniel 7:14);
וְאַף שֶׁנִּרְאֶה בִּיטּוּל בֵּינְתַיִים, אֵלָּא מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and even though an interruption appears in the interim, it exists merely from the surface perspective of this earthly world;
וּכְמוֹ הַמִּיתָה דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דִּלְאַחַר תְּחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים יִהְיֶה הַמִּיתָה כְּשֵׁינָה בְּעָלְמָא
just like physical death in this world, which after the Resurrection of the Dead will be recognized as having been merely like sleep,
וְכִדְקָרוּ לַהּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם בִּלְשׁוֹן ״דְּמַךְ״
and as our Rabbis everywhere designate death by the Aramaic term damach [fell asleep];
וְאִיתָא בְּפֶרֶק הַדָּר (עֵרוּבִין ס״ה עַמּוּד א׳): ״וְנִינוּם טוּבָא וְכֵן טוּבָא״
and it is taught in Eruvin (65a): "and we slept deeply, and it was beneficial";
אֶלָּא שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין נִגְלֶה, וְאָז יִתְגַּלֶּה זֶה
except that in this world it is not manifest, whereas then this truth will be unveiled.
וְכָךְ כָּל הֶפְסֵק הַמַּלְכוּת דְּבֵית דָּוִד שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דִּ״בְשׁוּב ה׳ אֶת שִׁיבַת צִיּוֹן הָיִינוּ כְּחֹלְמִים״ (תְּהִלִּים קכ״ו:א׳), וְיִהְיֶה זֶה כְּמוֹ בַּחֲלוֹם

And so too with the cessation of the Davidic dynasty in this world: for "When Hashem brought back the captivity of Zion, we were like dreamers" (Tehillim 126:1), and this exile will appear as a mere dream;
דְּכָל יָמָיו שֶׁל דָּוִד לֹא רָאָה חֲלוֹם טוֹב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת נ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳)
for all the days of David he never saw a good dream, as written in Berachos (55b),
וְהָיָה חוֹלֵם לוֹ שֶׁהוּא נוֹפֵל בְּיַד אוֹיְבָיו וְנִיטַּל מַלְכוּתוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכֵּן הָיָה בְּפֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
dreaming that he was falling into the hand of his enemies and his monarchy was severed, just as it occurred in outer reality in this world;
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הוּא הַכֹּל חֲלוֹם וְדִמְיוֹן בְּעָלְמָא, שֶׁהַחֲלוֹם הוֹרָאוֹתָיו רַק עַל מַה שֶּׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה דֶּרֶךְ דִּמְיוֹן
but in absolute truth it is all a dream and an illusion, for dreams reflect only that which belongs to this world by way of imagination;
דְּעַל כֵּן מְלוּכַת יוֹסֵף נִגְלָה לוֹ בַּחֲלוֹם
wherefore the monarchy of Yosef was revealed to him in dreams (Bereishis 37),
כִּי מַלְכוּתוֹ הָיָה רַק לְשָׁעָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְלֹא מַלְכוּת הַקַּיֶּמֶת לָעַד
because his reign was strictly temporary within this world, and not a kingdom that endures forever.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁתַּרְגּוּם אוּנְקְלוֹס עַל פָּסוּק ״הֲמָלֹךְ תִּמְלֹךְ [עָלֵינוּ] וְגוֹמֵר״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״ז:ח׳): ״אַתְּ סָבוּר לִמְמַלְכָא״
And this is what Targum Onkelos translates on the verse "Shall you indeed reign over us?": "Do you imagine (at savur) that you will reign?";
כִּי הֵם הִרְגִּישׁוּ דְּמַלְכוּתוֹ הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַדִּמְיוֹן וְהַסְּבָרָא וּמַחֲשָׁבָה
for the brothers sensed that his kingship belonged merely to the realm of imagination, logical hypothesis (sevara), and mortal thought;
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ לֹא הָיָה דָּבָר רֵיק
except that Yosef's imaginations were not hollow illusions,
וְכָל מַה שֶּׁיִּהְיֶה בְּפֹעַל הַנִּגְלֶה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא עוֹלַם הַדִּמְיוֹן וְהַחֲלוֹם, הָיָה גַּם כֵּן בְּדִמְיוֹנוֹתָיו וַחֲלוֹמוֹתָיו:
and whatever was destined to manifest in actual deed within this world—which is the world of imagination and dreams—was accurately portrayed in his visions and dreams.

7.h: The theme: The contrast between the valor of Yosef and the valor of Yehudah, and the purifications of the Patriarchs and tribes. In this world, kingship was not given immediately to Yehudah because earthly perfection requires concrete, outward restraint (hagdara b'fo'al), which is the rung of Yosef HaTzaddik. This corresponds to Adar, created through the letter Kuf (Kadosh, denoting the fence around sexual immorality, Shabbos 104a). If one breaches this fence, he requires the letter Hei (this world / teshuvah). David HaMelech raised the yoke of repentance and merited eternal life; in contrast, Mashiach ben Yosef will be slain (Sukkah 52a) because according to the strict justice of outward boundaries, any subtle trace of the Serpent's instigation must be cleansed through physical death. Yet "Yehudah prevailed above his brethren" (I Divrei HaYamim 5:2): Yosef’s might subdued the nations and the foreign lusts in the heart, while Yehudah’s might subdued the inner spiritual deficiencies of his own brethren. The tribes still possessed subtle traces of the Serpent's instigation that required purifications (beirurim), which is why the sorrow of Yosef assaulted Yaakov right after the tribes were born. To undergo his own purification, Yosef was sold into the depravity of Egypt as a slave, totally subjugated to his master; there he conquered his passion against Potiphar's wife, rescued by the image of his father's visage (demus diyukno shel aviv, Sotah 36b), which reminded him of the unblemished perfection of Yaakov's bed.

p: וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה לֹא הִגִּיעַ הַמְּלוּכָה לִיהוּדָה, כִּי הַשְּׁלֵימוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא מִצַּד הַהַגְדָּרָה בְּפֹעַל
And from this perspective kingship did not initially arrive unto Yehudah, for perfection in this world requires concrete protective restraint (hagdara b'fo'al);
וְזֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּיוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, וְהוּא נֶגֶד חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּאוֹת קוּ״ף הַמּוֹרֶה ״קָדוֹשׁ״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת (ק״ד עַמּוּד א׳)
and this is the spiritual rung of Yosef the Righteous, corresponding to the month of Adar created through the letter Kuf denoting "holy" (kadosh) as written in Shabbat (104a);
וְ״כָל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא גֶּדֶר עֶרְוָה — שָׁם אַתָּה מוֹצֵא קְדוּשָׁה״ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כ״ד:ו׳)
and "wherever you find a fence against sexual immorality, there you find holiness" (Vayikra Rabbah 24:6);
וּמִי שֶׁכְּבָר יָצָא דִּלְעֵיל בַּהַךְ, רָמוּז בְּאוֹת הֵ״א שֶׁבּוֹ נִבְרָא עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מְנָחוֹת כ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
and one who has already stepped outside that fence must enter back through the letter Hei through which this world was created (Menachos 29b);
שֶׁשָּׁם הַחֲטָאִים, וְצָרִיךְ לִתְשׁוּבָה עִילָּאָה וְתַתָּאָה שֶׁהֵם ב׳ הַהֵהִי״ן דְּהַשֵּׁם
for therein occur sins, requiring higher and lower repentance (teshuvah ila'ah and teshuvah tata'ah), which are the two letters Hei of the Name Havayah;
וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא שֶׁהֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה (מוֹעֵד קָטָן ט״ז עַמּוּד ב׳), הוּא שֶׁזָּכָה לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם דְּזֶהוּ רַק עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה
and David HaMelech, peace be upon him, who raised up the yoke of repentance (Moed Katan 16b), merited eternal life, which is attained exclusively through repentance.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף יֵהָרֵג, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סֻכָּה נ״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
This is not so with Mashiach ben Yosef, who will be slain, as written in Sukkah (52b);
דְּ״[כִּי אָדָם] אֵין צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ [אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה טּוֹב] וְלֹא יֶחֱטָא״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כ), וְ״הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַחֹטֵאת הִיא תָמוּת״ (יְחֶזְקֵאל י״ח:ד׳)
for "there is not a righteous man upon earth that does good and sins not" (Koheles 7:20), and "the soul that sins, it shall die" (Yechezkel 18:4);
כְּפִי מִשְׁפָּטוֹ בַּהַגְדָּרָה, אֵין תַּקָּנָה לִמְעַט הַחֵטְא דְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ אֶלָּא קְבוּרָה
according to the strict justice of outward boundaries, there is no remedy for the subtle trace of the Serpent's instigation except physical burial.
אֲבָל: ״[כִּי] יְהוּדָה גָּבַר בְּאֶחָיו״ (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א ה:ב)
But: "For Judah prevailed above his brethren" (I Divrei HaYamim 5:2);
כִּי גְּבוּרָה דְּיוֹסֵף הוּא בָּעַמִּים שֶׁעֲלֵיהֶם הָיָה עִיקַּר מַלְכוּתוֹ, הַיְינוּ בִּכְבִישַׁת הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁהֵם כֹּחוֹת הָעַמִּים שֶׁבַּלֵּב
for the valor of Yosef operated over the nations over whom his primary monarchy was established, namely in conquering the yetzer which embodies the forces of the nations within the heart;
וּגְבוּרָה דִּיהוּדָה ״בְּאֶחָיו״ — הַיְינוּ בִּכְבִישַׁת הַחֶסְרוֹנוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּכָל אֶחָיו
whereas the valor of Yehudah was "above his brethren," subduing and rectifying the internal deficiencies present within all his brethren.
כִּי גַּם בְּכָל הַשְּׁבָטִים יֵשׁ אֵיזֶה חִסָּרוֹן בְּכָל אֶחָד בַּתּוֹלָדָה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מֵעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ, שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַן בָּהֶם עֲדַיִין לְגַמְרֵי כִּבְיַעֲקֹב אֲבִיהֶם דְּלֹא מֵת

For within all the tribes there existed a hereditary deficiency derived from the Serpent's instigation, which had not yet been completely rectified within them as it had within their father Yaakov who never died;
כִּי הוּא זָכָה לָזֶה דְּחַיִּים שֶׁלֹּא בְּיֵצֶר הָרָע כִּבְעוֹלָם הַבָּא בְּי״ז שָׁנִים אַחֲרוֹנוֹת שֶׁהָיָה בְּמִצְרַיִם, דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ: ״וַיְחִי יַעֲקֹב״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מ״ז:כ״ח)
for Yaakov merited a life devoid of the yetzer hara like the World to Come during his final seventeen years in Egypt, whereof it is written: "And Jacob lived" (Bereishis 47:28);
דְּאָז הָיָה שְׁלֵימוּת חַיּוּתוֹ וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחַ נַפְשׁוֹ בְּמִדָּתוֹ וְצוּרָתוֹ הַחֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד
for then his life attained perfection, his soul-root reflecting his form engraved upon the Throne of Glory;
וְהֵם נוֹלְדוּ לִפְנֵי זֶה, שֶׁעֲדַיִין הָיָה צָרִיךְ לְבֵירוּרִים
while the tribes were born prior to that perfection, when spiritual purifications (beirurim) were still required;
דְּאַף שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לֵישֵׁב בְּשַׁלְוָה אַחַר לֵידַת כָּל הַשְּׁבָטִים, שֶׁרָאָה בִּנְיַן כָּל קוֹמַת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּזַרְעוֹ וְחָשַׁב דִּכְבָר נִתְבָּרֵר

for although Yaakov sought to dwell in tranquility after the birth of the tribes (Bereishis Rabbah 84:3), seeing the complete stature of Knesset Israel constructed in his seed and assuming everything was refined,
קָפַץ עָלָיו רוֹגְזוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף (שָׁם)
the anguish of Yosef sprang upon him (ibid.):
הָרוֹגֶז הַבָּא מִדַּרְגָּא דְּיוֹסֵף שֶׁהֵבִיא דִּבָּתָם רָעָה, לְהַרְאוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם גַּם כֵּן חֶסְרוֹנוֹת עֲדַיִין דִּצְרִיכִים לְבֵירוּרִים
the agitation arising from the attribute of Yosef who brought their evil report, demonstrating that there still remained deficiencies requiring purifications;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִמֵּילָא גַּם הוּא צָרִיךְ לְבֵירוּרִים יַעֲקֹב עַצְמוֹ, וְכֵן יוֹסֵף שֶׁזִּיו אִיקוֹנִין שֶׁלּוֹ דּוֹמֶה לוֹ
and consequently Yaakov himself required further refinement, as did Yosef whose visage resembled his father's.
וְ״לְעֶבֶד נִמְכַּר יוֹסֵף״ (תְּהִלִּים ק״ה:י״ז), דְּבֵירוּרָיו הֵם בָּזֶה: שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בֵּין הָעַמִּים וּבִמְקוֹם עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ וְשָׁקוּעַ בֵּינֵיהֶם
And "Yosef was sold for a servant" (Tehillim 105:17), his refinement consisting of this: that he be placed among the nations, in the epicenter of the land's depravity, submerged among them,
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ שׁוּם כֹּחַ הֲרָמַת רֹאשׁ נֶגְדָּם כְּעֶבֶד נֶגֶד רַבּוֹ
possessing no autonomy to raise his head against them, like a slave before his master;
וְשָׁם נִתְבָּרֵר כְּפִיַּית יִצְרוֹ נֶגֶד אֲדוֹנְתוֹ, כִּי לֹא כָאֵלֶּה חֵלֶק יַעֲקֹב אַף שֶׁשָּׁקוּעַ בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁשָּׁקוּעַ
and there the conquest of his yetzer was clarified against Potiphar's wife, proving that the portion of Yaakov is not like the nations even when submerged in the depths;
וְזֶהוּ דְּמוּת דְּיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו שֶׁנִּרְאָה לוֹ (סוֹטָה ל״ו עַמּוּד ב׳) לְהוֹצִיאוֹ מִתֹּקֶף הַשִּׁיקּוּעַ
and this was the likeness of his father's visage that appeared to him (Sotah 36b) to extract him from the grip of temptation,
עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָכוֹל לְהַצִּיל עַצְמוֹ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי זְכִירַת שָׁרְשׁוֹ מִמִּטָּתוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב הַשְּׁלֵימָה
so that he could rescue himself only through recalling his root in the unblemished bed of Yaakov;
וְזִיו אִיקוֹנִין שֶׁל מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ אֵין שָׁם פְּסֹולֶת כְּלָל
and the radiant likeness of his spiritual rung wherein in ultimate truth there exists no dross at all,
רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה צָרִיךְ לְבֵירוּרִין, דְּיֵשׁ עֲדַיִין אֵיזֶה חִסָּרוֹן הַנִּרְאֶה מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּחִסָּרוֹן בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ:
yet in this world purifications are necessary, because there still appears on the surface of this world a defect that seems to touch the root.

7.h: The theme: The eleven curses of Mount Ebal, the secret of Shimon and Yehudah, and the rectification of all flaws through the Davidic monarchy. The eleven curses on Mount Ebal (Devarim 27) correspond to the tribes, with Shimon excluded from an individual curse just as he was omitted from Moshe's individual blessing (Devarim 33); Rashi explains that Shimon's blessing was included within Yehudah. The deficiency of Yehudah was manifested through Shimon (the sin of Shittim), and its rectification was realized in Yehudah (the Davidic monarchy), both sharing the attribute of holy Gevurah. Shimon's zealotry was his anger ("cursed be their anger, for it was fierce", Bereishis 49:7) against whoever brought an evil report against the holy tribes; yet excess fury led him into the error of wishing to cast away Yosef. When one becomes cruel to the merciful, he eventually becomes merciful to the cruel: Shimon's harshness against Yosef led his prince Zimri to show perverted compassion to Cozbi at Shittim. Cozbi contained a reincarnated spark of Dinah (who was the spiritual counterpart of Yosef, as the liturgical poet writes: siluf Dinah b'Yehosef); Zimri mistakenly viewed her as his destined partner like Tzipporah. The ultimate rectification of Gevurah is realized through Yehudah, who pours his fury upon the idolatrous nations, while toward Israel his power is channeled through judicial righteousness and awe rather than anger. Through the Davidic monarchy and the power of repentance, all eleven curses are sweetened, revealing that in their inward root Israel is entirely free of dross.

p: וְהֵם הַיַּ״א אֲרוּרִים שֶׁהֵם נֶגֶד הַשְּׁבָטִים (דְּבָרִים כ״ז:ט״ו–כ״ה)
And these correspond to the eleven curses on Mount Ebal (Devarim 27:15–25) which parallel the tribes;
וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י דְּשִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁלֹּא בֵּרְכוֹ, לֹא אָמַר ״אָרוּר״ נֶגְדּוֹ גַּם כֵּן
and Rashi explained that Shimon, whom Moshe did not bless individually, was not designated an individual curse either;
וּבְפָרָשַׁת הַבְּרָכָה פֵּירֵשׁ דְּבִרְכַּת שִׁמְעוֹן כְּלוּלָה בִּיהוּדָה
and in Parashat VeZos HaBerachah Rashi explained that the blessing of Shimon was included within Yehudah (Devarim 33:7);
וְנִרְאֶה לִי דְּגַם לְעִנְיַן הָאֲרוּרִין כֵּן, וּלְהֵיפֶךְ: דְּהַחִסָּרוֹן דִּיהוּדָה כָּלוּל בְּשִׁמְעוֹן
and it appears to me that regarding the curses the reverse is true: the potential deficiency of Yehudah was embedded within Shimon,
דִּשְׁנֵיהֶם כְּלוּלִים יַחַד גַּם בַּנַּחֲלָה דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
for both were territorially integrated together within the land of Israel (Yehoshua 19:1);
וְהַחִסָּרוֹן נִיכָּר בְּשִׁמְעוֹן בְּמַעֲשֵׂה דְּשִׁטִּים, וְהַתִּיקּוּן בִּיהוּדָה בְּמַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד
the deficiency manifesting in Shimon in the incident of Shittim (Bamidbar 25), and its rectification emerging in Yehudah through the monarchy of the House of David;
וּשְׁנֵיהֶם חַד כֹּחַ הַגְּבוּרָה דִּקְדֻשָּׁה
both sharing a single root in holy Gevurah.
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵצֶל שִׁמְעוֹן, מִצַּד הִתְגַּלּוּת הַחִסָּרוֹן הַנִּיכָּר בּוֹ, נִקְרָא ״אַף״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״אָרוּר אַפָּם כִּי עָז״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מ״ט:ז׳)
Except that within Shimon, from the perspective of the revealed deficiency perceived within him, it was termed wrath (af): "Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce" (Bereishis 49:7);
דְּזֶהוּ הָאֲרוּרָה וְהַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁבּוֹ: תֹּקֶף כַּעְסוֹ נֶגֶד הַמּוֹצִיא דִּבָּה עַל שִׁבְטֵי יָהּ
for this was the flaw: the fury of his anger against whoever brought an evil report against the tribes of Hashem;
כִּי הוּא הַמַּכִּיר בְּיוֹתֵר קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּעַל כֵּן נִתְקַנֵּא גַּם כֵּן בִּשְׁכֶם: ״כִּי חֶרְפָּה הִוא לָנוּ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״ד:י״ד), וּ״נְבָלָה עָשָׂה בְיִשְׂרָאֵל״ (שָׁם:ז׳) דַּיְיקָא

for he was the most fiercely conscious of the holiness of Israel, wherefore he became zealous at Shechem: "for that were a reproach unto us" (Bereishis 34:14), and "he has wrought folly in Israel" (ibid. 34:7) specifically;
אֲבָל מִשֶּׁבָּא לִכְלַל כַּעַס, בָּא לִכְלַל טָעוּת בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר עַצְמוֹ
but once he succumbed to wrath, he stumbled into error in that very domain (Pesachim 66b),
לַחְשׁוֹב לִדְחוֹת אֶת יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן אֶחָד מִשִּׁבְטֵי יָהּ, לַחְשׁוֹב עָלָיו שֶׁהוּא רָאוּי לִדְחוֹת חַס וְחָלִילָה
presuming to reject Yosef who was likewise one of the holy tribes, assuming he deserved to be cast away, God forbid;
וְשֶׁאֵין מִטָּתוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב שְׁלֵימָה חַס וְחָלִילָה וְיֵשׁ חִסָּרוֹן בִּקְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל
and imagining that Yaakov's bed was not unblemished, God forbid, and that a deficiency existed in the sanctity of Israel;
וּמִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ חִסָּרוֹן גַּם בּוֹ שֶׁהֲרֵי כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹי אֶחָד, וְהוּא חֶסְרוֹן הַהַכָּרָה בִּקְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל
and consequently a flaw existed within Shimon himself, for all Israel are one nation, his error being a failure to recognize the absolute holiness of Israel;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה אַכְזָר עַל הָרַחֲמָנִים, נַעֲשָׂה גַּם כֵּן רַחֲמָן עַל הָאַכְזָרִים בְּשִׁטִּים
and through becoming cruel unto the compassionate [Yosef], he became compassionate unto the cruel [the Midianites] at Shittim (Yoma 22b);
וְכַדֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (פֶּרֶק ב׳ הֲלָכָה ח׳): ״לָא בִּישׁ לִי דַּאֲמַרְתְּ עַל טָהוֹר טָמֵא, אֶלָּא סוֹפָךְ לוֹמַר עַל טָמֵא טָהוֹר״
as stated in the Yerushalmi (Avodah Zarah 2:8): "It is not merely bad that you declared the pure impure, but your end will be to declare the impure pure";
דְּהָא בְּהָא תַּלְיָא, דְּהָאוֹמֵר עַל טוֹב רַע, אוֹמֵר גַּם כֵּן עַל רַע שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד אוֹתוֹ הַטּוֹב שֶׁהוּא טוֹב
for one leads to the other: whoever calls good evil will ultimately call the evil opposite that good, good (Yeshayah 5:20).
וְזֶהוּ כָּזְבִּי שֶׁהָיָה בָּהּ נִיצוֹץ דִּינָה כִּידוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִיזַ״ל
And this was Cozbi who contained a spark of Dinah as known from the Arizal (Sha'ar HaPesukim, Balak);
וְדִינָה הָיְתָה חִילּוּף שֶׁל יוֹסֵף, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הַפַּיְיטָן: ״סִילּוּף דִּינָה בִּיהוֹסֵף״ כִּידוּעַ (פִּיּוּט לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה)
and Dinah was the intended counterpart exchanged with Yosef in the womb (Berachos 60a), as the liturgical poet writes: siluf Dinah b'Yehosef;
וּבָהּ הָיָה הָרָע שֶׁלְּעֻומָּתוֹ בְּ״זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:יד)
and within her lay the evil opposite holiness in the principle of "one against the other";
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה פָּגַע בָּהּ אוֹתוֹ חִוְיָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁפָּגַע בּוֹ אֲדוֹנְתוֹ
whereby that serpent of Shechem assaulted Dinah just as Potiphar's wife assaulted Yosef;
וּלְפִי שֶׁהִיא ״קַרְקַע עוֹלָם״ שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ כֹּחַ כְּבִישַׁת הַיֵּצֶר
and because a woman is legally passive (karka olam, Sanhedrin 74b) and lacks the aggressive power of conquering the yetzer,
דְּדַרְכּוֹ שֶׁל אִישׁ לָצֵאת לַמִּלְחָמָה וְלֹא שֶׁל אִשָּׁה דְּדַעְתָּהּ קַלָּה
for it is the way of a man to wage war and not a woman whose mind is impressionable (Kiddushin 80b);
עַל כֵּן הֵטִיל בָּהּ זוּהֲמָא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פ:י״א) עָלֶיהָ: דְּהַנִּבְעֶלֶת לְעוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת קָשֶׁה לִפְרוֹשׁ
wherefore Shechem cast defilement into her, as the Sages stated (Bereishis Rabbah 80:11): she who is cohabited with by an uncircumcised pagan finds it hard to separate;
וְנִשְׁאַר בְּזִמְרִי שֶׁהוּא ״שָׁאוּל בֶּן הַכְּנַעֲנִית״, שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם) ״בֶּן דִּינָה וְכוּלֵיהּ״ דְּנִקְרֵאת בְּשֵׁם כְּנַעֲנִית כָּאן, עַיֵּין שָׁם
and there remained within Zimri—who is Shaul son of the Canaanitess (Bereishis 46:10), expounded by the Sages (ibid.) as the son of Dinah who was impregnated by Shechem the Canaanite—
אוֹתָהּ זוּהֲמָא שֶׁהֵטִיל בָּהּ כְּנַעַן זֶה, וּמֵאוֹתָהּ זוּהֲמָא הָיָה גַּם כֵּן לֵידַת שָׁאוּל זֶה
that very defilement which that Canaanite had cast into her, whence was born this Shaul;
וְעַל כֵּן טָעָה בְּכָזְבִּי גַּם כֵּן לְדַמּוֹתָהּ לְצִפּוֹרָה, לְפִי שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיָה לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְאוֹתוֹ זוּהֲמָא שֶׁבָּהּ גַּם כֵּן, וְאָמַר לְרַע ״טוֹב״
wherefore Zimri erred regarding Cozbi to equate her with Tzipporah, possessing an affinity to that defilement, calling evil "good";
וְשִׁמְעוֹן נְשָׂאָהּ לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם כְּדֵי לְתַקְּנָהּ שֶׁתּוּכַל לִפְרוֹשׁ וְשֶׁיִּתְפָּרֵד הַזּוּהֲמָא
and anciently Shimon had married Dinah for the sake of Heaven to rectify her so that she could separate and the defilement be detached (Bereishis Rabbah 80:11);
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת מִצַּד הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּ״אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב״ שֶׁבּוֹ, בְּיָדוֹ הוּא כֹּחַ הַהַפְרָדָה דְּכָל מִינֵי רָע דְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת מֵהַטּוֹב דִּקְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל
for in truth from the root of "truth to Jacob" within him, in his hand was the power to sever all evil of the nations from the good of Israel;
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא חָשַׁב שֶׁכְּבָר הוּא הַשְּׁלֵימוּת הַגָּמוּר שֶׁבַּכֹּחַ נִגְלֶה גַּם בְּפֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁאֵין לְהוֹצִיא דִּבָּה כְּלָל עַל זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל
except that he assumed that this absolute potential perfection was already manifest in actual deed in this world, so that no critical judgment should ever be leveled against Israel;
וּבֶאֱמֶת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עֲדַיִין אֵינוֹ נִגְלֶה וְצָרִיךְ לְבֵירוּרִים מִפְּנֵי עֵירוּב דְּעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע הַבָּא מֵעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ
whereas in truth in this world it is not yet fully revealed, requiring purifications on account of the mixture of the Tree of Knowledge brought by the Serpent;

וְהָרָע הוּא מַמָּשׁ לְעֻומַּת הַטּוֹב, וּבְאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא כֹּחַ הַטּוֹב, בּוֹ הוּא כֹּחַ הָרָע לְנֶגְדּוֹ הַמַּעֲלִים כֹּחַ הַטּוֹב וּמַרְאֶה הַחִסָּרוֹן בְּאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and evil stands directly opposite good, so that in the very attribute wherein resides the greatest power of good, there lurks the corresponding power of evil that conceals the good;
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא בְּאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ עַצְמוֹ
wherefore Shimon's defect emerged within that very attribute of zealotry itself.
וְהַבֵּירוּר בִּשְׁלֵימוּת הַתִּיקּוּן הוּא עַל יְדֵי יְהוּדָה
And the consummate purification and rectification is accomplished through Yehudah;
שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא שְׁלֵימוּת כֹּחַ הַגְּבוּרָה דִּקְדֻשָּׁה לִדָּבֵק בְּמִדּוֹתָיו שֶׁ״שּׁוֹפֵךְ זַעְמוֹ עַל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת וְגוֹמֵר״ (תְּהִלִּים ע״ט:ו׳)
within whom resides the perfection of holy Gevurah, cleaving to His attributes to "pour out His wrath upon the nations that know You not" (Tehillim 79:6);
וְכֵן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם יָדָיו חַדּוֹת וַחֲרוּצוֹת לִרְדּוֹת עוֹלָמוֹ וְשׁוֹפֵךְ זַעְמוֹ עַל עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
and so David HaMelech, peace be upon him, had sharp and decisive hands to govern the world and pour wrath upon the heathen;
וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל, אַף דְּגַם כֵּן מֶלֶךְ בְּמִשְׁפָּט וְצָרִיךְ שֶׁתְּהֵא אֵימָתוֹ עָלֶיךָ (סַנְהֶדְרִין כ״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
while toward Israel, although a king rules in justice and his awe must be upon you (Sanhedrin 22a),
נִקְרָא מִדַּת גְּבוּרָתוֹ ״מִשְׁפָּט״ וּ״מוֹרָא״, וְלֹא זַעַם וָאַף כְּלָל
his Gevurah is termed "justice" and "awe," and not fury or wrath at all;
דְּעַל יָדוֹ הוּא בֵּירוּר תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת דִּקְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם פְּסֹולֶת כְּלָל וְשֶׁאֵין שׁוּם מָקוֹם לִזְעוֹם נֶגֶד אֶחָד מִזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
for through him is clarified the ultimate perfection of Israel's holiness: that they possess no intrinsic dross, and there is no room to direct wrath against a single descendant of Yaakov Avinu;
וְעַל כֵּן אֵין ״אָרוּר״ בְּפֹעַל נֶגְדּוֹ
wherefore no curse was uttered on Mount Ebal against Yehudah;
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הוּא הַמְתַקֵּן גַּם כָּל אוֹתָם יַ״א אֲרוּרִים גַּם כֵּן, לוֹמַר שֶׁגַּם בָּהֶם אֵין שׁוּם חִסָּרוֹן
for in truth Yehudah rectifies all those eleven curses as well, establishing that in their ultimate root they contain no defect;
וַאֲפִילּוּ חָטָא כְּבָר שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְגַּלָּה הַחִסָּרוֹן בְּפֹעַל, הוּא יָכוֹל לְהִתְגַּבֵּר נֶגֶד זֶה בְּכֹחַ הַתְּשׁוּבָה
and even when one has already sinned so that the defect manifested in deed, he can overcome it through the power of repentance,
שֶׁיְּתוּקַּן הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁבַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ, וּמִמֵּילָא יְתוּקַּן הַקּוֹדֵם גַּם כֵּן:
whereby the root defect is rectified, and automatically the past transgression is sweetened as well!

7.h: The theme: The renewal of the month of Nissan created through the final letter Hei, and entering through the higher portal of the penitent (pesach ha-elyon). Nissan is the first of the twelve lunar renewals, created through the final letter Hei of the Name Havayah, representing the Shechinah that channels the divine light of Atzilus down into the souls of Israel. Israel is compared to the moon, destined to be renewed like her (Sanhedrin 42a). The Shechinah is termed "a time to act for Hashem" (es la'asos la-Hashem, Tehillim 119:126; Zohar, Vayikra 56a), from which all temporal changes across Space, Time, and Soul (Olam, Shanah, Nefesh) descend. In the letter Hei of this world, "first comes darkness and then light" (Shabbat 77b); when a person sins and falls out through the opening at the bottom of the Hei, he cannot easily re-enter through that same lower opening (pesach ha-tachton, the gate of the righteous, which relies on the memory that an act is forbidden), especially if he repeated the sin until it appeared permitted to him (Yoma 86b). Instead, a penitent must ascend and enter through the higher opening of the Hei (pesach ha-elyon): evaluating all actions through the single supreme criterion of whether they bring gratification (nachas ruach) to the Creator.

p: וְזֶהוּ הַחֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן מִי״ב חִדּוּשִׁים דִּלְבָנָה שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּאוֹת הֵ״א
And this is the month of Nissan among the twelve renewals of the moon, which was created through the letter Hei (Sefer Yetzirah 5:2);
שֶׁהִיא אוֹת מֵאוֹתִיּוֹת הֲוָיָ״ה, וְהִיא הֵ״א אַחֲרוֹנָה
which is a letter from the letters of the Name Havayah, being the final Hei [representing Malchus];
כִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְשְׁלוּ לַלְּבָנָה שֶׁעֲתִידִים לְהִתְחַדֵּשׁ כְּמוֹתָהּ, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב (סַנְהֶדְרִין מ״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
for Israel are compared to the moon, destined to be renewed like her, as written in Sanhedrin (42a);
וְהַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה ״רֹאשׁ חֳדָשִׁים״ (שְׁמוֹת י״ב:ב׳), כִּי הוּא רֵאשִׁית לְכָל הַחִדּוּשִׁים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ
and this month is "the beginning of months" (Shemos 12:2), being the primary head of all monthly renewals that exist within her;
כִּי כָּל חִידּוּשׁ הוּא עַל יְדֵי קַבָּלַת אוֹר שֶׁמְּקַבֶּלֶת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ בִּתְקוּפוֹתֶיהָ
for every lunar renewal is generated through the reception of light which she receives from the sun in its seasonal cycles;
וּכְפִי הָאוֹר דְּשֶׁמֶשׁ בְּאוֹתוֹ חֹדֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן דְּשָׁנָה כְּפִי שִׁינּוּיֵי מַהֲלָכָהּ בְּעִתּוֹתֵי הַשָּׁנָה, כֵּן הוּא הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת הַלְּבָנָה הַמְקַבֶּלֶת מִמֶּנָּה
and according to the solar light in that month at that seasonal juncture, according to the variations of the sun's circuit throughout the year, so is the renewal of the moon that receives from it;
וְכָךְ הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא עַל יְדֵי קַבָּלָתָם אוֹר הֲוָיָ״ה יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמֵּאִיר לָהֶם מֵאֲצִילוּת אוֹרוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
and thus the spiritual renewal of the Children of Israel is produced through receiving the light of Havayah, blessed be He, illuminating them from the emanation of His divine light of Atzilus,
שֶׁהֶאֱצִיל אוֹר הַמּוּשָּׂג לַתַּחְתּוֹנִים שֶׁהוּא אוֹר שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַשּׁוֹכֶנֶת בְּקֶרֶב הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְהַשִּׂיג אוֹר זֶה
having emanated an intelligible light accessible to the lower realms, which is the light of His Shechinah dwelling within the souls of Israel so that they may grasp this illumination;
וְהִיא הַנִּקְרָא ״עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה׳״ (תְּהִלִּים קי״ט:קכו), וְכִידוּעַ בַּזֹּוהַר (חֵלֶק ג׳ נ״ו עַמּוּד א׳) עַל פָּסוּק ״וְאַל יָבֹא בְכָל עֵת״ (וַיִּקְרָא ט״ז:ב׳)
and the Shechinah is termed "a time (es) to act for Hashem" (Tehillim 119:126), as known in the Zohar (III, 56a) on the verse "that he come not at all times (b'khol es)" (Vayikra 16:2);
כִּי מִמֶּנָּה נִמְשָׁךְ כָּל שִׁינּוּיֵי הָעִתִּים וְהַזְּמַנִּים, כִּי הִיא הַמַּשְׁפִּיעָה לַנִּבְרָאִים
for from the Shechinah are drawn all fluctuations of seasons and times, she being the conduit that channels influx unto created beings;
וְכָל הַנִּבְרָאִים הֵם תַּחַת הַזְּמַן וַחֲלוּקִים הַכֹּל בְּ״עוֹלָם וְשָׁנָה וָנֶפֶשׁ״ (סֵפֶר יְצִירָה ג:ג)
and all created beings exist beneath time, differentiated across Space (Olam), Time (Shanah), and Soul (Nefesh);
וְהֵם חֲלוּקַת י״ב חָדְשֵׁי הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁמִּצַּד הַמְשָׁכַת הַהַשְׁפָּעָה לְי״ב שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
these corresponding to the division of the twelve months of the year drawn down unto the twelve tribes of Israel;
וְרֵאשִׁית הַהַמְשָׁכָה הוּא לְמֶלֶךְ הָאוּמָּה שֶׁהוּא רֹאשׁ הָאוּמָּה וְרֹאשׁ הַמְקַבְּלִים
and the primary head of this influx flows to the king of the nation, who is the head of the people and foremost among the recipients;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁסּוֹף הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ הִיא גַּם כֵּן מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת כִּידוּעַ
just as the culmination of the emanator is likewise the attribute of Malchus as is known;
וְהוּא הָרֵאשִׁית דְּהִתְחַדְּשׁוּת אוֹר אַחַר הַהֶעְלֵם וְהַכִּיסּוּי
and Nissan is the inception of the renewal of light following darkness and concealment,
דְּ״[כִּי הִנֵּה] הַחֹשֶׁךְ יְכַסֶּה אֶרֶץ [וַעֲרָפֶל לְאֻמִּים]... וְעָלַיִךְ יִזְרַח [ה׳ וּכְבוֹדוֹ עָלַיִךְ יֵרָאֶה]״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ס:ב)
wherein "For, behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the peoples; but upon you Hashem will shine, and His glory shall be seen upon you" (Yeshayah 60:2);
וְגַם ״כִּי אֵשֵׁב בַּחֹשֶׁךְ — ה׳ אוֹר לִי״ (מִיכָה ז:ח)
and also: "though I sit in darkness, Hashem is a light unto me" (Michah 7:8);
לְהָאִיר הַשַּׁחַר מִתּוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ וְקַדְרוּתָא דְּצַפְרָא (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת פֶּרֶק א׳ הֲלָכָה א׳)
illuminating the dawn precisely out of the deep pitch-black darkness preceding daybreak (Yerushalmi Berachos 1:1);
דְּזֶהוּ הַ״טּוֹב מְאֹד״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית א:לא) שֶׁבְּיֵצֶר הָרָע (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ט:ז)
this being the "very good" inherent within the yetzer hara;
כִּי ״בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין, אֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים [יְכוֹלִין לַעֲמוֹד]״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת ל״ד עַמּוּד ב׳)
for "in the place where penitents stand, even wholly righteous men cannot stand," as written in Berachos (34b);
וְעַל יְדֵי הַחֵטְא, כְּשֶׁזּוֹכֶה אַחַר כָּךְ לִתְשׁוּבָה, מַגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגָה יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה
and through sin, when one subsequently merits repentance, he reaches an even higher spiritual rung.
וְהַהֵ״א רוֹמֶזֶת עַל זֶה, שֶׁבָּהּ בְּרִיאַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה (מְנָחוֹת כ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
And the letter Hei alludes to this, through which this physical world was created (Menachos 29b);
דִּבְרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר דַּיְיקָא נְהוֹרָא (שַׁבָּת ע״ז עַמּוּד ב׳)
for first comes darkness and then specifically emerges light (Shabbat 77b);
אַחַר דִּלְעֵיל בַּהַךְ בְּפֶתַח עֶלְיוֹן יוֹתֵר, דְּלָא מִסְתַּיַּיעָא מִלְּתָא לְמֵיעַל בְּפֶתַח שֶׁיָּצָא בוֹ עַצְמוֹ (מְנָחוֹת שָׁם)
after which one must enter back through a higher opening, seeing that it is not feasible to re-enter through the very opening through which he fell out (Menachos 29b);
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיָּשׁוּב מֵעַתָּה לִהְיוֹת צַדִּיק גָּמוּר וּלְהִתְנַהֵג כְּצַדִּיק גָּמוּר וּכְאִלּוּ לֹא חָטָא
meaning: that he attempt to return immediately to the status of a wholly righteous man, behaving as if he had never sinned;
דְּלָא מִסְתַּיַּיעָא, שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר מְסִיתוֹ שֵׁנִית
for this does not succeed, because the yetzer incites him a second time;
וְ״אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ — אֵין יָכוֹל לוֹ״ (קִדּוּשִׁין ל׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
and "were not the Holy One, blessed be He, assisting him, he could not overcome it" (Kiddushin 30b);
וְהָעֵזֶר הוּא מַה שֶּׁזּוֹכֵר שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה אָסוּר וְכוֹבֵשׁ יִצְרוֹ
and that normal divine aid consists of remembering that the act is halachically forbidden and conquering his yetzer;
אֲבָל אַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר נִכְשַׁל וְחָטָא, אֵין סִיּוּעַ זֶה מוֹעִיל לוֹ, שֶׁכְּבָר גָּבַר עָלָיו הַיֵּצֶר לַהֲסִיתוֹ לַדָּבָר הָאָסוּר
but once he has already stumbled and sinned, this aid no longer avails him, for the yetzer has already overpowered him to seduce him toward the forbidden;
וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן אִם עָבַר וְשָׁנָה, דְּנַעֲשָׂה לוֹ כְּהֶיתֵּר (יוֹמָא פ״ו עַמּוּד ב׳)
and all the more so if he repeated the transgression, whereby it became to him as if permitted (Yoma 86b);
דְּעַל כֵּן פַּעַם אַחַת וּשְׁנִיָּה מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ וְלֹא נֶחְשָׁב עֲדַיִין לְחֵטְא עַד פַּעַם שְׁלִישִׁית, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יוֹמָא פ״ו עַמּוּד א׳)
wherefore for a first and second offense he is forgiven, and the stain is not indelibly fixed until the third repetition, as written in Yoma (86a);
דְּאָז נִכְתַּם עֲוֹנוֹ, כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא שָׁב לִיכָּנֵס דֶּרֶךְ פֶּתַח הַבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה אַחַר פַּעַם שְׁנִיָּה
for then his iniquity is indelibly stained, since he failed to enter through the portal of penitents after the second occurrence;
חֶטְאוֹ הַשְּׁלִישִׁי הוּא אֶצְלוֹ כְּהֶיתֵּר, וְלֹא בְּקַל כָּל כָּךְ יִתְעוֹרֵר לָשׁוּב מִמֶּנּוּ כִּבְפַעַם רִאשׁוֹנָה וּשְׁנִיָּה
so his third sin appears to him as if permitted, and he will not be easily stirred to repent from it as on the first and second occasions;
וְעַל כֵּן לָא מִסְתַּיַּיעָא לֵיהּ אִם יִכָּנֵס בַּפֶּתַח הַתַּחְתּוֹן, שֶׁהוּא מִ״שַּׁעַר לַה׳ צַדִּיקִים יָבֹאוּ בוֹ״ (תְּהִלִּים קי״ח:כ׳), לְהַגְדִּיר עַצְמוֹ מִצַּד מַה שֶּׁהַדָּבָר אָסוּר

and therefore it does not avail him to enter through the lower opening—which is "the gate of Hashem, the righteous shall enter into it" (Tehillim 118:20)—attempting to fence himself merely because the thing is forbidden;
רַק צָרִיךְ לְרוֹמֵם עַצְמוֹ לְמַדְרֵגָה גְּבוֹהָה יוֹתֵר שֶׁהוּא הַפֶּתַח הָעֶלְיוֹן
but he must rather elevate himself unto a far higher spiritual rung, which is the upper aperture [of the Hei]:
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲשׂוֹת דָּבָר מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ לְנַחַת רוּחַ וּמִילּוּי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
namely, refusing to perform any action whatsoever that does not bring gratification and fulfillment to the will of the Blessed Name.
וּבָזֶה, אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה לוֹ כְּהֶיתֵּר, מִכָּל מָקוֹם מַכִּיר דְּאֵינוֹ עֲשִׂיַּית רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל כָּל פָּנִים
And in this high contemplation, even if the sin appears to him as if technically permitted, he nevertheless recognizes that it does not fulfill the divine will of the Blessed Name;
וּכְשֶׁמֵּשִׂים לֵב לְהִתְבּוֹנֵן אִם הוּא רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמַה רָצוֹן יֵשׁ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּזֶה, וְשֶׁהוּא אֵינוֹ חָפֵץ לַעֲשׂוֹת דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and when he focuses his heart to reflect whether it fulfills Hashem's will, what divine pleasure could possibly exist in it, and that he has no desire to do anything outside Hashem's will,
בָּזֶה הוּא נִמְלָט מִכָּל מִינֵי הַסָּתַת הַיֵּצֶר וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּתֹקֶף הַנִּסָּיוֹן
through this he escapes all incitements of the yetzer, even in the fierce heat of severe temptation;
וְכַנּוֹדָע הַסִּיפּוּר מַה שֶּׁקָּרָה לְאֶחָד הַמְיוּחָד שֶׁבַּקְּדוֹשִׁים בַּדּוֹר שֶׁלִּפְנֵי פָנֵינוּ
as is known the holy story regarding what occurred to a unique holy master in the generation preceding our own (the Chozeh of Lublin);
וְזֶהוּ הַשַּׁעַר שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה יָבוֹאוּ בוֹ שֶׁהוּא מָקוֹם גָּבוֹהַּ יוֹתֵר
and this is the gate through which penitents enter, which is a higher and more transcendent plane;
וְהוּא הַפֶּתַח הַתַּחְתּוֹן שֶׁבְּהֵ״א רִאשׁוֹנָה דְּהַשֵּׁם, וּבְהֵ״א אַחֲרוֹנָה הוּא פֶּתַח הָעֶלְיוֹן, דְּהַתַּחְתּוֹן הוּא הַפֶּתַח הַפָּתוּחַ לַצַּדִּיקִים:

and this corresponds to the lower opening in the first letter Hei [Binah] of the Name, while in the final letter Hei [Malchus] it is the upper aperture, the lower opening being the doorway open to the righteous.

7.h: The theme: The dual leaders of each generation, the widening of boundaries through repentance, and the awakening of Nissan. In every month the Shechinah is renewed, tasting the freshness of a virgin whose portal is opened anew, mirroring ritual separation (niddah) which ensures a wife remains as beloved as at the wedding hour (Niddah 31b). "Yiftach in his generation is like Shmuel in his generation" (Rosh Hashanah 25b): R' Baruch of Mezhibozh taught that whoever opens a new portal in divine service is the true leader of his generation. In every era there are two leaders—embodying Mashiach ben David (penitents) and Mashiach ben Yosef (the wholly righteous). All Israel are called "the remnant of Yosef" (Amos 5:15) and "Yehudim" (after Yehudah). The straight line of Yosef avoids any lateral deviation; yet when one sins and repents, turning the crooked into straight (Yeshayah 40:4), his line must be thickened to encompass the breadth of the deviation. This widens his spiritual territory into the boundless heritage of Yaakov (nachalah bli metzarim), elevating the penitent above the tzaddik. In Tishrei, Israel repents through human initiative from below (isarusa d'lesata), crying "Turn us unto You and we shall return" (Eichah 5:21); in Nissan, Hashem awakens salvation from Above (isarusa d'le'eila) through sheer grace, wherefore it is called Nissan (from nes, a supernatural wonder). At the Exodus, Hashem commanded them to take a lamb—the deity of Egypt—and eat it, for Israel are shepherds who follow their Master without question ("I remember the devotion of your youth... your following Me in the wilderness", Yirmiyah 2:2).

p: וּבְכָל חֹדֶשׁ הִיא מִתְחַדֶּשֶׁת וְטוֹעֲמִים טַעַם בְּתוּלָה שֶׁפִּתְחָהּ סָתוּם וְצָרִיךְ לִפְתּוֹחַ מֵחָדָשׁ
And in every month the Shechinah is renewed, tasting the freshness of a virgin whose entrance is closed and must be opened anew;
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (נִדָּה ל״א עַמּוּד ב׳) בְּטַעַם נִדָּה: כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּהֵא חֲבִיבָה [עַל בַּעְלָהּ כִּשְׁעַת כְּנִיסָתָהּ לַחֻפָּה] כָּל שָׁעָה כְּשָׁעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה
as the Sages stated (Niddah 31b) regarding the reason for separation: so that she remain beloved unto her husband constantly as at the initial hour of her marriage;
וְזֶהוּ ״יִפְתָּח בְּדוֹרוֹ כִּשְׁמוּאֵל בְּדוֹרוֹ״ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳)
and this is "Yiftach in his generation is like Shmuel in his generation" (Rosh Hashanah 25b),
שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי בְּשֵׁם רַבִּי בָּרוּךְ קָדוֹשׁ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
which I heard in the name of the holy Rabbi Baruch [of Mezhibozh], of blessed memory:
דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר: מִי שֶׁפּוֹתֵחַ שַׁעַר חָדָשׁ בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּדוֹרוֹ, הוּא הַמַּנְהִיג הָאֲמִיתִּי כִּשְׁמוּאֵל בְּדוֹרוֹ
meaning that whoever opens (yiftach) a new portal in the service of the Blessed Name in his generation is the true leader like Shmuel in his generation;
דִּבְכָל דּוֹר יֵשׁ הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת וּפְתִיחָתוֹ הוּא עַל יְדֵי מַנְהִיג הַדּוֹר
for in every generation there is a novel spiritual renewal whose opening is forged by the leader of that generation;
וּבְכָל דּוֹר יֵשׁ שְׁנֵי מַנְהִיגִים דּוּגְמַת מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד וּמָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף, וּבִפְרָט בְּעִקְּבְתָא דִּמְשִׁיחָא
and in every generation there exist two leaders mirroring Mashiach ben David and Mashiach ben Yosef, especially in the footsteps of the Messiah;
וְהֵם נֶגֶד שְׁתֵּי הַמַּדְרֵיגוֹת דְּבַעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה וְצַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים, וְהֵם פּוֹתְחִים מֵחָדָשׁ שְׁנֵי שְׁעָרִים אֵלּוּ בְּכָל דּוֹר
and they correspond to the two spiritual levels of penitents (ba'alei teshuvah) and the wholly righteous (tzaddikim gemurim), opening these two portals anew in every generation;
וְכָל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל כְּלוּלָה מִשְּׁנֵיהֶם, כִּי שְׁנֵיהֶם כּוֹלְלִים כָּל הָאוּמָּה
and every Jewish soul is incorporated of both, for both embrace the entire nation:
שֶׁהֲרֵי כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָאִים עַל שֵׁם יוֹסֵף ״שְׁאֵרִית יוֹסֵף״ (עָמוֹס ה:טו), וְעַל שֵׁם יְהוּדָה ״יְהוּדִים״
for all Israel are designated upon the name of Yosef as "the remnant of Joseph" (Amos 5:15), and upon the name of Yehudah as "Jews" (Yehudim);
וְהוּא עִיקַּר שְׁמָם, מִשּׁוּם דְּ״[כִּי אָדָם] אֵין צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ [אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה טּוֹב וְלֹא יֶחֱטָא]״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כ)
and "Jews" is their primary title, because "there is not a righteous man upon earth that does good and sins not" (Koheles 7:20);
וּמִיּוֹסֵף הֵם רַק ״שְׁאֵרִית״, דְּעִיקָּרוֹ נִטְמַע וְנֶאֱבַד בְּגָלוּת עֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים
and from Yosef they are merely a "remnant," seeing that the bulk of his tribe assimilated and was lost in the exile of the Ten Tribes;
וְהַיְינוּ דְּיֵשׁ בְּכָל אֶחָד עִנְיָנִים שֶׁהוּא צַדִּיק בָּהֶם
meaning that within every single person there exist matters wherein he is a tzaddik,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ הָרִאשׁוֹנִים בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כָּל הַיָּד (נִדָּה י״ד עַמּוּד א׳) גַּבֵּי חַמָּרִין: דִּלְגַבֵּי דָּבָר זֶה נִקְרָאִים כְּשֵׁרִים וּלְזֶה רְשָׁעִים
as the early commentators wrote in Niddah (14a) regarding donkey-drivers: that relative to one specific matter they are termed upright and to another wicked,
וְהוּא בָּהֶם מַדְרֵיגַת צַדִּיק גָּמוּר
and in those specific traits they embody the level of a wholly righteous man.
וּפְתִיחָתוֹ מֵחָדָשׁ לְהִתְחַדֵּשׁ הוּא בְּחֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר
And the initial opening to become renewed occurs in the month of Adar;

וּמָצִינוּ בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה נִקְרָא ״אֲדָר״... וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּבֵיצָה (ט״ו עַמּוּד ב׳): ״הָרוֹצֶה שֶׁיִּתְקַיְּימוּ נְכָסָיו, יִטַּע בָּהֶן אֲדָר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ׳אַדִּיר בַּמָּרוֹם ה׳׳ (תְּהִלִּים צ״ג:ד׳)״

and we find in the words of the Sages that it is called Adar... as written in Beitzah (15b): "Whoever wishes his property to endure should plant an adar [a majestic tree], as it is said: 'Hashem on high is mighty (addir)' (Tehillim 93:4)";
...וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף שֶׁתִּיחֵם וְחִילֵּק הָאָרֶץ לַשְּׁבָטִים וּלְקַרְקַף גַּבְרָא
...and Yehoshua bin Nun was from the seed of Yosef, who set borders and divided the land to the tribes and to each individual head (Bava Batra 122a);
כִּי דַּרְגָּא דְּיוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק הוּא לֵילֵךְ בְּקַו הַיּוֹשֶׁר בְּלֹא נְטִיָּה
for the attribute of Yosef the Righteous is to walk in the straight line of integrity without lateral deviation;
וּבָזֶה כָּל אֶחָד הוֹלֵךְ בַּקַּו שֶׁלּוֹ וְאֵין שָׁם עֵירוּב חֲלָקִים
and in this manner each person walks in his own boundary without intermingling of portions;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כְּשֶׁחָטָא וְנִתְעַקֵּם, כְּשֶׁחוֹזֵר לַעֲשׂוֹת ״הֶעָקֹב לְמִישׁוֹר״ (יְשַׁעְיָה מ:ד), הֲרֵי נִתְרַחֵב גְּבוּלוֹ כְּמִדַּת עִיקּוּם הַקַּו
unlike when one sinned and became crooked: when he repents to make "the crooked straight" (Yeshayah 40:4), behold his spiritual boundary is broadened according to the dimension of the curve;

שֶׁכָּל קַו הַמִּתְעַקֵּם הֲרֵי יֵשׁ לוֹ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת יוֹתֵר לַצַּד שֶׁמִּתְעַקֵּם, וּכְשֶׁרוֹצִים לַעֲשׂוֹתוֹ יָשָׁר צָרִיךְ לְהַעֲבוֹת הַקַּו כְּמִדַּת רוֹחַב הָעִיקּוּם וְיָשׁוּב לִהְיוֹת קַו יָשָׁר עָב וְרָחָב

for any line that bends expands further toward the side to which it curves, and when one seeks to make it straight he must thicken the line to match the breadth of the curve, returning as a straight, broad, and thickened line;
וְזֶהוּ מַעֲלַת הַבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עַל צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים, דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְרַחֵב גְּבוּלוֹ יוֹתֵר
and this is the superiority of penitents over the wholly righteous, for through this their spiritual territory expands all the more;
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְנַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהִיא ״נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים״ (שַׁבָּת קי״ח עַמּוּד ב׳)
and this occurs when one arrives at the heritage of Yaakov Avinu which is "a heritage without boundaries" (Shabbat 118b);
וְאֵין שָׁם ״אֲדָר״ הַמַּגְבִּיל, שֶׁהוּא הַזְּמַן שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם עֲדַיִין נַחֲלַת גּוֹיִם וְצָרִיךְ לִמְחִיַּיִת עֲמָלֵק
where there is no longer the limiting boundary of Adar, which is the time when the heritage of the nations still exists and requires the eradication of Amalek.
וְאָז זוֹכֶה לְפֶתַח דְּנִיסָן, וְהוּא רֵאשִׁית הַהִתְחַדְּשׁוּת לְמַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
And then he merits the portal of Nissan, which is the inception of renewal for the kings of Israel;
הַיְינוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּנִקְרָאִים עַל שֵׁם יְהוּדָה שֶׁבּוֹ כֹּחַ תִּיקּוּן הַחִסָּרוֹן
meaning the root of Knesset Israel designated after Yehudah, within whom resides the power to rectify all deficiency;
וְזֶהוּ כָּל עִיקַּר עִנְיַן הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת: לְקַבֵּל אוֹר חָדָשׁ אַחַר שֶׁהָיָה חִסָּרוֹן וְהֶעְדֵּר אוֹר
and this is the primary essence of renewal: to receive a new illumination after there had been deficiency and the absence of light;
וְרֵאשִׁית הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת זֶה בְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ בְּחִסָּרוֹן פְּרָטִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּאוֹתוֹ נֶפֶשׁ הוּא בְּנִיסָן, שֶׁהוּא זְמַן גְּאוּלָּתֵנוּ וּפְדוּת נַפְשֵׁנוּ מִכָּל מִינֵי רָע
and the primal head of this renewal within each soul for its specific deficiency unfolds in Nissan, the season of our redemption and the liberation of our souls from all manner of evil.
וְתִשְׁרֵי שֶׁאָז זְמַן תְּשׁוּבָה בַּעֲשֶׂרֶת יְמֵי תְּשׁוּבָה, הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שָׁבִים לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִצַּד עַצְמָם וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם
And Tishrei, which is the season of repentance during the Ten Days of Repentance, represents Israel returning unto the Blessed Name through their own human initiative and toil;
כִּידוּעַ דְּאָנוּ טוֹעֲנִין: ״הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ [ה׳] אֵלֶיךָ וְנָשׁוּבָה״ (אֵיכָה ה:כא), וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ טוֹעֵן: ״שׁוּבוּ אֵלַי וַאֲשׁוּבָה אֲלֵיכֶם״ (מַלְאָכִי ג:ז; אֵיכָה רַבָּה ה:כא)

as is known that we argue: "Turn us unto You, Hashem, and we shall return" (Eichah 5:21), while the Blessed Name argues: "Return unto Me, and I will return unto you" (Malachi 3:7; Eichah Rabbah 5:21);
וְדִידַן נָצַח כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה י״א עַמּוּד א׳): ״בְּנִיסָן עֲתִידִין לִיגָּאֵל״
and our claim prevails according to the authority who holds (Rosh Hashanah 11a): "in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed";
וּגְאוּלָּה דְּנִיסָן הוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְעוֹרֵר, דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא ״נִיסָן״ לְשׁוֹן ״נֵס״
for the redemption of Nissan is that which the Blessed Name initiates from Above, wherefore it is called Nissan related to nes [miracle];
כִּי כְּשֶׁשָּׁבִים, הֲרֵי הַיְשׁוּעָה בְּמִשְׁפָּט, וְאֵין נִקְרָא ״נֵס״ רַק מַה שֶּׁהוּא נֵס גָּמוּר בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת כִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם דְּהוֹצִיא ״גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי״ (דְּבָרִים ד:לד)

for when man repents from below the salvation follows strict justice, whereas a true "miracle" is that which is wondrous throughout all worlds like the Exodus from Egypt when He extracted "a nation from the midst of another nation" (Devarim 4:34);
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: דְּהַלָּלוּ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכוּלֵיהּ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״וְאַתְּ עֵרֹם וְעֶרְיָה״ (יְחֶזְקֵאל ט״ז:ז׳)
as the Sages stated: "These are idolaters and these are idolaters," and as written: "whereas you were naked and bare" (Yechezkel 16:7);
רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרוֹב רַחֲמָיו וַחֲסָדָיו שָׁלַח שֶׁפַע אוֹר פִּתְאֹם לָהֶם
but the Blessed Name in His abundant mercies poured forth an overflow of light suddenly upon them.
וְזֶהוּ מִצְוַת הַפֶּסַח שֶׁצִּוָּה לָהֶם לִיקַּח ״שֶׂה לְבֵית אָבֹת״ (שְׁמוֹת י״ב:ג׳)
And this is the mitzvah of the Passover sacrifice: commanding them to take "a lamb according to their fathers' houses" (Shemos 12:3);
שֶׁהוּא בְּעִירָא דְּמִצְרָאֵי דָּחֲלִין לֵיהּ וְעִבְרָאֵי אָכְלִין לֵיהּ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה ט״ז:ג׳)
which was the beast that the Egyptians deified and the Hebrews ate (Shemos Rabbah 16:3);
כִּי רוֹעֵי צֹאן הָיוּ הַשְּׁבָטִים וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, דְּזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנֶּמְשְׁלוּ לְצֹאן הַנִּמְשָׁכִים אַחֲרֵי הָרוֹעֶה וְאֵין חוֹקְרִין אַחֲרָיו כְּלָל
for the tribes and Yaakov Avinu were shepherds (Bereishis 47:3), this being the root of Israel who are compared to sheep following after the shepherd without questioning his paths at all;
וְזֶהוּ: ״[זָכַרְתִּי לָךְ] חֶסֶד נְעוּרַיִךְ [אַהֲבַת כְּלוּלֹתָיִךְ] לֶכְתֵּךְ אַחֲרַי בַּמִּדְבָּר בְּאֶרֶץ לֹא זְרוּעָה״ (יִרְמְיָה ב:ב)
and this is: "I remember for you the devotion of your youth, your love as a bride, your following Me in the wilderness, in a land that was not sown" (Yirmiyah 2:2);
וְלֹא חָשְׁשׁוּ כְּלָל מַה יֹּאכְלוּ שָׁם
not worrying at all what they would eat there;
וְכֵן נִמְשְׁכוּ אַחַר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לְהַאֲמִין שֶׁיִּגְאָלֵם אַף שֶׁרָאוּ קוֹשִׁי הָעֲבוֹדָה וְתֹקֶף הַמְשַׁעְבְּדִים
and so they followed Moshe Rabbeinu, believing he would redeem them even when seeing the crushing weight of servitude;
וְזֶהוּ הַקְדָּמַת ״נַעֲשֶׂה״ לְ״נִשְׁמָע״ (שְׁמוֹת כ״ד:ז׳), וְלֹא עָלָה בְּלִבָּם פַּחַד שֶׁמָּא יְצַוֵּום דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא יוּכְלוּ לַעֲמוֹד בּוֹ:
and this was the precedence of "we will do" to "we will hear" (Shemos 24:7), no fear entering their hearts lest He command them something they could not endure.

7.h: The theme: The stubbornness of Israel versus the obstinacy of Pharaoh, and the reading of Parashat HaChodesh. When Israel prays "Turn us unto You and we shall return," we plead: even though salvation begins with an awakening from Above (isarusa d'le'eila), once You turn us we will run after You, unlike the nations who rejected the Torah. Egypt worshipped the ram because it embodied the unholy Yesod—rigid stubbornness (akshanus). Israel is called "stiff-necked" (am kesheh oref, Shemos 32:9), but their stubbornness is holy: "either a Jew or crucified" (Shemos Rabbah 42:9), yet toward Hashem they are easily enticed to return. While Rabbi Eliezer held that the redemption will occur in Tishrei (dependent on human repentance), Rabbi Yehoshua held that it will occur in Nissan (sparked by divine grace, preceded by the harsh decrees of a king like Haman in Adar). On Rosh Chodesh Nissan, the portion of HaChodesh is read; eating the Korban Pesach internalizes the humility of the sheep, and sprinkling the blood surrenders the animal soul (nefesh ha-bahamis) to Hashem. Pharaoh ("ha-oref", the stiff neck) stood upon the Nile (Bereishis 41:1), attempting through sorcery to compel supernal forces to submit to his desires; the righteous, by contrast, place themselves beneath Hashem ("and behold, Hashem stood above him", Bereishis 28:13). Reading Parashat HaChodesh draws down the illumination of the final letter Hei, advancing the redemption from potentiality into actuality.

p: וְזֶהוּ בַּקָּשָׁתֵנוּ: ״הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ וְגוֹמֵר״ (אֵיכָה ה:כא), וְלֹא לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
And this is our plea: "Turn us unto You, Hashem, and we shall return" (Eichah 5:21), a request not granted unto the nations of the world;
אַף שֶׁהוּא מִצִּדְּךָ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָנוּ כְּשֶׁתְּשִׁיבֵנוּ — נָשׁוּבָה, כִּי נִמְשָׁךְ תֵּיכֶף אַחֲרֶיךָ
for even though the initial turning must come from Your side, nevertheless when You turn us we will immediately return, running swiftly after You;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, דְּהֶחֱזִיר הַתּוֹרָה עַל כָּל אוּמָּה וְלָשׁוֹן וְלֹא קִבְּלוּהָ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ב׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
unlike the nations of the world, for He offered the Torah unto every nation and tongue and they refused to accept it, as written in Avodah Zarah (2b);
וּמִצְרָאֵי דָּחֲלִין מִמַּדְרֵגָה זוֹ וַעֲשָׂאוּהָ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
and the Egyptians feared this attribute of total surrender and made the sheep their idol;
כִּי הֵם ״עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מ״ב:ט׳) וִיסוֹד שֶׁבַּקְּלִיפָּה נֶגֶד יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁהוּא יְסוֹד שֶׁבַּקְּדֻשָּׁה, דְּעַל כֵּן מָלַךְ עֲלֵיהֶם
for they represented the "nakedness of the land" and Yesod within the unholy husk, opposite Yosef the Righteous who embodies holy Yesod, wherefore he ruled over them.
וְכָל יְסוֹד הוּא עַקְשָׁנוּת שֶׁתָּקוּעַ בְּמַדְרֵיגָתוֹ כִּיסוֹד קַיָּים שֶׁאֵין לָזוּז
And every manifestation of Yesod is unshakeable obstinacy, fixed firmly in its place like an immovable foundation;
וְכָךְ קִבַּלְתִּי בְּסוֹד סַמְמָנֵי הַקְּטֹרֶת: דְּ״קִנָּמוֹן תִּשְׁעָה״ (כְּרֵיתוֹת ו׳ עַמּוּד א׳) רוֹמֵז לִיסוֹד שֶׁהוּא הַתְּשִׁיעִי מֵעֵילָּא לְתַתָּא
and thus I received regarding the secret of the incense: that "cinnamon nine measures" (Kerisos 6a) alludes to Yesod which is the ninth Sefirah from Above to below;
וּמִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָּא הוּא חָכְמָה
and counted from below to Above it is Chochmah;
וְהַיְינוּ דְּאֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָעַקְשָׁנוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם הוּא נִמְשָׁךְ מֵהַחָכְמָה
meaning that with the Children of Israel their obstinacy is drawn from holy Chochmah;
וּבְחֵטְא דְּעֵגֶל שֶׁהָיָה עַל יְדֵי שֵׁם ״עֲלֵה שׁוֹר״ שֶׁהֶעֱלָה אֲרוֹנוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף דְּהוּא מִכֹּחוֹ
and in the sin of the Calf which was forged through the holy Name Aleh Shor that raised the coffin of Yosef (Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 19), which drew from his power;

דְּעַל כֵּן גַּם יָרָבְעָם שֶׁמִּזַּרְעוֹ עָשָׂה כֵּן, שֶׁחָשַׁב שֶׁזֶּהוּ הִתְגַּבְּרוּת כֹּחַ הַשּׁוֹר שֶׁבַּקְּדֻשָּׁה שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ יוֹסֵף ״בְּכוֹר שׁוֹרוֹ [הָדָר לוֹ]״ (דְּבָרִים ל״ג:י״ז) וְתִתְעַלֶּה מַלְכוּתוֹ

wherefore Jeroboam who was of Yosef's seed did likewise (I Melachim 12:28), assuming this was the exaltation of the holy Ox—the power of Yosef: "His firstling bullock, majesty is his" (Devarim 33:17)—so that his kingdom would be elevated;
נֶאֱמַר שֶׁהֵם ״קְשֵׁי עֹרֶף״ (שְׁמוֹת ל״ב:ט׳), כִּי בָּא מִצַּד הָעַקְשָׁנוּת
it was said of them that they are a "stiff-necked people" (Shemos 32:9), for this error stemmed from unyielding obstinacy;
אַךְ הֵם קְשֵׁי עֹרֶף לְטוֹבָה: ״אוֹ יְהוּדִי אוֹ צָלוּב״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מ״ב:ט׳)
yet they are stiff-necked for the good: "Either a Jew or crucified!" as written in Shemos Rabbah (42:9);
וְאֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹחִים לְהִתְפַּתּוֹת
while toward the Blessed Name they are easily appeased to yield;
וְתֵיכֶף כְּשֶׁבָּא מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שָׁבוּ מֵעַקְשָׁנוּתָם
and immediately when Moshe Rabbeinu descended they repented from their stubbornness;
וְנִתְקַבְּלוּ בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, שֶׁהוּא זְמַן קַבָּלַת תְּשׁוּבָה לַכֹּל אִם יַעֲשׂוּ תְּשׁוּבָה
being accepted on Yom Kippur, which is the time of receiving repentance for all if they repent;
וְלֹא זְמַן הִתְעוֹרְרוּת לִתְשׁוּבָה וּבְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא קוֹדֶם הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא, דְּזֶה אֵינוֹ בְּתִשְׁרֵי רַק בְּנִיסָן
and not a season of awakening to repentance through an awakening from Above (isarusa d'le'eila) prior to human awakening from below (isarusa d'lesata), which belongs not to Tishrei but to Nissan.
וְעַל כֵּן רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דִּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (י״א רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳): ״בְּתִשְׁרֵי עֲתִידִין לִיגָּאֵל״
And therefore Rabbi Eliezer who holds in Rosh Hashanah (11a): "In Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed";
לְשִׁיטָתוֹ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (צ״ז סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דְּאִם יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין תְּשׁוּבָה — נִגְאָלִין, וְאִם לָאו — אֵין נִגְאָלִין״
is consistent with his view in Sanhedrin (97b): "If Israel perform repentance they are redeemed, and if not they are not redeemed";
וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְטַעֲמֵיהּ: ״דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַעֲמִיד [לָהֶם מֶלֶךְ שֶׁגְּזֵרוֹתָיו קָשׁוֹת כְּהָמָן וְיִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין תְּשׁוּבָה]״ (שָׁם)
while Rabbi Yehoshua is consistent with his view: "The Holy One sets up a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman, and Israel repent" (ibid.);
הַיְינוּ תֹּקֶף הַשִּׁעְבּוּד הוּא הַגּוֹרֵם הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא לְהָאִיר בִּלְבָבָם הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה
meaning the severity of the oppression is itself the catalyst of the divine awakening from Above to illuminate in their hearts the stirring of repentance;
וּמֶלֶךְ קָשֶׁה כְּהָמָן הוּא בַּאֲדָר, וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּנִיסָן נִגְאָלִין
and the harsh king like Haman arrives in Adar, and subsequently in Nissan they are redeemed;
וְעַל יְדֵי הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת הָאוֹר שֶׁמַּתְחִיל מֵרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ
through the renewal of light that begins on Rosh Chodesh.
וּבְרֵישׁ יַרְחָא הִזְהִירָם עַל הַפֶּסַח בְּפָרָשַׁת הַחֹדֶשׁ
And on the first of the month Moshe instructed them regarding the Passover sacrifice in Parashat HaChodesh (Shemos 12:1–20);
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת (פְּסָחִים ו׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) בְּשֵׁם רַבֵּינוּ תָּם: דִּלְכוּלֵי עָלְמָא מַאֲמַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָיָה בְּרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ
as Tosafos wrote in Pesachim (6b) in the name of Rabbeinu Tam: that according to all opinions the utterance of the Blessed Name occurred on Rosh Chodesh;
שֶׁאָז הַתְחָלַת הַמְשָׁכַת אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמִּתְחַדֵּשׁ בְּלִבְּבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּחֹדֶשׁ זֶה
for then is the beginning of channeling the divine light of the Blessed Name renewed in the hearts of Israel in this month;
וַאֲכִילַת הַקָּרְבַּן פֶּסַח רוֹמֵז לְהַבְלָעַת כֹּחַ זֶה דְּהַמְשָׁכָה כְּצֹאן בַּלֵּב
and the eating of the Passover offering alludes to absorbing this quality of following like sheep directly into the heart;
וּזְרִיקַת הַדָּם הוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַבַּהֲמִית שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, לוֹמַר דְּגַם כֹּחַ זֶה אָנוּ מוֹסְרִין לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and the sprinkling of the blood surrenders the animal soul (nefesh ha-bahamis) unto the Blessed Name, affirming that this vital force too we surrender unto Him;
וּמִטַּעַם זֶה הוּא שֶׁבָּא הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא מֵעַצְמָהּ, דְּהַכֹּל בְּמִשְׁפָּט
and for this reason the awakening from Above comes of itself, all being executed in justice:
דְּאָנוּ בֶּאֱמֶת רְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ אֶלָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְעַכְּבִים
for in truth our inner will is to perform His will, there being merely external hindrances;
וּכְשֶׁיֵּאוֹר עֵינֵינוּ שֶׁיָּסוּרוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה כָּל הַמְעַכְּבִים, אַחַר שֶׁ״יִמְשְׁכֵנוּ — אַחֲרֶיךָ נָרוּצָה״ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים א:ד) מֵעַצְמֵינוּ
and when our eyes are enlightened so that all hindrances depart, once "He draws us, we will run after You" of our own accord;
וְ״כָל בֶּן נֵכָר לֹא יֹאכַל בּוֹ״ (שְׁמוֹת י״ב:מ״ג), דְּהֵם אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לָזֶה כְּלָל
and "there shall no alien eat thereof" (Shemos 12:43), for they have no affinity with this self-nullification whatsoever.
וּבְמִצְרַיִם נִצְטַוּוּ עַל זֶה שֶׁנִּתְבָּרַר דָּבָר זֶה, כִּי הֵם מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ שֶׁאֵינָם יְכוֹלִים לְבַטֵּל רְצוֹנָם כְּלָל
And in Egypt they were commanded regarding this sacrifice to clarify this truth, for the Egyptians were the exact opposite, utterly incapable of nullifying their personal will;
כְּמוֹ אַחַר כָּל הַמַּכּוֹת שֶׁהִכִּיר הָאֱמֶת וְעִם כָּל זֶה הִכְבִּיד לִבּוֹ
as seen after all the plagues, where Pharaoh recognized the truth yet hardened his heart;
