וַאֲפִילּוּ אַחַר מַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת שֶׁרָאָה כֹּחַ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עָלָיו עַד שֶׁהוּכְרַח לְשַׁלְּחָם בְּרֶגַע הַמַּכָּה, אַחַר כָּךְ חָזַר לְעַקְשָׁנוּתוֹ לִרְדּוֹף עֲלֵיהֶם וּלְהַחֲזִירָם
and even after the plague of the firstborn when he saw Hashem's hand upon him and was forced to release them, he immediately returned to his obstinacy to pursue and recapture them;
וְהֵם דָּחֲלִין מִמִּדָּה זוֹ שֶׁל בִּיטּוּל רָצוֹן וְהַמְשָׁכָה אַחַר רוֹעֶה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ מַמָּשׁ הֵיפֶךְ שׁוֹרֶשׁ חַיּוּתָם שֶׁכָּל כֹּחָם הוּא הָעַקְשָׁנוּת
and the Egyptians abhorred this attribute of nullifying the will and following a shepherd, which is the absolute antithesis of their vitality whose power is stubbornness;
וְכִידוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִיזַ״ל דְּ״פַּרְעֹה״ אוֹתִיּוֹת ״הָעֹרֶף״, וְשָׁם הוּא קְשִׁיוּת הָעוֹרֶף
as known from the Arizal that Pharaoh
(פַּרְעֹה)
has the letters of Ha'Oref
(הָעֹרֶף,
the nape), the seat of stiff-necked obstinacy;
וְעַל כֵּן עָשׂוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁלָּהֶם טָלֶה, לוֹמַר שֶׁהָעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁלָּהֶם נִמְשָׁךְ מִדַּרְגָּא אַחֲרֵיהֶם
wherefore they made their deity a lamb, asserting that their god was drawn after them,
כִּי הֵם אֵין מְבַטְּלִים רְצוֹנָם רַק כֹּחַ הַמְנַהֲלָם מוּכְרָח לִימָּשֵׁךְ אַחֲרֵיהֶם וּלְבַטֵּל רְצוֹנוֹ מִפְּנֵי רְצוֹנָם
for they never nullify their will, but demand that the supernal force guiding them follow after them and submit its will to their lusts;
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה פ״ט (א׳): ״הָרְשָׁעִים — הֵן מִתְקַיְּימִין עַל אֱלֹהֵיהֶם, ׳וּפַרְעֹה... עֹמֵד עַל הַיְאֹר׳ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מ״א:א׳)״
and this is what the Sages expounded in Bereishis Rabbah (89:1): "The wicked stand above their gods: 'and Pharaoh stood upon the river' (Bereishis 41:1)";
שֶׁגַּם הַיְאוֹר שֶׁהוּא נָהָר הַמּוֹשֵׁךְ בּוֹ כֹּחַ הַמְּשִׁיכָה, וְזֶה כָּל כֹּחַ הַמַּיִם לִהְיוֹת מוֹשְׁכִין וְהוֹלְכִין אַחַר הַמַּמְשִׁיכָן
for the Nile is a flowing river possessing the property of downstream pull;
וַעֲמִידַת קְשִׁיוּת עָרְפּוֹ הוּא עַל הַיְאוֹר שֶׁהוּא מִלְּמַעְלָה וְעָלָיו, לְהַכְרִיחַ כֹּחַ עֶלְיוֹן הַמְנַהֲלוֹ לִימָּשֵׁךְ אַחֲרָיו
yet his stiff-necked stance was upon the river, asserting himself above it to force the higher power to bend after his volition;
שֶׁזֶּה כָּל עִנְיַן הָרְשָׁעִים: לֵילֵךְ בִּשְׁרִירוּת לִבָּם וְשֶׁיַּכְרִיחוּ מַעַרְכוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם שֶׁיְּמַלְּאוּ לָהֶם כָּל תַּאֲוָתָם
which is the hallmark of the wicked: to walk in the stubbornness of their heart and compel the celestial constellations to satisfy their desires;
וְזֶהוּ הַכְּשָׁפִים שֶׁהָיָה מָלֵא בְּמִצְרַיִם, שֶׁזֶּה כָּל עִנְיָנָם: לְהַכְחִישׁ פַּמַלְיָא שֶׁל מַעְלָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סַנְהֶדְרִין ס״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
and this was the sorcery that saturated Egypt, its entire purpose being to "contradict the celestial entourage," as written in Sanhedrin (67a),
וּלְהַכְרִיחַ הַכֹּחוֹת הָעֶלְיוֹנִים שֶׁיַּעֲשׂוּ כִּרְצוֹנָם וּמִילּוּי תַּאֲוָתָם, וְזֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְלִיפַּת מִצְרַיִם
forcing supernal forces to perform their will, this being the root husk of Egypt.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַצַּדִּיקִים: אֱלֹהֵיהֶם מִתְקַיֵּים עֲלֵיהֶם, ״וְהִנֵּה ה׳ נִצָּב עָלָיו״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ח:י״ג)
Unlike the righteous, whose God stands above them: "and, behold, Hashem stood above him" (Bereishis 28:13);
הוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְזַרְעוֹ צֹאן קָדָשִׁים
which is the spiritual rung of Yaakov Avinu and his seed, the holy flock;
לִהְיוֹת כָּל עֲמִידַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְהַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה — הוּא עָלָיו
the entire indwelling of the Blessed Name and His Shechinah below resting above him;
וְהוּא מַנִּיחַ עַצְמוֹ תַּחְתָּיו, כְּעִנְיַן: ״וְהֵם תֻּכּוּ לְרַגְלֶךָ [יִשָּׂא מִדַּבְּרֹתֶיךָ]״ (דְּבָרִים ל״ג:ג׳)
and he places himself completely beneath Him: "and they sat down at Your feet, receiving of Your words" (Devarim 33:3);
שֶׁהוּא מַדְרֵיגַת ״יַעֲקֹב אִישׁ תָּם״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:כ״ז), לִהְיוֹת ״תָּמִים [תִּהְיֶה] עִם ה׳ [אֱלֹהֶיךָ]״ (דְּבָרִים י״ח:י״ג)
which is the attribute of "Jacob was a simple man" (Bereishis 25:27), to be "wholehearted with Hashem your God" (Devarim 18:13),
לִימָּשֵׁךְ אַחֲרָיו בִּתְמִימוּת וְלֹא לְבַקֵּשׁ דָּבָר שֶׁזּוּלַת רְצוֹנוֹ כְּלָל
following after Him in simple faith without seeking anything outside His divine will;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִין לְמוֹרָא גָּדוֹל דְּגִלּוּי שְׁכִינָה, הַמַּפִּיל פַּחַד עַל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וּמֵאִיר לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּקֶרֶב לְבָבָם
and through this one merits the great awe of the revealed Shechinah, which casts dread upon the nations and enlightens the inward heart of Israel.
וְזֶהוּ קְרִיאַת פָּרָשַׁת הַחֹדֶשׁ, לִזְכּוֹת לְהֶאָרָה זוֹ דְּגִלּוּי שְׁכִינָה שֶׁהִיא הֵ״א אַחֲרוֹנָה
And this is the purpose of reading Parashat HaChodesh: to merit this illumination of the manifest Shechinah which is the final letter Hei,
הַבָּאָה לְהָאִיר בְּלִבְּבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּלְקָרְבָם לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, לִזְכּוֹת לִגְאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה בְּחֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן הַבָּא אַחֲרָיו
coming to illuminate the hearts of the Children of Israel and draw them near unto the Blessed Name, meriting complete redemption in the month of Nissan that follows;
וּבְכָל שָׁנָה וְשָׁנָה אֵין פְּעֻלּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל חוֹזֶרֶת רֵיקָם
and in each and every year the sacred actions of the Children of Israel never return empty,
וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״כֵּן יִהְיֶה דְבָרִי אֲשֶׁר יֵצֵא מִפִּי, לֹא יָשׁוּב אֵלַי רֵיקָם כִּי אִם עָשָׂה [אֶת אֲשֶׁר חָפַצְתִּי] וְגוֹמֵר״ (יְשַׁעְיָה נ״ה:י״א)
as it is written: "So shall My word be that goes forth out of My mouth: it shall not return unto Me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, etc." (Yeshayah 55:11);
וְכָל מִצְוֹת דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וּדְרַבָּנָן הֵם דְּבָרָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִפִּיו וְלֹא יַחְזְרוּ רֵיקָם, וּמַצְלִיחִים בִּשְׁלִיחוּתָם
and all commandments, biblical and rabbinic, are His divine words that went forth from His mouth and never return void, succeeding in their holy mission;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (תַּנְחוּמָא פָּרָשַׁת וַיִּגַּשׁ א׳): דְּהַמִּצְוֹת הֵם שְׁלוּחָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ
as the Sages stated (Tanchuma, Vayigash 1): the mitzvos are His divine emissaries;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין פּוֹעֲלִים גְּאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה עֲדַיִין בְּפֹעַל מַמָּשׁ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֵם פּוֹעֲלִים בְּכֹחַ
and although they do not effectuate complete redemption in actual deed as yet, nevertheless they operate in potentiality;
וּמְקָרְבִין הַדָּבָר בְּכָל שָׁנָה וְשָׁנָה לָצֵאת מֵהַכֹּחַ לַפּוֹעַל לְגַמְרֵי
bringing the reality closer each and every year to emerge completely from potential into actualization,
כְּשֶׁיַּגִּיעוּ לַמַּדְרֵיגָה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁל יְצִיאָה לַפּוֹעַל מַמָּשׁ, בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ אָמֵן:
when we arrive at the final stage of consummate realization, swiftly in our days, Amen!
The theme: The four New Years corresponding to the four letters of the Divine Name Ehyeh (אהי״ה) and the revelation of divine foreknowledge
Yedi'ah
versus free choice
Bechirah
. The four New Years enumerated at the start of tractate Rosh Hashanah parallel the four letters of the Name Ehyeh—the name of Keser—through which the Exodus from Egypt was initiated
"And they shall say to me: What is His name? ... Ehyeh has sent me unto you", Shemos 3:13–14
. The Exodus was the primal inception of all future redemptions, leaving the full stature of the cosmos to unfold across history. To Moshe alone was the phrase Asher Ehyeh
"I shall be that I shall be"
revealed, alluding to the future subjugations of exile
Berachos 9b

because ongoing purifications were necessary; yet to the people Moshe was commanded to say merely "Ehyeh has sent me," following the principle "sufficient unto the hour is the affliction." As explained in Zohar Chadash and the Ari's Arba Me'ot Shekel Kesef, Yedi'ah and Bechirah reside in two separate spiritual dimensions: in the realm of Foreknowledge there is no free choice, a reality concealed in this world but destined to be unveiled in the Future when the yetzer is destroyed and the days arrive in which "I have no pleasure"
Shabbos 151b
. Moshe, embodying Da'as, grasped this hidden realm where the heart's secret will binds with the intellect
liba l'fuma lo galya
, bridging the lower letter Hei
speech / Knesset Israel
with the higher letter Hei
heart / Binah
אַרְבָּעָה רָאשֵׁי הַשָּׁנִים הַנִּשְׁנִים בְּרֵישׁ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (ב׳ עַמּוּד א׳), נִרְאֶה לִי שֶׁהֵם נֶגֶד אַרְבַּע אוֹתִיּוֹת שֵׁם אֶהְיֶ״ה
The four New Years taught at the beginning of tractate Rosh Hashanah (2a) appear to me to correspond to the four letters of the Name Ehyeh
(א-ה-י-ה); שֶׁהוּא שֵׁם הַכֶּתֶר כִּידוּעַ
which is the Name associated with Keser [Crown] as is known;
וּבוֹ נִגְאֲלוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפָרָשַׁת שְׁמוֹת: ״וְאָמְרוּ לִי מַה שְּׁמוֹ [מָה אֹמַר אֲלֵהֶם] וְגוֹמֵר״ (שְׁמוֹת ג:יג), דְּאָמַר לוֹ תְּחִלָּה שֵׁם זֶה

and through It they were redeemed from Egypt, as written in Parashat Shemos: "and they shall say to me: What is His name? what shall I say unto them?" (Shemos 3:13), where Hashem initially communicated to him this Name;
דְּאוֹתָהּ גְּאוּלָּה הוּא הַתְחָלָה לְכָל הַגְּאוּלוֹת, וּמִמֶּנּוּ הוּא הַמְשָׁכַת כָּל הַקּוֹמָה
for that initial redemption was the inception of all subsequent redemptions, from which is drawn down the entire cosmic stature;
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא בְּלָשׁוֹן זֶה, דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁעָתִיד לִהְיוֹת עִמָּהֶם עוֹד
wherefore It is designated in this future phrasing [Ehyeh, "I will be"], meaning that He is destined to be with them further;
כִּי זֶהוּ רַק הַתְחָלָה, וּבֶאֱמֶת כְּלַל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה כּוּלּוֹ נִקְרָא רַק הַתְחָלָה, כִּפְרוֹזְדּוֹר לִפְנֵי טְרַקְלִין (אָבוֹת ד:טז)
for the Exodus was merely a beginning, and in truth this entire world in its totality is termed merely a beginning, like an antechamber (prozdor) before the palace banquet-hall (traklin, Avos 4:16).
וּלְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר: ״[אֶהְיֶה] אֲשֶׁר אֶהְיֶה״ (שְׁמוֹת ג:יד), וְדָרְשׁוּ מִזֶּה שִׁעְבּוּד גָּלֻיּוֹת
And to Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, Hashem said: "I will be that I will be" (Shemos 3:14), which the Sages expounded as alluding to the subjugation of future exiles (Berachos 9b);
הַיְינוּ שֶׁגִּילָּה לוֹ הַסּוֹד דְּגַם אַחַר כָּךְ יִהְיֶה רַק הַתְחָלָה, וּמִמֵּילָא נִמְשָׁךְ מִזֶּה שִׁעְבּוּד גָּלֻיּוֹת דְּעַדַיִין צָרִיךְ לְבֵירוּרִין

meaning that He revealed to Moshe the secret that even following the Exodus reality would remain merely an inception, whence inevitably followed the subjugations of exile because spiritual purifications (beirurim) were still required;
אַךְ לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אָמַר לוֹ שֶׁיֹּאמַר רַק ״אֶהְיֶה שְׁלָחַנִי [אֲלֵיכֶם]״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ט׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דַּיָּהּ לַצָּרָה בִּשְׁעָתָהּ״
but unto the Children of Israel He instructed Moshe to say merely "Ehyeh has sent me unto you," as the Sages of blessed memory stated (Berachos 9b): "Sufficient unto the affliction is its own hour";
וְהַיְינוּ דִּבְאֶמֶת בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה נַעֲשׂוּ חֵירוּת מִשִּׁעְבּוּד גָּלֻיּוֹת אִלּוּ לֹא חָטְאוּ אַחַר כָּךְ
for in truth at the Giving of the Torah they were granted absolute freedom from the subjugation of exiles (Eruvin 54a) had they not subsequently sinned;
וְהַחֵטְא הוּא בְּחִירָה
and sin is governed by human free choice.
וְאָמְנָם יָדוּעַ קֻשְׁיַת הַיְּדִיעָה וּבְחִירָה, שֶׁתֵּירְצוּ עַל זֶה בַּזֹּוהַר חָדָשׁ וּבְסֵפֶר ״אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף״ מֵהָאֲרִיזַ״ל עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַנִּסְתָּר

And indeed, the classical dilemma of Foreknowledge (Yedi'ah) and Free Choice (Bechirah) is known, which they resolved in Zohar Chadash and in the book Arba Me'ot Shekel Kesef of the Arizal according to the esoteric wisdom;
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַדְּבָרִים: דְּהֵם בִּשְׁנֵי מְקוֹמוֹת, וּבִמְקוֹם הַיְּדִיעָה בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין מָקוֹם לִבְחִירָה
and the root of the matter is: they dwell in two distinct spiritual dimensions, and in the realm of Foreknowledge there is in truth no place for free choice;
אֶלָּא שֶׁזֶּהוּ מָקוֹם הַנֶּעלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְעָתִיד לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא שֶׁיְּבוֹעַר הַיֵּצֶר וְיִבּוּטַל הַבְּחִירָה בֶּאֱמֶת
except that this is the transcendent dimension concealed in this world, destined to be revealed in the Future when the yetzer hara is purged and free choice is truly nullified;
וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת (קנ״א עַמּוּד ב׳): ״׳שָׁנִים אֲשֶׁר תֹּאמַר אֵין לִי בָהֶם חֵפֶץ׳ (קֹהֶלֶת י״ב:א׳) — אֵלּוּ יְמוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ״
and as written in Shabbat (151b): "'years wherein you shall say: I have no pleasure in them' (Koheles 12:1)—these are the days of the Messiah";
וְאָז יְבוֹרַר גַּם עַל כָּל חֲטָאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁסְּדוּרִים וּבָאִים מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְּרֵאשִׁית, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא (שַׁבָּת פ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
and then it will be clarified regarding all the sins of Israel that they were ordered and advancing from the six days of Creation, as written in Perek Rabbi Akiva (Shabbat 89b);
וְהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה הַיְּדִיעָה דְּהַכֹּל הָיָה מִידִיעָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרֵאשִׁית הַבְּרִיאָה
meaning when Foreknowledge is revealed, showing that all was encompassed within His divine knowledge at the inception of Creation.
וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא מְקוֹם הַבְּחִירָה
But in this world resides the arena of free choice;
וְעַל כֵּן רַק לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה בְּסוֹד הַדַּעַת, נִתְגַּלָּה סוֹד הַיְּדִיעָה וּמַה שֶּׁבִּידִיעָתוֹ
wherefore solely unto Moshe Rabbeinu, who embodied the mystical secret of Da'as, was revealed the mystery of divine Foreknowledge and that which resides within His foreknowledge;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה מ״ב:ט׳): ״אַתָּה רוֹאֶה רְאִיָּה אַחַת וַאֲנִי רוֹאֶה שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת, שֶׁעֲתִידִים וְכוּלֵיהּ״
as the Sages stated (Shemos Rabbah 42:9): Hashem said, "You see a single vision and I see two visions, that they are destined, etc.";
כִּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁנִּבְחַר לְגוֹאֵל הִגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ, לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת לוֹ דָּבָר דְּ״לִבָּא לְפוּמָא לָא גַּלְיָא״ (קֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה י״ב:י׳)
for Moshe Rabbeinu who was chosen as redeemer attained this lofty rung, having revealed to him that which "the heart does not reveal to the mouth" (Koheles Rabbah 12:10);
כִּי הַדַּעַת הוּא מְקוֹם חִבּוּר מַחֲשֶׁבֶת הַמּוֹחַ עִם רְצוֹן הַלֵּב הַנֶּעְלָם גַּם מִכֹּחוֹת הַמִּתְפַּשְּׁטוֹת מֵהַלֵּב לַגּוּף
for Da'as is the juncture unifying the thought of the brain with the concealed will of the heart, hidden even from the faculties spreading from heart to body;
כָּל שֶׁכֵּן לְפוּמָא שֶׁהוּא מַדְרֵגָה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁבּוֹ הַהִתְגַּלּוּת לְזוּלַת
and all the more so hidden from the mouth, which is the final rung wherein communication to an outside other manifests;
דְּהוּא דַּרְגָּא דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ תּוֹרָה מִפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה
which is the level of Knesset Israel in this world who received the Torah directly from the mouth of the Almighty (Makkos 24a),
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״יִשָּׁקֵנִי מִנְּשִׁיקוֹת פִּיהוּ״ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים א:ב)
after the manner of "Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth" (Shir HaShirim 1:2).
וּמַדְרֵגַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁעָלָה לַמָּרוֹם, מַדְרֵגָה הַמְרוֹמֶמֶת מִמַּדְרֵיגוֹת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And the level of Moshe Rabbeinu who ascended on High was elevated above the earthly rungs of this world;
הַיְינוּ מֵהֵ״א אַחֲרוֹנָה לָרִאשׁוֹנָה, דְּהוּא מִפּוּמָא לְלִבָּא
namely, ascending from the final letter Hei [Mouth / Malchus] to the first letter Hei [Heart / Binah];
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ל״ג עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דְּיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם לְגַבֵּי מֹשֶׁה מִלְּתָא זוּטְרָתִי״
and this is what they stated in Berachos (33b): "Fear of Heaven relative to Moshe is a minor thing";
כִּי לְגַבֵּי כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹאֵל מֵהֶם רַק זֶה, דְּזֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
for relative to Knesset Israel the Blessed Name asks of them merely this awe (Devarim 10:12), this being the designated rung of Knesset Israel;
כִּידוּעַ דְּיִרְאָה הִיא תַּרְעָא לְאַעֲלָא גּוֹ מְהֵימְנוּתָא (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק ב׳ ס׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
as is known, awe is the gate to enter into faith (Zohar II, 60a);
וְעִיקָּרָהּ בַּלֵּב כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיוֹמָא ע״ב עַמּוּד ב׳ עַל פָּסוּק ״וְלֵב אָיִן״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ז:ט״ז)
and its primary seat is in the heart as written in Yoma (72b) on the verse "seeing he has no heart" (Mishlei 17:16);
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין ק״ו עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דְּרַחֲמָנָא לִבָּא בָּעֵי״
and as written in Perek Chelek (Sanhedrin 106b): "the Merciful One desires the heart";
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִן הַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ, דְּצָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַפֶּה מְדוּבָּק עִם הַלֵּב
unlike lip service, where it is required that the mouth be cleaved unto the heart;
וְזֶה כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא
and this is the entire striving of Knesset Israel until the Future:
שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ כוּלָּם לְמַדְרֵגַת הֵ״א רִאשׁוֹנָה, לִהְיוֹת ״תְּרֵין רֵעִין דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין״ (זֹוהַר)
that all shall merit the level of the first letter Hei [Binah], becoming "two companions that never part" (Zohar III, 4a);
כְּשֶׁיִּזְכּוּ לְהִזְדַּכְּכוּת הַלֵּב לְגַמְרֵי, דְּ״לְבָבוֹ יָבִין וְשָׁב [וְרָפָא לוֹ]״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ו:י):
when they merit the complete purification of the heart, wherein "his heart shall understand, and he shall return, and be healed" (Yeshayah 6:10).
The theme: Moshe at the Burning Bush, the three crowns
Torah, Priesthood, Royalty
, and the three spiritual rungs of Ani, Attah, and Hu (אני, אתה, הוא). When Hashem first revealed Himself at the burning bush, Moshe declared "Here am I"
Hineni
, sensing his readiness for both Priesthood and Kingship
Shemos Rabbah 2:6

. Yet Hashem commanded "Draw not near hither," revealing that the final purification had not yet arrived. The temporary perfection Israel tasted at Sinai was authentic for that hour, and through the purifications of exile they will regain those crowns, as expounded on "and everlasting joy upon their heads"
Yeshayah 35:10; Shabbat 88a
. The three crowns—Torah, Kehunah, and Malchus
Avos 4:13
—correspond to the three grammatical and mystical pronouns: Ani [I], Attah [You], and Hu [He]. Ani corresponds to Malchus
"and I am prayer", Tehillim 109:4
, the indwelling of the divine presence within the hearts of Israel. Attah corresponds to Priesthood
Kehunah
: direct visual encounter with the Sovereign
"You are a priest forever", Tehillim 110:4
, standing as a servant before the King, reflecting the golden frontplate
Tzitz, from hatzatzah, gazing
upon Aharon's forehead bearing the Name Havayah, and embodying Yitzchak Avinu who saw Hashem before him
"I have set Hashem always before me", Tehillim 16:8
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם זָכָה לָזֶה מִיָּד בַּהִתְגַּלּוּת הָרִאשׁוֹן, עַד שֶׁאָמַר: ״הִנְנִי״ — לִכְהֻנָּה, ״הִנְנִי״ — לְמַלְכוּת (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה ב:ו)

And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, merited this insight immediately at the first revelation at the bush, saying: "Here am I"—ready for the Priesthood, "Here am I"—ready for the Monarchy (Shemos Rabbah 2:6);
שֶׁרָאָה עַצְמוֹ מוּכָן לִהְיוֹת גּוֹאֵל הָאֲמִיתִּי, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה הַדּוֹר זַכַּאי עֲדַיִין לָזֶה
perceiving himself equipped to be the ultimate, final Redeemer, except that the generation was not yet worthy of this;
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר לוֹ: ״אַל תִּקְרַב הֲלֹם״ (שְׁמוֹת ג:ה), גִּילָּה לוֹ דָּבָר זֶה דְּ״אֲשֶׁר אֶהְיֶה״ דְּעַדַיִין לֹא הִגִּיעַ גְּמַר הַבֵּירוּר
wherefore Hashem said to him: "Draw not near hither" (Shemos 3:5), revealing to him through "I shall be that I shall be" that the ultimate culmination of purification had not yet arrived;
אֶלָּא שֶׁלִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לְהוֹדִיעַ זֶה
but unto the Children of Israel it was impossible to disclose this reality,
כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מָקוֹם לִבְחִירָה, שֶׁיְּבַקְשׁוּ לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל לְהַגִּיעַ לַטּוֹב וְהַשְּׁלֵימוּת הַגָּמוּר
in order that space remain for free choice, so that they would exert effort to attain goodness and absolute perfection,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁזָּכוּ לָזֶה לְשָׁעָה בִּשְׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
as they indeed merited temporarily at the hour of the Giving of the Torah.
וְאִלְמָלֵא יָדְעוּ מִקּוֹדֶם שֶׁעֲתִידִים לְקַלְקֵל אַחַר כָּךְ, וְשֶׁאֵין זֶה מַדְרֵגָה קְבוּעַ וְקַיֶּמֶת עֲדַיִין בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לְבָבָם שֶׁלֹּא יוּכְלוּ לָזוּז מִמֶּנָּה
And had they known beforehand that they were destined to corrupt their ways afterward, and that this lofty rung was not yet permanently fixed within their hearts beyond all slip;
לֹא הָיוּ יְכוֹלִים לִזְכּוֹת לָהּ גַּם לְשָׁעָה
they would not have been able to merit it even for that temporary hour;
וְרַק עַל יְדֵי הַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁחָשְׁבוּ שֶׁהֵם בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן וְשֶׁאֵין דָּבָר חוֹצֵץ, זָכוּ לִהְיוֹת בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן עַל כָּל פָּנִים לְשָׁעָה
and only through the concealment wherein they assumed they were already on that plane without impediment did they truly merit to be so for that hour;
וּלְאוֹתוֹ שָׁעָה הָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּפְסַק אַחַר כָּךְ
and for that specific hour it was absolute truth, even though it was subsequently interrupted;
וּ״שְׂפַת אֱמֶת״ הוּא מַה שֶּׁ״תִּכּוֹן לָעַד״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ב:י״ט), כְּבָר אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּוהַר (חֵלֶק א׳ קמ״א עַמּוּד ב׳): ״כּוֹנַנְתָּ״ לֹא כְּתִיב אֶלָּא ״תִּכּוֹן״
and "the lip of truth shall be established forever" (Mishlei 12:19), the Zohar expounding (I, 141b): "it is not written 'was established' in the past, but 'shall be established' in the future";
הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בַּהֹווֶה בְּפֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה ״כּוֹנַנְתָּ״ מִיָּד, רַק דְּ״תִּכּוֹן״ לֶעָתִיד
meaning it is not immediately consolidated in the present reality of this world, but will be permanently established in the Future;
וְאוֹתָהּ מַדְרֵגָה שֶׁזָּכוּ לָהּ לְשָׁעָה בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם וּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַיְּימָה אֶצְלָם אַחַר כָּךְ, הַהֶפְסֵק לֹא הָיָה אֶלָּא לְפִי שָׁעָה
and that sublime rung they merited temporarily at the Exodus and Sinai, though not permanently sustained, its cessation was merely temporary;
דְּכָל חַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִקְרָא ״חַיֵּי שָׁעָה״ (שַׁבָּת י׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
for the entire life of this world is termed "temporary life" (Shabbat 10a);
וְאַחַר שֶׁיִּצָּרְפוּ וְיִתְלַבְּנוּ בְּכָל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה, יָשׁוּבוּ לַמַּדְרֵיגוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת
and after being refined and whitened across all the exiles through repentance (Daniel 12:10), they will return to those primal levels,
וְ״כִימֵי צֵאתְךָ [מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם אַרְאֶנּוּ נִפְלָאוֹת]״ (מִיכָה ז:טו)
as in: "According to the days of your coming out of the land of Egypt will I show unto him marvelous things" (Michah 7:15),
וְ״שִׂמְחַת עוֹלָם עַל רֹאשָׁם״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ל״ה:י׳), וְדָרְשׁוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּפֶרֶק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא (שַׁבָּת פ״ח עַמּוּד א׳): שִׂמְחָה שֶׁמֵּעוֹלָם, הַכְּתָרִים דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה
and "everlasting joy shall be upon their heads" (Yeshayah 35:10), which the Sages expounded in Shabbat (88a): the joy that was from of old, referring to the spiritual crowns of Sinai;
רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁאָז הִשִּׂיגוּ תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת כָּל הַקּוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה עַד הַכֶּתֶר
meaning that then they grasped the consummate perfection of the full cosmic stature reaching unto Keser.
וּשְׁלֹשָׁה כְּתָרִים הֵם: כֶּתֶר תּוֹרָה, כְּהֻנָּה, וּמַלְכוּת (אָבוֹת ד:יג)
And there are three crowns: the crown of Torah, the crown of Priesthood, and the crown of Kingship (Avos 4:13);
הֵם נֶגֶד שָׁלֹשׁ מַדְרֵיגוֹת: ״אֲנִי״, ״אַתָּה״, ״הוּא״
corresponding to the three divine rungs of Ani [I], Attah [You], and Hu [He]:
״אֲנִי״ הוּא מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת כַּנּוֹדָע בְּסוֹד ״וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה״ (תְּהִלִּים ק״ט:ד׳)
Ani [I] is the attribute of Malchus as known in the mystery of "and I am prayer" (Tehillim 109:4);

וְעַל זֶה רָמְזוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב: מֵ״אֲנִי״ שֶׁל בָּשָׂר וָדָם שֶׁאָמַר ״אֲנִי פַרְעֹה״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מ״א:מ״ד), אַתָּה לָמֵד לְ״אֲנִי״ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא כְּשֶׁיֹּאמַר ״אֲנִי אֲנִי הוּא״ (דְּבָרִים ל״ב:ל״ט; בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פ״ט:ד׳)

and to this the Sages alluded: from the Ani of flesh and blood when Pharaoh said "I am Pharaoh" (Bereishis 41:44), you deduce regarding the Ani of the Holy One when He proclaims "I, even I, am He" (Devarim 32:39; Bereishis Rabbah 89:4);
כִּי הִתְגַּלּוּת מִדַּת מַלְכוּת הוּא בְּמִלַּת ״אֲנִי״
for the manifest presence of Malchus is revealed in the word Ani;
וּבְ״הֶחָלִיל״ (סֻכָּה נ״ג עַמּוּד א׳): ״אִם אֲנִי כָּאן — הַכֹּל כָּאן״
and in tractate Sukkah (53a): Hillel said, "If Ani [the Shechinah] is here, all is here";
הוּא בְּסוֹד ״נָעוּץ תְּחִלָּתָן בְּסוֹפָן״ (סֵפֶר יְצִירָה א:ז), וְ״סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה — בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה״
this embodying the mystery of "their beginning is wedged in their end" (Sefer Yetzirah 1:7), and "the end of action is rooted in the initial thought."
וּכְהֻנָּה הוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּ״אַתָּה״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״אַתָּה כֹהֵן לְעוֹלָם״ (תְּהִלִּים ק״י:ד׳)
And Priesthood (Kehunah) is the spiritual rung of Attah [You], as it is written: "You are a priest forever" (Tehillim 110:4);
וְהַיְינוּ דְּ״אֲנִי״ הוּא הַמַּדְרֵגָה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּתוֹךְ לִבְּבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
meaning that Ani is the level where the Blessed Name dwells within the hearts of Israel;
וְ״אַתָּה״ הוּא הַכָּרַת הַנֹּוכַח שֶׁאוֹמְרִים בְּכָל הַבְּרָכוֹת, שֶׁהוּא כְּעֶבֶד הָעוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ
while Attah is the direct address of presence recited in all blessings ("Blessed are You"), standing like a servant directly before the King;
וְזֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דַּעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁזָּכָה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לִהְיוֹת מִזַּרְעוֹ
and this is the rung of sacrificial service (Avodah) which Avraham Avinu merited should descend from his seed;
כִּי הוּא נִמְשָׁךְ מִצַּד מִדַּת חַסְדּוֹ: דְּאַבְרָהָם הוֹלִיד אֶת יִצְחָק, רָזָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה
for it issued from the attribute of his kindness: "Avraham begot Yitzchak" (Bereishis 25:19), the mystery of Avodah;
וְהוּא הוֹלִיד יַעֲקֹב שֶׁצוּרָתוֹ חֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד, הוּא רָזָא דְּ״אַתָּה״ הָרוֹמֵז לְשֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה
and Yitzchak begot Yaakov whose form is engraved upon the Throne of Glory, representing the mystery of Attah alluding to the Name Havayah;
וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת: ״אַתָּה ה׳״ (תְּהִלִּים קי״ט:י״ב)
and so is it formulated in numerous scriptural verses: "Blessed are You, Hashem" (Tehillim 119:12);
וְזֶהוּ הַשֵּׁם הַכָּתוּב בַּצִּיץ שֶׁעַל מֵצַח אַהֲרֹן שֶׁהוּא הַכֶּתֶר כְּהֻנָּה
and this is the Divine Name inscribed upon the golden Tzitz upon Aharon's forehead (Shemos 28:36), which is the Crown of Priesthood;
עַל יְדֵי דְּהוּא כּוּלּוֹ ״קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳״ לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ
by virtue of its being entirely "Holy unto Hashem" before Him, blessed be His Name;
וְ״צִיץ״ לְשׁוֹן רְאִיָּה (מֵצִיץ מִן הַחֲרַכִּים, שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ב:ט)
and tzitz denotes sight (from "peering [metzitz] through the lattice", Shir HaShirim 2:9);
שֶׁזֶּהוּ מַדְרֵגַת הָרְאִיָּה שֶׁאָדָם רוֹאֶה הָעוֹמֵד נִכְחוֹ
this being the level of direct visual perception where one beholds the One standing before him;
וְהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּיִצְחָק, דִּמְחַוֵּי לְהוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעֵינֵיהּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא (שַׁבָּת פ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
and this is the spiritual rung of Yitzchak, regarding whom the Holy One points Him out directly to their eyes, as written in Perek Rabbi Akiva (Shabbat 89b);
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עַל יְדֵי הָעֲבוֹדָה זוֹכֶה לִרְאוֹת הַנֹּוכַח
for through sacred sacrificial service one merits to gaze upon the divine Presence;
דַּרְגָּא דְּ״שִׁוִּיתִי ה׳ לְנֶגְדִּי תָמִיד״ (תְּהִלִּים ט״ז:ח׳), שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְכָל כֹּהֵן הָעוֹבֵד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ תָּמִיד, שֶׁהוּא הַנִּקְרָא ״כֹּהֵן״:
the level of "I have set Hashem always before me" (Tehillim 16:8), required of every priest who ministers unto the Blessed Name continually, who is termed a Kohen.

8.h: The theme: The Crown of Torah as Hu [He], the mystery of "I am He and no other" (Ani Hu v'lo acheir), and the conduits of children, life, and sustenance (banei, chayei, u-mezonei). The Crown of Torah is the supreme rung of Hu [He], the transcendent hidden realm cleaved to Israel alone, whence supernal Chochmah emerges from Ayin [Nothingness]. The Torah in this world represents the "fallen fruit" (novelot) of supernal wisdom (Bereishis Rabbah 17:5), wherein absolute Foreknowledge is clothed in human free choice. On the first night of Pesach, Hashem revealed: "I am He and no other" (Ani Hu v'lo acheir)—uniting the lowest manifestation of the Shechinah (Ani / Malchus) with the most transcendent hidden light (Hu / Keser), empowering Israel to merit the Crown of Torah. At the Exodus, when Israel lay in spiritual degradation, Hashem created a "pure heart" ex nihilo (yesh me-ayin) out of the transcendent source called Ayin (the Mazal of Israel), from which stream children, life, and sustenance (banei, chayei, u-mezonei, Moed Katan 28a). Sustenance (mezonei) corresponds to the Table of Kings (Keser Malchus); Children (banei) corresponds to the Altar (Keser Kehunah), bringing peace between husband and wife through the Priesthood (the Sotah water restoring the letters of the Divine Name in procreation); Life (chayei) corresponds to the Torah, the Tree of Life (Keser Torah), the Central Pillar that binds all existence to the supernal Keser.

p: וְכֶתֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִכּוּלָּם, הוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּ״הוּא״
And the Crown of Torah which is exalted above them all is the spiritual rung of Hu [He];
שֶׁהוּא עֹומֶק הַנֶּעְלָם שֶׁדְּבוּקִים בּוֹ כָּל זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל
which is the transcendent, concealed depth unto which all the seed of Israel are cleaved;
דְּעַל כֵּן כּוּלָּם זָכוּ לְקַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה, מַה שֶּׁלֹּא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי (תְּהִלִּים קמ״ז:כ׳) שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם
wherefore they all merited receiving the Torah, which He did not do for any gentile nation (Tehillim 147:20), who possess no connection to this concealed root;
שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ נִמְשֶׁכֶת הַחָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן כַּנּוֹדָע
from which supernal Chochmah is drawn ex nihilo from Ayin, as is known;
וְנוֹבְלוֹת שֶׁלָּהּ הִיא הַתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה י״ז:ה׳)
and the "fallen fruit" (novelot) of this supernal wisdom is the Torah, as written in Bereishis Rabbah (17:5);
הַיְינוּ דְּהַתּוֹרָה הִיא חָכְמָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, אֶלָּא דְּשָׁם הוּא הַיְּדִיעָה שֶׁלֹּא נִתְגַּלָּה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, רַק הַבְּחִירָה שֶׁהִיא הַנּוֹבְלוֹת שֶׁלָּהּ
meaning that the Torah is His divine wisdom, except that on High it is absolute Foreknowledge which is not manifest in this world, where operates only free choice which is its fallen reflection,
כְּעָלֶה הַנּוֹבֶלֶת מֵהָאִילָן דְּנִרְאֵית כְּנִפְרֶדֶת מֵהָאִילָן, וּבֶאֱמֶת הִיא הִיא מֵעֶצֶם הָאִילָן
like a leaf falling from a tree which appears severed from the tree, yet in truth is of the very substance of the tree;
וְרֹאשׁ הַחָכְמָה הוּא הַכֶּתֶר, וְהוּא כֶּתֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּ״הוּא״ שֶׁנָּעוּץ גַּם כֵּן בְּדַרְגָּא דְּ״אֲנִי״
and the head of Chochmah is Keser, which is the Crown of Torah, the rung of Hu which is likewise wedged in the rung of Ani [Malchus].
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּגְלָה לִי בַּחֲלוֹם [יוֹם א׳ דְּפֶסַח תרכ״ה] פֵּירוּשׁ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּהַגָּדָה: ״אֲנִי הוּא וְלֹא אַחֵר״
And as was revealed to me in a dream [on the first day of Pesach, 5625 / 1865] regarding the explanation of the Haggadah: "I am He and no other";
דְּגִילָּה אָז דָּבָר זֶה: דְּ״אֲנִי״ שֶׁהוּא מַדְרֵגָה אַחֲרוֹנָה דְּגִלּוּי שְׁכִינָה שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה בְּקֶרֶב כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּלֵיל פֶּסַח
that Hashem revealed this truth: that Ani, which is the bottom-most level of the Shechinah manifest within all the souls of Israel on the night of Pesach,
הוּא עַצְמוֹ מַדְרֵגָה הַיּוֹתֵר עֶלְיוֹנָה הַנֶּעְלֶמֶת, דַּרְגָּא דְּ״הוּא״, שֶׁנֶּעְלַם מֵהֶם עֲדַיִין אָז לְגַמְרֵי
is itself the most supreme concealed rung, the level of Hu, which was then still hidden from them completely;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִתְגַּלָּה לָהֶם דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁהוּא ״הוּא״ וְלֹא אַחֵר שֶׁאֵינוֹ דָּבָר אַחֵר
nevertheless it was revealed to them that Ani is identical with Hu, and not an alienated "other";
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיָה לוֹ אֲחִיזָה בְּכָל הַקּוֹמָה, שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לִזְכּוֹת אַחַר כָּךְ לְכֶתֶר תּוֹרָה
and through this union Israel acquired a hold throughout the entire cosmic stature, enabling them subsequently at Sinai to merit the Crown of Torah.
וְהֵם ג׳ רֵאשִׁית שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דִּפְסָחִים (פְּסָחִים ה׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
And these correspond to the three primordials (reishis) mentioned in the first chapter of Pesachim (5a);
דְּהַכֶּתֶר הוּא הָעֹומֶק רֵאשִׁית שֶׁנָּתוּן עַל גַּבֵּי הָרֹאשׁ
for Keser is the primordial depth resting above the head;
וּשְׁבִיתַת יוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח הוּא הַשָּׂגַת הַכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן
and the cessation of work on the first festival day of Pesach is the attainment of the Supernal Crown,
שֶׁבִּשְׁמוֹ הָיָה תְּחִלַּת הַשְּׁלִיחוּת דִּגְאוּלַּת מִצְרַיִם, שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה לָהֶם עֹומֶק רֵאשִׁית הַנֶּעְלָם מִכָּל בְּרִיָּה
in whose Name (Ehyeh) began the mission of the Exodus, revealing to them the primordial depth concealed from all creatures;
וְאֵינוֹ מוּשָּׂג בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֶלָּא מִצַּד הַהֶעְלֵם
which is attained in this world solely by way of concealment.
וּכְפִי תֹּקֶף הִשְׁתַּקְּעוּתָם אָז, הָיוּ צְרִיכִים לְהַמְשִׁיךְ לָהֶם אוֹר עֶלְיוֹן גָּבוֹהַּ מְאֹד כְּטַעַם: ״לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא לִי [אֱלֹהִים] וְגוֹמֵר״ (תְּהִלִּים נ״א:י״ב)

And according to the intensity of their defiled immersion in Egypt, it was necessary to channel unto them a sublime light from on High, after the manner of: "Create me a clean heart, O God" (Tehillim 51:12);
דִּ״בְרִיאָה״ רָצָה לוֹמַר יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן
for "creation" (beriah) signifies existence ex nihilo from Nothingness (yesh me-ayin);
דַּאֲפִילּוּ מְשׁוּקָּע בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁמְּשׁוּקָּע, עַד שֶׁכְּפִי כָּל מַדְרֵיגוֹת וְהִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁל יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן נִגְלָה הַקִּלְקוּל
so that even if an individual is submerged in the lowest depths where corruption permeates all revealed levels,
יוּכַל לִפְעוֹל בְּרַחֲמִים רַבִּים לִבְרוֹא לֵב טָהוֹר יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן
Hashem can operate in abundant mercies to create a pure heart ex nihilo;
הַיְינוּ מֵהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם הַנִּקְרָא ״אַיִן״, שֶׁהוּא הַמַּזָּל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
namely from the concealed root termed Ayin [Keser], which is the celestial source (Mazal) of Israel,
שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ נוֹזְלִים כָּל מִינֵי שֶׁפַע: ״בָּנֵי, חַיֵּי וּמְזוֹנֵי״ (מוֹעֵד קָטָן כ״ח עַמּוּד א׳) לְנַפְשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם חֵלֶק ה׳ וּדְבוּקִים בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם הַזֶּה

from which stream all manners of divine influx: children, life, and sustenance (banei, chayei, u-mezonei, Moed Katan 28a) unto the souls of Israel who are the portion of Hashem cleaved unto this hidden root.
וְהַשֶּׁפַע ״בָּנֵי, חַיֵּי וּמְזוֹנֵי״ הֵם גַּם כֵּן נֶגֶד ג׳ כְּתָרִים
And the threefold influx of "children, life, and sustenance" corresponds likewise to the three crowns:
״מְזוֹנֵי״ הוּא שֻׁלְחַן מְלָכִים, וְזֵר שֶׁל שֻׁלְחָן הוּא הַכֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת (יוֹמָא ע״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
Sustenance (mezonei) corresponds to the Table of Kings, the crown-border of the Table being the Crown of Royalty (Yoma 72b);
וְשֻׁלְחָנֵנוּ גָּדוֹל מִשֻּׁלְחָנָם, וְהַכֶּתֶר נִמְשָׁךְ מִכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן שֶׁהִיא הַמַּזָּלָא
and our table is greater than their table (Avos 6:5), this royal crown being drawn from the Supernal Crown which is the Mazal;
״וּבָנֵי״ הוּא נֶגֶד זֵר שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ, שֶׁהוּא הַמֵּשִׂים שָׁלוֹם בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם
and Children (banei) corresponds to the crown-border of the Altar, which establishes peace between Israel and their Father in Heaven;
דְּעַל כֵּן הַמְגָרֵשׁ אִשְׁתּוֹ רִאשׁוֹנָה מִזְבֵּחַ מוֹרִיד עָלָיו דְּמָעוֹת (סַנְהֶדְרִין כ״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
wherefore regarding one who divorces his first wife, the Altar sheds tears over him (Sanhedrin 22a);
וְעַל יְדֵי הַבָּנֵי: ״[וּ]רְאֵה בָנִים לְבָנֶיךָ שָׁלוֹם עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל״ (תְּהִלִּים קכ״ח:ו׳)
and through children peace is realized: "and see your children's children; peace be upon Israel" (Tehillim 128:6);
דְּבָזֶה הוּא עִיקַּר הַשְּׁלוֹם בַּיִת, שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר מְכֻוָּון הַשְּׁלוֹם בַּיִת וְהַבִּנְיָן עֲדֵי עַד, דְּ״אֵין אִשָּׁה אֶלָּא לְבָנִים״ (כְּתוּבּוֹת נ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
for herein lies the essence of domestic harmony (shalom bayis), the primary objective of marriage and the enduring building, for "a wife is primarily for children" (Kesubos 59b);
וְאַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן אוֹהֵב שָׁלוֹם וְרוֹדֵף שָׁלוֹם (אָבוֹת א:יב)
and Aharon the Kohen loved peace and pursued peace (Avos 1:12);
וּבְסוֹטָה: ״וְהֵבִיא הָאִישׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ אֶל הַכֹּהֵן״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר ה:טו), שֶׁהוּא הַשּׁוּשְׁבִינָא דְּמַטְרוֹנִיתָא
and in the case of the suspected adulteress (Sotah): "then shall the man bring his wife unto the priest" (Bamidbar 5:15), he being the celestial groomsman of the Matron (Shechinah);
יוּכַל לָדַעַת אִם זָכוּ לִהְיוֹת שֵׁם יָ״הּ בֵּינֵיהֶם (סוֹטָה י״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
being able to discern whether they merited having the Divine Name Yud-Hei dwell between them (Sotah 17a);
וְאָז: ״וְנִקְּתָה וְנִזְרְעָה זָרַע״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר ה:כח)
and if innocent: "she shall be cleared, and shall conceive seed" (Bamidbar 5:28);
לִהְיוֹת הַשֵּׁם שָׁלֵם בִּבְתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת אַחֲרוֹנוֹת הָרוֹמְזוֹת לְבֵן וּבַת, דְּבָזֶה קַיָּים פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה
completing the Divine Name through the final two letters (Vav-Hei) alluding to son and daughter, fulfilling procreation;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּ״אַתָּה״ וְשֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה שֶׁעַל מֵצַח אַהֲרֹן
this being the rung of Attah and the Name Havayah upon Aharon's forehead;
דְּעַל יָדוֹ הוּא הַמְשָׁכַת הַבָּנֵי אַף לְמִי שֶׁלֹּא זָכָה לָזֶה בִּזְכוּתָא וּכְפִי הַטֶּבַע
through which children are channeled even to one who did not merit it through ordinary desert or according to natural law;

לִהְיוֹת כֹּחַ נִבְרָא יֵשׁ מֵהָאַיִן הַנֶּעְלָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁזָּכָה לָזֶה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא הַצּוּר שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ חֻצַּב אוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית, לִהְיוֹת כּוּלָּם שָׁרְשָׁם כֵּן
creating existence ex nihilo from the hidden Ayin, as Avraham Avinu merited, who is the rock whence Israel was hewn (Yeshayah 51:1).
וְ״חַיֵּי״ הִיא הַתּוֹרָה, שֶׁהִיא ״עֵץ חַיִּים״ (מִשְׁלֵי ג:יח) וְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם
And Life (chayei) is the holy Torah, which is "a tree of life" (Mishlei 3:18) and eternal life;
וְהוּא קַו הָאֶמְצָעִי דְּאָחֵיד בְּכוּלָּא, וּבְגוּף כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן עַצְמוֹ שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הַמְשָׁכַת הַכֹּל:
being the Central Pillar that binds all existence, rooted in the very essence of Keser Elyon whence all blessings flow.

8.h: The theme: The primordial depth revealed on the first day of Pesach, the name of Mashiach, and the three supernal crowns. On the first day of Pesach—the head of all festivals and the inception of Israel's national existence—the primordial depth of Keser was unveiled. In reward for this revelation, Israel will merit the name of Mashiach, which embodies the root holiness of the nation destined to endure forever ("the lip of truth shall be established forever", Mishlei 12:19). This reflects "their beginning is wedged in their end" (ne'utzan techilasan b'sofam): "The first unto Zion: Behold, behold them" (Yeshayah 41:27)—"Zion" denoting the gates distinguished in Halachah (Berachos 8a), and "the first" denoting the Crown of Torah (Keser Elyon), embracing the souls of Israel who arose in divine thought at the inception of Creation. Through ongoing remembrance of the Exodus in every generation, this light gradually emerges from concealment into full manifestation, culminating in the Resurrection of the Dead on Pesach. While the first day of Succos represents Yaakov journeying to Succos (the mystery of the Name Havayah and the rebuilding of the Temple / Avodah), and the taking of the Lulav accomplishes the subjugation of Esav (the first of the nations) and Gog (the last of the nations) through the elevation of Malchus (Ani), all three crowns were rooted simultaneously on Pesach through the transcendent name Ehyeh. Six months prior to the Exodus (in Tishrei) forced labor ceased, and twelve months prior (in Nissan) the first tidings arrived, awakening the spark of faith in the Name Ehyeh (I will be), advancing in Tishrei to the present liberation of the Name Havayah, and culminating on the night of the Exodus in the great awe of the revealed Shechinah: "I am Hashem—I am He and no other."

p: וְרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח שֶׁהוּא רֹאשׁ לְכָל הַזְּמַנִּים וּמוֹעֲדִים וְרֵאשִׁית בִּנְיַן אוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית, נִתְגַּלָּה לָהֶם עֹומֶק רֵאשִׁית זֶה

And the first day of Pesach, which is the head of all sacred seasons and appointed festivals, and the primary inception of the building of the Israelite nation, there was revealed unto them this primordial depth of Keser;
וּבִשְׂכַר זֶה יִזְכּוּ גַּם כֵּן לִשְׁמוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ
and in reward for this they will likewise merit the name of Mashiach (Pesachim 54a);
וְיָדוּעַ דְּהַשֵּׁם הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַדָּבָר, וְשֵׁם הָאָדָם מוֹרֶה עַל שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ
and it is known that the name is the spiritual root of an entity, and a person's name indicates the essential root of his soul;
וְשֵׁם מָשִׁיחַ הוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דִּקְדֻשַּׁת אוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה לֶעָתִיד, כַּאֲשֶׁר ״יִכּוֹן לָעַד״ הַ״שְׂפַת אֱמֶת״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ב:י״ט) שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה בַּהַתְחָלָה

and the name of Mashiach is the root of the holiness of the Israelite nation that will be revealed in the Future, when "the lip of truth" (Mishlei 12:19) which was initially unveiled at the inception shall be "established forever";
וְהוּא הַנְּעִיצַת תְּחִלָּתָן בְּסוֹפָן (סֵפֶר יְצִירָה א:ז) שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה: ״רִאשׁוֹן לְצִיּוֹן הִנֵּה הִנָּם״ (יְשַׁעְיָה מ״א:כ״ז)
and this is the wedging of their beginning in their end (Sefer Yetzirah 1:7) which will then be unveiled: "The first unto Zion: Behold, behold them" (Yeshayah 41:27);
דְּ״צִיּוֹן״ הֵם הַשְּׁעָרִים הַמְצוּיָּנִים בַּהֲלָכָה, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרָכוֹת (ח׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
for "Zion" refers to the gates distinguished (metzuyanim) in Halachah, as written in Berachos (8a);
וְהָרִאשׁוֹן הַיְינוּ הַכֶּתֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא הַכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן
and "the first" denotes the Crown of Torah which is Keser Elyon;
״הִנֵּה הִנָּם״ — הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁעָלוּ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה א:ד), וּדְבוּקִים בְּשָׁרְשָׁם בַּכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן הַנֶּעְלָם

"behold, behold them"—these are the souls of the Children of Israel who arose in divine thought at the beginning of Creation (Bereishis Rabbah 1:4), cleaved in their root unto the concealed Supernal Crown.
וְזֶהוּ הִתְגַּלּוּת עֹומֶק רֵאשִׁית הָאוֹר שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם
And this was the manifestation of the primordial depth of light that was revealed at the Exodus from Egypt;
אַחַר הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּזֵכֶר לִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁיַּעֲשׂוּ בְּכָל שָׁנָה וְשָׁנָה
emerging through the ongoing spiritual toil in remembering the Exodus from Egypt which Israel perform in each and every year;
שֶׁיֵּצֵא הָאוֹר מְעַט מְעַט מֵהַהֶעְלֵם עַד שֶׁיָּבוֹא לַגִּילּוּי הַגָּמוּר וְיִזְכּוּ לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם
so that the light emerges little by little from concealment until arriving at consummate revelation, meriting eternal life;
דְּעַל כֵּן תְּחִיַּיִת הַמֵּתִים יִהְיֶה בְּפֶסַח, וּמַפְטִירִין זֶה בְּחוֹל הַמּוֹעֵד פֶּסַח (יְחֶזְקֵאל ל״ז)
wherefore the Resurrection of the Dead will occur on Pesach, and we read this as the Haftarah on the intermediate Sabbath of Pesach (Yechezkel 37).
וּשְׁבִיתַת יוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן דְּסֻכּוֹת הִיא הַשָּׂגַת דַּרְגָּא דְּ״[וְ]יַעֲקֹב נָסַע סֻכֹּתָה״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״ג:י״ז), שֶׁהוּא רָזָא דְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה כִּידוּעַ

And the cessation of work on the first festival day of Succos is the attainment of the rung of "And Jacob journeyed to Succos" (Bereishis 33:17), which is the mystical secret of the Name Havayah as is known;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִזְכּוּ לְבִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁהוּא ״סֻכַּת שָׁלוֹם״ וְרָזָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה
and through this they will merit the rebuilding of the Temple which is the "Tabernacle of Peace" (Succas Shalom) and the mystery of sacrificial service (Avodah);
וְרִאשׁוֹן דְּלוּלָב, בּוֹ נִיצּוּחַ הָאוּמּוֹת, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ל:ב)
and the first day of taking the Lulav, through it is achieved the triumph over the nations, as written in Vayikra Rabbah (30:2);
וּכְרִיתַת זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו שֶׁהוּא הָרֵאשִׁית דְּגוֹיִם וְכֶתֶר דְּסִטְרָא אָחֳרָא
and the cutting off of the seed of Esav who is the "first of the nations" and the crown of the Other Side (Sitra Achra);
עַל יְדֵי הִתְעַלּוּת קוֹמַת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּרָזָא דְּ״אֲנִי״ וְכֶתֶר מַלְכוּתָם עַל כָּל הַגּוֹיִם
accomplished through the elevation of the stature of Knesset Israel in the mystery of Ani [Malchus] and their royal crown over all the nations;
וְעַל כֵּן מַפֶּלֶת גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג בְּסֻכּוֹת, שֶׁעֵשָׂו הוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן דְּאוּמּוֹת וְגוֹג הוּא הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁבָּהֶם
wherefore the downfall of Gog and Magog will occur on Succos, Esav being the first of the adversary nations and Gog being the last among them.
וְכָל ג׳ כְּתָרִים אֵלּוּ נִתְגַּלּוּ בְּפֶסַח מִצַּד הִתְגַּלּוּת שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ עִיקַּר הַתְחָלַת הַגְּאוּלָּה
And all these three crowns were revealed on Pesach from the revelation of the root of Keser Elyon, whence originates the primary beginning of the redemption;

עַל יְדֵי זֶה אָמַר לוֹ תֵּיכֶף אַחַר כָּךְ: ״כֹּה תֹאמַר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל: ה׳ אֱלֹהֵי אֲבֹתֵיכֶם [אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם אֱלֹהֵי יִצְחָק וֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב שְׁלָחַנִי אֲלֵיכֶם] וְגוֹמֵר״ (שְׁמוֹת ג:טו)

through which Hashem said to Moshe immediately afterward: "Thus shall you say unto the children of Israel: Hashem, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me unto you, etc." (Shemos 3:15);
וְגִילָּה לָהֶם שֵׁם הַהֲוָיָ״ה שֶׁהוּא ״אֱלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם״ עַל יְדֵי הִתְכַּלְּלוּתָם בְּמִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הַבָּחִיר שֶׁבָּאָבוֹת
revealing unto them the Name Havayah who is "the God of your fathers," through their integration into the attribute of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, the chosen of the Patriarchs;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס״ג:ב׳) דְּכוּלָּם נִקְרְאוּ יַעֲקֹב
as the Sages of blessed memory stated (Bereishis Rabbah 63:2) that all three Patriarchs were included in the name Yaakov;
וּדְ״זֶה שְּׁמִי לְעֹלָם״ (שְׁמוֹת ג:טו), וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא לְעוֹלָם — ״לְעַלֵּם״ כְּתִיב (פְּסָחִים נ׳ עַמּוּד א׳), דְּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נֶעְלָם
and that "this is My Name forever (l'olam)" (Shemos 3:15), although it means forever, it is written defectively to read "to conceal (l'alem)" (Pesachim 50a), for in this world it is hidden;
כִּי הוּא הַמְשָׁכַת הַקַּו אֶמְצָעִי שֶׁמִּכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן הַנֶּעְלָם עַד סוֹף כָּל דַּרְגִּין
because It is the channeling of the Central Pillar extending from the concealed Keser Elyon down to the termination of all rungs;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא הָאֲחִיזָה בַּכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן הַנֶּעְלָם
and through this Israel acquires a hold within the concealed Supernal Crown,
שֶׁמִּצַּד הַהֶעְלֵם כָּל הַהַשָּׂגָה הוּא רַק שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַשָּׂגַת אוֹר זֶה הוּא יָכוֹל לְהַגִּיעַ לְהַשָּׂגַת מַדְרֵיגוֹת הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת דְּיֵשׁ מֵאַיִן
where from the aspect of concealment all human perception consists merely in this: that through perceiving this light one is enabled to attain the expanding levels of existence ex nihilo from Ayin.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּשִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים קוֹדֶם נִתְבַּטְּלָה עֲבוֹדָה מֵהֶם, וְהַיְינוּ בְּתִשְׁרֵי (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה י״א עַמּוּד א׳)
And it is known that six months prior to the Exodus forced labor was abolished from them, namely in Tishrei (Rosh Hashanah 11a);
וּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֳדָשִׁים קוֹדֶם הָיְתָה הַתְחָלַת הַבְּשׂוֹרָה, דְּהַיְינוּ בְּנִיסָן הַקּוֹדֵם (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה ט:יב)
and twelve months prior was the initial tidings of redemption, namely in the preceding Nissan (Shemos Rabbah 9:12);
וְנִרְאֶה לִי דְּאָז בְּנִיסָן הַקּוֹדֵם הָיְתָה הִתְגַּלּוּת הַתְחָלַת דְּנִיצוֹצוֹת הָאוֹר בְּקֶרֶב הַלְּבָבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
and it appears to me that then, in that preceding Nissan, occurred the initial revelation of the sparks of light within the hearts of the Children of Israel,
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהֶאֱמִינוּ דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל כָּל פָּנִים עָתִיד וּמוּכָן לְגָאֳלָם, וְהוּא הַשָּׂגַת הַשֵּׁם אֶהְיֶ״ה
through their believing that the Blessed Name was in any event destined and prepared to redeem them, which was the perception of the Name Ehyeh [I will be];
וּבְתִשְׁרֵי שֶׁכְּבָר הִשִּׂיגוּ קְצָת חֵירוּת בַּהֹווֶה, הוּא הַשָּׂגַת הַשֵּׁם הֲוָיָ״ה
and in Tishrei, when they had already attained partial physical freedom in the present, was the perception of the Name Havayah [present existence];
וּבְנִיסָן שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁבּוֹ נִגְאֲלוּ, הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַמּוֹרָא גָּדוֹל דְּגִלּוּי שְׁכִינָה
and in the following Nissan wherein they were fully redeemed, was the manifestation of the great awe of the revealed Shechinah,
עַל יְדֵי ״וְעָבַרְתִּי [בְאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם]... אֲנִי ה׳״ (שְׁמוֹת י״ב:י״ב), דְּנִתְגַּלָּה דַּ״אֲנִי הוּא וְלֹא אַחֵר״:
through "And I will pass through the land of Egypt... I am Hashem" (Shemos 12:12; Passover Haggadah), where it was revealed that "I am He and no other."
The theme: The letters of Ehyeh (אהי״ה), the Crown of a Good Name
Keser Shem Tov

, and the essence of Yosef and Yehudah. The three crowns correspond to the three distinct letters Aleph-Yud-Hei of the Name Ehyeh: the Aleph is the transcendent head of all; the Yud is the inception of actualized perception ex nihilo, which expands into the letter Vav of the Name Havayah
the Central Pillar / Crown of Torah
; the lower Hei is the crown of the final Hei of Havayah
Crown of Royalty
. The first letter Hei of Ehyeh crowns the first Hei of Havayah, representing the Crown of a Good Name
Keser Shem Tov
which ascends above all three
Avos 4:13; Koheles 7:1

. A "good name" is not a separate entity, but describes one who excels in Torah, Avodah, or Gemilus Chasadim—the three pillars of the world, which unite in the foundation of the single pillar called Tzaddik
Chagigah 12b; Mishlei 10:25
. Israel is called "the remnant of Yosef," embodying the consummate tzaddik who strictly adheres to the halachah; yet human exertion alone cannot escape all blemish
"there is not a righteous man upon earth that does good and sins not", Koheles 7:20

. When Yosef brought an evil report against his brothers, he evaluated them from the standard of the consummate tzaddik. In truth, Israel is named after Yehudah—whose name spells the Tetragrammaton with the letter Dalet (דלות, spiritual poverty). Originally a Dalet, the soul recognizes its absolute deficiency and receives the divine seed from Above, expanding the Dalet into the fertile letter Hei, achieving the perfection of Knesset Israel.
וּשְׁלֹשָׁה כְּתָרִים שֶׁל ג׳ מַדְרֵיגוֹת אֵלּוּ הֵם הָרְמוּזִים בְּג׳ אוֹתִיּוֹת אָלֶ״ף יוּ״ד הֵ״א דְּשֵׁם אֶהְיֶ״ה
And the three crowns of these three rungs are alluded to in the three letters Aleph-Yud-Hei of the Name Ehyeh
(א-ה-י-ה): אָלֶ״ף הוּא הָרֵאשִׁית הַכֹּל וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם
the Aleph is the primordial head of all and the concealed root;
וְיוּ״ד הוּא הַתְחָלַת הַהִתְגַּלּוּת דְּיֵשׁ מֵאַיִן, וּמִמֶּנּוּ הַתְחָלַת הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת אוֹת הַוָּי״ו דְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה, קַו הָאֶמְצָעִי וְכֶתֶר שֶׁלּוֹ
and the Yud is the inception of manifestation ex nihilo from Ayin, whence begins the expansion of the letter Vav of the Name Havayah, being the Central Pillar and its Crown [Torah];
וְהַהֵ״א [הָאַחֲרוֹנָה] הוּא הַכֶּתֶר דְּהֵ״א אַחֲרוֹנָה שֶׁל שֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה
and the final Hei of Ehyeh is the crown of the final letter Hei of the Name Havayah [Royalty].
וְאֵלּוּ הַג׳ אוֹתִיּוֹת נִבְדָּלִים זֶה מִזֶּה, אֲבָל אוֹת הָרְבִיעִית הִיא כְּפוּלָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה גַּם כֵּן הַהֵ״א כְּפוּלָה
And these three letters are distinct from one another, but the fourth letter is doubled [the letter Hei appearing twice], just as in the Name Havayah the letter Hei is likewise doubled;
וְהֵ״א רִאשׁוֹנָה דְּשֵׁם אֶהְיֶ״ה הוּא הַכֶּתֶר לְהֵ״א רִאשׁוֹנָה דְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה
and the first letter Hei of the Name Ehyeh is the crown of the first letter Hei of the Name Havayah [Binah];
וְהוּא הַ״כֶּתֶר שֵׁם טוֹב״ שֶׁעוֹלֶה עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן (אָבוֹת ד:יג)
and it is the Crown of a Good Name (Keser Shem Tov) which ascends above them all (Avos 4:13);
דְּ״טוֹב שֵׁם מִשֶּׁמֶן טוֹב״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:א), שֶׁבּוֹ נִמְשְׁחוּ כֹּהֲנִים וּמְלָכִים שֶׁהֵם ב׳ כְּתָרִים
for "A good name is better than precious oil" (Koheles 7:1), with which oil priests and kings were anointed, representing two crowns;
גַּם שֶׁמֶן רוֹמֵז לְחָכְמָה כִּידוּעַ שֶׁהוּא כֶּתֶר תּוֹרָה, וְכֵן: ״אֵין טוֹב אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה״ (בְּרָכוֹת ה׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
furthermore, oil alludes to Chochmah as is known, which is the Crown of Torah, and likewise: "there is no good other than Torah" (Berachos 5a);
וְשֵׁם טוֹב — טוֹב מִכּוּלָּם, וְהוּא הָעוֹלֶה עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן, הַיְינוּ עַל גַּבֵּי כָּל שְׁלֹשֶׁת כְּתָרִים אֵלּוּ
and a "good name" is better than them all, ascending above all these three crowns.
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם טוֹב אֵינוֹ דָּבָר בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, כִּי כָּל שֵׁם טוֹב צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִתְפָּס בְּאֵיזֶה דָּבָר שֶׁבַּעֲבוּרוֹ הוּא הַשֵּׁם טוֹב שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ
For a "good name" is not an independent, isolated attribute, seeing that every good name must be anchored within some specific virtue on account of which the person possesses that good name:
וְזֶה יֵשׁ לוֹ שֵׁם טוֹב שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל תּוֹרָה, וְזֶה בַּעֲבוֹדָה, וְזֶה בִּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים
this one possessing a good name because he is a master of Torah, that one in Avodah, and another in Gemilus Chasadim,
שֶׁהֵם הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה כְּתָרִים וְעַמּוּדִים שֶׁעֲלֵיהֶם הָעוֹלָם קַיָּים
which are the three crowns and pillars upon which the world endures;
וּבְמָקוֹם אַחֵר (חֲגִיגָה י״ב עַמּוּד ב׳) אִיתָא: ״עַל עַמּוּד אֶחָד הָעוֹלָם עוֹמֵד, וְצַדִּיק שְׁמוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ׳וְצַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם׳ (מִשְׁלֵי י:כה)״
and elsewhere it is taught (Chagigah 12b): "Upon a single pillar the world stands, and Tzaddik is its name, as it is said: 'but the righteous is an everlasting foundation' (Mishlei 10:25)";
הוּא כְּלַל כָּל הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה עַמּוּדִים, הֵם נַעֲשִׂים בִּיסוֹד עַמּוּד אֶחָד בְּצִדְקַת הַצַּדִּיק הוּא הַכּוֹלְלָם
this being the synthesis of all three pillars, which are unified within Yesod as a single pillar through the righteousness of the Tzaddik who encompasses them all;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבִּפְרָטִים הֵן חֲלוּקִין, שֶׁגַּם הַצַּדִּיקִים חֲלוּקִים בְּמַדְרֵיגוֹתֵיהֶם זֶה מִזֶּה לְשָׁלֹשׁ מַדְרֵיגוֹת נֶגֶד ג׳ אֲבָהָן, בִּכְלָלָם הוּא אֶחָד

even though in particular details they are differentiated, the righteous themselves dividing in their ranks into three categories corresponding to the Three Patriarchs, yet in their collective unity they are one;
וְ״עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים לְעוֹלָם יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ס:כא), הוּא הָעוֹלָם שֶׁהַצַּדִּיק יְסוֹדוֹ
and "Your people also shall be all righteous, they shall inherit the land forever" (Yeshayah 60:21)—"land" being the world whose foundation is the Tzaddik.
דְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָאִים ״שְׁאֵרִית יוֹסֵף״ (עָמוֹס ה:טו) שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר תּוֹלְדוֹתָיו שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל״ז:ב׳)
For all Israel are designated "the remnant of Joseph" (Amos 5:15), who is the primary offspring of Yaakov (Bereishis 37:2);

הַיְינוּ גִּילּוּי הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת מַדְרֵיגוֹת אֲבָהָן בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּצַדִּיק גָּמוּר שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא מִשּׁוּרַת מִשְׁפַּט הַתּוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדָה וּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים הַחִיּוּבִים עַל כָּל אִישׁ יִשְׂרְאֵלִי

meaning the manifest expansion of the Patriarchs' rungs revealed in this world in the consummate tzaddik who never deviates from the statutory boundaries of Torah, Avodah, and Gemilus Chasadim incumbent upon every Jew;
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הָאָדָם מִצַּד מַה שֶּׁהוּא נִבְדָּל
and this constitutes the perfection of man from the perspective of his differentiated human stature;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״אַל יִתְהַלֵּל חָכָם [בְּחָכְמָתוֹ וְאַל יִתְהַלֵּל הַגִּבּוֹר בִּגְבוּרָתוֹ אַל יִתְהַלֵּל עָשִׁיר בְּעָשְׁרוֹ]״ (יִרְמְיָה ט:כב)
and concerning this it is said: "Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, let not the rich man glory in his riches" (Yirmiyah 9:22),
הֵם שְׁלֹשֶׁת עַמּוּדֵי עוֹלָם אֵלּוּ: חָכָם בַּתּוֹרָה, וְגִבּוֹר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ יִצְרוֹ בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְעָשִׁיר בַּעַל גְּמִילוּת חֲסָדִים

these corresponding to these three pillars of the world: the wise in Torah, the mighty who conquers his yetzer in divine service (Avodah), and the rich who performs acts of lovingkindness (Gemilus Chasadim);
וְאֵין בָּהֶם כְּדֵי הִתְהַלְּלוּת לִזְכּוֹת לְשֵׁם טוֹב עַל יְדֵי זֶה
yet in these self-attained accomplishments alone there is no ground for glorying so as to merit a true "good name" through them;
״כִּי אִם בְּזֹאת יִתְהַלֵּל הַמִּתְהַלֵּל הַשְׂכֵּל וְיָדֹעַ אוֹתִי כִּי אֲנִי ה׳ עֹשֶׂה חֶסֶד מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה [בָּאָרֶץ כִּי בְאֵלֶּה חָפַצְתִּי נְאֻם ה׳]״ (שָׁם:כ״ג)

"but let him that glories glory in this, that he understands and knows Me, that I am Hashem Who exercises lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness in the earth; for in these things I delight, says Hashem" (ibid. 9:23);
הֵם גַּם כֵּן ג׳ אֵלּוּ: ״חֶסֶד״ הוּא תּוֹרַת חֶסֶד, וּ״מִשְׁפָּט״ הוּא הַדָּן אֶת יִצְרוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּמְגִלָּה (ט״ו עַמּוּד ב׳), וּ״צְדָקָה״ הַיְינוּ גְּמִילוּת חֲסָדִים

these likewise mirroring these three: "lovingkindness" is the Torah of kindness (Mishlei 31:26), "judgment" is judging one's yetzer (Megillah 15b), and "righteousness" is acts of charity and lovingkindness.
וְצָרִיךְ שֶׁיֵּדַע שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הָעוֹשֶׂה הַכֹּל בְּקֶרֶב הָאָרֶץ וְלִבּוֹת בְּנֵי אָדָם
And man must know that the Blessed Name is the One Who effects everything within the earth and the hearts of men;
דִּבְאֶמֶת ״אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ״ (דְּבָרִים ד:לה), וְגַם ״כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ״ (יְשַׁעְיָה כ״ו:י״ב)
for in truth "there is none else beside Him" (Devarim 4:35), and "all our works You have wrought for us" (Yeshayah 26:12);
וְכָל זֶה שֶׁהוּא חוֹשֵׁב שֶׁהוּא חָכְמָתוֹ וּגְבוּרָתוֹ וְעָשְׁרוֹ, הַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ וּבְחִירָתוֹ הַטּוֹבָה
and all that a person presumes to be his own wisdom, might, and wealth, derived from his personal exertion and righteous choice;
זֶהוּ מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁבּוֹ הִתְגַּלּוּת הַבְּחִירָה, וּכְאִילּוּ הָאָדָם נִפְרָד מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
this perspective belongs solely to this world wherein free choice operates, making it appear as if man were an autonomous entity severed from the Blessed Name;
וְעַדַיִין לֹא הִגִּיעַ לְתַכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת הַדְּבֵיקוּת בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאֵינָם נִפְרָדִים כְּלָל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
having not yet attained that consummate cleaving unto the Living God possessed by collective Israel who are never severed from the Blessed Name.
וּבֶאֱמֶת מִצַּד בְּחִירָתוֹ וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ: ״[כִּי אָדָם] אֵין צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ [אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה טּוֹב] וְלֹא יֶחֱטָא״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כ)
And in truth, from the perspective of mortal free choice and independent striving: "there is not a righteous man upon earth that does good and sins not" (Koheles 7:20);
וְ״לֹא יִצְדַּק לְפָנֶיךָ כָל חָי״ (תְּהִלִּים קמ״ג:ב׳), לִהְיוֹת בְּמַדְרֵיגַת צַדִּיק בִּשְׁלֵימוּת שֶׁלֹּא יֶחֱטָא
and "in Your sight shall no man living be justified" (Tehillim 143:2), to exist on the plane of a consummate tzaddik who never stumbles into sin;
דִּבְכָל אֶחָד יֵשׁ חִסָּרוֹן בְּעַל כָּרְחוֹ
for within every single human being there exists an inevitable deficiency against his will.
וְזֶהוּ הַדִּבָּה רָעָה שֶׁהֵבִיא יוֹסֵף עַל אֶחָיו, דְּמִצַּד מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ יֵשׁ חִסָּרוֹן בְּכָל אֶחָיו שֶׁאֵין צַדִּיקִים בִּשְׁלֵימוּת

And this was the evil report that Yosef brought regarding his brothers (Bereishis 37:2), for from the vantage of his spiritual rung there existed a deficiency in all his brothers, they not being consummate tzaddikim;
וּמִצַּד מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ נִקְרָאִים רַק ״שְׁאֵרִית יוֹסֵף״, כִּי בְּכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן שְׁאֵרִית מִמַּדְרֵיגָתוֹ
and from the vantage of his level they are termed merely "the remnant of Joseph," because within every Jew there remains a remnant of Yosef's attribute of restraint;
דְּכוּלָּם צַדִּיקִים גַּם כֵּן, אֲבָל לֹא עַצְמוּתוֹ בִּשְׁלֵימוּת נִגְלֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
for all are indeed righteous, yet his consummate essence is not openly manifest in this world.
דִּבְשֵׁם הָעֶצֶם נִקְרְאוּ עַל שֵׁם יְהוּדָה
Rather, in their essential national designation they are called after Yehudah (Yehudim);
שֶׁהוּא נִקְרָא כּוּלּוֹ עַל שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּצֵירוּף אוֹת הַדָּלֶ״ת הָרוֹמֶזֶת עַל דַּלּוּת (סוֹטָה י׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
whose name
(יְהוּדָה)
contains the entire four-letter Name of the Holy One (Yud-Hei-Vav-Hei), with the addition of the letter Dalet alluding to poverty (dalus, Sotah 10b);
וְהֵ״א דָּלֶ״ת הֲוַות, רַק בָּתַר דְּקַבִּילַת עוּבָּרָא נַעֲשָׂה הֵ״א (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק א׳ ר״נ עַמּוּד ב׳)
and the letter Hei was originally an impoverished Dalet
which only after receiving the fertile seed from Above became pregnant and expanded into a Hei
Zohar I, 250b);
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם ״דַּל״, ״עָנִי״ וְכוּלֵיהּ, בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְדַבֵּר
and in every place where Scripture speaks of the "poor" and "destitute," it refers to Israel;
שֶׁזֶּה כָּל מַעֲלָתָם: שֶׁהֵם מַכִּירִים חֶסְרוֹנָם וְשֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם כֹּחַ וְשׁוּם דָּבָר רַק מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֵן וּמַשְׁפִּיעַ וְעוֹזֵר
for this is their supreme virtue: that they recognize their profound deficiency, knowing they possess no independent power or merit except what the Blessed Name gives, bestows, and assists;
וְזֶהוּ: ״הַשְׂכֵּל וְיָדֹעַ אוֹתִי כִּי אֲנִי ה׳ וְגוֹמֵר״ (יִרְמְיָה ט:כג)
and this is: "that he understands and knows Me, that I am Hashem, etc." (Yirmiyah 9:23);
וְאָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁפִּיעַ לָהֶם, וְנַעֲשָׂה מִדָּלֶ״ת — הֵ״א, שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל:
and then the Blessed Name pours forth His influx unto them, and the impoverished Dalet is transformed into the fertile Hei, which is the consummate perfection of Knesset Israel!

8.h: The theme: The superiority of the penitent over the wholly righteous (ba'alei teshuvah over tzaddikim) and the crown of an everlasting name (shem olam). The ultimate cleaving will be realized when Israel is called by the Name of the Holy One (Bava Batra 75b) through Mashiach ben David from the seed of Yehudah. This is achieved through repentance, where the penitent ascends above the wholly righteous (Berachos 34b) into the transcendent realm of divine Foreknowledge (Yedi'ah) above free choice, where all past sins are rectified and transformed into merits. While the wholly righteous man operates within strict boundaries (hagdara) like precious oil fragrant only from chamber to hall (Koheles Rabbah 7:1), the penitent shatters all boundaries, acquiring his world in a single moment like Elazar ben Dordaya (Avodah Zarah 17a). This is the "good name" whose fragrance spreads from one end of the world to the other (Yevamos 16a), fulfilling: "and he smelled the fragrance of his garments" (Bereishis 27:27)—which Chazal read as "the fragrance of his traitors" (bogdav, Sanhedrin 37a), the sublime fragrance of sinners who repented. Consummate tzaddikim secure a lasting name through their physical children (shem olam d'Yosef / she'eirit Yosef); but the penitent, from within the brokenness of his heart ("Hashem is near unto them that are of a broken heart", Tehillim 34:19), merits an everlasting name (shem olam) directly within Hashem's house (Yeshayah 56:5). Even when darkness strikes the righteous (like David with Batsheva, arranged by Hashem to establish the yoke of repentance, Avodah Zarah 5a), it serves to reveal the divine light. At the final judgment, the righteous weep because they mistakenly thought their triumph over the yetzer had been achieved through their own strength; only then do they recognize that without divine aid they could never have conquered that mountain, arriving at the truth of the place where penitents stand.

p: וְזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית הַדְּבֵיקוּת עַד שֶׁיִּקָּרֵא כּוּלּוֹ בְּשֵׁם ה׳
And this is the consummate height of cleaving, until the person is designated entirely with the Name of Hashem;
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ע״ה עַמּוּד ב׳): ״עֲתִידִים צַדִּיקִים שֶׁיִּקָּרְאוּ בִּשְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא״
as the Sages stated (Bava Batra 75b): "In the Future the righteous will be called by the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He";
וְזֶהוּ כְּשֶׁיַּגִּיעַ לְתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת דְּלֶעָתִיד עַל יְדֵי מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד מִזֶּרַע יְהוּדָה
and this will unfold upon arriving at the ultimate perfection of the Future through Mashiach ben David from the seed of Yehudah;
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל נִגְאָלִין בּוֹ
which is achieved through repentance, through which Israel is redeemed;
וּ״מְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִים — אֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים יְכוֹלִים לַעֲמוֹד״ (בְּרָכוֹת ל״ד עַמּוּד ב׳), שֶׁהוּא מָקוֹם יוֹתֵר עֶלְיוֹן
and "in the place where penitents stand, wholly righteous men cannot stand" (Berachos 34b), which is a far higher, more transcendent realm;
כִּי צָרִיךְ לְהַגִּיעַ לִמְקוֹם הַיְּדִיעָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַבְּחִירָה
for one must reach the dimension of Foreknowledge (Yedi'ah) that transcends free choice;
שֶׁמִּשָּׁם הוּא תִּיקּוּן הַקּוֹדֵם שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה שׁוּם חִסָּרוֹן, מֵאַחַר שֶׁדָּבוּק בִּמְקוֹרוֹ וְהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
whence issues the retroactive rectification of the past so that no blemish remains, since all is cleaved to its Source and all is seen as flowing from the Blessed Name;
וְאָז מִתְעַלִּים כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמַּדְרֵיגַת הֵ״א אַחֲרוֹנָה לָרִאשׁוֹנָה
and then Knesset Israel ascends from the rung of the final letter Hei [Malchus] to the first letter Hei [Binah],
שֶׁהִיא רָזָא דְּעוֹלָם הַבָּא, ״יָמִים שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם חֵפֶץ״ (שַׁבָּת קנ״א עַמּוּד ב׳) וּבְחִירָה
which is the mystery of the World to Come, the days in which "I have no pleasure" (Shabbat 151b) and free choice ceases.
וּבְזֹאת יִתְהַלֵּל הַמִּתְהַלֵּל שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לְכֶתֶר שֵׁם טוֹב
And in this glory may one glory who merits the Crown of a Good Name;
דְּשֶׁמֶן טוֹב מֵרִיחַ רַק מִקִּיטוֹן לִטְרַקְלִין (קֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה ז:א)
for precious oil emits its fragrance merely from the chamber to the parlor (Koheles Rabbah 7:1);
דְּצַדִּיק גָּמוּר הוּא בַּהַגְדָּרָה כָּל אֶחָד כְּפִי קַו הַמִּדָּה שֶׁלּוֹ כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא אָדָם
for the wholly righteous man operates within measured boundaries, each according to his measured line as a mortal human being;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה פּוֹרֵץ כָּל מִינֵי הַגְדָּרוֹת
whereas the penitent shatters all manner of restrictive boundaries;
וּבְשַׁעֲתָא חֲדָא וּבְרִגְעָא חֲדָא יוּכַל לִקְנוֹת עוֹלָמוֹ, וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁקּוֹרִין לוֹ ״רַבִּי״ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן דּוֹרְדַיָא (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה י״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
and in a single hour and in a single moment he can acquire his world, and not only that, but they designate him "Rebbe," as with Rabbi Elazar ben Dordaya (Avodah Zarah 17a);
שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִמִּדַּת וּמַדְרֵיגַת הַשָּׂגַת אָדָם, שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג וְלָבוֹא בְּרֶגַע אֶחָד מֵהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת תַּכְלִית הַחֹשֶׁךְ לְאוֹר גָּדוֹל
which transcends all standard human perception: to be capable in a single flash of leaping from immersion in absolute darkness into great light!
וְזֶהוּ הַשֵּׁם טוֹב שֶׁהוּא מִסּוֹף עוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ, עַיֵּין יְבָמוֹת (ט״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
And this is the good name whose fragrance spreads from one end of the world to the other, see Yevamos (16a);
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״וַיָּרַח אֶת רֵיחַ בְּגָדָיו״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:כ״ז) — ״רֵיחַ בּוֹגְדָיו״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין ל״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
and concerning this it is said: "and he smelled the fragrance of his garments (begadav)" (Bereishis 27:27)—which the Sages read: "the fragrance of his traitors (bogdav)" (Sanhedrin 37a);
דְּאַחַר שֶׁשָּׁבוּ מֵהֶם הוּא עִיקַּר הָרֵיחַ טוֹב הַמֵּרִיחַ בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
for when they repent, from them issues the sweetest fragrance that perfumes the entire universe;
וּכְדָנִיֵּאל, חֲנַנְיָה, מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה שֶׁהֵם בַּעֲלֵי שֵׁם טוֹב הַנִּזְכָּרִים בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א:ג) עַל פָּסוּק ״טוֹב שֵׁם״
and like Daniel, Chananyah, Mishael, and Azaryah, who are the possessors of the good name mentioned in the Midrash (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:3) on the verse "A good name is better than precious oil";
שֶׁהֵם בְּגָלוּת בָּבֶל אַחַר תֹּקֶף הַחֲטָאִים עַד שֶׁגָּרְמוּ תַּכְלִית הָרִיחוּק וְגָלוּת הָאָרֶץ
who lived in the Babylonian exile after the intensity of sins had caused the ultimate distancing and expulsion from the Holy Land;
כְּשֶׁחָזְרוּ לְהִתְקָרֵב, זָכוּ לְ״יָד וָשֵׁם [טוֹב מִבָּנִים וּמִבָּנוֹת] שֵׁם עוֹלָם [אֶתֶּן לוֹ] אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִכָּרֵת״ (יְשַׁעְיָה נ״ו:ה׳)
yet when they turned to draw near again, they merited "a monument and a name better than sons and daughters, an everlasting name that shall not be cut off" (Yeshayah 56:5).
כִּי הַשֵּׁם עוֹלָם דְּיוֹסֵף הוּא רַק בַּבָּנִים, ״כִּי הִפְרַנִי אֱלֹהִים בְּאֶרֶץ עָנְיִי״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מ״א:נ״ב)
For the everlasting name of Yosef operates specifically through children: "For God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction" (Bereishis 41:52);
שֶׁאִם הוּא אֵינוֹ צַדִּיק, יוּכַל לְהִתְתַּקֵּן בְּזַרְעוֹ, דִּ״בְרָא מְזַכֵּי אַבָּא״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סַנְהֶדְרִין ק״ד עַמּוּד א׳)
for if a person is not righteous, he can be redeemed through his seed, for "a son confers merit upon his father," as written in Sanhedrin (104a);
וּ״שְׁאֵרִית יוֹסֵף״ הֵם בָּנָיו, שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַשְּׁאֵרִית שֶׁל הָאָדָם
and "the remnant of Joseph" refers to his children, which is the biological remnant of man;
וְזֶהוּ הַשֵּׁם וּשְׁאָר שֶׁל הַצַּדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים בְּתוֹלְדוֹתֵיהֶם בְּגַשְׁמִיּוּת בְּבָנִים
and this is the enduring name and remnant of the wholly righteous through physical children,
לְמִי שֶׁלֹּא הִשְׁתַּלֵּם בְּרוּחָנִיּוּת בְּמִצְוֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים שֶׁהֵם עִיקַּר תּוֹלְדוֹתֵיהֶם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים (תַּנְחוּמָא נֹחַ ב׳)
for one who has not fully perfected himself spiritually in mitzvos and good deeds, which are the primary offspring of the righteous (Tanchuma, Noach 2).
אֲבָל הַבַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה, מִתּוֹךְ הַמְּרִירוּת וּשְׁבִירוּת לִבּוֹ, דְּ״קָרוֹב ה׳ לְנִשְׁבְּרֵי לֵב״ (תְּהִלִּים ל״ד:י״ט), וְ״[אֶשְׁכּוֹן... וְ]אֶת דַּכָּא [וּשְׁפַל רוּחַ]״ (יְשַׁעְיָה נ״ז:ט״ו)

But with the penitent, out of the deep bitterness and contrite breaking of his heart—for "Hashem is near unto them that are of a broken heart" (Tehillim 34:19), and "I dwell with him that is of a contrite and humble spirit" (Yeshayah 57:15)—
מֵאִיר לוֹ הָאוֹר שֶׁל שׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתוֹ, שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַשָּׂגַת עַצְמִיּוּת שֵׁם הָאָדָם הַמּוֹרֶה עַל שָׁרְשׁוֹ
there shines upon him the radiant light of his soul's primal root, which is the comprehension of man's essential name reflecting his root;
וְהוּא הַ״שֵּׁם עוֹלָם״ שֶׁנִּיתַּן לָהֶם בְּבֵיתוֹ וְחוֹמוֹתָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ
and this is the "everlasting name" (shem olam) given unto them within His house and His walls, blessed be His Name (Yeshayah 56:5);
לֹא מִצַּד תּוֹלְדוֹתֵיהֶם וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, רַק מִצַּד שָׁרְשָׁם בָּעוֹלָם הָעֶלְיוֹן וַאֲצִילוּת קָדְשׁוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא בֵּיתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
not from the perspective of their physical progeny or earthly striving, but from their transcendent root in the supernal world of Atzilus, which is His holy abode;
וּמִשָּׁם אֲצִילוּת כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם חֵלֶק ה׳, דְּמַאן דְּנָפַח — מִתּוֹכוֹ נָפַח
whence emanate all the souls of Israel who are the portion of Hashem, for "whoever breathes, breathes from his innermost essence" (Tanya, ch. 2);
וְזֶהוּ שֵׁם עוֹלָם שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת נִכְרָת כְּלָל
and this is an eternal name that can never be cut off:
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ יַגְדִּיל עֲווֹנוֹת זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ, אֵין נֶעֱקָר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמֶּנּוּ, הַיְינוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם שֶׁבּוֹ
for even should one multiply sins one above the other, the name of Israel is never uprooted from him, that is, his concealed soul-root!
וְאוֹר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה
And this light cannot be attained in this world except through repentance;
כִּי כָּךְ בְּרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם: בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא (שַׁבָּת ע״ז עַמּוּד ב׳)
for such was the creation of the cosmos: first came darkness and then light (Shabbat 77b);

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ב:ה): ״׳חֹשֶׁךְ׳ — זֶה מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים, ׳וְאוֹר׳ — זֶה מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים, וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ בְּמִי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא חָפֵץ וְכוּלֵיהּ״

and the Sages of blessed memory expounded (Bereishis Rabbah 2:5): "'Darkness'—these are the deeds of the wicked; 'and light'—these are the deeds of the righteous; and I would not know in which of them the Holy One delights, etc.";
וְדַיֵּיק ״מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים״, דְּוַדַּאי אֵין חֵפֶץ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּרְשָׁעִים, וְלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ לִשְׁאוֹל זֶה עַל זֶה בַּמֶּה חָפֵץ
and the text specifically emphasizes "the deeds of the wicked," for certainly the Blessed Name takes no delight in wicked people, and it is unthinkable to question whether He delights in them;
אֲבָל הַחֹשֶׁךְ שֶׁהוּא מִכְּלַל בְּרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן ״בּוֹרֵא חֹשֶׁךְ״ (יְשַׁעְיָה מ״ה:ז׳), דְּכָךְ רָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה גַּם זֶה
but darkness which is part of the architecture of Creation—the Blessed Name being termed "the Creator of darkness" (Yeshayah 45:7), having willed that this too exist—
הֲרֵי רָאִינוּ דְּיֵשׁ חֵפֶץ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, זֶהוּ מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים
behold we see there is a divine purpose in the deeds of the wicked:
כִּי יֵשׁ צַדִּיקִים אֲשֶׁר מַגִּיעַ אֲלֵיהֶם כְּמַעֲשֵׂה הָרְשָׁעִים (קֹהֶלֶת ח:יד), כְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּנִסָּיוֹן דְּבַת שֶׁבַע
for there are righteous men who encounter circumstances resembling the deeds of the wicked (Koheles 8:14), like David HaMelech in the trial of Batsheva;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלִּבּוֹ הָיָה חָלָל בְּקִרְבּוֹ וְהָיָה צַדִּיק גָּמוּר, הִזְמִין לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַעֲשֵׂה רְשָׁעִים כְּדֵי לְהָקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה׳ עַמּוּד א׳)

where even though his heart was slain within him and he was a consummate tzaddik, the Blessed Name arranged for him an action resembling the wicked in order to establish the yoke of repentance for the multitude (Avodah Zarah 5a);
דְּדָבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי חֹשֶׁךְ הַקּוֹדֵם
for this revelation is impossible except through preceding darkness!
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בַּחֲגִיגָה (ט״ו עַמּוּד א׳), וְסוֹטָה (כ״ב עַמּוּד א׳), וּבְבָבָא בַּתְרָא (ט״ז עַמּוּד א׳): ״בָּרָאתָ צַדִּיקִים, בָּרָאתָ רְשָׁעִים״
And regarding this they stated in Chagigah (15a), Sotah (22a), and Bava Batra (16a): "You have created the righteous, You have created the wicked";
וַהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ (נִדָּה ט״ז עַמּוּד ב׳): ״צַדִּיק וְרָשָׁע — לָא קָאָמַר״
yet behold, they explicitly declared (Niddah 16b): "whether one will be righteous or wicked the angel does not decree"!
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת: ״בּוּצִין מִקַּטְפֵיהּ יְדִיעַ״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת מ״ח עַמּוּד א׳)
But in truth: "A cucumber is recognized from its initial blossom," as written in Berachos (48a);
וְיוּכְלוּ לְהַכִּיר גַּם בִּילָדִים, דְּיֵשׁ שֶׁתְּחִלַּת יְצִירָתוֹ בְּטֶבַע טוֹב לַהֲלוֹךְ בְּתֹם וָיֹשֶׁר, וְיֵשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ
and one can perceive even in young children that one is formed with an innate disposition to walk in simplicity and uprightness, while another has the opposite tendency;
וְהוּא בִּכְלַל ״חָכָם״ אוֹ ״טִפֵּשׁ״
this falling into the decreed category of "wise" or "foolish" (Niddah 16b);
דְּאֵין הַכַּוָּונָה בְּחָכְמָה אֱנוֹשִׁית, רַק חָכְמַת הָאֱמֶת לְהִתְנַהֵג כְּפִי הָרָאוּי מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה
for the intention refers not to mundane worldly intelligence, but to the wisdom of truth: behaving as is fitting according to holy wisdom.
וְאֵין זֶה עִנְיָן לִבְחִירַת צַדִּיק וְרָשָׁע
And this disposition does not coerce the moral choice of being righteous or wicked;

דְּגַם מִי שֶׁנִּבְרָא צַדִּיק יִצְרוֹ מִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו בְּכָל יוֹם, וְ״צוֹפֶה רָשָׁע לַצַּדִּיק וּמְבַקֵּשׁ לַהֲמִיתוֹ״ (תְּהִלִּים ל״ז:ל״ב; קִדּוּשִׁין ל׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) וּלְהַטּוֹתוֹ לְדֶרֶךְ הַמָּוֶת, וְהַבְּחִירָה בְּיָדוֹ

for even one born with a righteous nature faces a yetzer that overpowers him every day, where "the wicked watches the righteous, and seeks to slay him" (Tehillim 37:32; Kiddushin 30b), and the choice remains in his hands;
וְכֵן הַנִּבְרָא רָשָׁע, הַבְּחִירָה בְּיָדוֹ לִכְפּוֹת יֵצֶר לְבָבוֹ שֶׁבַּתּוֹלָדָה, וְלָשׁוּב אֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְלִזְכּוֹת לִמְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין
and likewise one born with a turbulent, wicked disposition has the free choice to subdue his inborn inclinations, returning unto the Blessed Name to merit the place where penitents stand;
וְאֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּא בִּטְרוּנְיָא עִם בְּרִיּוֹתָיו (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ג׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
for the Blessed Name does not act tyrannically with His creatures (Avodah Zarah 3a).
וְעַל כֵּן: ״כָּל הַגָּדוֹל מֵחֲבֵירוֹ — יִצְרוֹ גָּדוֹל הֵימֶנּוּ״ (סֻכָּה נ״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
And therefore: "Whoever is greater than his fellow, his yetzer is greater than he" (Sukkah 52a);
וְלָכֵן: צַדִּיקִים נִדְמֶה לָהֶן כְּהַר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם (סֻכָּה נ״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
and therefore: to the righteous the yetzer hara appears like a towering mountain, as written there (Sukkah 52a);
שֶׁהִתְגַּבְּרוּת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע עֲלֵיהֶם עָצוּם מְאֹד, מַקְבִּיל לְכֹחַ הַטּוֹב הָעֶצֶם שֶׁבָּהֶם בְּטֶבַע תּוֹלַדְתָּן
for the assault of the yetzer upon them is immensely fierce, corresponding symmetrically to the formidable innate goodness of their natural soul;
וְעַל כֵּן יוֹשְׁבִים וּבוֹכִים: ״הֵיאַךְ יָכֹלְנוּ לִכְבּוֹשׁ [הַר גָּבוֹהַּ כָּזֶה] וְכוּלֵיהּ״ (שָׁם)
wherefore in the Future they sit and weep: "How were we ever able to conquer so towering a mountain, etc.!" (ibid.);
וּבְכִיָּה זוֹ מַה טִיבָהּ, אַדְּרַבָּא הָיָה לָהֶם לִשְׂמוֹחַ שֶׁזָּכוּ לִכְפּוֹת הַר גָּדוֹל כָּזֶה
and what is the meaning of this weeping? On the contrary, should they not rejoice that they merited to conquer so mighty a mountain?
אֲבָל הַצַּדִּיקִים הֵם הַחוֹשְׁבִים שֶׁהוּא בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם
But the righteous are those who during life assumed that their victory was achieved through their own human striving;
וְאָז מַכִּירִים הָאֱמֶת דְּהֵם לֹא יָכְלוּ לִכְפּוֹת כְּלָל הַר גָּדוֹל אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ
and then, in the light of the Future, they perceive the truth: that they could never have conquered that great mountain were not the Holy One assisting them!
וּמַכִּירִים הָאֱמֶת דְּהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
Recognizing the ultimate truth that everything derives from the Blessed Name;
וְעַל כֵּן בּוֹכִים עַל טָעוּתָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְשֶׁלֹּא זָכוּ לְהַכִּיר זֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and therefore they weep over their mistaken presumption in this world, and that they did not merit to fully perceive this truth in this life;
שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגַת הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין:
which is the supreme attainment of the place where penitents stand!

8.h: The theme: Relying on one's own merit versus divine attribution, the Crown of a Good Name (Keser Shem Tov), and repentance through the first letter Hei. "Whoever hangs his deliverance upon his own merit, Heaven hangs it upon the merit of others" (Berachos 10b): when a person attributes spiritual attainment to his own striving, he remains separate from Hashem, so Heaven shows him that all is from Him; but when he nullifies himself and acknowledges that everything is from Hashem, Hashem attributes everything to him ("the earth He has given to the children of men", Tehillim 115:16). At the final judgment, the yetzer appears to the wicked as fine as a strand of hair (Sukkah 52a), and they weep because it was within their grasp to conquer it. The penitent who attains this brokenhearted weeping in his lifetime achieves the Crown of a Good Name (Keser Shem Tov) which transcends all crowns, issuing light directly out of darkness.
