This is the mystery of the halachic dissolution of vows (hatarat nedarim), which "hover in the air and have nothing to lean upon" (Chagigah 10a): while biblical verses support the law, the deepest halachot are derived from the crowns of the letters (kitrei otiyot) expounded by Rabbi Akiva (Menachos 29b), rooted in the white space and air (avir) between the written lines.

p: וְהָעִנְיָן: דְּהָאוֹתִיּוֹת נִקְרָאִים בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה (פֶּרֶק ד׳ מִשְׁנָה ט״ז) ״אֲבָנִים״, וְהַמִּלּוֹת הַנִּבְנוֹת מֵהָאוֹתִיּוֹת ״בָּתִּים״
And the explanation is: letters are designated in Sefer Yetzirah (4:16) "stones" (avanim), and the words constructed from the letters are termed "houses" (batim);
שֶׁהוּא בִּנְיָן קָבוּעַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם יְסוֹד קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּים
being an established edifice possessing a fixed and enduring foundation;
כִּי הֵם אוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ ״אֱמֶת״ (מִשְׁלֵי כ״ג:כ״ג), וּ״שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד״ (שָׁם י״ב:י״ט) כְּבִנְיָן קָבוּעַ, וְלֹא דָּבָר הַמִּטַּלְטֵל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ קְבִיעוּת וְקִיּוּם

for they are the letters of the Torah of which "truth" is written (Mishlei 23:23), and "the lip of truth shall be established forever" (ibid. 12:19) like a permanent structure, and not a movable object lacking stability.
וְעַל כֵּן אִיתָא בִּמְגִלָּה (ט״ז עַמּוּד ב׳): ״וֶאֱמֶת — שֶׁצְּרִיכָה שִׂרְטוּט כַּאֲמִתָּהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה״
Wherefore it is taught in Megillah (16b): "and the truth is that it requires scored lines (sirtut) like the truth of the Torah";
יִחֲסוּ זֶה לְמִדַּת הָאֲמִתּוּת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
the Sages attributing this requirement to the quality of absolute truth in the Torah;
כִּי גַּם הַשִּׁיטִין וְשׁוּרוֹת הָעַמּוּד הִמְשִׁילוּ לְבִנְיַן הַחוֹמָה, בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב שָׁם: ״אֲרִיחַ עַל גַּבֵּי לְבֵנָה וְכוּלֵיהּ״, עַיֵּין שָׁם
for the written lines and rows of a column they likewise compared to the construction of a masonry wall, in what is written there: "a half-brick over a brick, etc.," see there;
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא ״שׁוּרָה״ עַל שֵׁם הַחוֹמָה, שֶׁנִּקְרָא גַּם כֵּן ״שׁוּר״ בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב, וּבַאֲרַמִּי ״שׁוּרָא״
wherefore a line of text is called a shurah after a wall, which is termed shur in biblical Hebrew and shura in Aramaic;
שֶׁכְּמוֹ שֶׁמִּלָּה אַחַת נִקְרָא ״בַּיִת״, כֵּן כָּל הַשּׁוּרָה נִקְרָא ״חוֹמָה״
so that just as a single word is termed a "house," so the entire line is termed a "wall";
וְעַל כֵּן צָרִיךְ שִׂרְטוּט, שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה אֶחָד יוֹצֵא וְאֶחָד נִכְנָס
and therefore scored lines are required, so that one letter does not protrude outward and another recede inward;
דְּאָז אֵינוֹ דּוּגְמַת חוֹמָה הַקְּבוּעָה, רַק כָּל אוֹת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ כְּדָבָר הַמִּטַּלְטֵל וְלֹא הַקָּבוּעַ וְקַיָּים
for then it would not resemble a sturdy wall, each letter standing isolated like a loose, movable object lacking permanence;
וּכְאַאֲמִתּוּת שֶׁל תּוֹרָה הוּא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה ״קְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא״ לָעַד
and like the truth of the Torah which is established and enduring forever;
עַל כֵּן צָרִיךְ שִׂרְטוּט שֶׁיִּהְיוּ קְבוּעִים בְּיוֹשֶׁר כְּמִשְׁפַּט הַקְּבוּעוֹת
therefore scored lines are necessary so that letters be fixed in upright alignment according to the rule of permanent structures.
וְהַלָּמֶ״ד הוּא בּוֹלֵט וְיוֹצֵא מִן הַשִּׂרְטוּט, וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא ״מִגְדָּל״ — לֹא אֶבֶן וּבַיִת
But the letter Lamed
protrudes and ascends beyond the scored line, wherefore it is termed a "tower"—not an ordinary stone or house;
דְּהַמִּגְדָּל הוּא הַמִּיטַּלְטֵל מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם וְאֵינוֹ קָבוּעַ
for a wooden tower is an object that moves from place to place and is not permanently fixed;
וְהַיְינוּ גַּגּוֹ שֶׁל לָמֶ״ד, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתַב הֶ״עָרוּךְ״
this referring to the ascending roof of the Lamed, as the Aruch wrote;
כִּי גוּפוֹ צָרִיךְ שֶׁלֹּא יֵצֵא מִשִּׂרְטוּט כְּכָל הָאוֹתִיּוֹת
for its lower body must align within the scored line like all other letters;
וְנִמְצָא הַגַּג יֵשׁ לוֹ סְמִיכָה לְמַטָּה עַל הָאוֹת
and thus the ascending roof has a firm base below upon the body of the letter.
אֲבָל קְבִיעוּת כָּל הָאוֹתִיּוֹת הוּא בַּשִּׂרְטוּט שֶׁל מַעְלָה, וּמִלְּמַטָּה אֵין צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ שָׁוִין כְּלָל
However, the fixed alignment of all standard letters is anchored at the upper scored line, while below they need not be aligned at all;
דְּאֵין הַקְּבִיעוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם מִצַּד מַטָּה, דְּהַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַמְקַבְּלִים הַשְׁפָּעָתָם
for their permanence does not derive from below, namely from the human recipients of their divine influx;
דְּבָזֶה אֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה בְּכָל מָקוֹם וּבְכָל זְמַן וּבְכָל נֶפֶשׁ, וְהַכֹּל כְּפִי עֵרֶךְ הַמְקַבֵּל
for below, reception is not uniform across every space, time, and soul, but varies according to the capacity of the recipient;
וּפְעָמִים ״נָהָר יֶחֱרַב וְיָבֵשׁ״ (אִיּוֹב י״ד:י״א) חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, הַשְׁפָּעַת אֵיזֶה אוֹת לְאֵיזֶה נֶפֶשׁ אִם פָּגַם בּוֹ
and sometimes "the river fails and dries up" (Iyov 14:11), God forbid, withholding the influx of a specific letter unto a soul if he blemished it;
אֲבָל קְבִיעוּתָם הַקַּיָּים לָעַד הוּא בְּעִנְיַן עַצְמוּתָם וְקַבָּלַת שִׁפְעָם מִלְּמַעְלָה
but their eternal permanence resides in their essential nature and their reception of divine influx from Above;
דְּהַתּוֹרָה נִצְחִיּוּת שֶׁהִיא תּוֹרַת אֱמֶת, הַיּוֹצֵאת מֵאֲמִיתָּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ הַבִּלְתִּי בַּעַל תַּכְלִית שֶׁאֵין לוֹ הֶפְסֵק
for the Torah is eternal truth flowing from His infinite truth, blessed be His Name, which knows no cessation.
וְגַגּוֹ שֶׁל לָמֶ״ד הוּא לְהֵיפֶךְ: יֵשׁ לוֹ קְבִיעוּת לְמַטָּה וְלֹא לְמַעְלָה
And the roof of the Lamed is the exact reverse: it possesses a base below, but no upper limit above;
שֶׁהוּא הָעוֹמֵד עַל גַּבֵּי הָאוֹת וּמַשְׁפִּיעַ לָאוֹת, אֲבָל אֵין לוֹ קְבִיעוּת לְמַעְלָה אִם יַאֲרִיךְ אוֹ יְקַצֵּר
standing above the letter and channeling influx into the letter, yet having no fixed measure above whether it extends long or short;
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ כִּתְרֵי אוֹתִיּוֹת וְהַתָּגִין שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי הָאוֹתִיּוֹת דְּגַם כֵּן אֵין לָהֶם קְבִיעוּת לְמַעְלָה
resembling the crowns and tagin atop the letters which likewise have no upper ceiling;
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם אֵינָם מִגּוּף הָאוֹת... וְהַכֶּתֶר כָּךְ הוּא קְבִיעוּתוֹ לִהְיוֹת עוֹמֵד עַל גַּבֵּי הָרֹאשׁ
except that the tagin are not part of the letter's essential body, a crown being designed to rest atop the head;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא כֶּתֶר וְעוֹמֵד לְמַעְלָה, אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא נִטְפָּל לְהַגּוּף הַנִּכְתָּר, וּקְבִיעוּתוֹ הוּא בִּקְבִיעַת הַגּוּף
and even though the crown stands above, it is secondary to the crowned body, its position being fixed by the body;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן גַּג הַלָּמֶ״ד שֶׁהוּא מִגּוּפוֹ שֶׁל אוֹת, וְאֵין הָאוֹת נִשְׁלָם כְּלָל עֲדַיִין שָׁם בְּגוּפוֹ שֶׁל מַטָּה אֵצֶל הַשִּׂרְטוּט
whereas the roof of the Lamed is of the very body of the letter, the letter being completely unfinished in its lower body near the scored line;
רַק כּוּלּוֹ עִם הַגַּג אוֹת אֶחָד, עַל כֵּן כּוּלּוֹ אֵין לוֹ קְבִיעוּת עַל יְדֵי הַגַּג
but the entire ascender together with the base forms a single letter, wherefore the entire letter is liberated from upper limitation through its roof;
וְזֶהוּ הַפְּרִיחָה בָּאֲוִיר, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (חֲגִיגָה י׳ עַמּוּד א׳): ״הֶיתֵּר נְדָרִים — פּוֹרְחִין בָּאֲוִיר וְאֵין לָהֶם עַל מַה שֶּׁיִּסְמוֹכוּ״
and this is the "hovering in the air," after the manner stated in Chagigah (10a): "The dissolution of vows hovers in the air and has nothing to lean upon";
פֵּירֵשׁ רַשִׁ״י שֶׁהוּא מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, וְרֶמֶז מוּעָט בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
Rashi explaining: it derives from the Oral Torah, having merely a faint hint in the Written Torah.
וְאֵין הַכַּוָּונָה בְּרֶמֶז זֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא מִקְּרָא דְּ״הוּא אֵינוֹ מוֹחֵל וְכוּלֵיהּ״ (חֲגִיגָה י׳ עַמּוּד א׳) וְכַיּוֹצֵא בוֹ

And the intention of this "faint hint" does not refer to the scriptural derivations cited in the Gemara: "he shall not break his word—he cannot dissolve, but others can dissolve for him," and the like;
דְּהָנֵי מַאן דְּאָמְרֵי סְבִירָא לְהוּ ״יֵשׁ לָהֶם עַל מַה שֶּׁיִּסְמוֹכוּ״, עַיֵּין שָׁם בַּגְּמָרָא
for those authorities explicitly hold that "they do have what to lean upon," see in the Gemara there;
דְּכָל דְּרָשׁ מִלְּשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב, הֲרֵי יֵשׁ לוֹ סָמַךְ בַּכְּתָב
for any exposition derived from the biblical text has a textual support in script;
אֲבָל הַפְּרִיחָה בָּאֲוִיר הוּא מַה שֶּׁאֵין לוֹ רֶמֶז דְּרָשׁ בְּגוּפוֹ שֶׁל כְּתָב
but "hovering in the air" signifies that which possesses no textual hermeneutic in the body of the script;
אֶלָּא רְמִיזָא בְּעָלְמָא בְּכִתְרֵי אוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דּוֹרֵשׁ (מְנָחוֹת כ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
but merely an ethereal allusion within the crowns of the letters which Rabbi Akiva expounded (Menachos 29b);
שֶׁכְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה י״ח:כ״א): דִּבְלוּחוֹת בֵּין דִּבּוּר לְדִבּוּר הָיוּ כָּל מִצְוֹתֶיהָ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה
for just as the Sages stated (Bamidbar Rabbah 18:21): on the Tablets of the Covenant, between each commandment were inscribed all the detailed mitzvos of the Torah;
כָּךְ בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב בֵּין שִׁיטָה לְשִׁיטָה רָמוּז כָּל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כּוּלָּהּ
so within the Written Torah, between line and line is hinted the entire Oral Torah;
וְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁתַּלְמִיד וָתִיק עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֵּאָה פֶּרֶק ב׳ הֲלָכָה ד׳), דְּלֵיכָּא מִידֵי דְּלָא רְמִיזֵי בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא (תַּעֲנִית ט׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
and everything that a veteran disciple is destined to innovate, for there is nothing that is not hinted in the Torah;
הַכֹּל רָמוּז בָּאֲוִיר שֶׁבֵּינְתַיִים, בַּתָּגִין וְכִתְרֵי הָאוֹתִיּוֹת וְכַיּוֹצֵא
all is hinted within the intervening air, within the tagin and crowns of the letters;
וְזֶהוּ כַּוָּונַת הַלָּשׁוֹן ״פּוֹרְחִין בָּאֲוִיר״: הַיְינוּ הָאֲוִיר שֶׁבֵּין הַכְּתָב:
and this is the true meaning of the phrase "hovering in the air": namely, the white air between the written lines!

12.h: The theme: The fixed body of the Written Torah versus the soaring heights of the Oral Torah and the letter Lamed. The body of the script is the permanent structure built by the King of the Universe, its divine influx descending equally unto all mortals; hence the Written Torah is accessible and open to all (ketivah u-menacha). In contrast, the Oral Torah was entrusted to the Sages to innovate each according to his intellect; from the perspective of the human recipient, its insights flash in the mind like a soaring flight without fixed permanence, appearing and disappearing. In the dissolution of vows, the prohibition of the vow is biblically fixed and accessible to all ("he shall do according to all that proceeds out of his mouth", Bamidbar 30:3); but its release requires the wisdom of an expert scholar (yachid mumcheh) or three laymen who form a court (Sanhedrin 3a) to discover a novel opening (pesach), wherefore the Torah left it "hovering in the air." The letter Lamed is an integral letter of the written alphabet, yet it soars as a tower higher than an ordinary house. Lamed denotes learning (limud), whence flows the study and vitality of the Oral Torah. "The words of the Scribes are more beloved than the wine of the Torah" (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2), for while the Written Torah is prophetic perception (like Moshe Rabbeinu), "a sage is superior to a prophet" (Bava Batra 12a), grasping through the Holy Spirit (Ruach HaKodesh) the supernal Chochmah above the Written Torah (which is merely the fallen fruit of higher wisdom, Bereishis Rabbah 17:5). Prophecy is bounded and fixed by divine decree; the Holy Spirit of the Oral Torah, though hovering without a visible foundation, soars boundlessly like the neck of the Lamed, ascending above all cosmic limitations into the infinite will of the Creator.

p: וְגוּפוֹ שֶׁל כְּתָב הוּא בִּנְיָן הַקָּבוּעַ וְקַיָּים שֶׁבָּנָה וְקָבַע מַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
And the body of the script is the established and permanent edifice that the King of the Universe built and established;
וְהַהַשְׁפָּעָה מִצִּידּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּקְבִיעוּת שָׁוֶה
and the divine influx from His side descends in uniform permanence;
עַל כֵּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב כְּתִיבָא וּמַנָּחָא לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם (קִדּוּשִׁין ס״ו עַמּוּד א׳)
wherefore the Written Torah is written and laid open for all who enter the world (Kiddushin 66a);
וְהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא מַה שֶּׁנִּמְסַר לַחֲכָמִים לְחַדֵּשׁ וּלְהַשִּׂיג, כָּל אֶחָד כְּפִי כֹּחוֹ וְחָכְמָתוֹ
whereas the Oral Torah is that which was entrusted unto the Sages to innovate and grasp, each according to his capacity and wisdom;
וּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ חָכָם אֵין מַשִּׂיג וּמְחַדֵּשׁ כְּלוּם
and one who is not wise perceives and innovates nothing;
וְכָל הַהַשָּׂגָה הוּא מִצַּד הַמְקַבֵּל, וּמִצִּידּוֹ אֵין לוֹ קְבִיעוּת
and the entire perception operates from the side of the recipient, possessing from his vantage no fixed stability;
וַאֲפִילּוּ לְאוֹתוֹ הַמַּשִּׂיג, הַהַשָּׂגָה הִיא דֶּרֶךְ פְּרִיחָה בַּשֵּׂכֶל בְּלֹא קְבִיעוּת, פַּעַם נִגְלֶה וּפַעַם נֶעְלָם
and even for that perceptive master, the comprehension flashes through the intellect like a soaring flight without static permanence, now revealed and now concealed.
וְהֶיתֵּר נְדָרִים, אַף שֶׁהוּא הֲלָכָה מְקֻבֶּלֶת וְלֹא מֵחִדּוּשׁ חֲכָמִים
And the dissolution of vows, although it is an established halachah received by tradition and not an arbitrary rabbinic innovation;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוֹאִיל וְהַדָּבָר נִמְסַר לַחֲכָמִים לִהְיוֹת לְשׁוֹנָם מַרְפֵּא וְשֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְהַתִּיר מַה שֶּׁאָסְרָה תּוֹרָה, וְאֵין בָּזֶה הֲלָכָה קְבוּעָה
nevertheless, since the matter was entrusted to the Sages that their tongue be healing, empowered to release that which the Torah prohibited without a rigid statutory formula;
וְאֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה לְגוּפוֹ שֶׁל נֶדֶר: אִם יִרְצֶה יֶאֱסוֹר עַל עַצְמוֹ, דְּזֶה מָסוּר לְכָל אֶחָד וְאֵין צָרִיךְ חָכְמָה כְּלָל
and it is not comparable to the taking of a vow, where if a person wills he can forbid an object upon himself, which is accessible to anyone without requiring wisdom;
וְאִם כֵּן אֵין אִיסּוּרוֹ מִצַּד כֹּחוֹ וְחָכְמָתוֹ, אֶלָּא מִצַּד הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁקָּבְעָה עָלָיו דְּ״כְּכָל הַיֹּצֵא מִפִּיו יַעֲשֶׂה״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר ל:ג), ״לֹא יַחֵל [דְּבָרוֹ]״ (שָׁם)

and if so, the prohibition does not stem from human wisdom, but from the Torah which decreed: "he shall do according to all that proceeds out of his mouth; he shall not break his word" (Bamidbar 30:3);
וְשַׁפִּיר נִכְתַּב אִיסּוּרוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה בְּהֶדְיָא, וְיֵשׁ לוֹ עַל מַה לִסְמוֹךְ
and properly was its prohibition recorded explicitly in the Torah, having solid ground upon which to lean;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַהֶיתֵּר דְּתָלוּי בְּחָכְמָה, שֶׁהֲרֵי נִמְסַר לַחֲכָמִים: יָחִיד מוּמְחֶה דַּוְוקָא אוֹ הֶדְיוֹטוֹת שְׁלֹשָׁה דַּוְוקָא
whereas the dissolution depends upon wisdom, having been committed unto the Sages: exclusively an ordained expert (yachid mumcheh) or three laymen (Bechoros 36b);
שֶׁהֵם בֵּית דִּין לְכָל דָּבָר הַצָּרִיךְ בֵּית דִּין, דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר דְּלֵיכָּא חַד דִּגְמִיר (סַנְהֶדְרִין ג׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
who constitute a rabbinical court for all judicial matters, it being impossible that at least one of them is not learned (Sanhedrin 3a);
וְיֵשׁ בָּהֶם חָכְמָה, וְתָלוּי כְּפִי הַשָּׂגַת חָכְמַת הַמַּתִּירִים
they possessing wisdom, dissolution depending upon the depth of the resolving scholars;
דְּהֶחָכָם יוֹתֵר יוּכַל לִמְצוֹא פֶּתַח לַנֶּדֶר מַה שֶּׁאֵין אַחֵר יָכוֹל לִמְצוֹא
for a greater sage can uncover an opening of regret for a vow which another could never detect;
דְּעַל כֵּן הָיוּ הוֹלְכִים לַחֲכָמִים לְבַקֵּשׁ פֶּתַח, וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּנְדָרִים
wherefore people would travel to the Sages to seek an opening, as recorded throughout Nedarim;
וְעַל כֵּן הִשְׁאִירַתּוּ תוֹרָה ״פּוֹרֵחַ בָּאֲוִיר״, שֶׁכֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּמְסַר לַחֲכָמִים, מִצַּד הַשָּׂגַת הַחֲכָמִים אֵין לוֹ קְבִיעוּת
therefore the Torah left it "hovering in the air," for having been entrusted to the Sages, from the perspective of human perception it has no fixed boundary.
וְהַלָּמֶ״ד הוּא גּוּף אוֹת שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְגַם כֵּן אֵין לוֹ קְבִיעוּת וּפוֹרֵחַ בָּאֲוִיר
And the letter Lamed is an integral letter of the written alphabet, yet it too possesses no upper boundary, hovering in the air;
רַק שֶׁהוּא ״מִגְדָּל הַפּוֹרֵחַ״, לִהְיוֹתוֹ אוֹת גָּמוּר דִּכְתָב הַבּוֹנֶה בַּיִת, וְזֶה מִגְדָּל הַגָּבוֹהַּ מִבַּיִת כְּמַשְׁמָעוּת ״מִגְדָּל״ בְּכָל מָקוֹם
except that it is a "soaring tower," being a complete letter of script that builds a word/house, yet stands as a tower soaring higher than a house as the term migdal implies everywhere;
וְכֵן הַמִּגְדָּל דְּדוֹר הַפַּלָּגָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״א:ד׳)
and so the tower of the Generation of Dispersion (Bereishis 11:4);
וְ״לָמֶ״ד״ הוּא לְשׁוֹן לִימּוּד, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הוּא הַלִּימּוּד וְהַיְנִיקָה דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and Lamed
signifies learning (limud), whence derives the study and sustenance of the Oral Torah;
וְ״חֲבִיבִים דִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים יוֹתֵר מִיֵּינָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה״ (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ל״ה עַמּוּד א׳; שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה א:ב)
and "the words of the Scribes are more beloved than the wine of the Torah" (Avodah Zarah 35a; Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2);
כִּי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הוּא הַשָּׂגַת הַנְּבוּאָה מִנָּבִיא גָּדוֹל כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, וְ״חָכָם עָדִיף מִנָּבִיא״ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא י״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
for the Written Torah is prophetic perception through a supreme prophet like Moshe Rabbeinu, yet "a sage is superior to a prophet" (Bava Batra 12a);
כִּי הוּא מַשִּׂיג בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ מִקּוֹדֶשׁ הָעֶלְיוֹן חָכְמָה עִילָּאָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, שֶׁהִיא ״נוֹבְלוֹת חָכְמָה עֶלְיוֹנָה״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה י״ז:ה׳)
for the sage grasps through the Holy Spirit from supernal holiness the supreme Chochmah which transcends the Written Torah (which is merely the fallen fruit of higher wisdom, Bereishis Rabbah 17:5);
וְכִידוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִיזַ״ל בְּ״שַׁעַר הַנְּבוּאָה״ בִּנְבוּאַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מֵאֵיזֶה מָקוֹם הָיָה
and as known from the Arizal in Sha'ar HaNevu'ah regarding the cosmic source of Moshe's prophecy;
וְהוּא גִּילָּה רָזֵי עוֹלָמוֹת הָעֶלְיוֹנִים יוֹתֵר
the sage revealing mysteries of even higher spiritual worlds;
וְלֹא שֶׁמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא הָיָה מַשִּׂיג מַה שֶּׁהוּא הִשִּׂיג
and not that Moshe Rabbeinu did not grasp what the sage grasped;
דִּבְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ וַדַּאי הָיָה מַשִּׂיג, וְנִגְלָה לוֹ כָּל מַה שֶּׁתַּלְמִיד וָתִיק עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ
for through the Holy Spirit Moshe certainly grasped it, having revealed to him everything that a veteran disciple would innovate;
וְזֶהוּ הַשָּׂגַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁמִּצַּד הַחָכְמָה וּבִינַת הַלֵּב
this being the comprehension of the Oral Torah through wisdom and the understanding of the heart;
אֲבָל בִּנְבוּאָה מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֶרְאָה וְגִילָּה לוֹ כְּדֶרֶךְ הַשָּׂגַת הַנְּבִיאִים, זֶה לֹא נִגְלָה לוֹ רַק כְּפִי מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ
but in prophecy, that which the Blessed Name revealed to him after the manner of prophets, was revealed strictly according to its bounded level.
וְהַשָּׂגַת הַנְּבוּאָה גְּדוֹלָה מִצַּד שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ יְסוֹד עַל מַה לִסְמוֹךְ
And the perception of prophecy is immense because it possesses an absolute foundation upon which to lean;
שֶׁהִיא דְּבַר ה׳ אֲשֶׁר עָלָיו אֵין לְהוֹסִיף וְלֹא לִגְרוֹעַ (דְּבָרִים י״ג:א׳), וְהֵם דְּבָרִים קְצוּבִים וּקְבוּעִים וְקַיָּימִים
being the word of Hashem to which nothing can be added or diminished (Devarim 13:1), which are measured, fixed, and enduring words;
וּמִצַּד זֶה הַשָּׂגַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁל חַכְמֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה גְּדוֹלָה
while from another vantage the Holy Spirit of the sages of the Oral Torah is greater:
שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁפּוֹרַחַת בָּאֲוִיר, כִּי אֵין לָהּ יְסוֹד קָבוּעַ לִסְמוֹךְ עָלָיו בְּבֵירוּר לָדַעַת שֶׁהוּא דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים וְשֶׁהֵן הֵן הַדְּבָרִים הַנֶּאֱמָרִים בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
for although it hovers in the air, lacking a rigid textual anchor to verify with certainty that it is the words of the Living God spoken in the Holy Spirit,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁהוּא מוֹצִיאָם מֵחָכְמַת לִבּוֹ וְאוּלַי טוֹעֶה בְּדִמְיוֹנוֹ
since the sage draws them from the wisdom of his heart and might err in imagination;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם נֶגֶד זֶה הַלָּמֶ״ד גָּבוֹהַּ גָּבוֹהַּ מִכָּל הָאוֹתִיּוֹת
nevertheless, countering this vulnerability, the Lamed soars high, higher than all the letters;
שֶׁהַשָּׂגָתוֹ בְּלֹא קֶצֶב וּגְבוּל
its perception knowing no measure or boundary;
וּלְמַעְלָה מִכָּל שֶׁפַע הַהַשָּׂגָה הַנִּקְצָב בִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּבְרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁהָיָה בָּאוֹתִיּוֹת, שֶׁהֵם הַמַּגְבִּילוֹת כָּל דָּבָר:
and elevated far above all the influx of perception measured out by the will of the Blessed Name in the creation of the world through letters, which limit and define all things!

12.h: The theme: The letter Lamed as king of the letters, the heart as sovereign of the body, and the dual nature of royalty (boundary versus boundless breach). In Otiyot d'Rabbi Akiva, the letter Lamed stands tallest because it is like a king positioned in the center of the alphabet, alluding to the heart which is sovereign over the organs (Sefer Yetzirah 6:3). Malchus is the mouth, the Oral Torah (Torah she-b'al Peh), through which "by me kings reign" (Mishlei 8:15). A king embodies two extremes: on one hand, "a king by justice establishes the land" (Mishlei 29:4), rigorously contracting (tzimtzum) his realm with statutory boundaries (dina d'malchuta), for without a sovereign "each man does what is right in his own eyes" (Shoftim 17:6); on the other hand, regarding his royal prerogatives, "a king may breach a fence to make a pathway and none may protest" (Bava Batra 100b; Sanhedrin 20b), reflecting the boundless expansion of initial Thought wedged in the final deed (ne'utzan techilatan b'sofan). Scripture asks: "Have you been appointed to rebuke a king?" (cf. II Divrei HaYamim 25:16). While ordinary mortals are rebuked as equals ("you shall surely rebuke your neighbor", Vayikra 19:17), a king cannot forgo his honor (Kiddushin 32b) and his awe must remain upon all. The esoteric reason one cannot easily rebuke a king is that a monarch possesses a profound depth of understanding in his heart (Binah she-ba-lev), at times compelling him to act outside normative boundaries for the sake of Heaven (es la'asos la-Hashem hefeiru Torasecha, Tehillim 119:126). His heart is unfathomable ("the heart of kings is unsearchable", Mishlei 25:3), yet out of his profound responsibility comes extreme awe: "once a king bows, he does not straighten again" (Berachos 34b). This is the "tower hovering in the air" (migdal ha-pore'ach ba-avir): holy awe fears even in good deeds lest subtle defect remain; yet when awe precedes wisdom, wisdom is sustained, becoming "a tower of strength into which the righteous runs and is exalted" (Mishlei 18:10), running with unhindered confidence because his heart is firmly anchored in Hashem.

p: וּבְ״אוֹתִיּוֹת דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא״ אִיתָא: לָמָּה לָמֶ״ד גָּבוֹהַּ — שֶׁהוּא כְּמֶלֶךְ בָּאוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁהוּא בְּאֶמְצָעָם
And in Otiyot d'Rabbi Akiva it is taught: Why is the letter Lamed tall? Because it is like a king among the letters, situated in their middle;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אִיתָא שָׁם שֶׁרוֹמֵז לַלֵּב
and subsequently it is taught there that Lamed alludes to the heart;
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ ״הַלֵּב מֶלֶךְ בַּגּוּף״ כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה (פֶּרֶק ו׳ מִשְׁנָה ג׳)
which matches "the heart is king over the body" as written in Sefer Yetzirah (6:3);
וּ״מַלְכוּת — פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרִינַן לַהּ״, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ תִּקּוּן ק״ז (תִּקּוּנֵי זֹוהַר)
and "Malchus is the mouth, the Oral Torah we call it," as written at the start of Tikkun 17 (Tikkunei Zohar);
דְּ״בִי מְלָכִים יִמְלֹכוּ״ (מִשְׁלֵי ח:טו), הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
for "by me kings reign" (Mishlei 8:15), meaning through the wisdom of the Oral Torah;
דְּ״הַמֶּלֶךְ פּוֹרֵץ [גָּדֵר לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ] וְכוּלֵיהּ וְאֵין מוֹחִין בְּיָדוֹ״ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ק׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
where "a king may breach a fence to make a pathway for himself and none may protest" (Bava Batra 100b),
שֶׁהוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת בְּלֹא גְּבוּל
this representing boundless expansion;
כִּי הַסּוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁשָּׁם תַּכְלִית הַצִּמְצוּם, נָעוּץ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה שֶׁמִּשָּׁם מְקוֹר הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת
for the final deed, wherein lies the ultimate contraction (tzimtzum), is wedged in the initial Thought whence flows the source of all expansion.
וְהַמֶּלֶךְ אֲשֶׁר ״בְּמִשְׁפָּט יַעֲמִיד אָרֶץ״ (מִשְׁלֵי כ״ט:ד׳), לְצַמְצֵם מְדִינָתוֹ לִהְיוֹת הַכֹּל בִּגְבוּל
And the king who "by justice establishes the land" (Mishlei 29:4), contracts his realm so that all functions within strict boundaries;
דִּכְשֶׁאֵין מֶלֶךְ ״אִישׁ הַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו יַעֲשֶׂה״ (שׁוֹפְטִים כ״א:כ״ה)
for when there is no king "every man does that which is right in his own eyes" (Shoftim 21:25);
וּמִדַּת ״דִּינָא דְּמַלְכוּתָא״ הוּא לְצַמְצֵם הַנְהָגַת אוֹתָם שֶׁתַּחְתָּיו
and the judicial principle of the "law of the kingdom" (dina d'malchuta) is to restrict and regulate the conduct of his subjects;
וּבְנוֹגֵעַ לְצָרְכּוֹ הוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת, דְּכָל הָאָמוּר בְּפָרָשַׁת מֶלֶךְ — מֶלֶךְ מוּתָּר בּוֹ (סַנְהֶדְרִין כ׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
while regarding his royal needs he possesses absolute expansion, for whatever is stated in the biblical chapter of the king (I Shmuel 8), a king is permitted to practice (Sanhedrin 20b);
וְנֶאֱמַר: ״הַלְהוֹכֵחַ לַמֶּלֶךְ נְתָנוּךָ״ (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ב כ״ה:ט״ז), דִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ נִרְאֶה שֶׁאֵין לְהוֹכִיחַ הַמֶּלֶךְ
and it is said: "Have you been made of the king's counsel to rebuke him?" (II Divrei HaYamim 25:16), whose plain sense indicates that a king is not to be rebuked;
וְאוּלַי דָּרְשׁוּ: ״הוֹכֵחַ תּוֹכִיחַ אֶת עֲמִיתֶךָ״ (וַיִּקְרָא י״ט:י״ז) דַּוְוקָא, וּמֶלֶךְ אֵין קָרוּי עֲמִיתְךָ שֶׁאֵימָתוֹ עָלֶיךָ
and perhaps they expounded: "you shall surely rebuke your fellow (amitecha)" (Vayikra 19:17) specifically, whereas a king is not called your equal (amitecha), his awe being upon you;
וְאַף עַל פִּי דְּגַם תַּלְמִיד לְרַב נִתְרַבָּה
and even though the obligation of rebuke was extended to a disciple rebuking his teacher;
אֶפְשָׁר סָבְרֵי דְּרַב יָכוֹל לִמְחוֹל עַל כְּבוֹדוֹ (קִדּוּשִׁין ל״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
one can say: a Torah teacher has the prerogative to forgo his honor (Kiddushin 32a),
וְכֵיוָן דִּבְיָדוֹ לִמְחוֹל וְיוּכַל לִהְיוֹת עֲמִיתוֹ קָרִינַן בֵּיהּ עֲמִיתְךָ
and since it is within his power to forgo his honor and become his fellow's equal, we apply unto him the term amitecha;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מֶלֶךְ, דִּלְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין כְּבוֹדוֹ מָחוּל, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (ל״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
unlike a king, regarding whom according to all opinions his royal honor cannot be waived, as written in Kiddushin (32a);
וּמִיהוּ לְשׁוֹן ״נְתָנוּךָ״ מַשְׁמָע דְּצָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת אָדָם גָּדוֹל וּמְיוּחָד לָזֶה לְמַעֲלָתוֹ, וְאוֹתוֹ לֹא נְתָנוּהוּ וּמִינּוּהוּ עַל זֶה
however, the phrasing "have they appointed you" implies that one must be uniquely distinguished in stature for this, and this individual was not commissioned for it;
וְאוּלַי רָצָה לוֹמַר נְתָנוּךָ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם, דְּהַנְּבִיאִים הָיוּ מוֹכִיחִים הַמְּלָכִים בִּדְבַר ה׳ וְלֹא מֵעַצְמוֹ
and perhaps it means: were you appointed from Heaven? For the prophets rebuked kings strictly by the explicit word of Hashem and not from their own initiative.
אֲבָל קִבַּלְתִּי הַפֵּירוּשׁ: כִּי הַמֶּלֶךְ יֵשׁ לוֹ עֹומֶק בַּבִּינָה שֶׁבְּלִבּוֹ מַה שֶּׁלֹּא נִגְלָה לְאָדָם אַחֵר
But I received the true explanation: a king possesses an unfathomable depth of Binah within his heart that is not revealed to any other person;
עַד שֶׁמֵּחֲמָתוֹ מוּכְרָח פְּעָמִים לַעֲבוֹר עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה עַל דֶּרֶךְ ״עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת [לַה׳ הֵפֵרוּ תוֹרָתֶךָ]״ (תְּהִלִּים קי״ט:קכו)
so that on account of it he is sometimes compelled to bypass words of Torah in the manner of: "It is time to act for Hashem; they have made void Your law" (Tehillim 119:126);
וְאֵין יָכוֹל לְהוֹכִיחוֹ אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לִמְקוֹמוֹ וּמַדְרֵיגָתוֹ וְיוֹדֵעַ מַעֲמַקֵּי לְבָבוֹ
and none can rebuke him except one who has reached his spiritual station and perceives the inner depths of his heart;
וְהַכֹּל מִצַּד הַדְּבֵיקוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לִבּוֹ עִם עֹומֶק רֵאשִׁית דְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַנֶּעְלָם מֵעֵין כֹּל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
all this flowing from the cleaving of his heart's depths unto the primordial depth of divine Thought concealed from all in this world;
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה יָכוֹל לִפְרוֹץ כָּל הַגְּדָרִים וְהַגְּבוּלִים, כִּי יֵשׁ לוֹ תַּכְלִית הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת בְּלִי גְּבוּל
and from this aspect he is empowered to breach all fences and boundaries, possessing absolute, boundless expansion;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״[שָׁמַיִם לָרוּם וָאָרֶץ לָעֹמֶק] וְלֵב מְלָכִים אֵין חֵקֶר״ (מִשְׁלֵי כ״ה:ג׳)
as it is said: "The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings is unsearchable" (Mishlei 25:3);
וּמִצַּד צִמְצוּמוֹ בָּא לוֹ תֹּקֶף הַיִּרְאָה יוֹתֵר מִכָּל אָדָם
while from the perspective of his contraction comes an intensity of awe surpassing that of any other mortal,
כְּמָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ל״ד עַמּוּד ב׳): ״מֶלֶךְ כֵּיוָן שֶׁכָּרַע — שׁוּב אֵינוֹ זוֹקֵף״
as the Sages stated in Berachos (34b): "once a king bows in prayer, he does not straighten again until he finishes";
וְהוּא מִצַּד עֹוצֶם יִרְאַת ה׳ הַחוֹפְפוֹ
this deriving from the immense awe of Hashem that envelops him.
וְזֶה נִקְרָא ״דְּפָרַח בַּאֲוִירָא״
And this is what is termed "hovering in the air";
שֶׁהַיָּרֵא אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם דָּבָר מְבוֹרָר לִסְמוֹךְ עָלָיו
for one who truly fears has no tangible earthly pillar upon which to lean;
דִּבְכָל דָּבָר יָרֵא וְרוֹעֵד, אֲפִילּוּ בְּמַעֲשֶׂה הַטּוֹב בְּבֵירוּר, אוּלַי יֵשׁ אֵיזֶה פְּגָם וְחִסָּרוֹן
trembling in all matters, even in an undeniably good deed, lest there lurk some hidden blemish or deficiency;
בְּאֹפֶן שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם יְסוֹד לִהְיוֹת לְרַגְל אֲחִיזָה וּסְמִיכָה בּוֹ
in such a manner that he possesses no firm foothold to lean upon below;
וְזֶהוּ יִרְאָתוֹ הַקּוֹדֶמֶת לְחָכְמָתוֹ (אָבוֹת ג:ט), דְּ״רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה — יִרְאַת ה׳״ (תְּהִלִּים קי״א:י׳)
and this is his awe preceding his wisdom (Avos 3:9), for "the beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem" (Tehillim 111:10);
וְאַחַר כָּךְ עַל יְדֵי זֶה חָכְמָתוֹ מִתְקַיֶּימֶת
and subsequently through this his wisdom is preserved;
וְ״הַחָכְמָה תָּעֹז לֶחָכָם״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:יט), וְנַעֲשָׂה ״מִגְדַּל עֹז״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ח:י׳) אֲשֶׁר ״בּוֹ יָרוּץ צַדִּיק [וְנִשְׂגָּב]״ (שָׁם)
and "wisdom strengthens the wise" (Koheles 7:19), becoming "a tower of strength" (Mishlei 18:10) into which "the righteous runs, and is set on high";
הָרִיצָה הוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת בְּאֵין מַעְצוֹר
the "running" representing expansion without restraint;
כִּי ״נָכוֹן לִבּוֹ בָּטֻחַ בַּה׳״ (תְּהִלִּים קי״ב:ז׳), וְעַל זֶה ״סָמוּךְ לִבּוֹ לֹא יִירָא״ (שָׁם:ח׳):
for "his heart is steadfast, trusting in Hashem" (Tehillim 112:7), and upon this "his heart is established, he shall not be afraid" (ibid. 112:8).

12.h: The theme: The month of Tishrei, the mystery of the foundation hovering in the air (Yesod), and the elevation of Erev Yom Kippur. The month of Tishrei begins on Rosh Hashanah in intense awe and trembling before the depth of judgment, advancing through the Ten Days of Repentance which constitute a complete spiritual stature of crowning Hashem as King. The eve of Yom Kippur reaches the attribute of Yesod within Malchus—the ultimate "tower hovering in the air," where the entire body rests upon the foundation, while the foundation has nothing beneath it to lean upon. In the holy union, Yesod is the bestowing power in the male and the receiving vessel in the female whence offspring issue, fulfilling the purpose of Creation ("He created it not a waste, He formed it to be inhabited", Yeshayah 45:18). Yet reaching this goal demands seeking the ultimate purpose of the purpose itself: why bear children if generations continue endlessly without higher meaning? The true purpose is to raise godly seed (zera Elokim, Malachi 2:15) that proclaims the glory of Heaven, wedging the end back into the primordial beginning (ne'utzan sofan b'techilasan). This explains the incense spice "cinnamon nine" (kinamon tish'ah, Kerisos 6a): Yesod is the ninth Sefirah from Above to below, and Chochmah is ninth from below to Above; the perfection of Yesod is when it binds directly with Chochmah. Yesod is a soaring tower whose head reaches the heavens, yet hovers in the air because its true foundation must be anchored Above in divine Thought. Erev Yom Kippur is the preparation for Yom Kippur just as Friday prepares for Shabbat; through the sanctity of Yesod, Malchus (Imma Tata'ah) ascends into Binah (Imma Ila'ah), the "gate of freedom" (tar'a d'cheiru) and a foretaste of the World to Come, elevating this physical earth into the Supernal Land.

p: וְכָךְ הוּא הַחֹדֶשׁ תִּשְׁרֵי: תְּחִלָּתוֹ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בְּתֹקֶף הַיִּרְאָה וְהַפַּחַד מִמִּדַּת הַמִּשְׁפָּט וְעֹומֶק הַדִּין
And such is the month of Tishrei: its beginning on Rosh Hashanah is in the full intensity of awe and trembling before the attribute of justice and the depth of judgment;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַתְחִילִים יְמֵי רָצוֹן, וּמִתְפַּשְּׁטִים וְהוֹלְכִים בַּעֲשֶׂרֶת יְמֵי תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁהֵם מִדַּת קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה
and subsequently the days of divine favor begin, expanding through the Ten Days of Repentance which constitute the measure of a complete spiritual stature;
וְהַכֹּל מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁאָנוּ מַמְלִיכִים אוֹתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ עָלֵינוּ אָז
all of this reflecting the attribute of Malchus, for we crown Him as King over us then;
וְעֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הוּא עַד הַיְסוֹד בָּהּ
and the eve of Yom Kippur reaches unto the Yesod within her [Malchus];
דְּזֶהוּ עִיקַּר ״דְּפָרַח בַּאֲוִירָא״: שֶׁכָּל הַגּוּף נִשְׁעָן עַל הַיְסוֹד, וְהַיְסוֹד אֵין לוֹ עַל מִי לְהִשָּׁעֵן
this being the essential core of "hovering in the air": the entire body leans upon the foundation (Yesod), while the foundation has nothing beneath to lean upon;
כִּידוּעַ שֶׁיְּסוֹד הוּא בּוֹ כֹּחַ הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ בִּדְכוּרָא וְכֹחַ הַמְקַבֵּל בְּנוּקְבָא שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הַהוֹלָדָה אַחַר כָּךְ
as is known that in Yesod resides the bestowing power in the male and the receiving vessel in the female whence subsequent birth issues;
וְזֶה יְסוֹד בִּנְיַן כָּל קוֹמָה, וְתַכְלִית הַמְכֻוָּון לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ וּלְקַבֵּל וּלְהוֹלִיד
this being the foundation of every spiritual stature, the ultimate purpose to bestow, receive, and reproduce;
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה מְכֻוָּון הַבְּרִיאָה, דְּ״לֹא תֹהוּ בְרָאָהּ — לָשֶׁבֶת יְצָרָהּ״ (יְשַׁעְיָה מ״ה:י״ח)
which was the very objective of Creation: "He created it not a waste, He formed it to be inhabited" (Yeshayah 45:18);
וּבָזֶה אֲחִיזַת כָּל קוֹמָה שֶׁתַּגִּיעַ לְהַשְׁלָמָתָהּ שֶׁהוּא לְתַכְלִית הַמְכֻוָּון בָּהּ
and herein lies the integration of every stature to attain its completion in its designated purpose.
וּכְשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לַתַּכְלִית, הַתַּכְלִית עַצְמוֹ צָרִיךְ בֵּירוּרִים
And when one arrives at the purpose, that purpose itself requires spiritual clarification:
דְּעַדַיִין מַה הַמְכֻוָּון בְּתַכְלִית זֶה, וְצָרִיךְ תַּכְלִית לְתַכְלִיתוֹ
for what is the ultimate intent in this purpose, requiring a purpose for the purpose;
וְתַכְלִיתוֹ הוּא שֶׁחוֹזֵר לַהַתְחָלָה: דְּ״כֹּל פָּעַל ה׳ לַמַּעֲנֵהוּ״ (מִשְׁלֵי ט״ז:ד׳), לְקִילּוּסוֹ, שֶׁיַּכִּיר הַהַתְחָלָה
and its ultimate purpose is that it return to the beginning: for "Hashem made all things for His purpose" (Mishlei 16:4), for His praise, that creation recognize the Source;
וּכְמוֹ דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל: הָאָדָם חוֹשֵׁב תַּכְלִיתוֹ לְהוֹלִיד בָּנִים לִפְרוֹת וְלִרְבּוֹת
as by way of parable: a man assumes his purpose is to father children to be fruitful and multiply;
וְאַחַר שֶׁהוֹלִיד בֵּן, מַה תַּכְלִית יֵשׁ מִבֵּן יוֹתֵר מִמֶּנּוּ
yet once he has begotten a son, what greater purpose is there in the son than in the father?
וְאִם גַּם הוּא יוֹלִיד בָּנִים וְיֵלְכוּ הַדּוֹרוֹת עַד אֵין קֵץ, מַה בֶּצַע מִכָּל זֶה
and if that son likewise begets children and generations continue endlessly, what profit is there in all this?
וְהַתַּכְלִית: שֶׁיּוֹלִיד בֵּן ״זֶרַע אֱלֹהִים״ (מַלְאָכִי ב:טו), הַמַּכִּיר וּמְפַרְסֵם כְּבוֹד שָׁמַיִם בָּעוֹלָם
Rather, the true purpose is that he beget a son who is "godly seed" (Malachi 2:15), who recognizes and publicizes the glory of Heaven in the world;
וְהוּא הַחְזָרַת הַכֹּל לְעֹומֶק רֵאשִׁית, וּנְעִיצַת הַסּוֹף בַּהַתְחָלָה (סֵפֶר יְצִירָה א:ז)
this being the return of all things unto the primordial depth, wedging the end into the beginning (Sefer Yetzirah 1:7);
וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְהַתַּכְלִית שֶׁהִיא הַיְסוֹד, צָרִיךְ לְהַשִּׂיג הַתַּכְלִית לַתַּכְלִית שֶׁהוּא הַהַתְחָלָה
wherefore when one arrives at the purpose which is Yesod, he must grasp the purpose of the purpose which is the inception;
וְזֶה נֶעְלָם וְאֵין לוֹ יְסוֹד, שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט לְמַעְלָה לְעֹומֶק רֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה
and this is concealed and lacks a physical base, requiring that it expand upward into the primordial depth of Thought.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה יוּבַן גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁקִּבַּלְתִּי בְּסוֹד ״קִנָּמוֹן תִּשְׁעָה״ (כְּרֵיתוֹת ו׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
And in this manner will likewise be understood what I received regarding the secret of "cinnamon nine measures" (Kerisos 6a):
דְּרוֹמֵז לְהַיְסוֹד שֶׁהוּא הַתְּשִׁיעִי מֵעֵילָּא לְתַתָּא, וְהַחָכְמָה הוּא תְּשִׁיעִי מִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָּא
alluding to Yesod which is the ninth Sefirah from Above to below, while Chochmah is ninth from below to Above;
וּשְׁלֵימוּת הַיְסוֹד הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה נִמְשָׁךְ וּמְחוּבָּר וּמְיוּחָד עִם הַחָכְמָה
and the consummate perfection of Yesod is realized when it is drawn, bound, and unified with Chochmah;
וְהוּא מְכֻוָּון גַּם כֵּן עַל פִּי דַּרְכֵּינוּ: שֶׁכְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לַסּוֹף, צָרִיךְ לַחֲזוֹר לַהַתְחָלָה
which aligns precisely with our principle: when one reaches the end, he must return to the beginning.
וְהֲגַם דְּהַיְסוֹד אֵינוֹ עֲדַיִין הַסּוֹף לְגַמְרֵי
And although Yesod is not yet the absolute termination;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁבַּהַתְחָלָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמַּתְחִיל מִכֶּתֶר, מִכָּל מָקוֹם רֵאשִׁית הַגִּלּוּי דְּיֵשׁ מֵאַיִן הוּא הַחָכְמָה
just as at the beginning, although emanation commences from Keser, nevertheless the inception of manifestation ex nihilo is Chochmah;
כָּךְ בַּסּוֹף, אַף דִּגְמַר הַכֹּל הוּא בְּמַלְכוּת, הוּא בִּיצִיאַת הַפְּעֻלָּה לְגַמְרֵי לַפּוֹעַל
so at the end, although the final culmination is in Malchus, that represents the total emergence of the act into physical deed;
אֲבָל כֹּחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה כּוּלָּם מִסְתַּיְּימִים בִּיסוֹד
but the active faculties themselves all terminate within Yesod;

וְהַמַּלְכוּת הוּא דּוּגְמַת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁאַחַר שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְּרֵאשִׁית, דִּכְבָר בְּשִׁשָּׁה יָמִים נִשְׁלַם כָּל הַמְּלָאכָה וְלֹא הָיָה הָעוֹלָם חָסֵר אֶלָּא מְנוּחָה (רַשִׁ״י בְּרֵאשִׁית ב:ב)
and Malchus is comparable to the Sabbath day following the six days of Creation, where during the six days the entire work was completed and the world lacked only rest (Rashi on Bereishis 2:2);
אוֹ כְּמוֹ שִׁשָּׁה קְצוֹת שֶׁל הַמָּקוֹם וְגוּף הַמָּקוֹם הַכּוֹלְלָם
or like the six spatial extremities and the body of space that encompasses them,
שֶׁהַשִּׁשָּׁה קְצוֹת גַּם כֵּן הֵם כּוֹלְלִים וּמַגְדִּירִים כָּל הַמָּקוֹם, אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵלּוּ בִּפְרָט וְזֶה בִּכְלָל
for the six extremities define the space in detail while space itself contains them in general.
וּלְפִיכָךְ הַיְסוֹד ״מִגְדָּל גָּבוֹהַּ רֹאשׁוֹ בַּשָּׁמַיִם״, אֲבָל ״פּוֹרֵחַ בָּאֲוִיר״
Therefore Yesod is a soaring tower whose head is in the heavens, yet "hovers in the air";
שֶׁהַיְסוֹד שֶׁלּוֹ צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת לְמַעְלָה, וְשָׁם הוּא נֶעְלָם, וְאֵין נִגְלֶה אֶלָּא לְכָל חַד לְפוּם מַה דִּמְשַׁעֵר בְּלִבֵּיהּ (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק א׳ ק״ג עַמּוּד ב׳)
for its true foundation must be anchored on High, where it is concealed, revealed only unto each according to what he measures in his heart (Zohar I, 103b);
וְלָכֵן נִקְרָא עֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֶׁהוּא הֲכָנָה לְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים כְּמוֹ עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת הֲכָנָה לַשַּׁבָּת
and therefore the eve of Yom Kippur prepares for Yom Kippur just as the eve of Shabbat prepares for Shabbat;
כִּי מִקְּדֻשַּׁת הַיְסוֹד בָּא אַחַר כָּךְ לְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
for from the sanctity of Yesod one subsequently enters into Yom Kippur;
שֶׁיָּדוּעַ דְּאָז מִתְעַלָּה הַמַּלְכוּת אֶל הַבִּינָה, דְּנַעֲשָׂה מֵאִימָּא תַּתָּאָה — אִימָּא עִילָּאָה
as is known that on Yom Kippur Malchus ascends unto Binah, the Lower Mother (Imma Tata'ah) being transformed into the Supernal Mother (Imma Ila'ah);
שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת בִּסְלִיחַת כָּל הַחֲטָאִים, וְלִהְיוֹת ״תַּרְעָא דְּחֵירוּ״ (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק ג׳ ק״ח עַמּוּד ב׳) וּמֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא
which is the ultimate expansion in the forgiveness of all sins, becoming the "gate of freedom" (tar'a d'cheiru) and a foretaste of the World to Come;
שֶׁאָז יִהְיֶה הִתְעַלּוּת כָּל הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, לִהְיוֹת מֵאֶרֶץ הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה — אֶרֶץ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה:
when the entire physical world will be elevated, transforming the lower earth into the Supernal Land!

12.h: The theme: The tower of strength (Migdal Oz), the fast of Yom Kippur versus the Manna, and the double merit of eating on the ninth of Tishrei. The "tower of strength" (Migdal Oz) is formed following the climax of holy awe; it is Imma Ila'ah (Binah), which does not contradict the statement that it is Knesset Israel (Imma Tata'ah), because Malchus becomes a tower of strength when it ascends and binds with Binah (the letter Lamed). In this tower dwell the Holy One and the "certain pauper" (chad miskena)—the supernal union of Hashem and His Shechinah, where "the Name of Hashem" is Yesod d'Nukva and "into it the righteous runs" is Yesod d'Dechura. On Yom Kippur there is no physical eating or drinking, mirroring the World to Come where the righteous sit enjoying the radiance of the Shechinah (Berachos 17a), reflecting the mystery of Israel sustaining their Father in Heaven ("My bread for My sacrifices", Bamidbar 28:2; Zohar III, 7b). Eating on Erev Yom Kippur is accounted as if one fasted both the ninth and the tenth (Berachos 8b): every commanded meal of Israel contains the taste of Manna (food eaten by angels, Yoma 75b). The Gemara arranges the discourses on Manna in tractate Yoma (ch. 8) because the Manna mirrors the fast of Yom Kippur: abstaining from bodily food merits the spiritual enjoyment of the Shechinah. Had the Torah not commanded eating on the ninth, pious individuals would have afflicted their bodies with fasting; Hashem chose instead that man prepare through sanctified eating. Because goodness operates with abundant measure, experiencing even a trace of holiness beforehand elevates the physical food into the sanctity of Manna. Thus, eating on the ninth serves as preparation like fasting (ke-ilu hit'anah teshi'i), while simultaneously providing the spiritual delight of the tenth (ke-ilu hit'anah asiri), elevating Yesod d'Nukva into Yesod d'Imma.

p: וְזֶהוּ הַ״מִּגְדַּל עֹז״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ח:י׳) שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה אַחַר תֹּקֶף הַיִּרְאָה
And this is the "tower of strength" (Mishlei 18:10) formed following the intensity of holy awe;
וְעַל כֵּן שַׁפִּיר אָמְרוּ: ״דָּא אִימָּא עִילָּאָה״ (תִּקּוּנֵי זֹוהַר תִּקּוּן נ״ה צ״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
wherefore the Sages of the Zohar rightly declared: "this is the Supernal Mother (Imma Ila'ah)";
וְאֵינוֹ סוֹתֵר מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב: ״דָּא כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל״ (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק ג׳ קס״ד עַמּוּד ב׳), דְּהַיְינוּ אִימָּא תַּתָּאָה
and this does not contradict what is written elsewhere: "this is Knesset Israel," which is the Lower Mother (Imma Tata'ah);
כִּי מַה שֶּׁנִּקְרָא ״מִגְדַּל עֹז״ הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר מִתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת וּמִתְחַבֶּרֶת לְאִימָּא עִילָּאָה
for she is termed a "tower of strength" specifically when she expands and binds unto the Supernal Mother;
שֶׁהִיא עִיקַּר אוֹת הַלָּמֶ״ד, וּמִגְדָּל הַגָּבוֹהַּ שֶׁרֹאשׁוֹ בַּשָּׁמַיִם, דְּהוּא לִבָּא וְיוֹנֶקֶת מֵהַחָכְמָה
which is the essence of the letter Lamed, the towering structure whose head reaches the heavens, being the heart that nurses from Chochmah.
וְאָמְנָם מִצַּד עַצְמָהּ הֵן ״תְּרֵין רֵעִין דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין״ (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק ג׳ ד׳ עַמּוּד א׳), וְאֵין שָׁם פְּרִיחָה בָּאֲוִיר
And indeed, in their own supernal realm Chochmah and Binah are "two companions that never part" (Zohar III, 4a), where no "hovering in the air" exists;
אֶלָּא מִצַּד הִתְעַלּוּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וּשְׁכִינַת עוּזּוֹ לְשָׁם
this hovering applying solely to the ascent of Knesset Israel and the Shechinah thither;
וְזֶהוּ ״דְּדָיְירִין קֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְחַד מִסְכְּנָא״ (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק א׳ ו׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
and this is: "there dwell the Holy One, blessed be He, and a certain pauper" (Zohar I, 6a);
הַיְינוּ יִחוּד קֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ
which is the supernal union of the Holy One and His Shechinah;
וְזֶהוּ: ״[מִגְדַּל עֹז] שֵׁם ה׳״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ח:י׳), הַיְינוּ יְסוֹד דְּנוּקְבָא
and this is: "a tower of strength is the Name of Hashem," referring to Yesod d'Nukva;
״בּוֹ יָרוּץ צַדִּיק [וְנִשְׂגָּב]״ (שָׁם) — יְסוֹד דִּדְכוּרָא
"into it the righteous runs, and is set on high"—referring to Yesod d'Dechura;
וְהַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הוּא כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעִים לְ״מִגְדַּל עֹז״
and expansive liberation is realized upon entering this tower of strength.
וְעַל כֵּן בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים אֵין אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה, מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא
And therefore on Yom Kippur there is no eating or drinking, mirroring the World to Come;
דְּ״צַדִּיקִים יוֹשְׁבִים״ (בְּרָכוֹת י״ז עַמּוּד א׳) — הוּא צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם
where "the righteous sit" (Berachos 17a)—which is the Tzaddik, the foundation of the world (Yesod);
״וְנֶהֱנִין מִזִּיו הַשְּׁכִינָה״ (שָׁם) — הוּא יְסוֹד דְּנוּקְבָא, וְהָעִנְיָן עָמוֹק
"and enjoy the splendor of the Shechinah"—which is Yesod d'Nukva, and the concept is profound;
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק ג׳ ז׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״יִשְׂרָאֵל מְפַרְנְסִין לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם״, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״[אֶת] קָרְבָּנִי לַחְמִי [לְאִשַּׁי]״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ח:ב׳)
after the manner of what they stated (Zohar III, 7b): "Israel sustains their Father in Heaven," as it is said: "My offering, My bread for My sacrifices made by fire" (Bamidbar 28:2).
וּבְעֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הָאֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה ״כְּאִלּוּ מִתְעַנֶּה״ (בְּרָכוֹת ח׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
And on the eve of Yom Kippur eating and drinking is accounted "as if one fasted" (Berachos 8b);
הַיְינוּ שֶׁגַּם הַהֲנָאוֹת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הֵם שְׁקוּלִים כַּהֲנָאוֹת דְּעוֹלָם הַבָּא
meaning that even the physical delights of this world are weighed equally with the delights of the World to Come;
שֶׁכָּל אֲכִילַת מִצְוָה שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל אוֹכְלִים יֵשׁ בּוֹ טַעַם מָן
for every commanded mitzvah eating of Israel possesses the taste of Manna;
וְהוּא מַמָּשׁ דּוּגְמַת הַמָּן שֶׁהוּא לֶחֶם שֶׁמַּלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אוֹכְלִים (יוֹמָא ע״ה עַמּוּד ב׳), וְגַם כֵּן הֲנָאָה רוּחָנִית דְּמֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא
it being literally like the Manna which is the bread eaten by ministering angels (Yoma 75b), and likewise a spiritual delight reflecting the World to Come;
דְּעַל כֵּן סִדְּרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה הַמַּאֲמָרִים מֵעִנְיַן הַמָּן בְּפֶרֶק ״יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים״ (יוֹמָא פֶּרֶק ח׳)
wherefore our Rabbis of blessed memory arranged the talmudic discourses concerning the Manna specifically within the chapter Yom HaKippurim (Yoma, ch. 8);
כִּי אֲכִילַת הַמָּן הוּא מַמָּשׁ דּוּגְמַת הַתַּעֲנִית דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
for the eating of the Manna is the exact counterpart of the fast of Yom Kippur,
שֶׁהַכַּוָּונָה בּוֹ לִזְכּוֹת עַל יְדֵי זֶה לַאֲכִילָה הָרוּחָנִית דְּעוֹלָם הַבָּא
the intent being to merit through it the spiritual nourishment of the World to Come;
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אֲכִילָה וְלֹא שְׁתִיָּה, עַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִין לַהֲנָאָה הָרוּחָנִית דְּזִיו הַשְּׁכִינָה עַל יְדֵי הָרִיחוּק מֵהֲנָאָה הַגַּשְׁמִית
through abstaining from food and drink meriting the spiritual delight of the Shechinah's radiance by distancing from corporeal pleasure.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ח׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): דַּאֲכִילַת תְּשִׁיעִי ״כְּאִלּוּ הִתְעַנָּה תְּשִׁיעִי וַעֲשִׂירִי״
And this is what they expounded (Berachos 8b): that eating on the ninth is "as if he fasted on the ninth and tenth";
כִּי תַּעֲנִית עֲשִׂירִי הַיְינוּ אֲכִילָה הָרוּחָנִית
for the fast of the tenth is spiritual nourishment;
וְתַעֲנִית תְּשִׁיעִי הוּא מַה שֶּׁהָיִינוּ עוֹשִׂים בְּעַצְמֵנוּ אִלְמָלֵא צִוְּתָה הַתּוֹרָה בַּאֲכִילָה, לְסַגֵּף הַגּוּף לְכַפָּרַת עָוֹן
while a fast on the ninth is what mortals would have undertaken voluntarily had the Torah not commanded eating, afflicting the body for the atonement of sin;
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁמִּתְעַנִּין הַיְחִידִים בַּעֲשֶׂרֶת יְמֵי תְּשׁוּבָה, כְּדֵי לְהָכִין עַצְמוֹ עַל יְדֵי זֶה לַקְּדוּשָׁה דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
after the manner that pious individuals fast during the Ten Days of Repentance to prepare themselves for the sanctity of Yom Kippur;
אֲבָל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא בָּחַר בָּזֶה לַהֲכָנָה בְּעֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
but the Blessed Name did not choose fasting as the preparation on the eve of Yom Kippur;
שֶׁהוּא הַכְּנִיסָה לְהַרְגָּשַׁת הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב מִזִּיו הַשְּׁכִינָה דְּעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁבְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
which is the entrance into the heart's perception of Binah from the Shechinah's radiance of the World to Come;
גַּם בִּשְׁעַת הֲכָנָה שֶׁמֵּכִין עַצְמוֹ לִקְדוּשָׁה כָּזוֹ, הֲרֵי הוּא כְּבָר כְּלִי מוּכָן לָזֶה שֶׁיָּכוֹל לָבוֹא לִידֵי קְדוּשָׁה כָּזוֹ
for in the very hour of preparation one is already a prepared vessel capable of receiving such sanctity.
וְאִם בְּמִדַּת פּוּרְעָנוּת אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מ״ג:ב׳): עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מַכָּה לְפָנֶיהָ וּלְאַחֲרֶיהָ
And if regarding punishment the Sages stated (Bereishis Rabbah 43:2): idolatry strikes both before and after;
כָּל שֶׁכֵּן בְּמִדָּה טוֹבָה הַמְרוּבָּה
how much more so in the abundant measure of goodness!
וּכְבָר יֵשׁ הַרְגָּשַׁת שֶׁמֶץ מִקְּדוּשָׁה גַּם מִקּוֹדֶם
A trace of holiness is already experienced beforehand;
וּבִקְדֻשָּׁה כָּזוֹ שֶׁהוּא רַק הִתְגַּלּוּת הַהֶעְלֵם לַהֲבִיאוֹ לִידֵי גִּלּוּי עַל יְדֵי הַהַחְזָרָה לַמָּקוֹר, הֲרֵי יֶשְׁנָהּ מִתְּחִלָּה גַּם כֵּן
and in such holiness—which is the unveiling of that which was hidden through returning to the Source—it is already present from the inception;
רַק שֶׁהִיא בְּהֶעְלֵם, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הֲרֵי כְּבָר יֵשׁ הַרְגָּשָׁה בַּהֶעְלֵם שֶׁהוּא הֶעְלֵם שֶׁהֲרֵי מוּכָן לָבוֹא מִיָּד לְגִלּוּי
merely existing in concealment, yet being felt in concealment as a potential ready to burst immediately into revelation;
וּבְהַרְגָּשָׁה זוֹ מִתְקַדֵּשׁ וּמִתְעַלֶּה גַּם הַהֶעְלֵם
and in this awareness the concealment itself is sanctified and elevated;
וְעַל כֵּן הֲגַם שֶׁהוּא עֲדַיִין בְּהֶעְלֵם, הָאֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה הַגּוּפָנִית דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הִיא מִתְקַדֶּשֶׁת בִּקְדֻשַּׁת הַמָּן
wherefore even while still in concealment, the corporeal eating and drinking of this world is sanctified with the holiness of the Manna;
וְעַל יָדָהּ הוּא הֲכָנָה לָבוֹא לַהֲנָאָה הָרוּחָנִית דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
serving as the direct preparation to arrive at the spiritual delight of Yom Kippur.
וְזֶהוּ ״כְּאִלּוּ הִתְעַנָּה תְּשִׁיעִי״ — הַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ הֲכָנָה לִקְדֻשַּׁת הַיּוֹם דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים כַּהֲכָנַת הַתַּעֲנִית וְסִיגּוּף הַגּוּף
And this is "as if he fasted on the ninth"—possessing the preparation for the day's holiness like physical affliction;
וְנוֹסָף עַל זֶה ״כְּאִלּוּ הִתְעַנָּה עֲשִׂירִי״ גַּם כֵּן
and in addition to this "as if he fasted on the tenth" as well:
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן הֲנָאָה רוּחָנִית כִּבְתַעֲנִית עֲשִׂירִי
namely containing within the meal the spiritual delight of the fast of the tenth;
אֶלָּא שֶׁאָז הוּא רַק ״כְּאִלּוּ״ וּבְדֶרֶךְ הַדִּמְיוֹן כִּי עֲדַיִין הִיא בְּהֶעְלֵם
except that on the ninth it is "as if" and by way of anticipation because it remains in concealment;
וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הוּא בְּגִילּוּי וּבְפֹעַל
while on Yom Kippur it manifests in open revelation and deed;
וְזֶהוּ הִתְעַלּוּת הַיְסוֹד דְּנוּקְבָא לִיסוֹד אִימָּא:
and this is the elevation of Yesod d'Nukva unto Yesod d'Imma!

12.h: The theme: The ascent of Yesod d'Dechura to Yesod d'Abba on Succos, the letter Lamed as an intentional deviation, and the riddle of the Elders of Athens. Following Yom Kippur, the elevation of the male foundation unto Yesod d'Abba (Chochmah) unfolds on Succos—the culmination of the cycle beginning in Rosh Hashanah—where the intensity of awe transforms into the peak of joy during the Water Drawing celebration (Simchat Beit HaSho'evah, Yerushalmi Sukkah 5:1), drawing down the Holy Spirit from supreme wisdom. The name Tishrei signifies release and forgiveness: tishrei v'simchol ("may You release and pardon", Vayikra Rabbah 29:9). While every sin is an aberration from the straight row, Israel's transgressions were preordained in primordial thought ("like these cosmic years that have been ordered since the six days of Creation", Shabbat 89b), proving that an occasional departure from order is itself part of the cosmic design. This is embodied in the letter Lamed, which belongs to the straight row of the alphabet yet protrudes above it. The Elders of Athens challenged Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya: "Build us a house in the air of the world" (Bechorot 8b), perceiving that Israel dwells in a "tower hovering in the air" without a fixed worldly base. Though Israel sins throughout the year and the nations assume they are abandoned, Yom Kippur arrives and atones for them, turning intentional sins into merits (as the sin of the Golden Calf led to the Tabernacle). The Torah concludes with the letter Lamed in the word "Israel" (l'einei kol Yisrael), teaching that while the Written Torah consists of permanent stones and houses, its ultimate completion is wedged in the soaring Lamed—the Oral Torah, which draws sustenance from the conclusion of the Written Torah. Creation began with the letter Beis (the house of the world open to the north), but because mankind fell from rectitude, Israel's true habitation is not the rigid earthly house of the Beis, but the soaring tower of the Lamed.

p: וְהִתְעַלּוּת הַיְסוֹד דִּדְכוּרָא לִיסוֹד אַבָּא הוּא אַחַר כָּךְ בְּסֻכּוֹת
And the elevation of the male foundation (Yesod d'Dechura) unto the foundation of the Father (Yesod d'Abba / Chochmah) unfolds subsequently on Succos;
שֶׁהוּא הַסִּיּוּם דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, שֶׁמִּתֹּקֶף הַיִּרְאָה בָּא לְתֹקֶף הַשִּׂמְחָה דִּ״זְמַן שִׂמְחָתֵנוּ״
which is the culmination of the cycle of Rosh Hashanah, where from the intensity of awe one arrives at the intensity of joy in "the season of our gladness";
שֶׁמִּשָּׁם שׁוֹאֲבִין רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ בְּשִׂמְחַת בֵּית הַשּׁוֹאֵבָה (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי סֻכָּה פֶּרֶק ה׳ הֲלָכָה א׳)
whence they drew the Holy Spirit during the Rejoicing of the Water Drawing (Yerushalmi Sukkah 5:1);
שֶׁהוּא רוּחַ מִקּוֹדֶשׁ הָעֶלְיוֹן הִיא חָכְמָה עִילָּאָה
which is a divine spirit drawn from supernal holiness, the supreme Chochmah;
וּמְחִילַת הַחֲטָאִים בְּחֹדֶשׁ זֶה
and the pardon of sins occurs in this month;
וּבְוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה כ״ט:ט׳): דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא ״תִּשְׁרֵי״ — ״תִּשְׁרֵי וְתִמְחוֹל וְכוּלֵיהּ״
and in Vayikra Rabbah (29:9): wherefore it is called Tishrei—an idiom of "may You release (tishrei) and pardon, etc.";
נִרְאֶה דְּזֶהוּ עִיקַּר יְסוֹד עִנְיַן הַחֹדֶשׁ כּוּלּוֹ
it appears that this is the primary foundation of the entire month:
שֶׁרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הוּא הֲכָנָה לְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, וְסֻכּוֹת נִמְשָׁךְ אַחֲרָיו
that Rosh Hashanah is a preparation for Yom Kippur, and Succos follows thereafter,
שֶׁמִּזֶּה בָּא הַשִּׂמְחָה וְהַחִסָּיוֹן בְּצֵל ה׳
whence emerges holy joy and taking refuge beneath the shadow of Hashem.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי כָל חֵטְא הוּא יְצִיאָה מֵהַשּׁוּרָה
And this is because every sin is an aberration from the straight row;
אֲבָל חֲטָאֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם בֶּאֱמֶת ״כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת וְכוּלֵיהּ״, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא (שַׁבָּת פ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
yet the sins of the Children of Israel are in truth "like these cosmic years that have been ordered and advancing since the six days of Creation," as written in Shabbat (89b);
הַיְינוּ שֶׁגַּם זֶה מֵהַסֵּדֶר, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה דָּבָר יוֹצֵא מֵהַסֵּדֶר אֵיזֶה פַּעַם
meaning that even this is part of the divine design: that something should deviate from order at times;
וְזֶהוּ אוֹת הַלָּמֶ״ד, שֶׁהוּא מִכְּלַל שׁוּרַת הָאוֹתִיּוֹת אַף שֶׁהוּא יוֹצֵא מֵהַשּׁוּרָה
and this is the letter Lamed
which belongs to the row of the alphabet even though it protrudes above the line;
וְעַל כֵּן דָּבָר זֶה הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד, ״[וְ]לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי״ (תְּהִלִּים קמ״ז:כ׳)
wherefore this unique secret belongs to Israel alone, and "He has not dealt so with any nation" (Tehillim 147:20);
דְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִמָּקוֹם זֶה, וְדָיְירֵי בְּהַהוּא מִגְדָּלָא
for the soul-root of Knesset Israel originates from this high realm, dwelling within that soaring tower.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ סָבֵי דְּבֵי אַתּוּנָא בִּבְכוֹרוֹת (ח׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״בְּנִי לַן בֵּיתָא בַּאֲוִירָא דְּעָלְמָא״
And this is what the Elders of the Academy of Athens challenged in Bechorot (8b): "Build us a house in the air of the world!";
שֶׁיָּדְעוּ עִנְיַן יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם דָּרִים בְּ״מִגְדָּל הַפּוֹרֵחַ בָּאֲוִיר״
for they perceived the mystery of Israel: that they dwell in a "tower hovering in the air";
הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם יְסוֹד קָבוּעַ בְּשׁוּם דָּבָר
meaning that they possess no rigid worldly foundation in anything;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכְּבָר נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה בְּהַגְדָּרַת הַמַּעֲשִׂים, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֵם חוֹטְאִים כָּל הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹצְאִים מִשּׁוּרַת הַתּוֹרָה הַמַּגְדֶּרֶתָם
and although the Torah was given with strict boundaries for actions, nevertheless they stumble during the year and step outside the line of the Torah that fences them;
וּכְסְבוּרִים אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁכְּבָר הִזְנִיחָם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and the nations of the world assume that the Blessed Name has abandoned them,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בָּעֵגֶל (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה מ״א:א׳)
as the Sages related regarding the sin of the Golden Calf (Shemos Rabbah 41:1);
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וּמִתְכַּפֵּר לָהֶם
and subsequently Yom Kippur arrives and atones for them;
וְעוֹד נַעֲשִׂים מִזְּדוֹנוֹת זְכֻיּוֹת (יוֹמָא פ״ו עַמּוּד ב׳)
and furthermore, their intentional sins are converted into merits (Yoma 86b);
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁזָּכוּ עַל יְדֵי עֵגֶל לִמְלֶאכֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְגִלּוּי שְׁכִינָה כְּשֶׁנִּתְרַצָּה
just as through the Golden Calf Israel merited the construction of the Tabernacle and the indwelling of the Shechinah when Hashem was reconciled.
וְזֶהוּ סִיּוּם הַתּוֹרָה בְּאוֹת לָמֶ״ד [״לְעֵינֵי כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל״]
And this is the conclusion of the Torah with the letter Lamed [in the final word Yisrael, Devarim 34:12];
הַמּוֹרֶה עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכְּבָר נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה הַכּוֹלֶלֶת אֲבָנִים וּבָתִּים וְחוֹמוֹת, הֵם שׁוּרוֹת הַכְּתָב הַמַּגְדִּירוֹת הָאָדָם
indicating this path: that although the Torah was given comprising stones, houses, and walls—the straight lines of script that fence man;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם ״סוֹף דָּבָר הַכֹּל נִשְׁמָע״ (קֹהֶלֶת י״ב:י״ג), שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ כָּלוּל בְּאוֹת הַלָּמֶ״ד הַפּוֹרֵחַ בָּאֲוִיר
nevertheless "the end of the matter, all having been heard" (Koheles 12:13), all is enclosed within the letter Lamed that hovers in the air;
דִּבְאֶמֶת הַכֹּל פּוֹרֵחַ בָּאֲוִיר עֲדַיִין בְּלֹא יְסוֹד קַיָּים
for in absolute truth everything still hovers in the air without a rigid worldly foundation;
וְזֶהוּ הַיְסוֹד שֶׁל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הַמַּתְחִיל וְיוֹנֵק מִסִּיּוּם הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
and this is the foundation of the Oral Torah, which begins and nurses directly from the conclusion of the Written Torah;
דִּבְאֶמֶת אֵין שְׁלֵימוּת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
for in truth the Written Torah attains completion solely through the Oral Torah.
וְהַקָּרָאִים שֶׁפָּקְרוּ בָּהּ, אַף תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב אֵין לָהֶם
And the Karaites who apostatized and rejected the Oral Torah possess no Written Torah either;
כִּי מֵהַכְּתָב לֹא יוֹדְעִים כְּלוּם שֶׁהַכֹּל פּוֹרֵחַ בָּאֲוִיר עֲדַיִין, וְאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם מִצְוָה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת כְּלָל
for from the written text alone one can comprehend nothing, all remaining suspended in the air, leaving them without a single mitzvah in its proper fulfillment;
וּמְסַיֵּים בְּמִלַּת ״יִשְׂרָאֵל״, שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַלָּמֶ״ד
and the Torah concludes with the word "Israel," who are likewise the root of the Lamed;
וְתַכְלִית הַתּוֹרָה וְהַמְכֻוָּון בָּהּ הוּא רַק הַשְׁלָמַת הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְנַפְשׁוֹתָם הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה
and the ultimate purpose and objective of the Torah is solely the perfection of Knesset Israel, their souls being the metaphysical source of the Torah;
וְהַהַתְחָלָה הוּא בִּ״בְרֵאשִׁית״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית א:א), שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל מַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית וְכָל הַנִּבְרָאִים
and the beginning of the Torah is in Bereishis (Bereishis 1:1), which encompasses the entire work of Creation and all creatures;
וְעַל כֵּן מַתְחִיל בְּבֵי״ת הָרוֹמֵז לִכְלַל הָעוֹלָם שֶׁדּוֹמֶה לוֹ, דִּצְדַד צָפוֹן פָּתוּחַ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא כ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳)
wherefore it opens with the letter Beis
alluding to the cosmos which resembles it, being open on the northern side as the Sages stated (Bava Batra 25b);
וְ״הָאֱלֹהִים עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כט), וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ מַכִּירִין אֱלָהוּתוֹ וְכִי ״אַתָּה פְעַלְתּוֹ״
and "God made man upright" (Koheles 7:29), intending that the entire universe recognize His Godliness and that "You have wrought it";
אֶלָּא שֶׁגָּרַם הַחֵטְא בַּסּוֹף וְיָצְאוּ מַה שֶּׁיָּצְאוּ, וְלֹא נִשְׁאַר לְחֶלְקוֹ אֶלָּא יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּלְבַד
except that sin intervened, the nations falling away, leaving unto His portion Israel alone;
וְאַף הֵם בִּכְלַל הַיְצִיאָה מֵהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ, וְאֵין דָּרִים עוֹד בַּבַּיִת הַדּוֹמֶה לְבֵי״ת כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה בִּתְחִלַּת הַבְּרִיאָה אִלְמָלֵי לֹא חָטְאוּ
and even Israel stepped outside the rigid line, no longer dwelling in the stable house resembling the Beis as envisioned in the initial Thought had man not sinned;
רַק בַּמִּגְדָּל הַפּוֹרֵחַ שֶׁהוּא הַלָּמֶ״ד:
but rather within the soaring tower hovering in the air, which is the letter Lamed!

12.h: The theme: The mitzvah of Sukkah as departing into a temporary dwelling, and the lunar calendar versus the solar calendar. The mitzvah of Sukkah in Tishrei commands departing from a permanent home into a temporary dwelling (tzo mi-dirat keva v'sheiv b'dirat ara'i, Sukkah 2a), for Israel possesses no rigid permanence in worldly structures. The heathen nations cannot comprehend how a people can dwell in the air; perceiving that Israel establishes a dwelling in the air (the letter Lamed belonging to the row of letters), the Athenian elders asked: "Build us a house in the air!" Rabbi Yehoshua demonstrated that Israel possesses this power through the Divine Name—cleaving unto the Blessed Name Who is the "rock of their heart" and Who permeates the cosmic air, establishing a spiritual foundation where no physical base exists. To show the Athenians that they have no affinity with this realm, he answered: "Bring me bricks and mortar from the air" (Bechorot 8b), for if a gentile steps outside the line, he is destroyed forever without recovery. Therefore, the ultimate eschatological trial of the nations will be the mitzvah of Sukkah (Avodah Zarah 3a), a mitzvah tailored exclusively for the native-born in Israel (kol ha-ezrach b'Yisrael yeshvu va-sukkot, Vayikra 23:42), whereas gentiles can endure only a permanent house. This mirrors the sun and the moon: the nations reckon by the sun (Sukkah 29a) which has fixed permanence ("the sun knows its going down", Tehillim 104:19), while Israel reckons by the moon which has no fixed circuit (Rosh Hashanah 25a), its light waxing and waning. Out of this lunar concealment comes continuous renewal (chidushin), representing the Oral Torah. When the nations claim from the Written Torah "We are Israel" (Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 34), Hashem answers: "Only he who holds My secret mystery—the Oral Torah—is Israel," living within and nursing from the letter Lamed that teaches them.

p: וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן מִצְוַת הַסֻּכָּה שֶׁבְּחֹדֶשׁ זֶה: לָצֵאת מִדִּירַת קֶבַע לְדִירַת עֲרַאי (סֻכָּה ב׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
And this is likewise the mitzvah of the Sukkah in this month: to depart from a permanent dwelling into a temporary dwelling (Sukkah 2a);
כִּי אֵין לְיִשְׂרָאֵל שׁוּם קְבִיעוּת בְּשׁוּם דָּבָר
for Israel possesses no rigid worldly permanence in anything;
וְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֵין מְבִינִים זֶה: אֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר לָדוּר בָּאֲוִיר
and the nations of the world cannot comprehend this: how is it possible to dwell in the air?
שֶׁמַּשִּׂיגִים שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם בָּזֶה דִּירָה וּבַיִת בָּאֲוִיר, שֶׁהֲרֵי גַּם הַלָּמֶ״ד מִכְּלַל הַשּׁוּרָה
for they perceive that Israel establishes an authentic habitation and home in the air, seeing that the Lamed remains an integral part of the alphabet row;
מַשְׁמָע מִזֶּה דְּיֵשׁ סֵדֶר וּקְבִיעוּת לִיצִיאָה זוֹ
implying that there is an order and stability to this departure outside the line;
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: ״בְּנִי לַן וְכוּלֵיהּ״ (בְּכוֹרוֹת ח׳ עַמּוּד ב׳), לְהַרְאוֹת לָהֶם גַּם כֵּן אֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר זֶה
and toward this the Athenian elders challenged: "Build us a house in the air," demanding that he show them how this could be;
וְהֶרְאָם שֶׁהוּא יֵשׁ לוֹ כֹּחַ לָזֶה עַל יְדֵי שֵׁם
and Rabbi Yehoshua demonstrated that he possessed the power to do so through the Divine Name;
הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי דְּבֵיקוּתָם בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן בַּאֲוִירָא דְּעָלְמָא
meaning through Israel's cleaving unto the Blessed Name Who likewise permeates the cosmic air;
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא ״צוּר לְבָבָם״ (תְּהִלִּים ע״ג:כ״ו) וּבוֹ הוּא יְסוֹדָם, וְעַל כֵּן יְכוֹלִים לַעֲשׂוֹת יְסוֹד בָּאֲוִיר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ יְסוֹד
and the Blessed Name is the rock of their heart and in Him is their foundation, wherefore they can establish a foundation in the air that lacks an earthly base.
וּבְוַדַּאי כְּמוֹ שֶׁיָּכוֹל עַל יְדֵי שֵׁם לַעֲמוֹד בָּאֲוִיר, כָּךְ הָיָה יָכוֹל לִבְנוֹת בַּיִת שָׁם גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי שֵׁם
And certainly, just as he was able through the Divine Name to suspend himself in the air, so could he have built a house there through the Name;
אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא צָרִיךְ לָזֶה, רַק כְּלַפֵּי שְׁאֵלָתָם ״בְּנִי לַן וְכוּלֵיהּ״, הֶרְאָה לָהֶם שֶׁהֵם אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לָזֶה וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם זֶה
but he did not need to perform this, seeking merely in response to their challenge to show them that they have no affinity with this reality and it is impossible for them;
עַל כֵּן אָמַר: ״אַיְיתֵי לִי לִיבְנֵי וְטוּנֵי״ (בְּכוֹרוֹת ח׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
wherefore he answered: "Bring me bricks and mortar from the air!"
שֶׁאִם אַתֶּם רוֹצִים לִהְיוֹת לָכֶם בַּיִת כָּזֶה, צְרִיכִים אַתֶּם לְהָכִין הַהֲכָנוֹת הַצְּרִיכוֹת
meaning: if you desire to possess such a celestial home, you must prepare the prerequisite spiritual preparations;
וַהֲרֵי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָכֶם לְהָכִין עַצְמְכֶם לָזֶה כְּלָל, כִּי דָּבָר בִּלְתִּי מוּשָּׂג לָכֶם וְלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ לָכֶם כְּלָל
and behold it is impossible for you to prepare yourselves for this, being incomprehensible and completely foreign to you;
כִּי אִם יָצְאוּ מֵהַשּׁוּרָה, הֵם יוֹצְאִים וְאוֹבְדִים לְגַמְרֵי וְאֵין לָהֶם תְּקוּמָה עוֹד לְמַפַּלְתָּן
for if the gentiles step outside the line, they fall and perish completely, having no recovery from their downfall.
וְעַל כֵּן נִסָּיוֹן הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת לֶעָתִיד יִהְיֶה בְּמִצְוַת סֻכָּה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ג׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
Wherefore the future eschatological test of the idolaters will be through the mitzvah of Sukkah (Avodah Zarah 3a);
דְּזֶה שַׁיָּיךְ רַק ״לְהָאֶזְרָח בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״ (וַיִּקְרָא כ״ג:מ״ב)
for this applies exclusively unto "the native-born in Israel" (Vayikra 23:42);
אֲבָל הֵם אֵין יְכוֹלִין לִסְבּוֹל כְּלָל אֶלָּא דִּירַת קֶבַע וְדָבָר קָבוּעַ
whereas the nations are utterly incapable of bearing anything other than a permanent dwelling and a rigid structure;
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁמּוֹנִין לַחַמָּה (סֻכָּה כ״ט עַמּוּד א׳) שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ קְבִיעוּת
and this is why they reckon by the sun (Sukkah 29a) which has fixed permanence,
דְּ״שֶׁמֶשׁ יָדַע מְבוֹאוֹ״ (תְּהִלִּים ק״ד:י״ט)
for "the sun knows its going down" (Tehillim 104:19);
אֲבָל יָרֵחַ לֹא יָדַע מְבוֹאוֹ, פְּעָמִים בַּאֲרוּכָה פְּעָמִים בִּקְצָרָה (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כ״ה עַמּוּד א׳) שֶׁאֵין לוֹ קְבִיעוּת
whereas the moon knows not its going down, its circuit being sometimes long and sometimes short (Rosh Hashanah 25a), having no static permanence;
וְכֵן אֵין קְבִיעוּת לְאוֹרוֹ: פַּעַם נֶעְלָם וּפַעַם נִגְלֶה, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יֵשׁ הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת בְּכָל פַּעַם
and likewise its light has no static constancy: now waning and now waxing, whereby there is perpetual renewal at each cycle;
וְזֶהוּ הַחִידּוּשִׁין דִּבְאוֹרַיְיתָא שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and this is the dynamic innovation of the Oral Torah;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב דִּכְתִיבָא וּמַנָּחָא, אֵין שָׁם חִידּוּשִׁין
unlike the Written Torah which is written and laid open, where no new textual additions can be made.
וְלָכֵן אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם טוֹעֲנִין עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב: ״אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל״, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנְחוּמָא (פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תִשָּׂא ל״ד)
And therefore the nations of the world argue on the basis of the Written Torah: "We are Israel," as written in Tanchuma (Ki Tisa §34);
וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵשִׁיב: ״מִי שֶׁמִּסְטוֹרִין שֶׁלִּי בְּיָדוֹ וְכוּלֵיהּ״
and the Holy One responds: "Whoever holds My secret mystery in his hand is Israel";
דְּהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּלִבְּבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
for the Oral Torah resides exclusively within the hearts of the Children of Israel,
שֶׁהֵם דְּדָיְירִין וְיוֹנְקִין מֵאוֹת הַלָּמֶ״ד הַמְלַמַּדְתָּם:
who dwell within and nurse from the soaring letter Lamed that teaches them!

12.h: The theme: The Second Tablets on Yom Kippur as the source of the Oral Torah, and the opening and closing of the Talmud with the letter Mem. On Yom Kippur the Second Tablets were given—the rectification following the shattering of the first and the deviation from the line. From the Second Tablets derives the vitality of the Oral Torah (Zochor to the masculine Written Torah, Shomor to the feminine Oral Torah / Second Tablets). In the Future, when the Oral Torah is completed, it too will become Written Torah (the Second Tablets), while the First Tablets—presently the broken tablets resting in the Ark—will be restored when death is swallowed up forever (Yeshayah 25:8), death being the esoteric mystery of the breaking of the Tablets (Tikkunei Zohar). Then the light of the moon (the Oral Torah) will be as the light of the sun (the Written Torah), and the light of the sun will be sevenfold like the light of the seven days of Creation (Yeshayah 30:26). The Decalogue begins with Aleph (Anochi) and ends with Chaf (l're'echa), the letters immediately preceding Beis and Lamed which begin and end the Torah (B-L, the root of Torah). The Oral Torah opens with the letter Mem (Me'eimatai, Berachos 2a)—the letter following the Lamed which concludes the Written Torah—and concludes with the letter Mem (b'shalom, Uktzin 3:12). While the Written Torah was completed at Sinai, the Oral Torah has no end: veteran disciples innovate new insights daily, returning to its beginning like flowing streams (el mekom she-ha-nechalim holchim sham hem shavim lalechet, Koheles 1:7). Even in the Messianic era, the Oral Torah will continuously cycle into deeper renewals. The Babylonian Talmud—the consummate embodiment of the Oral Torah where all future insights are hinted—likewise opens with Mem (Me'eimatai) and concludes with Mem (Torah u-ma'asim tovim / b'shalom), remaining stationed at the Mem, constantly tasting higher and clearer illuminations of divine truth.

p: וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים נִיתְּנוּ לוּחוֹת אַחֲרוֹנוֹת (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכ״א עַמּוּד א׳)
And on Yom Kippur the Second Tablets were given (Bava Batra 121a);
שֶׁהוּא הַתִּיקּוּן שֶׁאַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל וִיצִיאָה מֵהַסֵּדֶר
which is the rectification that follows corruption and stepping outside the line;
וּמִשָּׁם הוּא הַיְנִיקָה דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and from there is the life-sustenance of the Oral Torah;
כִּידוּעַ דְּ״זָכוֹר״ (שְׁמוֹת כ:ח) לִדְכוּרָא, וְ״שָׁמוֹר״ (דְּבָרִים ה:יב) לְנוּקְבָא, וְלוּחוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת בְּסוֹד הַנּוּקְבָא
as is known that "Remember" is masculine [the Written Torah], and "Observe" is feminine [the Oral Torah], the Second Tablets standing in the mystery of the Feminine;
וּלְעָתִיד כְּשֶׁיּוּשְׁלַם כָּל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, יִהְיֶה מֵהֶם גַּם כֵּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְהֵם הַלּוּחוֹת אַחֲרוֹנוֹת
and in the Future when the Oral Torah is completed, it too will become Written Torah, being embodied in the Second Tablets;
וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הִיא הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁהֵם לְעֵת עַתָּה שִׁבְרֵי לוּחוֹת הַמּוּנָּחוֹת בָּאָרוֹן (בְּרָכוֹת ח׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
while the Written Torah is the First Tablets, which are presently the broken tablets resting in the Ark (Berachos 8b);
וְאָז כְּשֶׁ״בֻּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח״ (יְשַׁעְיָה כ״ה:ח׳), יָשׁוּבוּ גַּם לוּחוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת לְקַדְמוּתָן
and then when "He will swallow up death forever" (Yeshayah 25:8), the First Tablets will likewise return to their pristine wholeness;
כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתִּקּוּנִים שֶׁהַמִּיתָה הוּא סוֹד שְׁבִירַת הַלּוּחוֹת
as written in the Tikkunim that physical death is the esoteric mystery of the shattering of the Tablets;
וְאָז יִהְיֶה ״[וְהָיָה] אוֹר הַלְּבָנָה כְּאוֹר הַחַמָּה״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ל:כו), שֶׁהֵם הַלּוּחוֹת דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
and then "the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun" (Yeshayah 30:26), which are the Tablets of the Written Torah;
״וְאוֹר הַחַמָּה [יִהְיֶה שִׁבְעָתַיִם] כְּאוֹר שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים״ (שָׁם), שֶׁאָדָם צוֹפֶה בּוֹ מִסּוֹף עוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ (חֲגִיגָה י״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
"and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of the seven days" (ibid.), through which man gazed from one end of the universe to the other (Chagigah 12a);
שֶׁזֶּהוּ אוֹר לוּחוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁהָיָה אָז חֵירוּת מִמַּלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת וְיֵצֶר הָרָע עַל יָדָם (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
this being the light of the First Tablets through which there was complete freedom from the Angel of Death and the yetzer hara (Avodah Zarah 5a),
כְּמוֹ לֶעָתִיד שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה עוֹד מְחִיצָה הַמַּבְדֶּלֶת וּמַעֲלֶמֶת הָאוֹר כְּלָל
as in the Future when no dividing partition will obscure the light at all.
וְהַלּוּחוֹת מַתְחִילוֹת בְּאָלֶ״ף [״אָנֹכִי״] וּמְסַיְּימוֹת בְּכַ״ף [״לְרֵעֶךָ״]
And the Ten Commandments on the Tablets open with the letter Aleph [in Anochi] and conclude with the letter Chaf [in l're'echa];
הֵם אוֹתִיּוֹת הַקּוֹדְמוֹת לְאוֹתִיּוֹת בֵּי״ת לָמֶ״ד שֶׁבְּהַתְחָלַת וְסִיּוּם הַתּוֹרָה [״בְּרֵאשִׁית״ — ״יִשְׂרָאֵל״]
which letters (Aleph-Chaf,
א-ך)
directly precede the letters Beis-Lamed
(ב-ל)
that begin and conclude the Torah [Bereishis to Yisrael];
כִּי הֵם הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ לַתּוֹרָה
for the Tablets are the primordial root of the Torah;
וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה מַתְחִיל בְּמֵ״ם: ״מֵאֵימָתַי״ (בְּרָכוֹת ב׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
and the Oral Torah begins with the letter Mem: "From when (Me'eimatai) do we read the Shema in the evening?" (Berachos 2a);
שֶׁהוּא אוֹת דִּלְאַחַר הַלָּמֶ״ד שֶׁמִּסְתַּיֶּימֶת בּוֹ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
which is the letter immediately following the Lamed with which the Written Torah concludes;
וּמְסַיֵּים גַּם כֵּן בְּמֵ״ם: ״בְּשָׁלוֹם״ (עוּקְצִין פֶּרֶק ג׳ מִשְׁנָה י״ב)
and the Mishnah concludes likewise with the letter Mem: "with peace (b'shalom)" (Uktzin 3:12);
כִּי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב כְּבָר נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה וְנִשְׁלְמָה שֶׁאֵין עוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב יוֹתֵר
for the Written Torah was given and sealed, there being no further Written Torah;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה לֹא נִשְׁלַם עֲדַיִין, דְּעַדַיִין עֲתִידִים תַּלְמִידִים וָתִיקִים לְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד
unlike the Oral Torah which is not yet concluded, for veteran disciples are destined to innovate within it every single day continually;
וְעַל כֵּן בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁמַּתְחִיל, שָׁם הוּא מְסַיֵּים
wherefore in the very place it begins, there it concludes:
שֶׁבְּכָל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁגִּילָּה רַבִּי בַּמִּשְׁנָיוֹת, עַדַיִין לֹא גִּילָּה כְּלוּם
that in all the Oral Torah revealed by Rebbe in the Mishnayot, he has as yet revealed nothing compared to the infinite whole;
וְעַדַיִין הוּא כְּאִלּוּ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כּוּלָּהּ בִּשְׁלֵימוּתָהּ עַדַיִין מוּנַּחַת לְלִבּוֹת הַחֲכָמִים הָעֲתִידִים לָבוֹא לְחַדֵּשׁ מִלִּבָּם
and it is still as though the entire Oral Torah in its fullness is laid open for the hearts of the future sages to innovate from their souls;
וּ״לִמְקוֹם שֶׁהַנְּחָלִים הֹלְכִים שָׁם הֵם שָׁבִים לָלָכֶת״ (קֹהֶלֶת א:ז), וְאֵין שָׁם סִיּוּם כְּלָל
and "unto the place whither the rivers go, thither they go again" (Koheles 1:7), there being no final termination at all.
וְגַם בִּכְלַל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא כֵּן שֶׁאֵין לוֹ סִיּוּם כְּלָל
And in the totality of the Oral Torah it is likewise so, having no cessation;
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ שֶׁאָז יִהְיֶה שְׁלֵימוּת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, עַדַיִין יִהְיֶה חוֹזֵר חָלִילָה
so that even in the Messianic era when the Oral Torah attains completion, it will cycle repeatedly anew,
לָשׁוּב לְהַשִּׂיג הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת בְּאוֹתָן הַהַשָּׂגוֹת עַצְמָן שֶׁהִשִּׂיגוּ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
returning to attain fresh insights within the selfsame perceptions grasped in this world;
כִּי ״גָבֹהַּ מֵעַל גָּבֹהַּ שׁוֹמֵר וּגְבֹהִים עֲלֵיהֶם״ (קֹהֶלֶת ה:ז)
for "one higher than the high watches, and there are higher than they" (Koheles 5:7).
וְעַל זֶה רוֹמֵז פְּתִיחַת וַחֲתִימַת הַתַּלְמוּד בַּבְלִי בְּאוֹת הַמֵּ״ם
And to this alludes the opening and closing of the Babylonian Talmud with the letter Mem
(מ); כִּי הַתַּלְמוּד הוּא שְׁלֵימוּת כָּל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כּוּלָּהּ
for the Talmud is the consummate synthesis of the entire Oral Torah;
דְּלֵיכָּא מִידֵי מַה שֶּׁשּׁוּם תַּלְמִיד וָתִיק עָתִיד לְחַדֵּשׁ עַד יְמוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ דְּלָא רְמִיזֵי בַּתַּלְמוּד
there being nothing that any veteran disciple is destined to innovate until the days of Mashiach that is not hinted in the Talmud;
וְזֶהוּ חֲתִימַת הַתַּלְמוּד שֶׁעָלָיו אֵין לְהוֹסִיף וּמִמֶּנּוּ אֵין לִגְרוֹעַ
and this is the sealing of the Talmud to which nothing can be added and from which nothing can be diminished;
וּמְסַיֵּים גַּם כֵּן בַּמַּה שֶּׁמַּתְחִיל, דִּלְאַחַר הַסִּיּוּם גַּם כֵּן עֲדַיִין עוֹמֵד בַּהַתְחָלָה
and it concludes with that with which it begins, for following the conclusion one still stands at the beginning;
וְלֹא שֶׁחוֹזֵר לַהַתְחָלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁהוּא אוֹת הָאָלֶ״ף, רַק לְאוֹת הַמֵּ״ם עַצְמָהּ
and not returning to the initial inception of the alphabet which is the Aleph, but unto the letter Mem itself;
כִּי עַדַיִין הוּא עוֹמֵד עַל הַשָּׂגָה זוֹ שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגַת כְּלָלוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כּוּלָּהּ
for he still stands upon this perception which is the totality of the entire Oral Torah;
דִּבְכָל פַּעַם מַשִּׂיג אוֹר בָּהִיר יוֹתֵר בְּאוֹתָהּ הַשָּׂגָה עַצְמָהּ, מַה שֶּׁלֹּא טָעַם עַד הֵנָּה עֲדַיִין
attaining each time a brighter light within that very perception which he had never tasted until now;
וְזֶהוּ הַהִתְחַדְּשׁוּת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד
and this is the renewal that will unfold in the Future:
הַיְינוּ הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת שֶׁל טְעִימוֹת בְּאוֹתָהּ הַשָּׂגָה עַצְמָהּ, עַד שֶׁנִּרְאֵית כְּמוּשָּׂג חָדָשׁ אֶצְלוֹ, וְכָאָמוּר:
namely the renewal of tastings within the selfsame perception, until it appears to him as a brand-new concept, and as stated!
The theme: The creation of Adar through the letter Kuf (ק), laughter
sechok
, the Leviathan, and Purim. According to Sefer Yetzirah
, Hashem crowned the letter Kuf in laughter, tying to it Pisces
Dagim
in the cosmos, Adar in the year, and the spleen
tchol
in the soul
Berachos 61b
. The fish of the cosmos is the Leviathan—"this Leviathan You have formed to play with"
Tehillim 104:26
—the source of supernal laughter on High
Avodah Zarah 3b; Bava Batra 74b
. In the yearly cycle, Adar is the season of increasing joy
Ta'anis 29a
, the opposite of crying
Koheles 3:4
