. The Gemara
Avodah Zarah 3b
distinguishes two categories of divine laughter: laughing with His creatures
sechok im beriyotav
and laughing over His creatures
sechok al beriyotav
. Purim embodies laughter over the downfall of Haman. While Hashem does not personally rejoice over the fall of the wicked
"He does not rejoice, but He causes others to rejoice", Megillah 10b
, on that unique day "He that sits in heaven laughs"
Tehillim 2:4
over the exposed falsehood of the nations who seek to mimic Israel. Esav and Amalek
"first among the nations"
refuse to be humble servants, wrapping themselves in talitot like a swine displaying split hooves to declare itself kosher
Vayikra Rabbah 13:5
. Haman imagined that the King of kings chose him over Israel
Esther 6:6; Zohar III, 109a
, but was reduced to mockery when forced to lead Mordechai as a royal servant. In this world, filling one's mouth with unrestrained laughter is forbidden
Berachos 31a
regarding the downfall of enemies; but in the holy joy of a mitzvah
sechok im beriyotav
, a person may rejoice with a full mouth
"I am wearing Tefillin!", Berachos 30b
, for all mitzvos and Torah must be performed in holy ecstasy
Zohar III, 56a
חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר נוֹצַר בְּאוֹת קוּ״ף, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה (סוֹף פֶּרֶק ה׳ מִשְׁנָה י׳): ״הִמְלִיךְ אוֹת קוּ״ף בִּשְׂחוֹק וְכוּלֵיהּ, וְצָר בּוֹ דָגִים בָּעוֹלָם״
The month of Adar was formed through the letter Kuf
as written in Sefer Yetzirah (5:10): "He crowned the letter Kuf in laughter, tied a crown to it, and formed with it Pisces in the cosmos, Adar in the year, and the spleen in the soul";
וְנִרְאֶה לִי דְּהַיְינוּ: ״לִוְיָתָן זֶה יָצַרְתָּ לְשַׂחֶק בּוֹ״ (תְּהִלִּים ק״ד:כ״ו)
and it appears to me that this alludes to: "this Leviathan You have formed to play with" (Tehillim 104:26);
שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הַשְּׂחוֹק לְמַעְלָה, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ג׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) וּבְ״הַסְּפִינָה״ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ע״ד עַמּוּד ב׳)
whence derives the supernal laughter on High, as written at the beginning of Avodah Zarah (3b) and in Bava Batra (74b);
וּבְוַדַּאי מַזַּל דָּגִים שֶׁבָּרָקִיעַ הוּא דּוּגְמַת דַּג הַלִּוְיָתָן רֹאשׁ דְּגֵי הַיָּם
and certainly the constellation of Pisces (Dagim) in the firmament mirrors the great fish Leviathan, the head of all sea creatures;
וַאֲדָר בַּשָּׁנָה שֶׁבּוֹ ״מַרְבִּין בְּשִׂמְחָה״ (תַּעֲנִית כ״ט עַמּוּד א׳) וּמִמֶּנּוּ הַשְּׂחוֹק
and Adar in the year is the season wherein "we increase in joy" (Ta'anis 29a), whence issues holy laughter;
כִּי הוּא הֵיפֶךְ הַבֶּכִי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּכ״ח עִתִּים דְּקֹהֶלֶת (ג:ד): שֶׁזֶּה מִתּוֹךְ הָעֶצֶב וְהָאֵבֶל וְזֶה מֵרוֹב הַחֶדְוָה וְהַשִּׂמְחָה

for laughter is the opposite of weeping, as stated among the twenty-eight seasons of Ecclesiastes (Koheles 3:4): weeping flowing from sorrow and mourning, while laughter issues from abundant gladness and joy;
וּמִנְהַג קַדְמוֹנִים לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּפוּרִים כָּל מִינֵי שְׂחוֹק
and it is the ancient custom of our forebears to enact all manners of joyous play on Purim;
וְעַיֵּין סַנְהֶדְרִין (ס״ד עַמּוּד ב׳): ״כִּי מְשַׁוְורְתָּא דְּפוּרְיָא״ וּבְרַשִׁ״י
and see Sanhedrin (64b): "like the jumping fire-pit of Purim," and Rashi there;
וּטְחוֹל בַּנֶּפֶשׁ שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הַשְּׂחוֹק, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּ״הָרוֹאֶה״ (בְּרָכוֹת ס״א עַמּוּד ב׳)
and the spleen (tchol) in the soul is the physiological source of laughter, as written in Berachos (61b).
וְזֶה וָזֶה [שְׂחוֹק ״עִם בְּרִיּוֹתָיו״ וּשְׂחוֹק ״עַל בְּרִיּוֹתָיו״] כִּי הֵם שְׁנֵי מִינֵי שְׂחוֹק
And both of these are established, for there are two distinct categories of divine laughter:
״עִם בְּרִיּוֹתָיו״ — וְזֶהוּ שְׂחוֹק דְּלִוְיָתָן, ״וְעַל בְּרִיּוֹתָיו״ — כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ג׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
laughing with His creatures—which is the joyful play with the Leviathan; and laughing over His creatures—as written in Avodah Zarah (3b);
וְזֶהוּ שְׂחוֹק דְּפוּרִים עַל מַפַּלְתּוֹ שֶׁל הָמָן
and this is the laughter of Purim over the downfall of Haman;
שֶׁהוּא אֵינוֹ שָׂשׂ וְאֵין שְׂחוֹק לְפָנָיו אֶלָּא אוֹתוֹ יוֹם בִּלְבַד: ״יוֹשֵׁב בַּשָּׁמַיִם יִשְׂחָק [ה׳ יִלְעַג לָמוֹ]״ (תְּהִלִּים ב:ד)

for Hashem does not personally rejoice over the fall of the wicked, no mocking laughter existing before Him except on that day alone when "He that sits in the heavens shall laugh; the Lord shall have them in derision" (Tehillim 2:4);
כְּשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה שִׁקְרוּת הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת בְּקַבָּלַת הַמִּצְוֹת, דְּאֵינוֹ מַפָּלָה לָהֶם גַּם כֵּן
when the duplicity of the idolaters regarding the fulfillment of the commandments is unveiled (Avodah Zarah 3b), which is not truly an injury unto them;
רַק גִּלּוּי הָאֱמֶת, שֶׁיּוֹדוּ בְּמַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא יִרְצוּ לְהִתְדַּמּוֹת לָהֶם, רַק לִהְיוֹת עֲבָדִים לָהֶם דִּלְכָךְ נוֹצָרוּ
but merely the revelation of truth, that they acknowledge the supreme virtue of Israel and no longer seek to mimic them, but desire to be servants unto them for which purpose they were created;
אֲבָל ״אֲחֵרִים מֵשִׂישׂ״ גַּם בְּמַפַּלְתָּן, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב (מְגִלָּה י׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
yet "He causes others to rejoice" even in the downfall of the wicked, as written in Megillah (10b);
וּבְיוֹתֵר בְּמַפַּלְתּוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק שֶׁזֶּהוּ ״רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ד:כ׳)
and all the more so in the downfall of Amalek who is the "first of the nations";
שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְמוֹחֲתוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא נִשְׁאָר מִמֶּנּוּ זֵכֶר, וְלֹא שֶׁיִּהְיוּ עֲבָדִים כִּשְׁאָר עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים
who must be blotted out until not a memory remains of him, not even being permitted to survive as servants like other gentiles;
כִּי הוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים שֶׁרוֹצִים לְהִתְדַּמּוֹת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, כִּי הוּא מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ עֵשָׂו: דַּ״הֲלוֹא אָח עֵשָׂו לְיַעֲקֹב״ (מַלְאָכִי א:ב)
for he embodies that root within the nations who seek to falsely mimic Israel, deriving from the root of Esav: "Was not Esau Jacob's brother?" (Malachi 1:2).
וְכֵן אִיתָא: דִּלְעָתִיד מִתְעַטֵּף בְּטַלִּיתוֹ וּבָא לֵישֵׁב אֵצֶל יַעֲקֹב בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ, וּמִשָּׁם יוֹרִידוֹ ה׳
And so it is taught: in the Future Esav wraps himself in a prayer shawl (tallit) and comes to sit beside Yaakov in the study hall, and from there Hashem casts him down;
כִּי זֶה כָּל כֹּחוֹ: לִפְשׁוֹט טְלָפַיִם כַּחֲזִיר וְלוֹמַר שֶׁהוּא טָהוֹר, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה י״ג:ה׳)
for this is his entire strategy: to display split hooves like a swine and claim that he is kosher, as written in Vayikra Rabbah (13:5);
וְכֵן הָמָן אָמַר: ״לְמִי יַחְפֹּץ הַמֶּלֶךְ [לַעֲשׂוֹת יְקָר יוֹתֵר מִמֶּנִּי]״ (אֶסְתֵּר ו:ו)
and so Haman said in his heart: "To whom would the king delight to do honor more than to myself?" (Esther 6:6);
וְיָדוּעַ מִדִּבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (זֹוהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ג׳ ק״ט עַמּוּד א׳): דְּ״הַמֶּלֶךְ״ סְתָם — בְּמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים מְדַבֵּר
and it is known from the Sages (Zohar III, 109a) that an unqualified "king" speaks homiletically of the King of kings;
וְחָשַׁב דְּהוּא חָשׁוּב אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כֵּן, דְּלֹא בְּחִנָּם גִּדְּלוֹ וּמָסַר יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּיָדוֹ לְאַבְּדָם
Haman assuming that he was exceedingly precious unto the Blessed Name, reasoning that not for naught had Hashem exalted him and surrendered Israel into his hand to destroy them;
לְפִי שֶׁהֵם ״יָשְׁנוּ מִן הַמִּצְוֹת״ (מְגִלָּה י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳), וְדִמָּה דְּבָחַר בּוֹ תַּחְתָּם
seeing that Israel had become "asleep from the commandments" (Megillah 13b), and he imagined that Hashem chose him in their stead;
וְהָיָה לִשְׂחוֹק וּלְלַעַג אַחַר כָּךְ כְּשֶׁשָּׁמַע דִּבְרֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ כִּי חָפֵץ הוּא בְּמָרְדֳּכַי הַיְּהוּדִי וְשֶׁהוּא יִהְיֶה עֶבֶד לְפָנָיו
and he was turned into ridicule and mockery when he heard the King command that he desired to honor Mordechai the Jew, and that Haman must serve as a menial slave before him;
שֶׁעַל זֶה נוֹצְרוּ הָאוּמּוֹת, וְהֵם כְּשֶׁיְּגוּלֶּה הָאֱמֶת לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא יִתְרַצּוּ בְּכָךְ
for toward this service the nations were created, and when truth is unveiled in the Future they will consent to this status;
אֲבָל עֲמָלֵק אֵין מִתְרַצֶּה בְּכָךְ, כִּי הוּא הַתַּמְצִית דְּעֵשָׂו בִּפְשִׁיטַת טְלָפַיִם
but Amalek will never consent to this, being the absolute concentration of Esav's deceptive display of split hooves;
וְכָל שָׁרְשׁוֹ הוּא מִצַּד הַשֶּׁקֶר הַזֶּה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ כֹּחַ בְּעָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק קַיָּים
his entire essence drawing power from this falsehood which holds sway in this world of deceit as long as the seed of Amalek endures.
וּכְשֶׁיִּמָּחֶה זִכְרוֹ, הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה מְצִיאוּת עוֹד לַשֶּׁקֶר וּלְעָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא, שֶׁהַכֹּל יַכִּירוּ הָאֱמֶת
And when his memory is blotted out, meaning that no existence will remain for falsehood and the world of deceit, and all shall recognize the truth;
הוּא הַזְּמַן שֶׁ״יוֹשֵׁב בַּשָּׁמַיִם יִשְׂחָק״ (תְּהִלִּים ב:ד), מִבֵּירוּר מַעֲשֵׂה אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁהָיָה הַכֹּל רַק שֶׁקֶר וְלִפְנִים

that will be the hour when "He that sits in the heavens shall laugh" (Tehillim 2:4) over the exposure of the deeds of the nations, that all their righteousness was mere hypocrisy and outward pretense.
וְאָז: ״יִמָּלֵא שְׂחוֹק פִּינוּ״ (תְּהִלִּים קכ״ו:ב׳), כְּשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה הָאֱמֶת דְּכָל יְמֵי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה ״הָיִינוּ כְּחֹלְמִים״ (שָׁם:א׳) וְהוֹלְכִים בְּדִמְיוֹן

And then: "our mouth shall be filled with laughter" (Tehillim 126:2), when the truth is revealed that throughout the days of this world "we were like dreamers" (ibid. 126:1), walking in mere imagination;
כִּי הוּא כּוּלּוֹ עוֹלַם הַשֶּׁקֶר וְהַדִּמְיוֹן, אֶלָּא שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵינוֹ נִגְלֶה
for this physical world is entirely a world of falsehood and imagination, except that in this life it is not openly recognized;
וְעַל כֵּן: ״אָסוּר לָאָדָם שֶׁיְּמַלֵּא שְׂחוֹק פִּיו בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה״, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק אֵין עוֹמְדִין (בְּרָכוֹת ל״א עַמּוּד א׳)
wherefore: "It is forbidden for a person to fill his mouth with laughter in this world," as written in Berachos (31a);
וְהַיְינוּ שִׂמְחָה יְתֵירָה וּלְמִבְדַּח טוּבָא
meaning excessive frivolity and wild laughter;
וְזֶהוּ הַשְּׂחוֹק סְתָם דִּכְלַפֵּי מַעְלָה בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שָׁם (ג׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
this being the unqualified laughter referred to on High in Avodah Zarah (3b);
וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתְבוּ בְּתוֹסָפוֹת שָׁם דְּ״אַחֵיךְ״ דִּבְבָבָא מְצִיעָא (נ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳) הַיְינוּ בְּדִיחוּתָא בְּעָלְמָא, עַיֵּין שָׁם
and as Tosafos wrote there that "Hashem laughed (achich)" in Bava Metzia (59b) signifies a gentle smile of delight, see there;
שֶׁכְּשֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ מִמֶּנּוּ לְמַטָּה לָאָדָם, הוּא בָּא בְּמִילּוּי פֶּה עַל דֶּרֶךְ: ״יִמָּלֵא פִי תְּהִלָּתֶךָ״ (תְּהִלִּים ע״א:ח׳)
which, when drawn down from Him to man, manifests as a full mouth after the manner of: "My mouth shall be filled with Your praise" (Tehillim 71:8);
וְזֶהוּ אִילּוּ הָיָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כֵּן שָׂשׂ מִזֶּה וְהוּא תְּהִלָּתוֹ כְּמוֹ לֶעָתִיד בְּאוֹתוֹ יוֹם
and this full laughter would be permitted were the Blessed Name likewise rejoicing over the destruction of the wicked as His supreme praise, as will occur in the Future on that great day;
אֲבָל כֵּיוָן דְּהוּא אֵינוֹ שָׂשׂ אַף דַּאֲחֵרִים מֵשִׂישׂ, אֵין לִהְיוֹת בְּמִילּוּי פֶּה שֶׁאֵינוֹ כָּל כָּךְ דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה
but since He does not rejoice even while causing others to rejoice, one must not engage in laughter with a full mouth, which lacks proper reverence toward Heaven;
וְזֶהוּ בִּשְׂחוֹק דְּ״עַל בְּרִיּוֹתָיו״
this applying strictly to laughter over His creatures [their downfall].
אֲבָל ״עִם בְּרִיּוֹתָיו״, הוּא הַנִּמְשָׁךְ לְמַטָּה בְּלֵב הָאָדָם בְּשִׂמְחָה שֶׁל מִצְוָה
But laughter with His creatures is that which is drawn down below into the human heart in the joy of a mitzvah (simchah shel mitzvah);
זֶהוּ גַּם בְּמִילּוּי פֶּה וּלְמִבְדַּח טוּבָא
this joy is permitted even with a full mouth and intense rejoicing;
כְּמָה שֶׁאָמַר שָׁם (בְּרָכוֹת ל׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״אֲנָא תְּפִלִּין מַנַּחְנָא״
as Mar the son of Rabina replied when questioned why he rejoiced so intensely (Berachos 30b): "I am wearing Tefillin!";
וְלָאו דַּוְוקָא תְּפִלִּין, אֶלָּא הוּא הַדִּין כָּל הַמִּצְוֹת וְעֵסֶק הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בְּשִׂמְחָה
and not Tefillin exclusively, but the same law applies unto all commandments and engagement in Torah which must be fulfilled in ecstatic joy,
כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּוהַר רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת אַחֲרֵי (חֵלֶק ג׳ נ״ו סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳):
as written in the Zohar at the beginning of Parashat Acharei Mot (III, 56a)!

13.h: The theme: Masculine versus feminine song, the liver and spleen of Esav and Amalek, and the wine of the Torah. Laughter born of internal soul-delight is masculine (d'dechura), possessing fierce potency; laughter over the downfall of creatures receives its stimulation from an outside other, being feminine (d'nukva), lacking inherent strength. Therefore, all songs composed in this world over the downfall of the nations are termed feminine (shirah), representing weakened vigor; in the Future, a masculine song (shir chadash, Tehillim 98:1) will be sung with a mouth full of laughter. Most laughter in this world of evil is the "laughter of the fool" (Koheles 7:6), where the hour temporarily plays in his favor (ha-sha'ah mesacheket lo, Raya Mehemna, Pinchas 232b). This is the laughter of the spleen (tchol), which feeds on the dross of the liver. Esav is the liver of the world (anger, blood, murder); Amalek, the concentrated extraction of Esav, is the spleen of the world, whose entire occupation is mockery (leitzanus)—"Smite a scorner" (Mishlei 19:25)—this is Amalek (Shemos Rabbah 27:6), deriding the truth. Haman enjoyed temporary good fortune as the richest man of the nations (Esther Rabbah 2:3), but his worldly success was a passing game, ending as an object of ridicule to all. Because worldly laughter easily degenerates into levity leading to sexual immorality (sechok v'kalut rosh margilim l'ervah, Avos 3:13), Hashem crowned the letter Kuf in laughter: Kuf signifies holiness (Kadosh, Shabbat 104a) and a fence around immorality (Yevamos 20a). Righteous anger is the anger of scholars (rugza d'rabbanan, Ta'anis 4a), holy Gevurot directed solely against the evil of Amalek. The words of Torah are compared to wine, drawn from Gevurah: to those who turn left it is a lethal poison, but to those who turn right it gladdens the human heart and makes one wise (Shabbat 88b; Yoma 76b).

p: וּשְׂחוֹק זֶה הוּא מֵהַשַּׁעֲשׁוּעַ וְהַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁבְּנַפְשׁוֹ, זֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דִּדְכוּרָא וְעַל כֵּן הוּא בְּתֹקֶף
And this laughter issues from the inner delight and joy within the soul, being a masculine rung (d'dechura), wherefore it possesses supreme potency;
אֲבָל הַשְּׂחוֹק שֶׁ״עַל בְּרִיּוֹתָיו״ מְקַבֵּל הַשַּׁעֲשׁוּעַ מֵאֲחֵרִים, דַּרְגָּא דְּנוּקְבָא וְעַל כֵּן אֵינוֹ בְּתֹקֶף
while the laughter over His creatures receives its stimulation from outside entities, being a feminine rung (d'nukva), wherefore it lacks intrinsic power;
וְעַל כֵּן כָּל הַשִּׁירוֹת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁנֶּאֶמְרוּ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עַל מַפַּלְתָּן שֶׁל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הוּא בִּלְשׁוֹן נְקֵבָה [שִׁירָה] שֶׁהִיא הַתָּשַׁת כֹּחַ
and therefore all songs uttered in this world over the downfall of the idolaters are formulated in the feminine gender (shirah), which indicates weakened vigor;
רַק לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא יוּשַׁר ״שִׁיר חָדָשׁ״ (תְּהִלִּים צ״ח:א׳) לְשׁוֹן זָכָר, דְּ״יִמָּלֵא שְׂחוֹק פִּינוּ״ (שָׁם קכ״ו:ב׳) וְיִהְיֶה בְּתֹקֶף הַשִּׂמְחָה
but in the Future a "new song" (shir chadash, Tehillim 98:1) will be sung in the masculine gender, when "our mouth will be filled with laughter" in the full power of joy;
כִּי יִהְיֶה גַּם שִׂמְחָה זוֹ בִּכְלַל שִׂמְחָה שֶׁל מִצְוָה וְשַׁעֲשׁוּעַ שֶׁבְּעֶצֶם
for that joy too will then be subsumed within the joy of a mitzvah and essential soul-delight;
מֵאַחַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ שְׂחוֹק וְשִׂמְחָה גַּם כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה מִזֶּה, הֲרֵי הַשִּׂמְחָה נִמְשֶׁכֶת מִמַּעְלָה בְּעַצְמִיּוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ
since laughter and joy will then exist Above from this downfall, joy streaming from on High into the very essence of the soul;
וְהַשְּׂחוֹק הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, וּכְשֶׁהַשִּׂמְחָה בְּעַצְמִיּוּת הַלֵּב מִתְמַלֵּא הַפֶּה שְׂחוֹק
and laughter is the manifest expression of joy in the heart, and when joy fills the heart's essence the mouth overflows with laughter.
וּלְפִי שֶׁרוֹב הַשְּׂחוֹק דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהָרָע גּוֹבֵר בּוֹ הוּא ״שְׂחֹק הַכְּסִיל״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:ו)
And because the majority of laughter in this world where evil predominates is the "laughter of the fool" (Koheles 7:6);
וְשֶׁ״הַשָּׁעָה מְשַׂחֶקֶת לוֹ״ הַנִּזְכָּר בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא פִּינְחָס (רל״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
where "the hour plays in his favor," mentioned in Raya Mehemna (Pinchas 232b);
שֶׁהוּא שְׂחוֹק דִּטְחוֹל דְּנָטֵיל מִפְּסֹולֶת דִּפְסֹולֶת דְּכָבֵד
which is the laughter of the spleen (tchol) feeding upon the dross of the dross of the liver;
שֶׁהוּא עֵשָׂו ״אִישׁ שָׂעִיר״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:י״א) דְּנָטֵיל כָּל עֲכִירֵי וְטִנּוּפָא דְּלִבָּא, וְ״נָשָׂא הַשָּׂעִיר... אֶת כָּל עֲוֹנֹתָם״ (וַיִּקְרָא ט״ז:כ״ב), עַיֵּין שָׁם
he being Esav the "hairy man" (sa'ir, Bereishis 27:11) who absorbs all the murky filth of the heart: "and the goat (sa'ir) shall bear upon him all their iniquities" (Vayikra 16:22), see there;
וְהַיְינוּ דִּבְעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם לֵב הָעוֹלָם שֶׁמֵּהֶם תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים לְכָל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ שֶׁגַּם כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת יוֹנְקִים מֵהֶם
meaning that in this world the Children of Israel are the heart of the cosmos whence issue the currents of life for all creation, all nations drawing sustenance from them;
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּתַעֲנִית (ג׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָעוֹלָם בְּלֹא יִשְׂרָאֵל
wherefore the Sages stated in Ta'anis (3b): the world cannot exist without Israel;
וְכֵן בְּכָל דָּבָר, דְּאִם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם יִכְלֶה יִשְׂרָאֵל, יֹאבַד וְיִכְלֶה כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
and so in all things: were Israel to vanish, God forbid, the entire universe would perish;
וּכְבַעַל חַי שֶׁנִּיטַּל לִבּוֹ דְּאֵין לוֹ חַיּוּת עוֹד
like a living creature whose heart is removed, possessing no further life;
וְעֵשָׂו הוּא נֶגֶד הַכָּבֵד בָּעוֹלָם מִצַּד הָרָע, שֶׁבּוֹ הַכַּעַס וְהָרְצִיחָה
and Esav corresponds to the liver in the world from the side of evil, wherein resides fury and bloodshed;
וַעֲמָלֵק שֶׁהוּא הַפְּסֹולֶת דִּפְסֹולֶת דְּעֵשָׂו, נִרְאֶה לִי שֶׁהוּא הַטְּחוֹל בָּעוֹלָם מִצַּד הָרָע שֶׁהוּא פְּסֹולֶת דִּפְסֹולֶת דְּכָבֵד
and Amalek, who is the concentrated dross of Esav, appears to me to be the spleen in the world from the side of evil, the dross of the dross of the liver;
וְכָל עִסְקוֹ בִּשְׂחוֹק וְלֵיצָנוּת
his entire occupation consisting of frivolous laughter and scoffing;
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה כ״ז:ו׳): ״׳לֵץ תַּכֶּה׳ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ט:כ״ה) — זֶה עֲמָלֵק״
wherefore they expounded in Shemos Rabbah (27:6): "'Smite a scorner' (Mishlei 19:25)—this is Amalek";
שֶׁזֶּה כָּל עִנְיָנוֹ: בִּשְׂחוֹק דְּ״עַל בְּרִיּוֹתָיו״
his entire essence operating in mocking laughter over others;
וְהֵיפֶךְ הַשְּׂחוֹק הָאֲמִיתִּי, כִּי הוּא מַלְעִיג עַל הָאֱמֶת
being the antithesis of holy laughter, for he scoffs at the sacred truth.
וְ״הַשָּׁעָה מְשַׂחֶקֶת לוֹ״ בְּעוּתְרָא דְּהַאי עָלְמָא כְּהָמָן שֶׁהָיָה עָשִׁיר שֶׁבְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם (אֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ב:ג)
And "the hour played in his favor" in the physical wealth of this world like Haman, who was the wealthiest man among the nations (Esther Rabbah 2:3);
אֲבָל רַק לְשָׁעָה כְּדֶרֶךְ הַמְשַׂחֵק, וְסוֹפוֹ הָיָה הוּא לִשְׂחוֹק לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם
but merely for a fleeting hour like a passing game, and his end was that he became an object of mockery to all who enter the world;
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק מָצוּי עֲדַיִין בָּעוֹלָם, הָרָע וְהַשֶּׁקֶר גּוֹבֵר
and as long as the seed of Amalek endures in the world, evil and falsehood dominate;
וְהַשְּׂחוֹק הַמָּצוּי הוּא מִצַּד הָרָע, הוּא הַשְּׂחוֹק שֶׁל ״קַלּוּת רֹאשׁ הַמַּרְגִּיל לְעֶרְוָה״ (אָבוֹת ג:יג)
and standard worldly laughter stems from the unholy side, being the laughter of "levity that accustoms a man to sexual immorality" (Avos 3:13);
עַל כֵּן הִמְלִיךְ אוֹת קוּ״ף בִּשְׂחוֹק, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הוּא הַמּוֹלֵךְ וּמוֹשֵׁל בּוֹ
therefore Hashem crowned the letter Kuf in laughter, that it reign and govern over it;
וְהַקּוּ״ף מוֹרֶה ״קָדוֹשׁ״ כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת (ק״ד עַמּוּד א׳)
the Kuf denoting "Holy" (Kadosh), as written in Shabbat (104a);
וְהוּא הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא גֶּדֶר עֶרְוָה, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב פֶּרֶק ב׳ דִּיבָמוֹת (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כ״ד:ו׳)
being the place where you find a fence against sexual immorality (Vayikra Rabbah 24:6);
דְּהַשְּׂחוֹק שֶׁיָּצַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הוּא רַק שְׂחוֹק שֶׁמִּצַּד הַקְּדוּשָׁה
for the laughter that the Blessed Name created in the world was intended solely as laughter from the side of holiness;
וְ״הָאֱלֹהִים עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כט), וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה כּוּלּוֹ טוֹב אַף הָעֲכִירוּת וְהַפְּסֹולֶת שֶׁבּוֹ
and "God made man upright" (Koheles 7:29), intending that he be entirely good, even his sediment and dross;
וְהַכַּעַס שֶׁבַּכָּבֵד יִהְיֶה רַק ״רוּגְזָא דְּרַבָּנָן דְּטָב בְּכָל סִטְרִין״ (תַּעֲנִית ד׳ עַמּוּד א׳), וּבִמְקוֹם שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְצַוֶּוה לִכְעוֹס
and the anger of the liver should be solely "the zeal of the scholars which is good in all aspects" (Ta'anis 4a), directed where the Blessed Name commands to be zealous;
וְזֶהוּ הַגְּבוּרוֹת הַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרַהּ נָפְקָא, וְיֵשׁ בָּהּ דִּינֵי דִּינִין
these being the holy Gevurot whence the Torah issues, containing strict judicial laws;
אֲבָל הַכֹּל נֶגֶד סִטְרָא דְּרָע שֶׁשָּׁרְשׁוֹ בְּזֶרַע עֲמָלֵק
but all aimed against the side of evil rooted in the seed of Amalek;
וּכְשֶׁיְּבוֹעֲרוּ מִן הָעוֹלָם, ״יְבֻקַּשׁ אֶת עֲוֹן יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֵינֶנּוּ״ (יִרְמְיָה נ:כ), וְיִהְיֶה כּוּלּוֹ טוֹב מִכָּל סִטְרִין
and when they are expunged from the world, "the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none" (Yirmiyah 50:20), all becoming good from every side.
דְּעַל כֵּן נִמְשְׁלוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְיַיִן, וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד הַגְּבוּרָה שֶׁבָּהּ
Wherefore words of Torah are compared to wine, from the attribute of Gevurah within her;
[כִּי הַתּוֹרָה כּוֹלֶלֶת הַכֹּל וְנֶגֶד כָּל ג׳ אֲבָהָן: דְּנִקְרֵאת גַּם כֵּן ״תּוֹרַת חֶסֶד״ (מִשְׁלֵי ל״א:כו) וְעַל זֶה נִמְשְׁלָה לְחָלָב
[for the Torah encompasses all three Patriarchs: being called the "Torah of kindness" (Mishlei 31:26), compared to milk;
וְ״תוֹרַת אֱמֶת״ (מַלְאָכִי ב:ו) וְעַל זֶה נִמְשְׁלָה לִדְבַשׁ
and the "Torah of truth" (Malachi 2:6), compared to honey;
וּשְׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת אֵלּוּ הוּא מִצַּד הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת, וְגַם תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בִּכְלָל
both titles reflecting outward expansion and the Oral Torah;
אֲבָל מִצַּד עַצְמוּתָהּ נִקְרֵאת ״תּוֹרַת ה׳״ (תְּהִלִּים י״ט:ח׳), עַל זֶה נִמְשְׁלָה לְיַיִן
but in her essential core she is called "the Torah of Hashem" (Tehillim 19:8), compared to wine;
שֶׁרוֹמֵז רַק לְתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, כִּדְמַשְׁמַע מִמַּה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה א:ב): ״חֲבִיבִים דִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים יוֹתֵר מִיֵּינָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה״
alluding to the Written Torah, as implied by: "the words of the Scribes are more beloved than the wine of the Torah"];
כִּי הַיַּיִן יֵשׁ שׁוֹתֵהוּ וְטוֹב לוֹ, וְיֵשׁ וְכוּלֵיהּ (יוֹמָא ע״ו עַמּוּד ב׳)
for wine, there is one who drinks and it is good for him, and another for whom it is disastrous (Yoma 76b);
כְּמוֹ בְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן וְנֹחַ שֶׁהֵבִיא יְלָלָה לָעוֹלָם (סַנְהֶדְרִין ע׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
as with Adam HaRishon and Noach, where wine brought lamentation to the world (Sanhedrin 70a);
וְלַמַּשְׂמְאִילִים בָּהּ — סַמָּא דְּמוֹתָא (שַׁבָּת פ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳)
and for those who turn left within the Torah, it becomes a potion of death (Shabbat 88b);
אֲבָל לַמַּיְימִינִים בָּהּ: ״יַיִן יְשַׂמַּח לְבַב אֱנוֹשׁ״ (תְּהִלִּים ק״ד:ט״ו), וְ״חַמְרָא... פִּקְחִין״ (יוֹמָא ע״ו עַמּוּד ב׳), וְזֶהוּ רַק בְּזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל:
but for those who turn right within her: "wine gladdens the heart of man" (Tehillim 104:15), and wine makes one wise, this virtue belonging exclusively unto the seed of Israel!

The theme: Yitzchak Avinu as the root of holy laughter, the two annunciations of his birth, and the holy vision of old age. Holy laughter began with Yitzchak Avinu, the first of Israel’s seed born from the womb in holiness and circumcised on the eighth day
unlike Avraham who was the father of converts, Sukkah 49b
. Yitzchak was born after the inception of the two thousand years of Torah; regarding him it is written: "and he brought him wine, and he drank"
Bereishis 27:25

, bringing blessings upon Yaakov. Yitzchak is the root of the holy Gevurot; through his birth, laughter entered the world and his very name is Yitzchak (יִצְחָק, "he shall laugh"). The word tzchok never appears in the Torah until the annunciation of his birth: "and Abraham fell upon his face, and laughed"
Bereishis 17:17
—the laughter of Hashem with His creatures
sechok im beriyotav
. In the second annunciation delivered by angels, the phrasing changed: Hashem had said "I will give you a son of her"
attributing the masculine Gevurot to Avraham where evil has no hold
; the angels said "and lo, Sarah your wife shall have a son"
Bereishis 18:10
, attributing it to the feminine side
Nukva
where the feet descend unto death
Mishlei 5:5
, for the angels foresaw that the evil Gevurot of Esav would issue from him. They did not fathom the depth of "for in Isaac shall your seed be called"
Bereishis 21:12
—"in Isaac, and not all of Isaac"
Nedarim 31a
, Esav not being reckoned his seed at all. In the Future, Yitzchak will be the leader of Israel
"for You are our Father", Yeshayah 63:16; Shabbat 89b
, pointing out the Holy One directly to their eyes. In this world Yitzchak became blind, accounted as dead
Nedarim 64b
, because worldly sight was removed from him after gazing at the Shechinah at the Binding
Bereishis Rabbah 65:10
, meriting eye-to-eye vision in old age devoid of sorrow and the yetzer hara
Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah, ch. 5
, a foretaste of the Future when "eye to eye shall they see, when Hashem returns to Zion"
Yeshayah 52:8
and our mouth is filled with laughter.
וְהִתְחִיל בְּיִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא רֵאשִׁית זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל הַנּוֹלָד מִבֶּטֶן בִּקְדֻשָּׁה וְנִימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה
And holy laughter began with Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him, who is the first of the seed of Israel born from the womb in holiness and circumcised at eight days;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּנִקְרָא (סֻכָּה מ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): ״תְּחִלָּה לַגֵּרִים״
unlike Avraham Avinu who is termed "the first of the converts" (Sukkah 49b);
וְכֵן יִצְחָק נוֹלַד אַחַר הַתְחָלַת שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ט׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
and likewise Yitzchak was born following the inception of the two thousand years of Torah (Avodah Zarah 9a);
וּבוֹ נֶאֱמַר: ״וַיָּבֵא לוֹ יַיִן וַיֵּשְׁתְּ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:כ״ה), וְהָיָה לְהָבִיא הַבְּרָכוֹת עַל יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ אוּמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית
and concerning him it is said: "and he brought him wine, and he drank" (Bereishis 27:25), which served to bring the blessings upon Yaakov who is the root of the Israelite nation;
כִּי הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַגְּבוּרוֹת הַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת דִּלְמַיְימִינִים בָּהּ
for Yitzchak is the root of the holy Gevurot for those who turn right within the Torah;
עַל כֵּן בְּלֵידָתוֹ הֵבִיא הַצְּחוֹק לָעוֹלָם, וְכֵן עִיקַּר שְׁמוֹ עַל שֵׁם הַצְּחוֹק
wherefore at his birth he brought holy laughter into the world, his primary name being designated after laughter;
וְלֹא נִמְצָא בַּתּוֹרָה מִלַּת ״צְחוֹק״ לִפְנֵי הִתְבַּשְּׂרוּת לֵידַת יִצְחָק
and the word tzchok is never found in the Torah prior to the annunciation of the birth of Yitzchak;
דְּשָׁם נֶאֱמַר: ״וַיִּפֹּל אַבְרָהָם עַל פָּנָיו וַיִּצְחָק״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ז:י״ז)
for there it is said: "Then Abraham fell upon his face, and laughed" (Bereishis 17:17);
דְּאָז נִתְעוֹרֵר וְנִתְחַדֵּשׁ הִתְגַּלּוּת הַצְּחוֹק דִּקְדֻשָּׁה בָּעוֹלָם
then awakened and renewed the manifestation of holy laughter in the world;
וְאָז תֵּיכֶף גִּילָּה לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כֵּן שְׁמוֹ שֶׁהוּא ״יִצְחָק״ עַל שֵׁם זֶה (שָׁם:י״ט)
and immediately the Blessed Name revealed to him his name: that he shall be called Yitzchak after this laughter (ibid. 17:19);
וּשְׂחוֹק זֶה הוּא דְּ״עִם בְּרִיּוֹתָיו״
and this laughter is the laughter with His creatures.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בִּבְשׂוֹרָה שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַצְמוֹ רַק עַל יְדֵי הַמַּלְאָכִים, נִשְׁתַּנָּה הַלָּשׁוֹן
And afterward in the second annunciation, which occurred not through the Blessed Name directly but through the angels, the phrasing changed;
דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָמַר: ״[וְגַם] נָתַתִּי מִמֶּנָּה לְךָ בֵּן״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ז:ט״ז), וְכֵן אַחַר כָּךְ: ״יֹלֶדֶת לְךָ בֵּן״ (שָׁם:י״ט), יִחֲסוּ אֵלָיו
for the Blessed Name had said: "I will give you a son also of her" (Bereishis 17:16), and "shall bear you a son" (ibid. 17:19), attributing the son to Avraham;
שֶׁהֵם הַגְּבוּרוֹת דְּמִסִּטְרָא דִּדְכוּרָא דְּשָׁם אֵין יְנִיקָה לָרָע כָּל כָּךְ
these being the Gevurot of the masculine side (d'dechura) where evil has no grasp;
אֲבָל הֵם אָמְרוּ: ״וְהִנֵּה בֵן לְשָׂרָה אִשְׁתֶּךָ״ (שָׁם י״ח:י׳), יִחֲסוּהוּ לְסִטְרָא דְּנוּקְבָא דְּ״רַגְלֶיהָ יֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת״ (מִשְׁלֵי ה:ה) כַּנּוֹדָע
but the angels said: "and, lo, Sarah your wife shall have a son" (Bereishis 18:10), attributing him to the feminine side (d'nukva) whose "feet go down to death" (Mishlei 5:5) as is known;
דְּשָׁם הוּא יְנִיקַת הָרָע מִצַּד הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת עַד הָרַגְלִין שֶׁהוּא סוֹף הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת
for there resides the sustenance of evil through the downward extension unto the feet;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהֵם רָאוּ שֶׁיֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ גַּם כֵּן הַגְּבוּרוֹת רָעוֹת דְּעֵשָׂו
meaning that the angels foresaw that from him would likewise issue the evil Gevurot of Esav;
וְלֹא יָדְעוּ הַמַּעֲמַקִּים שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה אַחַר כָּךְ בַּתּוֹרָה בְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי בְיִצְחָק יִקָּרֵא לְךָ זָרַע״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״א:י״ב)
not knowing the profound depths revealed afterward in the Torah: "for in Isaac shall your seed be called" (Bereishis 21:12);
שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּנְדָרִים (ל״א עַמּוּד א׳): ״וְלֹא כָּל יִצְחָק״, דְּאֵין עֵשָׂו קָרוּי זַרְעוֹ כְּלָל
which the Sages expounded in Nedarim (31a): "in Isaac, and not all of Isaac," Esav not being designated his seed at all;
וְנִמְצָא בֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה כּוּלּוֹ קֹדֶשׁ
and consequently in truth Yitzchak was entirely holy!
וּלְעָתִיד כְּשֶׁיְּבוֹרַר זֶה, יִהְיֶה הוּא רֹאשׁ הַהַנְהָגָה כַּנּוֹדָע מֵהָאֲרִיזַ״ל
And in the Future when this is clarified, Yitzchak will be the head of divine governance as known from the Arizal;
וְנִרְמַז בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שַׁבָּת פ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳ עַל פָּסוּק ״כִּי אַתָּה אָבִינוּ״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ס״ג:ט״ז)
alluded to in Shabbat (89b) on the verse "For You are our Father" (Yeshayah 63:16);
וְהוּא מַחְוֵי לְהוּ אָז הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעֵינַיְיהוּ כִּדְאִיתָא הָתָם
where Yitzchak points out the Holy One directly to their eyes;
כִּי זֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּיִצְחָק, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיָה סוֹמָא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הֶחָשׁוּב כְּמֵת (נְדָרִים ס״ד עַמּוּד ב׳)
for this is the spiritual rung of Yitzchak, on account of which he was blind in this world (Bereishis 27:1), the blind being accounted as dead (Nedarim 64b);
שֶׁנִּסְתַּלֵּק מִמֶּנּוּ חֵיזוּ דְּהַאי עָלְמָא, עַל יְדֵי דִּבִשְׁעַת מִיתָתָן רוֹאִין הַשְּׁכִינָה (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה י״ד:ג׳)
worldly vision having departed from him, seeing that at the hour of death mortals behold the Shechinah (Bamidbar Rabbah 14:3);
וְכֵן הוּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁרָאָה בִּשְׁעַת עֲקֵידָה כִּמְשַׁאזַ״ל (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס״ה:י׳)
and so through having beheld the Shechinah at the Binding (Bereishis Rabbah 65:10),
זָכָה לִרְאִיָּה כָּזוֹ בְּעֵת הַזִּקְנָה
he merited such vision in old age;
כְּשֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְתַכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּתוֹ, חַיִּים שֶׁלֹּא בְּצַעַר וְשֶׁלֹּא בְּיֵצֶר הָרָע, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (פֶּרֶק ה׳), שֶׁהוּא מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא
reaching his consummate perfection: a life without sorrow and without the yetzer hara (Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah, ch. 5), which is a foretaste of the World to Come;
דְּעַל יְדֵי תֹּקֶף הַיִּרְאָה זָכָה לִקְדֻשַּׁת הָרְאִיָּה דְּעַיִן בְּעַיִן
through the intensity of awe meriting the holy sight of "eye to eye";
וְכֵן לֶעָתִיד: ״[כִּי] עַיִן בְּעַיִן יִרְאוּ בְּשׁוּב ה׳ צִיּוֹן״ (יְשַׁעְיָה נ״ב:ח׳), דְּאָז ״יִמָּלֵא שְׂחוֹק פִּינוּ״ (תְּהִלִּים קכ״ו:ב׳)
and so in the Future: "for they shall see eye to eye, when Hashem returns to Zion" (Yeshayah 52:8), when "our mouth will be filled with laughter" (Tehillim 126:2);
שֶׁיִּתְרַבֶּה הַצְּחוֹק בָּעוֹלָם בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת וְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ
laughter abounding in the world through the manifestation of Yitzchak's rung.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם סוֹף סוֹף מִצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וּתְחִלַּת בְּרִיאָתוֹ
Nevertheless, from the perspective of this earthly world and its initial creation;
מֵאַחַר דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם יָצָא מִמֶּנּוּ עֵשָׂו, הֲרֵי לֹא הָיָה מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה
since Esav issued from him, his bed was not unblemished;
וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן קוֹדֶם שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ דְּעַדַיִין הָיָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה גָּנוּז בּוֹ
and all the more so prior to Esav's birth when this root was still concealed within him;
וְעַל כֵּן נִכְתְּבוּ גַּם דִּבְרֵי הַמַּלְאָכִים, שֶׁגַּם דִּבְרֵיהֶם אֱמֶת לִשְׁעָתֵיהּ:
wherefore the words of the angels were likewise recorded in Scripture, their words being true for that hour.

13.h: The theme: Sarah's laughter in her inwardness (b'kirbah), the fear of sin, and the root of Amalek. The angels attributing the son to Sarah aroused the unholy dimension of laughter—the root of Amalek from the seed of Esav who scoffs at divine truth. From this derived: "And Sarah laughed within herself (va-titzchak Sarah b'kirbah), saying: After I am waxed old shall I have pleasure?" (Bereishis 18:12). God forbid that Sarah doubted Hashem's omnipotence; rather, "within herself" (b'kirbah) means that from the perspective of her own personal merit it seemed impossible. Sarah reasoned: if during her youth when her physical strength was vigorous in divine service she did not merit a child, how could she merit it now in old age when bodily strength had waned? This was akin to Yaakov Avinu fearing lest sin cause him to forfeit the promise (Berachos 4a). She assumed that bringing down so exalted a soul required intense physical toil (hishtadlus), and added: "and my lord is old also" (Bereishis 18:12), assuming Avraham's bodily strength had likewise waned. While aging scholars increase in wisdom (Shabbat 152a), bodily strength to perform physical deeds in this world weakens with age. Hashem responded: "Is anything too wondrous for Hashem?" (Bereishis 18:14)—meaning: the limits of human exertion are fully known to Me, yet My grace operates beyond human power. Hashem took issue with Sarah because this subtle deficiency in her faith derived from the dross destined to issue from Yitzchak [Esav], which had not yet been separated and refined.

p: וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיָה הִתְעוֹרְרוּת לְמִדַּת הַצְּחוֹק דְּמִצַּד הָרָע
And through this was aroused the attribute of laughter from the side of evil;
שֶׁהוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ דַּעֲמָלֵק שֶׁמִּזֶּרַע עֵשָׂו הַמַּלְעִיג עַל דִּבְרֵי אֱמֶת
which is the root of Amalek descended from Esav, who mocks words of sacred truth;
וּמִזֶּה נִמְשַׁךְ: ״וַתִּצְחַק שָׂרָה בְּקִרְבָּהּ [לֵאמֹר: אַחֲרֵי בְלֹתִי הָיְתָה לִּי עֶדְנָה וַאדֹנִי זָקֵן]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ח:י״ב)
and from this derived: "And Sarah laughed within herself, saying: After I am waxed old shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?" (Bereishis 18:12);
שֶׁזֶּה כְּבִלְתִּי מַאֲמִין וְצוֹחֵק דֶּרֶךְ הַלְעָגָה עַל דִּבְרֵי אֱמֶת
this appearing like one who does not believe and laughs in mockery over words of truth;
וְחָלִילָה שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה מַאֲמֶנֶת בִּיכֹלֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and God forbid that Sarah did not believe in the omnipotence of the Blessed Name!
אֲבָל ״בְּקִרְבָּהּ״ דַּיְיקָא, שֶׁמִּצַּד עַצְמָהּ הָיָה רָחוֹק אֶצְלָהּ זֶה, שֶׁאָמְרָה ״אַחֲרֵי בְלֹתִי וְגוֹמֵר״
But "within herself" (b'kirbah) specifically: from her own personal perspective it seemed remote, saying "after I am waxed old";
רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁהֶחֱזִיקָה עַצְמָהּ שֶׁבִּנְעוּרֶיהָ הִשְׁתַּדְּלָה הַרְבֵּה יוֹתֵר בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִבְּזִקְנוּתָהּ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהּ עוֹד כֹּחַ כָּל כָּךְ
meaning that she evaluated herself: in her youth she had exerted herself far more vigorously in divine service than in her old age when her physical strength was diminished;
וְאִם בְּיַלְדוּתָהּ לֹא זָכְתָה לָזֶה, אֵיךְ תִּזְכֶּה לְכָךְ עַתָּה שֶׁאֵין עוֹבֶדֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּל כָּךְ וְאֵין מַעֲשֶׂיהָ כְּדָאִים כָּל כָּךְ
and if in her youth she had not merited a child, how could she merit it now when her bodily strength was weak and her deeds seemingly less worthy?
וַהֲרֵי זֶה עַל דֶּרֶךְ יִרְאַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם ״שֶׁמָּא יִגְרוֹם הַחֵטְא״ (בְּרָכוֹת ד׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּבְטַח
and behold, this follows the pattern of Yaakov Avinu who feared "lest sin cause the promise to be withheld" (Berachos 4b) even though he had been divinely promised;
וְכֵן הִיא חָשְׁבָה: אַף דְּהַהַבְטָחָה אֱמֶת, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הִיא צְרִיכָה הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לָזֶה גַּם כֵּן
and so Sarah reasoned: even though the promise is true, it still requires human striving to receive it;
וּבִשְּׂרוּם שֶׁאִם עַתָּה גַּם כֵּן יוּגְעוּ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם כִּבִימֵי נְעוּרֵיהֶם, יַעֲלֶה בְּיָדָם לְהַמְשִׁיךְ שֶׁפַע הַקְּדוּשָׁה בְּנֶפֶשׁ יְקָרָה שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ יִבָּנֶה אוּמָּה קְדוֹשָׁה
the angels announcing that if they would now exert themselves as in their youth, they would succeed in drawing down the influx of holiness into an exalted soul from whom a holy nation would be built,
שֶׁעַל זֶה הָיָה כָּל תַּכְלִית מְבוּקָּשָׁם בְּהוֹלָדַת בֵּן
this being their entire objective in desiring a son.
אֲבָל הִיא הִרְגִּישָׁה בְּנַפְשָׁהּ חוּלְשַׁת הַכֹּחוֹת לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִפְּנֵי הַזִּקְנָה, וְאָמְרָה: ״וַאדֹנִי זָקֵן״
But Sarah felt in her body the weakening of physical faculties for divine service due to advanced age, and said: "my lord is old also";
שֶׁלֹּא אוּכַל לִתְלוֹת גַּם כֵּן שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הוּא הַמִּתְגַּבֵּר כָּל כָּךְ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וַעֲבוֹדָה עַתָּה, שֶׁגַּם הוּא כְּבָר הִזְקִין וְתַשׁ כֹּחוֹ
meaning: I cannot rely upon my husband to supply that intense bodily exertion now, for he too has grown old and his physical strength has waned;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁ״זִקְנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים... מוֹסִיפִין חָכְמָה״ (שַׁבָּת קנ״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
and although "elderly Torah scholars add wisdom as they age" (Shabbat 152a);
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַכֹּחַ לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁמִּצַּד הַגּוּף, שֶׁזֶּהוּ הָעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
nevertheless the capacity for divine service from the physical body, which is the labor of this world,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל לִזְכּוֹת לַהַטּוֹבוֹת וּבְרָכוֹת שֶׁמִּצַּד הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁהוּא בִּרְכַּת ה׳ בָּנִים דְּגַם כֵּן הוּא רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
through which one merits the earthly blessings of this world, such as children which exist only in this life;
וּמִצַּד הַגּוּף דָּבָר זֶה נֶחְלַשׁ עַל יְדֵי הַזִּקְנָה, וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה אֶצְלָהּ רָחוֹק שֶׁיִּתְקַיֵּים
and regarding the body this faculty weakens through old age, wherefore it seemed to her remote that it could be realized.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: ״הֲיִפָּלֵא מֵה׳ דָּבָר״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ח:י״ד)
And concerning this the Blessed Name answered: "Is anything too wondrous for Hashem?" (Bereishis 18:14);
רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא נֶעְלַם מִמֶּנִּי דָּבָר זֶה, שֶׁגַּם אֲנִי יוֹדֵעַ כֹּחַ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם
meaning: this limitation is not concealed from Me, for I too know the natural boundaries of their striving;
וְעַל כֵּן חָרָה לוֹ עַל זֶה, כִּי יָדַע הַחִסָּרוֹן זֶה שֶׁבֶּאֱמוּנָתָהּ נִמְשַׁךְ לָהּ וְנִתְגַּלָּה לְפֹעַל בְּקִרְבָּהּ
and therefore Hashem took issue with this, because He knew that this subtle deficiency in her faith was drawn unto her and revealed within her,
עַל יְדֵי הַפְּסֹולֶת שֶׁעָתִיד לָצֵאת מִיִּצְחָק שֶׁעֲדַיִין לֹא נִפְרַשׁ וְנִתְבָּרַר:
through the dross destined to issue from Yitzchak [Esav] which had not yet been separated and refined!

13.h: The theme: Sarah's denial, the root cause of her laughter, and Yishmael's unholy mockery (metzachek). When Hashem Himself addressed Avraham, He likewise said: "and Sarah shall have a son" (Bereishis 18:14), attributing the offspring to the feminine side. When Sarah denied it saying "I laughed not; for she was afraid" (ibid. 18:15), she did not speak a falsehood before the Knower of hearts; rather, she defended herself by explaining that her laughter was not cynical derision, but arose from holy awe—trembling lest she lacked the physical strength and merit for so momentous a promise. Hashem countered: "Nay; but you did laugh" (ibid.), for the primal trigger was the awakening of laughter descending into the realm of the Sitra Achra where "her feet go down to death" (Mishlei 5:5). Once Yitzchak was born, laughter spread throughout the cosmos ("all that hear will laugh with me", Bereishis 21:6), and the other side immediately seized its share. When Yitzchak was weaned, Sarah saw Yishmael "mocking" (metzachek, Bereishis 21:9), which Chazal interpret as the three cardinal sins: idolatry, sexual immorality, and bloodshed (Bereishis Rabbah 53:11). These parallel the three cosmic dimensions of World, Year, and Soul: sexual immorality is laughter with creatures; bloodshed is laughter over creatures; and idolatry is the spleen (tchol) in the soul uniting male and female in corruption—the "strange god within the body of man" (Shabbat 105b), which is the root of Amalek, "first of the nations." Anger and lust lead directly to idolatry (Shabbat 105b; Sanhedrin 63b). Sarah immediately perceived that Yishmael must be cast out so as not to defile Yitzchak, who brought into the world only the laughter of holiness.

p: וְעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר שָׁם עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַצְמוֹ גַּם כֵּן: ״וּלְשָׂרָה בֵן״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ח:י״ד), יִחֲסוּ לְנוּקְבָא מִצַּד זֶה
And therefore it was said there by the Blessed Name Himself likewise: "and Sarah shall have a son" (Bereishis 18:14), attributing him to the feminine side (Nukva) from this aspect;
וְהִיא הִכְחִישָׁה ״כִּי יָרֵאָה״ (שָׁם:ט״ו)
and she denied it, "for she was afraid" (ibid. 18:15);
וְחָלִילָה לָהּ לְדַבֵּר שֶׁקֶר, וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן לִפְנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיָּדְעָה שֶׁהוּא בּוֹחֵן לִבּוֹת
and God forbid that she should speak a falsehood, and all the more so before the Blessed Name Whom she knew examines all hearts;
וְגַם עִיקַּר הַצְּחוֹק הָיָה בְּקִרְבָּהּ וְלֹא נוֹדַע לַבְּרִיּוֹת רַק מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גִּילָּהוּ לְאַבְרָהָם, וְאֵיךְ תַּכְחִישׁוּ
and moreover the primary laughter occurred within herself and was unknown to creatures except that the Blessed Name revealed it to Avraham, so how could she deny it?
רַק הַכַּוָּונָה: שֶׁהִיא הִתְנַצְּלָה לוֹמַר: לֹא צָחַקְתִּי דֶּרֶךְ מַלְעִיג וּבִלְתִּי מַאֲמִין כְּלָל
Rather, the meaning is: she offered an apology saying: I did not laugh in mockery or as one who disbelieves at all;
אֶלָּא ״כִּי יָרֵאָה״, וּמִצַּד הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁמָּא לֹא תוּכַל לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּפִי הָרָאוּי לְהַבְטָחָה כָּזוֹ, הוּא שֶׁצָּחֲקָה
but "because she feared," and out of holy fear lest she be unable to exert herself in divine service as is fitting for such a promise, she laughed;
וְכֵן הָיָה הָאֱמֶת כְּדַעְתָּהּ
and such was indeed the truth according to her perspective;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם נֶחְשַׁב זֶה הַכְחָשָׁה כְּלַפֵּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא הַיּוֹדֵעַ מַעֲמַקֵּי לִבָּהּ
nevertheless this was accounted a denial before the Blessed Name Who knows the inward depths of her heart;
וְיָדַע שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהּ לִירָא מִזֶּה כְּפִי תֹּקֶף אֱמוּנָתָהּ
knowing that she ought not to have feared this given the powerful intensity of her faith;
אֶלָּא שֶׁהִתְעוֹרְרוּת מִדַּת הַצְּחוֹק וְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּתוֹ עַד סִטְרָא דְּרָע וְ״רַגְלַיִן הַיּוֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת״ (מִשְׁלֵי ה:ה) לְלֵיצָנוּת וְהַלְעָגָה, הוּא שֶׁגָּרַם לָזֶה
but the awakening of the attribute of laughter and its downward expansion unto the side of evil and the "feet that descend unto death" (Mishlei 5:5) into mockery and derision, was what caused this;
עַל כֵּן אָמַר: ״לֹא כִּי צָחָקְתְּ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ח:ט״ו), שֶׁהַצְּחוֹק וְהִתְעוֹרְרוּתוֹ הוּא הָיָה הַגּוֹרֵם זֶה, לֹא הַיִּרְאָה
wherefore Hashem replied: "Nay; but you did laugh" (Bereishis 18:15), for the laughter and its awakening was the true cause, not the fear.
וְאַחַר שֶׁנּוֹלַד יִצְחָק וְנִתְפַּשֵּׁט הַצְּחוֹק בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם, דְּ״כָּל הַשֹּׁמֵעַ [יִצְחַק לִי] וְגוֹמֵר״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״א:ו׳)
And after Yitzchak was born and laughter spread throughout the entire world, for "all that hear will laugh with me, etc." (Bereishis 21:6);
אָז תֵּיכֶף נִתְפַּשֵּׁט בְּכָל סִטְרִין עַד שֶׁסִּטְרָא דְּרָע קָלַט אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ
then immediately it expanded unto all sides until the Sitra Achra [the Other Side] captured its share;
וְנֶאֱמַר שָׁם מִיָּד אַחַר שֶׁנִּגְמַל יִצְחָק, שֶׁהוּא כְּשֶׁנִּתְפַּשֵּׁט מִדַּת עַצְמִיּוּתוֹ וְנִפְרַשׁ מִשְּׁדֵי אִמּוֹ מִלִּהְיוֹת גָּדֵל עוֹד עַל מִדַּת אֲבוֹתָיו

and it is stated there immediately after Yitzchak was weaned (Bereishis 21:8)—which was when his essential attribute expanded and he parted from his mother's breasts, no longer being nurtured solely upon the attribute of his parents;
אָז: ״וַתֵּרֶא שָׂרָה אֶת בֶּן הָגָר [הַמִּצְרִית אֲשֶׁר יָלְדָה לְאַבְרָהָם] מְצַחֵק״ (שָׁם:ט׳)
then: "And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne unto Abraham, mocking (metzachek)" (ibid. 21:9);
וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה נ״ג:י״א): ״אֵין ׳מְצַחֵק׳ אֶלָּא עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, גִּלּוּי עֲרָיוֹת, וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים״
and the Sages expounded in Bereishis Rabbah (53:11): "'Mocking' (metzachek) denotes nothing other than idolatry, sexual immorality, and bloodshed";
וְהֵם שְׁלֹשָׁה מִינֵי צְחוֹק נֶגֶד הַג׳ דְּעוֹלָם, שָׁנָה, נֶפֶשׁ הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
and these are three categories of unholy laughter corresponding to World, Year, and Soul mentioned above:
גִּלּוּי עֲרָיוֹת הוּא ״עִם בְּרִיּוֹתָיו״, וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים הוּא ״עַל בְּרִיּוֹתָיו״
sexual immorality is laughter with creatures [corrupt union], and bloodshed is laughter over creatures [destruction];
וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הוּא דּוּגְמַת טְחוֹל שֶׁבַּנֶּפֶשׁ הַכּוֹלְלָם יַחַד זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה
and idolatry mirrors the spleen (tchol) in the soul which encompasses them both together, male and female;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָ״אֵל זָר״ שֶׁבְּגוּפוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם (שַׁבָּת ק״ה עַמּוּד ב׳), שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק ״רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ד:כ׳) שֶׁכָּלוּל מִשְּׁנֵיהֶם
this being the root of the "strange god" within the body of man (Shabbat 105b), which is the root of Amalek, "first of the nations," encompassing both traits;
דְּאָפְיָם שֶׁל כְּלַל הָאוּמּוֹת וְכָל מִינֵי רָע שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם שָׁרְשָׁם בְּכַעַס וְתַאֲוָה, שֶׁעֲלֵיהֶם אַזְהָרַת ״לֹא תִרְצַח״ וְ״לֹא תִנְאָף״ (שְׁמוֹת כ:יג)

for the character of the nations and all evil in the world is rooted in anger and lust, concerning which stand the prohibitions "You shall not murder" and "You shall not commit adultery" (Shemos 20:13);
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ שָׁרְשָׁם הוּא ״אָנֹכִי״ וְ״לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ״ (שָׁם:ב׳–ג׳)
and the root of their root is the first two commandments: "I am Hashem" and "You shall have no other gods" (ibid. 20:2–3);
כִּי עַל שְׁנֵיהֶם מָצִינוּ בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁמְּבִיאִים לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
for regarding both anger and lust we find in the words of the Sages that they lead directly to idolatry:
עַל כַּעַס בְּשַׁבָּת (ק״ה עַמּוּד ב׳) גַּבֵּי שׁוֹבֵר כְּלִי בַּחֲמָתוֹ: ״כָּךְ דַּרְכּוֹ שֶׁל יֵצֶר הָרָע וְכוּלֵיהּ עַד וְכוּלֵיהּ״
on anger in Shabbat (105b) regarding one who breaks a vessel in wrath: "Such is the craft of the yetzer hara: today it says to him do this, until tomorrow it says go serve idols";
וְכַלָּשׁוֹן זֶה גַּם כֵּן גַּבֵּי תַּאֲוָה בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כָּל הַיָּד (נִדָּה י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳)
and with this exact phrasing likewise regarding lust in Niddah (13b);
וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ס״ג עַמּוּד ב׳): ״לֹא עָבְדוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֶלָּא לְהַתִּיר לָהֶם עֲרָיוֹת [בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא]״
and so is it taught in Sanhedrin (63b): "Israel served idols only to permit themselves public sexual immorality."
וְתֵיכֶף אָמְרָה שָׂרָה: ״[כִּי] לֹא יִירַשׁ [בֶּן הָאָמָה הַזֹּאת] עִם בְּנִי עִם יִצְחָק״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״א:י׳) דַּיְיקָא
And immediately Sarah declared: "for the son of this bondwoman shall not be heir with my son, even with Isaac" (Bereishis 21:10) specifically;
שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא הֵבִיא הַצְּחוֹק לָעוֹלָם וּמֵחֲמָתוֹ הָיָה, הִרְגִּישָׁה מִיָּד שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהַפְרִידוֹ וּלְהַבְדִּילוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ שׁוּם הִתְחַבְּרוּת וְשַׁיָּיכוּת עִמּוֹ

for even though Yitzchak brought laughter into the world and on his account it emerged, she sensed immediately that Yishmael must be severed and separated so that he have no attachment or connection with him;
כִּי הוּא אֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לִצְחוֹק זֶה דְּרָע כְּלָל
for Yitzchak has no connection to this evil laughter at all;
כִּי הוּא עוֹרֵר בָּעוֹלָם רַק הַצְּחוֹק שֶׁמִּסִּטְרָא דִּקְדֻשָּׁה לְבַד
having awakened in the world exclusively the laughter of the side of holiness;
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּצַּד הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת דְּטוֹב וָרָע בָּעוֹלָם מֵחֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן, בְּכָל דָּבָר שֶׁמִּתְגַּלֶּה הַטּוֹב מִיָּד מִתְגַּלֶּה גַּם הָרָע שֶׁלְּעֻומָּתוֹ:
except that through the mixture of good and evil in the cosmos resulting from the sin of Adam HaRishon, whenever good is revealed, immediately the corresponding evil opposite it is likewise revealed!

13.h: The theme: Yitzchak sporting with Rivkah (metzachek), the status of Esav, and Bar Koziba removing the spleen. In Gerar, Scripture records: "and, behold, Isaac was sporting (metzachek) with Rebekah his wife" (Bereishis 26:8). The Midrash explains this occurred after the prolonged mourning for Avraham Avinu (Bereishis Rabbah 64:5), on the day of whose death Esav turned to evil ways (ibid. 63:12) and was severed from the seed of Yitzchak. In Kiddushin (18a) the Gemara states that Esav had the status of an apostate Jew (Yisrael mumar): prior to his apostasy he bore the name of Israel and was circumcised on the eighth day. Although an ordinary Jew remains an Israelite even after sinning (Yisrael af al pi she-chata Yisrael hu, Sanhedrin 44a), that applies strictly to the seed of Yaakov whose three-ply cord can never be severed; in the seed of Yitzchak, when Esav apostatized, he departed from Israel entirely. Once that dross was severed, Yitzchak's holiness became manifest, his marital joy with Rivkah reflecting holy Gevurot—rejoicing out of awe and awing out of joy (Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah, ch. 3). In holiness, anger and love are unified; in unholiness, they are severed. Yitzchak encompassed both the liver (kaved, bloodshed/Esav) and the spleen (tchol, mockery/Amalek). The liver is vital to life (if punctured entirely, the animal is a treifah), corresponding to the primary attribute of Gevurah; the spleen is secondary (an animal whose spleen is removed remains kosher). Bar Koziba (Bar Kochba) had 60,000 soldiers with their spleens removed (netulei tchol) and their toes engraved (cf. Yerushalmi Ta'anit 4:5; Eichah Rabbah 2:4). Believing he was the Messiah destined to eradicate Amalek (the cosmic spleen), Bar Koziba assumed the spleen was an unnecessary organ destined to be excised, believing the conquerors of Amalek must be their exact physical opposite, like Yosef ("I fear God", Bereishis 42:18) vanquishing Amalek ("and he feared not God", Devarim 25:18; Bava Batra 123b).

p: וּבְיִצְחָק נִמְצָא לְשׁוֹן ״מְצַחֵק״ אַחַר כָּךְ בִּגְרָר: ״וְהִנֵּה יִצְחָק מְצַחֵק [אֵת רִבְקָה אִשְׁתּוֹ] וְגוֹמֵר״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ו:ח׳)
And regarding Yitzchak we find the expression "sporting" (metzachek) subsequently in Gerar: "and, behold, Isaac was sporting with Rebekah his wife, etc." (Bereishis 26:8);
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס״ד:ה׳): דְּהָיָה אַחַר אֲרִיכוּת יָמִים דַּאֲבֵילוּת דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and the Sages expounded (Bereishis Rabbah 64:5): that this occurred after the prolonged days of mourning for Avraham Avinu;
שֶׁבְּיוֹם שֶׁמֵּת יָצָא עֵשָׂו לְתַרְבּוּת רָעָה (שָׁם פָּרָשָׁה ס״ג:י״ב), וְנִפְרַד מִלִּהְיוֹת נִקְרָא עוֹד זֶרַע יִצְחָק
on the day of whose death Esav went out to evil ways (ibid. 63:12) and was severed from being termed the seed of Yitzchak;
וּבְקִדּוּשִׁין (י״ח עַמּוּד א׳) אִיתָא: דְּעֵשָׂו ״יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר״
and in Kiddushin (18a) it is taught: that Esav had the legal status of an "apostate Israelite";
וְהַיְינוּ דְּקוֹדֶם שֶׁיָּצָא לְתַרְבּוּת רָעָה הָיָה עָלָיו שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנִימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה, אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּמֵּד
meaning that prior to his apostasy he bore the name of Israel and was circumcised on the eighth day, but then apostatized;
וְאַף דִּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם מוּמָר: ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא — יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין מ״ד עַמּוּד א׳)
and although in an Israelite even an apostate remains an Israelite ("even though he has sinned, he is an Israelite", Sanhedrin 44a);
זֶהוּ רַק בְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב שֶׁכְּבָר נִפְקַע חֶבֶל הַנַּחֲלָה בְּג׳ חוּטִין דְּאֵין יָכוֹל לִינָּתֵק עוֹד
that holds true strictly in the seed of Yaakov whose inheritance was bound in a three-ply cord that can never be severed;
אֲבָל בְּזֶרַע יִצְחָק, אַף דְּהָיָה נִקְרָא תְּחִלָּה בְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל, מִשֶּׁנִּשְׁתַּמֵּד וְיָצָא לְתַרְבּוּת רָעָה יָצָא מִכְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
but in the seed of Yitzchak, although originally called an Israelite, once he apostatized he departed from the collective of Israel entirely;
וְאָז שֶׁכְּבָר נִפְרַד הַפְּסֹולֶת שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עוֹד שַׁיָּיכוּת עִמּוֹ, הִתְחִיל לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת קְדוּשָׁתוֹ
and then, when the dross was severed having no further connection with him, Yitzchak's sanctity began to be manifest.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהָאֲבֵילוּת עִכֵּב, שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ הַשִּׂמְחָה וְהַצְּחוֹק דִּילֵיהּ שֶׁהוּא ״עִם בְּרִיּוֹתָיו״ הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מֵהַשִּׂמְחָה
However, the mourning for Avraham delayed this, mourning being the antithesis of joy and Yitzchak's holy laughter with his creatures which flows from joy;
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא בִּקְדֻשָּׁה, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג׳): ״אֲנִי יָרֵאתִי מִתּוֹךְ שִׂמְחָתִי וְשָׂמַחְתִּי מִתּוֹךְ יִרְאָתִי״
and this manifests in holiness, as written in Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah (ch. 3): "I awed out of my joy and I rejoiced out of my awe";
כִּי הַגְּבוּרוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת הוּא תֹּקֶף הַיִּרְאָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּגִין דְּאִיהוּ רַב וְשַׁלִּיט (זֹוהַר חֵלֶק א׳ י״א עַמּוּד ב׳), וְיֵשׁ לוֹ שִׂמְחָה גַּם כֵּן מִזֶּה
for holy Gevurot are the intense awe of the Blessed Name because He is great and sovereign (Zohar I, 11b), from which awe one derives supreme joy;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַגְּבוּרָה רָעָה שֶׁבְּכַעַס וּרְצִיחָה הִיא הֵיפֶךְ הַשִּׂמְחָה
whereas the evil Gevurah of anger and murder is the direct opposite of joy;
וְהַצְּחוֹק הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מִמֶּנָּה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא ״עַל בְּרִיּוֹתָיו״ בְּלֵיצָנוּת
and the laughter drawn from it is solely over creatures in cynical mockery;
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל מִינֵי רָע יֵשׁ לָהֶם חִבּוּר, וְהָיָה עֵשָׂו פָּרוּץ בַּעֲרָיוֹת גַּם כֵּן
nevertheless all modes of evil are interconnected, and Esav was steeped in sexual immorality as well;
וְעַל כֵּן נָשָׂא בַּת יִשְׁמָעֵאל (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ח:ט׳), אֲבָל זֶהוּ רַק עַל דֶּרֶךְ ״עֲבֵירָה גּוֹרֶרֶת עֲבֵירָה״ (אָבוֹת ד:ב)
wherefore he married the daughter of Yishmael (Bereishis 28:9), this following the principle of "one transgression drags another transgression in its wake" (Avos 4:2);
אֲבָל שׁוֹרֶשׁ רִשְׁעוּתוֹ בִּרְצִיחָה הוּא אַדְּרַבָּא הֵיפֶךְ מִתַּאֲוָה
yet the core root of his wickedness was bloodshed, which is the antithesis of lust;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּקְדֻשָּׁה הֵם כְּלוּלִים יַחַד מַמָּשׁ
unlike in holiness where awe and love are harmoniously integrated together.
וְעַל כֵּן נִרְאֶה שֶׁמִּדַּת יִצְחָק בִּכְלַל הָעוֹלָם הוּא נֶגֶד ב׳ אֵבְרֵי הַכָּבֵד וּטְחוֹל שֶׁבְּעוֹלָם קָטָן שֶׁהוּא הָאָדָם
And therefore it appears that the attribute of Yitzchak in the macrocosm corresponds to the two organs of the liver and the spleen within the human microcosm;
וְאֶצְלוֹ הָיוּ כְּלוּלִים שְׁנֵיהֶם יַחַד
and within Yitzchak both were unified together in holiness;
וְכֵן בִּפְסֹולְתּוֹ יָצָא הַפְּסֹולֶת שֶׁבִּשְׁנֵי אֵיבָרִים אֵלּוּ
and likewise from his dross issued the corruption of these two organs;
אֶלָּא דְּשָׁם לֹא הָיוּ כְּלוּלִים יַחַד, רַק נִתְחַלְּקוּ לִשְׁנַיִם, שֶׁמִּצַּד הָרָע הֵם נִפְרָדִים וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר
except that in evil they were not unified, but divided into two separate entities, being alienated from one another as explained;
וְהֵם עֵשָׂו וַעֲמָלֵק שֶׁהֵם נֶגֶד הָרָע שֶׁבִּשְׁנֵיהֶם
these being Esav [the liver] and Amalek [the spleen], corresponding to the evil in both;
וְהַכָּבֵד הוּא אֵבֶר שֶׁהַחַיּוּת תָּלוּי בּוֹ, שֶׁאִם נִיטַּל כּוּלּוֹ — טְרֵיפָה (חֻלִּין מ״ו עַמּוּד א׳)
and the liver is a vital organ upon which life depends, where if it is entirely removed the animal is a treifah (Chullin 46a);
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר מִדַּת הַגְּבוּרָה שֶׁהוּא מִכְּלַל עֶשֶׂר מִדּוֹת הַקּוֹמָה
this being the primary attribute of Gevurah among the ten Sefirotic attributes;
וְהַטְּחוֹל אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא נִטְפָּל לוֹ, שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵין הַחַיּוּת תָּלוּי בּוֹ כָּל כָּךְ, שֶׁהֲרֵי אִם נִיטַּל כּוּלּוֹ — כְּשֵׁרָה וִיכוֹלָה לִחְיוֹת (שָׁם נ״ד עַמּוּד ב׳)
while the spleen is merely secondary to it, physical life not depending upon it critically, for if it is entirely removed the animal is kosher and can live (ibid. 54b).
וְאָז בְּבֶן כּוֹזִיבָא דְּהָיָה לוֹ שִׁשִּׁים אֶלֶף נְטוּלֵי טְחוֹל וַחֲקוּקֵי כַּפּוֹת רַגְלַיִם
And regarding Ben Koziba who commanded 60,000 soldiers with their spleens excised and their feet engraved (cf. Yerushalmi Ta'anit 4:5; Eichah Rabbah 2:4);
נִרְאֶה לִי לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁהוּא מָשִׁיחַ, וְיִהְיֶה מְחִיַּיִת זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק לְגַמְרֵי עַל יָדוֹ
it appears to me that because he assumed he was Mashiach through whom the seed of Amalek would be wiped out entirely;
וְיָדַע דַּעֲמָלֵק נֶגֶד הַטְּחוֹל וְהוּא יִמָּחֶה לְגַמְרֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִשָּׁאֵר מִמֶּנּוּ כְּלוּם
and knowing that Amalek corresponds to the spleen, destined to be blotted out until nothing remains;
סָבוּר שֶׁכְּמוֹ כֵן זֶה הָאֵבֶר בָּאָדָם הוּא מֵהַמּוֹתָרוֹת שֶׁסּוֹפוֹ לִמְחוֹת
he reasoned that this bodily organ is likewise a superfluity destined to be abolished;
וְלֶעָתִיד לֹא יִהְיֶה אֵבֶר זֶה בָּאָדָם, וְעַל כֵּן בְּמִלְחַמְתּוֹ עִמָּהֶם חָשַׁב דְּהַמְנַצְּחִים צְרִיכִים לִהְיוֹת הָפְכִיִּים מַמָּשׁ מֵהֶם
and that in the Future this organ will not exist in man, wherefore in battling Amalek he assumed that the victors must be their exact physical antithesis;
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכ״ג עַמּוּד ב׳; בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ע״ג:ז׳): ״אֵין עֲמָלֵק נוֹפֵל אֶלָּא בְּיַד זַרְעָהּ שֶׁל רָחֵל״
wherefore the Sages stated (Bava Batra 123b; Bereishis Rabbah 73:7): "Amalek falls only by the hand of the descendants of Rachel";
דְּבֵיהּ כְּתִיב ״וְלֹא יָרֵא אֱלֹהִים״ (דְּבָרִים כ״ה:י״ח), וּבְיוֹסֵף נֶאֱמַר ״אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים אֲנִי יָרֵא״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית מ״ב:י״ח)
for of Amalek it is written "and he feared not God" (Devarim 25:18), while of Yosef it is said "I fear God" (Bereishis 42:18);
שֶׁהוּא הֶפְכּוֹ, וְעַל כֵּן יוּכַל לְנַצְּחוֹ:
Yosef being his polar opposite, and therefore able to vanquish him!

13.h: The theme: The heaviness of the spleen, the battle of Rephidim, the heavy hands of Moshe, and the error of Bar Koziba. The spleen weighs down upon man: all spiritual lethargy and sluggishness toward Torah and mitzvos derive from Amalek, who injects thoughts of cynicism and mockery into the heart. Through this, the heart weakens, reflecting the nature of the yetzer hara which "descends and incites, ascends and accuses, descends and takes the soul" (Bava Batra 16a). This unfolded at Rephidim, where Israel's hands slackened (rafu yedeihem) from words of Torah (Bechorot 5b); immediately, Amalek arrived to wage physical war (Shemos 17:8). Israel is the heart of the cosmos; their spiritual laxity weighed down even Moshe Rabbeinu ("and Moses' hands were heavy", Shemos 17:12), for the leader reflects the generation (Arachin 17a). While in Israel the weight penetrated the heart, in Moshe it touched only the physical hands. When Moshe raised his hands toward Heaven, Israel prevailed (Rosh Hashanah 29a), for the leader of the generation infuses divine awakening into his people. Haman likewise accused Israel: "there is a people scattered abroad... asleep from the commandments" (Megillah 13b). Bar Koziba erred in removing the spleens and incising the feet of his soldiers to eradicate slothfulness and sin; the Sages rebuked him: "How long will you turn Israel into blemish-ridden men?" (Yerushalmi Ta'anit 4:5). Hashem created nothing in vain, and all bodily organs—even the spleen and the soles of the feet—exist for the sake of holiness and the honor of Heaven (kol pa'al Hashem la-ma'anehu, Mishlei 16:4). Where the nations manifest absolute defilement, Israel reveals supreme holiness.

p: וְהַטְּחוֹל מַכְבִּיד עַל הָאָדָם
And the spleen weighs heavily upon man;
כִּי כָל הַכֹּובֶד וְהָעַצְלוּת שֶׁבָּאָדָם לְתוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת בָּא מֵעֲמָלֵק, שֶׁמַּכְנִיס הִרְהוּרֵי לֵיצָנוּת לַלֵּב
for all the heaviness and lethargy within a person toward Torah and mitzvos derive from Amalek, who injects thoughts of mockery into the heart;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הַלֵּב מִתְרַפֶּה וּמִתְעַצֵּל מֵהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בַּתּוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and through this the heart becomes faint and sluggish from striving in Torah and the service of the Blessed Name;
וּתְחִלָּה הוּא פּוֹעֵל בַּלֵּב וְאַחַר כָּךְ הוּא בָּא וְנִלְחָם
and initially he operates within the heart, and afterward he comes and wages open war;
כְּמִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל יֵצֶר הָרָע: ״יוֹרֵד וּמֵסִית, עוֹלֶה וּמַקְטְרִיג, יוֹרֵד וְנוֹטֵל נְשָׁמָה״ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ט״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
matching the strategy of the yetzer hara: "it descends and seduces, ascends and accuses, descends and takes the soul" (Bava Batra 16a);
וְכָךְ בִּרְפִידִים שֶׁרָפוּ יְדֵיהֶם מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּכוֹרוֹת ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
and so at Rephidim where their hands slackened from words of Torah (Bechorot 5b);
דְּדָבָר זֶה בָּא לָהֶם מִצַּד הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק שֶׁהָיָה מָצוּי בָּעוֹלָם
this sluggishness having infected them from the root of Amalek present in the cosmos;
וְהֵם לֵב הָעוֹלָם, וְכָל מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם מִצַּד הָעֵירוּב דְּטוֹב וָרָע הַיֵּצֶר רָע מַכְנִיסוֹ גַּם בְּלֵב אִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי
for Israel is the heart of the world, and whatever exists in the world from the mixture of good and evil the yetzer introduces into the heart of the Jew;
וּצְרִיכִים לְנַצְּחוֹ, וְאָז יְנוּצַּח וְיִכְלֶה אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ הָרָע שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם בְּפֹעַל גַּם כֵּן
and they are required to overcome it, whereby that evil cosmic force is vanquished in physical reality as well;
וְהֵם שֶׁלֹּא נִצְּחוּהוּ וְרָפוּ יְדֵיהֶם, שֶׁנִּכְנַס בְּלִבָּם כֹּובֶד וְעַצְלוּת, מִיָּד: ״וַיָּבֹא עֲמָלֵק [וַיִּלָּחֶם עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּרְפִידִם]״ (שְׁמוֹת י״ז:ח׳) לְהִלָּחֵם בְּפֹעַל

and they, having failed to conquer it, their hands slackening as heaviness and lethargy entered their hearts, immediately: "Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim" (Shemos 17:8) in actual war!
וִידֵי מֹשֶׁה גַּם כֵּן כְּבֵדִים, כִּי הַכֹּובֶד שֶׁבְּלִבְּבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי הָעֲכִירוּ דִּטְחוֹל הַמַּכְבִּיד, פָּעַל גַּם כֵּן כֹּובֶד לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And Moshe's hands were likewise heavy (Shemos 17:12), for the heaviness in the hearts of Israel from the murkiness of the spleen affected Moshe Rabbeinu as well;
שֶׁ״הַפַּרְנָס — לְפִי הַדּוֹר״ (עֲרָכִין י״ז עַמּוּד א׳), וְקִלְקוּלֵי הַדּוֹר גּוֹרְמִים אֵיזֶה קִלְקוּל לַפַּרְנָס גַּם כֵּן
for "the leader matches the generation" (Arachin 17a), and the flaws of the generation cause a corresponding blemish in the leader;
אֶלָּא שֶׁבּוֹ לֹא הִגִּיעַ הַכֹּובֶד לַלֵּב כְּלָל, רַק לַיָּדַיִם וְאֵבְרֵי הַפְּעֻלָּה הַגּוּפָנִיִּים
except that in Moshe the heaviness never touched the heart, but reached only the hands and physical organs of action;
שֶׁמִּצַּד הַגּוּף שֶׁהוּא גּוּפָנִי הָיָה לוֹ קְצָת שַׁיָּיכוּת וְחִבּוּר לָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַגּוּפָנִי
having through his physical body an attachment to this corporeal world;
״וְהָיָה כַּאֲשֶׁר יָרִים מֹשֶׁה יָדוֹ״ (שְׁמוֹת י״ז:י״א) וְהִתְחַזֵּק נֶגֶד כֹּחַ עֲמָלֵק הַמַּכְבִּיד, ״וְגָבַר יִשְׂרָאֵל״ (שָׁם)
"and it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand," strengthening himself against the heavy force of Amalek, "that Israel prevailed" (ibid.);

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כ״ט עַמּוּד א׳): ״וְכִי יָדָיו שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה [עוֹשׂוֹת מִלְחָמָה אוֹ שׁוֹבְרוֹת מִלְחָמָה]? אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל [מִסְתַּכְּלִים כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה וּמְשַׁעְבְּדִין אֶת לִבָּם לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם — הָיוּ מִתְגַּבְּרִים]״

and the Sages expounded (Rosh Hashanah 29a): "Did the hands of Moses wage war or break war? Rather, whenever Israel looked heavenward and subjugated their hearts to their Father in Heaven, they prevailed";
וְעַדַיִין קָשֶׁה: אִם כֵּן לֹא הָיָה לַקְּרָא לִתְלוֹתוֹ בִּידֵי מֹשֶׁה
yet it remains difficult: if so, why did Scripture anchor victory in the hands of Moshe?

אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּפִי מַדְרֵיגָתָם אָז, שֶׁזֶּה קָרוֹב שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִזּוּהֲמַת מִצְרַיִם וְעַדַיִין לֹא קִבְּלוּ הַתּוֹרָה וְלֹא הִטָּהֲרוּ לְגַמְרֵי בִּסְפִירַת נְקִיִּים דְּמַ״ט יְמֵי הַסְּפִירָה
But in truth, according to Israel's spiritual level then, having recently emerged from Egyptian defilement, before receiving the Torah and before being purified across the 49 days of the Counting;
כַּאֲשֶׁר הִתְעוֹרֵר כֹּחַ עֲמָלֵק שֶׁהוּא הִתְעוֹרְרוּת כֹּחוֹ הַמַּכְבִּיד הַלְּבָבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּתֹקֶף הַיֵּצֶר
when the power of Amalek arose, weighing down the hearts of Israel in the assault of the yetzer;
לֹא הָיָה כֹּחָם יָפֶה נֶגְדּוֹ רַק עַל יְדֵי סִיּוּעַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, דְּ״דוֹר — לְפִי פַּרְנָס״ גַּם כֵּן
their own strength was insufficient against him without the assistance of Moshe Rabbeinu, for "a generation matches its leader" as well;
כִּי הוּא יָכוֹל לְהַכְנִיס גַּם כֵּן רוּחַ הִתְעוֹרְרוּת לְטוֹבָה בְּלִבְּבוֹת בְּנֵי דוֹרוֹ
he having the capacity to breathe an awakening of goodness into the hearts of his contemporaries;
וְזֶהוּ: ״אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ — אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לוֹ״ (קִדּוּשִׁין ל׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
and this is: "were not the Holy One assisting him, he could not overcome it" (Kiddushin 30b);
וְהָעֵזֶר הוּא לִפְעָמִים עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים, וּבִפְרָט עַל יְדֵי פַּרְנַס הַדּוֹר שֶׁהוּא לֵב הַדּוֹר וּמִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים לְכָל דּוֹרוֹ
this divine help often arriving through others, particularly through the shepherd of the generation who is the heart of his era, whence stream life for his people;
וְעַל כֵּן כַּאֲשֶׁר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הִתְגַּבֵּר נֶגֶד כֹּובֶד שֶׁבָּא לְיָדָיו וְכֹחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה שֶׁלּוֹ
wherefore when Moshe Rabbeinu prevailed against the heaviness in his hands and physical faculties;
גָּרַם גַּם כֵּן הִתְגַּבְּרוּת לְלִבְּבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהִסְתַּכֵּל כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה וּלְשַׁעְבֵּד לִבָּם לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם
he generated a spiritual awakening in the hearts of Israel to gaze heavenward and subjugate their hearts to their Father in Heaven.
וְעַל כֵּן נִצְטַוּוּ בִּזְכִירָה עִנְיַן עֲמָלֵק: ״זָכוֹר אֵת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לְךָ עֲמָלֵק״ (דְּבָרִים כ״ה:י״ז)
And therefore Israel was commanded regarding the remembrance of Amalek: "Remember what Amalek did unto you" (Devarim 25:17);
כִּי זֶה כָּל עִנְיַן עֲמָלֵק: לְהַכְנִיס כֹּובֶד לַלֵּב עַל יְדֵי הִרְהוּרֵי דְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים שֶׁל לֵיצָנוּת וְכַדּוֹמֶה הַמַּשְׁכִּיחַ הַכֹּל, וּבָזֶה מִתְרַפֶּה מִכָּל טוֹב
for this is the essence of Amalek: to inject heaviness into the heart through idle thoughts of cynicism that induce forgetfulness, thereby slacking from all goodness;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִמֵּילָא נַעֲשָׂה ״רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ד:כ׳)
and through this he becomes "the first of the nations,"
שֶׁהוּא הַהֲכָנָה לִהְיוֹת מוּכָן לְהִשְׁתַּקְּעוּת שֶׁל כָּל מִינֵי רָע שֶׁבְּכָל שִׁבְעִים אוּמּוֹת
being the gateway preparing man to sink into all the corruptions of the seventy nations;
מֵאַחַר שֶׁמְּפַנֶּה לִבּוֹ לְבַטָּלָה וְנִתְרוֹקֵן מִדִּבְרֵי קְדוּשָׁה
once the heart is emptied into vanity and vacated of words of holiness;
וּבְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַזְּכִירָה לְבַד דַּי לִמְחוֹת זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק, שֶׁכְּשֶׁזּוֹכֵר עִנְיָן זֶה כְּבָר נִסְתַּלֵּק הַשִּׁכְחָה
and through the awakening of remembrance alone one blots out the memory of Amalek, for remembering dispels forgetfulness.
וְכֵן הָמָן טָעַן: ״יְשֵׁנִים הֵם מִן הַמִּצְוֹת״ (מְגִלָּה י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳)
And so Haman argued: "They are asleep from the commandments" (Megillah 13b);
וְשֵׁינָה זוֹ שֶׁהוּא הָעַצְלוּת וְהַכֹּובֶד מֵהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת, בָּא גַּם כֵּן מִכֹּחוֹ
this sleep of sluggishness and heaviness issuing directly from his unholy power;
וְאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ בְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה תְּחִלָּה יוֹרֵד וּמֵסִית, אַחַר כָּךְ הוּא עוֹלֶה וּמַקְטְרִיג
that very force which initially descends and incites, subsequently ascends and accuses!
וְזֶה עִנְיַן נְטוּלֵי טְחוֹל דְּבֶן כּוֹזִיבָא, שֶׁלֹּא יַכְבִּיד עֲלֵיהֶם
And this explains the spleen-excised soldiers of Ben Koziba, that heaviness not weigh upon them;
דְּחָשַׁב שֶׁבָּזֶה יְנַצַּח עֲמָלֵק לְמוֹחָתוֹ מִן הָעוֹלָם לְגַמְרֵי
assuming that through this he would vanquish Amalek and blot him out completely;
כִּי חָשַׁב דְּמִצַּד הַקְּדוּשָׁה הַטְּחוֹל כָּלוּל בַּכָּבֵד, וּמַה שֶּׁנִּפְרַד לִשְׁנַיִם הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַסִּטְרָא דְּרָע שֶׁבּוֹ
reasoning that in holiness the spleen is absorbed within the liver, its separation into a distinct organ existing only on the side of evil;
וַחֲקִיקַת כַּפּוֹת הָרַגְלַיִם הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד ״דְּרַגְלֶיהָ יֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת״ (מִשְׁלֵי ה:ה)
and the excision/incising of the feet was likewise because "her feet go down to death" (Mishlei 5:5);
וְהֵם הָעֲווֹנוֹת שֶׁאָדָם דָּשׁ בַּעֲקֵבָיו (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה י״ח עַמּוּד א׳) הַבָּאִים מִצַּד הַשִּׁכְחָה וְהָעַצְלוּת וְהֶעְדֵּר הַזְּרִיזוּת
these being the sins that a man tramples with his heels (Avodah Zarah 18a), arising from forgetfulness, lethargy, and lack of alacrity;
וְטָעָה גַּם כֵּן לַחְשׁוֹב דְּהַתִּיקּוּן לְהָסִיר זֶה לְגַמְרֵי, דְּחָשַׁב שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת זֶה מִכְּלַל מוֹתָרוֹת הַגּוּף דְּסוֹפָן לַאֲבַדּוֹן
and he erred in presuming the rectification was to physically remove these, viewing them as bodily superfluities destined for destruction;
עַד שֶׁאָמְרוּ לוֹ חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל: ״עַד מָתַי אַתָּה עוֹשֶׂה יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין״ (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי תַּעֲנִית פֶּרֶק ד׳ הֲלָכָה ה׳)
until the Sages of Israel rebuked him: "How long will you render Israel blemish-ridden men?" (Yerushalmi Ta'anit 4:5);
כִּי חַס וְשָׁלוֹם שֶׁבָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דָּבָר אֶחָד לְבַטָּלָה
for God forbid that the Blessed Name created a single entity in vain!
וְ״הָאֱלֹהִים עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כט), וְהַכֹּל לְצֹרֶךְ קְדוּשָׁה
And "God made man upright" (Koheles 7:29), and all was formed for the sake of holiness;
וְאִם יֶחְסַר דָּבָר הוּא בַּעַל מוּם, וְחָסֵר מִמַּה שֶּׁרָאָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּחָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁהוּא רָאוּי לְצוּרַת הָאָדָם
and if a single organ is missing he is blemished, lacking what the Blessed Name in His divine wisdom deemed fitting for the human form;
וְכָל הַכֹּחוֹת שֶׁבּוֹ כּוּלָּם יֵשׁ בָּהֶם צֹרֶךְ לִכְבוֹד שָׁמַיִם, דְּ״כֹּל פָּעַל ה׳ לַמַּעֲנֵהוּ״ (מִשְׁלֵי ט״ז:ד׳), לְקִילּוּסוֹ
and all faculties within him are necessary for the glory of Heaven, for "Hashem made all things for His purpose" (Mishlei 16:4), for His praise;
וְאַדְּרַבָּא: בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵצֶל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הוּא תֹּקֶף הַטּוּמְאָה, אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא תֹּקֶף הַקְּדוּשָׁה:
and on the contrary: in that very domain where among the nations lies the intensity of defilement, within the Children of Israel shines the intensity of supreme holiness!

The theme: Secular drunkenness versus holy Purim joy, the letter Kuf (ק) sanctifying the spleen, and the gradual blotting out of Amalek. When the nations drink and become intoxicated, their speech descends into mockery, theatrical frivolity, obscenity, and promiscuity, as exemplified by the banquet of Ahasuerus who commanded Vashti to appear naked
Esther 1:10–11

. This marked the opening of the Megillah, awakening the unholy power of Haman—the laughter of the fool who temporarily enjoys good fortune. The narrative concludes at Esther's banquet; though dining with the king and his viceroy naturally involved royal amusement, it did not cause Esther to forget her inward cleaving unto Hashem, whereby she merited Haman's downfall and the eradication of Amalek. The Blessed Name crowned the letter Kuf in laughter
Sefer Yetzirah 5:10
so that laughter remain holy within Israel. The Purim feast was established with drinking and joy to demonstrate that Israel’s joy is intrinsically bound to holiness: drinking even unto ad d'lo yada
"until he does not know", Megillah 7b

does not sever a Jew from his divine cleaving, for his loss of conscious awareness was undertaken for the sake of a mitzvah. Through this, Amalek's power—which thrives on inserting forgetfulness into the heart—is uprooted. Each Hebrew letter possesses a unique light, sanctifying a specific organ and season; the letter Kuf purifies the laughter of the soul and the spleen, eradicating the evil of Amalek. Through Purim each year, even when observed simply as routine custom
mitzvat anashim melumadah
, the heart is incrementally purified until the final Purim, immediately following which Israel will be redeemed in Nissan.
וּכְשֶׁאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אוֹכְלִים וְשׁוֹתִים וּמִשְׁתַּכְּרִים, הֵם מְדַבְּרִים דִּבְרֵי לֵיצָנוּת וְשַׁעֲשׁוּעֵי תֵּיאַטְרָאוֹת וְכָל מִינֵי תִּפְלוּת וּזְנוּת
And when the nations of the world eat, drink, and become intoxicated, they speak words of mockery, theatrical amusements, and all manners of vulgarity and promiscuity (Megillah 12b);
כִּסְעוּדָתוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע [אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ] דְּצִוָּה לְהָבִיא וַשְׁתִּי עֲרוּמָּה
like the banquet of that wicked one [Ahasuerus], who commanded to bring Vashti naked (Esther 1:11; Megillah 12b);
וּבָזֶה הוּא הַתְחָלַת הַמְּגִלָּה, כִּי בְּעִנְיָן זֶה הָיָה תְּחִלַּת הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַכֹּחַ דְּהָמָן
and herein lies the opening of the Megillah, for in this very matter occurred the initial arousal of the unholy power of Haman;
שֶׁהוּא ״שְׂחֹק הַכְּסִיל״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:ו) וּמִי שֶׁ״הַשָּׁעָה מְשַׂחֶקֶת לוֹ״
who embodies the "laughter of the fool" (Koheles 7:6) and one for whom "the hour plays in his favor" (Esther Rabbah 2:3);
וְסוֹפוֹ הָיָה בַּמִּשְׁתֶּה דְּאֶסְתֵּר
and his ultimate end arrived at the banquet of Esther;
דְּוַדַּאי מִשְׁתֶּה שֶׁעָשְׂתָה לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ כָּמוֹהוּ וּמִשְׁנֵהוּ, מִסְּתָמָא הָיָה בּוֹ כָּל מִינֵי שְׂחוֹק וְשַׁעֲשׁוּעַ מְלָכִים
for certainly a banquet hosted before a monarch such as him and his viceroy naturally contained all manner of royal laughter and amusement;
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהָיְתָה עִמָּהֶם בַּמִּשְׁתֶּה, גַּם הִיא הִשְׁתַּעְשְׁעָה בָּזֶה עִמָּהֶם
and since she was with them at the feast, she too participated outwardly in this amusement with them;
וְכָל זֶה לֹא הוֹעִיל לְהַשְׁכִּיחָהּ מֵעִיקַּר הַמְכֻוָּון שֶׁבְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לְבָבָהּ בִּדְבֵיקוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
yet all this festive play did not succeed in causing her to forget the core intention cleaved in the depths of her heart unto the Blessed Name;
דְּלוּלֵי כֵן לֹא הָיְתָה זוֹכָה לְנִיצּוּחַ הָמָן וּמְחִיַּיִת עֲמָלֵק בָּזֶה
for had it not been so, she would not have merited the vanquishing of Haman and the eradication of Amalek through this feast.
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִמְלִיךְ אוֹת הַקּוּ״ף בִּשְׂחוֹק (סֵפֶר יְצִירָה פֶּרֶק ה׳ מִשְׁנָה י׳), שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כּוּלּוֹ מִצַּד הַקְּדוּשָׁה אֵצֶל מִי שֶׁהוּא חֵלֶק ה׳ וְנַחֲלָתוֹ
For the Blessed Name crowned the letter Kuf in laughter (Sefer Yetzirah 5:10), that it exist entirely from the side of holiness within one who is Hashem's portion and heritage;
וְכָךְ נִקְבַּע לְזֵכֶר הַנֵּס סְעוּדַת פּוּרִים בְּמִשְׁתֶּה וְשִׂמְחָה
and thus was instituted in commemoration of the miracle the Purim feast with drinking and joy;
לְבָרֵר שֶׁשִּׂמְחַת יִשְׂרָאֵל דָּבוּק בִּקְדֻשָּׁה, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעוֹשִׂין כָּל מִינֵי שְׂחוֹק וְשַׁעֲשׁוּעִים
to clarify that the joy of Israel is cleaved unto holiness, even while engaging in all manner of laughter and festive amusement;
שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵין עוֹשִׂין כֵּן אֶלָּא בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן שֶׁהַמִּצְוָה בְּשִׂמְחָה וּבִסּוּמֵי
seeing that they do not act so except at that appointed time when the mitzvah is to rejoice and become pleasantly intoxicated;
הֲרֵי דְּכָל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם רַק לְשֵׁם שָׁמָיִם
proving that all their deeds are performed strictly for the sake of Heaven;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּתְבַּסֵּם ״עַד דְּלָא יָדַע [בֵּין אָרוּר הָמָן לְבָרוּךְ מָרְדֳּכַי]״ (מְגִלָּה ז׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) שֶׁהוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַהֶעְלֵם וְהַשִּׁכְחָה
and through this, even though one becomes intoxicated "until he does not know between cursed is Haman and blessed is Mordechai" (Megillah 7b), which is the absolute depth of concealment and oblivion;
עֲדַיִין לֹא נֶעֱקַר מִדְּבֵיקוּתוֹ בִּקְדֻשָּׁה אֲפִילּוּ כִּמְלֹא נִימָא
he is not uprooted from his cleaving unto holiness even by a hairsbreadth;
מֵאַחַר שֶׁבִּיאָתוֹ לִידֵי שִׁכְחָה זוֹ הַיְינוּ לְכַוָּונַת מִצְוָה וּלְשֵׁם שָׁמָיִם
since his arrival at this state of forgetfulness was solely for the intention of a mitzvah and for the sake of Heaven.
וּבָזֶה נֶעֱקַר כֹּחַ עֲמָלֵק מִשָּׁרְשׁוֹ, שֶׁכָּל כֹּחוֹ הוּא בְּהַכְנָסַת הַשִּׁכְחָה בַּלֵּב וְהֶעְדֵּר הַיְּדִיעָה שֶׁבָּזֶה נִבְנֶה ״רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ד:כ׳)

And through this, the power of Amalek is uprooted at its core, for his entire strength lies in introducing forgetfulness into the heart and the absence of consciousness, through which the "first of the nations" is built;
אֲבָל זֶהוּ אֵצֶל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
yet this forgetfulness dominates only among the heathen nations;
אַךְ אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִתְבָּרַר עַל יְדֵי שִׂמְחַת פּוּרִים שֶׁלָּהֶם שֶׁגַּם בְּשִׂמְחָתָם ״לֹא יִתְעָרַב זָר״ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ד:י׳)
while among the Children of Israel it is clarified through their Purim joy that even in their celebration "a stranger does not intermeddle" (Mishlei 14:10);
דְּ״לֹא כְאֵלֶּה חֵלֶק יַעֲקֹב״ (יִרְמְיָה י:טז), וְ״לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי״ (תְּהִלִּים קמ״ז:כ׳)
for "not like these is the portion of Jacob" (Yirmiyah 10:16), and "He has not dealt so with any nation" (Tehillim 147:20);
שֶׁהֲגַם שֶׁמִּתְבַּסְּמִים וּמִשְׁתַּקְּעִים בְּמִינֵי שְׂחוֹק, אֵינוֹ שְׂחוֹק שֶׁל קַלּוּת רֹאשׁ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
so that even when becoming intoxicated and immersed in laughter, it is not the laughter of levity, God forbid;
רַק דְּבוּקִים בִּקְדֻשָּׁה עַל יְדֵי אוֹת הַקּוּ״ף
but they remain cleaved unto holiness through the letter Kuf;
שֶׁכָּל אוֹתִיּוֹת הָאָלֶ״ף־בֵּי״ת יֶשְׁנָם גַּם כֵּן בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
for all letters of the alphabet exist within the soul-root of every single Jew;
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה יֵשׁ לָהֶם כֹּחַ הַדִּבּוּר בִּלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ בְּכָל כַּ״ב אוֹתִיּוֹת
through which they possess the holy faculty of speech in the Holy Tongue across all twenty-two letters;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן עוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁמְּדַבֵּר בִּלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ — לְשׁוֹנוֹ סָרוּחַ
unlike an idolater who speaks the Holy Tongue, whose speech remains spiritually foul;
כִּי אֵין לָהֶם אֲחִיזָה בְּשׁוּם אוֹת מֵאוֹתִיּוֹת הַקֹּדֶשׁ, וְדִבּוּרָם רַק כִּנְעִירַת בְּהֵמוֹת וְצִפְצוּף עוֹפוֹת
possessing no grasp within any holy letter, their speech being merely like the braying of beasts and the chirping of birds.
וְכָל אוֹת יֵשׁ לוֹ אוֹר מְיוּחָד וּקְדֻשָּׁה מְיוּחֶדֶת, וּמֵאִיר בְּאֵבֶר מְיוּחָד בַּגּוּף, וּבִזְמַן מְיוּחָד בַּשָּׁנָה
