וּכְפִי מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם כָּךְ נַעֲשָׂה הָעֵת מוּכָן, לֹא שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ כֵּן
and according to Israel's deeds the hour is determined, not possessing an intrinsic destiny of its own.
וּבְתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב עַל יְדֵי חֵטְא דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר בַּמְּרַגְּלִים, נִקְבַּע הַבְּכִיָּה לַדּוֹרוֹת עַל גָּלוּת הָאָרֶץ בְּאוֹתוֹ עֵת לְפִי שֶׁמָּאֲסוּ בָּהּ
And on the Ninth of Av through the sin of the Spies, generational weeping over exile was fixed at that season because they despised the Holy Land;
וּמִיתַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בַּאֲדָר לֹא הָיְתָה כְּלָל מִצַּד חֵטְא בְּאוֹתוֹ עֵת
while the passing of Moshe Rabbeinu in Adar was not on account of any sin associated with that season;
רַק לְפִי שֶׁבּוֹ נוֹלַד, וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא ״מְמַלֵּא שְׁנוֹתֵיהֶם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים מִיּוֹם לְיוֹם״ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה י״א עַמּוּד א׳)
but because in Adar he was born, and the Holy One completes the years of the righteous from day to day (Rosh Hashanah 11a);
לְפִי שֶׁמִּיתָתָם אֵינוֹ עֹונֶשׁ, רַק הִתְעַלּוּת לְמַדְרֵגָה יוֹתֵר גְּבוֹהָה וּלְעוֹלָמוֹת עֶלְיוֹנִים
for their passing is not a punishment, but an ascension unto a more exalted rung and supernal worlds;
וְהַשְׁאָרַת כֹּחָם וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם בְּחַיּוּתָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לִהְיוֹת נִקְבָּע בְּנַפְשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
bequeathing their lifelong spiritual labor to be permanently established within the souls of Israel;
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא בַּיּוֹם שֶׁנּוֹלַד, שֶׁאָז הוּא הַתְחָלַת הִתְנוֹצְצוּת אוֹר אוֹתוֹ נֶפֶשׁ וְהִתְגַּלּוּתוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
wherefore it occurs on the day he was born, which marks the initial sparkling of that soul's light in this world;
וְ״טוֹב יוֹם הַמָּוֶת מִיּוֹם הִוָּלְדוֹ״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:א), שֶׁהוּא יוֹם הִתְנוֹצְצוּת אוֹרוֹ בְּמַדְרֵיגוֹת עֶלְיוֹנִים הַנֶּעְלָמִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and "better is the day of death than the day of one's birth" (Koheles 7:1), being the day his light radiates within supernal worlds concealed from this world;
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹרוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לִהְיוֹת חָקוּק כֵּן בְּלִבְּבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
and likewise the manifestation of his light in this world to become engraved within the hearts of Israel;
אֲבָל הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד הַהֶעְלֵם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דְּאֵין כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל מַמָּשׁ כָּמוֹהוּ, רַק שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם כֹּחַ זֶה בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לִבָּם
being manifest in inward concealment, for not all Israel are consciously like Moshe, but possess his spiritual potency within the depths of their hearts;

וְכָךְ בְּמִיתַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הַשָּׂגַת הַתּוֹרָה, נִשְׁאַר כֹּחַ זֶה בְּכָל הַלְּבָבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּהַשָּׂגַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהִיא גַּם כֵּן תּוֹרָה שְׁלֵימָה
and so through Moshe's death his power of Torah comprehension was bequeathed into all Jewish hearts as the perception of the Oral Torah;
אֲבָל הַשָּׂגָתָהּ בְּמִסְטוֹרִין, הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת גָּמוּר שֶׁהִיא תּוֹרַת ה׳ וּדְבַר ה׳ כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
yet grasped through inward mysteries (mistorin), not with the open prophetic clarity that Moshe possessed;
רַק שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג מִצַּד מַעֲמַקֵּי לִבּוֹ שֶׁגָּנוּז בָּהֶם כֹּחַ הַהַשָּׂגָה לְתוֹרַת ה׳
grasping it from the depths of his heart wherein is hidden the capacity to attain Hashem's Torah;

וְכָל יְמֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא הָיָה שׁוּם אָדָם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יָכוֹל לְהַשִּׂיג בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ, רַק מַה שֶּׁהָיָה שׁוֹמֵעַ מִפִּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, כִּי הֵם הָיוּ דּוֹר מְקַבְּלֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב:
for during Moshe's lifetime no individual could innovate Torah independently, but only what he heard from Moshe's mouth, being the generation that received the Written Torah!

17.h: The theme: The cancellation of Torah as its foundation (bitulah shel Torah zehu yisudah), Otniel ben Kenaz, and the cessation of prophecy. The Oral Torah began after Moshe's death: during the days of mourning for Moshe, three hundred halachot were forgotten (Temurah 16a), but the Sages taught that "the suspension of Torah study is its very foundation" (Menachos 99a). Through the forgetting of these laws, Otniel ben Kenaz toiled in rigorous analytical argumentation (pilpul) and restored them (Temurah 16a). This inaugurated the Oral Torah—attaining divine truth through the Holy Spirit within the Sages (Bava Batra 12a; Ramban). The nations presumed that Moshe's death marked the end of the Torah, but in truth it was the birth of the Oral Law; Haman's decree likewise became the foundation for Israel re-accepting the Torah (kiyyemu ve-kiblu, Shabbat 88a). The foundational era of the Oral Torah was established by the Men of the Great Assembly, the authors of rabbinic enactments, fences (seyag la-Torah), and hermeneutic principles (Avos 1:1). As prophecy ceased, Haman sensed that the era of direct revelation had closed and that the canon of biblical scripture was sealed; but he did not know that "the words of the Scribes are more beloved than the wine of the Torah" (Avodah Zarah 35a). Divine revelation is greatest specifically within deep concealment: "He has set me in dark places—this is the Babylonian Talmud" (Eichah 3:6; Sanhedrin 24a), whose cryptic debates conceal the mysteries of Torah. Moshe is the collective Da'as of Israel (the "generation of knowledge", dor de'ah), Da'as being the Holy Spirit. His death was the concealment of explicit Da'as, leading to the requirement of drinking on Purim "until he does not know" (ad d'lo yada). Haman assumed that the cessation of Da'as was permanent, unaware that Adar was the month of Moshe's birth and the inception of transcendent revelation through concealment.

p: וְהַתְחָלַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הָיָה אַחַר מִיתַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And the inception of the Oral Torah occurred following the death of Moshe Rabbeinu;
וּבִימֵי אֶבְלוֹ נִשְׁתַּכְּחוּ אוֹתָן הֲלָכוֹת שֶׁהוּא סִילּוּק הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהָיָה בְּמוֹתוֹ
and during the days of his mourning hundreds of halachot were forgotten (Temurah 16a), representing the withdrawal of Torah upon his death;
אֲבָל מָצִינוּ (מְנָחוֹת צ״ט עַמּוּד א׳): דְּ״בִיטּוּלָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה — זֶהוּ יְסוֹדָהּ״
yet we find in Menachos (99a): "the suspension of Torah study is its very foundation";
וְעַל יְדֵי הַשִּׁכְחָה יָגְעוּ וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּ לַעֲמוֹד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּכֹחַ פִּלְפּוּלָם, עַד שֶׁהֶחֱזִירָן עָתְנִיאֵל בֶּן קְנַז בְּפִלְפּוּלוֹ (תְּמוּרָה ט״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
and through that forgetfulness scholars toiled through rigorous argumentation until Otniel ben Kenaz restored them through his pilpul (Temurah 16a);
וְזֶהוּ הַתְחָלַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגַת חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְתַלְמִידִים וָתִיקִים בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁבְּקִרְבָּם כְּמִפִּי הַנְּבוּאָה
and this was the beginning of the Oral Torah: the perception of the Sages and veteran disciples through the Holy Spirit within them like prophecy;
שֶׁהִיא הַנְּבוּאָה שֶׁלֹּא נִסְתַּלְּקָה מֵהַחֲכָמִים, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (י״ב עַמּוּד א׳), עַיֵּין שָׁם בָּרַמְבַּ״ן
this being the prophecy that was never removed from the Sages (Bava Batra 12a; Ramban);
וּמַסִּיק שָׁם: דְּאָמַר גַּבְרָא רַבָּא מִלְּתָא וְיָהֵיב טַעְמָא, וְאִתְּאַמַר הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי כְּוָותֵיהּ, דְּזֶהוּ רַק בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ

concluding there: an eminent master states an insight with a rationale, and it is subsequently found that it was taught as a Halachah to Moshe from Sinai, which operates strictly through the Holy Spirit;

וְכָךְ הַחְזָרַת עָתְנִיאֵל אוֹתָן הֲלָכוֹת לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי, וּמִיתַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הִיא שֶׁגָּרְמָה לָזֶה שֶׁנֶּחְקַק בְּכָל הַלְּבָבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כֹּחַ הַהַשָּׂגָה דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
and so Otniel's restoration of those halachot and Moshe's death caused the capacity for Torah innovation to become engraved in all Jewish hearts.
וְהָאוּמּוֹת שֶׁאֵין יוֹדְעִים מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה חָשְׁבוּ דְּמִיתָתוֹ הוּא בִּיטּוּלָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה
And the nations, knowing nothing of the Oral Torah, assumed that Moshe's death was the abolition of the Torah;
וּמִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִרְאֶה כֵן, אֲבָל הוּא רַק לִפְנִים וְלֹא עַל הָאֱמֶת
and to outward appearance in this world it seemed so, but that was merely superficial;
וְכָךְ גְּזֵירַת הָמָן אַאוֹתוֹ חֹדֶשׁ הָיָה רַק לִפְנִים, אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת אַדְּרַבָּא זֶהוּ יְסוֹדָהּ, דְּאָז ״קִיְּימוּ מַה שֶּׁקִּבְּלוּ כְּבָר״ (שַׁבָּת פ״ח עַמּוּד א׳)
and so Haman's decree targeting Adar was merely superficial, becoming in truth its very foundation when "they confirmed what they had already accepted" (Shabbat 88a);
וְעִיקַּר יְסוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הִתְחִיל אָז מֵאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה כַּנּוֹדָע, שֶׁהֵם מְיַסְּדֵי כָּל הַגְּזֵירוֹת וְתַקָּנוֹת חֲכָמִים וְכָל הַדְּרָשׁוֹת וְהַלִּימּוּדִים
and the primary foundation of the Oral Torah was established by the Men of the Great Assembly, the authors of rabbinic enactments, fences, and hermeneutic expositions;

שֶׁכָּל שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת לִימּוּד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא מֵאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה, וְשִׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק מִשְּׁיָרֵיהֶם רֹאשׁ לְשַׁלְשֶׁלֶת חַכְמֵי הַמִּשְׁנָה, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ אָבוֹת (פֶּרֶק א׳ מִשְׁנָה ב׳)
the chain of Oral Law descending from the Great Assembly, with Shimon HaTzaddik among their survivors standing as the head of the Tannaitic chain (Avos 1:2);
וְעַל זֶה הָיָה אִמְרוֹתֵיהֶם: ״הַעֲמִידוּ תַלְמִידִים הַרְבֵּה, וַעֲשׂוּ סְיָג לַתּוֹרָה״ (שָׁם מִשְׁנָה א׳), שֶׁזֶּה כָּל עִנְיָנָם
and toward this stood their directives: "raise up many disciples, and make a fence around the Torah" (ibid. 1:1).
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁנִּפְסְקָה אָז הַנְּבוּאָה שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת דְּבַר ה׳ בְּפֹעַל
And through prophecy ceasing at that time, which had been the open revelation of the word of Hashem;
וְזֶה הִשִּׂיג הָמָן עַל דֶּרֶךְ: אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם רוֹאִים וְאֵין יוֹדְעִים מַה רוֹאִים
Haman perceiving this after the manner of the nations: who see but do not understand what they see;
וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיהוּ לָא חָזֵי, מַזָּלֵיהּ חָזֵי כִּי קָרוֹב הָעֵת דִּסְתִימַת חָזוֹן וּנְבוּאָה
and though he did not see, his supernal Mazal saw that the time was near for the sealing of vision and prophecy;
וּבְאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר הָיוּ אַחֲרוֹנֵי הַנְּבִיאִים וְלֹא קָם עוֹד נָבִיא חָדָשׁ
in that generation living the final prophets (Chaggai, Zechariah, and Malachi), with no new prophet arising;

וְהִרְגִּישׁ דְּהוּא דּוֹר שֶׁל הִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַנְּבוּאָה, כִּי בְּמִיתַת אוֹתוֹ דּוֹר נִסְתַּם חָזוֹן וְנֶאֶסְרָה הַכְּתִיבָה לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, כִּי נִפְסַק גַּם כְּתִיבַת דִּבְרֵי קַבָּלָה שֶׁהוּא כְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
he sensing that prophecy was departing, vision being sealed and the canon of biblical scripture closed.
אֲבָל לֹא יָדַע שֶׁזֶּהוּ יְסוֹד וְהַתְחָלָה לְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וְדִבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים הַחֲבִיבִים עוֹד יוֹתֵר מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ל״ה עַמּוּד א׳)
But he did not know that this was the foundation and inception of the Oral Torah and the words of the Scribes, which are more beloved than the wine of the Torah (Avodah Zarah 35a);
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא הֶעְלֵם, הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת יוֹתֵר, כִּי כֵן הוּא תֹּקֶף הַהִתְגַּלּוּת כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא מִתְגַּלֶּה גַּם בְּהֶעְלֵם
and though it is concealment, it is an even greater revelation, for the peak of revelation is demonstrated when it shines from within concealment;
וּכְפִי תֹּקֶף הַהֶעְלֵם, כֵּן הוּא תֹּקֶף הַהִתְגַּלּוּת
and matching the depth of concealment is the intensity of revelation;
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (כ״ד עַמּוּד א׳): ״׳בְּמַחֲשַׁכִּים הוֹשִׁיבַנִי [כְּמֵתֵי עוֹלָם]׳ (אֵיכָה ג:ו) — זֶה תַּלְמוּדָהּ שֶׁל בָּבֶל״
after the manner stated in Sanhedrin (24a): "'He has set me in dark places, as they that be dead of old' (Eichah 3:6)—this is the Babylonian Talmud";
שֶׁהוּא הַהִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁבְּתַכְלִית הַחַשְׁכוּת וְהַהֶעְלֵם
being the revelation of divine light within the deepest darkness and obscurity;
וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּוהַר דְּחַבְרִין בַּבְלָאֵי יָדְעוּ לְהַעְלִים הַדְּבָרִים
and as written in the Zohar: the Babylonian companions knew how to conceal divine mysteries within mundane debates;
כִּי בַּתַּלְמוּד בַּבְלִי גָּנוּז כָּל הַמִּסְטוֹרִין דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה כַּנּוֹדָע
for within the Babylonian Talmud are hidden all the secret mysteries of the Torah.
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא הַדַּעַת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּנּוֹדָע, דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא דּוֹרוֹ ״דּוֹר דֵּעָה״ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ט:א)
And Moshe Rabbeinu is the collective Da'as of Israel, wherefore his generation is termed the "generation of knowledge" (Vayikra Rabbah 9:1);
כִּי דַּעַת הוּא רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ (רַשִׁ״י שְׁמוֹת ל״א:ג׳), שֶׁהוּא הַמְשָׁכַת אוֹר נֶעְלָם דְּכֶתֶר שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵהַחָכְמָה דְּהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם
for Da'as is the Holy Spirit, channeling the transcendent light of Keser which is above human wisdom;
וְזֶה כָּל חָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, לְהַמְשָׁכַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם
this being Moshe's wisdom: drawing down words of Torah directly from the Almighty transcending mortal perception;
וּמִיתָתוֹ הוּא גְּנִיזַת הַדַּעַת בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת, הַיְינוּ שֶׁדְּבַר ה׳ יָקָר וְאֵין חָזוֹן נִפְרָץ בְּפֹעַל (שְׁמוּאֵל א ג:א)
and his death was the concealment of explicit Da'as, where "the word of Hashem was precious, there was no frequent vision" (I Shmuel 3:1);
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֶשְׁנוֹ בְּכֹחַ דְּלֹא נִסְתַּלֵּק מֵהַחֲכָמִים
yet it remained in potentiality, never having departed from the Sages;
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם סְבוּרִים שֶׁמַּשִּׂיגִים זֶה בְּכֹחַ חָכְמָתָם, וְאֵין גָּלוּי שֶׁזֶּה דַּעַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְהַשָּׂגָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת חָכְמָתוֹ, וּבֶאֱמֶת הוּא רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
except that they assume they grasp it through their own intellectual power, it not being obvious that it is the Holy Spirit, when in truth it is the Holy Spirit;
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן הַבִּסּוּם בְּפוּרַיָּא ״עַד דְּלָא יָדַע״, שֶׁהוּא הִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַדַּעַת דַּרְגָּא דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and this is the purpose of becoming intoxicated on Purim "until he does not know," reflecting the withdrawal of conscious Da'as, the rung of Moshe;
דִּלְהַשָּׂגַת חָכְמָה צָרִיךְ יִשּׁוּב הַדַּעַת, וְעַל כֵּן: שָׁתָה רְבִיעִית — אַל יוֹרֶה (עֵירוּבִין ס״ד עַמּוּד א׳), דְּאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהַשִּׂיג בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה לַאֲמִיתּוֹ
for to attain conscious wisdom one requires settled composure of mind, wherefore one who drank a quarter-log of wine may not render halachic rulings (Eruvin 64a);
וְהָמָן חָשַׁב דְּאָז הָיָה גְּנִיזַת הַדַּעַת דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְגַמְרֵי, כִּי חָשַׁב שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן תַּחַת הַזְּמָן וְהָעֵת גּוֹרֵם
and Haman assumed that this was the permanent obliteration of the Torah's intellect, assuming Israel was governed by time;
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא יָדַע דְּאָז נוֹלַד, וְנִמְצָא הָעֵת אַדְּרַבָּא מוּכָן אֶל הַהֵיפֶךְ
wherefore he was blind to the fact that Moshe was born in Adar, the season being prepared for the opposite;
וְגַם הַמִּיתָה הוּא הֲכָנָה אֶל הַהִתְגַּלּוּת הַיְתֵירָה שֶׁבַּהֶעְלֵם גַּם כֵּן:
and even his death was the direct preparation for the greater revelation within concealment!

17.h: The theme: Purim as illumination in the absence of Da'as, wisdom among the nations vs. Torah in Israel, and the prophecy of Balaam. Israel originally sought to establish Purim as a full Yom Tov, believing that through their own merit they had sanctified time; but when it was revealed that their deliverance was cloaked in nature (lifnim), they recognized that the time remained in the concealment of Da'as. Yet Israel perceives divine truth even in the absence of conscious intellect (ad d'lo yada). While the nations possess human wisdom regarding which a blessing is recited ("Blessed is He Who gave of His wisdom to flesh and blood", Berachos 58a; Megillah 16a), "if a person says to you: there is wisdom among the nations, believe him; if he says: there is Torah among the nations, do not believe him" (Eichah Rabbah 2:13). Torah is Da'as—the influx of the Holy Spirit from Chochmah Ila'ah, which belongs exclusively to Israel. In this world, the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil creates an external counterfeit for everything: opposite Moshe's Da'as, Balaam arose boasting "who knows the knowledge of the Most High" (Bamidbar 24:16; Sifrei, Devarim §357). Moshe requested that the Shechinah never rest upon the nations, which was fulfilled upon his passing (Berachos 7a; Bava Batra 15b); thereafter, direct prophecy departed from the nations. The wisdom of the gentiles is human intellect, whose ultimate truth consists in recognizing Israel's supremacy, as Balaam foresaw and as the nations will demonstrate in the Future, ten men grasping the corner of a Jew's garment to serve him (Zechariah 8:23). Haman's wise counselors recognized this in his final hour, perceiving that if Mordechai is of the seed of the Jews, Haman is doomed to fall (Esther 6:13).

p: וּתְחִלָּה חָשְׁבוּ לְקָבְעוֹ יוֹם טוֹב, שֶׁחָשְׁבוּ דְּהָיָה הַנֵּס בֶּאֱמֶת וּדְהֵם בִּזְכוּתָם קִדְּשׁוּ הָעֵת עַל יְדֵי ״דִּמְקַדְּשֵׁי לִזְמַנֵּי״ (בֵּיצָה י״ז עַמּוּד א׳) וּבָזֶה נִתְהַפֵּךְ
And initially they sought to establish Purim as a full Yom Tov, assuming that the miracle was an overt supernatural suspension and that in their merit they had sanctified the season;
אֲבָל אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה לָהֶם דְּלֹא הָיָה אֶלָּא לִפְנִים, נִתְגַּלָּה לָהֶם דְּלֹא קִידְּשׁוּ לִזְמַנֵּי כְּלָל, שֶׁהָעֵת נִשְׁאַר כְּמוֹת שֶׁהָיָה בִּגְנִיזַת הַדַּעַת
but once it was revealed that their deliverance was cloaked within nature (lifnim), they realized they had not sanctified the season into a festival, the time remaining in the concealment of Da'as;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מַשִּׂיגִים וְיוֹדְעִים גַּם בְּהֶעְדֵּר הַדַּעַת
nevertheless the Children of Israel perceive and cleave unto Hashem even in the suspension of conscious Da'as;
וְזֶהוּ הַבִּסּוּם ״עַד דְּלָא יָדַע״, וְאָז הוּא עִיקַּר הַהֶבְדֵּל בֵּין אָרוּר הָמָן לְבָרוּךְ מָרְדֳּכַי, הַיְינוּ בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לָעַמִּים
this being the drinking "until he does not know," wherein lies the essential distinction between cursed is Haman and blessed is Mordechai, between Israel and the nations;
כִּי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא הַדַּעַת הִיא ״מוֹרָשָׁה קְהִלַּת יַעֲקֹב״ (דְּבָרִים ל״ג:ד׳), וְ״לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי״ (תְּהִלִּים קמ״ז:כ׳)
for the Torah which is divine Da'as is the exclusive heritage of the congregation of Jacob.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ חֲכָמִים גַּם בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם דִּמְבָרְכִין עֲלֵיהֶן: ״שֶׁנָּתַן מֵחָכְמָתוֹ [לִבְשָׂר וָדָם]״, כְּמָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּ״הָרוֹאֶה״ (בְּרָכוֹת נ״ח עַמּוּד א׳)
And although there exist sages among the nations over whom a blessing is recited: "Who has given of His wisdom unto flesh and blood" (Berachos 58a);
וְנִתְגַּלָּה זֶה בַּכָּתוּב אֵצֶל הָמָן, דַּחֲכָמָיו הִרְגִּישׁוּ בְּמַפַּלְתּוֹ, וְלָמְדוּ מִזֶּה בִּמְגִלָּה (ט״ז עַמּוּד א׳): דַּאֲפִילּוּ בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם נִקְרָא ״חָכָם״
and this was demonstrated regarding Haman, whose sages foresaw his downfall, the Gemara in Megillah (16a) deducing: even among the heathen a person can be termed a "sage";
כִּי עִיקַּר חָכְמָה הוּא חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה, וְחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁמְּבָרְכִין עֲלֵיהֶן הַיְינוּ חֲכָמִים בַּתּוֹרָה
yet primary wisdom is the wisdom of the Torah, the blessing over Jewish sages applying strictly to scholars of Torah;
וְהָמָן שֶׁחָשַׁב לְאַבֵּד זֶה, וַדַּאי חָשַׁב דְּעִיקַּר הַחָכְמָה אֶצְלוֹ, כִּי ״זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:יד)
and Haman, seeking to destroy Torah, assumed that supreme wisdom resided with him, for "God has made one opposite the other" (Koheles 7:14);

וְהָיָה לוֹ חֶבְרָה שֶׁל חֲכָמִים מֵחַכְמֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, שֶׁחָשַׁב שֶׁעֲלֵיהֶם יִהְיֶה הַשְׁרָאַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָכְמָתוֹ בָּעוֹלָם וְהוּא בְּרֹאשָׁם, דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָאִים ״חֲכָמָיו״ שֶׁשַּׁיָּיכִים לוֹ, כִּי עֲמָלֵק הוּא ״רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ד:כ׳)

surrounding himself with pagan philosophers, presuming that divine wisdom rested upon them with himself at their head, wherefore they are called "his wise men" (Esther 6:13), Amalek being the head of the nations.

וּכְבָר אָמְרוּ (אֵיכָה רַבָּה ב:י״ג): ״אִם יֹאמַר לְךָ אָדָם: יֵשׁ חָכְמָה בַּגּוֹיִם — תַּאֲמֵן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ׳וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי חֲכָמִים מֵאֱדוֹם׳ (עֹבַדְיָה א:ח); יֵשׁ תּוֹרָה בַּגּוֹיִם — אַל תַּאֲמֵן״

And the Sages already declared (Eichah Rabbah 2:13): "If a person says to you: there is wisdom among the nations—believe him, as it is said: 'I will destroy the wise men out of Edom' (Ovadiah 1:8); if he says: there is Torah among the nations—do not believe him";
כִּי הַתּוֹרָה הוּא הַדַּעַת שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגַת חָכְמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵחָכְמַת אָדָם
for the Torah is divine Da'as, the perception of Hashem's wisdom which transcends mortal human reason;
וְאַף עַל פִּי דְּהַכֹּל הוּא ״זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה״, דְּמִצַּד עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע יֵשׁ בְּכָל דָּבָר עֵירוּב טוֹב וָרָע
and although all exists "one opposite the other," the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil creating a mixture of good and evil;
וְאֵין שׁוּם הֶיכֵּר לָזֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא שֶׁהָרָע מַרְאֶה עַצְמוֹ לָעַיִן כְּמוֹ הַטּוֹב
no clear distinction appearing in this world of falsehood where evil disguises itself as good;

וְגַם בְּדַעַת הַתּוֹרָה דַּרְגָּא דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה בְּדוֹרוֹ בִּלְעָם, דְּאָמְרוּ עָלָיו (סִפְרֵי דְּבָרִים שנ״ז): ״אֲבָל בְּאֻומּוֹת הָעוֹלָם קָם״, שֶׁהִתְפָּאֵר עַצְמוֹ: ״וְיֹדֵעַ דַּעַת עֶלְיוֹן״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ד:ט״ז)
and even opposite the Torah Da'as of Moshe Rabbeinu there arose in his generation Balaam (Sifrei, Devarim §357) who boasted: "and who knows the knowledge of the Most High" (Bamidbar 24:16).
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָה עַל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, וְנָתְנוּ לוֹ (בְּרָכוֹת ז׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
And Moshe Rabbeinu was the one who requested that the Shechinah never rest upon the nations, and it was granted to him (Berachos 7a);
הַיְינוּ לֹא מִיָּד, רַק אַחַר מוֹתוֹ, שֶׁהֲרֵי בִּלְעָם הָיָה אַחַר כָּךְ בְּסוֹף יָמָיו
meaning not immediately, but after his death, for Balaam prophesied at the conclusion of Moshe's life;
וְכֵן הוּא לְשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (ט״ו עַמּוּד ב׳): דְּמִכִּי מִית מֹשֶׁה לֹא אִתְנַבּוֹ עוֹד מֵאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
and so is the phrasing in Bava Batra (15b): from the time Moshe died, prophecy departed from the nations;
וְהַיְינוּ דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ ״אֹהֵב מִשְׁפָּט״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ס״א:ח׳) וְהַכֹּל בְּמִשְׁפָּט
the Blessed Name executing all things in strict justice;
וּמִצַּד מִשְׁפַּט הַנְהָגַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַכֹּל צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת ״זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה״
the governance of this world requiring balanced opposition;
וְכָל זְמַן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַשָּׂגָה דְּדַעַת עֶלְיוֹן... הוּכְרַח לִהְיוֹת כֵּן בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
and as long as Moshe lived and Israel possessed direct perception of supernal Da'as, an evil counterpart was permitted among the nations.
אֲבָל מִשֶּׁמֵּת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, נִגְנַז הַדַּעַת שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ כִּבְדוֹר דֵּעָה דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
But once Moshe Rabbeinu died, explicit Da'as—the open revelation of the Holy Spirit as witnessed in the "generation of knowledge"—was hidden;
דְּ״רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה עַל הַיָּם מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָאָה יְחֶזְקֵאל״ (מְכִילְתָּא בְּשַׁלַּח ג׳; זֹוהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בְּשַׁלַּח ס״ד עַמּוּד ב׳)
where a maidservant at the Sea beheld what Yechezkel never saw;
וְכֵן בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, וְ״לֹא קָם נָבִיא עוֹד... כְּמֹשֶׁה״ (דְּבָרִים ל״ד:י׳), שֶׁהִיא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַדַּעַת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עַד שֶׁנִּתְפַּשֵּׁט לְכָל נַפְשׁוֹת דּוֹרוֹ
and so at Sinai, with no prophet ever arising like Moshe, whose manifest Da'as had illuminated all the souls of his era;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אַחַר מוֹתוֹ נִגְנַז הַהִתְגַּלּוּת, וְ״שָׁבַק לָן חַיִּים״ זֶה בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב וְלֹא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת
whereas following his death open revelation was sealed, bequeathing this vitality into the inward depths of the heart rather than in open sight;
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא הַמִּסְטוֹרִין הַנֶּעְלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְאֵין גָּלוּי אֶלָּא לְלִבְּבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
this being the esoteric mystery concealed in this world, revealed exclusively unto the hearts of the Children of Israel.
וּלְפִיכָךְ ״אֵין תּוֹרָה בַּגּוֹיִם״, שֶׁהַהִתְגַּלּוּת דְּתוֹרָה בְּלִבְּבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מַה שֶּׁמַּשִּׂיגִים דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה... זֶהוּ נֶעְלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
Wherefore "there is no Torah among the nations," for the revelation of Torah within the hearts of Israel—grasping insights transcending human reason—is hidden in this world;
שֶׁהוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם בֶּאֱמֶת דֶּרֶךְ נְבוּאָה וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
they being in absolute truth words of Torah from Heaven through the Holy Spirit;
כִּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין נִיכָּר רַק שֶׁהוּא דִּבְרֵי חָכְמָה שֶׁחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְחַדְּשִׁים בְּחָכְמָתָם וְשִׂכְלָם
for in this world it appears merely as scholarly wisdom which Jewish sages innovate through their intellect;
וְזֶה יֵשׁ גַּם בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם חָכְמָה וָשֵׂכֶל
and human intellect exists among the nations of the world as well;
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֶצְלָם הוּא חָכְמָה בְּעָלְמָא, וְאֵינוֹ תּוֹרָה, דְּהַיְינוּ הַמְשָׁכַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ מֵחָכְמָה עֶלְיוֹנָה
except that within the nations it is secular wisdom, not Torah drawn from supernal Chochmah;
רַק הוּא חֵלֶק הַחָכְמָה שֶׁל בָּשָׂר וָדָם מִצַּד שֶׁהוּא בָּשָׂר וָדָם
being merely the mortal wisdom of flesh and blood as flesh and blood.
וְזֶה כָּל הַחָכְמָה שֶׁל בָּשָׂר וָדָם וְחַכְמֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הָאֲמִיתִּיִּים: שֶׁיַּכִּירוּ תֹּקֶף מַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל
And this is the ultimate wisdom of authentic gentile philosophers: that they recognize the supreme spiritual virtue of Israel;
וְזֶה הָיָה כָּל הַשָּׂגַת בִּלְעָם הָרָשָׁע בִּנְבוּאָתוֹ: לְהַשִּׂיג תֹּקֶף מַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל מַה שֶּׁאֵין מוּשָּׂג לְהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם כְּלָל, וְזֶה נִקְבַּע בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
this being the entire attainment of wicked Balaam in his prophecy: to perceive the greatness of Israel which is incomprehensible to human intellect, recorded in the Torah (Bamidbar 23–24);
וְכָךְ לֶעָתִיד שֶׁ״יִשְׁפּוֹךְ רוּחוֹ עַל כָּל בָּשָׂר״ (יוֹאֵל ג:א), הַשָּׂגַת אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם יִהְיֶה שֶׁיַּשִּׂיגוּ מַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל
and so in the Future when Hashem pours His spirit upon all flesh (Yoel 3:1), the understanding of the nations will be to perceive Israel's greatness;
שֶׁיֹּאחֲזוּ עֲשָׂרָה אֲנָשִׁים מִכֹּל לְשׁוֹנוֹת הַגּוֹיִם בִּכְנַף אִישׁ יְהוּדִי (זְכַרְיָה ח:כג)
that ten men from all languages of the nations will take hold of the skirt of a Jew (Zechariah 8:23);
לִהְיוֹת עֲבָדִים לוֹ, רוֹעֵי צֹאן וְאִכָּרִים וְכוֹרְמִים (יְשַׁעְיָה ס״א:ה׳)
to serve as his servants, shepherds, plowmen, and vinedressers (Yeshayah 61:5);
כִּי יָבִינוּ שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִיתָם כְּשֶׁיִּהְיוּ עֲבָדִים לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
understanding that this is their ultimate purpose: to be servants unto the Children of Israel.
וְכֵן זֶה כָּל חָכְמַת חַכְמֵיהֶם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כִּי אֵין נִקְרָא ״חָכְמָה״ אֶלָּא הַכָּרַת הָאֱמֶת
And so is all wisdom of their sages in this world, for nothing is termed "wisdom" other than the perception of truth;
דְּמַה שֶּׁהוּא שֶׁקֶר אֵינוֹ חָכְמָה אֶלָּא מִצַּד הַדִּמְיוֹן הַכּוֹזֵב, וּבֶאֱמֶת הוּא סִכְלוּת
for falsehood is not wisdom, but deceitful imagination, being in truth folly;
וְחַכְמֵי הָמָן שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם תֹּקֶף חָכְמָה... הִשִּׂיגוּ זֶה דְּמַעֲלַת זֶרַע הַיְּהוּדִים וְשֶׁהָמָן מוּכְרָח לִיפּוֹל
and the wise men of Haman, who possessed profound worldly wisdom, recognized the greatness of the seed of the Jews and that Haman was doomed to fall;
וְהִגִּיעוּ לָזֶה בַּסּוֹף כְּשֶׁהָיָה סָמוּךְ לַנְּפִילָה, וּכְבָר הָיָה אַתְחַלְתָּא בְּפֹעַל
reaching this conclusion at the very end when his downfall was imminent, having already begun in deed;
וְהָיָה מוּכָן כְּבָר לָבוֹא לִידֵי גְּמָר, שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ לָזֶה כָּל כָּךְ חָכְמָה הַמְצוֹרֶפֶת לְדַעַת בִּידִיעַת הַנֶּעְלָם
it being poised for completion, requiring no profound prophetic Da'as of the hidden;
שֶׁזֶּה אֵינוֹ בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, רַק אֵצֶל חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא נִסְתַּלְּקָה הַנְּבוּאָה מֵהֶם
which divine perception is withheld from the nations, belonging exclusively to the sages of Israel from whom prophecy was never removed;
וְגַם אָז עַדַיִין הָיְתָה הַנְּבוּאָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא נִסְתַּלְּקָה עַדַיִין מִימוֹת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and even then prophecy still existed in Israel, having not yet departed since the days of Moshe;
רַק לְעִנְיַן הַהַשָּׂגָה דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה הָיָה רַק לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּלְבַד, שֶׁעַד יוֹם מוֹתוֹ הוֹסִיף תּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת:
except regarding the independent innovation of the words of the Torah itself, which was unique to Moshe Rabbeinu alone, who added Torah and mitzvos until the day of his passing!

17.h: The theme: Moshe writing the final eight verses with tears, the cessation of prophecy of Torah laws, and Israel's mastery over astronomical time. Before his death, Moshe fulfilled the final commandment of writing a Sefer Torah, writing thirteen scrolls for each tribe and the Ark (Midrash Tehillim 90:3; Yerushalmi Sotah 5:6). A Torah scroll lacking a single letter is invalid (Menachos 29b); hence Moshe wrote the final eight verses depicting his death with tears (b'dema, Bava Batra 15a) as his soul departed, concluding the Pentateuch. From then on, "it is not in heaven" (Devarim 30:12)—no further direct legislative revelation descended from Heaven in this world. Prophecy thereafter served solely to admonish Israel to observe the Torah and to foretell the future. The nations counterpart to this is astrology (itzganinut); gentiles tremble before celestial omens (Yirmiyah 10:2), but Israel does not, for the stars govern time, and the nations are under time (tachat ha-zman). Israel is above time (l'ma'lah min ha-zman); Hashem alters planetary orbits at will, as He told Avraham regarding Jupiter (Tzedek, Shabbat 156b). When prophecy ceased, it was replaced by the intense expansion of the Oral Torah (Torah she-b'al Peh), re-accepted out of love in the days of Ahasuerus (Shabbat 88a; Midrash Tanchuma, Noach §3). Prophecy emanates from Netzach and Hod, whereas the Holy Spirit (Ruach HaKodesh) of the Sages is hewn from supernal Chochmah, transcending the prophecy of all prophets. In the First Temple, righteous leaders craved the explicit clarity of prophecy; in the Second Temple, despite the absence of the Shechinah, the splendor of Torah culminated in the deep, nocturnal secrets (mistorin) of the Oral Law (Sefer Heichalot).

p: וּמִצְוָה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה דִּכְתִיבַת סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה הָיָה לִפְנֵי מוֹתוֹ
And the final commandment of writing a Sefer Torah was fulfilled by Moshe Rabbeinu immediately prior to his death;
שֶׁקִּיֵּים בְּעַצְמוֹ גַּם כֵּן מִצְוַת ״[וְעַתָּה] כִּתְבוּ לָכֶם [אֶת הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת] וְגוֹמֵר״ (דְּבָרִים ל״א:י״ט)
fulfilling within himself likewise the command: "Now therefore write you this song for you, etc." (Devarim 31:19);
שֶׁכָּתַב שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר סִפְרֵי תוֹרוֹת (מִדְרַשׁ תְּהִלִּים פָּרָשָׁה צ׳:ג׳, וְעַיֵּין יְרוּשַׁלְמִי סוֹטָה סוֹף פֶּרֶק ה׳)
writing thirteen Torah scrolls, one for each of the twelve tribes and one for the Ark of the Covenant (Midrash Tehillim 90:3; Yerushalmi Sotah 5:6);
וּמִצְוָה זוֹ לֹא נִשְׁלְמָה אֶלָּא בְּמוֹתוֹ
and this commandment was completed only at the precise moment of his death;
שֶׁסֵּפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁחָסֵר אוֹת אַחַת — פָּסוּל (מְנָחוֹת כ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
for a Torah scroll lacking even a single letter is completely invalid (Menachos 29b);
וְגַם אוֹתָן שְׁמוֹנָה פְּסוּקִים הָיָה כּוֹתֵב בְּדֶמַע (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ט״ו עַמּוּד א׳) בְּעֵת יְצִיאַת נִשְׁמָתוֹ
and even those final eight verses depicting his death Moshe was writing with tears (b'dema) as his soul departed (Bava Batra 15a);
שֶׁאָז גָּמַר מִצְוָה הָאַחֲרוֹנָה וְדִבּוּרֵי תּוֹרָה הָאַחֲרוֹנִים
for in that instant he concluded the final commandment and the ultimate words of the Written Law;
וְאָז יָצְאָה נַפְשׁוֹ, וְנִגְנַז הַנְּבוּאָה דְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה
and then his soul departed, and prophecy imparting new words of Torah was permanently concealed;
דְּמֵעַתָּה: ״לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא״ (דְּבָרִים ל:יב), שֶׁאֵין עוֹד הִתְגַּלּוּת דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
for from that hour onward: "it is not in heaven" (Devarim 30:12; Bava Metzia 59b), there being no further legislative revelation of Torah from Heaven in this world;
וְכָל נְבוּאוֹת הַנְּבִיאִים הָיָה רַק לְהַזְהִיר עַל קִיּוּם הַתּוֹרָה וּבְהוֹדָעַת הָעֲתִידוֹת דֶּרֶךְ נְבוּאָה
and all subsequent prophecies of the prophets served solely to admonish the people regarding the observance of the Torah and to make known future events through vision.
וְדָבָר זֶה יֵשׁ לְעוּמָּתוֹ בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם חָכְמַת הָאִצְטַגְנִינִים, אֲשֶׁר יַגִּידוּ גַּם כֵּן הָעֲתִידוֹת כְּפִי אוֹתוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם
And opposing this in parallel among the nations of the world exists the wisdom of astrologers, who likewise predict the future according to the signs of the heavens;
״[וּמֵאֹתוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם אַל תֵּחָתּוּ] כִּי יֵחַתּוּ הַגּוֹיִם מֵהֵמָּה״ (יִרְמְיָה י:ב) — וְלֹא יִשְׂרָאֵל
"and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the nations are dismayed at them" (Yirmiyah 10:2)—but not Israel;
כִּי הוֹרָאָתָם הוּא מִצַּד הָעֵת וְהַזְּמָן הַנִּקְבָּע כְּפִי הוֹרָאַת הַכּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁמֵּהֶם הוּא סִידּוּר הָעִתִּים
for the predictions of the astrologers derive from temporal time determined by the planetary orbits whence cosmic seasons are arranged;
וְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לְמַטָּה מֵהַזְּמָן, וְעַל כֵּן הָעֲתִידוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם הוּא תָּלוּי בְּהָעִתִּים וְכֹוכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
and the nations of the world are subordinate to time, wherefore their future is bound to celestial seasons and constellations;
אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַעְלָה מֵהַזְּמָן
but Israel transcends time;

וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא תַּחַת הַזְּמָן, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֵם מַשִּׂיגִים כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְשַׁנֶּה עִתִּים וּמַחֲלִיף הַזְּמַנִּים וּמְסַדֵּר הַכּוֹכָבִים כִּרְצוֹנוֹ

and although they reside physically in this world which is under time, they perceive that in truth the Blessed Name alters the seasons, changes the times, and arranges the stars according to His will;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (שַׁבָּת קנ״ו עַמּוּד ב׳): ״מַאי דַּעְתָּךְ, דְּקָאֵי צֶדֶק בְּמַעֲרָב? מְהַדַּרְנָא לֵיהּ לְמִזְרָח״
as He said to Avraham Avinu (Shabbat 156b): "What is your calculation, that Jupiter (Tzedek) stands in the west? I will turn it back to the east!";
כִּי עַל יְדֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל ״דִּמְקַדְּשֵׁי לִזְמַנֵּי״ (בֵּיצָה י״ז עַמּוּד א׳) מִשְׁתַּנֶּה הָעֵת מִמַּה שֶּׁהָיָה
for through Israel who sanctifies the seasons, the appointed time is modified from its natural course;
וְכָל הַשָּׂגָתָם הָעֲתִידוֹת הָיָה עַל יְדֵי נְבוּאָה
and all of Israel's foreknowledge of the future was attained through direct prophecy.
וּמִשֶּׁנִּסְתַּלְּקָה הַנְּבוּאָה, דְּנִרְאֶה לִי דְּהָיָה זֶה עַל יְדֵי הִתְגַּבְּרוּת כֹּחַ הַחָכְמָה דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
And when prophecy ceased—which appears to me to have occurred through the intensification of the wisdom of the Oral Torah;
אַחַר דְּ״הָדַר קִבְּלוּהָ בִּימֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ״ (שַׁבָּת פ״ח עַמּוּד א׳) מֵאַהֲבַת הַנֵּס, בְּתֹקֶף וְחֵשֶׁק הַלֵּב
after "they re-accepted it in the days of Ahasuerus" (Shabbat 88a) out of love for the miracle, in the full passion and yearning of the heart;
דִּתְחִלָּה הָיָה עִיקַּר הַכְּפִיָּה דְּ״הַר כְּגִיגִית״ עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
for initially the coercion of "holding the mountain over them like a cask" was over the Oral Torah;
שֶׁצָּרִיךְ יְגִיעָה רַבָּה לְהוֹצִיא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מֵחָכְמַת הַלֵּב וְלַעֲמוֹד עַל אֲמִיתַּת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
which demands immense toil to extract words of Torah from the heart's wisdom and verify their absolute truth;
וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנְחוּמָא פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ (סִימָן ג׳), יְעוּיַּן שָׁם בִּפְנִים בָּזֶה
as written in Midrash Tanchuma (Noach §3), see inside there;
וְאָז קִבְּלוּ זֶה בְּרָצוֹן: לִיגַע וְלַעֲמוֹל בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and then in the days of Mordechai and Esther they accepted this willingly: to labor and toil in the Oral Law;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לִנְבוּאַת הַחֲכָמִים, לְהַשִּׂיג הַכֹּל בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁבְּלִבָּם
and through this they merited the prophecy of the Sages, perceiving divine truth through the Holy Spirit within their hearts;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא מַדְרֵגָה יוֹתֵר קְטַנָּה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַהַשָּׂגָה יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה
and even though the vessel of the Holy Spirit is a lower conscious level than classical prophecy, the substantive perception is incomparably greater;
וּבְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ יְכוֹלִים לְהַשִּׂיג הַרְבֵּה יוֹתֵר בְּמַדְרֵיגוֹת יוֹתֵר גְּבוֹהוֹת
for through the Holy Spirit scholars can grasp far deeper insights into the highest celestial realms;
כִּי הַשָּׂגַת כָּל נָבִיא הוּא רַק כְּפִי מַדְרֵיגָתוֹ
for the vision of every classical prophet was bounded strictly according to his prophetic level;
וְכָל נְבוּאַת הַנְּבִיאִים הוּא רַק בְּנֵצַח וָהוֹד שֶׁמִּשָּׁם יְנִיקַת הַנְּבִיאִים כַּנּוֹדָע
and all prophecy of the prophets is rooted merely in the Sefirot of Netzach and Hod whence prophets draw as is known;

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ הוּא הַמְשָׁכָה מִקּוֹדֶשׁ הָעֶלְיוֹן, חָכְמָה עֶלְיוֹנָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מַעְלָה הַרְבֵּה מֵהַשָּׂגַת כָּל הַנְּבִיאִים, אַף נְבוּאַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כַּנּוֹדָע
whereas the Holy Spirit of Torah novellae is drawn directly from supernal Chochmah, which transcends by far the prophetic vision of all prophets, even the prophecy of Moshe Rabbeinu as is known;
וְכִידוּעַ בְּכִתְבֵי הָאֲרִיזַ״ל שֶׁגִּילָּה הַרְבֵּה דְּבָרִים שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵיגַת הַשָּׂגַת הַנְּבִיאִים, כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב בְּעַצְמוֹ בְּ״שַׁעַר הַנְּבוּאָה״
as known in the writings of the Arizal who revealed secrets far above the grasp of the prophets, as he wrote in Sha'ar HaNevu'ah;
וְלֹא שֶׁהַנְּבִיאִים לֹא הִשִּׂיגוּ זֶה
and not that the biblical prophets could not comprehend this;
רַק שֶׁמִּצַּד הַנְּבוּאָה שֶׁהִיא הַהַשְׁפָּעָה הַגְּלוּיָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם לֹא הִשִּׂיגוּ זֶה
but from the channel of prophecy, which is open revelation from Heaven, they did not receive it;
אֲבָל הִשִּׂיגוּ מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁהָיָה בְּקִרְבָּם גַּם כֵּן, דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה יְכוֹלִין לְהַשִּׂיג כָּל הַנֶּעְלָמוֹת
yet they did grasp it through the internal wisdom of the Holy Spirit within them, through which one can fathom all hidden secrets.
אֶלָּא שֶׁבִּדְוֹר הַנְּבִיאִים הָיָה עִיקַּר הַחֵשֶׁק וְהַהִשְׁתּוֹקְקוּת שֶׁל רָאשֵׁי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְצַדִּיקֵי הַדּוֹרוֹת לִנְבוּאָה, שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגָה בְּרוּרָה שֶׁהוּא מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
However, in the era of the prophets the primary longing of the leaders and tzaddikim was for classical prophecy, which is a lucid, unambiguous revelation from Heaven;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַשָּׂגַת חָכְמָה שֶׁהוּא נֶעְלֶמֶת, שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר שֶׁאֵינָן אֶלָּא דִּמְיוֹנוֹת כּוֹזְבוֹת שֶׁל עַצְמוֹ וְלֹא תּוֹרַת אֱמֶת בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
unlike the internal perception of wisdom which is concealed, where there is vulnerability that the insight might be subjective imagination rather than true Torah through the Holy Spirit;
וְהֵם חָשְׁקוּ לְדָבָר בָּרוּר וִידִיעָה בְּרוּרָה, וּלְכָךְ לֹא הָיָה אָז הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַחָכְמָה דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כָּל כָּךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
and they yearned for explicit clarity and definitive knowledge, wherefore the expansion of the Oral Torah was not so widespread in the First Commonwealth;
וּכְמְפוֹרָשׁ בְּ״סֵפֶר הֵיכָלוֹת״: דְּעִיקַּר זִיוָהּ וַהֲדָרָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה הָיָה בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁרְתָה בּוֹ שְׁכִינָה
as explicitly stated in Sefer Heichalot: the true radiance and splendor of Torah flourished during the Second Temple, even though the Shechinah did not overtly rest upon it (Yoma 21b);
עַיֵּין שָׁם כַּמָּה לְשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁל שֶׁבַח שֶׁהָיָה אָז
see there the numerous expressions of praise for that era;
וּדְבִשְׁבִיל שֶׁהֵם חָשְׁקוּ לְכָךְ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְגַלֶּה לָהֶם סוֹדוֹת הַתּוֹרָה הִבְטִיחָם עַל זֶה
and because the sages of the Second Temple passionately yearned for Hashem to reveal the secrets of Torah, He promised them this;
וְהוּא הַהִתְגַּלּוּת דֶּרֶךְ חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, וְהֵם חָשְׁקוּ בְּכָךְ לְהַשִּׂיג הַשָּׂגוֹת יְתֵירוֹת, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא דֶּרֶךְ הֶעְלֵם
this being the revelation through the wisdom of the Oral Torah, they having desired to attain these higher perceptions even though cloaked in intellectual concealment;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיָה הִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַנְּבוּאָה
and through this preference occurred the departure of classical prophecy:
הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי תֹּקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם לְהִתְגַּלּוּת חִדּוּשִׁין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת הַנְּבִיאִים
namely through the supreme desire they harbored for the novellae of Torah which transcend the reach of the prophets;
וּמִסְטוֹרִין דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בְּלִבָּם בְּדֶרֶךְ הֶעְלֵם שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת לַיְלָה, נִסְתַּלְּקָה הַנְּבוּאָה שֶׁנִּמְשְׁכָה מִנְּבוּאַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and through embracing the nocturnal mystery of the Oral Torah in their hearts, classical prophecy flowing from Moshe departed;
דְּעַל כֵּן בָּאוּ דִּבְרֵיהֶם גַּם כֵּן בִּכְתָב דּוּגְמַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת יוֹם, דְּהַיְינוּ הִתְגַּלּוּת בָּרוּר שֶׁלֹּא בְּמַחֲשַׁכִּים וְהֶעְלֵם:
wherefore the words of the earlier prophets were recorded in writing like the Written Torah, which embodies the attribute of Day, that is, lucid revelation without darkness or obscurity!

17.h: The theme: Haman anticipating the end of prophecy, the descent of pagan sorcery to the feet of death, and the Greek philosophical denial of the occult. Haman—perceiving through his astrologers who see but do not understand—sensed that he was destined to trigger the cessation of prophecy. He sought to seal divine vision entirely by destroying the Torah, assuming that Adar, the month of Moshe's passing, was propitious for this. When prophecy existed in Israel to reveal the future, an unholy parallel existed among the nations through astrology, divination, and witchcraft. Yet while prophecy issued from the word of Hashem, it was not the legislative Torah from supernal Chochmah, descending from the lower attributes at the level of the "feet" (raglin). The feet descend to the realm of death ("her feet go down to death", Mishlei 5:5; ve-Atah mechayeh et kulam, Nechemyah 9:6), whence the nations derived their occult vitality. When counsel was lost from the children of Israel, gentile divination rotted as well ("is counsel perished from the prudent? is their wisdom vanished?", Yirmiyah 49:7). At the beginning of the Greek empire prophecy departed (Seder Olam Rabbah §30), and the foundation of the Oral Torah was laid. In counterpoint, Greek philosophy and rationalism arose, denying astrology, sorcery, and everything transcending human intellect. In Israel, true wisdom is the attainment of the Holy Spirit, enabling sages to know the future through Torah wisdom, as Rabban Gamliel perceived through the Holy Spirit (Eruvin 64b). Torah wisdom recognizes that authentic truth transcends mortal logic; hence Jewish sages are called "knowers of the times" (yod'ei ha-ittim), whereas among the nations, philosophers and astrologers are two divided disciplines.

p: וְהָמָן שֶׁהִרְגִּישׁ זֶה כְּדֶרֶךְ הַשָּׂגַת אִצְטַגְנִינָיו, וְחַכְמֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם ״רוֹאִין וְאֵינָם יוֹדְעִין מַה רוֹאִים״ (סוֹטָה י״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
And Haman, who sensed this through his astrologers—the sages of the heathen "seeing but not knowing what they see" (Sotah 12b);
רָאָה שֶׁהוּא יִהְיֶה סִיבָּה לְהִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַנְּבוּאָה
foresaw that his crisis would bring about the cessation of prophecy;
חָשַׁב לִסְתּוֹם חָזוֹן לְגַמְרֵי בְּאִיבּוּד הַתּוֹרָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, שֶׁחָשַׁב שֶׁזֶּה כֹּחוֹ
and he schemed to seal divine vision completely through the annihilation of the Torah, God forbid, assuming this was within his power;
וְהַחֹדֶשׁ שֶׁמֵּת בּוֹ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הַגּוֹרֵם גְּנִיזַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְהִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַנְּבוּאָה דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, הוּא עֵת מוּכָן לָזֶה
and the month wherein Moshe died—which had triggered the sealing of the Written Torah and the departure of legislative prophecy—he deemed the propitious hour for this.
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁהָיָה הַנְּבוּאָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לָדַעַת עֲתִידוֹת בְּדֶרֶךְ יְדִיעָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם
And as long as prophecy existed in Israel to know the future through heavenly knowledge transcending human intellect;
הָיָה גַּם בָּהֶם יְדִיעָה זוֹ ״זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:יד), בִּידִיעַת הָאִצְטַגְנִינִים וְקוֹסְמִים וּמְכַשְּׁפִים שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן יְדִיעוֹת שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵחָכְמָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם
there existed among the nations an unholy parallel ("one opposite the other", Koheles 7:14) through astrologers, diviners, and sorcerers whose knowledge likewise transcended human intellect;
אֲבָל לֹא מִצַּד הַמְשָׁכָה מִדַּעַת עֶלְיוֹן שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם, דְּדָבָר זֶה לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם עוֹד מִשֶּׁמֵּת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
but not through an influx drawn from supernal Da'as above the heavens, which departed from them when Moshe died;
רַק מִצַּד יְדִיעַת הָעִתִּים בְּכֹוכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת וְכַדּוֹמֶה, כִּמְעוֹנֵן שֶׁמְּחַשֵּׁב עִתִּים (סַנְהֶדְרִין ס״ה עַמּוּד ב׳)
but solely through calculating temporal times via constellations and stars, like a soothsayer (me'onen) who calculates astrological seasons (Sanhedrin 65b);
וְכֵן כָּל חָכְמַת הַקֶּסֶם וְהַכִּישׁוּף הוּא מִצַּד פְּעֻלּוֹת שֶׁתַּחַת הַזְּמָן וּלְמַטָּה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
and likewise all sorcery and magic operate through forces beneath time and under the sun.
כִּי ״זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה״: כְּמוֹ הַשָּׂגַת הַנְּבִיאִים, אַף שֶׁהָיָה בִּדְבַר ה׳, לֹא הָיָה הַשָּׂגַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא הַמְשָׁכָה מֵחָכְמָה עֶלְיוֹנָה
For one stood opposite the other: just as prophetic vision, though by the word of Hashem, was not the revelation of new Torah laws drawn from Chochmah Ila'ah;
דְּזֶה ״לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא״ (דְּבָרִים ל:יב), רַק הוּא מִמַּדְרֵיגוֹת תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת בְּסוֹד הָרַגְלִין
for Torah law "is not in heaven," prophecy descending from the lower attributes in the mystery of the "feet" (Netzach and Hod);
וְיָדוּעַ בְּסוֹד ״רַגְלֶיהָ יֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת״ (מִשְׁלֵי ה:ה), כִּי הָרַגְלִין נוֹקְבִין וְיוֹרְדִין עַד סוֹף כָּל דַּרְגִּין בְּסוֹד ״וְאַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם״ (נְחֶמְיָה ט:ו)
and it is known in the mystery of "her feet go down to death" (Mishlei 5:5), the feet piercing downward to the terminus of all rungs in the mystery of "and You preserve them all" (Nechemyah 9:6);
וְעַל כֵּן יְנִיקַת אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מֵהָרַגְלִין הָיָה מִשֶּׁלְּמַטָּה מַטָּה, מְקוֹם הַמָּוֶת מַמָּשׁ
wherefore the sustenance of the nations from the divine feet was drawn from the nethermost realms, the very locus of death;
וּמִשֶּׁאָבְדָה עֵצָה מִבָּנִים, אָז נִסְרְחָה חָכְמָתָם גַּם כֵּן (יִרְמְיָה מ״ט:ז׳)
and when holy counsel was lost from the children of Israel, their pagan wisdom deteriorated as well: "Is counsel perished from the prudent? is their wisdom vanished?" (Yirmiyah 49:7).
וּבִתְחִלַּת מַלְכוּת יָוָן הָיָה הִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַנְּבוּאָה, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵדֶר עוֹלָם (רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ל׳)
And at the beginning of the Greek empire occurred the final departure of prophecy, as written in Seder Olam Rabbah (§30);
וְאָז הָיָה יְסוֹד חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and then was established the foundation of the wisdom of the Oral Torah;
וְ״זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה״ הִתְחִילָה אָז חָכְמַת יְוָנִית וּפִילוֹסוֹפְיָא
and in parallel opposition began Greek rational philosophy;
שֶׁהִכְחִישׁוּ הָאִצְטַגְנִינוּת וְהַכִּישׁוּף וְכַדּוֹמֶה חָכְמוֹת שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִשֵּׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי
which denied astrology, sorcery, and all esoteric wisdoms that transcend human reason;
דְּרַק אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל חָכְמָתָם הוּא הַשָּׂגַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, וְיוּכְלוּ לְהַשִּׂיג עֲתִידוֹת גַּם כֵּן דֶּרֶךְ חָכְמָה וּבְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
for within Israel alone wisdom is the attainment of the Holy Spirit, enabling them to perceive future events through Torah wisdom and the Holy Spirit;
וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק הֲדַר (עֵירוּבִין ס״ד עַמּוּד ב׳): ״מִכָּאן שֶׁכִּיוֵּון רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ״
as written in Eruvin (64b): "From here it is proven that Rabban Gamliel targeted his words through the Holy Spirit";
וְכֵן בְּכַמָּה דּוּכְתֵּי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ מֵחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
and so in numerous passages regarding the Holy Spirit resting upon the sages of Israel;
וְכָל חָכְמָתָם הוּא לְהַשִּׂיג שֶׁיֵּשׁ חָכְמָה לְמַעְלָה מִשֵּׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי
their entire wisdom being to know that there exists a divine wisdom above human intellect;
וְשֶׁכָּל הַשָּׂגָתָם אֵינוֹ מִצַּד הַשָּׂגַת שֵׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי כְּלָל
and that their Torah perception does not operate through mortal logic at all.
וְעַל כֵּן אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַחֲכָמִים הֵם ״יֹדְעֵי הָעִתִּים״ גַּם כֵּן
Wherefore within Israel the Torah sages are likewise the "knowers of the times";
דִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ הוּא יְדִיעַת הָעֵת דֶּרֶךְ אִצְטַגְנִינוּת אוֹ עוֹנְנוּת שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם
which in its plain sense denotes knowledge of the future beyond human reason;
וְאֵצֶל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הֵם ב׳ מִינִים:
whereas among the nations of the world, rational philosophers and astrologers are two completely separate classes!

17.h: The theme: The royal decree to "all who know religion and law" (Dat va-Din), and the Jewish Sanhedrin as masters who establish time. Scripture states: "for so was the king's manner toward all that knew law and judgment (dat va-din)" (Esther 1:13). Dat is legislation enacted by authorities possessing knowledge transcending human intellect; Din is rational jurisprudence based on human logic. Ancient nations judged civil matters by rational logic (din) while consulting oracles, soothsayers, and idols for suprarational statutes (dat). Haman said of Israel: "their laws (dateyhem) are diverse from all people" (Esther 3:8), because the Torah is suprarational divine wisdom; "neither keep they the king's laws (datei ha-melech)" (ibid.) refers to imperial whims that defy human reason, unlike civil taxes which fall under dina d'malchuta dina (Gittin 10b). Ahasuerus consulted "the wise men who knew the times" (Esther 1:13)—which Chazal identify as the Jewish Sanhedrin, combining wisdom and knowledge of the times in a single title. While gentile astrologers merely report what they see in the stars, the Sages of Israel arrange time itself, the calendar being committed to their jurisdiction to intercalate years and sanctify months. Ahasuerus questioned whether Vashti was liable to execution according to Torah wisdom (Chochmah) and whether the propitious moment (Et) had arrived to execute a queen. Heaven orchestrated this so the Sanhedrin would arouse the remedy before the blow. The Sages who attended the feast initially erred; but following their stumble, their hearts smote them (like David in I Shmuel 24:5; Alshich), returning to Hashem with full repentance and awakening the divine cure.

p: וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר: ״כִּי כֵן דְּבַר הַמֶּלֶךְ לִפְנֵי כָּל יֹדְעֵי דָּת וָדִין״ (אֶסְתֵּר א:יג)
And this is what Scripture states: "for so was the king's manner toward all that knew law and judgment (dat va-din)" (Esther 1:13);
״דָּת״ הוּא נִימוּס הַמְחוֹקָק עַל פִּי יוֹדְעִים וּבַעֲלֵי דַּעַת, שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם וְשֵׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי
Dat is a statute enacted by authorities possessing knowledge transcending human reason and mortal intellect;
״וְדִין״ הוּא מִשְׁפַּט הַשֵּׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי
while Din is civil law derived from rational human intellect;
וְכָל דָּבָר הָיוּ שׁוֹפְטִים עַל פִּי חָכְמַת הַשֵּׂכֶל, וְעַל פִּי הַיְּדִיעוֹת שֶׁהָיָה אֶצְלָם בְּמַה שֶּׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשֵּׂכֶל
the ancients judging all matters via rational logic and through suprarational divination;
כְּמִנְהַג הָעַמִּים הַקַּדְמוֹנִים בְּעִנְיַן כָּל דָּבָר פְּרָטִי: לִקְסוֹם קֶסֶם וְלִשְׁאוֹל בִּתְרָפִים וְכַיּוֹצֵא
as was the custom of ancient nations regarding every particular dilemma: casting lots, consulting teraphim, and the like;
וְכָל הַדָּתוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם הֵם חֻוקִּים נוֹסְדוּ לָהֶם מִקּוֹסְמִים וְאִצְטַגְנִינִים וּמְכַשְּׁפִים וְכַיּוֹצֵא מֵעוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
all their pagan religions being statutes instituted by diviners, astrologers, and sorcerers.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר גַּם עַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל: ״וְדָתֵיהֶם שֹׁנוֹת [מִכָּל עָם]״ (אֶסְתֵּר ג:ח), כִּי הַתּוֹרָה הִיא גַּם כֵּן לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשֵּׂכֶל
Wherefore Haman argued regarding Israel: "and their laws (dateyhem) are diverse from all people" (Esther 3:8), for the Torah likewise transcends human reason;
״וְאֶת דָּתֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ [אֵינָם עֹשִׂים]״ (שָׁם), כִּי כֵן הוּא מִנְהָגָם שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ יוּכַל לִגְזוֹר וְלַחְקוֹק דָּת כִּרְצוֹנוֹ אֲפִילּוּ נֶגֶד הַשֵּׂכֶל, רַק שֶׁהוּא רְצוֹן הַמֶּלֶךְ
"neither keep they the king's laws (datei ha-melech)" (ibid.), for it was their custom that a monarch could legislate suprarational decrees according to his whim;
וְעַל כֵּן הוּא נִקְרָא ״דָּת״ וְלֹא ״דִּין״ שֶׁהוּא מַה שֶּׁעַל פִּי הַשֵּׂכֶל, כְּגוֹן נְתִינַת מִסִּים וְכַיּוֹצֵא
wherefore an arbitrary royal decree is called Dat and not Din (which is rational law such as tax collection);
דְּעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (גִּיטִּין י׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דִּינָא דְּמַלְכוּתָא — דִּינָא״, וְלֹא הָיוּ עוֹבְרִים עַל זֶה
regarding which the Gemara ruled: "the law of the kingdom is law" (dina d'malchuta dina, Gittin 10b), which Jews never transgressed;
רַק ״דָּתֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ״ זֶה אֵין בִּכְלַל דִּינָא דְּמַלְכוּתָא, וְלֹא הָיוּ עוֹשִׂים
but arbitrary pagan religious decrees are excluded from dina d'malchuta, and Israel refused to obey them.
וְהַמֶּלֶךְ שָׁאַל לַחֲכָמִים שֶׁהֵם ״יֹדְעֵי הָעִתִּים״, דִּכְלָלִינְהוּ בְּחַד דְּלֹא אָמַר ״וְיֹדְעֵי הָעִתִּים״
And the king consulted the sages who were "the knowers of the times," joining both titles as one without a connective vav;
מִזֶּה אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: דְּהֵם חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁאֶצְלָם הַחָכְמָה וִידִיעַת הָעִתִּים... הַכֹּל אֶחָד
from which the Sages deduced (Megillah 12b): these are the Sages of Israel, in whom wisdom and knowledge of the times are identical;
כִּי חָכְמָתָם הוּא חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם
their wisdom being the divine Torah transcending human logic;
וְנִכְלָל בַּתֹּאַר ״יֹדְעֵי״ דְּהוּא הַדַּעַת, שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ בְּהַמְשָׁכָה מִלְּמַעְלָה מֵחָכְמַת אָדָם
encompassed in the title "knowers" (yod'ei), alluding to Da'as, the attainment of the Holy Spirit from Above;
וְאֵצֶל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הַיְּדִיעָה הוּא מִצַּד הָעֵת כִּי הֵם תַּחַת הָעֵת
whereas among the nations knowledge is dictated by time, they being subordinate to time.
וְעַל זֶה הָיְתָה שְׁאֵלָתוֹ: אִם מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה מַגִּיעַ לָהּ מִשְׁפַּט הַמִּיתָה, וְאִם מִצַּד הָעֵת מַגִּיעַ לָהּ זֶה שֶׁרָאוּי כָּךְ לְפִי הָעֵת וְהָעוֹנָה הַהִיא לְהָמִית מַלְכָּה
And this was the inquiry: whether according to legal wisdom death was warranted, and whether according to the propitious hour it was fitting to execute a queen;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת עִיקַּר מִשְׁפָּטָהּ רַק מִצַּד הָעֵת
and in truth her execution was destined specifically on account of the propitious hour:
דְּהַצָּלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי זֶה אַחַר כָּךְ בִּגְזֵירַת הָמָן שֶׁחָשַׁב עִתִּים לְהַשְׁמִידָם
for the future salvation of Israel from Haman, who sought an auspicious time to destroy them;
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָשַׁב הָעֵת דְּהַקְדָּמַת הָרְפוּאָה בַּהֲרִיגַת וַשְׁתִּי
while the Blessed Name calculated the hour to bring the cure before the blow through the execution of Vashti;
עַל כֵּן שָׁאַל גַּם כֵּן עֵצָה לַחֲכָמִים יוֹדְעֵי הָעִתִּים, שֶׁנִּמְלַךְ בַּסַּנְהֶדְרִין שֶׁהֵם מְסַדְּרֵי הָעִתִּים
wherefore the King took counsel with the Sages of the Sanhedrin who arrange the times;
וְזֶהוּ ״יוֹדְעִים לְקַדֵּשׁ [חֳדָשִׁים וּלְעַבֵּר שָׁנִים] וְכוּלֵיהּ״ (מְגִלָּה י״ב עַמּוּד ב׳), שֶׁהוּא סִידּוּר הָעִתִּים דִּשְׁנוֹת הַחַמָּה וְחָדְשֵׁי הַלְּבָנָה
this being "they who know how to sanctify months and intercalate years" (Megillah 12b), which is the cosmic arrangement of solar years and lunar months;
וְלֹא כְּיוֹדְעֵי הָעִתִּים דְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁהֵם יוֹדְעִים הוֹרָאַת הָעֵת, וּכְפִי מַה שֶּׁרוֹאִים הוֹרָאַת הָעֵת הֵם מַגִּידִים
unlike gentile astrologers who merely read the signs of the hour, reporting what they observe;
אֲבָל חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם מְסַדְּרִים הָעִתִּים, שֶׁהָעִתִּים מְסוּרִים בְּיָדָם לְשַׁנּוֹת וּלְסַדֵּר כִּרְצוֹנָם
but the Sages of Israel establish the times, time being delivered into their hands to adjust and arrange according to their will.
וּבְוַדַּאי חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהָיוּ שָׁם בַּסְּעוּדָה וְחָשְׁבוּ תְּחִלָּה שֶׁכָּךְ רָאוּי, הַטָּעוּת הָיְתָה רַק קוֹדֶם מַעֲשֶׂה
And certainly the Sages of Israel who were present at the feast and initially rationalized that it was proper to attend, their error existed only prior to the deed;
אֲבָל תֵּיכֶף אַחַר כָּךְ וַדַּאי הִתְבּוֹנְנוּ וְעָמְדוּ עַל הָאֱמֶת
but immediately afterward they contemplated and realized the truth;
דְּ״אֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְשַׁל בָּהֶם״ (גִּיטִּין מ״ג עַמּוּד א׳)
for "a man does not comprehend the true depths of Torah unless he stumbles in them" (Gittin 43a);
וְאַחַר הַמִּכְשׁוֹל עוֹמֵד עַל הָאֱמֶת
and following the stumbling one arrives at the absolute truth;
וְכִידוּעַ דִּבְרֵי הָאַלְשִׁיךְ עַל פָּסוּק ״וַיַּךְ לֵב דָּוִד [אֹתוֹ]״ (שְׁמוֹת א כ״ד:ה׳)
and as known the explanation of the Alshich on "and David's heart smote him" (I Shmuel 24:5):
דְּמִתְּחִלָּה שֶׁהָיָה נוֹגֵעַ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה שָׁאוּל אוֹיְבוֹ, לֹא יָכוֹל לַעֲמוֹד עַל הָאֱמֶת
initially, having personal bias because Saul pursued him, he could not fathom the objective truth;
וְהַבֵּירוּר הוּא אַחַר הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁנִּתְחָרֵט ״וַיַּךְ לִבּוֹ״
the clarification emerging after the act when he repented and his heart smote him;
וּבְוַדַּאי נִתְחָרְטוּ וְשָׁבוּ בְּכָל לֵב עַל זֶה, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הִתְעוֹרְרָה הָרְפוּאָה:
and the Sanhedrin certainly repented with all their heart over their attendance, and through this heartfelt repentance the divine cure was awakened!

17.h: The theme: Hashem consulting the Sages, Memuchan digging his own pit, and the limit of gentile foresight. The King of kings consulted the Sages of Israel regarding Vashti just as He consulted the souls of the righteous prior to creating Man ("Let us make man", Bereishis Rabbah 8:7). In every generation, the eminent Torah leaders constitute the Heavenly Court on Earth: Hashem does nothing without their counsel, the righteous ruling in the fear of God with power to annul divine decrees (Moed Katan 16b; Bereishis 18:17). The time had arrived for the rebuilding of the Second Temple at the close of Jeremiah's seventy years. Recognizing that they had sinned by attending the banquet, the Sanhedrin refused to rule based on their personal Torah merit; instead, they invoked the collective merit of the Temple sacrifices, which even simple Jews passionately yearned to restore. In the earthly court, when Ahasuerus consulted them, they recused themselves from judging Vashti, refusing to let an accuser become an advocate (ein kateigor na'aseh saneigor, Berachos 59a). Their inward repentance caused Heaven to inspire Memuchan—who is Haman (Megillah 12b)—to dig his own pit by counseling Vashti's execution, preparing his own gallows. From that moment he was called Memuchan, being prepared (muchan) for retribution. Haman was blinded by pride, whereas authentic wisdom belongs to one who foresees future consequences (eizehu chacham haro'eh et ha-nolad, Tamid 32a). Haman’s pagan astrologers possessed a trace of foresight, warning him that if Mordechai is of the seed of the Jews he would fall (Esther 6:13); yet Haman stubbornly refused to believe his own downfall, pleading for his life before Esther.

p: וְזֶהוּ הַשְּׁאֵלָה דְּמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
And this was the inquiry of the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He;
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ח:ז) עַל פָּסוּק ״נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית א:כו): דִּבְנִשְׁמוֹתֵיהֶן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים נִמְלָךְ
after the manner the Sages expounded in Bereishis Rabbah (8:7) on the verse "Let us make man" (Bereishis 1:26): that He consulted the souls of the righteous;
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁאָלָם אִם מוּכָנִים לְמַה שֶּׁהוּא רוֹצֶה מִצּוּרַת הָאָדָם הַשָּׁלֵם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
the Blessed Name asking them if they were prepared for the consummate form of Man in this world.
וְכָךְ בַּהֲכָנַת הַצָּלָה זוֹ שֶׁהוּא הַיְסוֹד לַחֲזָרַת קַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
And so in preparing this salvation which was the foundation for re-accepting the Written and Oral Torah;
דְּבָזֶה הָיָה הִתְהַפְּכוּת הָעֵת לִהְיוֹת ״בִּיטּוּלָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה״ שֶׁחָשַׁב הָמָן בִּגְנִיזַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְהִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַנְּבוּאָה
wherein occurred the inversion of time, turning the perceived "destruction of the Torah" (which Haman assumed through the sealing of the Written Torah and cessation of prophecy);

זֶה ״יְסוֹדָהּ דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה״ שֶׁהִיא עִיקַּר כְּרִיתַת הַבְּרִית, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּגִיטִּין (ס׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) וּבִשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה עַל פָּסוּק ״כִּי עַל פִּי הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה [כָּרַתִּי אִתְּךָ בְּרִית]״ (שְׁמוֹת ל״ד:כ״ז)
into the very foundation of the Oral Torah, which is the primary covenant of Israel (Gittin 60b; Shemos Rabbah 47:1);
שָׁאַל לְחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹדְעֵי הָעִתִּים אִם הֵם מוּכָנִים לְכָךְ
Hashem inquired of the Sages of Israel who know the times if they were prepared for this mission;
וְ״כִי כֵן דְּבַר הַמֶּלֶךְ״ (אֶסְתֵּר א:יג), הַיְינוּ כִּי כָּךְ מִשְׁפְּטֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: לִהְיוֹת הַכֹּל עַל פִּי מִשְׁפְּטֵי הַתּוֹרָה
and "for so was the king's manner" (Esther 1:13): for such are the ways of Hashem, conducting all things according to the jurisprudence of the Torah;
״דָּת וָדִין״ הוּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
"law and judgment" (dat va-din) embodying the Written Torah and Oral Torah;
וְיֵשׁ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מַעְלָה וְסַנְהֶדְרֵי עֶלְיוֹנָה יוֹדְעֵי דָּת וָדִין שֶׁעַל פִּיהֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דָּן דִּין הַכֹּל
there existing a Heavenly Court and supernal Sanhedrin knowing law and judgment through whom the Blessed Name adjudicates all things;
וְהֵם בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר רָאשֵׁי חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר, וְהֵם הַסַּנְהֶדְרֵי גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר
these being in every generation the preeminent Sages of Israel who constitute the Great Sanhedrin of their era.
וְאַף מִשֶּׁבָּטְלוּ הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין, רָאשֵׁי חַכְמֵי הַדּוֹר הָרְאוּיִם לִהְיוֹת מִכְּלַל הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין אִילּוּ הָיָה סַנְהֶדְרֵי גְּדוֹלָה, יֵשׁ בְּכָל דּוֹר כְּפִי הָרָאוּי לְאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר
And even after the Sanhedrin was dissolved, the leading Torah sages of each generation who would have sat on the Sanhedrin guide the era;
וְהֵם גַּם כֵּן הַבֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מַעְלָה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִמְלָךְ בָּהֶם וְאֵין עוֹשֶׂה דָּבָר בְּלֹא דַּעְתָּם
and they constitute the Heavenly Court with whom the Blessed Name consults, executing nothing without their consensus;
כִּי ״[צַדִּיק] מוֹשֵׁל בְּיִרְאַת אֱלֹהִים״ (שְׁמוּאֵל ב כ״ג:ג׳; שַׁבָּת ס״ג עַמּוּד א׳), וְיָכוֹל לְבַטֵּל גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גּוֹזֵר
for "the righteous rules in the fear of God" (II Shmuel 23:3; Shabbat 63a), empowered to annul what the Blessed Name decrees;
וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּגְזֵירַת סְדוֹם: ״הַמְכַסֶּה אֲנִי מֵאַבְרָהָם [אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי עֹשֶׂה]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ח:י״ז), וְנִמְלַךְ בּוֹ
as written regarding Sodom: "Shall I hide from Abraham that which I do?" (Bereishis 18:17), consulting him;
וְכָךְ אָז נִמְלַךְ בְּחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהֵם עוֹרְרוּ זְכוּת הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת
and so then Hashem consulted the Sages of Israel, and they awakened the merit of the Temple sacrifices;
כִּי הִגִּיעַ זְמַן בִּנְיַן בַּיִת שֵׁנִי שֶׁהִבְטִיחַ לְיִרְמְיָה לְקֵץ שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה (יִרְמְיָה כ״ט:י׳)
for the time had arrived for the rebuilding of the Second Temple promised to Jeremiah at the end of seventy years (Yirmiyah 29:10).
וּלְפִי שֶׁיָּדְעוּ שֶׁחָטְאוּ, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשָּׁבוּ וּבְכֹחַ תְּשׁוּבָתָם הוּא שֶׁיְּעוֹרְרוּ הַהַצָּלָה וְהָרְפוּאָה בְּעִנְיַן וַשְׁתִּי
And because they knew they had stumbled by attending the banquet, even though they had repented;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֵם שֶׁהָיָה חֶטְאָם נֶגְדָּם עַדַיִין וְלֹא הֶאֱמִינוּ עַדַיִין שֶׁנִּתְקַבְּלָה תְּשׁוּבָתָם
nevertheless, their sin standing before them, not daring to presume their repentance had been fully accepted;
לֹא רָצוּ לָבוֹא בִּזְכוּת עַצְמָם, וְלִשְׁפּוֹט מִצַּד עַצְמָם שֶׁהֵם בְּתוֹרָתָם מְקַיְּימִים הָעוֹלָם וְשֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבַטֵּל וּלְאַבֵּד הַתּוֹרָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
they refused to plead their own merit, arguing that their Torah study preserves the cosmos;
שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה הוּא מִצַּד זְכוּת עַצְמָם שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה מַרְבִּיצֵי הַתּוֹרָה
for that would rely upon their personal virtue as leaders of the Great Assembly;
וְהֵם בָּאוּ לִתְלוֹת בִּזְכוּת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהוּא זְכוּת הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל זוֹכִין לָהּ
and they chose instead to invoke the collective merit of all Israel: the merit of the Temple sacrifices shared by all;
וַאֲפִילּוּ הָעַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ כּוּלָּם הִשְׁתּוֹקְקוּ לָהּ מְאֹד
which even the most simple, unlearned Jews passionately yearned to see restored;
וְלֹא בָּאוּ דֶּרֶךְ גְּזֵירָה כְּמִשְׁפַּט ״צַדִּיק גּוֹזֵר [וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַיֵּים]״ (תַּעֲנִית כ״ג עַמּוּד א׳)
not commanding via decree like "the righteous decrees and the Holy One fulfills" (Ta'anis 23a);
כִּי לֹא הֶחֱזִיקוּ עַצְמָם צַדִּיקִים אַחַר שֶׁהִרְגִּישׁוּ חֶטְאָם
for they did not hold themselves righteous after feeling their fault;
רַק בָּאוּ דֶּרֶךְ בַּקָּשָׁה וְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת רַחֲמִים, שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ יְרַחֵם עֲלֵיהֶם
approaching solely through supplication, pleading that the Blessed Name Himself have compassion upon them.
וּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: דְּמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אָמְרוּ ״מִי יַקְרִיב וְכוּלֵיהּ״
And regarding what the Sages stated: that the ministering angels argued, "Who will bring offerings before You, etc.";
נִרְאֶה לִי דְּ״מַאן מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת — רַבָּנַן״, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּנְדָרִים (דַּף כ׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
it appears to me that the ministering angels allegorically denote the Rabbis, as written in Nedarim (20b);
וְכֵן הוּא הַדָּבָר בְּפֹעַל בְּמַלְכוּתָא דְּאַרְעָא: שֶׁכְּשֶׁשָּׁאַל אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ לַסַּנְהֶדְרִין, סִילְּקוּ עַצְמָם מִדִּין זֶה
and so was the matter reflected in the earthly kingdom: when Ahasuerus consulted the Sanhedrin, they recused themselves from the judgment of Vashti;
כִּי לֹא רָצוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַדִּין עַל יְדֵי גְּזֵירָתָם
not wanting the verdict to issue through their judicial decree;
כִּי לֹא רָאוּ עַצְמָם כְּדָאִים לְכָךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַנֵּס נַעֲשָׂה עַל יָדָם
not considering themselves worthy that the miracle be wrought through their agency;
בְּחָשְׁבָם כִּי הֵם הַחוֹטְאִים וְגוֹרְמִים קִיטְרוּג, וְ״אֵין קַטֵּיגוֹר נַעֲשָׂה סַנֵּיגוֹר״ (בְּרָכוֹת נ״ט עַמּוּד א׳)
thinking that having attended the feast they were the sinners, and "an accuser cannot become a defender" (Berachos 59a);
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם בֶּאֱמֶת הֵם פָּעֲלוּ עִיקַּר נֵס זֶה בְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּת תְּשׁוּבָתָם שֶׁזֶּה גָּרַם שֶׁיִּשְׁאַל לָהֶם
yet in truth they effected the primary miracle through their heartfelt repentance, which prompted the king to consult them;
שֶׁבָּזֶה הִתְבּוֹנְנוּ וְיָדְעוּ דְּלֹא לְחִנָּם שָׁאַל לָהֶם, רַק כִּי לָהֶם הַדָּבָר שַׁיָּיךְ לְתַקֵּן זֶה
perceiving that not in vain did the king approach them, but because it was their task to repair the breach;
וְעוֹרְרוּ רַחֲמִים לְמַעְלָה בְּהַזְכָּרַת זְכוּת הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת
awakening supernal compassion by recalling the merit of the Temple sacrifices.
עַד שֶׁנִּשְׁלַח מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם בְּלֵב מְמוּכָן, שֶׁהוּא הָמָן בְּעַצְמוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִלָּה י״ב עַמּוּד ב׳)
Until Heaven placed it into the heart of Memuchan—who is Haman himself, as the Sages stated (Megillah 12b);
שֶׁהוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ יַחְפּוֹר שׁוּחָה לוֹ, וְהֵכִין רְפוּאָה לְמַכָּתָן וּפֻרְעָנוּת לְעַצְמוֹ
that he himself should dig his own pit, preparing the cure for Israel's blow and retribution for himself;
וּמֵאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ ״מְמוּכָן״, שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה אָז מוּכָן לְאוֹתוֹ פֻּרְעָנוּת
and from that hour he was called Memuchan, having become prepared (muchan) for retribution:
תְּחִלָּה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לִפְנִים, וְאַחַר כָּךְ בֶּאֱמֶת לוֹ
initially threatening Israel superficially (lifnim), and subsequently falling in absolute truth upon himself;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ הֵכִין הָעֵץ בְּעַצְמוֹ (אֶסְתֵּר ז:ט), כָּךְ הֵכִין לוֹ עִיקַּר הַפֻּרְעָנוּת מִתְּחִלָּה בְּעֵצָה זוֹ
and just as he prepared the gallows for himself (Esther 7:9), so he engineered his own destruction through his counsel to execute Vashti;
הַכֹּל הָיָה הוּא גּוֹרֵם לְעַצְמוֹ, כִּי הוּא חָשַׁב עַצְמוֹ חָכָם מִכָּל בְּנֵי דּוֹרוֹ, דְּעַל כֵּן חָשַׁב הַשְׁאָרַת הַחָכְמָה בּוֹ
he bringing everything upon himself, imagining himself wiser than all his contemporaries;
וְזֶהוּ קְפִיצָתוֹ בָּרֹאשׁ מִפְּנֵי גַּאֲוָתוֹ בְּחָכְמָה יוֹתֵר מִכּוּלָּם
this explaining why he jumped forward to speak first (Megillah 12b), driven by intellectual arrogance;
וְ״אֵיזֶהוּ חָכָם — הָרוֹאֶה אֶת הַנּוֹלָד״ (תָּמִיד ל״ב עַמּוּד א׳), דְּזֶהוּ עִיקַּר חָכְמָה הָאֲמִיתִּית דְּחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
while "who is wise? He who foresees consequences" (Tamid 32a), this being the authentic wisdom of the Sages of Israel.
וְגַם חֲכָמָיו שֶׁהָיוּ מֵחַכְמֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁאֵין חָכְמָתָם מְחוּבֶּרֶת עִם דַּעַת שֶׁהוּא יְדִיעַת הַנּוֹלָד וְהֶעָתִיד
And even Haman's counselors from the wise men of the nations—whose wisdom was not integrated with divine Da'as to perceive the future;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִצַּד שֶׁאָז לֹא נִסְתַּלְּקָה הַנְּבוּאָה עַדַיִין, וְהָיָה כֹּחַ יְדִיעָה גַּם בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
nonetheless, since prophecy had not yet completely departed and a residual capacity for foresight existed among the nations;
אַף שֶׁהָיָה שֶׁלֹּא מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֵם שֶׁהָיוּ נֶגֶד הַתְחָלַת הַחָכְמָה דְּחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְסוֹף הַנְּבוּאָה
they who stood opposite the inception of the Oral Torah and the end of prophecy;
זָכוּ לְשֶׁמֶץ דְּבַר חָכְמָה בִּרְאִיַּית הַנּוֹלָד הַקָּרוֹב מְאֹד לְמַרְאֵה עֵינֵיהֶם בְּמַפַּלְתּוֹ שֶׁל הָמָן
merited a faint trace of wisdom in perceiving the imminent downfall of Haman right before their eyes;
אֲבָל הָמָן עַצְמוֹ לֹא הֶאֱמִין גַּם בָּזֶה
but Haman himself refused to believe even this;
וַאֲפִילּוּ אַחַר שֶׁרָאָה הַצָּרָה לְנוֹכַח עֵינָיו בְּדִבְרֵי אֶסְתֵּר לַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו
and even after he beheld the catastrophe facing him when Esther denounced him to the king;
וְנוֹדַע לוֹ שֶׁהִיא מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל וְשֶׁמַּפַּלְתּוֹ קְרוֹבָה כְּדִבְרֵי חֲכָמָיו
knowing she was Jewish and that his ruin was at hand as his wise men had predicted;
עַל כָּל זֶה חָשַׁב עַדַיִין לְהִמָּלֵט וּלְבַקֵּשׁ עַל נַפְשׁוֹ מֵאֶסְתֵּר:
despite all this he still deluded himself that he could escape, falling upon the couch to plead for his life before Esther!

17.h: The theme: Haman's folly, his assault on Esther, the name Memuchan as mere preparation, and Shushan Purim. The Blessed Name exposed Haman's sheer foolishness: whatever he cunningly devised to elevate himself and harm others redounded to his own ruin from beginning to end. When Ahasuerus returned and exclaimed: "Will he even force the queen before me in the house?" (Esther 7:8), this narrative was recorded to reveal the depth of wicked depravity: even at the very threshold of Gehinnom, the wicked do not repent (Eruvin 19a). Haman threw himself upon the couch intentionally to violate and defile Esther, plotting that even if begun under duress, she would eventually succumb to unholy intimacy—as stated regarding Dinah that once a woman is defiled by an uncircumcised pagan, it is difficult to detach her (Bereishis Rabbah 80:11)—hoping to bring her under his influence to forget her people and ancestral heritage. He still refused to acknowledge that all events were divinely orchestrated for Israel's salvation, continuing to plot how to fulfill his evil schemes; in that instant his verdict was sealed for absolute destruction. Amalek is the "first of the nations" (reishit goyim), having power solely in the initial thought (machshavah) without the ability to actualize it into lasting deed (po'al), for had his cosmic evil actualized, the world could not endure. Thus he is called Memuchan—meaning mere preparation (hachanah) without completion, an inception devoid of an end. Through his own gallows he unwittingly prepared the cure before the blow, awakening Israel's heart to re-accept the Torah out of love; on account of this preparatory spark, his descendants merited to study Torah in Bnei Brak (Sanhedrin 96b). While the fourteenth of Adar commemorates the salvation from the decree, the fifteenth commemorates the rectification of Shushan’s feast where the cure was hatched, establishing Shushan Purim for all generations.

p: וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֶרְאָה סִכְלוּתוֹ, שֶׁבְּכָל מַה שֶּׁהִתְחַכֵּם לְהֵטִיב לְעַצְמוֹ וּלְהָרַע לְזוּלָתוֹ הוֹסִיף רָעָה לְעַצְמוֹ מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף
And the Blessed Name demonstrated Haman's sheer foolishness, for in all that he cunningly devised to benefit himself and harm others, he brought increased evil upon himself from beginning to end;
שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ אָמַר: ״הֲגַם לִכְבּוֹשׁ אֶת הַמַּלְכָּה [עִמִּי בַּבָּיִת]״ (אֶסְתֵּר ז:ח)
when the king exclaimed: "Will he even force the queen before me in the house?" (Esther 7:8);
וְלֹא לְחִנָּם נִכְתַּב סִפּוּר זֶה גַּם כֵּן, רַק לְהוֹדִיעַ עַד הֵיכָן רִשְׁעוּת הָרְשָׁעִים, שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ עַל פִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם אֵין חוֹזְרִים (עֵירוּבִין י״ט עַמּוּד א׳)

and not in vain was this narrative recorded in the Megillah, but to make known the fathomless depth of the wicked's depravity, that even at the very portal of Gehinnom they do not repent (Eruvin 19a);
וְלֹא אָמַר שֶׁקֶר ״לִכְבּוֹשׁ״, דִּדְבַר שֶׁקֶר וּמַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ לֹא הָיָה נִכְתָּב בַּמְּגִלָּה
and Ahasuerus spoke no falsehood in saying "to force," for an untruth or an event that never occurred would not have been inscribed in the holy Megillah;
אֲבָל הָמָן נָפַל לְאָנְסָהּ וּלְטַמְּאָהּ
but Haman actually fell upon the couch intending to violate and defile her;
וְכַוָּונָתוֹ הָיְתָה: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁתְּחִלָּתָהּ בְּאוֹנֶס, סוֹף יִהְיֶה בְּרָצוֹן
and his demonic intention was: even though it begin under duress, it would ultimately turn to consent;
שֶׁיַּכְנִיס בָּהּ זוּהֲמָא, דְּעַל יְדֵי הַנִּבְעֶלֶת לְעָרֵל קָשֶׁה לִפְרוֹשׁ, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פ׳:י״א) בְּדִינָה אַף שֶׁהָיָה בְּאוֹנֶס

injecting into her unholy defilement, for once a woman has intimacy with an uncircumcised pagan it is difficult to detach her, as written in Bereishis Rabbah (80:11) regarding Dinah even though it began under duress;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל אַחַר כָּךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת כִּרְצוֹנוֹ, שֶׁגַּם הִיא תִּמָּשֵׁךְ אַחֲרָיו וְתִשְׁכַּח עַמָּהּ וּמוֹלַדְתָּהּ
and through this he hoped to manipulate her according to his whim, that she too would be drawn after him and forget her people and her kindred;
וְעַדַיִין לֹא הוֹדָה וְלֹא הִכִּיר אֵיךְ הַכֹּל סִיבּוֹת מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם לְהַצָּלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל
and even then he refused to concede or recognize how all these circumstances were heavenly orchestrations for Israel's salvation;
רַק עָמַד עֲדַיִין בְּשֶׁלּוֹ, וְחָשַׁב מַחֲשָׁבוֹת לְקַיֵּים מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ
persisting obstinately in his rebellion, contriving schemes to fulfill his malice;
וּבָזֶה נִגְמַר דִּינוֹ לֵיאָבֵד מִן הָעוֹלָם, כִּי אֵין בּוֹ עוֹד תִּקְוָה וְתוֹחֶלֶת אֲפִילּוּ עַל פִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם
and in that moment his verdict was sealed for absolute destruction from the world, having no lingering hope or remedy even at the gate of Gehinnom.
וְהוּא ״רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם״ (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ״ד:כ׳), וְאֵין בּוֹ כֹּחַ הַיְצִיאָה לַפּוֹעַל
And he embodies "the first of the nations" (Bamidbar 24:16), possessing no capacity to emerge into enduring actualization;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּל רָעָתוֹ וְכֹחוֹ נֶגֶד יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה רַק בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁחָשַׁב עַל הַיְּהוּדִים לְאַבְּדָם, אֲבָל לֹא הוֹצִיא לַפּוֹעַל כְּלוּם
and just as his entire malice against Israel remained confined to thought—plotting to destroy the Jews without actualizing a single murder;
כָּךְ כָּל חָכְמָתוֹ הָיָה בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה, וּכְשֶׁיָּצָא לַפּוֹעַל נִרְאָה שֶׁהוּא סִכְלוּת
so his entire wisdom existed merely in abstract thought, and when brought to deed it was revealed as utter folly;
כִּי כְּפִי כֹּחַ הָרָע שֶׁבּוֹ, אִילּוּ הָיָה מוֹצִיא הַכֹּל לַפּוֹעַל לֹא הָיָה קִיּוּם לָעוֹלָם
for given the intensity of evil within him, had he actualized his schemes the universe could not have endured;
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא נְתָנוֹ אֱלֹהִים לְהָרַע וּלְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט
wherefore God did not permit him to inflict harm or expand outwardly;
וְנִשְׁאַר בְּכֹחוֹ שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הָרֵאשִׁית, דְּהַיְינוּ בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה לְבַד
remaining locked within his primal power, namely within potential thought alone;
וּכְשֶׁבָּא לָצֵאת לַפּוֹעַל לֹא עָלָה בְּיָדוֹ כְּלוּם
and when he sought to actualize it, nothing succeeded in his hand;
וּבָזֶה נֶאֱבַד מִן הָעוֹלָם, כִּי נִפְסַק כֹּחוֹ מִהְיוֹת רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם
and through this he perished from the world, his capacity as "first of the nations" being severed;
שֶׁנִּפְסַק כֹּחַ הַהַמְשָׁכָה מִמֶּנּוּ לְהַשְׁלָמַת קוֹמָתוֹ דְּאָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל
the conduit channeling from him to complete the stature of the Primordial Corrupt Man being cut off.
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא ״מְמוּכָן״ (אֶסְתֵּר א:טז), שֶׁהָיָה הֲכָנָה לְבַד
Wherefore he was designated Memuchan (Esther 1:16), having existed merely as a preparation (hachanah);
וְכָל רֵאשִׁית וְהַתְחָלָה הוּא הֲכָנָה לַגְּמָר וְסוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה
every beginning and inception serving as preparation for the final culmination and deed;
וְהוּא הָיָה הֲכָנָה לְבַד וְהַתְחָלָה בְּלֹא סוֹף
while he was merely a preparation, a beginning lacking a conclusion;
וְאָז בִּשְׁעַת הֲכָנַת הָרְפוּאָה עַל יָדוֹ קוֹדֶם לַמַּכָּה, דְּנִמְצָא שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה מַכָּה כְּלָל מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ וְהַכֹּל רַק כְּפִי טָעוּת מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ
and at the very hour he prepared the cure before the blow, it emerged that there was never any blow from the beginning, all having been his erroneous imagination;
נִמְצָא לֹא הָיָה אֶלָּא הֲכָנָה לְבַד
thus proving he was merely an instrument of preparation;
וְדֶעַל יְדֵי זֶה הֵכִין לְלֵב בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְקַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה מֵאַהֲבָה
and through this he prepared the hearts of Israel to re-accept the Torah out of boundless love;
וּמִצַּד הַזֶּה זָכָה לִבְנֵי בָנָיו שֶׁלָּמְדוּ תוֹרָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ״ו עַמּוּד ב׳)
and from this aspect he merited that his descendants taught Torah in Bnei Brak (Sanhedrin 96b);
וְהוּא מִצַּד הַטּוֹב שֶׁבְּשֵׁם ״מְמוּכָן״ שֶׁהָיָה הֲכָנָה לְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
this deriving from the spark of good within the name Memuchan, serving as the preparation for the Oral Torah;
דְּעַל כֵּן נִקְרָא כֵּן אָז כְּשֶׁהֵכִין הָרְפוּאָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וְשַׁחַת לְעַצְמוֹ
wherefore he was called thus in the hour he prepared the remedy for Israel and self-destruction for himself.
וְנִמְצָא: הַמִּשְׁתֶּה דְּשׁוּשָׁן מִצַּד חֶטְאָם הָיָה הַתְחָלַת הַגְּזֵירָה, וּמִצַּד תְּשׁוּבָתָם הַתְחָלַת הָרְפוּאָה וְהַיְשׁוּעָה
And thus it is found: the banquet of Shushan was through their stumble the inception of the decree, and through their repentance the inception of healing and salvation;
וְכֵן הַסּוֹף, הָעִיקָּר בְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַתְּפִלָּה וְהַצּוֹמוֹת לְבַטֵּל הַגְּזֵירָה הָיָה מָרְדֳּכַי וַחֲבֵירָיו וְתַלְמִידָיו בְּנֵי שׁוּשָׁן
and so too in the end, the primary awakening of prayer and fasting to annul the decree was spearheaded by Mordechai, his colleagues, and his disciples, the residents of Shushan;
כִּי הֵם הַנִּכָּרִים בְּעוֹבִי קוֹרַת גְּזֵירָה זוֹ
they having borne the direct brunt of this decree;
וְעַל כֵּן נִקְבַּע גַּם יוֹם טַ״ו שֶׁנָּחוּ בוֹ בְּנֵי שׁוּשָׁן לְבַד גַּם כֵּן לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל
wherefore the fifteenth of Adar, on which the Jews of Shushan alone rested, was likewise established as a commemorative day for all Israel;
