And according to some of our Sages (Rashi on I Melachim 10:13): Nebuchadnezzar descended from the seed of Solomon through the Queen of Sheba;
כִּי כָּל כֹּחַ הֶעְלֵם הִתְגַּלּוּת דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בָּא רַק עַל יְדֵי הִתְחַבְּרוּתוֹ בְּנָשִׁים נָכְרִיּוֹת
for the concealment of David's light emerged solely through Solomon's union with foreign women;
דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְעַלֵּם קְדֻשַּׁת הַבְּרִית מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, ״דְּלָא מְבַשְׁקַר לֵיהּ״ כְּמָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין (י״ט עַמּוּד א׳)
through which the sanctity of the covenant is obscured from Israel so that Avraham does not recognize them (Eruvin 19a);
שֶׁבְּדָבָר זֶה הָיָה כָּל צֹרֶךְ הוֹדָעַת תִּיקּוּנוֹ דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁלֹּא פָגַם בִּבְרִית קֹדֶשׁ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
regarding which lay the necessity of announcing David's rectification, that he had never blemished the holy covenant.
וְעִיקַּר שְׁלֵימוּת הַבְּרִית הוּא נִיכָּר כַּאֲשֶׁר כָּל זַרְעוֹ גַּם כֵּן בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת
And the true wholeness of the covenant is recognizable when all of one's offspring are in consummate perfection;
כְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁזָּכָה לִהְיוֹת ״מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה״ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה קֶרִי מִיָּמָיו כְּמָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (ע״ו עַמּוּד א׳)
like Yaakov Avinu who merited an unblemished bed because he never experienced nocturnal emission in his days (Yevamos 76a);
וְעַל כֵּן כָּל זַרְעוֹ לֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא — יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא
wherefore from his seed no outcast shall be severed, for even if he sins he remains an Israelite;
וְנִקְרָא ״מָהוּל״ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעָרֵל לְגַמְרֵי, דְּאֵין הָעָרְלָה נִקְרֵאת אֶלָּא עַל שֵׁם אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כְּמָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּנְדָרִים (ל״א עַמּוּד ב׳)
being called circumcised even if uncircumcised, for the foreskin is designated solely upon the heathen (Nedarim 31b);
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד כֹּחַ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקְּדוּשָׁה דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּכָל זַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו
this deriving from the holy root of Yaakov present within all his descendants;
וְהוּא מִצַּד הַהַתְחָלָה בִּקְדוּשָׁה דְּמִתּוֹלָדָה וּמִבֶּטֶן לִשְׁמֶךָ הֵם נִימּוֹלִים
stemming from inborn congenital sanctity where from the womb they are circumcised to His Name;
וְכָל הַחֲטָאִים וּפְגָמֵי הַבְּרִית הֵם רַק מִצַּד ״הַהוּצֵי הַסּוֹבְבִים לָאָסָא״ (סַנְהֶדְרִין מ״ד עַמּוּד א׳) וּמַעֲלִימִים אוֹתָהּ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה:
all sins and blemishes of the covenant being merely external briars encircling the myrtle (Sanhedrin 44a), veiling it in this world!

20.h: The theme: King David raising the yoke of repentance, Jeconiah's decree overturned through the Great Sanhedrin, and Semiramis taking the kingdom. David raised the yoke of repentance (Avodah Zarah 5a), rectifying all blemishes through the Book of Psalms to cut down the thorns encircling the celestial rose. Like Yaakov who never died (Ta'anit 5b), David is alive and enduring; physical death entered the world through Adam's 130 years of impurity (Eruvin 18b), which David and Mashiach rectify. David tasted the Tree of Life ("he asked life of You, and You gave it him", Tehillim 21:5). Whoever rectifies the covenant completely—whether through sinless purity like Yaakov and Eliyahu or consummate repentance like David—is promised that his seed will endure forever ("his seed shall endure forever", Tehillim 89:37). Yet when Nebuchadnezzar's power arose, exiling Jeconiah (Yechonyah) and the craftsmen, the decree was issued: "Write you this man childless" (Yirmiyah 22:30), threatening to extinguish the Davidic dynasty. The Great Sanhedrin placated Nebuchadnezzar's queen, Semiramis (Vayikra Rabbah 19:6; Esther Rabbah 3:2), who persuaded the emperor to allow Jeconiah's wife into the dungeon. This was the true taking of royalty (natlu malchut) by Semiramis: overriding Nebuchadnezzar to preserve the Davidic seed and destroy his memory! In the dungeon, Jeconiah's wife saw blood and he separated from her, rectifying his past sins of cohabiting during impurity (niddah, which carries the penalty of childlessness, Vayikra 20:21). Through this self-restraint the monarchy of David was rebuilt. The decree was worded "Write you this man childless"—commanded to be written in Jeremiah to record human consequence and the majesty of repentance, paving the way for the destruction of the house of Nebuchadnezzar!

p: וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא ״הַגֶּבֶר הֻקַם עֹל״ (שְׁמוּאֵל ב כ״ג:א׳) שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ה׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
And King David, peace be upon him, is the man who raised the yoke of repentance (II Shmuel 23:1; Avodah Zarah 5a);
שֶׁבָּא לְתַקֵּן כָּל הַפְּגָמִים אַחַר הַחֵטְא
who arose to rectify all blemishes following the Fall;
וְעַל זֶה הוּא כָּל מִזְמוֹרֵי תְּהִלִּים שֶׁחִבֵּר: לְזַמֵּר עָרִיצִים, וּלְהַכְרִית הַחוֹחִים וְקוֹצִים הַסּוֹבְבִים הַשּׁוֹשַׁנָּה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה
toward this point all the psalms he composed: to prune tyrants and sever the thorns and briars encircling the supernal Rose;
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם הוּא ״חַי וְקַיָּם״ כְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּ״לֹא מֵת״ (תַּעֲנִית ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
wherefore he too is "alive and enduring" like our father Jacob who never died (Ta'anit 5b);
כִּי כָּל עִיקַּר הַמִּיתָה הוּא לְתַקֵּן חֵטְא זֶה שֶׁהִתְחִיל בּוֹ אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ בְּאוֹתָן מֵאָה וּשְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין (י״ח עַמּוּד ב׳)
for the essence of death is to repair that blemish begun by Adam through the Serpent during those 130 years of impurity (Eruvin 18b).
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם: דְּחָסִיד גָּדוֹל הָיָה וְהִתְחִיל בִּתְשׁוּבָה, לֹא זָכָה עַדַיִין לִתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵימָה
And although the Talmud states that Adam was a great pious master who initiated repentance, he did not attain consummate repentance;
כִּבְגִלְגּוּלָיו שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ בְּדָוִד, וְאַחֲרָיו בְּמָשִׁיחַ שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ
as achieved in his subsequent reincarnations in David, and after him in Mashiach who will be revealed speedily in our days;
וְיִזְכֶּה לֶאֱכֹל וּלְהַאֲכִיל מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים לְכָל הָרְאוּיִם לְכָךְ, וְ״אָכַל וָחַי לְעֹלָם״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג:כב)
who will merit to eat and feed from the Tree of Life unto all who are worthy, that they "eat, and live forever" (Bereishis 3:22);
וְדָוִד כְּבָר זָכָה לְעַצְמוֹ לִטְעוֹם מֵאִילָנָא דְּחַיֵּי לִהְיוֹת ״חַי וְקַיָּם״
and David already merited personally to taste of the Tree of Life to be alive and enduring;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״חַיִּים שָׁאַל מִמְּךָ — נָתַתָּה לּוֹ, אֹרֶךְ יָמִים עוֹלָם וָעֶד״ (תְּהִלִּים כ״א:ה׳)
as it is said: "He asked life of You, and You gave it him, even length of days forever and ever" (Tehillim 21:5);
וְכֵן כָּל מִי שֶׁתִּיקֵּן הַבְּרִית לְגַמְרֵי
and so too anyone who rectifies the covenant completely:
בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא חָטָא מֵעוֹלָם כְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְאֵלִיָּהוּ מַלְאַךְ הַבְּרִית
whether he who never sinned like our father Jacob and Eliyahu the angel of the covenant;
בֵּין שֶׁחָטָא וְשָׁב בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵימָה כְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
or he who sinned and returned in consummate repentance like King David.
וְעַל כֵּן הוּבְטַח דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם גַּם כֵּן עַל הַשְׁלָמַת זַרְעוֹ וְקִיּוּמָם לָעַד
Wherefore King David was likewise promised the eternal preservation of his seed;
וְנֶאֱמַר: ״אִם יַעַזְבוּ בָנָיו [תּוֹרָתִי]... זַרְעוֹ לְעוֹלָם יִהְיֶה [וְכִסְאוֹ כַשֶּׁמֶשׁ נֶגְדִּי]״ (תְּהִלִּים פ״ט:ל״א, ל״ז)
as stated: "If his children forsake My law... his seed shall endure forever, and his throne as the sun before Me" (Tehillim 89:31, 37);
כִּי כְּבָר הִשְׁלִים נַפְשׁוֹ כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁעַצְמִיּוּתוֹ נַעֲשָׂה כֵּן
for he perfected his soul to the degree that his essence became transformed into this holy endurance;
דְּמִזֶּה בְּהֶכְרֵחַ כָּל זַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו כֵּן שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת
whence perforce all his seed inherit this trait so that they can never be alienated;
וְגַם: ״אִם יַעַזְבוּ וְגוֹמֵר״ — הוּא רַק לְשָׁעָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
and "if his children forsake My law" applies merely temporarily in this world;
אֲבָל ״לֹא יִדַּח מֵהֶם נִדָּח״ מִצַּד כֹּחַ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁבְּקִרְבָּם בְּמִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת
but no outcast shall be severed from them on account of David's royal power within them;
כְּמוֹ בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל מִצַּד כֹּחַ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּמִדַּת ״אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב״ (מִיכָה ז:כ) שֶׁבְּקִרְבָּם
just as across all Israel no soul is severed through the truth of Jacob within them.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, בְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּת כֹּחַ נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּבְּרוּת הַסִּטְרָא דְּרָע הַמַּעֲלִים קְדֻשַּׁת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
Nevertheless, upon the awakening of Nebuchadnezzar's power, which was the strengthening of the husk concealing David's holiness;
וְגָבַר אוֹיֵב לְהַגְלוֹת יְכָנְיָה וְ״הֶחָרָשׁ וְהַמַּסְגֵּר״ (מְלָכִים ב כ״ד:י״ד) שֶׁעִמּוֹ
and the enemy prevailed to exile Jeconiah and the craftsmen and smiths with him (II Melachim 24:14);
נִגְזַר עַל יְכָנְיָה: ״כִּתְבוּ אֶת הָאִישׁ הַזֶּה עֲרִירִי״ (יִרְמְיָה כ״ב:ל׳)
it was decreed upon Jeconiah: "Write you this man childless" (Yirmiyah 22:30);
וְהָיָה עוֹמֵד לִכְלוֹת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כָּל זֶרַע בֵּית דָּוִד מִן הָעוֹלָם
the royal seed of David standing on the verge of extinction, God forbid;
אַחַר שֶׁהָרַג נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר כּוּלָּם וְנִשְׁאַר יְכָנְיָה לְבַדּוֹ
after Nebuchadnezzar slew them all and Jeconiah remained alone;

עַד שֶׁעָמְדָה סַנְהֶדְרֵי גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל דַּעְתָּהּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה י״ט:ו׳): שֶׁפִּיְּיסוּ לַגְּדֻלַּת, וְהִיא לַמַּלְכָּה, וְהִיא לַמֶּלֶךְ
until the Great Sanhedrin took counsel (Vayikra Rabbah 19:6), winning over the warden, who persuaded the queen, who persuaded the king.

[וְנִרְאֶה לִי שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (אֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ג׳:ב׳): ״מִנָּשִׁים שֶׁנָּטְלוּ מַלְכוּת — שְׁמִירָמִית״, וְהִיא זוֹ אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּ״מַתְּנוֹת כְּהֻנָּה״
[And it appears to me that concerning this the Midrash states (Esther Rabbah 3:2): "Among the women who seized royal power was Semiramis"—who was the wife of Nebuchadnezzar, see Matnot Kehunah;
וְלֹא מָצִינוּ בַּכָּתוּב מִמֶּנָּה שֶׁתִּטּוֹל מַלְכוּת כְּלוּם נֶגֶד נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר ״הַמַּרְעִישׁ אֶרֶץ, מַרְגִּיז מַמְלָכוֹת״ (יְשַׁעְיָה י״ד:ט״ז)
for we find no biblical chronicle of her exercising sovereignty against Nebuchadnezzar who shook kingdoms (Yeshayah 14:16);
אֲבָל הַכַּוָּונָה עַל הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל: שֶׁבְּדָבָר זֶה שֶׁפָּעֲלָה הִיא מִנְּבוּכַדְנֶצַּר נֶגֶד רְצוֹנוֹ, וְהוּא לִסְתּוֹר וּלְבַטֵּל כָּל כֹּחוֹ וּלְהַאֲבִיד כָּל זֵכֶר לוֹ
but the reference is to her extracting this decree from Nebuchadnezzar against his will, which undermined his power and destroyed his memory;
כִּי ״זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:יד), וְהָא בְּהָא תַּלְיָא, וְאֵין נְטִילַת מַלְכוּת גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה
for God made one opposite the other, and there is no greater seizure of sovereignty than this;
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה שָׁם: ״מַה שְּׁמָהּ?״ כִּי לֹא דָּבָר קַל נַעֲשָׂה עַל יָדָהּ, וְצָרִיךְ לֵידַע שְׁמָהּ, כִּי הַשֵּׁם הוּא הוֹרָאַת עִיקַּר כֹּחַ הָאָדָם הַהוּא בַּעַל הַשֵּׁם
wherefore the Midrash asks: "What was her name?" for her name embodies the spiritual essence of her power;
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן פְּלוּגְתַּת שְׁלֹשָׁה מַאן דְּאָמְרֵי שָׁם בִּשְׁמָהּ, וְלֹא יַחְלְקוּ אָמוֹרָאִים בְּעִנְיְנֵי מִילֵּי דְּעָלְמָא וְדָבָר שֶׁל מַה בְּכָךְ
the debate of the Amoraim regarding her name expressing profound mysteries, not casual worldly trivialities;
וְלֹא יִכְתְּבוּ זֶה בַּמִּדְרָשׁ דֶּרֶךְ פְּלוּגְתָּא דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ נַפְקָא מִינַּהּ כְּלָל וְשִׁינּוּיִים קַלִּים שֶׁבִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמָהּ
for the Midrash records no dispute devoid of practical spiritual consequence;
אֲבָל וַדַּאי יֵשׁ בָּזֶה עִנְיָנִים עֲמוּקִים בִּידִיעַת שְׁמָהּ הָעַצְמִי הָרָאוּי לָהּ כְּפִי עִנְיָנָהּ וְכֹחַ פְּעֻלָּתָהּ, וְאֵין כָּאן מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ יוֹתֵר בָּזֶה]
but expressing deep truths regarding her essential name and power, and this is not the place to elaborate further].
וְשִׁלְשְׁלוּ לוֹ אִשְׁתּוֹ, וְרָאֲתָה דָם וּפֵירַשׁ
And they lowered his wife down into the dungeon, and she saw blood and Jeconiah separated from her;
וּבָזֶה הָיָה תִּיקּוּנוֹ בִּתְשׁוּבָה עַל מַה שֶּׁחָטָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם: ״בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם לֹא קִיַּימְתֶּם מִצְוַת זִיבָה״ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה י״ט:ו׳)
and herein lay his rectification in repentance for past sin, as the Sages stated: "In Jerusalem you did not observe the commandment of flux" (Vayikra Rabbah 19:6);
נִרְאֶה דְּזֶה הָיָה חֶטְאוֹ: בִּבְעִילַת נִדָּה, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן פְּגַם הַבְּרִית בַּאֲכִילַת פַּגָּה, שֶׁהֲרֵי רְאוּיָה לוֹ אַחַר כָּךְ
this having been his fault: cohabitation during niddah, which is a blemish of the covenant in consuming unripe fruit (paga), seeing that she is permitted unto him afterward;
וְעָנְשׁוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה: ״עֲרִירִי״ (וַיִּקְרָא כ:כא), דִּגְבֵי עֲרִירִי דְּאֵשֶׁת אָחִיו כְּתִיב ״נִדָּה הִוא״
and its biblical punishment is childlessness (ariri), as written regarding a brother's wife: "it is an impurity (niddah)" (Vayikra 20:21);
וְעַיֵּין בְּתוֹסָפוֹת רֵישׁ יְבָמוֹת (ב׳ עַמּוּד א׳ דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל: ״אֵשֶׁת״)
and see Tosafos at the beginning of Yevamos (2a, s.v. Eshet);
וְתִיקֵּן עַתָּה: שֶׁבָּא דְּבַר עֲבֵירָה לְיָדוֹ וּפֵירַשׁ, וְאַחַר הַפְּרִישׁוּת זְמַן רַב
and Jeconiah rectified it now: an opportunity for sin coming to his hand and he separated, remaining in separation for a long time;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה חָזַר וְנִבְנָה מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד
and through this the kingdom of the House of David was rebuilt.
וּתְחִלַּת הַגְּזֵירָה הָיָה גַּם כֵּן בִּלְשׁוֹן ״כִּתְבוּ״, לֹא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֵן, רַק שֶׁיִּכְתְּבוּ כֵן
And the decree was formulated with the word "Write" (Yirmiyah 22:30), not that it become immutable fact, but that it be inscribed;
וְנִתְקַיֵּים שֶׁנִּכְתַּב כָּךְ בְּסֵפֶר יִרְמְיָה
being fulfilled by being recorded in the Book of Jeremiah;
וּכְתִיבָה זוֹ גַּם כֵּן לֹא דָּבָר רֵיק הוּא, שֶׁנִּשְׁאַר כָּתוּב כֵּן לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד: כְּדֵי לֵידַע כַּמָּה הַחֵטְא גּוֹרֵם, וְכַמָּה כֹּחַ הַתְּשׁוּבָה גָּדוֹל
and this writing is not in vain, remaining inscribed forever to make known how severe is sin and how immense is repentance;
וּלְהָקִים עַל יְדֵי זֶה עוֹלָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה, שֶׁזֶּה כָּל עִנְיַן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְכָל זַרְעוֹ מִבֵּית דָּוִד
raising the yoke of repentance, which is the mission of King David and his royal seed;
וּבָזֶה זָכוּ אַחַר כָּךְ אָבְדַן בֵּית נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר מִן הָעוֹלָם, שֶׁבָּזֶה כָּל כֹּחַ סִטְרָא דְּרָע הַמִּתְקוֹמֵם נֶגֶד דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם:
and through this they merited the destruction of the house of Nebuchadnezzar, shattering the unholy power that opposed David!

20.h: The theme: Esther rectifying Solomon's foreign wives, the Oral Torah expanding from the Great Assembly, and conquering Amalek before rest (be-hani'ach). There remained the unholy side opposing King Solomon, which Esther arose to rectify through a transgression for the sake of Heaven (aveirah lishmah), entering the mixture of human seed and bestial seed from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. Da'as denotes union ("and Adam knew Eve", Bereishis 4:1); Solomon sought to transform the Tree of Knowledge into the Tree of Life, and the Sages in Shushan and Esther succeeded in this. Through the miracle of Esther, Israel re-accepted the Torah out of love—the Tree of Life (Eitz HaChayim, Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah ch. 1). Then began the revelation of the Oral Torah through the Men of the Great Assembly, who taught: "raise up many disciples" (transmitting the Oral Law from master to student) and "make a fence around the Torah" (enacting rabbinic hedges). During the prophetic era, Israel sought prophecy (bnei ha-nevi'im); from the Great Assembly onward, all Israel sought wisdom in the Oral Torah (talmidei chachamim), completing Kingship. This began after the eradication of Amalek in the days of Haman, for Amalek causes the slackening of hands from Torah (attacking at Rephidim, Bechorot 5b). When the voice is not the voice of Jacob in synagogues and study halls, the hands are the hands of Esav (Bereishis Rabbah 65:20); the Oral Torah requires exhausting labor (Tanchuma, Noach §3), over which the mountain had been coerced as a cask. In Ahasuerus's days they re-accepted the Oral Torah out of love, toiling without fatigue having blotted out Amalek's coldness. The command to blot out Amalek applies after appointing a king and when Hashem grants rest (be-hani'ach, Devarim 25:19). Establishing a king is establishing the Oral Torah; yet during rest (hani'ach), when a person seeks ease, the Torah warns not to cast off the yoke of divine service to pursue personal desires, for that is true servitude to the yetzer. One who accepts the yoke of Torah is freed from the yoke of government and worldly toil (Avos 3:5; Sanhedrin 99b); man is born to toil in Torah, placing upon himself the yoke like an ox to the plow (Avodah Zarah 5b). King Saul, whose monarchy was borrowed, failed to destroy Agag; his descendants Mordechai and Esther finished the task, establishing the eternal monarchy of the House of David!

p: וְנִשְׁאַר רַק הַסִּטְרָא דְּנֶגֶד שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And there remained only the unholy side opposing King Solomon, peace be upon him;
שֶׁעַל זֶה בָּאתָה אֶסְתֵּר לְתַקֵּן גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי ״עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ״ (נָזִיר כ״ג עַמּוּד ב׳)
which Esther arose to rectify likewise through a "transgression for the sake of Heaven";
וְעֵירוּב זֶרַע אָדָם וְזֶרַע בְּהֵמָה מִסִּטְרָא דְּעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע
entering the mixture of human seed and bestial seed from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil;
דְּ״דַּעַת״ לְשׁוֹן הִתְחַבְּרוּת, כְּמוֹ: ״וְהָאָדָם יָדַע [אֶת חַוָּה אִשְׁתּוֹ]״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ד:א)
Da'as being an expression of union: "And the man knew Eve his wife" (Bereishis 4:1);
וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּקֵּשׁ לַעֲשׂוֹת מֵעֵץ הַדַּעַת — עֵץ הַחַיִּים
and King Solomon had sought to transform the Tree of Knowledge into the Tree of Life;
וְכֵן חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּשׁוּשָׁן וְאֶסְתֵּר שֶׁבָּאוּ לְתַקֵּן זֶה, וְעָלְתָה בְּיָדָם
and so the Sages of Israel in Shushan and Esther came to rectify this, and succeeded in their hand.
דְּעַל יְדֵי נֵס זֶה שֶׁבָּא עַל יְדֵי אֶסְתֵּר, חָזְרוּ לְקַבֵּל הַתּוֹרָה מֵאַהֲבָה
For through this miracle wrought through Esther, Israel returned to receive the Torah out of love;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עֵץ הַחַיִּים, דְּ״אֵין עֵץ חַיִּים אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה״, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ [רַבָּה פֶּרֶק א׳]
which is the Tree of Life, for "there is no Tree of Life save Torah" (Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah, ch. 1);
וְאָז הָיָה מִתְּחִלַּת הִתְגַּלּוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהִתְחִיל מֵאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה
and then marked the beginning of the revelation of the Oral Torah inaugurated by the Men of the Great Assembly;
וְהֵם שֶׁאָמְרוּ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק א׳ מִשְׁנָה א׳): ״הַעֲמִידוּ תַלְמִידִים הַרְבֵּה״ — לְהַרְבִּיץ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁצָּרִיךְ קַבָּלָה תַּלְמִיד מֵרַב דַּוְוקָא
who commanded (Avos 1:1): "raise up many disciples"—to disseminate the Oral Law, requiring direct reception from master to student;
״וַעֲשׂוּ סְיָג לַתּוֹרָה״ (שָׁם) — הֵם הוֹסָפוֹת כָּל הַתַּקָּנוֹת וְהַסְּיָגִים שֶׁכּוּלָּם מֵאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה
"and make a fence around the Torah" (ibid.)—being all the rabbinic enactments instituted by the Great Assembly.
וְזֶהוּ יְסוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהוּתְחַל כְּבָר עַל יְדֵי דָּוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה, דְּ״מַלְכוּת — פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינָן לָהּ״ (פָּתַח אֵלִיָּהוּ)
And this is the foundation of the Oral Torah begun by David and Solomon: "Malkhut is the Mouth, which we designate the Oral Law";
אֲבָל כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהָיְתָה הַנְּבוּאָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, הָיָה עִיקַּר הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לָבוֹא לְמַדְרֵיגַת נְבוּאָה, וְנִקְרְאוּ ״בְּנֵי הַנְּבִיאִים״ (מְלָכִים ב ב:ג)
but so long as prophecy existed in Israel, their striving focused upon attaining prophecy, being called "the sons of the prophets" (II Melachim 2:3);
וּמֵאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה וְאֵילָךְ הִתְחִילוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל לְהַשִּׂיג מַדְרֵיגַת הַחָכְמָה בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, וְנִקְרְאוּ ״תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים״
and from the Great Assembly onward, all Israel began to strive for wisdom in the Oral Torah, designated "Torah scholars";
וְזֶהוּ הַשְׁלָמַת כֹּחַ הַמַּלְכוּת
this being the consummate completion of Kingship.
וְהִתְחִיל אַחַר מְחִיַּיִת עֲמָלֵק דִּימֵי הָמָן, שֶׁהוּא הַגּוֹרֵם רִפּוּי יָדַיִם מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
And this began following the blotting out of Amalek in the days of Haman, who causes the slackening of hands from Torah;
דְּעַל כֵּן בָּא לִלְחוֹם בִּרְפִידִים (שְׁמוֹת י״ז:ח׳; בְּכוֹרוֹת ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
wherefore Amalek attacked at Rephidim (rifeyon yadayim, Bechorot 5b);
וּמִמֶּנּוּ נִמְשָׁךְ הַקְּרִירוּת וְהָעַצְלוּת בְּלִבְּבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
whence issued the chilling coldness and lethargy within Jewish hearts toward Torah;
דִּכְשֶׁאֵין ״הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב״ בְּבָתֵּי כְּנֵסִיּוֹת וּבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת, אָז ״הַיָּדַיִם יְדֵי עֵשָׂו״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:כ״ב; בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ס״ה:כ׳)
for when the voice is not the voice of Jacob in synagogues and study halls, the hands are the hands of Esav (Bereishis Rabbah 65:20);
וּלְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה צָרִיךְ יְגִיעָה גְּדוֹלָה
and the Oral Torah requires exhausting labor;
וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנְחוּמָא פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ (סִימָן ג׳): דְּעַל כֵּן עִיקַּר כְּפִיַּית ״הַר כְּגִיגִית״ הָיָה עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, עַיֵּין שָׁם
as written in Tanchuma (Noach §3): the coercion of holding the mountain like a cask applied specifically to the Oral Torah, see there;
וְאִם כֵּן מַה דְּ״הָדַר קִבְּלוּהָ בִּימֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ מֵאַהֲבָה״ (שַׁבָּת פ״ח עַמּוּד א׳), הַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן הָעִיקָּר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב
and if so, their re-acceptance out of love in the days of Ahasuerus applied primarily to the Oral Torah;
וְקִבְּלוּ לְהִתְיַיגֵּעַ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּלֹא רִפּוּי יָדַיִם, כִּי מָחוּ מִלִּבָּם זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק הַמַּרְפֶּה
resolving to toil in Torah without slackening, having blotted out the chilling memory of Amalek from their hearts.
וְעַל כֵּן צִיוּוּי דִּמְחִיַּיִת עֲמָלֵק הוּא אַחַר הֲקָמַת מֶלֶךְ: ״וְהָיָה בְּהָנִיחַ [ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְךָ מִכָּל אֹיְבֶיךָ] וְגוֹמֵר״ (דְּבָרִים כ״ה:י״ט)
Wherefore the commandment to blot out Amalek applies after appointing a king: "when Hashem your God has given you rest from all your enemies, etc." (Devarim 25:19);
שֶׁהֲקָמַת מַלְכוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא הַעֲמָדַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
for establishing the monarchy of Israel is the establishment of the Oral Torah;
וּ״בְהָנִיחַ״ — בִּשְׁעַת נַיְיחָא שֶׁאָדָם מְבַקֵּשׁ מְנוּחָה אֵין חָפֵץ בִּיגִיעָה
and "in giving you rest"—in an hour of ease when man desires rest, he shuns exhausting toil;
וְהִזְהִירָה תּוֹרָה עַל זֶה: שֶׁהַנַּיְיחָא דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא ״מִכָּל הָאוֹיְבִים מִסָּבִיב״
and the Torah warned: that Hashem's rest is "from all enemies round about";
הֵם הַדְּאָגוֹת הָעוֹלָמוֹת וְתַאֲוַת הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה הַמַּטְרִיד
these being worldly anxieties and the troubling lusts of the yetzer hara;
וְלֹא לִפְרוֹק כָּל עוֹל מֵעָלָיו וְלִהְיוֹת הַנַּיְיחָא לֵילֵךְ בִּשְׁרִירוּת לִבּוֹ
not casting off all yoke to walk in the stubbornness of one's heart;
דְּזֶהוּ תַּכְלִית הָעוֹל וְהַטִּירוּד שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם נַיְיחָא כְּלָל, כִּי טָרוּד בְּיִצְרוֹ הַמַּטְרִידוֹ בְּכָל מִינֵי תַּאֲווֹת וְכַדּוֹמֶה
for indulgence is the ultimate bondage lacking peace, troubled by the yetzer in endless lusts.
אֲבָל: ״הַמְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל תּוֹרָה — מַעֲבִירִין מִמֶּנּוּ עוֹל מַלְכוּת וְעוֹל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ״ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ג׳ מִשְׁנָה ה׳)
But: "Whoever accepts upon himself the yoke of Torah, Heaven removes from him the yoke of government and the yoke of worldly toil" (Avos 3:5);
שֶׁהֵם ב׳ מִינֵי שִׁעְבּוּד וּטְרָדוֹת כְּלָלִיּוֹת
these being the two universal bondages;
וְעַל כָּל אֶחָד: ״אָדָם לְעָמָל יוּלָּד״ (אִיּוֹב ה:ז) — רַק לַעֲמַל תּוֹרָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ״ט סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳)
and concerning every soul: "man is born unto toil" (Iyov 5:7)—solely for the toil of Torah (Sanhedrin 99b);
וְעַל כָּל אֶחָד: ״בְּהָנִיחַ... תִּמְחֶה״, וְלֹא יֵשֵׁב בְּנַיְיחָא וְשַׁלְוָה וְהַשְׁקֵט
and regarding all: "when He gives you rest... you shall blot out," not sitting in idle ease;
רַק יָשִׂים עַל לִבּוֹ לִמְחוֹת זִכְרוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק
but setting his heart to blot out the remembrance of Amalek;
הַיְינוּ דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁל עַצְלוּת וְרִפּוּי מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִלִּבּוֹ עַל יְדֵי בַּקָּשַׁת נַיְיחָא
that is, banishing the lethargy and slackening from Torah born of seeking worldly ease;
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיְּקַבֵּל עָלָיו עֻלָּהּ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״וְיָשִׂים עַצְמוֹ כְּשׁוֹר לָעוֹל [וְכַחֲמוֹר לַמַּשָּׂא]״ (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) בְּעֵסֶק הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
placing himself like an ox to the yoke and a donkey to the burden in toiling in the Oral Torah (Avodah Zarah 5b).
וְזֶה אַחַר שֶׁהֵקִימוּ מֶלֶךְ, שֶׁהוּא בִּנְיַן קוֹמַת הַמַּלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם
And this applies after appointing a king, which is the construction of the Kingdom of Heaven;
שֶׁהוּא רָזָא דְּ״אֵשֶׁת חַיִל״ (מִשְׁלֵי ל״א:י׳) הָעוֹסֶקֶת תָּמִיד בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת ״מַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיהָ״ (שָׁם:ל״א) וּ״פְרִי כַפֶּיהָ״
this being the esoteric mystery of the "Woman of Valor" toiling unceasingly in the work of her hands and fruit of her palms;
וּלְפִי שֶׁשָּׁאוּל שֶׁהָיְתָה הַמַּלְכוּת שְׁאוּלָה בְּיָדוֹ לֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדוֹ לְקַיְּימָהּ בִּשְׁלֵימוּת
and because King Saul, whose kingdom was borrowed in his hand, did not succeed in sustaining it in perfection;
בָּאוּ זַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו מָרְדֳּכַי וְאֶסְתֵּר לִגְמוֹר מְחִיָּיתָם מַה שֶּׁהִשְׁאִיר הוּא מֵאֲגָג
his descendants Mordechai and Esther arose to finish the eradication of what Saul had spared of Agag;
וּלְקוֹמֵם עַל יְדֵי זֶה מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד הַקַּיָּים לָעַד:
restoring through this the eternal monarchy of the House of David!

20.h: The theme: Why Purim was not established as a full Yom Tov, Darius building the Second Temple, and the failure of the Second Return through foreign marriages. The Sages initially thought to establish Purim as a work-prohibited festival (Yom Tov), believing they had completely blotted out the seed of Amalek from the world. Had this occurred, the final redemption would have arrived; but Israel remained "the servants of Ahasuerus" (Megillah 14b), the Divine Name and Throne remaining incomplete. Witnessing the government entrusted unto Esther and Mordechai, they assumed they were subjects of Esther who clothed herself in the Kingdom of Heaven. Yet the generation of Israel—the "children of prophets"—refused to accept Purim as a Yom Tov, for despite the great salvation, building the Second Temple was denied unto Esther (Ahasuerus granting her "unto half the kingdom"—excluding the Temple that stood in the middle, Megillah 15b). The Temple was rebuilt decades later by her son Darius. Although Darius was halachically pure from his mother (a child of a Jewish mother and gentile father being kosher, Kiddushin 68b), he was born of the demon-counterpart (sheidah, Etz Chayim, Sha'ar Kelipat Nogah ch. 6; Arba Me'ot Shekel Kesef 82a) which Esther separated from her holy essence. Had the mixture of the Tree of Knowledge been completely rectified, all evil would have vanished, Ahasuerus's memory would have perished like Nebuchadnezzar's, and Esther would have married Zerubbabel the governor of Judah to reign over the entire earth! Israel was worthy of miracles in the days of Ezra like the days of Joshua (Berachos 4a); had they ascended en masse as in the First Commonwealth, the redemption would have been eternal like silver that never rots (Yoma 9b; Yerushalmi). But sin prevented this: the men of the Second Temple intermarried with foreign women (Zohar II, 7a), causing the blemish to return. Esther's union was under duress as an aveirah lishmah rectifying Solomon; their marriages were willful transgressions. Because the final rectification was not achieved, Purim was not accepted as a full Yom Tov!

p: וְעַל כֵּן חָשְׁבוּ לִקְבּוֹעַ יוֹם טוֹב גַּם כֵּן
And therefore the leaders initially thought to establish Purim as a full Yom Tov as well;
כִּי חָשְׁבוּ שֶׁכְּבָר עָלְתָה בְּיָדָם לִמְחוֹת זִכְרוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק מִן הָעוֹלָם לְגַמְרֵי
assuming they had already succeeded in blotting out the remembrance of Amalek from the world completely;
וְאֵין יוֹם טוֹב גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה
and there is no greater festival than this.
וְאִם הָיָה כֵן, הָיָה רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת הַגְּאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה
And had it been so, the redemption would have been consummate;
וַהֲרֵי ״אַכַּתֵּי עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן״ (מְגִלָּה י״ד עַמּוּד ב׳)
yet "we are still the servants of Ahasuerus" (Megillah 14b);
וְעַדַיִין אֵין הַשֵּׁם שָׁלֵם וְהַכִּסֵּא שָׁלֵם (תַּנְחוּמָא תֵּצֵא י״א)
and the Divine Name and Throne are not yet whole;
רַק שֶׁבְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה שֶׁרָאוּ עִיקַּר הַנְהָגַת הַמַּלְכוּת בְּיַד אֶסְתֵּר וּמָרְדֳּכַי
except that at that hour when they beheld the imperial administration entrusted unto Esther and Mordechai;
חָשְׁבוּ דְּבֶאֱמֶת לָאו עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ הֵם, רַק תַּחַת מֶמְשֶׁלֶת אֶסְתֵּר הַיְּהוּדִית שֶׁלָּבְשָׁה מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם
they assumed they were not subjects of Ahasuerus, but lived under the governance of Esther the Jewess who clothed herself in the Kingdom of Heaven;
וְיָשְׁבָה עַל כִּסֵּא ה׳ כְּעֵין שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, וּלְתַקֵּן לִהְיוֹת הַכִּסֵּא שָׁלֵם
sitting upon the throne of Hashem like King Solomon, rectifying the Throne to make it whole.
אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר ״בְּנֵי נְבִיאִים״ (פְּסָחִים ס״ו עַמּוּד א׳) לֹא קַבִּילוּ עֲלַיְיהוּ
But the common people of Israel in that generation, the "children of prophets," refused to accept Purim as a full Yom Tov;
דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיָה יְשׁוּעָה גְּדוֹלָה עַל יָדָהּ
for although a monumental salvation was wrought through her;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדָהּ בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
nevertheless the rebuilding of the Holy Temple was not achieved through her hand;
שֶׁאָמַר אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ: ״עַד חֲצִי הַמַּלְכוּת״ (אֶסְתֵּר ה:ג) — ״וְלֹא דָּבָר הַחוֹצֵץ״ (מְגִלָּה ט״ו עַמּוּד ב׳)
Ahasuerus having declared: "unto half the kingdom"—excluding the Temple which divides the kingdom (Megillah 15b);
וְרַק עַל יְדֵי דָּרְיָוֶשׁ בְּנָהּ נִבְנָה
being rebuilt decades later by her son Darius.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיָה טָהוֹר מֵאִמּוֹ, וְ״גּוֹי הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל — הַוָּלָד כָּשֵׁר״ (קִדּוּשִׁין ס״ח עַמּוּד ב׳)
And although Darius was halachically kosher from his mother, for "a gentile who cohabits with a Jewish woman—the child is kosher" (Kiddushin 68b);
וּלְדַעַת כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים [פּוֹסְקִים] אֵין צָרִיךְ גֵּירוּת
and according to numerous halachic authorities he requires no conversion;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא לֹא נוֹלַד מִצַּד הַטּוֹב וְהַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁבְּאֶסְתֵּר
nevertheless he was not born from the side of good and holiness within Esther;
וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּ״עֵץ חַיִּים״ שַׁעַר קְלִיפַּת נֹגַהּ פֶּרֶק ו׳, וּבְסוֹף סֵפֶר ״אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף״ (דַּף פ״ב רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳)
as written in Etz Chayim (Sha'ar Kelipat Nogah ch. 6) and in Arba Me'ot Shekel Kesef (82a);
דְּהוּא נוֹלַד מֵהַשֵּׁידָה שֶׁהוּא צַד הָרָע שֶׁבָּהּ שֶׁיָּדְעָה לְהַפְרִישׁוֹ מִמֶּנָּה, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם
that he was conceived from the demon-counterpart (sheidah), the evil element which she separated from herself, see there;
וְהוּא הָרָע הַמְעוֹרָב בְּכָל אֶחָד מִצַּד אֲכִילַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע שֶׁחָשְׁבָה לְתַקֵּן
this being the residual evil mixed within humanity from the Tree of Knowledge which she sought to rectify.
וְאִילּוּ נִתְקַן, הָיָה הַכֹּל טוֹב, וְהָרָע שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְהַפֵּךְ לְטוֹב הָיָה מִתְבַּעֵר מִן הָעוֹלָם לְגַמְרֵי
And had it been fully rectified, all would have become good, and that evil which cannot be transformed would have vanished entirely;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱבַד כָּל זֵכֶר דִּנְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר, כָּךְ הָיָה נֶאֱבַד כָּל זֵכֶר דַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ
and just as every remembrance of Nebuchadnezzar perished, so would have perished every remembrance of Ahasuerus;
וְאֶסְתֵּר הָיְתָה נִשֵּׂאת לִזְרֻבָּבֶל פַּחַת יְהוּדָה (חַגַּי א:א), וְהָיוּ מוֹלְכִים עַל כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
and Esther would have been married unto Zerubbabel the governor of Judah (Chaggai 1:1), reigning over the entire earth!

וּכְבָר הָיוּ רְאוּיִם לְכָךְ בְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרָכוֹת (ד׳ עַמּוּד א׳): ״רְאוּיִם הָיוּ לְנֵס בִּימֵי עֶזְרָא בְּבִיאָה שְׁנִיָּה כְּבִימֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וּבִיאָה רִאשׁוֹנָה, אֶלָּא שֶׁגָּרַם הַחֵטְא״

And they were worthy of this in that generation: "Israel was worthy of an overt miracle in the days of Ezra at the second entry into the Land as in the days of Joshua at the first entry, but sin prevented it" (Berachos 4a);
וְאִילּוּ בָּאוּ אָז כִּבִיאָה רִאשׁוֹנָה, הָיוּ בָּאִים כּוּלָּם
and had they ascended then like the first entry, all of Israel would have returned;
וְהָיָה גְּאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה דְּלֹא נֶחְרַב עוֹד
and the redemption would have been complete, the Second Temple never being destroyed;
וְכִדְאִיתָא בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי (שְׁבִיעִית פֶּרֶק ו׳ הֲלָכָה א׳): דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ בַּבְלָאֵי דַּאֲבָהָתוֹי חָרְבִין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
as the Jerusalem Talmud relates (Shevi'it 6:1): the Babylonians who refused to ascend caused the Temple to be destroyed;
וְרָמְזוּ זֶה גַּם כֵּן בְּיוֹמָא (ט׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב ״כְּכֶסֶף״ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ח:ט) דְּאֵין הָרָקָב שׁוֹלֵט בּוֹ, רָצָה לוֹמַר דְּתִהְיֶה גְּאוּלָּה קַיֶּימֶת לָעַד
hinted in Yoma (9b) on "as silver" (Shir HaShirim 8:9) which rot cannot dominate, signifying an eternal redemption.
וְגָרַם הַחֵטְא — הוּא נְשִׂיאַת הַנָּשִׁים נָכְרִיּוֹת (עַיֵּין עֶזְרָא ט; זֹוהַר חֵלֶק ב׳ ז׳ עַמּוּד א׳), שֶׁחָזַר הַקִּלְקוּל לִמְקוֹמוֹ
And the sin that prevented it was marrying foreign women (Ezra 9; Zohar II, 7a), whereby the blemish returned to its place;
כִּי אֶסְתֵּר הָיְתָה בְּאוֹנֶס וַ״עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ״, וְתִיקְּנָה דִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן עַל דֶּרֶךְ עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ
for Esther was taken under duress in an aveirah lishmah, rectifying King Solomon who likewise acted for the sake of Heaven;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הֵם
whereas the people of the Second Temple married foreign women out of carnal desire;
וְסוֹף סוֹף לֹא נִגְמַר עַדַיִין הַתִּיקּוּן הַגָּמוּר אָז, וְעַל כֵּן לֹא קַבִּילוּ יוֹם טוֹב:
and ultimately the consummate rectification was not completed then, wherefore Israel did not accept Purim as a work-prohibited Yom Tov!

20.h: The theme: The custom of refraining from work on Purim, the expansion of the Oral Law after the Destruction, and Rabbi Akiva's comprehensive vision. Although strictly speaking Purim was not established as a full festival prohibiting labor, the Jewish people adopted a widespread customary restriction against work (Megillah 5b) in order not to be distracted from the joyful obligations of feasting and merrymaking. This custom likely originated following the destruction of the Temple, when the Sages intensified their spiritual efforts in establishing the Oral Torah (Torah she-b'al Peh). This effort culminated with Rabbi Akiva, who structured general principles and specific details (Yerushalmi Shekalim 5:1), perceiving profound secrets that even Moshe Rabbeinu was not explicitly shown in his generation (Bamidbar Rabbah 19:6). As Koheles Rabbah expounds on "the words of the wise are as goads" (Koheles 12:11): when are their teachings most firmly planted? When their masters are gathered from the world. With the destruction of the Temple—the very wellspring of wisdom drawn through the Holy Spirit—the remaining few scholars exerted extraordinary labor in Torah study, meriting unprecedented revelations and reinforcing the celebration of Purim, whose core joy commemorates the voluntary re-acceptance of the Oral Torah out of love.

p: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מִמִּנְהָגָא בְּעָלְמָא נָהוּג אִיסּוּר מְלָאכָה, כִּדְאִיתָא שָׁם (מְגִלָּה ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
And nevertheless, by widespread custom there is an observed prohibition of work on Purim, as taught in Megillah (5b);
וְהוּא כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא לְהִתְבַּטֵּל מֵחוֹבַת מִשְׁתֶּה וְשִׂמְחָה
and this is in order that a person not be distracted from the obligatory feast and rejoicing.
וְנִרְאֶה לִי דְּהִתְחִילוּ בְּמִנְהָג זֶה אַחַר הַחֻרְבָּן
And it appears to me that they initiated this custom following the destruction of the Temple;
שֶׁאָז הִתְאַמְּצוּ עוֹד יוֹתֵר בִּיסוֹד הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
for then they exerted themselves even more intensely in laying the foundations of the Oral Torah;
עַד שֶׁקָּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שֶׁיִּסַּד כְּלָלוֹת וּפְרָטוֹת, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דִּשְׁקָלִים (פֶּרֶק ה׳ הֲלָכָה א׳)
until Rabbi Akiva arose and established general rules and specific details, as written in the Jerusalem Talmud (Shekalim 5:1);
וְ״כָל יְקָר — רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ״ (אִיּוֹב כ״ח:י׳), מַה שֶּׁלֹּא נִגְלָה לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, כִּדְאִיתָא בְּבַמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה פָּרָשַׁת חֻקַּת (פָּרָשָׁה י״ט:ו׳)
and "his eye saw every precious thing" (Iyov 28:10), perceiving what was not openly revealed even unto Moshe Rabbeinu, as taught in Bamidbar Rabbah (19:6).
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּקֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה י״ב:י״א) עַל פָּסוּק ״דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים כַּדָּרְבֹנוֹת״ (קֹהֶלֶת י״ב:י״א): אֵימָתַי? בִּזְמַן שֶׁבַּעֲלֵיהֶן נֶאֱסָפִים מֵהֶם
And this is after the manner stated in Koheles Rabbah (12:11) on the verse "The words of the wise are as goads": when are they as goads? In the hour when their masters are gathered from the world;
וְכָךְ בַּחֻרְבָּן שֶׁנֶּאֶסְפוּ כָּל חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמְקוֹם הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁמִּשָּׁם הָיוּ שׁוֹאֲבִין הַחָכְמָה בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
and so at the Destruction, when all the sages of Israel and the Holy Temple (whence they drew wisdom through the Holy Spirit) were taken;
וְנִשְׁאֲרוּ מְעַט מֵהַרְבֵּה, נִתְאַמְּצוּ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וִיגִיעָה יְתֵירָה
and only a few survivors remained of the many, they exerted themselves with extraordinary effort and toil;
וְעַל כֵּן זָכוּ לְמַה שֶּׁזָּכוּ בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת
wherefore they merited what they merited with supreme elevation;
וְעַל כֵּן קִיְּימוּ וְקִבְּלוּ גַּם כֵּן שִׂמְחַת פּוּרִים בְּיוֹתֵר
and therefore they confirmed and embraced the joy of Purim with greater intensity;
מִדְּעִיקַּר הַשִּׂמְחָה בּוֹ רַק עַל מַה דִּ״לַיְּהוּדִים הָיְתָה אוֹרָה״ (אֶסְתֵּר ח:טז) — ״זוֹ תּוֹרָה״ (מְגִלָּה ט״ז עַמּוּד ב׳)
seeing that the essential joy of Purim is that "the Jews had light"—"this is Torah" (Megillah 16b);
בְּקַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה מֵאַהֲבָה, שֶׁזָּכוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר:
through re-accepting the Torah out of love, meriting thereby the universal expansion of the Oral Law as explained!

20.h: The theme: Rebbe compiling the Mishnah, his planting on Purim, and the distinction between the servitude of Pharaoh and the ongoing servitude of Ahasuerus. Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi (Rebbe) concluded the era of the Tannaim, compiling the Mishnah which serves as the foundational text of the entire Oral Law, hinting at every future insight. Rebbe descended from King David; his compilation aimed to establish the spiritual stature of Kingship (Malkhut), bringing about the ingathering of the exiles through the study of the Mishnayot (Vayikra Rabbah 7:2 on Hoshea 8:10). Rebbe was worthy of being Mashiach had his generation merited (Sanhedrin 98b), remaining "alive and enduring" even after his physical death (Kesubos 103a). Rebbe planted joyous saplings on Purim (Megillah 5b) to teach that despite the great joy of the Torah, our gladness remains incomplete without the ultimate rest of a Yom Tov, because "we are still the servants of Ahasuerus" (Megillah 14b) and the fasts of Tisha B'Av and the Seventeenth of Tammuz have not yet been uprooted. From Pharaoh's bondage Israel was completely redeemed, for their souls became free through the Torah; but the subjugation to the unholy empire of Ahasuerus persists as long as we dwell in exile under secular monarchs. During the Second Temple, most of Israel remained in the diaspora; had all ascended en masse, the redemption would have been permanent like silver that never rots. Rebbe bathed on the Seventeenth of Tammuz to lighten the burden of exile, and sought to uproot Tisha B'Av when it coincided with Shabbat by drawing upon the Sabbath's holiness to turn it into gladness, though the Sages did not concede because the appointed End had not yet arrived. Rebbe's joyful planting on Purim symbolized the gathering of disciples around Torah (Ta'anit 7a), demonstrating that the greatness of Torah study is revealed specifically when performed from within the darkness of exile and worldly labor!

p: וְרַבִּי [יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא] הוּא סוֹף הַתַּנָּאִים מְיַסְּדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, וְכוֹלְלָם יַחַד בְּחִבּוּר הַמִּשְׁנָה שֶׁעָשָׂה
And Rebbe [Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi] was the seal of the Tannaim who founded the Oral Torah, gathering their teachings into the compilation of the Mishnah;
שֶׁהוּא יְסוֹד כָּל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וְכוֹלֵל הַכֹּל
which is the foundation of the entire Oral Law, encompassing all things;
וְכִידוּעַ דִּכְמוֹ שֶׁלֵּיכָּא מִידֵי דְּלָא רְמִיזָא מֵאוֹרַיְיתָא, הָכִי נַמֵּי לֵיכָּא מִידֵי מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה דְּלָא רְמִיזָא בְּחִבּוּר הַמִּשְׁנָה
and as is known: just as there is nothing that is not hinted in the Written Torah, so there is nothing in the Oral Torah that is not hinted in the Mishnah;
וְכִוֵּון בָּזֶה לְכוֹנֵן קוֹמַת הַמַּלְכוּת כַּנּוֹדָע, וְרָמוּז בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ז׳:ב׳) עַל פָּסוּק: ״גַּם כִּי יִתְנוּ בַגּוֹיִם עַתָּה אֲקַבְּצֵם״ (הוֹשֵׁעַ ח:י)

aiming through this to establish the stature of Kingship, as hinted in Vayikra Rabbah (7:2) on: "Yea, though they study (yitnu, read as yishnu / Mishnah) among the nations, now will I gather them" (Hoshea 8:10);
דְּעַל יְדֵי לִימּוּד הַמִּשְׁנָיוֹת יִהְיֶה קִיבּוּץ גָּלֻיּוֹת
teaching that through the study of the Mishnayot the ingathering of the exiles will occur;
דְּהוּא אָתֵי מִדָּוִד, עַל כֵּן הָיָה כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ בָּזֶה
and being descended from David, all his striving focused upon this goal.
וּכְמָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (צ״ח סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״אִי מִן חַיַּיָּא הוּא — כְּגוֹן רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ״
And as the Sages stated in Sanhedrin (98b): "If Mashiach is among the living, he is someone like our holy Master [Rebbe]";
וְלֹא בְּחִנָּם נְקָטוּהוּ לְמָשָׁל, רַק מִסְּתָמָא הָיָה הוּא רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת מָשִׁיחַ אִילּוּ הָיָה הַדּוֹר זַכַּאי
and not in vain did they cite him as an example, for he was worthy of being the Messiah had his generation possessed merit;
וְגַם הוּא ״חַי וְקַיָּם״, כְּמַשְׁמָעוּת עוּבְדָא דִּכְתוּבּוֹת (ק״ג סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳) דְּאָתֵי כָּל בֵּי שִׁמְשֵׁי
and he too is "alive and enduring," as indicated by the incident in Kesubos (103a) where he visited his home every twilight after his passing;
וְנָטַע נְטִיעָה שֶׁל שִׂמְחָה בְּפוּרִים (מְגִלָּה ה׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳)
and Rebbe planted a planting of joy on Purim (Megillah 5b);
לְהוֹרוֹת נָתַן: דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשִּׂמְחָתוֹ גְּדוֹלָה מִקַּבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה דְּפוּרִים
to demonstrate that although the joy of re-accepting the Torah on Purim is immense;
עַדַיִין אֵין הַשִּׂמְחָה שְׁלֵימָה לִהְיוֹת בְּנַיְיחָא גְּמוּרָה כְּיוֹם טוֹב
our gladness is not yet complete enough to enjoy the work-prohibited rest of an official festival;
כָּל זְמַן דְּ״אַכַּתֵּי עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן״ (שָׁם י״ד עַמּוּד א׳), וְלֹא נֶעֶקְרוּ עַדַיִין תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב וְשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר בְּתַמּוּז
so long as "we are still the servants of Ahasuerus" (ibid. 14a) and the fasts of Tisha B'Av and the Seventeenth of Tammuz remain unabolished.
דְּאַף שֶׁנֶּאֱבַד נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר הַמַּחֲרִיב הָרִאשׁוֹן, כָּל דְּעַדַיִין קְלִיפַּת אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ קַיֶּימֶת — עַדַיִין הַגָּלוּת קַיָּים
For even though Nebuchadnezzar the first destroyer was destroyed, as long as the husk of Ahasuerus endures the exile persists;
שֶׁלֹּא לְחִנָּם נָקְטוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (שָׁם) הַלָּשׁוֹן: ״אַכַּתֵּי עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן״ עַיֵּין שָׁם
for not casually did the Gemara employ the phrase "we are still the servants of Ahasuerus";
אַף דִּכְבָר אָבְדָה מַלְכוּתוֹ וּמֶמְשַׁלְתּוֹ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אוֹתוֹ חֵלֶק רָע הַשַּׁיָּיךְ לוֹ לֹא נֶאֱבַד מִן הָעוֹלָם לְגַמְרֵי עַדַיִין, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין הַגְּאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה
for although his physical dynasty vanished, the evil husk of his empire has not been eradicated from the world as long as redemption remains incomplete.
כִּי מִפַּרְעֹה הָיְתָה גְּאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה, דְּשָׁם הָיָה הַגָּלוּת בְּעַבְדוּת, וּכְבָר יָצָאנוּ מֵעַבְדוּת לְחֵירוּת
For from Pharaoh redemption was complete, the Egyptian exile being chattel slavery from which we were totally liberated;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָנוּ בַּגָּלוּת וַעֲבָדִים לְמַלְכֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת, אֵינוֹ דֶּרֶךְ עַבְדוּת גָּמוּר כִּבְמִצְרַיִם
and although we dwell in exile subject to foreign rulers, it is not chattel slavery as in Egypt;
וַאֲפִילּוּ מִי שֶׁמִּשְׁתַּעְבְּדִים בּוֹ עֲבוֹדַת עֶבֶד בְּפָרֶךְ, הוּא בֶּן חוֹרִין מִצַּד הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּקִרְבּוֹ, שֶׁכָּל הָעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה הוּא חֵרוּת מֵהַכֹּל (אָבוֹת ו:ב)
and even one subjected to crushing labor is spiritually a free man through the Torah, for he who engages in Torah is free from all bondage (Avos 6:2);
וּלְפִיכָךְ מֵעַבְדוּת דְּפַרְעֹה כְּבָר יָצָאנוּ וְאֵין עוֹד בָּעוֹלָם מִשֶּׁנִּיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה וְנִבְחַרְנוּ לְעַם ה׳
wherefore from Pharaoh's servitude we are forever liberated since the Giving of the Torah.
אֲבָל עַבְדוּת דַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אַכַּתֵּי יֶשְׁנוֹ, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁאָנוּ בַּגָּלוּת תַּחַת יַד מַלְכֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
But the servitude of Ahasuerus persists so long as we remain in exile under foreign monarchs;
וַאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמַּלְכוּת הָרְשָׁעָה, הַיְינוּ הַקְּלִיפָּה דְּמַלְכוּת דְּסִטְרָא אָחֳרָא שֶׁלְּעוּמַּת מַלְכוּת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּקְדֻשָּׁה
Ahasuerus being the root of the wicked empire, the unholy husk of Kingship standing opposite King Solomon in holiness;
וְעַל כֵּן אִיתָא גַּם כֵּן בִּכְתוּבּוֹת (נ״א סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): ״הָא בְּמַלְכוּת אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ״, נְקָטוּהוּ לְמָשָׁל עַל מַלְכוּת גְּדוֹלָה דְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
wherefore Kesubos (51b) cites "in the kingdom of Ahasuerus" as the archetype of a great gentile empire;
אַף דְּיֵשׁ לוֹמַר לְפִי שֶׁאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ קִבֵּץ בְּתוּלוֹת לִזְנוּת, שָׁם הָיָה אַדְּרַבָּא לִישָּׂא אַחַת מֵהֶם, וְלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ דְּוַדַּאי לֹא יִשָּׂאֶנָּה, וְדֶרֶךְ שִׁבְיָה לֹא מָצִינוּ בוֹ
even though Ahasuerus gathered maidens to marry one of them rather than holding captive prisoners;
אֲבָל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמַּלְכוּת הָרְשָׁעָה כַּאֲשֶׁר הִיא בְּכָל תֹּקֶף כָּבוֹד וִיקָר עֹשֶׁר וּגְדוּלָּה נִקְרֵאת עַל שְׁמוֹ
the archetypal wicked empire displayed in the height of honor, wealth, and majesty being called after his name.
וְאַף בִּזְמַן בַּיִת שֵׁנִי נִשְׁאֲרוּ רוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּגָּלוּת תַּחַת יַד מַלְכֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
And even during the Second Temple the majority of Israel remained in the diaspora under foreign rule;
וְאִילּוּ עָלוּ כוּלָּם כְּחוֹמָה וְיָצְאוּ מִכְּלַל עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ וּמַלְכֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת, הָיְתָה בֶּאֱמֶת גְּאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא עוֹד רָקָב שׁוֹלֵט
and had they all ascended like a wall, shaking off the servitude of Ahasuerus, the redemption would have been complete, untouched by rot;
אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא עָלוּ כוּלָּם, וּמִיּוֹם שֶׁגָּלוּ בְּחֻרְבָּן רִאשׁוֹן לֹא יָצְאוּ כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל מִכְּלַל גָּלוּת עַדַיִין
but they did not all ascend, and from the First Destruction collective Israel has never departed from exile.
וְזֶהוּ הָרְחִיצָה דְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר בְּתַמּוּז, שֶׁהִשְׁתַּדֵּל לְהָקֵל עוֹל הַגָּלוּת שֶׁבַּעֲבוּרוֹ נִקְבְּעוּ הַצּוֹמוֹת, שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים שְׁמָד חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
And this was Rebbe's bathing on the Seventeenth of Tammuz, striving to lighten the burden of exile that caused the fasts, preventing persecutions;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בִּקֵּשׁ לַעֲקוֹר תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לְגַמְרֵי עַל יְדֵי שֶׁחָל פַּעַם אַחַת בְּשַׁבָּת
and afterward he sought to uproot Tisha B'Av completely when it coincided with Shabbat;
וְנִתְאַמֵּץ אָז עַל יְדֵי קְדֻשַּׁת שַׁבָּת הַחוֹפֶפֶת עָלָיו לִהְיוֹת נִדְחֶה לְגַמְרֵי וְשֶׁיֵּהָפֵךְ לְשָׂשׂוֹן וּלְשִׂמְחָה
seeking through the Sabbath's holiness to abolish it entirely and transform it into gladness;
אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הוֹדוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים, כִּי לֹא הִגִּיעַ הַקֵּץ עַדַיִין
except that the Sages did not concede, for the appointed End had not yet arrived.
וְהַתְחָלָתוֹ בְּעֵסֶק זֶה דַּעֲקִירַת תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב הָיָה עַל יְדֵי הַנְּטִיעָה דְּפוּרִים
And his initiation of this endeavor to uproot Tisha B'Av began through his planting on Purim;
שֶׁהַנְּטִיעָה שֶׁל שִׂמְחָה הוּא לְהַרְאוֹת שִׂמְחָתוֹ בְּיוֹם זֶה עַל יְדֵי הַנְּטִיעָה, שֶׁרוֹמֵז לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּלְקִיבּוּץ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
that joyous planting demonstrating his gladness through planting, which alludes to words of Torah and assembling scholars;
וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַעֲנִית (ז׳ עַמּוּד א׳): ״׳כִּי הָאָדָם עֵץ הַשָּׂדֶה׳ (דְּבָרִים כ:יט)... אִם תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הָגוּן הוּא — מִמֶּנּוּ תֹאכֵל״
as written in Ta'anit (7a): "'for man is as the tree of the field'—if he is a worthy Torah scholar, from him you shall eat";
וְאָמְרוּ שָׁם אַחַר כָּךְ: ״לָמָּה נִמְשְׁלוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּעֵץ... קָטָן מַדְלִיק אֶת הַגָּדוֹל וְכוּלֵיהּ״
and the Talmud continues: "why are words of Torah compared to wood? A small branch kindles a large log";
וְזֶה טַעַם מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (ט״ז רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳): בַּעֲצֶרֶת עַל פֵּירוֹת הָאִילָן
and this is the deeper reason why on Shavuot judgment is rendered on the fruit of trees (Rosh Hashanah 16a).
וְעִיקַּר שִׂמְחַת הַפּוּרִים שֶׁלּוֹ הָיָה שֶׁזָּכָה עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְאוֹתָהּ הַנְּטִיעָה שֶׁל שִׂמְחָה
And Rebbe's essential joy on Purim was that he merited that planting of gladness;
שֶׁזָּכָה לָהּ בַּיְשִׁיבָה הַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ, שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר הָיָה כָּל כְּנֵסִיַּית חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶצְלוֹ
meriting the great academy where all the scholars of Israel were gathered under him;
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּגִיטִּין (נ״ט עַמּוּד א׳): ״מִימוֹת מֹשֶׁה וְעַד רַבִּי לֹא מָצִינוּ תּוֹרָה וּגְדֻלָּה בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד, וְכֵן מֵרַבִּי עַד רַב אַשִׁי״
wherefore Gittin (59a) states: "from Moshe until Rebbe we find not Torah and greatness united in one place, and from Rebbe until Rav Ashi";
כִּי לִיסוֹד הַתּוֹרָה הֶכְרֵחַ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כָּל הַתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים יַחַד תַּחַת רֹאשׁ וּמַנְהִיג אֶחָד
for the foundational codification of Torah requires all scholars united under a single head;
אִם לַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב בִּימֵי מֹשֶׁה, וְכֵן לַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בִּימֵי רַבִּי וְרַב אַשִׁי מְיַסְּדֵי הַמִּשְׁנָה וְהַתַּלְמוּד
both for the Written Torah under Moshe, and the Oral Torah under Rebbe and Rav Ashi who compiled the Mishnah and the Talmud;
שֶׁהוּא פֵּירוּשׁ הַמִּשְׁנָה שֶׁהֵם כְּלָלוּת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁבְּיָדֵינוּ, וְזֶהוּ הַנְּטִיעָה שֶׁל שִׂמְחָה שֶׁלּוֹ בְּפוּרִים
which constitute the sum of the Oral Law in our hands, this being his joyous planting on Purim.
וְעִיקַּר שִׂמְחָתוֹ עַל יְדֵי עֲשִׂיַּית מְלָאכָה דַּיְיקָא
And his primary celebration was expressed specifically through performing work;

כִּי אִילּוּ הָיָה גְּאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה וְהָיָה נִכְלֶה הָרָע לְגַמְרֵי מִן הָעוֹלָם, אֵין רְבוּתָא מַה שֶּׁקִּבְּלוּ הַתּוֹרָה מֵאַהֲבָה וְשִׂמְחָה אַחַר שֶׁאֵין שָׂטָן וּפֶגַע רָע לְהַסִּית וְלִמְנוֹעַ
for had the redemption been complete and evil eradicated, there would be no novelty in embracing Torah with joy when no adversary incites or impedes;
וּבָזֶה הָיְתָה שִׂמְחָתוֹ יְתֵירָה: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה עַדַיִין גְּאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה לִהְיוֹת בְּנַיְיחָא גְּמוּרָה, וְ״אַכַּתֵּי עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן״
and in this his rejoicing was greater: that although redemption is not yet complete and we remain subjects of Ahasuerus;
וְ״הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה וְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכִיּוֹת״ הֵם הַמְעַכְּבִים בְּיָדֵינוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרָכוֹת (י״ז רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳)
and the yetzer and foreign rule impede our doing His will (Berachos 17a);
עַל כָּל זֶה אָנוּ זָכִינוּ לְקַבָּלַת תּוֹרָה מֵאַהֲבָה, וּלְהִתְיַיגֵּעַ בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
despite all this we merited to re-accept the Torah out of love and toil in the Oral Law;
עַד שֶׁבְּיָמָיו נִשְׁלַם שְׁלֵימוּת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בְּחִבּוּר הַמִּשְׁנָה שֶׁפָּשְׁטָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לִהְיוֹת דּוּגְמַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
until in his days the Oral Torah reached fruition in the Mishnah, becoming structured like the Written Law.
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר יִתְרוֹן הָאוֹר כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא בָּא מִתּוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ
And this is the supreme advantage of light when it breaks forth out of darkness (Koheles 2:13);
וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב גַּם כֵּן בְּתַנְחוּמָא פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה עַל פָּסוּק: ״הָעָם הַהֹלְכִים בַּחֹשֶׁךְ — רָאוּ אוֹר גָּדוֹל״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ט:א)
as written in Tanchuma (Noach §3) regarding the Oral Torah: "The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light" (Yeshayah 9:1);
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הַכֹּחַ רָצָה לַעֲקוֹר תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב: דְּ״גַם כִּי יִתְנוּ בַגּוֹיִם״ (הוֹשֵׁעַ ח:י), אַף בִּהְיוֹתָם נְתוּנִים תַּחַת יַד הַגּוֹיִם וְעַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ — ״עַתָּה אֲקַבְּצֵם״:
and through this strength Rebbe sought to uproot Tisha B'Av, for "though they study among the nations, now will I gather them"!

20.h: The theme: The Megillah recounting Ahasuerus's might as the surrounding husk, and the poverty of the Men of the Great Assembly. The Megillah recounts the might of Ahasuerus because his unholy empire mimics King Solomon’s holy monarchy like an ape before man. Ahasuerus sought to sit upon the throne of Hashem and boasted of his banquet, challenging whether such bliss exists in the World to Come (Esther Rabbah 2:4), imagining his rule was the Kingdom of Heaven in wisdom, might, and riches. In truth, he was merely the unholy husk encasing the fruit—the Men of the Great Assembly who were under his dominion. They embodied the true lower wisdom of Solomon; true might in subduing the yetzer, where they bound the inclination for idolatry and gouged out the eyes of the inclination for licentiousness (Yoma 69b); and true wealth, being content with their lot. Although they enjoyed peace in Babylonia and Persia (wherefore the majority refused to ascend to the Holy Land where poverty was severe, constructing a menorah of wood, Ribash §153), they joyfully chose dry bread in the Land of Israel over all the luxuries of the diaspora. They were worthy of the final redemption, matching the generation of Hezekiah who was considered for Mashiach (Sanhedrin 94a), neither requiring the bow of war (Bereishis Rabbah 35:2); yet sin delayed it, the unholy husk preceding the fruit like darkness preceding light (Shabbat 77b). At the end of the Megillah, even after Esther put on royalty, Ahasuerus laid a tax tribute (Esther 10:1) to mimic King Solomon who imposed levies (I Melachim 9:15), demonstrating that while the salvation was immense, Israel remained under imperial tribute.

p: וּלְכָךְ כָּלַל הַמְּגִלָּה גַּם כֵּן לְסַפֵּר תָּקְפּוֹ שֶׁל אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ
And therefore the Megillah includes the chronicle of the might of Ahasuerus;
שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ מַלְכוּת הָרִשְׁעָה הַמִּתְדַּמֵּית כְּקוֹף בִּפְנֵי אָדָם לַמַּלְכוּת הַקְּדוֹשָׁה דִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which is the power of the wicked kingdom mimicking the holy monarchy of King Solomon like an ape before man;
שֶׁהָיְתָה תֹּקֶף הִתְגַּלּוּת הַמַּלְכוּת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
which was the zenith of the revelation of holy Kingship in this world;
וּתְחִלָּתוֹ חָשַׁב לֵישֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא ה׳ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם דּוּגְמַת כִּסֵּא שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
Ahasuerus initially scheming to sit upon the throne of Hashem like the throne of King Solomon;
עַד שֶׁהִתְפָּאֵר מִמִּשְׁתֶּה שֶׁעָשָׂה, שֶׁאָמַר: ״אִית לְכוּ כְּהַאי גַּוְונָא לְעוֹלָם הַבָּא?״ כִּדְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ אֶסְתֵּר (פָּרָשָׁה ב׳:ד׳)
boasting at his feast: "Do you have anything like this in the World to Come?" (Esther Rabbah 2:4);
כִּי חָשַׁב כֹּחַ מַלְכוּתוֹ הוּא מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם וְשַׁלְוָה שְׁלֵימָה בְּחָכְמָה וּגְבוּרָה וְעֹשֶׁר
presuming his dominion was the Kingdom of Heaven in consummate wisdom, might, and riches.
כִּי הוּא קְלִיפַּת הַפְּרִי, שֶׁהֵם חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁהָיוּ אָז תַּחַת מַלְכוּתוֹ
For he was the outer husk encasing the fruit: the Sages of Israel and Men of the Great Assembly under his dominion;
שֶׁהֵם יְסוֹד הַחָכְמָה דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהִיא חָכְמַת שְׁלֹמֹה, ״חָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה״
who were the foundation of the Oral Torah, the wisdom of Solomon, lower wisdom;
וְהַגְּבוּרָה בִּכְבִישַׁת הַיֵּצֶר, דְּבִטְּלוּהוּ לְיִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וַחֲבָשׁוּהוּ וְנִקְרוּנְהוּ לְעֵינֵיהּ לְיִצְרָא דַּעֲרָיוֹת, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיוֹמָא (ס״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
and might in subduing the yetzer, abolishing the inclination for idolatry and blinding the inclination for immorality (Yoma 69b);
וְהָעֹשֶׁר הָאֲמִיתִּי דְּ״שָׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ״ (אָבוֹת ד:א)
and true riches in being content with one's lot (Avos 4:1);
כִּי הֵם הָיוּ אָז בְּבָבֶל וּפָרַס בְּשַׁלְוָה וְעֹשֶׁר, וּלְפִיכָךְ לֹא רָצוּ רוּבָּם לַעֲלוֹת
for they dwelled in Persia in wealth and ease, wherefore the majority refused to ascend;
כִּי בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיוּ בְּתַכְלִית הָעֹנִי אָז עַד שֶׁעָשׂוּ מְנוֹרָה שֶׁל עֵץ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כ״ד עַמּוּד ב׳)
in the Land of Israel poverty being so severe that they fashioned a Temple menorah of wood (Rosh Hashanah 24b);
וְעַיֵּין בְּרִיבָ״שׁ (סִימָן קנ״ג): דְּאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה הַמְתַקְּנִים הַתַּקָּנוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּשֶׁעָלוּ מֵהַגּוֹלָה הָיוּ עֲנִיִּים עַד מְאֹד וְכוּלֵיהּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם בֵּיאוּרוֹ
see Responsa of the Rivash (§153): the Men of the Great Assembly were impoverished when ascending from exile;

וְעַל כָּל זֶה בְּשִׂמְחַת לֵב בָּחֲרוּ בְּפַת חֲרֵבָה וְשַׁלְוָה בָּהּ (מִשְׁלֵי י״ז:א׳) בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִכָּל חֲמוּדוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ תַּחַת יַד מַלְכֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
yet with gladness of heart they chose dry bread and tranquility in the Holy Land over all worldly luxuries in the diaspora;
שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת לְאַתְחַלְתָּא דִּגְאוּלָּה, דְּעַל כֵּן זָכוּ לְבִיאָה שְׁנִיָּה וּבִנְיַן הַבַּיִת
being perfected for the dawn of redemption, wherefore they merited the second entry and the building of the Temple.
וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיוֹמָא (ט׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״דְּבִירָה תּוֹכִיחַ דְּרִאשׁוֹנִים עֲדִיפֵי״
As stated in Yoma (9b): the Temple proves that the earlier generations were superior;
וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה ל״ה:ב׳): דְּב׳ דּוֹרוֹת לֹא הוּצְרְכוּ לַקֶּשֶׁת: דְּחִזְקִיָּה וְאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה
and in Bereishis Rabbah (35:2): two generations did not require the sign of the rainbow: the generation of Hezekiah and the Men of the Great Assembly;
וּדְחִזְקִיָּה כְּבָר אָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (צ״ד עַמּוּד א׳): דְּבִקֵּשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַעֲשׂוֹתוֹ מָשִׁיחַ
and regarding Hezekiah, Sanhedrin (94a) states that Hashem sought to make him Mashiach;
וּמִסְּתָמָא גַּם בְּדוֹר אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה כֵּן, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר לְקַמָּן דִּרְאוּיִם הָיוּ וְכוּלֵיהּ, אֶלָּא שֶׁגָּרַם הַחֵטְא
and so with the Great Assembly who were worthy of miracles, but sin prevented it;
בְּתֹקֶף הַקְּלִיפָּה הַסּוֹבֶבֶת לַפְּרִי, וְהִיא גַּם כֵּן קוֹדֶמֶת לָהּ
through the husk encasing the fruit, which precedes the fruit;
וְכִבְרִיָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם: דִּ״בְרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא — וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא״ (שַׁבָּת ע״ז עַמּוּד ב׳)
matching Creation: first darkness, then light (Shabbat 77b);
וְעַל כֵּן בַּתְּחִלָּה הָיָה הִתְגַּלּוּת תָּקְפּוֹ דַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ: ״בְּהַרְאֹתוֹ אֶת עֹשֶׁר כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ״ (אֶסְתֵּר א:ד), תִּפְאֶרֶת מַלְכוּתוֹ הָרְשָׁעָה
wherefore the Megillah opens with the display of Ahasuerus's might and the glory of his wicked empire.
וְגַם בַּסּוֹף, אַחַר הִתְגַּלּוּת הַיְשׁוּעָה וּלְבִישַׁת אֶסְתֵּר הַמַּלְכוּת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה, עַל כָּל זֶה לֹא סָר תָּקְפּוֹ דַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ
And at the conclusion, even after the salvation and Esther clothing herself in holy royalty, Ahasuerus's power did not fully depart;
״וַיָּשֶׂם [הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרֹשׁ] מַס״ (אֶסְתֵּר י:א) גַּם כֵּן לְהִתְדַּמּוֹת לַתֹּקֶף דִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה בְּשִׂימַת מַס כַּכָּתוּב בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר
"and king Ahasuerus laid a tribute" (Esther 10:1), mimicking King Solomon who laid a tribute (I Melachim 9:15);
וְעַד שֶׁאָמְרוּ אַחַר כָּךְ לִרְחַבְעָם: ״אָבִיךָ הִכְבִּיד אֶת עֻלֵּנוּ״ (שָׁם י״ב:ד׳)
to the point that Israel told Rehoboam: "Your father made our yoke grievous" (ibid. 12:4);
וּרְחַבְעָם שֶׁהֵשִׁיב: ״אָבִי יִסַּר [אֶתְכֶם בַּשּׁוֹטִים, וַאֲנִי אֲיַסֵּר אֶתְכֶם בָּעַקְרַבִּים]״ (שָׁם:י״א), כִּי זֶהוּ תֹּקֶף הַמַּלְכוּת כַּאֲשֶׁר הִיא בְּתַכְלִית הַתֹּקֶף
Rehoboam responding: "my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions" (ibid. 12:11), this being the display of raw imperial power;
וְאַף זֶה אַחַר כָּךְ גַּם כֵּן הוֹסִיף עוֹד בְּעֹז מַלְכוּתוֹ בְּשִׂימַת מַס: ״וְכָל מַעֲשֵׂה תָקְפּוֹ וּגְבוּרָתוֹ... הֲלֹא הֵם כְּתוּבִים [עַל סֵפֶר דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים]״ (אֶסְתֵּר י:ב)
and Ahasuerus added unto his empire by laying taxes: "and all the acts of his power and of his might... are they not written" (Esther 10:2);
כִּי לֹא בָא לְהַזְכִּיר בַּמְּגִלָּה רַק שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ תֹּקֶף וּגְבוּרָה, וּדְ״אַכַּתֵּי עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן״:
recording in the Megillah his imperial might to remind us that "we are still the servants of Ahasuerus"!

20.h: The theme: The Megillah opening with the chronicle of servitude, light shining from within darkness, and the drunken serenity of Purim. In its literal sense, recounting Ahasuerus's might at the beginning and end was necessary out of dread of the empire, for Israel remained subjects under Persian rule. When the Sages initially hesitated to record the Megillah, arguing: "You will arouse jealousy and hatred against us among the nations" (Megillah 7a), Esther answered that the narrative was already inscribed in Persian chronicles. To appease imperial eyes, they recorded the greatness of Ahasuerus. Yet because the Megillah was dictated by the Holy Spirit, it contains no mundane secular history; recounting imperial might is an integral part of the miracle. The Talmud opens the homiletical introduction to Esther with: "For we are bondmen; yet our God has not forsaken us in our bondage" (Ezra 9:9; Megillah 11a), teaching that although we are still subjects of Ahasuerus, Hashem never abandoned us. "When I sit in darkness, Hashem shall be a light unto me" (Michah 7:8)—Israel toiling in Torah under foreign dominion, which is superior to study in tranquility (Yoma 9b). Wisdom was fully rectified in Israel, whereas among the nations wisdom vanished from Edom (Ovadiah 1:8). But regarding wealth, honor, and might, rectification was achieved only temporarily on Purim as a day of "feasting and gladness," where joy is experienced not through the holiness of the day as on a Yom Tov, but through the banquet of kings in worldly ease. Therefore one must drink ad d'lo yada, attaining mental composure through wine. Through this mitzvah, even mundane serenity is sanctified; one who has a legal dispute with a gentile should schedule it in Adar (Ta'anit 29b), for then Israel’s might dominates worldly foes. In Adar the fear of the Jews fell upon the nations, demonstrating that we are no longer servants of Ahasuerus, serving as the direct prelude to the ultimate redemption of Nisan, linking redemption to redemption!

p: וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ הַפְּשָׁט: סִפּוּר הַתֹּקֶף שֶׁלּוֹ בַּתְּחִלָּה וָסוֹף הוּא מִפְּנֵי מוֹרָא מַלְכוּת, בִּהְיוֹתָם ״אַכַּתֵּי עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ״ וִירֵאִים מֵהָאוּמּוֹת
And in its literal sense: recounting his might at the beginning and end was necessary out of dread of the empire, they remaining subjects of Ahasuerus, fearing the nations;

וּכְמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (מְגִלָּה ז׳ עַמּוּד א׳): דְּשָׁלְחוּ לְאֶסְתֵּר: ״קִנְאָה אַתְּ מְעוֹרֶרֶת עָלֵינוּ [לְבֵין הָאֻמּוֹת]״, רַק דֶּהֱשִׁיבָה: ״דִּכְבָר כְּתוּבָה אֲנִי [עַל דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים] וְכוּלֵיהּ״
as stated in Megillah (7a): they sent to Esther: "You will arouse jealousy against us among the nations," she responding: "I am already recorded in the chronicles";
וְעַל כֵּן הֻכְרְחוּ לִכְתּוֹב עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַכָּתוּב, וּלְהַרְאוֹת כְּאִילּוּ בָּאִים לְסַפֵּר תָּקְפּוֹ וּגְדוּלָּתוֹ דַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ
wherefore they were compelled to frame the narrative as though praising the might of Ahasuerus;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכְּפִי זֶה יִהְיֶה כָּל זֶה שֶׁלֹּא לְצֹרֶךְ הַנֵּס, אֲבָל בִּהְיוֹת הַמְּגִלָּה כּוּלָּהּ בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ וּמִכְּלַל הַכְּתוּבִים
and although this might appear unrelated to the miracle, the Megillah being composed through the Holy Spirit within the biblical canon;
אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בָּהּ סִפּוּרֵי דְּבָרִים מִמִּילֵּי דְּעָלְמָא
it is impossible that it contain mundane secular history.
אֲבָל גַּם זֶה גּוּפוֹ מִכְּלַל עִיקַּר הַנֵּס וּקְדֻשַּׁת הַיּוֹם: מַה דִּ״כְתֵי עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן״
But this itself is of the essence of the miracle and the sanctity of the day: that we remain the servants of Ahasuerus;
עַד שֶׁמִּפְּנֵי מוֹרָאוֹ וּכְבוֹדוֹ הֻכְרְחוּ גַּם כֵּן לְהַזְכִּיר תָּקְפּוֹ, וְעִם כָּל תָּקְפּוֹ לֹא עָצַר כֹּחַ נֶגֶד יִשְׂרָאֵל
such that out of his fear they recorded his might, yet with all his imperial power he could not prevail against Israel;
שֶׁגַּם הוּא רָצָה לְהַשְׁמִידָם כְּמָשָׁל דְּ״בַעַל הַתֵּל וּבַעַל הַחֲרִיץ״ (מְגִלָּה י״ד רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳)
he likewise desiring their destruction, as in the parable of the mound and the ditch (ibid. 14a);
וְזֶהוּ דְּפָתְחֵי לָהּ פִּתְחָא מֵהָכָא: ״כִּי עֲבָדִים אֲנַחְנוּ, וּבְעַבְדֻתֵנוּ לֹא עֲזָבָנוּ [אֱלֹהֵינוּ] וְגוֹמֵר״ (עֶזְרָא ט:ט), כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (שָׁם י״א רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳)
this being why the Sages opened their exposition with: "For we are bondmen; yet our God has not forsaken us in our bondage" (Ezra 9:9; Megillah 11a);
שֶׁזֶּהוּ כָּל עִנְיַן סִפּוּר הַמְּגִלָּה: בְּהוֹדָעַת תָּקְפּוֹ דַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ, דְּאַכַּתֵּי עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן וְעַל כָּל זֶה לֹא עֲזָבָנוּ ה׳
this being the theme of the Megillah: making known Ahasuerus's might to teach that though we are subjects, Hashem never abandoned us.
וְגַם: ״כִּי אֵשֵׁב בַּחֹשֶׁךְ — ה׳ אוֹר לִי״ (מִיכָה ז:ח), וְ״לַיְּהוּדִים הָיְתָה אוֹרָה״ (אֶסְתֵּר ח:טז) מִתּוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ הַגָּדוֹל
And also: "though I sit in darkness, Hashem shall be a light unto me" (Michah 7:8), and "the Jews had light" from within immense darkness;
וְזֶה עָדִיף, דְּאִיכָּא שִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכִיּוֹת וְקָעָסְקֵי בַּתּוֹרָה, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיוֹמָא (ט׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
and this is superior: toiling in Torah despite imperial subjugation (Yoma 9b);
וְכֵן אָז: קַבָּלַת עוֹל תּוֹרָה מֵאַהֲבָה עִם הֱיוֹתָם עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ
accepting the yoke of Torah out of love while remaining subjects of Ahasuerus;
וּכְפִי הַתֹּקֶף דַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ, כָּךְ ״זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה״ הָיָה הַתֹּקֶף דִּקְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל אָז
and matching the imperial might of Ahasuerus, in parallel opposition stood the mighty holiness of Israel;
שֶׁמֵּחֲמָתוֹ זָכוּ: ״לְאוֹרָה וְשִׂמְחָה וְשָׂשׂוֹן וִיקָר״ (אֶסְתֵּר ח:טז)
through which they merited light, gladness, joy, and honor (Esther 8:16).
וּמִצַּד הַחָכְמָה תִּיקְּנוּ הַכֹּל, וְלֹא נִשְׁאַר אֵצֶל אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ כְּלוּם, וְלֹא נִזְכַּר אֶצְלוֹ זֵכֶר מֵחָכְמָה
And regarding wisdom they rectified all things, no wisdom remaining with Ahasuerus;
רַק אֵצֶל הָמָן מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב לוֹ: ״חֲכָמָיו״ (אֶסְתֵּר ו:יג) עַל מַפַּלְתּוֹ
mentioned merely regarding Haman whose "wise men" predicted his fall;
וּבָזֶה אָבְדָה הַחָכְמָה גַּם מֵאֱדוֹם אָז, שֶׁלֹּא נִמְצָא רוֹשֶׁם דּוּגְמָא מֵחָכְמַת שְׁלֹמֹה עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אֶלָּא בְּלִבְּבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
wisdom vanishing from Edom (Ovadiah 1:8), the imprint of Solomon's wisdom residing solely within Jewish hearts;
וְרַק מִצַּד הַתֹּקֶף בְּעֹשֶׁר וְכָבוֹד וּגְבוּרָה, שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַן עַדַיִין לְגַמְרֵי
and only regarding riches, honor, and might, which were not yet permanently rectified;
אֶלָּא לִשְׁעָתוֹ בְּיוֹם הַפּוּרִים לְבַד, שֶׁנִּקְבַּע לְ״יוֹם מִשְׁתֶּה וְשִׂמְחָה״
but merely temporarily on Purim, established as a "day of feasting and gladness";
אַף שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ קְדֻשַּׁת יוֹם טוֹב לִהְיוֹת שִׂמְחָתוֹ מִצַּד קְדֻשַּׁת הַיּוֹם
possessing no work-prohibiting sanctity where joy flows from the day's holiness;
רַק עַל דֶּרֶךְ מִשְׁתֵּה מְלָכִים מִתּוֹךְ שַׁלְוָה וּכְמִשְׁתֵּה דַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ
but experienced after the manner of a royal banquet in serene ease like Ahasuerus's feast.
וְעַל כֵּן: ״חַיָּיב לְבַסּוֹמֵי עַד דְּלָא יָדַע״ (מְגִלָּה ז׳ עַמּוּד ב׳), דְּזֶה לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ בְּשִׂמְחָה שֶׁל קְדֻשַּׁת הַיּוֹם דְּיוֹם טוֹב
Wherefore one must drink ad d'lo yada (Megillah 7b), which does not apply to the spiritual joy of a Yom Tov;
אֲבָל עִיקַּר שִׂמְחַת הַפּוּרִים הוּא כְּעֵין שִׂמְחַת אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ בְּ״הַרְאֹתוֹ... אֶת כָּל יְקָר״ עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
Purim joy resembling the feast of Ahasuerus who showed off worldly honor;
וּמִתּוֹךְ הַבִּסּוּם ״עַד דְּלָא יָדַע״, יוּכַל כָּל אֶחָד לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁלְוָה וְתֹקֶף בְּמוֹחוֹ עַל יְדֵי הַיַּיִן דִּישַׂמַּח, וּבִפְרָט בְּעֵת שִׁכְרוּת
and through drinking ad d'lo yada every Jew experiences mental tranquility through gladdening wine;
אֶלָּא שֶׁאֶצְלָם הוּא מִצַּד חוֹבַת קִיּוּם הַמִּצְוָה לְבַד, עַל כֵּן הַכֹּל בִּקְדֻשָּׁה
except that within Israel it is fulfilled as an obligatory mitzvah, rendering it entirely holy;
וּבָזֶה יִקָּלֵט גַּם שִׂמְחָה כָּזוֹ שֶׁבְּדֶרֶךְ שַׁלְוָה כְּהָנְהוּ בְּנֵי גֵּיהִנָּם הָעוֹשִׂים כָּל יְמֵיהֶם כְּחַגִּים אֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ
elevating even secular tranquility unto holiness;
וְעַל כֵּן מַאן דְּאִית לֵיהּ דִּינָא בַּהֲדֵי גּוֹי — לֵידִין בַּאֲדָר (תַּעֲנִית כ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
wherefore he who has a lawsuit with a gentile should adjudicate it in Adar (Ta'anit 29b);
כִּי אָז הוּא כֹּחַ הַתֹּקֶף וּגְבוּרָה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נֶגֶד אוֹיְבֵיהֶם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה אָז עַל יְדֵי שֶׁקְּלָטוּהוּ מֵאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ
for then Israel's worldly might dominates their foes, having extracted it from Ahasuerus;
וּלְפִי שָׁעָה אָז בַּאֲדָר: ״נָפַל פַּחַד הַיְּהוּדִים עֲלֵיהֶם״ (אֶסְתֵּר ח:יז), וְלֹא נִיכָּר כְּלָל הֱיוֹתָם עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ
the dread of the Jews falling upon the heathen, obscuring their status as subjects;
וְכֵן לַדּוֹרוֹת לְעוֹלָם בְּפוּרִים שֶׁבְּכָל שָׁנָה יֵשׁ הִתְעוֹרְרוּת דָּבָר זֶה: דְּלָאו עַבְדֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ אֲנַן עוֹד
and so in every generation on Purim this realization awakens: that we are no longer subjects of Ahasuerus;
וְהוּא אַתְחַלְתָּא לִגְאוּלָּה שְׁלֵימָה הָעֲתִידָה לִהְיוֹת בְּנִיסָן הַסָּמוּךְ לוֹ
this being the direct prelude to the ultimate redemption destined to unfold in Nisan;
וְזֶהוּ ״הַמַּסְמִיךְ גְּאוּלָּה לִגְאוּלָּה — עָדִיף״ (מְגִלָּה ו׳ עַמּוּד ב׳), כִּי הַכֹּל עִנְיָן אֶחָד:
this being why "juxtaposing redemption to redemption is superior" (Megillah 6b), for all is a single unified reality!

21.h: The theme: Shavuot as the season of the Giving of the Torah (Zman Matan Torateinu), the prayer established by the Men of the Great Assembly, and the calendar dilemma. The core essence of the festival of Shavuot is that it is the season of the Giving of the Torah (Zman Matan Torateinu), as codified by the Men of the Great Assembly in the liturgy (Berachos 33a). One must wonder at the Magen Avraham (Orach Chaim 494:1), who cited Rambam’s wording attributing this title to our custom (minhageinu). In truth, it is an ancient, universally received liturgical foundation instituted by the Great Assembly, for every festival is designated upon the historical divine event wrought within it. The commentators struggled with Rabbi Yose’s talmudic position that the Torah was given on the seventh of Sivan (Shabbat 86b), as well as the calendar fact that according to all opinions the Giving of the Torah took place on the fifty-first day from the Omer offering. Attempting to resolve this by stating that the liturgy alludes to the second diaspora day of the festival is unsatisfactory, for in the Land of Israel only a single day is observed, which is the primary biblical commandment. How could the Torah establish the festival on the fiftieth day if the Giving of the Torah occurred on the fifty-first?

p: עִנְיַן הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת עִיקָּרוֹ בַּעֲבוּר שֶׁהוּא ״זְמַן מַתַּן תּוֹרָתֵנוּ״
The essence of the festival of Shavuot is primarily because it is the season of the Giving of our Torah;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּסְּדוּ אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה בְּנוּסַח הַתְּפִלָּה
as established by the Men of the Great Assembly in the liturgy of prayer;
שֶׁהֵם תִּיקְּנוּ הַתְּפִלּוֹת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרָכוֹת (ל״ג עַמּוּד א׳)
who instituted the prayers for Israel, as written in Berachos (33a);
וְהַתֵּימָהּ מִמָּגֵן אַבְרָהָם רֵישׁ סִימָן תצ״ד שֶׁכָּתַב: ״מִנְהָגֵנוּ לוֹמַר ׳זְמַן מַתַּן תּוֹרָתֵנוּ׳״ הוּא עַל פִּי פְּסַק הָרַמְבַּ״ם
and one must wonder at the Magen Avraham (beginning of §494) who wrote: "our custom to recite 'the season of the Giving of our Torah'" is based on the ruling of the Rambam;
תָּלֵי לַהּ בְּ״מִנְהָגֵנוּ״ מַה שֶּׁהוּא פָּשׁוּט אֵצֶל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ מִימוֹת עוֹלָם
attributing to "our custom" that which has been universally self-evident unto all Israel across the entire world from time immemorial!
וּבְוַדַּאי שֶׁהוּא מִיְסוֹד אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁהִתְקִינוּ כָּל בִּרְכוֹת הַתְּפִלּוֹת, וְלֵיכָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלַהּ שֶׁזֶּהוּ קְדֻשַּׁת הַחַג
And certainly it is from the foundation of the Men of the Great Assembly who instituted all liturgical blessings, none disputing that this constitutes the sanctity of the festival;
שֶׁכָּל חַג נִקְבַּע עַל אֵיזֶה עִנְיָן שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה לָנוּ בּוֹ
for every festival is established upon the specific divine event that was wrought for us within it;
וְקוּשְׁיָתוֹ: לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי דִּבְזַיִ״ן בְּסִיוָון נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה (שַׁבָּת פ״ו עַמּוּד ב׳)
and his difficulty arose according to Rabbi Yose, who maintains that the Torah was given on the seventh of Sivan (Shabbat 86b);
וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁהִקְשָׁה עוֹד: דִּלְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל הָיָה בְּנ״א (חֲמִשִּׁים וְאֶחָד) לַסְּפִירָה
and likewise what he further challenged: that according to all authorities the Giving of the Torah occurred on the fifty-first day of the counting;
מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב לְתָרֵץ בְּשֵׁם ״יֵשׁ מְפָרְשִׁים״ דְּרוֹמֵז לְיוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי, לֹא נִרְאֶה לֵיאָמֵר עַל עִיקַּר יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁהוּא יוֹם אֶחָד לְבַדּוֹ
and what commentators answered, that this liturgy alludes to the second diaspora festival day, cannot be said concerning the primary festival day which is a single day;
וּבְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין אוֹתוֹ לְבַד, וְכֵן הוּא עִיקָּרוֹ מִן הַתּוֹרָה
and in the Land of Israel they observe it alone, which is its primary biblical status;
וְאֵיךְ קְבָעַתּוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁלֹּא בְּיוֹם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, כֵּיוָן דְּעִיקָּרוֹ שֶׁהוּא זְמַן מַתַּן תּוֹרָה:
and how could the Torah establish the festival on a day other than the Giving of the Torah, seeing that its entire essence is the season of the Giving of the Torah?!

21.h: The theme: The fifty days of the Omer, the nocturnal flash of the Exodus versus the permanent acquisition of Sinai, and the double Sabbath. Scripture commands: "seven weeks shall there be complete; even unto the morrow after the seventh week shall you number fifty days" (Vayikra 23:15–16). Commentators questioned why the verse says "number fifty days" when only forty-nine are counted. The Zohar (III, 97a) compares the Omer counting to a woman counting her seven clean days, purifying the seven emotional traits (Middot), each comprising seven (49 days), with the fiftieth day corresponding to the understanding of the heart (Binah) whence all attributes flow. At the Exodus, the divine illumination descended in an unearned flash ("skipping over the mountains", Shir HaShirim 2:8; Shir HaShirim Rabbah): Hashem passed through Egypt in His glory, dispelling all darkness from their hearts. Yet that revelation was temporary, vanishing to require active human toil. The residual impression (reshimu) remained, enabling Israel through the forty-nine days of the Omer to re-acquire that light permanently, until at Sinai the Torah was given as an eternal gift (Matan Torah). Scripture designates the first day of Pesach "Shabbat" ("on the morrow after the Shabbat", Vayikra 23:15) because Shabbat represents an immutable holiness descending directly from Hashem without prior human effort, whereas a Yom Tov is sanctified through human initiative (Yisrael d'kadshinhu). The Omer counts forty-nine days to reach that lofty Sabbath-light of Pesach, with the fiftieth day being the culmination of all effort. One toils and then discovers the gift like a lost treasure found unexpectedly (yagati u-matzati, Megillah 6b; Sanhedrin 97a). In Creation, Hashem worked for six days and rested on the seventh; but Adam was created on Friday and entered Shabbat immediately, receiving an initial divine awakening (itaruta d'le'ila) before engaging in secular work. This is the mystery of the two Sabbaths (Shabbat 118b): Moshe received the commandment of Shabbat in the Manna on Sunday, but withheld telling Israel until Friday (Shemos 16:5; Bava Kamma 92a) because he knew Israel could not attain the holiness of Shabbat through their own effort until they had first experienced it as an unearned divine gift!

p: אֲבָל נִרְאֶה לִי דִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ דִּקְרָא בְּפָרָשַׁת אֱמוֹר: ״וּסְפַרְתֶּם לָכֶם... שֶׁבַע שַׁבָּתוֹת תְּמִימֹת תִּהְיֶינָה; עַד מִמָּחֳרַת הַשַּׁבָּת הַשְּׁבִיעִת תִּסְפְּרוּ חֲמִשִּׁים יוֹם״ (וַיִּקְרָא כ״ג:ט״ו–ט״ז)

But it appears to me that the plain meaning of the verse in Parashat Emor: "And you shall count unto you... seven complete Sabbaths shall there be; even unto the morrow after the seventh Sabbath shall you count fifty days" (Vayikra 23:15–16);
נִדְחֲקוּ בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן: הֲלֹא אֵין הַסְּפִירָה נ׳ (חֲמִשִּׁים) יוֹם
the commentators struggled with it likewise: for is not the actual counting only forty-nine days, and not fifty?
וּבְלָאו הָכִי יֵשׁ לְדַקְדֵּק בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב: ״עַד מִמָּחֳרַת הַשַּׁבָּת הַשְּׁבִיעִת״, נִרְאֶה כִּמְיוּתָּר
and aside from this one must analyze the biblical phrasing: "even unto the morrow after the seventh Sabbath," which appears completely superfluous!
וְנִרְאֶה כִּידוּעַ: עִנְיַן הַסְּפִירָה דּוּגְמַת סְפִירַת נְקִיִּים דְּאִשָּׁה (זֹוהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ג׳ צ״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
And it appears according to the known mystery: the counting of the Omer mirrors a woman counting her clean days (Zohar III, 97a);
לְזַכֵּךְ וּלְטַהֵר כָּל מִדּוֹתָיו שֶׁהֵם שֶׁבַע, כָּל אֶחָד כָּלוּל מִשֶּׁבַע
to refine and purify all seven emotional attributes, each comprising seven (making 49);
וְיוֹם הַנ׳ (הַחֲמִשִּׁים) הוּא נֶגֶד הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁמִּשָּׁם נִמְשָׁכִין כָּל הַמִּדּוֹת
and the fiftieth day corresponds to the understanding of the heart (Binah), whence stream all emotional attributes.
וּבִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הָיָה הִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁלֹּא בְּדֶרֶךְ הַדְרָגָה
And at the Exodus from Egypt there was an immense divine revelation that bypassed gradual ascension;
וְעַל זֶה רָמְזוּ בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ב׳:ח׳) עַל פָּסוּק: ״מְדַלֵּג עַל הֶהָרִים, מְקַפֵּץ [עַל הַגְּבָעוֹת]״ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ב:ח)
and concerning this the Sages hinted in Shir HaShirim Rabbah (2:8) on: "leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills" (Shir HaShirim 2:8);
דְּאַף שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ רְאוּיִם לְכָךְ, הֵאִיר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עֵינֵיהֶם עַל יְדֵי הַגִּלּוּי שְׁכִינָה שֶׁהָיָה בַּלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה
that even though they were unworthy, the Blessed Name illuminated their eyes through the revelation of the Shechinah on that night;
דְּ״וְעָבַרְתִּי בְאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם... אֲנִי וְלֹא הַשָּׁלִיחַ״ (שְׁמוֹת י״ב:י״ב; הַגָּדָה שֶׁל פֶּסַח)
when "I will pass through the land of Egypt... I and not an emissary" (Shemos 12:12; Passover Haggadah);
עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְכָל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה אוֹר בְּכָל חַדְרֵי לְבָבָם מֵאוֹר שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
through which all Israel experienced light within all the chambers of their heart from the radiance of His Shechinah;
